picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Carrefour SA (CA.PA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-10-26. Sources: five calls in the transcript bundle (Q3 2024 sales call 2024-10-23, full-year 2024 results 2025-02-19, Q1 2025 sales 2025-04-24, half-year 2025 results 2025-08-13, full-year 2025 results 2026-02-17), the screener's financial block (fiscal years 2021-2025 plus trailing twelve months, or TTM, to 2026-06-30), and dated public releases since the last call: the half-year 2026 results (late July 2026) and the Q3 2026 sales release of 2026-10-20. Live price used: EUR 13.775 on Euronext Paris (FMP quote, 2026-10-26).*

**Takeaway.** Carrefour is a turnaround story that keeps delivering the cost and cash pieces it controls while the earnings line keeps disappointing. Management's words about France, cost savings and cash have mostly been borne out; its words about Brazil and the group's earnings trajectory have not. On 2026-10-20, eight months into a new plan to 2030, it cut its 2026 targets for margin, earnings per share and cash. The stock is cheap on cash flow for a reason: returns on capital are thin and the earnings record is poor.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Late 2024 (Q3 2024 call, full-year 2024 call):** the story was "invest in price to win share." France had "our strongest investment in prices" and its "best price positioning since 2020" (2025-02-19). Brazil was the growth engine: "set to enjoy an attractive growth trajectory in 2025 and beyond." Argentina posted a record EUR 115 million profit.
- **Mid-2025 (H1 2025 call, 2025-08-13):** the story turned to portfolio surgery. The February 2025 strategic review produced, "in less than a quarter," the buy-out of Carrefour Brazil minorities, a 7% sale of the Carmila property company, and exclusive talks to sell Italy. The chief executive promised to be "radical" and that "we would continue to move and to take bold decisions." The Concordis European buying alliance was launched (2025-07-07).
- **Early 2026 (full-year 2025 call, 2026-02-17):** the tone became "steady delivery." Italy was sold, Romania signed. Brazil had gone from growth engine to a market "marked by record high interest rates and negative volumes," with the claim that "the cycle trough is now behind us." France core became the hero: operating margin at "the 3% milestone," market share "22%, its highest point since 2015." The 2030 plan followed the next day (operating margin 3.2% in 2028 and 3.5% in 2030, EUR 5 billion cumulative net free cash flow in 2026-2028, high single-digit adjusted earnings-per-share growth each year, payout 50-60% of adjusted earnings).
- **Since then (dated releases):** the half-year 2026 results confirmed all 2026 targets, Romania closed and a EUR 0.21 special dividend was paid on 2026-07-30. Then on 2026-10-20 the group cut its 2026 targets, blaming "the social and security situation in France" (lost footfall, curfew-shortened opening hours, higher security and logistics costs) and energy costs squeezing shoppers. The 2028 and 2030 targets were kept.

What was quietly dropped: Brazil as the growth driver; share buybacks (none since the French buyback tax, per the CFO on 2026-02-17); and the 2026 promise of earnings-per-share growth.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Steady delivery," recurring operating income rising (2025-02-19, 2026-02-17) | Net income fell from EUR 1.66 billion (2023) to EUR 723 million (2024) to EUR 319 million (2025); earnings per share from 2.31 to 0.47. Recurring operating income in 2025 was EUR 2.158 billion, 2.6% of sales, up only "excluding Cora & Match" and before currency. | Story richer than numbers. Growth exists only after two exclusions every year. |
| Cash generation is the strength: net free cash flow EUR 1.45 billion (2024), EUR 1.565 billion (2025), EUR 1.7 billion "at sight" for 2026 (CFO, 2026-02-17) | TTM free cash flow EUR 4.51 billion before leases in the screener; the company's own net free cash flow (after lease payments and interest) of ~EUR 1.5 billion is the right figure. But on 2026-10-20 the 2026 figure was cut to "slight decline" versus 2025. The CFO's EUR 250 million bridge to 1.7 billion did not survive eight months. | Partly matched, then missed. |
| France core margin at 3% (2026-02-17) | France core recurring operating income +11.3% in 2025 with +31 basis points of margin; but Cora & Match lost EUR 120 million (EUR 25 million before one-off integration costs) after prices were cut 6-7%. Q3 2026 France like-for-like sales only +1.2%. | Matched for the core; the acquired stores are still a drag. |
| Cost savings EUR 1.2 billion a year | Delivered every year as stated (EUR 1.1 billion excluding Italy in 2025). Yet gross margin is flat at ~19.1% and net margin is 0.4%: the savings are being reinvested in price, not reaching shareholders. | Delivered, but not visible in profit. |
| Balance sheet strengthened | Net debt excluding leases EUR 5.82 billion at 2026-06-30 (seasonal peak), EUR 10.79 billion including EUR 4.97 billion of lease liabilities. Altman Z (a solvency score; under 1.8 is the distress zone) is 1.8. Return on invested capital is 4.6%, likely below the cost of capital. | Adequate, not strong. Investment-grade funding is intact (EUR 500 million bond in September 2026, EUR 4 billion credit line extended to November 2031). |
| Working capital: receivables factoring is "neutral year-on-year" (2026-02-17) | About EUR 1.4 billion of receivables (mostly Brazilian card instalments, some French franchisees) are sold to banks. This flatters reported cash flow relative to a company that does not factor. | A yellow flag on cash quality; disclosed, not hidden. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Trajectory: Declining, then defensive.**
- 2024-10-23: upbeat - "a positive inflection in most markets," consumer confidence "at their highest level since the beginning of the inflation crisis."
- 2025-02-19: confident on France and Brazil, frank that 2024 was "a challenging year."
- 2025-08-13: offensive on strategy ("radicality," "bold decisions") but evasive on numbers: "we're not going to guide" on second-half margin; on Argentina, "I'm not going to give you an outlook."
- 2026-02-17: measured. Brazil shifted to defence ("our strict cost discipline helped protect margins"). France Christmas was called "a surprising trend."
- 2026-10-20 (release): the cut itself, attributed to outside forces (French social unrest, energy costs) rather than execution.

The shift is from offence (price investment, growth, portfolio action) to defence (cost discipline, external blame).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- 2025 targets ("slight growth in EBITDA, recurring operating income and net free cash flow") were met only loosely: EBITDA "stable," recurring operating income up 2.2% excluding Cora & Match, net free cash flow EUR 1.565 billion versus EUR 1.45 billion. Met on cash, flat to missed on the rest.
- Cora & Match integration cost EUR 145 million versus EUR 150 million guided (2026-02-17). Delivered.
- 2026 targets (margin +25 basis points or more, high single-digit adjusted earnings-per-share growth, cash up) were confirmed in late July 2026 and cut on 2026-10-20 to a margin of +0 to 15 basis points, earnings per share "stable to slight growth," net free cash flow "slight decline," capital spending cut to EUR 1.6 billion from EUR 1.7 billion.
- The screener shows an earnings beat rate of 5 of 8 quarters (62%) and three-year earnings-per-share decline of 36% a year.

There is no sandbagging pattern; the pattern is optimism that gets trimmed. **Reliability: Medium-Low** - high on cost and integration targets, low on group earnings.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Cash flow quality** (Rob Joyce, BNP Paribas, 2026-02-17): pushed on the EUR 1.7 billion target and on EUR 1.4 billion of factored receivables. Answered at length, and the cash target was cut eight months later.
- **Capital allocation** (Geoffroy Michalet, ODDO BHF, 2026-02-17): why no buyback, and what happens to the Romanian proceeds? Answer: the French buyback tax, a special dividend of about 30% of proceeds, the rest kept "for flexibility and a number of opportunities." Analysts worry the cash funds more deals rather than shareholders.
- **French franchisee dispute** (same call): management said "the door is always open" - no resolution offered.
- **Brazil consumer** (Frederick Wild, Jefferies, 2025-08-13): "well oriented" was challenged; Brazil volumes then went negative for the rest of 2025 and the market was still negative in Q3 2026.
- **Argentina** (2025-08-13): profit halved and management declined to give an outlook.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: 2026 guidance cut on 2026-10-20, only three months after it was confirmed and eight months into the new plan.
- Red: Earnings per share down from 2.31 (2023) to 0.47 (2025); return on invested capital 4.6%; net margin 0.4%.
- Red: Brazil, the former growth engine, has had negative market volumes since mid-2025 under record interest rates (2026-02-17, 2026-10-20).
- Red: EUR 1.4 billion of receivables factoring (disclosed more fully from 2026-02-17) flatters cash flow.
- Red: Unresolved dispute with a group of French franchisees (2026-02-17), in a model that is moving more stores to franchise.
- Green: France core margin reached 3% with recurring operating income +11.3% in 2025; French market share at 22%, the highest since 2015 (2026-02-17).
- Green: Portfolio pruning executed on schedule - Italy sold (2025), Romania sold and a EUR 0.21 special dividend paid 2026-07-30; 35-store sale-and-leaseback in France and Spain closed early October 2026.
- Green: Funding secure - EUR 500 million bond (September 2026), credit facility extended to 2031; ex-lease net debt cut by EUR 1.1 billion year on year at 2026-06-30.
- Green: Ordinary dividend raised 5% to EUR 0.97 (proposed 2026-02-17), about a 7% yield at today's price.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Excluding" creep.** Almost every positive number in 2025-2026 is stated "excluding Cora & Match," "excluding Italy," or "at constant currency." The group-level, reported trend is flat to down.
- **Capital spending as the swing factor.** The October cut trims France investment for the rest of 2026. That props up cash flow now but contradicts the plan's push to transform stores.
- **Leadership continuity.** The chief executive's mandate was renewed (proposed 2025-08-13). No new voices on the calls; the same team owns both the delivery and the misses.
- **Competition language.** France is framed as "narrowing the price gap with the market" - an admission that Carrefour is still more expensive than the discounters and Leclerc, and must keep spending gross margin to hold share.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning (portfolio reshaping toward France, Spain and Brazil).** Execution on disposals and costs is real; earnings conversion is not.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** whether the roughly EUR 1.5 billion of annual net free cash flow (about 15% of today's EUR 9.7 billion market value) is durable shareholder cash, or keeps being consumed by price investment, deals, factoring reversals and outside shocks. The 2026-10-20 cut is the first test of the new plan, and it was failed on cash.

**Moat.** Scale purchasing (Concordis, Eureka) and a dense French convenience-franchise network give a narrow, real moat. It is not widening: gross margin is flat around 19%, return on invested capital is 4.6% and the earnings base has shrunk for two years, though France core margin is improving. Call it narrow and stable.

**Secular threat.** The large-hypermarket format faces a slow shift of spending to discounters, convenience and online. Carrefour is answering with convenience stores (a record 456 opened in 2025) and e-commerce growth (+29% in Q2 2025). That is a manageable threat, not a terminal one. The cheapness is mostly a low-return, low-trust discount rather than a melting base - a value case only if cash keeps reaching shareholders.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: At PLN 238 you pay about 0.34 times book value (roughly PLN 703 a share) for a group holding about PLN 121 a share of net cash at 30 June 2026 (PLN 758m of cash and short-term investments against PLN 141m of debt, almost all leases) and no bank borrowings. The case for closing that gap now has a dated anchor it lacked in September. On 18 September 2026 Brussels announced provisional safeguard measures on grain-oriented electrical steel, in force from 25 September 2026 to 26 February 2027: imports inside quota pay the gap to a minimum price of EUR 2,800-3,400 a tonne, and above quota to EUR 3,500 a tonne. Stalprodukt is one of only two EU producers of this steel, the other being thyssenkrupp. Its electrical-steel division saw revenue fall 47% and prices 20% year on year in the first quarter of 2026, entirely on cheap imports, so a price floor attacks the exact cause of the loss. Meanwhile the group already reached a small operating profit in the second quarter of 2026 (EBIT +PLN 3.2m versus -PLN 27.5m in the first quarter) before any protection existed. Demand behind the niche is structurally supportive: European grid and transformer build-out needs exactly this steel. If the measure is made definitive by February 2027 and the division returns even to half its 2025 quarterly contribution, the group earns money again, the restructuring management deferred can be scoped rather than forced, and the controlling holders' authorisation to buy back and cancel 10% of the shares at PLN 205-250 (30 June 2026, PLN 135m reserve) becomes both affordable and accretive. Conditions: protection made definitive, zinc processing fees stabilising, capital spending trimmed toward depreciation.
picks.bear_thesis: The discount is earned. Return on invested capital has fallen for four straight years, from about 11% in 2022 to below zero in 2025 and on a trailing basis to June 2026; trailing free cash flow is -PLN 202m and group cash fell about PLN 383m in the eighteen months to 30 June 2026, with capital spending (PLN 278m trailing) running about 1.5 times depreciation while the group loses money. The second-quarter 'recovery' is a 0.3% operating margin on PLN 1.02bn of revenue, and the near-zero net loss leans on PLN 6.9m of interest earned on the very cash being spent. The provisional safeguard is not the end of the fork: it lapses on 26 February 2027 unless made definitive, transformer makers are lobbying against it on the grounds that the two EU producers cannot supply the market, and the quotas still admit roughly the past three years' average import volumes. The zinc unit, the one profitable division, depends on Polish state electricity compensation (PLN 26.5m in the first quarter of 2026 against a PLN 28.2m divisional result) and on concentrate processing fees that collapsed from USD 100-120 a tonne in September 2025 to about USD 20 by March 2026, with 2027 largely unpriced. About PLN 155m a year of unallocated corporate cost absorbs most of what the healthy businesses earn. The dividend is gone, the previous buyback authorisation (2024) was barely used, and the shares trade a few thousand a day, so neither a buyer nor an exit is assured. What would confirm the bear: a third-quarter report (expected in November 2026) showing continued cash burn, a definitive decision that weakens or drops the measure, or zinc processing fees staying negative into 2027.
picks.consensus_delta: The market prices Stalprodukt as a broken steel converter living off its cash, at about 0.34 times book. We largely agree about the operating business and are, if anything, more cautious than the headline numbers: returns on capital are negative, not the low positive figure screens show, and corporate cost absorbs most of what the healthy divisions earn. Where we disagree with the market is narrower than in September. The provisional EU safeguard, in force since 25 September 2026, is the first trade measure that protects the price of what Stalprodukt sells rather than what it buys, and the shares have moved only about 8% (from PLN 220 on 7 September to PLN 238 on 2 November) on it - a modest reaction for a measure that sets a EUR 2,800-3,500 a tonne import price floor on a division whose prices fell 20% in a year. The market seems to be waiting for proof in the reported numbers and for the definitive decision, which is a reasonable stance; we think the probability of a definitive measure is better than even because three member states asked for it and the provisional step has already been taken. That gap is worth about PLN 20-25 a share in our fair value, not a re-rating to book.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window, the months just ahead, holds three tests. First, the third-quarter report (expected in November 2026; the exact date was not verified) will cover a quarter almost entirely before protection began, so it will likely still show losses or near-breakeven and continued cash spending - a disappointment risk that is mostly timing. Second, the zinc business: processing fees fell to about USD 20 a tonne by March 2026 with some offers negative, and 2027 volumes are largely unpriced; annual benchmark talks for 2027 typically conclude around the turn of the year and could lock in another weak year. Third, the definitive electrical-steel decision by 26 February 2027, which transformer makers are lobbying against. There is no debt maturity and no liquidity risk: net cash of about PLN 600m covers several years of the current burn. The danger is slow erosion of that cushion, not a forced event.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-selling pressure to speak of. Free float is about a third of the shares and daily turnover runs from a few hundred to a few thousand shares (3,141 shares on 2 November 2026), so the register is dominated by the controlling holders and ArcelorMittal Sourcing at about 20%. The one mechanical event, the dividend's elimination at the 30 June 2026 meeting, has passed without a visible flush: the shares are up from about PLN 220 in September. A move to our PLN 225 level would most plausibly come from a European steel or materials de-rating - for example on a weak steel-price tape or a broader risk-off - rather than from forced holders. The shares traded at PLN 199.5 to 267 over the past year, with a 50-day average near PLN 228, so PLN 225 sits inside the normal range rather than requiring a crash.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near PLN 225, which a sector-wide sell-off in European steel and materials could deliver. The thesis holds, and it is in better shape than in September. On 18 September 2026 Brussels announced provisional protection for grain-oriented electrical steel, in force from 25 September 2026 to 26 February 2027, with import price floors of EUR 2,800-3,500 a tonne. That is the favourable branch of the regulatory fork we were waiting for, and it lifts our fair value from about PLN 262 to about PLN 285 a share. The rest of the case is unchanged: about PLN 121 a share of net cash at 30 June 2026, no bank debt, a second quarter that turned a small operating profit before any protection, and controlling holders who authorised buying back a tenth of the shares at PLN 205-250. What keeps us from buying at PLN 238 is that the discount to our fair value is just under 20%, the margin we require, and the business underneath still earns a negative return on capital, burns about PLN 200m a year of free cash and relies on a zinc unit whose processing fees have collapsed. The measure is provisional; it needs to be made definitive by February 2027 and to show up in reported cash flow. At PLN 225 the upside to fair value would be about 27%, enough to pay for those risks, with the downside cushioned by net cash and the board's own buyback range. Conviction stays at 3: the value case is real but the moat is eroding, and a cheap price on a cash-draining base is not yet a bargain. The shares trade thinly, so any position should be built slowly.
picks.forcing_function: Two dated items and one open-ended one. The definitive EU safeguard decision on grain-oriented electrical steel, which must come by the end of the provisional period on 26 February 2027 - a definitive measure at or near the provisional thresholds would make the electrical-steel recovery bankable. The full-year 2026 results (around March-April 2027), the first reported period with a full quarter of protection, which will show whether the division turns cash-positive. And, at the board's discretion over five years, a price and timetable for the PLN 135m buyback at PLN 205-250, which would retire up to a tenth of the shares near today's price.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Stalprodukt S.A. (STP.WA, Warsaw) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Updated 2026-11-02. Price used: PLN 238 (Warsaw close quote, 2026-11-02).*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this name: Stalprodukt does not hold English-language calls, and none is held by our licensed data provider. This dossier is built from the filed quarterly accounts (via our data provider, through the quarter ended 30 June 2026), the company's first-quarter 2026 report (published 20 May 2026) and annual-meeting resolutions of 30 June 2026 as recorded in this committee's prior work, and dated trade-press reporting on the European Commission's electrical-steel safeguard (Reuters via GMK Center, 18 September 2026; SteelOrbis, 21 September 2026). Where a claim below rests on a management statement, it is a written statement from a periodic report, not a call quote. Our live search budget ran out before we could check two items - any board action on the share buyback since 30 June 2026 and the exact date of the third-quarter report - so both are flagged as unverified. A note on identity: our stored peer file reads this ticker as Stalprofil, a steel distributor. That is wrong. STP on the Warsaw exchange is Stalprodukt, a converter and processor with three businesses: grain-oriented electrical steel (the specialised steel used in transformer cores), steel profiles, and the ZGH Boleslaw zinc and lead group.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Through 2021-22 this was a cash-rich, high-return group riding a steel and zinc upcycle: revenue PLN 5.90bn and net income PLN 474m in 2022. Since then the story has narrowed to survival plus one external hope. Revenue fell to PLN 3.74bn in 2025 (a 14% annual decline over three years) and the group slipped into losses (net income -PLN 51m in 2025). In 2026 the written narrative has been defensive and dependent on Brussels: the first-quarter report blamed a 47% revenue drop in electrical steel on Chinese imports and "the lack of effective market protection in the European Union", and said management was suspending in-depth restructuring until the Commission ruled. The dividend was eliminated at the 30 June 2026 meeting, and in the same meeting the controlling holders authorised buying back and cancelling up to 10% of the shares at PLN 205-250.

The arc has now taken one turn management asked for: on 18 September 2026 the Commission announced provisional safeguard measures on grain-oriented electrical steel, effective 25 September 2026 through 26 February 2027, with tariff-rate quotas (import quotas above which a higher price bar applies) and minimum-price thresholds of EUR 2,800-3,400 a tonne in quota and EUR 3,500 above quota. The narrative is therefore shifting from "waiting for protection" to "can protection be converted into profit, and will it be made definitive".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / narrative | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Electrical-steel collapse is import-driven, not self-inflicted | Q1 2026 division revenue -47% y/y, volume -35%, price -20% (Q1 report, 20 May 2026); group gross margin 4.2% in Q1 2026 | Consistent: a price-and-volume shock, not a cost blow-out |
| The group is turning the corner | Group EBIT: -PLN 21.3m (Q3 2025), -21.4m (Q4 2025), -27.5m (Q1 2026), +3.2m (Q2 2026). Q2 net loss only -PLN 1.3m | Partly true. Q2 is the best quarter in a year, but a 0.3% operating margin on PLN 1.02bn of revenue, and the near-breakeven net line rests on PLN 6.9m of interest earned on cash |
| The balance sheet is the safety net | Net cash PLN 617m at 30 June 2026 (cash and short-term investments PLN 758m, total debt PLN 141m, almost all leases) = about PLN 121 a share, roughly half today's market value | True, but draining: trailing free cash flow -PLN 202m; group cash fell about PLN 383m between end-2024 and mid-2026 |
| Capital spending is necessary investment | Trailing capital spending PLN 278m against depreciation PLN 183m (about 1.5 times) while loss-making | Spending ahead of proven returns; this is the main cash leak |
| Returns are low but positive | Return on invested capital fell from about 11% (2022) to below zero (2025 and trailing to June 2026), per filed accounts | The scan's "4.4%" figure is a stale misread; returns are negative |
| Shares are cheap; management will buy | Buyback authorised 30 June 2026 (PLN 135m, PLN 205-250, five-year window). The previous 2024 authorisation drew only a few thousand shares | Credible signal of the controllers' value view, weak record of execution; no board execution verified since |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable, defensive. The 2026 written commentary is cautious and externally focused (imports, Brussels, energy costs) with no numerical guidance. The one assertive act is capital-allocation: the buyback authorisation, which contradicts the gloomy operating tone and suggests the controlling family sees value below about PLN 250. The provisional safeguard gives management a tailwind it can point to, but there is no new management statement on file since it arrived.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium-low, largely because there is no guidance to test. The one dated forward claim - that a Commission decision would come within nine months of 27 March 2026 - has been honoured in part, early: provisional measures arrived within six months. The previous buyback authorisation (June 2024) was barely used, which tempers how much weight the new one deserves. Reliability: Medium on stated facts, Low on capital-return follow-through.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
No sell-side coverage of note is visible, and no call exists for analysts to push on. The questions an analyst would press and management has not answered in writing: (1) what the deferred restructuring of electrical steel looks like and costs if protection is not made definitive; (2) why capital spending runs above depreciation while the group loses money; (3) how the zinc business copes with processing fees that collapsed from USD 100-120 a tonne in September 2025 to about USD 20 by March 2026, with 2027 largely unpriced; (4) whether the zinc unit's profit survives without Polish state electricity compensation (PLN 26.5m in Q1 2026 alone).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: negative return on invested capital for two years running and still falling on a trailing basis (filed accounts, 2025 and TTM June 2026).
- Red: trailing free cash flow -PLN 202m and a PLN 383m cash decline in 18 months (to 30 June 2026).
- Red: zinc margin dependence on electricity subsidies and on concentrate processing fees that have collapsed (Q1 2026 report).
- Red: very thin trading; free float about a third of shares, a few hundred to a few thousand shares a day.
- Green: provisional EU safeguard on grain-oriented electrical steel in force from 25 September 2026 to 26 February 2027 with EUR 2,800-3,500 a tonne price thresholds (SteelOrbis, 21 September 2026). Stalprodukt is one of only two EU producers.
- Green: Q2 2026 operating result turned positive (+PLN 3.2m from -PLN 27.5m in Q1).
- Green: net cash of about PLN 121 a share and no bank debt; buyback authorised at PLN 205-250.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The controllers chose to stop the dividend and simultaneously authorise a buyback, a signal that they prefer to shrink the share count at sub-book prices rather than pay out cash - an implicit statement that they view PLN 205-250 as cheap. ArcelorMittal Sourcing's roughly 20% stake ties the group to its main supplier of hot-rolled input, which means the EU steel trade protection that lifted the flat-steel producers also raises Stalprodukt's own input costs; only the new electrical-steel measure protects what Stalprodukt sells. The safeguard quotas are set at the average of the previous three years' imports, so they cap a further surge but do not shut imports out; the price thresholds, not the quotas, are what should do the work.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: stable at a low level - one quarter of near-breakeven after a year of losses, with a regulatory tailwind newly in place but not yet visible in the numbers (the measure took effect five days before the third quarter ended). The single most important thing to weigh: the value case rests on a cash pile that is being spent at roughly PLN 40 a share a year; the provisional safeguard buys time and pricing, but unless the electrical-steel division turns cash-positive under protection and the measure is made definitive by 26 February 2027, the discount to book is earned, not a mispricing.

Moat: regulatory-licence and scale-cost (one of two EU producers of a strategic steel), now backed by provisional protection - but the returns evidence shows a moat that has failed to defend pricing (negative return on capital, falling for four years). That is an eroding moat, not a wide one. Secular threat: material, not terminal - structural Chinese overcapacity in electrical steel is a lasting pressure that only trade policy holds back, while grid and transformer demand is a genuine long-run support. The cheapness is part fear-print (net cash plus a protected niche) and part earned (a shrinking, subsidised zinc margin and a cash drain).

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

# EEFT - Euronet Worldwide - Forensic Dossier (Interrogator, 2026-11-02)

Live price used: $66.16 (NASDAQ: EEFT, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-02; +4.8% on the day; 52-wk range 57.48-83.97). Market cap ~$2.47bn -> ~37.4m shares.

## 1. What changed since the last committee read (2026-10-12)
- 2026-10-27 Q3 2026 results: revenue ~$1.2bn, adj. EPS $3.55 (-2% y/y; Zacks consensus $3.63 - a miss), adj. EBITDA $226.1m.
- Full-year 2026 guidance cut: revenue ~$4.375bn, adj. EBITDA ~$725m, adj. EPS growth ~10% (low end of the 10-15% band given in Feb-2026 / the May Investor Day framework). CFO: 2027 "on the lower end" of 10-15%.
- Stock fell to ~$59 on 2026-10-28 (below the committee's $62.50 wait level) on company news (the guidance cut), then recovered to $66.16 by 2026-11-02.
- Street PTs reset 2026-10-28: 84 / 80 / 63 (vs 94 in July).

## 2. Segment truth (Q3 2026, constant currency)
- Payments infrastructure (ex-EFT): revenue +9% (merchant acquiring + CoreCard), adj. OI flat, adj. EBITDA +4% (cost inflation; +$4.7m CoreCard PPA amortization).
- epay: revenue +5%, OI +5%, adj. EBITDA +6%. Q4 headwind: Steam gift-card removal, backfill uncertain.
- Cross-border (Ria/Xe/Dandelion): revenue -4%, OI -35%, adj. EBITDA -32% (US immigration policy, FX, ~$6m extra digital advertising). Digital transactions +34%; ~3/4 of digital customers new to the franchise. Sequential cc revenue decline improved (-5% Q2 -> -4% Q3); management calls US outbound "stabilizing to subtle improvement".
- Digital accelerators +30% in Q3, +33% YTD, ~26% of revenue.

## 3. Earnings quality
- Adjusted earnings (2025: $408m) run well above GAAP NI ($310m) - gap = amortization, share comp, non-cash items. TTM GAAP diluted EPS $6.15 vs adjusted run-rate ~ $10.5.
- FCF is the weak spot: TTM FCF $95m (scan), FCF -33% y/y, 3-yr FCF CAGR -14%. Euronet's reported FCF swings with ATM cash and settlement working capital, so single-period FCF understates owner earnings, but the persistent gap between adjusted EPS and cash conversion is the main forensic discount. Q3 operating cash flow $139m.
- Piotroski 5/9, Altman-Z 1.5 (depressed by settlement liabilities typical of payments companies - not a true distress signal, but not a clean bill either).

## 4. Balance sheet
- 2026-09-30: unrestricted cash ~$955m-1.0bn, total debt $2.18bn (incl. $1bn 0.625% 2030 convert), capitalized leases $142m. Net debt $1.36bn incl. leases ($1.22bn ex-leases). $913m of cash sits inside the ATM network (operational, not counted as cash here). Investment-grade target maintained.

## 5. Capital allocation
- Buybacks ~85% of earnings over 4 years; Q3 2026 $50m (~690k shares at ~$72). Buying back at higher prices than today; the stock now ~6x adj. EPS makes continuing buybacks accretive.
- M&A: CoreCard (closed Oct-2025), Kyodai, Credia Bank merchant acquiring. Diebold Nixdorf LOI (2026-10-26), Fireblocks stablecoin card issuing (2026-10-19), OLON launch (2026-10-21) - optionality, no near-term P&L.

## 6. Insider / positioning
- Open-market insider: 2 buys (3,781 sh) vs 10 sells (182,255 sh) - no insider conviction signal.
- Smart-money 34/100; PT velocity -15% vs year-ago. Positioning is washed but not capitulated.

## 7. Management credibility
- Guidance has now been missed/cut for 2026 after Feb and May reaffirmation; prior assertion (Oct-2025) of "double-digit EPS growth in 2026" is technically still met (~10%) but only at the bottom. Management consistently frames headwinds as "transitory"; cross-border has been worse than guided for 4 quarters. Credibility on near-term numbers: middling. Long-term strategic execution (EFT -> payments infrastructure, digital remittance) is visible in the numbers.

## 8. Key risks
- Cross-border structural decline (agent channel) from immigration policy and digital/stablecoin disintermediation.
- European travel/discretionary spend (ATM withdrawals), FX translation.
- Cost inflation in payments infrastructure (margins flat on +9% revenue).
- Cash conversion vs adjusted EPS.

picks.consensus_delta: The market prices Solvay as a leveraged, structurally challenged European commodity-chemicals stock whose dividend is about to be cut - and on the dividend the market is probably right: 2026 free cash flow of EUR 120-150 million cannot fund a roughly EUR 257 million payout at 2.4x leverage. Where we disagree is on terminal decline: the end markets (glass, food, feed, chips, tyres, magnets) are not shrinking, Green River is a low-cost soda-ash source, and about EUR 45 million of the 2026 EBITDA loss so far is a plant shutdown with a contractual recovery mechanism. We do not think the street is badly wrong at EUR 24.40, which sits close to our EUR 26.0 base value; the disagreement only pays if a dividend cut forces yield holders out at a materially lower price.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Solvay (SOLB.BR) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-10. Live price EUR 24.40 (Euronext Brussels, FMP quote). Sources: five earnings calls (2025-03-06, 2025-07-30, 2025-11-06, 2026-02-24, 2026-07-29), the screener's financial block, Solvay's preliminary Q3 release and guidance update of 2026-10-19 and its full Q3 release of 2026-11-04.*

**Bottom line:** Solvay is a real, essential-chemicals business (soda ash and bicarbonate, hydrogen peroxide, tyre silica, rare earths and fluorine specialties, and the Brazilian phenol/solvents unit Coatis) being run with genuine cost discipline, but its earnings have fallen every year since the 2023 Syensqo spin-off and management's cash promises have now slipped. The 2026-10-19 guidance cut took full-year underlying EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) to EUR 720-740 million (from a range implying roughly EUR 765-845 million) and free cash flow to EUR 120-150 million (from "at least EUR 200 million"), against a dividend that costs about EUR 257 million a year. The single most important fact for sizing: the dividend is no longer covered by cash, and the next scheduled decision on it is the full-year results in late February 2027.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **March 2025 (FY2024 call): "resilience" and the post-split story.** Philippe Kehren framed 2024 as "a pivotal chapter" in which "the spinoff has unlocked significant value", raised the cost-savings target from EUR 300 million to EUR 350 million by 2028, and positioned Solvay's products as "not commodities, but they are not specialties neither". Soda ash was described as at "the low end of the cycle".
- **July 2025 (H1 2025): first guidance cut, Coatis and seaborne soda ash.** The tone shifted to tariffs, a "progressive reduction of demand" and Chinese competition. Coatis was hit by Asian imports redirected to Brazil; seaborne soda ash prices fell. Rare earths entered the story as a strategic option (La Rochelle, permanent magnets) but explicitly conditioned on customer or state price floors.
- **November 2025 (Q3 2025): self-help and asset monetisation.** A EUR 40 million EBITDA gain from selling CO2 emission rights was presented as "definitely not a one-off" but "a business decision"; the Chief Operations Officer was put on the call to evidence the savings programme; Torrelavega (Spain) soda-ash capacity was cut by a third. China's "anti-involution" policy was introduced as the hoped-for fix for soda ash ("if and when").
- **February 2026 (FY2025): "we deliver" plus defend the footprint.** EBITDA EUR 881 million (-13%), free cash flow EUR 350 million. The narrative widened to European climate policy (emissions-trading reform, free allowances) and a promise of "a stable growing dividend and an investment-grade rating".
- **July 2026 (H1 2026): exogenous shock.** The Middle East conflict shut the Jubail (Saudi Arabia) peroxide plant; EBITDA fell 20% in Q2. Bicarbonate and electronic-grade peroxide were at "record sales levels"; restart was guided to "the second part of Q3". An analyst stated plainly that "the dividend won't be covered in '26".
- **After the last call (dated facts):** Jubail did not restart; on 2026-10-19 guidance was cut; on 2026-11-04 Q3 EBITDA printed EUR 173 million (-26.6% organically, 16.8% margin), leverage reached 2.4x, the interim dividend was held at EUR 0.97, and talks continued to contribute the rare-earths business (about EUR 80 million of EBITDA) to a joint venture with OneIM in which Solvay keeps a significant minority.

The arc runs from "we are resilient and the cycle is at the bottom" to "we are controlling what we can while the cycle and geopolitics keep moving against us".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Soda ash is at "the low end of the cycle" (Mar 2025) | Seaborne prices fell further in every subsequent quarter through Q3 2026; Soda Ash & Derivatives sales -6.8% in Q3 2026 | Wrong on timing; the trough kept deepening |
| "We are cash flow covering the dividend... Yes, always" (CFO, Mar 2025) | FCF EUR 361m (2024), EUR 350m (2025) covered the ~EUR 257m dividend; 2026 guide EUR 120-150m does not | Held for two years, broken for 2026 |
| Cost savings EUR 350m by 2028, EUR 300m by end-2026 | EUR 283m delivered by Q3 2026 | Delivered — the most credible claim on record |
| Healthy ~21% EBITDA margin through the trough | ~21% in 2025; 18.1% Q2 2026; 16.8% Q3 2026 | Eroding, partly temporary (Jubail, ~EUR 45m in Q2+Q3) |
| Balance sheet "healthy", leverage back to ~2x by year-end (Jul 2026) | Underlying net debt EUR 1.79bn, leverage 2.4x at Sept 2026; S&P BBB- (one notch above junk) | Missed so far; year-end test pending |
| Group EPS trajectory | EPS 19.85 (2023, spin-distorted) -> 2.10 (2024) -> 0.28 (2025); TTM 0.32 | Reported earnings near zero; cash flow is the better gauge |

Revenue: EUR 4.75bn (2025) per the screener; underlying EUR 4.3bn, -6% organically. The 3-year revenue decline (-33%) is mostly the Syensqo spin restatement, not organic collapse. Free cash flow: TTM EUR 316m (screener, through 2026-09-30), but 9M-2026 FCF to shareholders was only EUR 70m, so the trailing figure overstates the run-rate.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** March 2025 was offensive ("our ambition is clear... be the best"). July 2025 turned defensive ("clearly, this is not what we expected"). November 2025 leaned on self-help and one-time levers (CO2 sales, footprint cuts). February 2026 added a policy-lobbying layer ("we need the support of the authorities"). July 2026 was frank about unpredictability ("volatility is the name of the game") and declined to discuss 2027 ("very early to say anything about '27"). Guidance specificity has stayed decent, but the confidence behind it has fallen each year.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- 2025 EBITDA guidance: cut in July 2025, then delivered inside the revised range (EUR 881m).
- 2025 FCF: delivered (EUR 350m, above the ~EUR 300m guide).
- 2026 EBITDA: given in February 2026 as a 4-13% decline, confirmed on 2026-07-29 (with Jubail restart assumed in late Q3), cut on 2026-10-19 to EUR 720-740m (-16% to -18%).
- 2026 FCF: "at least EUR 200m" -> EUR 120-150m.

Two consecutive years of mid-year guidance cuts; cost targets met; cash conversion good until 2026. The earnings-beat rate of 4 of 7 quarters (57%) matches a management that is honest about what it controls but has repeatedly underestimated the external hits. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Dividend cover** (Barclays, Mar 2025; Berenberg, Jul 2026): answered with confidence in 2025, sidestepped in 2026 ("an important piece of the equation"). This is the question that turned into bad news.
- **Why invest so little if returns are high / why not monetise non-core units** (Barclays Mar 2025; JPMorgan Nov 2025 on fluorine at 12x EBITDA): "nothing is excluded" — and the rare-earths JV talks with OneIM (disclosed by 2026-11-04) suggest portfolio action is now real.
- **China soda-ash rationalisation**: asked every call; the answer since February 2026 has been "not yet".
- **2027 earnings path**: not answered.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: dividend uncovered in 2026 (FCF guide EUR 120-150m vs ~EUR 257m) after the "yes, always" promise of March 2025.
- Red: leverage 2.4x at Sept 2026 with a BBB- rating — little headroom to keep paying the dividend from debt.
- Red: two mid-year EBITDA guidance cuts in two years (Jul 2025, Oct 2026).
- Red: seaborne soda ash still falling (Q3 2026) with no Chinese capacity closures yet.
- Red: Jubail restart missed its "second part of Q3" guide; no new date.
- Green: EUR 283m of structural savings delivered (Q3 2026), ahead of plan.
- Green: bicarbonate and electronic-grade peroxide at record sales (Q2 2026); silica +9.2% and Coatis +19.1% sales in Q3 2026.
- Green: Jubail joint-venture contract has mechanisms to recover lost profitability (2026-10-19 release) — not in guidance.
- Green: rare-earths JV with OneIM would crystallise value for a ~EUR 80m-EBITDA unit while keeping exposure.
- Green: EU emissions-trading draft reform (Jul 2026) keeps free allowances — reduces the long-run carbon-cost threat to European plants.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The language moved from "resilience" (2025) to "transformation expenses" and "what we control" (2026) — a defensive register.
- One-time cash levers (CO2-rights sales, working-capital squeezes to "best-in-class" ~10% of sales) have been carrying free cash flow; they are finite.
- Portfolio language softened from "we will concentrate on" to "nothing is excluded", and now a partial disposal (rare earths) is in negotiation — a sign the board is willing to sell assets to protect the balance sheet and possibly the dividend.
- Holding the interim dividend at EUR 0.97 on 2026-11-04 while guiding FCF far below the payout signals the board wants to defer any cut to the February 2027 final-dividend decision.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: DETERIORATING.** The operational discipline is real, but the cash base no longer funds the dividend and leverage is rising toward the edge of investment grade. The single most important thing to weigh: the February 2027 final-dividend decision. A cut is the likeliest route for forced selling by yield-focused holders — which is also the most likely route to a genuinely cheap entry price.

**Moat:** a narrow, scale-and-cost moat — Green River (US) natural trona soda ash is among the world's lowest-cost sources, the hydrogen-peroxide "mega plant" technology is licensable, and ~80% of sales are local-for-local, which protects against freight and tariffs. But returns are falling (ROIC 6.9% today versus "almost 18%" cited by an analyst in March 2025) and margins have slid from ~21% to 16.8%, partly cyclical (Chinese overcapacity, Jubail) and partly structural (European synthetic soda ash under energy and carbon-cost pressure, hence the Torrelavega cut). The moat is real but eroding at the European edge.

**Secular threat:** manageable. The end markets (glass, food and feed, semiconductors, tyres, magnets) are not shrinking; the structural risk is European energy and carbon costs on the older synthetic soda-ash plants (an energy-transition cost burden), which management is addressing by shrinking and converting capacity. The cheapness looks more like a cyclical fear-print on a leveraged balance sheet than a structurally shrinking base — but it is not a clean franchise until cash covers the dividend again.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: The bull case is that Jungheinrich, the number-two European maker of forklifts and warehouse equipment, is being priced as if a cyclical trough were permanent. The nine-month statement of 10 November 2026 shows the bottom forming rather than deepening: orders rose 6.0% to 4,323 million euros, the reported operating margin recovered to 5.9% from 4.0% a year earlier as one-off costs fell from 162.9 million to 36.5 million, and management confirmed its 2026 forecast of 340-400 million euros of operating profit for the second time instead of cutting again. Growth is coming from the right place: automation orders rose about 20% to 878 million euros, a structurally growing business. Gross margin has held near 32% for years and rose through the 2021-22 inflation (29.1% to 30.9%), which says the product still carries pricing power. The balance sheet is roughly neutral (cash of 723 million against debt of 701 million at 30 June 2026), so there is no financing threat. The new 2030 target of an 8-9% margin, though lower than before, is what a recovery from today's 6-7% looks like, and Bernstein's Philippe Lorrain called the reset a de-risking step that could bring in long-term holders (10 November 2026). At 23.24 euros the shares trade near book value and at roughly 9-10 times a normalised 2.40-2.60 euros of earnings; if the margin returns to around 8% on about 5.9 billion euros of revenue, sum-of-the-parts value is near 35 euros. Conditions: the fourth quarter delivers the forecast and turns cash positive, European demand stops falling, and the regulator's review closes without a finding.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the screen is cheap for reasons that do not survive inspection, and that 10 November 2026 made two of them worse. First, cash: nine-month free cash flow was minus 106 million euros against plus 151 million a year earlier, so the 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow multiple rests on 2025 cash the business is not repeating; the full-year guide of above 50 million now needs roughly 156 million or more in the fourth quarter alone. Second, ambition: management cut its 2030 margin target to 8-9% from about 10%, which confirms the margin erosion visible in the numbers (adjusted 6.8% for nine months against 8.1% a year earlier; the third quarter on reported figures derives to about 5.4%, about 76 million on about 1.40 billion, using FMP's half-year operating profit of 165.8 million; one press report gives about 97 million for the quarter, which we cannot reconcile and may be adjusted). Third-quarter orders grew only 2.6%, slightly below expectations, and growth is concentrated in the smaller, lumpier automation business while the core truck business saw revenue fall 1.8% under Chinese price competition and high rates. Return on invested capital of about 5.8% is below the cost of capital. The effective tax rate was about 45% in the first half (59.0 million on 132.2 million of pre-tax profit). The German financial regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts, opened 21 July 2026 and tied to the Russia disposal, is still open with no timetable; a finding would undercut the argument that recent charges were one-off. The March 2026 forecast lasted four months, and only two of the last five quarters beat. The listed preference shares carry no vote, so no activist or bid can force value out. What would confirm it: a fourth quarter that misses the forecast or the cash guide (full-year results, late March 2027), a regulator finding, or a dividend cut that pushes income holders out.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrow. The street is pricing a long trough in European forklifts (Bank of America's 8 October 2026 underperform call, target 21 euros) and the shares sit about a third below where they started 2026. We think the market is roughly right on timing but slightly too pessimistic on the mid-cycle margin: the confirmed 2026 forecast, the 6.8% adjusted nine-month margin and management's own 8-9% 2030 target all point to a mid-cycle near or above 7%, which supports about 26 euros of value. But the gap is not large at 23.24 euros, and the market has a point on cash: a 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow screen is built on 2025, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow is minus 106 million euros. Nothing here is a terminal-decline pricing error large enough to buy today.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) runs to the full-year results in late March 2027. Three things can hurt before value converges: (1) the fourth quarter must deliver roughly 98-158 million euros of operating profit and about 156 million or more of free cash flow to meet the guide - a miss on cash would expose the low price-to-cash-flow screen as an artifact; (2) the regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts can publish a finding at any time with no notice; (3) European capital-spending demand under positive real rates and Chinese price competition in standard trucks can keep the core truck business shrinking (nine-month revenue there down 1.8%). There is no debt wall: cash of 723 million roughly matches debt of 701 million at 30 June 2026.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is modest. The preference shares carry no vote, so the holder base is income and value funds plus index holders (the shares are in the SDAX). A dividend cut in spring 2027 after a year of reported earnings well below 2024 could push income holders out, and the sector-wide selling seen in October 2026 (Bank of America's call covering KION too) is the most likely route to our 19.00 euro level. We see no index deletion, lock-up or spin-off dumping in prospect.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 19.00 euros, which a renewed sector-wide sell-off in European forklift makers could deliver.

The thesis holds. Today's nine-month statement (10 November 2026) confirmed the 2026 forecast instead of cutting it again, orders are up 6% and one-off costs have fallen sharply, so this still looks like a decent business in a cyclical trough rather than a broken one. But the statement did not deliver what we said would make us buy earlier: the adjusted margin was 6.8%, not above 7%, free cash flow was minus 106 million euros for nine months against plus 151 million a year earlier, and management lowered its 2030 margin goal to 8-9% from about 10%.

We trim fair value to 26.08 euros from 26.57: the core business at a mid-cycle 7.25% margin and eight times operating profit, the leasing arm near its estimated equity, less about 270 million euros of net debt once this year's cash outflow is counted. At 23.24 euros (Xetra, 10 November 2026) the discount is only about a tenth, short of the one-fifth this book requires, and the downside to our 16.53 euro adverse case is larger than the upside. At 19.00 euros the discount to fair value is well over a third and the remaining downside small, which is the asymmetry we want.

Conviction stays at a moderate 3, inherited from our last answer because no dated fact cleared an upgrade or broke the thesis: a narrow-moat number-two franchise whose margins and returns are eroding, with an open regulator review, a 45% tax rate and a guidance record that needed a cut in July. The value case alone also rates 3, capped by the eroding moat. We would move before 19.00 euros only on a dated fact: a fourth quarter that meets the forecast and the cash guide (late March 2027), or a clean close of the regulator's review.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard dated event that forces a re-rating. The candidates are routine: full-year 2026 results in late March 2027 (proof of fourth-quarter cash and the 2026 forecast met), and the close of the regulator's review (no date). The founding families control the vote, so no activist, tender or buyback campaign can be forced. The re-rating, if it comes, is a slow margin and cash recovery.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Jungheinrich AG (preference shares, Xetra JUN3.DE) - deep dive on management and the setup

As of 10 November 2026. No earnings-call transcript was available from FMP for this listing, and none could be found on the web for the nine-month statement published today. This dossier therefore reasons from the company's dated releases (first quarter, 23 July 2026 forecast cut, half-year report of 11 August 2026, nine-month statement of 10 November 2026, as reported in the press), the FMP quarterly statements and our screener figures. No management quotes are given because none could be sourced; where we derive a figure, we say so.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from growth ambition to damage control and back to a cautious "trough, then recovery" message.

- Early 2026: the company opened the year with a forecast it had to cut four months later. The first quarter was weak: operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and taxes) fell to 56.5 million euros from 104.5 million a year earlier, hit by a strike at the Lueneburg plant and price competition.
- 23 July 2026: an ad-hoc notice (a mandatory market announcement) revised the full-year forecast for the Industrial Trucks and Services segment and the group to EBIT of 340 to 400 million euros (a 6.2% to 7.0% margin, including about 40 million euros of one-off costs).
- 11 August 2026: the half-year report showed orders up about 8%, revenue flat at 2,669 million euros, and a group margin near 6.2%.
- 10 November 2026: the nine-month statement held the 2026 forecast, showed orders up 6.0% to 4,323 million euros, revenue up 1.5% to 4,068 million euros, and reported EBIT of 241.8 million euros (5.9% margin, against 4.0% a year earlier when one-offs were far larger). Adjusted for 36.5 million euros of one-offs, EBIT was 278.3 million euros, a 6.8% margin, down from 8.1% a year earlier. At the same time the company reset its long-term plan: the 2030 targets are now 7 to 8 billion euros of revenue and an 8% to 9% EBIT margin, down from roughly 10 billion euros and about 10% per a German trade report.

The quiet change is the long-term ambition. A 10% margin business has become an 8-9% margin business by the end of the decade, which matters more for the upside than for the downside.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / implied claim | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 forecast (EBIT 340-400m) is achievable | Nine-month reported EBIT 241.8m; Q4 must deliver about 98-158m. Q4 2025 delivered 131.6m reported (FMP). | Plausible at the low-to-mid end. |
| Margins recover from the trough | Adjusted nine-month margin 6.8% vs 8.1% a year earlier. Reported third quarter derived at about 76m on about 1.40bn (about 5.4%), using FMP's 165.8m half-year EBIT; one press report gives about 97m for the quarter, which may be an adjusted figure - we could not reconcile the two. | No clear recovery yet; flat at best. |
| Orders signal demand turning | Orders +6.0% for nine months, but the third quarter alone only +2.6% to just under 1.4bn, slightly below expectations. Automation orders +19.9% to 878m; core trucks +3.5%. | Real but slowing; growth comes from the smaller automation arm. |
| Cash generation (free cash flow above 50m for the year) | Nine-month free cash flow minus 106m euros vs plus 151m a year earlier. Q4 must produce roughly 156m+ to hit the guide. | The weakest link. The screener's 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow rests on 2025 cash that 2026 is not repeating. |
| Gross margin stability | Gross margin about 32.6% in the first half (870m on 2,669m); screen shows 32.2% stable; held through the 2021-22 inflation (29.1% to 30.9%). | Corroborated - pricing power on the product is intact. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining through July, stabilising since. The 23 July cut was defensive; the November release is cautious-steady (forecast held, long-term targets lowered to something believable). Bernstein's Philippe Lorrain called the lower targets a risk-reduction step that could attract long-term investors (as reported 10 November 2026). We rate the trajectory as still deteriorating on substance (lower long-term margins, negative cash flow) even as the tone has steadied.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-low. The March 2026 forecast lasted four months. The screener shows beats in only 2 of the last 5 quarters and earnings per share down 64% in 2025. The revised July forecast has now been confirmed once (10 November). The 2030 reset is a second admission that earlier ambition was too high. Reliability: Low-to-Medium, improving only if Q4 lands inside the range and cash turns positive.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without a transcript we can only infer the questions: (a) why free cash flow swung to minus 106m and whether the full-year cash guide is still realistic; (b) how much of the margin gap is Chinese price competition (structural) versus volume (cyclical); (c) the German financial regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts tied to the Russia disposal, opened 21 July 2026, for which we found no update; (d) the 45%-plus effective tax rate in the first half (59.0m of tax on 132.2m of pre-tax profit, FMP).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: nine-month free cash flow minus 106m (10 Nov 2026) against a full-year guide above 50m.
- Red: 2030 margin target cut to 8-9% from about 10% (10 Nov 2026).
- Red: adjusted margin 6.8% vs 8.1% a year earlier; third-quarter orders slightly below expectations.
- Red: regulator review of the June 2025 accounts still open (since 21 July 2026, no result found).
- Red: effective tax rate near 45% in the first half of 2026.
- Green: 2026 forecast confirmed on 10 November 2026, no second cut.
- Green: orders up 6% for nine months; automation orders up about 20%.
- Green: one-off costs fell to 36.5m from 162.9m a year earlier; reported margin up to 5.9% from 4.0%.
- Green: gross margin steady near 32%; balance sheet roughly neutral (cash 723m vs debt 701m at 30 June 2026 per FMP).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The target reset is the main signal: management is now anchoring the market to a lower, more achievable margin path, which removes a source of future disappointment but also caps the long-term upside the bull case used to lean on. Growth is migrating to automation, a more competitive and project-lumpy business. The listed preference shares carry no vote; control sits with the founding families, so no activist or bid can force value out.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT

Trajectory: DETERIORATING on substance (lower long-term margins, cash outflow this year), with a stabilising tone. The single most important thing for the director: whether the fourth quarter turns cash positive enough to meet the above-50m free-cash-flow guide - that decides whether the low price-to-cash-flow screen is real or a 2025 artifact.

Moat: a narrow but real moat from scale, a dense direct sales-and-service network and a large leasing and rental fleet that ties customers in (switching costs on service). Width is narrowing: return on invested capital about 5.8% is below the cost of capital, the margin has slid from about 8% to 6-7%, and management has cut its own end-of-decade margin target. That is an eroding moat trend, though from a cyclical trough rather than a collapse. Secular threat: Chinese low-price competition in standard trucks is a material but manageable pressure, not a terminal one - warehouse automation is a growth adjacency the company is winning in. The cheapness is mostly a cyclical fear print, with a real structural element on margins.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Harmony is a self-funding narcolepsy franchise priced like a melting ice cube even though the ice has a contractual floor. Average patients reached about 9,350 in Q3-2026, with 400 net adds in five of the last six quarters, against only about 20% brand penetration of roughly 80,000 diagnosed patients. picks.bear_thesis: This is a single-asset company with a dated cliff and one open door to an earlier one. picks.consensus_delta: The street treats Harmony as a 2030 cliff stock with litigation risk and pays about 5.5x free cash flow for it. # DMLP — Dorchester Minerals, L.P. — forensic dossier (2026-11-09)

Sources: FMP quote (DMLP $27.51, NASDAQ, USD, 2026-11-09), FMP quarterly income / balance / cash-flow statements through the Q3-2026 10-Q (filed 2026-11-05), FMP press releases and news (2026-09 to 2026-11), FMP commodity quotes (WTI $86.38, Henry Hub $3.22 on 2026-11-09). Dorchester does not hold earnings calls, so there is no transcript; management speaks through its quarterly distribution release, 10-Q/10-K and acquisition releases. No quotes are reproduced or invented below.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Dorchester is a debt-free partnership that owns perpetual oil and gas mineral and royalty interests (mainly Permian, Mid-Continent, and, since 2026, more Williston Basin acreage). It has no drilling capex: revenue comes from what operators pull out of its acreage, and nearly all cash is paid out every quarter as a variable distribution. The story management tells has not changed in years: buy minerals for newly issued units (not debt), pay everything out, keep the balance sheet clean. The 2025 annual numbers in the screener (revenue $153M, EPS $1.20, down 44%) captured the 2025 oil-price trough; 2026 has reversed that, with quarterly revenue of $58.9M (Q1), $56.1M (Q2) and $51.4M (Q3) against $32.4M and $35.4M in Q2 and Q3 of 2025, on the back of an oil spike (WTI 52-week range $55 to $119, 50-day average about $96, today $86).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Cash conversion is real: Q3-2026 operating cash flow $42.9M against net income $27.6M (depletion of $15.7M is the gap), with zero capex. Trailing four quarters of operating cash flow about $165M, or roughly $3.40 per unit on about 49M units.
- Balance sheet: $55.7M cash, no debt, $3.4M of lease liabilities (2026-09-30). Most of that cash funds the Q3 distribution of $0.882 per unit payable 2026-11-12 (about $43M), so the true surplus is small.
- Distributions follow cash: the Q2-2026 distribution was about $1.27 including a one-off settlement payment (about $0.96 underlying, per a 2026-10-17 Seeking Alpha note); Q3 is $0.88. The Q1-2026 income statement carries an unusual $25.5M cost-of-revenue line and odd working-capital swings (receivables -$26.9M in Q1, +$14.8M in Q2) — consistent with the settlement accrual moving through, not a sign of hidden trouble, but quarterly figures are lumpy.
- Unit count creeps up (47.3M mid-2025 to 48.8M weighted Q3-2026, more after the Williston deal) because acquisitions are paid in units. Per-unit, not total, cash is the number to watch.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Not measurable from calls (none held). Actions speak: an insider-buy ratio of 5.0 in the screener and CFO buying cited by a 2026-09-14 article point to steady insider confidence. Management continues to issue units for acreage, which signals they view the units as fairly priced, not cheap.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
No guidance is given. Distributions are mechanical: they reflect the prior quarter's receipts. Credibility is therefore high by construction; the risk is commodity prices, not management promises.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
No FMP analyst price-target coverage; I found no dated sell-side target and assume none. Third-party commentary (Seeking Alpha, 2026-10-17) expects near-term distributions approaching $1 per unit on oil near $100 — a view already dated by oil's fall to $86 today.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Green: no debt, no capex, near-100% payout, unit-funded acquisitions that add acreage without leverage, 2021-22 margins held (inflation-resilient label), insider buying.
Red: earnings are a direct function of oil and gas prices; the 2026 cash surge rides an oil spike that is already reversing (WTI down 5% today, about 10% below its 50-day average). Production on old acreage declines naturally; growth depends on continued unit-funded deals, which dilute. Quarterly accounting is lumpy (settlement in Q1/Q2-2026).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The screener's -67% "margin of safety" against a $9.19 fair value is an artifact of Buffett/EPV-style models applied to a depleting royalty with depletion charges far below its replacement value; the DCF at $67.6 is the opposite artifact (capitalizing peak cash). Neither is useful. The right lens is distribution yield on mid-cycle commodity prices. At $27.51 the Q3 run-rate ($3.53 annualized) is a 12.8% yield — but on $90-plus oil, not mid-cycle.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Disciplined and shareholder-aligned: pay out cash, buy acreage with units, never borrow. The value case is a fair-priced, high-quality commodity royalty, not a mispriced one. Price is about at mid-cycle fair value; the current yield flatters it because oil is elevated.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady.

# Bouvet ASA (BOUV.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup

**Debate date:** 2026-11-09 · **Price used:** NOK 49.10 (Oslo Bors listing, FMP live quote 2026-11-09) · **Market value:** about NOK 5.0B

**Source limits, stated up front.** No earnings-call transcript was bundled, FMP carries no transcript for this listing, the Quartr connector requires a subscription we do not have, and this session's web-search budget was exhausted before any search ran. Bouvet's investor page (bouvet.no/investor, fetched 2026-11-09) loaded but did not show the third-quarter 2026 report text; it does confirm that Bouvet publishes no forecasts and that "a substantial part of last year's after-tax profit" is paid out to owners. Everything below therefore reasons from FMP's reported quarterly and annual statements (through the quarter ending 2026-09-30) and the screener metrics. There are no management quotes in this dossier because we could not source any, and none are invented.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Bouvet is a Norwegian IT and digital consultancy (with a smaller Swedish arm) that sells consultant hours to public-sector bodies, energy and utility companies and large Nordic corporates. Its long-running story is simple: steady organic growth by hiring consultants, very little capital tied up, and nearly all profit handed back as dividends. The numbers carry that story through 2024: revenue rose from NOK 2.40B (2020) to NOK 3.92B (2024), about 13% a year, with operating margin held in a 12-13% band.

The story changed in 2025. Revenue was flat (NOK 3.91B, -0.2%) and earnings per share fell about 6% to NOK 3.46. The trailing twelve months (TTM) to 2026-09-30 extend that: revenue about NOK 3.88B (roughly -1% versus 2025) and diluted EPS about NOK 3.10. The narrative has moved from "growth compounder" to "mature cash machine in a soft Norwegian consulting market". Without a transcript we cannot say how management frames it.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim implied by the business model | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Organic growth | 3-year revenue growth of about 8% a year, but flat since 2024; Q3 2026 revenue NOK 865M vs NOK 870M a year earlier (-0.6%); Q2 2026 NOK 975M vs NOK 969M (+0.6%) | Growth has stalled for about two years |
| Stable margins | Operating margin (operating profit / revenue): 13.0% (2022), 12.1% (2023), 12.5% (2024), 12.1% (2025), about 11.2% TTM. Q3 2026 operating profit NOK 80M vs NOK 92M a year earlier (-12%); margin 9.3% vs 10.5% | Slipping, not collapsing |
| Asset-light, cash-generative | TTM free cash flow NOK 328M (about NOK 3.20/share), roughly equal to net income. Lease payments of about NOK 23M a quarter sit in financing, so lease-adjusted free cash flow is closer to NOK 240M | Real, but lease-adjusted cash is about 25% lower than the headline |
| High returns | Return on equity about 74%, return on invested capital about 42% (scan) | Exceptional, a product of paying out nearly everything and needing little capital |
| Shareholder returns | Dividends NOK 307M paid in Q2 2026 and NOK 72M in Q4 2025; NOK 50M of buybacks in Q1 2026 | Payout at or above earnings |
| Balance sheet | 2026-09-30: cash NOK 211M, borrowings NOK 67M, capitalised leases NOK 238M. Net debt including leases NOK 94M; net cash excluding leases about NOK 144M | Clean; Altman-Z 6.6 |

Data note: FMP's Q4 2025 cash-flow line shows net income of NOK 102M while the income statement shows NOK 72M. This looks like a vendor mapping mismatch; it does not change the annual picture.

The reported "gross margin" (19.5%, falling from 27.7% in 2022) is mostly a classification artefact of how FMP maps a consultancy's personnel costs. The operating margin is the honest measure and it is down about 1 point, not 8.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Not assessable from transcripts (none available). From the numbers alone the trajectory reads as Stable-to-Declining: four straight quarters of roughly flat revenue and a lower operating profit in two of the last three year-on-year comparisons.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Bouvet gives no financial guidance (confirmed on its investor page), so there is no promise-versus-delivery record to grade. The scan shows earnings beat consensus in only 2 of the last 7 quarters (29%), which says analysts have repeatedly been too optimistic about the recovery. Reliability of the business itself: High. Reliability of a near-term recovery call: Low.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without call transcripts we cannot name the questions management deflected. The obvious pressure points the numbers raise: (a) when does consultant utilisation and billing-rate pressure in Norway end; (b) is generative AI shrinking billable hours for routine development work; (c) can the company keep paying out more than it earns. No dated analyst price targets could be sourced (FMP has none for this listing and web search was unavailable), so we do not cite any.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Q3 2026 operating profit down about 12% year on year on flat revenue (quarter ending 2026-09-30).
- Red: TTM diluted EPS about NOK 3.10 vs NOK 3.69 in 2024, about 16% below the 2024 peak.
- Red: earnings beat rate of 29% over 7 quarters.
- Red: payout runs at or above earnings while earnings shrink; the dividend could be trimmed if the slide continues.
- Green: free cash flow still roughly equals net income; no debt problem; Altman-Z 6.6, Piotroski 7/9.
- Green: margins held through the 2021-22 inflation (operating margin up about 1.7 points), so wage inflation has historically been passed on.
- Green: Q3 2026 operating cash flow of NOK 83M versus NOK 12M a year earlier, suggesting better working-capital collection.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

Share count is steady at about 102-103M, so the buyback (NOK 50M in Q1 2026) mostly offsets employee share programmes. Interest income is falling (NOK 3M in Q3 2026 versus NOK 5M a year earlier) because the cash pile was paid out. Nothing in the statements suggests acquisitions or a change in capital-allocation policy.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: Stable. This is a well-run, debt-free consultancy whose earnings have rolled over by about 16% from the 2024 peak in a soft Norwegian market. The single thing the director must weigh is whether the margin slide is cyclical (utilisation and billing-rate pressure that reverses when public and energy IT budgets reopen) or the first sign of generative AI permanently compressing the hours clients buy.

Moat: narrow but real. The moat type is switching costs and embedded relationships with long-tenured public-sector and energy clients, plus local scale in Norway. Returns on capital remain very high (about 42% ROIC) and the operating margin has slipped only about 1 point, which is stable rather than eroding. The secular threat is material but not terminal: AI-assisted development may reduce hours per project, but Bouvet's work is weighted toward integration, advisory and regulated public-sector systems where the client still buys accountable people. The cheapness looks more like a cyclical earnings dip than a structurally shrinking base, but the discount is modest.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

# TF1 Group (TFI.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup
*Transcripts reviewed: 9M-2025 (2025-10-30), FY-2025 (2026-02-12), H1-2026 (2026-07-30), 9M-2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: EUR 6.09 (Euronext Paris, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
A year ago (2025-10-30) the story was "resilience": revenue stable, operating margin held near 11%, market-share gains in a falling linear advertising market, and TF1+ (the free streaming platform) growing advertising revenue about 41%. By the full-year call (2026-02-12) the frame was "the second phase of the strategic plan" - micro-payments, the Netflix distribution deal, and French-speaking international expansion - while advertising revenue was already down 4% for 2025. By H1-2026 (2026-07-30) the story had turned defensive: the margin target was cut to "mid- to high single-digit", and net profit roughly halved. The 9M-2026 call (2026-10-29) is a "we are on the road map" call: margin from activities (current operating profit before one-offs, divided by revenue) of 7.6% versus 10.9% a year earlier, advertising revenue down 9%, and the growth vocabulary now leans almost entirely on the Netflix partnership, the small-business ad platform and micro-payments.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong double-digit digital growth" | TF1+ ad revenue +19% over 9M-2026 (EUR 160M), +20.5% in Q3; total digital EUR 198M (+17%) | Delivered, but growth has halved from ~40% in 2025 |
| Digital offsets linear decline | Group advertising revenue EUR 1.0B, down 9% (about EUR 100M lost) versus roughly EUR 30M digital gain | Not true - the gap widened |
| Cost discipline protects margin | Programming costs down EUR 44M; margin still 7.6% vs 10.9% | Partial - costs cut, margin still fell about 3.3 points |
| "Very solid" balance sheet | Net cash EUR 382M at 2026-09-30 (EUR 587M cash vs EUR 207M debt at 2026-06-30) | True - the one clean pillar |
| "Growing dividend policy" | Dividend EUR 132M paid April 2026; free cash flow after working capital only EUR 16M over 9M-2026 (EUR 57M in H1, so Q3 was about minus EUR 41M) | Dividend is being paid out of the cash pile, not out of earnings |
| Earnings trajectory | EPS 0.97 (2024) to 0.72 (2025) to trailing 0.59; latest quarter EPS down 27% y/y | Decline is accelerating, not stabilising |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Declining. 2025-10-30: "successfully managed to mitigate" ad headwinds. 2026-02-12: offensive, with return-on-investment slides for advertisers. 2026-07-30: defensive, margin guidance cut. 2026-10-29: "visibility remaining limited", the market forecast of minus 6% "now seems slightly optimistic", and for 2027 "we see no near-term prospects for improvement in the macroeconomic and political environment or any reduction in the regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms." That last sentence is the most candid management has been in two years.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium. 2025 margin guidance was cut in October 2025 (from "broadly stable" to 10.5-11.5%) and then met at 11%. 2026 guidance was cut at H1 to mid- to high single-digit and is being met (7.6% at nine months). Management meets reset guidance; it does not forecast the down-leg well. The 9M-2026 results came in slightly above company-compiled consensus on revenue and margin.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Very thin coverage on the calls - the 9M-2026 call had only written questions from one broker (CIC). The questions were October/Q4 ad trends, 2027 visibility, the presidential election, Netflix monetisation, and programming costs. Management declined to give a programming-cost range and said Netflix revenue is ramping "more gradually than the audience" because ad load and CPM (price per thousand ad views) on Netflix are below TF1+ levels. Nobody asked about dividend cover, which is the real pressure point.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: dividend (EUR 132M) is about eight times nine-month free cash flow after working capital (EUR 16M) - 9M-2026.
- Red: advertising revenue down 9% with management saying the market has "deteriorated further" since May - 9M-2026.
- Red: no improvement seen for 2027; the 2027 presidential election likely reduces prime-time ad inventory - 9M-2026.
- Red: Studio TF1 operating profit down EUR 14M over nine months - 9M-2026.
- Green: audience share at an all-time high of 36.9% among women under 50 in September 2026, and linear ad market share up about 2 points in August-September - 9M-2026.
- Green: Netflix partnership "ahead of our expectations" on audience; TF1+ growth re-accelerated to 20.5% in Q3 - 9M-2026.
- Green: net cash of EUR 382M is roughly 30% of the market value.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The language moved from "gain market share" (a sign of strength in a stable market) to "regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms" - an admission that the problem is structural, not cyclical. Disclosure has shifted toward audience and usage metrics (streamers, transactions) and away from digital revenue per user. The micro-payment figures (about 2 million transactions year to date) are small in euros; their prominence on the call is a sign of how few growth levers remain.

## 8. BOTTOM LINE
A well-run, market-leading broadcaster in a shrinking market. Management executes against reset targets, keeps a strong net cash position, and is honest about 2027. But the earnings base is still falling, digital growth is not filling the linear hole, and the dividend now relies on the balance sheet.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory declining · a moat that is being eroded.
