picks.bull_thesis: Aegean is the dominant Greek network airline, carrying 16-17 million passengers a year from its Athens hub. It is going through a cyclical fuel and geopolitical shock with one of the strongest balance sheets among European mid-size carriers. Revenue compounded from EUR 1.69B (2023) to EUR 1.86B (2025) and kept growing in the first half of 2026 (+4% to EUR 817M) even with Middle East routes suspended. Unit revenue held above the prior year in the second quarter and, by management's 2026-09-15 indication, in the third, which management says beats short-haul peers. Liquidity stayed at about EUR 956M on 2026-06-30 after a EUR 200M bond repayment and about EUR 80M of dividends. Two cost headwinds are temporary or fading. The Pratt & Whitney engine groundings peaked at 14-15 aircraft in early 2026, fell to about 10 by summer and are guided to zero by end-2027, with undisclosed compensation from the engine maker. Jet fuel at about twice early-2026 levels is a shock the whole industry must pass into fares; Aegean has cut capacity growth to roughly flat for the fourth quarter, and forward winter fares are 'higher than the past' (2026-09-15). If fuel normalises or fares catch up by 2027, earnings return to the EUR 1.45-1.89 a share range of 2023-2025. On 8.5-9 times that, plus about EUR 1 a share of investment stakes (Athens Airport shares and others), the stock is worth EUR 15-17, in line with the broker consensus target of roughly EUR 16-16.5 (S&P Global and Investing.com aggregators, mid-2026 snapshots). Conditions: no prolonged demand collapse in Greek tourism, fares rising with fuel by spring 2027, and no damaging capacity war with low-cost carriers at Athens.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is an earnings mirage built on 2023-2025 peak conditions. TTM diluted EPS has already fallen to EUR 0.91 from EUR 1.65 for full-year 2025, the first half of 2026 lost EUR 3.3M and the first quarter alone lost EUR 21.7M. The real damage lands in 2027: only about 15% of next year's fuel is hedged, at prices about 20% above 2026 hedges (2026-09-15), so with jet fuel near twice early-2026 levels an unhedged fuel bill could rise by several hundred million euros against a company that earned EUR 148M in its good year. Underlying returns are thin: ROIC (return on invested capital) is 6.3%, the 25% ROE (return on equity) is leverage from EUR 963M of aircraft leases, and the Altman-Z solvency score is 1.5. The headline net cash is flattered: the EUR 956M of cash includes about EUR 523M of tickets already paid for future flights, and including leases the company carries net debt of EUR 676M. Low-cost carriers have added roughly 25% capacity to Greece since before COVID, and management has said it will 'defend' routes, meaning it will accept lower margins. Volotea (EUR 37M exposure) is 'significantly undercapitalized' and could need a write-down or more capital. If fuel stays high through 2027, earnings approach break-even. On 3.5 times a trough EBITDA of about EUR 300M less EUR 676M of lease-inclusive net debt, plus investments, the equity is worth EUR 5-7 a share, near book value of about EUR 5.85. Confirmation would come from a weak nine-month update (due 2026-11-16), a dividend cut in spring 2027, or 2027 hedges added at peak prices.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: little. The broker consensus target of roughly EUR 16-16.5 (S&P Global aggregator; Barclays Buy at EUR 17.50 on 2026-07-08 via Investing.com) and the screener's 61-71% margins of safety (the gap between price and estimated value) look stale. Both appear anchored on 2025 earnings power of EUR 1.65 a share, which the fuel shock has already broken: TTM EPS is EUR 0.91, and consensus forward EPS growth reads about zero. Most of those targets predate the second leg of the fuel spike that the Chairman described on 2026-09-15 ('100% higher' than at the start of the year), so they likely overstate 2027. The street is not pricing terminal decline either. At about 7 times 2025 earnings and 3.6 times EBITDA, the market prices a cyclical trough, which is roughly where our own base case sits. Our edge is not a disagreement on the franchise; it is discipline on price. The stock is worth buying only with at least a 20% discount to a fair value that already assumes a partial fuel recovery.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window, the next 3-9 months: (1) the nine-month trading update (2026-11-16) will show the third quarter, the most profitable quarter, absorbing unhedged fuel on about 35% of volume. (2) Winter 2026-27 (fourth quarter and first quarter) is structurally loss-making for Aegean ('I don't believe I will be around when I see Aegean breaking even in the first quarter'), and this winter falls with fuel near double and capacity flat, so a deeper first-quarter 2027 loss than the EUR 21.7M of 2026 is likely. (3) Full-year 2026 results and the dividend decision (around March-May 2027): a cut or skip after EUR 80M in 2026 would be read as management's view of 2027. (4) 2027 hedging: about 85% of fuel is unhedged, so management must buy hedges at elevated prices or stay exposed. (5) Volotea may need fresh capital or face a write-down (about EUR 0.40 a share at risk). There is no debt wall. The EUR 200M bond was repaid in March 2026, the July 2025 EUR 250M bond is long-dated, and liquidity of about EUR 950M rules out a liquidation event. The risk is earnings and multiple compression, not solvency.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure: moderate and sector-wide rather than company-specific. The smart-money score is low (13 of 100) and institutional flow is neutral (50). The shareholder base includes yield-oriented Greek and international holders attracted by the reinstated dividend (about EUR 0.90 a share in 2026, about 7.5% at today's price). A dividend cut in spring 2027 would push some of them out, a possible mechanical leg. The more likely seller is a sector-wide de-rating: airlines, refiners and Gulf-exposed names all resolve on the same oil and Hormuz driver (the catalyst-watch market brief.md, 2026-11-02). The stock is 21% up its 52-week range (low EUR 10.52, high EUR 15.36) and about 4% below its 200-day average (EUR 12.13), so part of that de-rating has already happened. A move back toward EUR 11 on a weak update or an oil spike is plausible.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near EUR 11.2, which a sector-wide sell-off in airlines on the oil and Middle East driver could deliver. The thesis holds. Aegean is a well-financed, dominant Greek network carrier with stable unit revenue, a fading engine problem and about EUR 950M of liquidity. Its earnings have been hit by a fuel shock that the whole sector shares. At EUR 11.67, though, the stock trades only about 18% below our base fair value of EUR 13.8, which sits under the 20% minimum discount this market backdrop requires. That fair value is built on normalised earnings of about EUR 1.50 a share (between the 2024 and 2025 results) at 8.5 times, plus investment stakes. It deliberately sits below the broker consensus near EUR 16-16.5, which appears anchored on pre-shock earnings. The swing factor is 2027 fuel: only about 15% is hedged, so a fuel bill near twice normal with no fare catch-up would push earnings toward break-even and the stock toward our EUR 7 downside case (about 1.2 times book). A recovery would point toward EUR 17. That two-sided, oil-driven outcome is also why this name should not be stacked with other oil-sensitive positions in the book. Conviction is moderate (3 of 5): the franchise and balance sheet are sound, but low returns on capital (about 6%), thin earnings visibility and a modest discount keep it from higher. The nine-month trading update due after today's close is the next dated read and was not available for this debate.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst, what forces the re-rating, is a move in fuel and fares, not a corporate event. In order: (a) a de-escalation in the Middle East that brings jet fuel down sharply (third-party, undated, two-sided); (b) evidence in the full-year 2026 results (around March 2027) that winter fares absorbed the fuel cost; (c) a maintained dividend in May 2027; (d) disclosure of Pratt & Whitney compensation; (e) the end of the engine groundings by end-2027, releasing a fully efficient A321neo fleet. No buyback, activist, asset sale or tender is in play. A counter-cyclical acquisition was floated ('whether it is by acquisition', 2026-09-15) and cuts both ways.

# Aegean Airlines (AEGN.AT): a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Sources: the earnings calls of 2025-03-18 (full-year 2024), 2025-09-17 (first half 2025) and 2026-09-15 (first half 2026), the screener's financial history, FMP half-year statements and the Athens quote (EUR 11.67 on 2026-11-16). The third-quarter and nine-month trading update is due after the Athens close today (2026-11-16) and was not available when this was written.*

## 1. Narrative arc

The story has moved from "growth and record results" to "survive the fuel shock and come out stronger".

- **March 2025 (full-year 2024):** the Chairman led with strength: the "most successful fourth quarter", revenue of about EUR 1.78B (+5%), EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) above EUR 400M and planned capacity growth of 8-9% for 2025. The growth drivers were a longer tourist season, Greeks travelling again after the debt crisis, more of the larger A321neo jets, a new maintenance (MRO) business and a stake in Volotea.
- **September 2025 (first half 2025):** still constructive, with revenue +5% on capacity +4% and higher unit revenue. The worries came in through the Middle East (the loss of Israel, Lebanon and Jordan routes cost about 135,000 passengers) and the Pratt & Whitney geared-turbofan (GTF) engine problem, with 11-14 aircraft grounded for inspections. A new longer-haul plan appeared: 2 XLR and 4 LR aircraft, India via an IndiGo codeshare.
- **September 2026 (first half 2026):** defensive. The Chairman opened with "many more challenges than anticipated", namely Middle East disruption again and jet fuel about "100% higher" than at the start of the year. First-half EBIT (operating profit) fell 35% and the first half turned to a small net loss of EUR 3.3M (after +EUR 48M a year earlier). Capacity growth was cut from the guided 7-9% to about 2.5% in the third quarter and roughly flat (minus 1% to plus 1%) in the fourth. The talk shifted from growth to "defend our routes", "being cautious" and "the profit does not come during the crisis, it comes the day after the crisis".

Dropped or muted along the way: the 8-9% growth ambition, the MRO profit story (never quantified) and Volotea as an upside option. By 2026 Volotea was described as "significantly undercapitalized" and "being challenged".

## 2. Claims vs financials

| Management claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Very strong cash flows" (every call) | Cash of about EUR 956M at 2026-06-30, unchanged from year-end 2025 after repaying a EUR 200M bond (March 2026) and paying about EUR 80M in dividends (May 2026). TTM free cash flow of EUR 504M. | Matches, with a caveat: about EUR 523M of that cash is deferred revenue (tickets sold for future flights) at the seasonal June peak. Some of the cash belongs to customers, not shareholders. |
| Revenue growth is resilient | Revenue: 2023 EUR 1.69B, 2024 EUR 1.78B, 2025 EUR 1.86B; first half 2026 EUR 817M (+4%). | Matches. Volume growth has stayed positive throughout. |
| Unit revenue held up better than at short-haul peers | Second quarter 2026 revenue +3% on flat capacity. | Matches the revenue line, but profit did not follow. |
| Earnings strength | Net income: 2023 EUR 170M, 2024 EUR 130M, 2025 EUR 148M. First half 2026 is a EUR 3.3M loss; TTM diluted EPS is EUR 0.91 against EUR 1.65 for full-year 2025. | Diverges now. Costs (fuel, carbon permits, GTF-related inefficiency) are rising faster than revenue. |
| Returns | ROE of 25% but ROIC (return on invested capital) of only 6.3%. Altman-Z (a solvency score) of 1.5. | The high ROE is leverage-driven, because leases are large (EUR 963M). Underlying returns are modest. |
| GTF groundings peak and then fade | 14-15 grounded in February-April 2026, down to about 10 in summer; guided to zero by end-2027. | Consistent with the September 2025 forecast of "12 to 14 for the next 12 to 14 months". Credible. |
| Hedged against fuel | About 65% hedged for the rest of 2026 at early-2026 prices; only about 15% for 2027, at prices about 20% higher. | The 2027 exposure is the single largest unpriced risk. |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory: declining (offensive to defensive)

- 2025-03: "another strong and successful year"; capacity growth of 8-9%.
- 2025-09: "cautious optimism for the overall year"; "in an airline where you see the cash flows as positive as ours, you shouldn't be too worried."
- 2026-09: "we will try to be cautious, but if attacked, we will defend ourselves"; on winter fares, "the indication is there, but not the conviction."

The language moved from growth to cost and capacity discipline. It stays measured rather than evasive. The Chairman openly declined to predict ("making predictions is not a good idea").

## 4. Guidance credibility: medium-high

- The 2025 guidance of 8-9% capacity growth delivered only about 4% in the first half of 2025, mostly because of external shocks (the Middle East and engine groundings) that management flagged on the calls.
- The 2026 guidance of 7-9% capacity growth was cut to roughly 2.5% (third quarter) and flat (fourth quarter). The cut was a deliberate response to fuel prices, which is prudent and not a miss of execution.
- The GTF grounding trajectory was forecast accurately.
- The screener's earnings-beat rate is 50% (1 of 2 quarters), which is thin coverage and uninformative.
- Management does not sandbag. It gives little numeric guidance, and what it gives has generally been honest about direction.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- **Pratt & Whitney compensation.** Asked directly in 2026-09; management refused to size it ("everybody around me is waving their hands"). This is a real, unquantified offset.
- **Fuel hedging for 2027.** Answered: only 15% hedged. Analysts are right to focus here.
- **Volotea.** Barclays asked whether the investment is at risk. Management distanced itself ("we are not managing the company"). About EUR 37M is exposed (EUR 32M of convertible debt and EUR 5M of equity), roughly EUR 0.40 a share, which is small but plausibly a write-down.
- **Unit costs.** In 2025-09 analysts flagged unit costs excluding fuel up about 7% in the second quarter. Management blamed under-use of idle aircraft and crews.

## 6. Red flags and green flags

Red flags:
- First half 2026 swung to a net loss (2026-09-15). The first quarter alone lost EUR 21.7M.
- 2027 fuel is only about 15% hedged (2026-09-15), and that hedge sits roughly 20% above 2026 levels.
- Volotea is described as undercapitalized (2026-09-15), so a write-down risk exists.
- FCF fell 68% year on year in the fiscal-year data, and ROIC is low at 6.3%.
- Rising regulatory costs (carbon permits, sustainable aviation fuel and air-traffic-control charges) appear on every call.

Green flags:
- Liquidity held at about EUR 950M after a EUR 200M bond repayment and EUR 80M of dividends (2026-06-30).
- Most of the fleet is financed at fixed rates; 4 of the 5 aircraft delivered in 2026 came through sale-and-leaseback deals (2026-09-15).
- Only 7 aircraft need financing over the next two years, against 14 in the last two (2026-09-15).
- A high share of new-generation aircraft, with the GTF problem fading through 2027.
- Unit revenue held above the prior year in the second and third quarters of 2026 despite network disruption.

## 7. Hidden signals

- "Defend our share where we think our strategic position might get affected" (2026-09): management expects competitors (low-cost carriers that have added roughly 25% capacity to Greece since before COVID) to test the domestic and Athens hub franchise during the downturn. Management is signalling it will accept lower margins to protect share.
- "Opportunities ... whether it is in fleet, whether it is in routes, whether it is by acquisition" (2026-09): with a strong balance sheet, the company may consider counter-cyclical M&A, which could be good or bad for shareholders.
- Dividends: paid for the first time in four years in 2024 and grown to about EUR 80M in 2026. Whether that holds in 2027 is the tell for management's private view of the fuel outlook.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict: stable

Capital allocation is disciplined: debt repaid, a dividend paid, capacity cut quickly, fixed-rate fleet financing. The trajectory of earnings has deteriorated cyclically, but the capital-allocation stance has not. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing is the 2027 fuel bill. With 85% of next year's fuel unhedged and jet fuel near twice its early-2026 level, full-year 2027 earnings depend on whether fares rise enough to pass the cost on. Management itself has "the indication but not the conviction."

**Moat.** Aegean's moat is narrow and real, built on scale and network. It is the dominant carrier on Greek domestic routes and at the Athens hub, a Star Alliance member with a premium product and a loyal home market ("our favorite tribe is actually Greeks"). The width is limited: ROIC of about 6% and steady low-cost competitor capacity into Greece. The trend is stable: gross margin has held at about 25% and the new fleet improves unit costs, but no widening is visible.

**Secular threat.** Manageable. Carbon-permit and sustainable-aviation-fuel mandates raise costs for the whole industry, and peers pass them on together. Neither threatens the terminal value of a dominant regional network carrier. The cheapness is mostly a cyclical fear-print (fuel and the Middle East), not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# VEF AB (VEFAB.ST) - Forensic dossier, 2026-11-02

Live price used: SEK 1.69 (FMP quote, Stockholm listing, 2 November 2026). The stock fell from SEK 1.99 on 23 October to SEK 1.81 on 26 October (about 4.2m shares traded, roughly six times normal) and has drifted to SEK 1.69, the bottom of its 52-week range (SEK 1.654 to 2.50). The trigger was dated and external: President Lula won Brazil's presidential runoff on 25 October 2026, reversing the first-round rally; the real (Brazil's currency) went from about 5.05 per dollar before the vote to about 5.44 today (FMP, 2 November), roughly 7% weaker.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Across five calls (22 Oct 2025 to 21 Oct 2026) the story moved in three steps: (a) "the portfolio is self-sustaining, exits are coming" in late 2025; (b) "we sold part of Juspay and are paying down debt" in Q1-Q2 2026 (one realisation, the $14.6m Juspay secondary); (c) "bonds repaid, a revolving credit facility in place, next priority is buybacks" on 21 October 2026. The constant thread is Creditas, the largest holding (about half of net assets), which management now frames as moving from venture to private equity and eventually to a public listing. The newest chapter - "Brazil is in a good place, our names are up 20-30%" - was spoken four days before the runoff and has already been reversed by the vote.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Net asset value (NAV, the stated value of the holdings less debt): $401.7m at 30 September 2026, down about 1% in the quarter and about 7.5% from $434m at December 2025. Management's attribution (+$10m company delivery, -$10m comparable multiples, -$3m currency) is internally consistent and checks against the bridge.
- 71% of the book is marked at the latest transaction (Creditas at the December 2025 Series G, Juspay at the January 2026 Series D follow-on) and was held flat with no new transactions. That is a policy choice, not evidence of value today; the Creditas mark is now about 11 months old and was set when Brazil traded far better than after the runoff.
- Konfio was marked down a further $5.1m (about 7% quarter on quarter), the second consecutive cut, attributed to the peso and comparable multiples while management concedes first-half delivery ran behind plan.
- Holding-level accounts are not operating accounts: "revenue" and the 21,686% net margin in the scan are fair-value changes. ROE -11% and ROIC -7.8% reflect NAV declines. Net debt about SEK 4m on the 30 September balance sheet (borrowings 24m, cash 20m - per the live correction; unit as given), i.e. modest leverage after the SEK 300m bond redemption and a SEK 150m revolving facility.
- NAV per share fell about 2% a year from 2020 to 2025: the compounding claim is about the portfolio companies, not about value per VEF share.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Steady, slightly more confident on operations (Creditas "ninth quarter of acceleration", Abhi past $100m run-rate revenue and profitable, Konfio "glass half full"), notably guarded on capital return ("it's not much of a buyback without cash, is it?"; nothing is real until an exit lands). The macro optimism was explicit and is now dated by the election outcome.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Operational guidance on Creditas has been delivered quarter after quarter. Exit guidance ("over the next 12-18 months") has been repeated on every call for a year with one partial realisation delivered; that piece is soft. Debt-reduction guidance was delivered in full (bonds repaid in Q3 2026).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Analysts (Redeye, others) pressed on: where liquidity for buybacks comes from (answer: exits, undated); Juspay's pricing power from India's payment-fee reform (delayed post-Diwali, timing unknown); Konfio's repeated markdowns; whether Brazil policy changes VEF's appetite. No analyst challenged the age of the Creditas mark directly; no FMP price-target coverage exists and none was found.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: about 60% of the portfolio is Brazil-exposed and the market-friendly outcome management leaned on did not happen (25 Oct 2026); stale transaction marks on 71% of the book; NAV per share has shrunk over five years; no funded mechanism to close the discount (now about 56% to stated NAV at SEK 9.76 per dollar). Green: real, growing, largely self-funding businesses; leverage cut; Abhi listing path offers a second realisation route; Juspay reform is an option that costs nothing.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The post-runoff sell-off was heavy-volume and macro-driven, not company news: no VEF announcement since 21 October (FMP news empty for 20 Oct - 2 Nov).
- Management's own words name the BRL, rates and Brazilian fintech comparables as the NAV drivers of the mark-to-model book; the Q4 2026 NAV (due January 2027) will carry a currency and multiple hit on Solfacil, Nibo and, via any re-mark, Creditas.
- A Lula government with looser fiscal policy implies a higher-for-longer Selic, which pressures lender margins and asset quality and pushes back any Creditas listing window.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Capital allocation is sound in direction (de-lever first, then buy back) but unfunded in practice. The value case is a closed-end discount on real assets whose marks are aging and whose single-country macro just turned against them. Credible operators, honest disclosure, no fabricated numbers; the weakness is a realisation path that depends on exit markets the election outcome has just made harder.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady.

picks.bull_thesis: Lyft is a cash-generating number-two marketplace priced as if robotaxis will make it obsolete, while the latest numbers say the opposite. In Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-05) rides grew 10% and accelerated in both the US and Canada, active riders reached 31.6M (the eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth), driver hours hit a record and adjusted EBITDA rose 47% to $204M, or 3.6% of bookings. Insurance, Lyft's largest variable cost, is genuinely falling: cost of revenue dropped to $871M from $927M a year earlier while volume grew, lifting gross margin to about 52% of revenue from 45%. The balance sheet holds about $644M of net cash (cash $1.90B against $1.26B of debt and leases at 2026-09-30), and buybacks have cut the share count about 8% in nine months, from roughly 411M to 379M. Partnerships now touch about 30% of North American rides, and Lyft Go (launched 2026-11-05, $9.99 a month with DoorDash's DashPass) should raise rider frequency. On autonomous vehicles Lyft is positioning as the operator robotaxi makers need - it runs Waymo's Nashville depot (opened October 2026, fleet growing by year-end) and is preparing Baidu's commercial launch in London in 2027 - which turns the main risk into an optional revenue line. If normalised free cash flow reaches about $950M and the market pays 9 times for it, the shares are worth about $24, in line with the highest street target of $23 (Evercore ISI, 2026-11-06). Conditions: ride growth stays at or above high single digits, adjusted margin keeps expanding toward the 4% of bookings management targets for 2027, and buybacks continue near $500M a year.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is partly an illusion of accounting and partly a fair price for a structural risk. First, the headline 6.4 times price-to-free-cash-flow is flattered: of roughly $1.27B of trailing operating cash flow, about $0.9B came from working-capital build, mostly insurance reserves (claims booked but not yet paid), and stock-based pay costs about $70-90M a quarter. Strip those out and recurring owner cash flow is nearer $550-800M, putting the stock at 8-11 times rather than 6. As insurance costs fall (the California reform), the reserve build that inflates cash flow should slow or reverse. Second, the quality of growth is slipping: bookings rose 17% but revenue only 8.1% in Q3 2026, sales and marketing jumped about 57% year on year to $382M, and Lyft Go adds another 8% rider credit - growth is being bought. Third, reported results keep carrying reserve hits (a $9.7M net loss in Q3 2026 from legal, tax and regulatory charges), and the 2025 net income of $2.84B was a one-off $2.9B tax benefit, not earnings power. Fourth, autonomous vehicles are a material threat: if Waymo or Tesla scale their own apps in Lyft's core US cities, Lyft becomes a low-margin fleet manager with return on invested capital already only about 7.8%. Insiders sold about 463 thousand shares on the open market against about 18 thousand bought, and the CFO changed in Q3 2026. In this case normalised free cash flow of about $550M at 6 times plus net cash gives about $10.40 a share. What would confirm it: revenue growth falling toward mid single digits, the $500M buyback target missed in Q4 2026, or a robotaxi operator launching a competing app in a top Lyft market.
picks.consensus_delta: The street sits on hold - 23 of 35 brokers rate it hold, 10 buy, 2 sell, with a consensus target near $18.31 (newest targets 2026-11-06: $18, $20 and $23). Where we disagree with the market: analysts anchor on the reported 6 times free-cash-flow multiple as proof of deep value; we think the honest multiple is nearer 8 times once insurance-reserve build and stock pay are removed, which puts our fair value ($18.95) close to consensus rather than far above it. Where we are more positive than the market: rides are accelerating and insurance costs falling in absolute terms, which the robotaxi-fear discount ignores.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): Q4 2026 results in early February 2027 must show whether the roughly $500M buyback target was met after only $50M in Q3, and whether Lyft Go's 8% credits and a 57% jump in sales and marketing spend compress adjusted margins. Further reserve charges for legal and regulatory matters, a Waymo or Tesla own-app launch in a top Lyft city, or a slowdown in discretionary spending under sticky inflation could each knock the stock back toward the low teens (the 52-week low is $12.46). The stock rose about 11% with the group on 2026-11-04 and then gave back about 4% after its own results, showing it trades as a sector factor.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is low: there is no index deletion, lock-up or dividend cut pending, and no forced holder base. The likely seller that would reach our level is a sector-wide sell-off in mobility and delivery names - the group moves together on robotaxi headlines and on Uber or DoorDash results, as it did on 2026-11-04. Insider open-market selling (28 sells of about 463 thousand shares against 3 buys of about 18 thousand) is a steady supply but not a flush.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near $15.75, which a sector-wide sell-off in the mobility and delivery group could deliver. Our answer is unchanged from 2026-10-12. The thesis holds: the Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-05 showed rides accelerating, record adjusted profit, falling insurance costs and a fifth straight quarter of more than $1B of trailing free cash flow, with about $644M of net cash and a share count shrinking about 8% this year. But at $16.86 our fair value of $18.95 is only about 12% above the price, short of the 20% cushion we require in this backdrop, and the cash-flow headline is flattered by insurance-reserve build. At $15.75 the discount clears 20% while the downside case of $10.40 is still well below. Robotaxis remain a material but not fatal risk; Lyft is positioning as the partner operators need. Conviction stays at 3: a good, improving business at a fair-to-cheap price, not yet a bargain.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating - is soft and undated: sustained proof that free cash flow stays above $1B as insurance reserves normalise, continued buybacks of about $500M a year at a sub-10 times multiple shrinking the share count, and visible AV partnership revenue (Nashville fleet expansion by year-end 2026, London with Baidu in 2027). picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Lyft (LYFT) - a deep dive on management and the setup (as of 2026-11-10)

Five earnings calls reviewed: Q3 2025 (2025-11-05), Q4 2025 (2026-02-10), Q1 2026 (2026-05-08), Q2 2026 (2026-08-06) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-05). Live price used: $16.86 (NASDAQ, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-10).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from "comeback" to "global, autonomous-ready platform". In Q3 2025 the CEO called Lyft "this comeback story" and leaned on record rides, the United Airlines partnership and newly signed autonomous-vehicle (AV) partners (Waymo, Tensor). Through 2026 the emphasis widened in three directions that management now calls "up, out, and forward": up (premium rides, business travel, the new Alcove chauffeur brand built on the TBR acquisition), out (FREENOW, the European taxi app bought in mid-2025, which "made Lyft a global company"), and forward (a hybrid human-plus-robotaxi network, starting with Waymo in Nashville and Baidu in London).

What has stayed constant is the financial spine: free cash flow (cash left after running the business and its capital spending) above $1 billion on a trailing basis, and share buybacks. What has quietly shrunk is the pace of buybacks inside the year: $300 million in Q1 2026, $100 million in Q2, $50 million in Q3, against an unchanged full-year target of about $500 million.

The newest thread is partnerships as a growth engine: about 30% of North American rides are now linked to a partner (Q2 2026), and on 2026-11-05 Lyft launched Lyft Go, a $9.99 a month membership bundled with DoorDash's DashPass that pays an 8% ride credit.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record" growth, bookings accelerating | Gross bookings +17% in Q3 2026 to $5.6B, down from about +23% in Q2 (Q2 still included part of the FREENOW year-on-year step-up). Rides +10%, accelerating in the US and Canada. Revenue +8.1% y/y to $1.82B and below estimates. | Partly matches - rides are genuinely accelerating; the bookings slowdown is mostly lapping an acquisition, but revenue growth is far slower than bookings. |
| "Most profitable quarter to date" | Adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, excluding stock pay and one-offs) $204M, +47% y/y, 3.6% of bookings. GAAP (reported) result was a net loss of $9.7M (-$0.03 a share), hit by legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes. | The adjusted figure is real; the reported loss shows the recurring cost of legal and insurance reserves that the adjusted number excludes. |
| Over $1B of trailing free cash flow for a fifth straight quarter | Trailing twelve-month (TTM) free cash flow about $1.16B (Q4 2025 $261M, Q1 $287M, Q2 $320M, Q3 $295M). But roughly $0.9B of the $1.27B operating cash flow came from working-capital build, largely insurance reserves (claims booked but not yet paid). Stock-based pay ran about $217M over the last three quarters. | The headline is accurate but flattered. Cash earned from operations excluding the reserve build and net of stock pay is closer to $0.6-0.8B. |
| "Bend the insurance cost curve" | Q3 2026 cost of revenue $871M fell year on year against $927M in Q3 2025 despite higher volume; gross margin rose to 52% of revenue from 45%. | Matches - the clearest corroborated claim. |
| Net income of $2.84B in 2025, EPS $6.81 | Almost entirely a one-off $2.9B tax benefit (release of a valuation allowance on past losses) in Q4 2025. Pre-tax income was negative in that quarter. | Accounting artefact; ignore for valuation. |
| Disciplined capital return | ~$500M of buybacks planned for 2026; share count down from about 411M (Q4 2025) to 379M (Q3 2026), roughly 8%. | Matches. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable to rising. The CEO's tone is consistently promotional ("Wow, Q3 was another record quarter", Q3 2025; "Neither rain nor heat nor the gloom of night can slow Lyft's business", Q3 2026 release). Guidance has become slightly less specific on unit economics - in Q3 2026 the new CFO declined to guide bookings per ride ("I don't think we're going to be able to give any specific guidance on this"). Language has shifted from defending the core (2023-24) to offence (AV, Europe, premium), while the CFO transition (Erin Brewer out, Michael Brous in, first call 2026-11-05) was framed as "continuity, not a reset".

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-High. In Q3 2025 management guided Q4 2025 bookings +17% to 20%; in Q1 2026 it guided bookings to accelerate to about 20% and adjusted EBITDA to grow over 30%, and Q2 delivered about 23% bookings growth. The Nashville AV depot opened on the promised October timing, and the European app roll-out and buyback target have both tracked what was said. The screener's 2-of-7 beat rate on reported EPS understates delivery, because the reported line is distorted by reserves and the tax release; on the operating metrics management guides to, delivery has been reliable. The Q3 2026 revenue miss is the one recent soft spot.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Bookings per ride and the gap between bookings growth (+17%) and revenue growth (+8%): management declined to quantify it (Q3 2026).
- AV capital needs: the CFO says AV build-out is funded "off the balance sheet" and is "relatively immaterial", with third-party capital expected later - no number given.
- Whether robotaxis cannibalise Lyft in markets where Waymo or Tesla run their own apps; the CEO asserts Lyft is growing in AV markets (Benzinga, 2026-11-06) but gives no market-level data.
- Rider incentive spending: rider-side investment has risen (sales and marketing $382M in Q3 2026 against $243M a year earlier) and Lyft Go adds another credit programme.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Q3 2026: reported net loss from legal, tax and regulatory reserve changes; revenue below estimates.
- Q3 2026: sales and marketing up about 57% year on year - growth is being bought partly with incentives.
- Free cash flow leans on insurance-reserve build, which can reverse if claims are paid down or insurance costs fall (California reform lowers the reserve need over time).
- Insider open-market activity: 3 buys of about 18 thousand shares against 28 sells of about 463 thousand shares.
- CFO change in Q3 2026.

Green flags:
- Rides accelerating in the US and Canada (Q3 2026), driver hours at a record, 31.6M active riders (eighth straight quarter of double-digit growth).
- Cost of revenue falling in absolute terms (Q3 2026) while volume grows.
- Net cash of about $644M at 2026-09-30; share count down about 8% in nine months.
- Concrete AV execution: Lyft staff took over Waymo's Nashville temporary depot on June 9, 2026 (per Q2 2026 call), depot opened October 2026, fleet to grow by year-end.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Global AV-ready mobility platform" has replaced "comeback story" - management is selling a strategic narrative that the market currently does not pay for.
- Buyback pace is back-end weighted in reverse: heavy in Q1, light in Q3. Combined with AV funding "off the balance sheet", watch whether the $500M target is met in Q4.
- The new CFO is an operator from the bikes and international businesses; his framing ("every dollar of efficiency... reinvest or return") hints at more investment in the newer lines.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: strengthening. The core marketplace is growing rides at double digits with rising adjusted margins and genuinely falling insurance costs, and the balance sheet is net cash. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: the headline 6x price-to-free-cash-flow is flattered by insurance-reserve float; on a normalised basis (net of stock pay and reserve build) the stock trades nearer 8-9x, which is cheap but not a deep discount.

Moat: a network (two-sided marketplace) moat that is narrow - Lyft is a clear number two in US ride-hailing with return on invested capital of about 7.8%, but margins are widening rather than falling, so it is not eroding. Secular threat: autonomous vehicles are a material, not terminal, risk. If robotaxi owners (Waymo, Tesla) choose to run their own demand apps, Lyft's role shrinks to fleet operator; Lyft's hedge is to be the preferred partner (Waymo Nashville, Baidu London, May Mobility Atlanta). The cheapness looks more like a fear discount on that risk than a structurally shrinking base - rides are still accelerating.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

Add net cash of about $0.64B (cash $1.90B less $1.26B debt and leases, 2026-09-30). Total about $7.16B over about 378M shares = about $18.95 a share. No value assigned to AV partnerships, Alcove or Lyft Go.

picks.bull_thesis: The market is paying close to nothing for two late-stage obesity drugs. At DKK 239.80 (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16) Zealand is valued at about DKK 15.9 billion, while at 2026-09-30 it held DKK 13.51 billion of cash and securities and DKK 4.19 billion of receivables (mostly Roche) against DKK 0.48 billion of debt - about DKK 15.3 billion, or DKK 231 a share, after current liabilities and the last tranche of the buyback. For an enterprise value (market value minus net cash) near zero, you own a 50/50 US and European profit share in petrelintide, an amylin analog (a copy of a gut hormone that makes people feel full) that Roche chose to take into a global three-trial Phase 3 program in September 2026 after seeing both Phase 2 trials, plus the same profit share on its combination with Roche's enicepatide (Phase 2 starting Q4 2026). Petrelintide's edge is tolerability: stomach-related dropouts of 1.5% versus 0% on placebo in ZUPREME-1 and 1.9% versus 1.7% in ZUPREME-2 - a profile management calls 'easy to start, and easy to stay on' (Q3 2026 call), in a market where, per the 2026-02-19 call, only a small fraction of patients exposed to GLP-1 drugs stay on them. Second, Zealand earns royalties and up to EUR 315 million of open milestones on Boehringer's survodutide, whose Phase 3 program is now complete: 16.6% weight loss in SYNCHRONIZE-1 (June 2026), up to 13.1% in diabetics (2026-10-01) and confirmed cardiovascular safety (2026-11-09), with filings in 2027 and liver-disease (MASH) data in 2027 that could widen its use. Third, management is disciplined with the cash: it bought back DKK 1.3 billion of stock at about DKK 295 (completed 2026-10-05) and guided 2026 costs to the low end of its range (2026-11-12). Conditions: Roche stays committed, Phase 3 pushes petrelintide toward the low-to-mid teens with placebo-like tolerability, survodutide is approved in 2027-28, and spending stays near DKK 2.5-3 billion a year.
picks.bear_thesis: The cash is spoken for, and the drugs are second-tier. The screener's 2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow, 70% net margin and DKK 522.8 discounted-cash-flow value capitalise one-off Roche payments: recurring revenue was DKK 4 million in Q3 2026, trailing free cash flow is minus DKK 1.53 billion and return on invested capital is about minus 25%. Petrelintide missed management's own 15-20% target twice - about 10.7% at 42 weeks in ZUPREME-1 and up to 9.2% at 28 weeks in diabetics - and the Q3 2026 call quietly replaced the target with 'double-digit weight loss'. Lilly's eloralintide is about a year ahead with stronger numbers and Novo is advancing amylin drugs of its own, so tolerability may be a feature of the class, not of Zealand's molecule. Survodutide passed its heart-safety test, but about one in five patients stopped treatment for stomach side effects (2026-11-09), so it enters a crowded GLP-1 market as a liver-focused niche product. Meanwhile management is widening the spending agenda - a Cambridge research hub, an AI-protein collaboration, small molecules, '10 clinical programs by 2030' - and has never quantified its share of Phase 3 costs. If spending runs at DKK 2.5-3 billion a year for four years and both drugs prove commercially marginal, the stock converges on spent-down cash of about DKK 135 a share. What would confirm it: Roche scaling back Phase 3, competitor amylin data that clearly beat petrelintide, a survodutide approval delay, or 2027 cost guidance above DKK 3.3 billion.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: after a slide from a 52-week high of DKK 556 to DKK 239.80, the market prices Zealand as if its pipeline were worth roughly nothing and its cash will simply be burned. We agree the petrelintide data were below management's own target and that Lilly leads the amylin class. But the street is underweighting three dated facts: Roche committed to a full global Phase 3 after seeing all the data; survodutide has cleared every Phase 3 hurdle including heart safety (2026-11-09) and heads to filing in 2027; and management returned DKK 1.3 billion through a buyback while guiding costs to the low end. The screener's own signals (2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow, DKK 522.8 discounted-cash-flow value) are wrong in the other direction - they capitalise one-off milestones - and we disregard them.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): there is no debt wall and no liquidity risk, so this is a valuation-drawdown risk, not a solvency one. The main hazards are competitor amylin data from Lilly (eloralintide) and Novo at medical meetings, which can re-rate the whole class; 2027 cost guidance (due with the full-year report around February 2027) if it rises above about DKK 3.3 billion as Phase 3 and the research expansion ramp; and any sign that Roche is slowing the petrelintide program. Survodutide's tolerability (about 19-21% dropping out for stomach effects in the outcomes trial) could trim regulators' or prescribers' enthusiasm, but its value is a small part of ours.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has largely played out: the stock is down about 57% from its 52-week high, sits about 20% below its 200-day average of DKK 298.6 and only about 9% above its 52-week low of DKK 220.6. Momentum and growth funds that held it as an obesity proxy have been leaving since the first Phase 2 readout in early 2026. There is no dividend base to liquidate and no index event identified; further selling would be fundamental (data or spending), not mechanical. The company's own buyback at about DKK 295 shows management saw value well above today's price.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds and the news since our last look on 10 November 2026 nudged it slightly in our favour: Boehringer's survodutide passed its heart-safety trial on 9 November and will be filed in 2027, and the 12 November quarterly report showed DKK 13.5 billion of cash and securities plus DKK 4.2 billion of receivables, with 2026 costs guided to the low end of the range - the spending scare we flagged did not happen. At DKK 239.80 you pay about DKK 15.9 billion for a company with roughly DKK 15.3 billion of net cash and receivables, and you get a half share of Roche's petrelintide program and a royalty on survodutide for very little. Correcting the share count for the October buyback (about 66.3 million shares) and lifting survodutide's odds roughly offset, so our base-case fair value is DKK 300 a share, about 25% above the price and clear of our 20% bar for buying in today's reflationary market. This is not a classic value floor: the cash is committed to an expensive Phase 3 and a widening research agenda, petrelintide's weight loss missed management's own target, and Lilly leads the class. So conviction stays moderate (3 of 5), the value case scores 3 of 5, and the debt-cycle backdrop, which punishes long-dated stories, is a headwind. # Zealand Pharma (ZEAL.CO) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Quote used: DKK 239.80 on the Copenhagen listing (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16). Transcripts read: Q1 2025 (2025-05-09), H1 2025 (2025-08-14), Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), full year 2025 (2026-02-19) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-12). The Q1 and H1 2026 calls were not in the bundle, so the 2026 readouts between February and November are reconstructed from the Q3 2026 call and the dated company announcements.*

**Bottom line.** Zealand is a clinical-stage peptide company whose stock is now worth less than the cash and partner receivables on its balance sheet net of near-term liabilities, plus a modest value for two late-stage obesity programs run with Roche and Boehringer Ingelheim. Management has hit nearly every timeline it set, but the clinical numbers have landed below the 15-20% weight-loss bar it set for its lead drug. The reported profits and the screener's 2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow are one-off milestone artifacts and should be ignored.

## 1. Narrative arc

- **Q1 2025 (2025-05-09):** the story was the newly signed Roche deal - "historic and transformative" - a 50/50 profit share on petrelintide (an amylin analog, a copy of a gut hormone that makes people feel full) in the US and Europe. The pitch: a better-tolerated alternative to GLP-1 drugs, targeting 15-20% weight loss.
- **H1 2025 (2025-08-14):** two leading programs (petrelintide and survodutide, Boehringer's glucagon/GLP-1 drug on which Zealand earns royalties). Amylin pitched as "the next major class". Rare-disease assets and dapiglutide still part of the story.
- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-13):** dapiglutide paused ("the GLP-1-based therapeutic space has become increasingly crowded"). The company narrowed to its two partnered obesity assets and talked of becoming "a generational biotech".
- **Full year 2025 (2026-02-19):** "the most defining and catalyst-rich year" in the company's history; a Boston research hub, AI-driven discovery, "more than 10 candidates into the clinic" in five years, and "5 product launches over the next 5 years".
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-12):** the language moved from weight-loss magnitude to "first-choice" and "easy to start, and easy to stay on". The research story widened again: a Cambridge (US) hub, a Generate Biomedicines AI-protein deal, small molecules via OTR, and a "multimodality metabolic health company". The rare-disease assets (dasiglucagon, glepaglutide) are now to be licensed out.

The arc is a pivot from a single-asset partnership story to a platform story, with the efficacy target quietly reframed from "15% to 20%" to "double-digit weight loss" with placebo-like tolerability.

## 2. Claims vs financials (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Secured enough capital to fund our journey towards profitability" (Q1 2025) | Cash and securities DKK 13.51bn and DKK 4.19bn of receivables against DKK 0.48bn of debt at 2026-09-30 (FMP statements). Down from DKK 15.11bn at end-2025, partly due to a roughly DKK 1.3bn share buyback completed 2026-10-05. | Holds. No financing risk for years. |
| Earnings strength (screener: net margin 70%, P/FCF 2.7x, EPS 90.22 in 2025) | 2025 revenue DKK 9.21bn and 2026 Q2 revenue DKK 4.49bn are Roche upfront and milestone payments. Recurring revenue was DKK 34m in Q1 2026 and DKK 4m in Q3 2026; TTM free cash flow is minus DKK 1.53bn; return on invested capital about minus 25%. | Does not hold. The cheapness on earnings is an artifact. |
| Cost discipline | 2026 operating-expense guidance DKK 2.7-3.3bn; on 2026-11-12 the CFO said guidance was narrowed "to the lower end". Q3 2026 net operating loss only DKK 54m after cost sharing. | Holds; burn is running below the feared DKK 3bn+. |
| Petrelintide 15-20% weight loss (Q3 2025, FY 2025) | ZUPREME-1: "up to 10.7% mean weight loss at week 42", GI discontinuation 1.5% vs 0% placebo. ZUPREME-2 (diabetics): up to 9.2% at week 28, A1c down up to 0.65 points (Q3 2026 call). | Missed the stated efficacy target; the tolerability claim held. |
| Survodutide competitive weight loss, comparable tolerability (Q3 2025) | SYNCHRONIZE-1 16.6% (June 2026), SYNCHRONIZE-2 up to 13.1% in diabetics (2026-10-01), SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT met cardiovascular safety (2026-11-09, AHA). Press reports put GI discontinuations around 19-21% in the outcomes trial. Boehringer confirmed global filings in 2027. | Efficacy and safety hold; tolerability is worse than management implied. |
| Five launches in five years | Glepaglutide received a positive opinion from the EU medicines committee (CHMP) in Q3 2026; survodutide filing 2027; petrelintide Phase 3 started 2026-09. | On track in part; rare-disease launches will be via out-licensing. |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory - Stable to slightly declining

- Q1 2025: "never been in a stronger position" - maximum confidence.
- H1 2025 and Q3 2025: still bold on targets ("We remain fully confident in the potential of petrelintide to deliver 15% to 20% weight loss in Phase III").
- FY 2025: "catalyst-rich year"; success defined as data reinforcing "approximately 15% to 20%".
- Q3 2026: no restatement of the 15-20% figure; replaced by "double-digit weight loss" and "a tolerability profile that is generally comparable to placebo". The CFO declined to say where cost savings came from.

Confidence on execution stays high; confidence on the efficacy number has been walked back. That is a defensive shift dressed in offensive language.

## 4. Guidance credibility - Medium

Delivered: ZUPREME-1 data in the first half of 2026 (guided Q1); Phase 3 start in the second half of 2026 (started 2026-09); ZUPREME-2 in the second half of 2026; combination Phase 2 (ZYNERGY, with Roche's enicepatide, formerly CT-388) now guided to Q4 2026 versus "first half of 2026" on 2026-02-19 - a slip of about two quarters. Operating expenses inside guidance. Missed: the efficacy target. Dasiglucagon manufacturing has been delayed repeatedly by a third-party facility. Timelines are reliable; outcome claims are not. The screener's 5-of-7 earnings beat rate is meaningless for a company whose revenue is milestone timing.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- Tolerability versus efficacy trade-off in amylins (Wells Fargo, Q3 2025; Danske, H1 2025 on the flat dose response in men). Management answered with the 480-patient Phase 2 - which then showed about 10.7%.
- Survodutide GI tolerability (UBS, Q3 2025): management promised "comparable" tolerability; the outcomes trial showed about one in five stopping for GI effects.
- Cost sharing with Roche and caps on spend (Goldman, Q1 2025): never quantified; "we are not yet providing clear guidance".
- Where cost savings came from (BNP Paribas, Q3 2026): not answered.
- Competitive position versus Lilly's eloralintide and Novo's amycretin and cagrilintide: always deflected with "best-in-class potential", never with head-to-head data.

## 6. Red flags / green flags

Red flags
- The 15-20% weight-loss target set in 2025 and reaffirmed on 2026-02-19 was not met in either Phase 2 trial; the Q3 2026 call no longer quotes it.
- Survodutide GI discontinuations of about 19-21% in the outcomes trial (reported 2026-11-09) contradict "comparable tolerability" (Q3 2025).
- Scope creep during the proof years: Boston/Cambridge hub, AI-protein collaboration, small molecules, "10 clinical programs by 2030" - spending that competes with returning cash.
- The combination Phase 2 slipped from the first half of 2026 to Q4 2026.
- Stock-page earnings, margins and DCF value are built on one-off milestone payments.

Green flags
- Roche - which saw all the Phase 2 data - started a roughly three-trial global Phase 3 program in 2026-09 and is co-funding it; a sophisticated partner voting with money.
- Survodutide's Phase 3 program is complete, cardiovascular safety is confirmed (2026-11-09) and Boehringer has committed to filing in 2027, which de-risks royalties and the remaining milestones.
- Placebo-like GI discontinuation for petrelintide in both Phase 2 trials (1.5% vs 0% and 1.9% vs 1.7%).
- Capital discipline: a DKK 1.3bn buyback at about DKK 295 (completed 2026-10-05) and 2026 costs guided to the low end.
- Positive EU committee opinion for glepaglutide in short bowel syndrome.

## 7. Hidden signals

- "End the weight loss Olympics" (Q3 2025) became the frame that pre-justified a sub-target result: the bar was moved before the data arrived.
- CT-388 is now called enicepatide - Roche is branding its own asset, a small sign the combination is a Roche priority.
- New voices: the Chief Scientific Officer (Utpal Singh, ex-Lilly) now speaks on every call and the platform narrative is his; investor relations changed hands (Eric Rojas replaced Adam Lange in 2026). The scientific voice talks of "polypharmacology" and China access - a broader, more expensive ambition.
- Management now says the rare-disease assets will be licensed, not commercialized - a quiet retreat from building a commercial organization.
- "Without relying on dilutive funding" was added to the Q3 2026 framing - reassurance that suggests investors have asked.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict

Trajectory: **PIVOTING** - from a partnership-milestone company to a platform research company, funded by a cash pile that today exceeds the market value of the equity net of liabilities. The single most important thing the director must weigh: the stock is a claim on about DKK 230 a share of net cash and receivables that management intends to spend, not return. The value case works only if (a) petrelintide earns a real share of the amylin market despite trailing Lilly on efficacy, or (b) management keeps returning surplus cash as it did in 2026. The buyback is the best evidence for (b).

**Moat.** Type: intangible (patented peptide molecules and 25 years of peptide know-how), validated by two big-pharma partners. Width: narrow - there are no product earnings, returns on capital are negative, and the tolerability edge looks like a property of the amylin class that Lilly and Novo share. Trend: stable - the patent estate and partner terms are unchanged; the competitive position neither widened nor collapsed in 2026.

**Secular threat.** None of the listed structural forces (AI displacement, disintermediation, reimbursement compression and so on) threatens the terminal value directly. The real risk is competitive and clinical - Lilly's and Novo's amylin programs and price competition in obesity - which is manageable, not terminal. The cheapness is a fear print around below-target data, not a structurally shrinking base, but the cash cushion is being consumed by design.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# NewPrinces S.p.A. (NWL.MI, formerly Newlat Food) — Forensic Dossier (2026-11-09)

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript was available: the FMP transcript and news endpoints return nothing for this Milan listing, the Quartr connector requires a subscription this account does not have, and this run's web-search budget was exhausted before a search could run (the company IR page answered HTTP 429). This dossier is therefore built from FMP's structured statements (annual 2024-2025, quarterly Q3-2025 to Q2-2026), the live quote, the screener metrics block and the peer file. No management quotes appear below because none could be sourced; nothing is invented. Facts about the deal history that come from our background knowledge and could not be re-checked this run are labelled as such.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The company has turned from a mid-sized Italian dairy and pasta maker (Newlat Food, about EUR 0.56B revenue in 2021) into a roll-up of food brands and, more recently, grocery retail. The financial record shows the steps: revenue of EUR 741M (2022) and EUR 793M (2023), then EUR 1.64B (2024), EUR 2.96B (2025), and about EUR 3.04B in the first half of 2026 alone (Q1 EUR 1.50B, Q2 EUR 1.54B). The company renamed itself NewPrinces in May 2025 (FMP profile) after combining with the UK canned-food group Princes, part of which now trades separately in London (PRN.L appears in the peer file, and the balance sheet carries EUR 175M of minority interests at 2026-06-30). The jump in half-year revenue to roughly a EUR 6B annual pace, together with EUR 1.40B of trade payables, matches our background understanding that the group bought Carrefour's Italian supermarket business (announced in July 2025; not re-verified this run). The story has moved from "cheap branded food compounder" to "turnaround of a large, low-margin grocery chain financed largely by its suppliers".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
The screener's headline cheapness does not survive a look at where the profit came from.

| Headline claim (screener) | What the statements show |
|---|---|
| EPS 8.71 for 2025, up 142% | FY2025 net income of EUR 410M includes EUR 308M of non-cash items deducted in the cash-flow statement, and Q4-2025 alone booked a EUR 262M "other" gain. That pattern fits a bargain-purchase gain (buying a business for less than its book value) on an acquisition. Underlying 2025 net income is closer to EUR 100M, about EUR 2.30 a share. |
| Price-to-free-cash-flow 2.6x | 2025 free cash flow of EUR 398M includes EUR 368M of working-capital inflow, mostly from taking on a retailer's supplier credit. Excluding that, free cash flow was about EUR 30M. That is a one-off float, not repeatable earning power. |
| Net margin 12.7%, ROE 22.6% | First half of 2026: a net loss of about EUR 11M (Q1 -EUR 24.2M, Q2 +EUR 13.1M) on EUR 3.04B revenue. Operating income was about EUR 20M, a margin of roughly 0.6%. |
| Net debt EUR 328M | At 2026-06-30: EUR 1.31B cash and short-term investments against EUR 1.29B of financial debt and EUR 381M of leases. FMP's net debt figure is EUR 402M including leases. The cash is largely owed to suppliers (EUR 1.40B of payables), so it is not spare cash. |
| Revenue growth +80% | Almost entirely acquired. No organic growth figure can be checked without the transcript. |

Retained earnings were negative EUR 11M at 2026-06-30, and Altman-Z (a bankruptcy-risk score) is 1.7, which sits in the grey zone.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
This cannot be assessed: no transcript. Rating: not rated. The share price speaks for the market's tone. It is at a 52-week high of EUR 26.30, up 8.9% on 2026-11-09 on about 3x average volume, three days before results. The reason for the move could not be verified.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
No guidance history could be sourced. The record shows the group delivered on making acquisitions, and that each one came with an accounting gain at purchase. Reliability: unscored (Low confidence by default, for lack of evidence).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
These come from the numbers, not from calls. (a) What is the stand-alone profitability of the retail chain, and how long will the turnaround take? (b) How much of the cash is supplier float, and what happens to it if payment terms normalise? (c) How do the minorities in Princes shrink the value left for NWL shareholders? (d) What do related-party flows with the controlling shareholder (Newlat Group S.A., the Mastrolia family) look like? No analyst price-target coverage could be found or verified.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- RED: Reported 2025 earnings are mostly a one-off acquisition gain (Q4-2025, about EUR 262M).
- RED: First half of 2026 shows a net loss and an operating margin below 1% on about EUR 3B of sales.
- RED: Liquidity depends on supplier credit (EUR 1.40B of payables against EUR 0.83B of inventory).
- RED: Complex structure. It is a controlled company, holds a listed subsidiary with minorities, and has negative retained earnings.
- GREEN: Q2-2026 returned to an operating profit (EUR 21M) after a Q1 operating loss. The direction is right.
- GREEN: The food businesses held gross margin through the 2021-22 inflation (17.1% to 18.0%). Branded staples pass costs on.
- GREEN: Gross cash of EUR 1.27B removes any near-term refinancing risk.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The rename to NewPrinces and the separate London listing of Princes point to a family holding that uses the listed company as a deal vehicle. Value may move between entities, and minorities are not the decision-makers. The weighted share count rose from about 43.9M to 46.6M in Q2-2026, so some share issuance happened. Capex rose from EUR 26M (2024) to EUR 197M (2025), which marks a shift from a light food business to a capital-heavy retail one.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: PIVOTING. The group is turning from a branded food maker into a food-plus-grocery-retail conglomerate. **The most important thing to weigh:** the screener sees EPS 8.71 and price-to-FCF 2.6x, but both come from a one-off purchase gain and a one-off working-capital float. The true run-rate is near break-even net income on about EUR 6B of sales. The case rests entirely on whether management can lift the retail chain's margin. That will show up in the Q3-2026 results (due about 2026-11-12) and the FY2026 results, not in the trailing numbers.

Moat: scale-cost and intangible-brand moats in the food brands are narrow but real (Napolina, Princes, Mukki and Centrale del Latte hold local leadership). Grocery retail has no moat. Group ROIC of 6.6% is below the cost of capital. Secular threat: Italian hypermarkets keep losing share to discounters, so the retail channel-shift threat is material for the acquired chain but manageable at group level. The cheapness is partly an accounting mirage rather than a pure fear-print.

Management credibility 2 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Otello is a debt-free wrapper around about 38% of Bemobi, a Brazilian recurring-bill and payments company. Bemobi grew adjusted revenue 22% in 3Q25 and 35% in 1Q26 (with the Paytime acquisition), runs at a roughly 33% EBITDA margin (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation), buys back its own shares and pays regular distributions. After a 26% one-day fall on 2026-10-26, which press reports put down to a sell-off in Brazilian small caps as long-term yields rose rather than to company news, Bemobi trades at roughly 8x our estimate of 2026 earnings. If Bemobi merely recovers to the high-20s reais, nearer an undated Itau BBA target of R$27, while Otello keeps its net cash and its costs low, Otello's value per share rises to the low-20s kroner. Leblon Equities was reported (Valor, 2026-10-28) buying Bemobi after the fall.
picks.bear_thesis: Otello is now a near-pure, unhedged bet on one Brazilian small cap and on the Brazilian real, and it carries a holding-company cost layer. The gap between Otello's price and the value of its Bemobi stake, which was the original edge, has largely closed (from about 32% to about 13%). It closed because the asset fell, not because Otello was re-rated. A 26% one-day drop with no company announcement found is unusual for a pure sector move, and we could not rule out a company-specific cause. Brazil's high interest rates, a December US rate-hike risk and a weak real could push Bemobi back to its R$21 year low or below. Otello has no dated plan to sell or distribute the stake, so nothing forces the gap to close. Its own earnings are near zero and its trailing free cash flow is slightly negative.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: a value buyer might see a 20% drop and call Otello cheaper. In fact the gap to its holdings has narrowed, from about 32% to about 13%, because Bemobi fell more than Otello did. The bargain has moved from Otello's discount to Bemobi itself, which trades at about 8x earnings, and that is a call on Brazilian interest rates rather than an edge specific to Otello.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is now to January 2027: Bemobi's 3Q26 results (estimated mid-November, unconfirmed), the US Federal Reserve's 8-9 December meeting (a rate hike is about 85% priced in) and the path of Brazilian rates. More selling in Brazilian small caps would hit Otello at roughly 0.9x Bemobi's moves.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure: the 26 October Bemobi drop came on about 2.0 million shares, against normal volume of 0.5-0.8 million, consistent with funds unwinding bets on falling rates. Otello traded 578k shares that day, against a typical 100-200k. Some of this is a wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers), and Leblon Equities was reported buying Bemobi afterwards.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near 16.0 kroner, which the sector-wide sell-off in Brazilian small caps could deliver. The thesis holds: Otello is still a debt-free holding company that owns about 38% of a growing Brazilian payments business. What changed is the price of that business, which fell 26% in a single day on 2026-10-26. That cut Otello's holdings to about 19.9 kroner per share and closed most of the gap that was our edge. After head-office costs and a single-asset discount, fair value is about 19.3 kroner, only about 12% above today's 17.24 kroner and short of the 20% bar. At 16.0 kroner the gap clears that bar. Bemobi at about 8x earnings looks cheap, but owning Otello is now mostly a bet on Brazilian rates, so we wait rather than chase.
picks.forcing_function: Nothing contractual. The catalyst would be a re-rating of Bemobi on its own results, or Otello acting to close the gap with a buyback, a distribution in kind or a sale of the stake. No such action has been announced.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# OTEC.OL — Otello Corporation ASA: a deep dive on management and the setup (2026-11-03)

Prices: Otello 17.24 kroner (Oslo, FMP quote, 2026-11-02 close). Bemobi (BMOB3, São Paulo) R$23.51 (2026-10-30 close). FX: 1 BRL = 1.7095 NOK (FMP, USD/NOK 9.294 / USD/BRL 5.437). Otello reports in US dollars. No earnings-call transcript was found; this dossier rests on the FMP balance sheet, FMP price history, a Quartr summary of the first-half 2026 report and dated press coverage. The web-search budget ran out partway through, so Bemobi's third-quarter 2026 results date and any company filing behind the 26 October drop could not be checked.

## 1. What the company actually is
Otello, the former Opera Software, is now a holding company. Its only material asset is a stake of about 38.2% (Quartr H1-2026 summary; Investing.com lists 38.55%) in Bemobi Mobile Tech, a listed Brazilian company that collects recurring bills (utilities, telecoms, education) and processes payments. The 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows the Bemobi stake carried at USD 122.2M, cash of USD 10.6M, no debt, and USD 2.6M of other liabilities. The screener's zero revenue and negative ROIC (return on invested capital) are simply what a holding company that books Bemobi by the equity method looks like. They are not an operating failure.

## 2. Earnings quality
First-half 2026 net income was USD 2.2M, well below the first half of 2025, which had one-off gains (Quartr). Trailing free cash flow is about -USD 0.7M: the holding company burns a little cash on head-office costs. Reported earnings per share swing with one-off items, so we value Otello on what it holds, not on its earnings.

## 3. Balance sheet and solvency
The holding company has no debt. Net cash after other liabilities is about USD 8.0M (74 million kroner, roughly 1.09 kroner per share). The Altman Z-score of 29 (a measure of bankruptcy risk) is meaningless here except to confirm there is no solvency risk. Treasury shares of USD 9.6M show past buybacks.

## 4. The underlying asset (Bemobi)
- 3Q25 (reported 2025-11-13): adjusted revenue R$187.5M (+22.3%), adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) R$62.7M (33.4% margin), adjusted net income R$46.8M (+88.7%).
- 4Q25: net income about R$61M (+31%, Guia do Investidor).
- 1Q26: revenue +35% year on year, helped by the Paytime acquisition (Investing.com summary).
- Bemobi runs a share buyback and pays interest-on-capital distributions (ex-date 18 August 2026). Itaú BBA has a buy rating with a R$27 year-end-2026 target, but the source is undated, so we use it only as context.
- At R$23.51 Bemobi's market value is about R$1.96B. That is roughly 8x our estimate of 2026 earnings (about R$240-260M, run-rate from 4Q25 plus growth), which is cheap for a business growing 20%+.

## 5. What changed since 2026-10-12 (dated)
- Bemobi rallied to R$34.55 on 2026-10-09 and R$33.85 on 2026-10-23, then **fell 26.0% on 2026-10-26** (R$25.04) and closed at R$23.51 on 2026-10-30.
- Otello followed it down: 22.55 kroner on 2026-10-23, then 18.50 kroner on 10-26 and 17.10 kroner on 10-30.
- The only explanation we found (Ad-hoc-News, citing Valor International on 2026-10-28) calls it a broad sell-off in Brazilian small caps: traders unwound bets on lower interest rates as long-term yields rose. That article reports no company announcement, and says Leblon Equities bought after the fall. **Caveat:** a 26% one-day drop in a single stock is extreme for a sector move. With the search budget gone, we could not rule out a company-specific trigger.
- 2026-10-14: SPX Gestão cut its Bemobi holding to 0.28%. This is a small, routine filing.

## 6. The look-through discount (the gap between Otello's price and the value of what it owns)
Bemobi stake: 38.4% × R$1.961B = R$753M = 1,288 million kroner, or 18.83 kroner per Otello share (68.37M shares). Add net cash of 1.09 kroner and the look-through NAV (net asset value) is about **19.9 kroner**. At 17.24 kroner, Otello trades about 13% below its NAV. On 2026-10-12 the gap was about 32% (NAV 31.4 kroner against a 21.40 kroner price). The wrapper discount has largely closed, because the asset fell rather than because Otello rose. Running costs of about USD 2-2.5M a year, valued at roughly 2 kroner per share, take up most of the remaining 13%.

## 7. Governance and management
Management is a small team that has historically returned capital through buybacks and special distributions (the Opera-era asset sales). The board says it remains positive on Bemobi's shift to payments (H1-2026 report). There is no stated plan to sell or distribute the stake, and no dated monetisation event exists. Insider buying in the screen is zero.

## 8. Red flags and open questions
- Otello now holds a single asset that trades at the mercy of Brazilian interest rates and the Brazilian real.
- The cause of the 26% drop is unverified.
- The inflation-resilience label "exposed" is an artefact of the holding company's near-zero revenue (a -6,600% "gross margin"). It says nothing about the business.
- The analyst target could not be dated, and the Bemobi 3Q26 results date is unconfirmed (3Q25 was reported on 2025-11-13).
- The "38.2% vs 38.55%" stake figure differs by source.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady.

picks.bull_thesis: Boyd Gaming is a disciplined regional casino operator trading near 11 times underlying earnings (about $6.6 of trailing twelve-month EPS, excluding the 2025 FanDuel gain, at $72.21). Its property margins have held near 38-40% for years (Midwest and South adjusted margin 38% in Q3 2026, 'consistent with our third quarter margins over the last several years'), it kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation, and the share count has fallen about 10% in a year (73.0M diluted shares in Q3 2026 vs 80.9M a year earlier). The core customer is healthy: excluding the Orleans and the Suncoast construction, Las Vegas Locals grew revenue and EBITDAR 3% in Q3 2026, backed by Southern Nevada wage growth near 6% and population growth twice the national rate. A visible pipeline adds earnings from 2027: the Norfolk, Virginia resort ('on time and on budget for a November 2027 opening'), the Suncoast and Orleans renovations finishing by early 2027, Par-A-Dice, and Sky River management fees that grew 13% in Q3 2026. If Las Vegas visitor traffic simply stops falling and Norfolk opens on time, a flat-to-growing EBITDAR base of roughly $1.33B with a shrinking share count supports a value in the low-to-mid $90s, and a re-rating toward peer multiples gives $110+. The conditions: margins hold, Norfolk opens on schedule, and the buyback is paced to free cash flow rather than debt.
picks.bear_thesis: The operating business is not growing. Reported Q3 2026 revenue ($990M) and adjusted EBITDAR ($319.6M) both fell about 1%, and the positive figures need management's adjustments for a closure, an asset sale, property taxes and tax pass-throughs. Las Vegas Locals EBITDAR fell 5% and Downtown 20% year on year, and the visitor softness management called near a turn in October 2025 ('much more positive than it was 3 months ago') has widened instead. Meanwhile buybacks run at $150M+ a quarter while trailing free cash flow was only $35M to 2026-06-30 (depressed by the roughly $360M FanDuel tax payment, but even normalized only about $250-300M a year after a $550-600M building program), so long-term debt has climbed from $2.27B in March to about $2.7B in September. That is a flat earnings base being levered up to shrink the share count, two years before the projects that are supposed to grow it open. Insiders sold 700,000 shares on the open market with no buys. The fiscal-2025 EPS of $22.56 and the screener's 487% margin of safety are artifacts of the one-off FanDuel gain. A consumer slowdown, more Las Vegas weakness, or a Norfolk delay would leave a regional casino at 6x EBITDAR worth the mid-$60s, with debt rising.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is not looking the wrong way. The consensus target is $87.70 (median $84, range $80-103), with five targets refreshed on 2026-10-23 after the print (Truist $95, Mizuho $103, Barclays $83, CBRE $85, Stifel $80). Analysts model a steady regional operator with modest growth (consensus forward EPS growth about 8%), which matches what management delivered. Where our view differs is on quality of the per-share growth, not on the level: the street credits the buyback without discounting that it is now partly funded with debt while EBITDAR is flat, and the post-print targets still assume the Las Vegas visitor softness turns, which management has predicted since October 2025 without it happening. The screener's headline margin of safety (487%) is not a disagreement with the market; it is the FanDuel one-off gain inflating 2025 earnings.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) holds no liquidity threat: total debt of about $2.7B against roughly $1.3B of annual EBITDAR is manageable, there is no near-term maturity wall in the materials, and the dividend is small. The risk is a slow grind: Q4 2026 and the first half of 2027 carry the Orleans room remodel (from early 2027) and the Suncoast room remodel (through Q1 2027), continued visitor softness in Las Vegas and Downtown, Hawaiian airfare pressure, and capital spending of roughly $140-155M a quarter for Norfolk ahead of any return. If buybacks keep running at $150M+ a quarter, leverage rises each quarter with no new earnings until November 2027. A consumer slowdown in a sticky-inflation backdrop would hit a flat base.
picks.positioning_washout: No forced-selling pressure is visible. Boyd has no index-deletion, lock-up or dividend-cut setup, and its holders are mostly long-only and value funds. Insider selling (23 open-market sales, about 700,000 shares, no buys) is a weak negative signal rather than a forced seller. Gaming stocks sold off broadly in Q3 2026 (a fund letter dated 2026-10-26 cites 'broad weakness in gaming stocks'), and the stock sits 12% below its 200-day average and about 25% up its 52-week range ($65-$91.41), so the sector selling has largely happened already.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. The thesis holds: Boyd Gaming is a steady, honestly run regional casino operator whose margins have stayed near 38% for years and whose share count has fallen about 10% in a year. Our base-case fair value is about $92 a share, a little above the street's $87.70, against a price of $72.21. We still pass, as this committee did on 2026-10-12, and the reason is the quality of the per-share growth, not the price. The third-quarter results on 2026-10-22 were the only new dated fact, and they confirmed the problem rather than fixing it: operating earnings were flat to down (adjusted EBITDAR $319.6M against $321.8M), Las Vegas Locals fell 5% and Downtown 20%, and the buyback is now partly paid for with new debt (total debt about $2.7B, up from $2.27B in March) while the projects that are meant to grow earnings open in late 2027 and 2028. Insiders have been selling, not buying. That is a flat business being levered up to shrink its share count, which is not the clean value case this book wants. What would change our answer: Las Vegas segment earnings growing again, or the buyback being paced to free cash flow with leverage stable, either of which we can check at the early-2027 results. Until then, Boyd is a fairly priced, decent business, not a buy.
picks.forcing_function: Nothing forces a re-rating in the next year. The buyback ($150M a quarter, $387M left at 2026-09-30) supports the share price but is already known. The real re-rating events are the Norfolk resort opening in November 2027 and a turn in Las Vegas visitor business, neither dated within our horizon in a way that would make it a catalyst. Next results are due in early February 2027 (about 103 days out).
