picks.bull_thesis:
Kogeneracja supplies district heating - hot water piped to buildings - and electricity to Wroclaw, a Polish city of about 640,000 people, from plants that make both at once (combined heat and power). At 84.20 zloty the whole company is valued at about 1.25 billion zloty. Over the twelve months to 30 June 2026 it earned about 334 million zloty of net profit (about 22.4 zloty a share) and generated 401 million zloty of free cash flow (cash left after capital spending): about 3.8 times earnings, 3.1 times free cash flow and 0.45 times the 188 zloty of book value (accounting net assets) per share.

The earnings step-up has a specific, finished cause. The 179-megawatt Czechnica-2 gas unit, a roughly 1.4 billion zloty project, was launched on 29 May 2025. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA, a proxy for operating cash earnings) rose from 485 million zloty in 2024 to about 718 million over the twelve months to June 2026, while quarterly capital spending has run below depreciation for three reported quarters. On 29 June 2026 the company also won contracted cogeneration support for its EC Wroclaw gas engines, so part of its revenue is no longer exposed to the power market.

The reporting is clean: a Piotroski score of 8 out of 9 (a nine-point accounting-health checklist) and results pre-announced to the decimal four times running. The June 2026 dividend of 2.58 zloty, the first since the 2021 year, shows the payout channel is open. If PGE, the 58% parent, lifts the payout at the 2027 meeting - the argument for retaining cash to build the plant has expired - or buys out the 42% it does not own, the shares re-rate toward book value.
picks.bear_thesis:
The earnings are real; the problem is that a minority shareholder cannot reach them, and nothing since 12 October has changed that.

At 30 June 2026 Kogeneracja held 16.1 million zloty of cash and 1,349.9 million zloty of 'other receivables' - more than its whole market value - most plausibly a cash-pool balance swept to the parent and lent back on the group's terms. PGE owns 58.06% and decides. On 28 May 2026 a minority pension fund asked for 6.71 zloty a share; the 11 June meeting gave 2.58 zloty, about 14% of profit, and the fund fell below 5% on 2 July.

The earnings are also flattered by a good moment. The June 2026 quarter swung to a 6.2 million zloty loss with gross profit down from 37.1 to 20.8 million. The heat tariff is cost-plus, so a supplier whose winter gross margin rose from 21.7% to 28.0% will share that gain at the next reset; the remaining coal units face rising carbon costs, and the announced full exit from coal plus the boiler tenders now under way mean a second spending wave that competes with dividends.

And the price has done the work: the shares rose from 78.50 zloty on 12 October to 87.90 at the high and 84.20 now with no announcement at all. At 84.20 the stock sits slightly above our base-case fair value of 82, so a buyer today is paying for the favourable case. A thin float - about 19% - cuts both ways when the flows reverse.
picks.consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the question is whether the market prices terminal decline into a business with stable or growing earnings power. Here it does not: it prices a governance discount, and at 84.20 zloty it prices it about where we do. There is no published analyst coverage, so there is no consensus forecast to be wrong. Where we disagree is narrow. First, the market may treat the post-project earnings partly as a windfall; capital spending below depreciation says at least half is structural, because the regulator can reset a tariff but cannot un-spend the build or un-award the June 2026 cogeneration support. Second, book value per share keeps compounding (about 188 zloty at 30 June 2026). Where the market may now be ahead of us: the shares rose about 7% since 12 October, touching 87.90, with no new fact; at today's price the market is giving more credit for a payout change than PGE's conduct so far supports.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) holds one near-certain soft spot and two probable ones; none is a solvency event. First, the September 2026 quarter, due in late November 2026, is structurally loss-making for a heat supplier (minus 15.0 million zloty a year earlier), and the June quarter's trough ran weaker than last year. Buyers who arrived on a low trailing multiple during the October run-up will read two loss quarters in a row and can sell into a float this thin. Second, the next heat-tariff decision: a supplier whose winter gross margin rose from 21.7% to 28.0% invites a harder look, and the reset date could not be sourced. Third, carbon and fuel, plus the coal-exit spending now being tendered. Not a risk: refinancing - total debt including leases of about 385 million zloty against about 718 million of twelve-month EBITDA, and interest income exceeds interest expense.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure here is slow, structural and real. PGE holds 58.06%; most of the rest sits with Polish open pension funds, which are structural net sellers of Warsaw small caps as members near retirement and assets transfer out of the system, regardless of valuation - and Nationale-Nederlanden's fund already fell below 5% on 2 July 2026 after its dividend request was cut. With normal daily turnover of a few thousand shares, unwinding even 1% of the company (about 149,000 shares) takes weeks and cannot clear without a price concession. That is the seller that could take the price back to our 66 zloty level - a wash-out, a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers. The level is not hypothetical: the shares traded at 59.40 within the last year and around 67 in August 2026. The 2 November session (20,296 shares, closing 3.2% lower after touching 81.20) shows how fast flows move this float in both directions.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 66 zloty, which the forced selling of Polish pension funds - holders who must sell regardless of value - could deliver.

The thesis holds. A 1.4 billion zloty gas unit launched on 29 May 2025 lifted twelve-month EBITDA to about 718 million zloty by June 2026, capital spending has run below depreciation for three quarters, twelve-month free cash flow is 401 million zloty, and the accounts score 8 out of 9 on the Piotroski checklist. At 84.20 zloty you pay about 3.8 times earnings and 0.45 times book.

But the price already reflects what a minority holder can reach - and since our 12 October look it has risen further with no news. PGE owns 58.06%, approved a 2.58 zloty dividend on 11 June 2026 (about 14% of profit) against a 6.71 zloty request, and at 30 June 2026 the company held 16.1 million zloty of cash against 1.35 billion zloty of group receivables. Valuing the heat franchise and generation separately and deducting 369 million zloty of net debt gives about 118 zloty a share before access; a 30% discount for a controlled entity that keeps its cash gives a fair value of 82 zloty, an adverse case of 36 and a favourable case of 145. At 84.20 the stock trades slightly above fair value; the required entry discount is cleared near 66 zloty, a level it traded around as recently as August 2026.

Nothing dated has changed since 12 October 2026 - the company has published nothing since its 8 September half-year report - so the answer is unchanged: a real, cleanly reported business at a governance-shaped discount, a soft catalyst with no fixed date in the 2027 annual meeting, and a hard cap on position size from a 19% float. Conviction stays at 3.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating - has no hard date. The scheduled decision point is the 2027 annual meeting, expected around June 2027, where PGE votes 58.06% on the 2026 profit; with the main build finished, a payout of 5 zloty or more would change the story, while the coal-exit spending gives PGE a reason to keep retaining. Unscheduled possibilities: a buy-out offer from PGE for the minority (nothing announced), a heat-tariff decision that confirms rather than resets the improved margin, or disclosure that the group receivable is an interest-bearing loan being repaid. None depends on interest-rate cuts, oil or artificial-intelligence spending - good driver independence - but all depend on a third party choosing to act.

*As of 2 November 2026. Price used: 84.20 zloty (PLN) on the Warsaw exchange (live quote from the paid data feed, 2 November 2026; previous close 87.00, 52-week range 59.40-87.90). All figures in zloty.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists in the paid data feed for this listing, and Kogeneracja - a Polish subsidiary of the state-controlled PGE group - does not hold English-language analyst calls. This dossier tests management's actions and public statements (results pre-announcements, the annual-meeting dividend decision, capital spending, regulatory filings) against the reported quarterly statements pulled from the paid feed on 2 November 2026. The paid news feed carries no item for this ticker since 1 October 2026. The company's own announcement list (bankier.pl, checked 2 November 2026) shows nothing after the half-year report of 8 September 2026, and the biznesradar.pl news page shows no company-specific item since then either. The web-search allowance for this run ran out after two searches, so a deeper Polish-language press check was not possible. No quotes are invented below.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story over the last two years has one spine: build gas-fired replacements for coal, switch them on, and harvest the cash. The 179-megawatt Czechnica-2 gas unit (roughly 1.4 billion zloty of investment) was launched on 29 May 2025. Through 2024 and the first half of 2025 the narrative was about spending; since the September 2025 quarter it has been about earnings. In the regulator's cogeneration-premium auction held 22-24 June 2026 the company entered its AK6-10 gas engines at EC Wroclaw (49.9 megawatts of electricity, 50 megawatts of heat) and won support (result announced 29 June 2026) - a correction to our earlier notes, which attached that premium to Czechnica-2. Company material also describes a full exit from coal across its three Wroclaw-area plants (418 megawatts of electricity and 1,080 megawatts of heat in total), and public tenders show gas- and electricity-fired water boilers being procured.

What has not changed is who decides where the cash goes. PGE owns 58.06%. The 11 June 2026 annual meeting approved a dividend of 2.58 zloty a share (about 14% of the 277 million zloty 2025 profit) - the first since the 2021 year - after a minority pension fund had asked for 6.71 zloty. For a minority shareholder the arc is: the earnings arrived, the cash mostly did not.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / action | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The new gas unit lifts earnings | Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) over the twelve months to 30 June 2026 were about 718 million zloty, against 485 million in 2024 | Matches |
| The capital programme is over | Quarterly capital spending of 39.2, 45.6 and 33.7 million in the last three reported quarters, below quarterly depreciation of 61-67 million | Matches - but the coal-exit plan and boiler tenders mean a second, smaller spending wave is coming |
| Results pre-announced accurately | Q1 2026 pre-announced at about 213 million, delivered 213.1 million; 2025 at about 277 million, delivered 277.0 million | Matches |
| Free cash flow is real | Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow 401 million zloty | Matches, but lumpy and seasonal |
| Cash belongs to shareholders | Cash of 16.1 million zloty at 30 June 2026 against 1,349.9 million of "other receivables" (most plausibly a group cash-pool balance with PGE) | Diverges |

The June 2026 quarter showed revenue of 471.6 million zloty (up 5.7%), gross profit down to 20.8 million from 37.1 million, EBITDA flat at 67.0 million and a net loss of 6.2 million zloty. That is the normal summer trough for a heat supplier, slightly weaker than last year. The September 2026 quarter, due in late November 2026, will also be seasonally weak (a 15.0 million zloty loss a year earlier).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable. Without calls, tone is read from conduct: management pre-announces winter-quarter results weeks early and to the decimal, and the June 2026 dividend - small as it is - was the first in four years. No guidance has been withdrawn and nothing defensive has been published since the half-year report of 8 September 2026.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High. The company does not issue forward guidance in the usual sense, but its results pre-announcements have matched the final numbers four times running. No evidence of sandbagging or misses.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

No sell-side price target exists in the paid feed for this listing, and none was found on Polish market-data sites. The pressure comes from shareholders: the pension fund that asked on 28 May 2026 for 6.71 zloty got 2.58 and cut its stake below 5% on 2 July 2026. The unanswered question remains what the 1.35 billion zloty receivable is, what rate it earns, and whether it is callable.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 (Q2 2026) net loss of 6.2 million zloty and negative operating cash flow in the summer quarter, worse than a year earlier at the gross-profit line.
- 🔴 (30 June 2026) 1,349.9 million zloty of other receivables against 16.1 million of cash - more than the company's market value, held where a minority holder cannot reach it.
- 🔴 (11 June 2026) a payout of about 14% of profit with the main build finished.
- 🔴 (October 2026) the shares rose from 78.50 to a 52-week high of 87.90 with no company announcement - the discount closed on flows, not news.
- 🟢 capital spending below depreciation for three straight reported quarters.
- 🟢 (29 June 2026) contracted cogeneration premium won for the EC Wroclaw gas engines.
- 🟢 Piotroski score of 8 out of 9 (a nine-point accounting-health checklist) and accurate pre-announcements.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

Book value per share keeps compounding - about 188 zloty at 30 June 2026 - so retained profit is kept, not lost. Interest income (13.9 million zloty in the June quarter) is double interest expense (6.7 million), consistent with the receivable being an interest-bearing group loan. Turnover on 2 November 2026 was 20,296 shares, roughly seven times the 2,845 shares of 12 October - unusually heavy for a 19% free float, and the day closed 3.2% lower after touching 81.20. The supply side drives this stock.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: strengthening at the operating level, unchanged at the shareholder level. The single thing to weigh: the value is real but controlled - PGE decides the payout and holds the cash. Size this as an access problem, not an earnings problem, and note that at 84.20 zloty the price already sits slightly above our base-case fair value.

Moat: a regulatory-licence moat - the licensed district-heating supplier to Wroclaw (about 640,000 people), with cost-plus tariffs. Narrow (returns on invested capital of about 6% on the screener's measure, about 11-12% on our post-project EBITDA basis - at or slightly above a Polish cost of capital) and stable. The secular threat is material, not terminal: the remaining coal units face rising carbon costs as free allowances for district heating phase down toward 2030, but dense-city district heat is not being displaced and the gas units are the transition answer. The cheapness is a governance and liquidity discount, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

picks.bull_thesis: MPC Container Ships rents small and mid-sized container ships to the big shipping lines on fixed-rate, multi-year contracts, and it has locked in more future business than at any point since it was founded in 2017. On the Q2 2026 call (2026-08-26) management reported a $2.2 billion contracted revenue backlog, worth about $1.4 billion of projected EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization), with about 99% of 2026 days, 85% of 2027, 60% of 2028 and about 40% of 2029 already chartered, at forward rates in the mid-$25,000s per day and rising slightly. That backlog alone covers most of today's market value of roughly $1.27 billion (NOK 11.9 billion at NOK 24.44, about 488 million shares after the placement). The balance sheet is strong: at 2026-06-30 debt was $439M against $417M of cash and short-term investments, 30 ships worth about $770M carry no debt, and the stated leverage ratio is 28.4%. The fleet has been renewed from an average 2007 build year to 2016 and is 78% eco tonnage, which both earns better charters and survives tightening emissions rules. Charter markets were firm: forward availability down 11% year on year, ships fixed about six months before expiry (a record), and a seven-ship Maersk package for 2027 signed after the quarter. The four 2023-24-built 7,000 TEU ships bought for about $340M come with 3-year charters that cover more than 40% of the price. Earnings are cheap: underlying profit of about $40M a quarter plus the new ships puts the stock near 6-7 times earnings, and the dividend (19 consecutive payments, $0.04 per quarter) yields about 6%. If the Red Sea and congestion distortions persist and asset values hold, the market will pay closer to full net asset value plus a premium for contracted cash, which supports the high end of our range. The business also passed through the 2021-22 inflation with gross margin rising from 17% to 62%, so it is not hurt by sticky inflation.
picks.bear_thesis: The numbers are past their peak and still falling. Revenue fell from $711M (2023) to $518M (2025), earnings per share fell about 18.5% a year over three years, and Q2 2026 EBITDA of $65.0M was about 41% below the $109.8M of Q2 2025. Q2 2026 net income of $69.4M flatters the run-rate because about $30M was non-operating, most likely ship-sale gains. Management is buying ships at what it admits are multi-year-high asset prices (newbuilding prices the strongest since 2008) and issued about 10% more shares to do it; the discount it claims is measured against newbuilding parity, which is itself inflated. The order book in the 6,000-8,000 TEU segment roughly tripled this year to over 30% of the fleet - exactly where MPCC just bought. Management itself says today's tightness is partly structural distortion: Red Sea and Hormuz rerouting add about 12% to TEU-miles and congestion ties up about 5% of capacity. If the Red Sea reopens, that capacity floods back at the same time as the newbuild wave, charter rates fall and second-hand values drop 25-40%, as they did in 2023. The backlog protects about three years of cash, but most of the value beyond it is the ships' residual value, which would be marked down. Underlying growth is negative and net debt rises to roughly $200-260M once the four-ship purchase is paid. The stock has already fallen from about NOK 27.85 (50-day average) to NOK 24.44 for reasons we could not verify this run. A Q2 2026 call figure of $170M for operating revenue does not reconcile with the $116.9M reported, a small forensic loose end. In this case equity value falls toward contracted cash flow less debt plus heavily discounted residual ship values.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is not pricing terminal decline; it is pricing a cyclical peak, and broadly correctly. At NOK 24.44 the stock trades near 1.0x pro forma book equity and about 5x run-rate EBITDA, in line with other ship lessors. Where we partly disagree: the contracted backlog ($2.2B revenue, about $1.4B EBITDA as of August 2026) covers most of the market value by itself, so the equity is less exposed to a charter-rate collapse than a 30-45% sector drawdown would imply over the next two years. Where we agree with the market: the residual value of the ships is priced off near-peak asset values while the 6,000-8,000 TEU order book swells, and management's own call concedes that part of today's tightness is temporary rerouting. We found no dated analyst price targets this run (web search unavailable and our data feed has no price-target coverage for this listing), so we do not quote a street number.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) is about headlines, not cash. 2026 is about 99% chartered and 2027 about 85%, net debt was near zero at 2026-06-30, and there is no maturity wall in sight. The risks over 3-9 months are: (1) a Red Sea or Hormuz de-escalation that releases about 12% of effective capacity and knocks second-hand ship values and lessor share prices across the sector; (2) the Q3 2026 report in late November 2026 showing a further year-on-year fall in EBITDA as old ships leave the fleet; (3) more acquisitions at high asset prices funded with equity. None threatens solvency; all could push the stock toward the low NOK 20s.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited. The shareholder base is yield-oriented and Norwegian-retail heavy; a dividend cut would trigger selling by income holders, but management reaffirmed the dividend range on 2026-08-26 and the backlog funds it. The more likely seller is a sector-wide de-rating of container-ship owners if the Red Sea reopens - that is a factor sell-off, not forced selling - and the August 2026 placement shares (about 44 million) could add supply if those buyers are underwater.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near NOK 23.70, which a sector-wide sell-off in container-ship owners - for example on a Red Sea reopening - could deliver. The thesis holds: the Q2 2026 call (2026-08-26) showed a $2.2 billion contracted backlog, near-full charter cover through 2027, near-zero net debt at quarter end and a 19th straight dividend. But this is a well-run cyclical asset owner at a cyclical high in ship values, not a franchise with a moat, and earnings are falling as boom-era charters roll off (Q2 2026 EBITDA down about 41% year on year). Our base-case value is NOK 28.5 per share, about 17% above today's NOK 24.44 - short of the 20% discount we require in today's backdrop - with an adverse case of NOK 17 if ship values reset. At NOK 23.70 the discount to fair value clears the bar while still sitting well above the adverse case. The backdrop (positive real rates rewarding cash now) suits the business, but it does not change the price discipline. Conviction is moderate: the contracted cash is real, the residual ship value is the swing factor, and the discount to peers is shared sector pricing rather than a company-specific edge. Note: web search was unavailable for this run, so news from September to November 2026 that may explain the recent fall from about NOK 28 is unverified and should be checked at the Q3 2026 report.
picks.forcing_function: No single dated event forces a re-rating. The steady driver is cash: about $65-80M of quarterly EBITDA, regular dividends and ship-sale gains converting the backlog into equity value. Dated checkpoints: the Q3 2026 report (late November 2026), new forward fixtures for the remaining 2027 open days, and the delivery of the four 7,000 TEU ships onto their 3-year charters. A sector shock from a Red Sea reopening is the most likely path to our entry level.

# MPC Container Ships ASA (MPCC.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup

**As of 2026-11-09.** Sources: the Q2 2026 earnings call (2026-08-26, via our licensed data feed - the only transcript read for this note), quarterly statements to 2026-06-30 from the same feed, and the screener's multi-year trajectory. Live quote: NOK 24.44 on the Oslo listing (2026-11-09); the company reports in US dollars (USD/NOK about 9.37). The Q3 2026 report is due in roughly 18 days and was not available. Our web-search budget was exhausted for this run, so we could not verify news from September to November 2026; anything that happened in that window is flagged as unverified below.

MPC Container Ships owns small and mid-sized container ships (feeders, roughly 1,000 to 7,000 TEU, where TEU is a twenty-foot container unit) and rents them on fixed-rate time charters (multi-year rental contracts) to the big shipping lines such as Maersk. It does not sell freight; it earns a daily rental rate per ship.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story in the latest call (Q2 2026) is "visibility by design": a contracted revenue backlog of $2.2 billion, charter cover of about 99% of 2026 days, 85% of 2027, 60% of 2028 and 39-40% of 2029, and a fleet that management says it has rebuilt from an average 2007 build year to an average 2016 build year since 2021. The emphasis has moved from harvesting the 2021-22 charter boom (the years of $669M-$711M revenue) to fleet renewal: selling older, less efficient ships, buying modern "eco" tonnage (fuel-efficient designs) at what management calls a 30-45% discount to newbuilding parity, and ordering newbuilds with long charters attached.

New in Q2 2026: a move up in ship size (four 2023-24-built 7,000 TEU ships for about $340M on 3-year charters to a top-five line), a $375M senior secured term loan, and - after quarter end - a $107M private placement of more than 44 million new shares and a seven-ship package with Maersk for charters starting in 2027.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (Q2 2026 call) | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "another solid quarter" | Q2 2026 revenue $116.9M vs $137.9M in Q2 2025 (down about 15%); EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) $65.0M vs $109.8M a year earlier | Solid in absolute terms, but underlying earnings are clearly lower than a year ago as boom-era charters roll off and old ships are sold |
| "$170 million in operating revenues" for the quarter | Reported Q2 2026 revenue in the statements is $116.9M; Q1 + Q2 together are $235.8M | Does not reconcile. Possibly a transcription error or a different definition; treat as unverified |
| "$65 million in adjusted EBITDA" | Statement EBITDA $65.0M | Matches |
| Net debt "actually closer to zero" | 2026-06-30: total debt $439M, cash $316M plus $101M short-term investments; net debt about $22M on that basis ($123M counting cash only) | Matches at quarter end, but before paying for the $340M four-ship purchase. Pro forma for that purchase and the $107M placement, net debt is roughly $200-260M (our estimate) |
| 30 debt-free vessels worth about $770M | Book value of all ships (property, plant and equipment) $1.04B at 2026-06-30 | Plausible; ship values are near multi-year highs, so market value likely exceeds book |
| Backlog $2.2B, about $1.4B of projected EBITDA | Cannot be verified line by line from the statements; consistent with about $65-80M of quarterly EBITDA over 4-5 years | Credible, contractual |
| Q2 profit | Net income $69.4M, of which about $30M is non-operating (most likely gains on ship sales) | Underlying quarterly profit closer to $40M; headline EPS of $0.16 flatters the run-rate |
| 19th consecutive dividend, $0.04 per share | Dividends paid $16.9M in Q2 2026, down from $22.2-22.3M per quarter through Q1 2026 | Payout is lower than in 2025; the yield at NOK 24.44 is roughly 6% annualized |

Multi-year trajectory: revenue $410M (2021) -> $669M (2022) -> $711M (2023) -> $540M (2024) -> $518M (2025); net income peaked at $435M in 2022 and was $237M in 2025. Earnings per share fell 18.5% a year over three years. The business is normalizing down from a once-in-a-generation charter spike; the renewal program is meant to put a floor under that, not to restore the peak.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable to confident (Q2 2026). Management describes the charter market as "very firm", tonnage as scarce, and liners fixing ships "8 to 9 months ahead of expiry". At the same time it hedges openly: the market "remains volatile and hard to predict", and the Iran conflict is named as "the key downside risk". The language is offensive (growth, acquisitions, capital raise) but anchored in contracted cover rather than spot bets. We have only one transcript in hand, so the trend across quarters is inferred from the financials and from management's own retrospective, not from quarter-by-quarter quotes.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management said in Q2 2026 that guidance "updated throughout the summer remains unchanged", with 2026 essentially fully chartered so the only swing factor is gains on ship sales. We do not have the guidance figures themselves and do not cite them. The screener records 7 of 7 quarters meeting or beating expectations, and with roughly 99% of 2026 days under fixed charters the room for a miss is small. Reliability: High, but for a mechanical reason - the revenue is contracted, so delivering it is not much evidence of skill.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Equity raise versus debt capacity (Q2 2026): an analyst asked why the company issued shares rather than borrowing against its debt-free fleet. The answer stressed speed and "investment capacity" for further deals - a growth answer, not a cost-of-capital answer. Raising equity near the top of a strong asset market while buying ships is a pattern worth watching.
- Dividend policy (Q2 2026): asked whether payouts might rise given record visibility, management reaffirmed the existing range and "the upper part of the range" but put growth investment first.
- Sustainability of forward fixing (Q2 2026): management conceded the usual supply-and-demand framework "is certainly not applicable anymore", leaning on disruptions (Red Sea and Hormuz rerouting adding about 12% to TEU-miles, congestion tying up about 5% of capacity, Panama draft limits). That is an admission that today's tightness rests partly on temporary distortions.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Underlying earnings are falling: Q2 2026 EBITDA down about 41% year on year; revenue down about 15%.
- Equity dilution of about 10% (44M+ new shares on about 444M) in Q3 2026 while asset prices are at multi-year highs.
- Buying ships at "multi-year highs" in asset prices (newbuilding prices "strongest since 2008") - the discount is measured against newbuilding parity, which itself is elevated.
- The order book in the 6,000-8,000 TEU segment has "roughly tripled this year to over 30%" (Q2 2026) - exactly the size MPCC just entered.
- A $170M revenue figure in the call that does not match the reported $116.9M.
- The stock has fallen from a 50-day average of about NOK 27.85 to NOK 24.44; the cause in September to November 2026 is unverified (no search available this run).

Green flags:
- Contracted cover of 99%/85%/60%/40% for 2026-2029 with top liners, including a fresh seven-ship Maersk package for 2027.
- Net debt near zero at 2026-06-30 and 30 debt-free ships; leverage ratio stated at 28.4%.
- Fleet modernization is real: average build year about 2016, eco share 78% of ships.
- A consistent record of returning cash: about $1.1B of distributions since 2021 by management's count, and 19 consecutive dividends.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary shifted from spot strength to "visibility", "resilience by design" and "close tonnage counterparts" - the language of a company preparing for a softer market, not one expecting a new boom.
- The move into 7,000 TEU ships widens the business beyond its feeder niche into a segment with a heavy order book; that is a strategic choice that dilutes its specialist positioning.
- The capital raise was framed as refilling "investment capacity" for "more attractive deals" - signalling more acquisitions to come at today's prices.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: PIVOTING - from harvesting boom-era charters toward a younger, larger fleet financed partly with new equity. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: the contracted backlog protects roughly three years of cash flow, but the residual value of the ships - most of the equity value beyond the backlog - is being priced off near-peak asset values while the order book swells and today's tightness depends partly on rerouting that could reverse if the Red Sea reopens.

Moat: none in the classic sense. A ship owner renting standardized tonnage has no switching costs, network effects or pricing power beyond what the cycle gives it; relationships with liners and a modern eco fleet are advantages, not a moat. Returns are high (ROIC 31%) but falling with the cycle, which is cyclical normalization rather than structural erosion. Secular threat: manageable - decarbonization rules penalize older, less efficient ships, but MPCC is actively selling those and its eco share is rising. The cheapness is mostly a cyclical-peak discount, not a terminal-value trap.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · no real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: 3i is a permanent-capital holding company whose NAV has compounded about 24% a year in book value per share over five years, and the latest numbers still show growth. NAV per share went from 3,030p (March 2026) to 3,131p (June) to 3,154p (September 2026), despite a 47p currency loss. The engine is Action, the European non-food discount retailer that makes up about three quarters of the portfolio. Action is still growing EBITDA at about 11% (nine months to P9 2026, +10.7% to 1.73bn EUR, with October accelerating to 1.96bn EUR year to date). It is opening at least 400 stores a year against a white-space estimate of about 7,700 European stores, and it is entering Croatia, Slovenia and Bulgaria, plus the US from 2027. Its scale lets it cut prices on over 1,000 items 'without any material impact on its economic model' (H1 FY27 call), and it is taking share in France per Nielsen data even in a weak consumer market. 3i's own capital allocation is shareholder-friendly. It bought back about 30m shares at about 2,495p, a 21% discount to the September NAV, which adds directly to NAV per share, and it has announced a second programme. It also keeps buying Action from fund investors at its own mark, which validates the 18.5x. Gearing is about 4% (net debt 1.38bn GBP against a 33.8bn GBP portfolio). Action expects about 2.25bn EUR of operating cash in 2026 and is deleveraging fast, so the distributions that fund dividends and buybacks keep coming. If Action's EBITDA grows about 12% over the next 12-18 months at an unchanged multiple, NAV moves into the 3,500-3,650p range, 35-40% above today's price. For that to hold, like-for-likes need to stay positive at 3-5%, the margin needs to hold near 14.7%, and the US entry costs must stay modest.
picks.bear_thesis: 3i is essentially a single-stock bet on Action's valuation multiple, and that multiple is softer than the headline. 3i applies 18.5x to 'LTM run rate EBITDA' of 2.8bn EUR, but Action's reported LTM operating EBITDA at P9 2026 was 2.54bn EUR. The run-rate figure annualises the year's new stores, so on reported earnings the mark is about 20x. That is rich for a retailer whose like-for-likes have fallen from 10.3% (2024) to about 4.9% (2025) to 3.4% (nine months of 2026), and which now has to cut prices on half its fixed range to keep volumes growing. Every turn of multiple is about 165p per 3i share, so a de-rating to 14-15x (where good European discount retailers can trade in a consumer downturn) takes 600-700p off NAV. Management itself describes energy-driven inflation that 'weighed heavily on consumers', the French consumer is weak, diesel and packaging costs are rising, and the US entry is an expensive test of a European format against Walmart, Dollar General and Costco. The rest of the private-equity book grew earnings only in the 'upper mid-single digits' (H1 FY27), down from mid-teens a year earlier. Listed private-equity holding companies routinely trade at 20-35% discounts to NAV, so the market may never close 3i's discount, especially with this much in one asset. Sterling strength against the euro would also cut NAV, since most assets are euro-denominated. The bear case is confirmed by negative like-for-likes at Action, a margin below 14%, or a multiple cut at the March 2027 year-end mark.
picks.consensus_delta: Is the market pricing decline into a company whose earnings power is still growing? Partly. At 2,582p the market pays about 82% of a NAV that has just reached a record 3,154p. In effect, it assumes either that Action's 18.5x mark is too high or that the discount to NAV is permanent. We agree that the mark is generous: it rests on run-rate EBITDA (2.8bn EUR) about 10% above reported LTM (2.54bn EUR), so on reported earnings it is about 20x, and like-for-likes have slowed to about 4%. That is why our base fair value of 3,050p sits below the reported NAV. Where we disagree with the market is on the earnings path. Action is still growing EBITDA about 11%, adding at least 400 stores a year, and gaining share in France. The buyback below NAV adds to value per share, and there is now a second programme. The market discount is about the multiple and concentration, not about earnings, and that gap is too small (about 18% to our base) to clear our 20% bar today.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window, the months just ahead (3-9 months). (1) Action's December trading is the biggest month of the year. Management already said Q4 'should have a higher-than-normal impact' on the 2026 result, so a weak Christmas in France or Germany would hit the guided 4% like-for-like and 14.7-14.8% margin at once. (2) The March 2027 year-end valuation could see a cut to the multiple if listed peers such as Costco and Dollarama de-rate further. Each turn is about 165p a share. (3) Sterling strength against the euro, after a 47p loss this half. (4) Spending on the 2027 US entry. There is no liquidation event, debt maturity or forced seller that could break the thesis: gearing is about 4%, and Action refinances easily (1.6bn EUR raised in October 2025, mostly fixed below 4.6%). The share price has shown it can fall: from 3,626p (52-week high) to a 52-week low of 1,825p, and to 2,311p as recently as 2026-10-23.
picks.positioning_washout: We see no forced selling by holders who must sell regardless of value. 3i is a FTSE 100 member held by long-only and income investors, with no lock-up, index change or redemption pressure in view. The more likely route to our buy level is a sector-wide sell-off in European consumer stocks, of the kind that took the shares to 2,311p on 2026-10-23 after weak French consumer news. A repeat on a soft Christmas trading update would put 2,530p within reach. On the other side, 3i's own buyback is a steady buyer below NAV, which limits how deep a sell-off can go.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near 2,530p, which a sector-wide sell-off in European consumer stocks could deliver. The thesis holds. The 12 November 2026 half-year results lifted NAV to a record 3,154p a share, Action is still growing EBITDA about 11% and opening at least 400 stores a year, and 3i finished a 750m GBP buyback below NAV and started another. We value the shares at about 3,050p. That is a little under the reported NAV, because 3i's 18.5x multiple on Action uses run-rate rather than reported earnings (about 20x on the reported figure), and like-for-likes have slowed to about 4% while the US entry adds cost. At 2,582p the shares sit about 18% below that value, just short of the 20% margin of safety this market backdrop asks for. The adverse case, which takes Action to 14.5x and trims the rest of the book, is about 2,350p. The favorable case, with Action growing about 12% at an unchanged multiple, is about 3,600p. The stock traded at 2,311p as recently as 23 October 2026, so the buy level is not far-fetched. This is the same answer the committee gave on 9 November. The only change is that the fair value and the buy level move up with the newly reported NAV. Our conviction stays at 3: a good, growing franchise, priced in line with listed private-equity peers, with heavy concentration in one retailer.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst, meaning what forces the re-rating: no single binding event. The re-rating levers are (1) the second buyback programme announced 2026-11-12, which buys shares about 18% below NAV and adds to NAV per share, (2) Action's full-year 2026 trading (Q4 heavy, with management expecting a stronger Q4 than last year), reported with 3i's FY27 results, usually in mid-May (the 2027 date was not verified), and (3) early proof that the US format works (first stores in 2027). None is binding or contractually dated, so they support the value case without forcing the gap closed on a timetable.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# 3i Group plc (III.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

Debate date: 2026-11-16. Price used: 2,582p (FMP live quote, London listing, pence sterling). Sources: the earnings-call transcripts of 2025-05-15 (full year FY25), 2025-11-13 (half year FY26) and 2026-11-12 (half year FY27), the screener metrics block, the balance-sheet correction in the bundle (net debt 1.38bn GBP at 2026-09-30, including 42m GBP of leases), and the 3i Q1 FY27 update (NAV 3,131p at 2026-06-30, found by web search).

How to read 3i: it is an investment company that holds stakes in private businesses and carries them at a valuation on its own balance sheet. Its "revenue" and "net income" are mostly gains in the value of those stakes, so the 95% net margin, the 178x price-to-free-cash-flow and the Piotroski score of 3 out of 9 (a nine-point accounting health check) are artefacts of investment-entity accounting, not signals. The right yardstick is net asset value (NAV, the value of the holdings minus debt, per share) and how much of it the market is willing to pay for. The scan's 62.6bn "net debt" is wrong; the balance-sheet figure is 1.38bn GBP.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has not changed in eighteen months; the tone around it has. In May 2025 the pitch was confident compounding: "the fifth consecutive year we have delivered a total return of over 20%", Action (the Dutch non-food discount retailer that is about three quarters of 3i's portfolio) at 10.3% like-for-like sales growth (sales in stores open more than a year) and 29% EBITDA growth (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) in 2024. In November 2025 the language turned cautious - France "clearly challenging", a risk that it "pulls us below the 6.1% like-for-like guidance". In November 2026 the half-year total return was 5%, Action's like-for-likes were 3.4% for nine months, and the backdrop was described as energy-driven inflation that "weighed heavily on consumers". The growth drivers have shifted from like-for-likes towards store openings (at least 400 in 2026, up from about 380 in 2025), new countries (Croatia, Slovenia, Bulgaria and the US from 2027) and price cuts on over 1,000 items to win volume. The capital-allocation story added something new: share buybacks, because the stock now trades below NAV.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (quarter) | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Consistent 20%-plus compounding (FY25 call) | NAV 2,542p (2025-03) -> 3,030p (2026-03, +19%) -> 3,131p (2026-06) -> 3,154p (2026-09). Book value per share 5-year growth 24% a year in the scan. | Holds over five years; the latest half (+5% total return) is the slowest in the series, hit by a 47p foreign-exchange loss. |
| Action keeps compounding earnings (all calls) | 2026 nine-month EBITDA +10.7% to 1.73bn EUR; LTM (last twelve months) operating EBITDA 2.54bn EUR at P9; ten-month EBITDA 1.96bn EUR with October stronger. | Growth intact but halved from 29% (2024) to roughly 11-13%. |
| 18.5x is a conservative multiple (H1 FY26, H1 FY27) | 3i applies 18.5x to "LTM run rate EBITDA of EUR 2.8 billion" for an enterprise value of 51.4bn EUR. Reported LTM operating EBITDA was 2.54bn EUR. | The run-rate figure (which annualises the year's new stores) is about 10% above reported LTM; on reported LTM the mark is about 20x. The "conservative" framing depends on which EBITDA you use. This is the main forensic caveat. |
| Third-party trades validate the mark (H1 FY27) | 3i bought more Action equity in the half "at a price consistent with the valuation multiple", taking its stake to 67.5% (62.3% in Oct 2025). | A real arm's-length check, though the counterparties are fund investors with liquidity needs. |
| Cash generation strong (H1 FY27) | Action cash 1.39bn EUR after a 450m EUR dividend; about 2.25bn EUR operating cash flow expected in 2026; 3i completed a 750m GBP buyback at about 2,495p average and announced a second programme. | Corroborated by the buyback actually executed. |
| Low gearing | Net debt 1.38bn GBP (1.34bn ex-leases) against a 33.8bn GBP portfolio, about 4%. Altman-Z 10.2. | Clean. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable, with a defensive tilt. May 2025: offensive ("budgeting for another good year of compounding growth"). November 2025: hedged on France, still upbeat on store openings ("ahead of our expectations"). November 2026: defensive on the macro ("a challenging scenario for business and consumers"), but specific and confident on Action's levers - price cuts "without any material impact on its economic model", market share gains in France per Nielsen data, Poland "winning market share". Guidance became more specific, not less: 2026 like-for-likes "around 4%", EBITDA margin "14.7% or 14.8%", at least 400 stores.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-High. The March 2025 capital markets day set 6.1% like-for-likes for 2025; management flagged the miss risk in November 2025 and the year came in at about 4.9% (as cited in our 2026-11-09 record; not re-fetched this pass). Store openings beat guidance two years running (about 380 vs the plan in 2025; at least 400 for 2026). The medium-term 5% like-for-like ambition has not been met in either 2025 or 2026. Management flags misses early rather than sandbagging, which is a good habit, but the like-for-like target has been too high twice.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- France and Germany consumer weakness (every call since May 2025). Management attributes it to the macro, not store maturity, citing the Netherlands as a mature market still growing.
- Margin pressure: diesel cost about 12m EUR extra this year, input and packaging inflation across the portfolio, price cuts on half the fixed assortment, and US set-up costs (about 20 staff so far). Asked whether the 14.7-14.8% margin would look "materially different without the U.S.", management said no.
- Temu and online: described as a "glancing blow".
- Buybacks versus buying more Action: management says buybacks make sense "while there is a dislocation in the share price".
- What was not asked: the gap between run-rate and reported EBITDA in the valuation mark.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Like-for-like deceleration: 10.3% (2024) -> about 4.9% (2025) -> 3.4% nine-month 2026 (H1 FY27 call).
- Valuation on run-rate EBITDA, about 10% above reported LTM (H1 FY27 call).
- Concentration: Action is about 25.5bn GBP of a 33.8bn GBP portfolio (H1 FY27), about three quarters of the book.
- The US entry in 2027 is a new, expensive and unproven market for a European format (H1 FY27).
- The rest of the private-equity book grew earnings only "upper mid-single digits" (H1 FY27), down from "just below mid-teens" (FY25).

Green flags:
- 96-98% of the private-equity portfolio by value grew earnings in every period reviewed.
- No material write-downs in three consecutive half-years.
- 3i bought back about 30m shares below NAV at about 2,495p, which adds to NAV per share.
- Action's fast deleveraging and strong cash conversion; pro forma leverage 3x in Oct 2025.
- Market share gains in France despite the weak consumer (H1 FY27, Nielsen).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The pivot from "we buy more Action when the shares trade at a premium" to "buybacks when they are not at a premium" is an implicit admission that the market no longer pays a premium for the Action exposure.
- "Long-term hold" now names two assets (Action, Royal Sanders); Royal Sanders keeps buying (Zwitsal, its 10th acquisition).
- The peer-multiple slide stresses that Costco and Dollarama "derated a little" yet still sit 6-8 turns above Action. Management is defending the mark in advance.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT

Trajectory: stable. The single most important thing for the director: 3i is a leveraged-to-one-asset bet on Action's EBITDA multiple. Each 1x on Action's multiple is worth about 1.6bn GBP, or about 165p per 3i share (2.8bn EUR run-rate EBITDA x 67.5% stake, about 1.9bn EUR, over roughly 990m shares). A move of plus or minus 3 turns is plus or minus about 500p, or about 20% of today's price. NAV growth is real, but the price you pay for it depends on whether Action keeps a premium retailer multiple while like-for-likes run at 3-4%.

Moat: Action has a scale-cost moat (buying power across 3,000-plus stores and 14-plus countries lets it cut prices on 1,000 items without hurting its economics) plus a white-space runway (about 7,700 potential European stores). The moat is narrow but real, and stable: margins are holding at 14.7-14.8% and market share is rising, though like-for-like growth has slowed. 3i itself has no moat beyond permanent capital and its record in selecting assets. Secular threat: online discount platforms (Temu) are a manageable channel-shift risk, not terminal. The cheapness is a fear-print about consumer cyclicality and multiple compression, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Porsche Automobil Holding SE (PAH3.DE) - forensic dossier, 2026-11-10

Source note: no earnings-call transcript was available (FMP has none for this listing and Porsche SE does not publish call transcripts in a form we could retrieve). This dossier is built from Porsche SE's own dated releases (Q1 2026 statement, H1 2026 report of August 2026, the nine-month statement published 2026-11-10), Volkswagen's Q3 2026 release of 2026-10-29 as reported by Just Auto, Reuters (via Euronext Live) and Investing.com coverage, live FMP quotes taken 2026-11-10, and the screener's financial block. No management quote is reproduced beyond what those reports carried. All figures are in euros on the Xetra listing.

The takeaway: Porsche SE is a leveraged holding company. It owns 53.3% of Volkswagen's voting shares and 25% plus one share of Porsche AG's voting shares, plus about EUR 0.67bn of smaller venture stakes, against EUR 5.1bn of net debt. Its own reported numbers are set by those two car makers. In 2026 both are getting worse, and the holding company is passing the write-downs through. Management is credible about the accounting but has little power over the earnings.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **2024-2025:** Porsche SE pitched itself as moving "into a diversified investment platform" with a portfolio-investments arm alongside its two core car stakes. The story rested on Volkswagen and Porsche AG paying dividends large enough to cover interest and Porsche SE's own dividend, with any extra cash going into new stakes.
- **Q1 2026 (statement, spring 2026):** the company called its start to the year "as expected", but it booked a non-cash write-down of about EUR 1.3bn on the Volkswagen stake. Net loss after tax was about EUR 0.9bn.
- **H1 2026 (August 2026):** loss of about EUR 2.2bn after write-downs of about EUR 3.0bn on Volkswagen and about EUR 0.2bn on Porsche AG. The adjusted result (stripping out those write-downs) was EUR 949m against EUR 1.11bn a year earlier. Net debt was EUR 5.0bn. The tone moved from "investment platform" to pressing Volkswagen for "swift action" on competitiveness.
- **September 2026:** the full-year adjusted-result guidance was cut, according to Reuters, to minus EUR 0.5bn to plus EUR 1.5bn.
- **Nine months 2026 (2026-11-10):** loss after tax of EUR 2.78bn (prior year: profit of EUR 1.24bn), after another write-down of the Volkswagen carrying value (amount not disclosed in the summary we saw). Adjusted result after tax EUR 930m, down about 42% from EUR 1.59bn. The Volkswagen share of profit fell to EUR 0.8bn from EUR 1.7bn. Porsche AG's share rose to EUR 0.2bn from EUR 0.1bn. Venture stakes added EUR 135m, mostly from marking up Quantum Systems. Net debt was EUR 5.10bn, flat on December 2025. Guidance was confirmed.

So the story has narrowed. The diversification theme is still there in the release, but the business is now about protecting a holding that two loss-hit car makers fund.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Net debt is under control (target EUR 4.7-5.2bn at year end) | EUR 5.10bn at 2026-09-30 vs EUR 5.099bn at 2025-12-31; screener balance sheet at 2026-06-30: borrowings EUR 6.90bn minus cash EUR 1.92bn = EUR 4.98bn | Holds, but only flat - nothing is paying it down |
| Adjusted earnings show the "real" result | Adjusted EUR 930m for nine months, but FY guidance now allows an adjusted loss of up to EUR 0.5bn, so Q4 could be deeply negative | The adjusted figure is shrinking fast; most of it is Volkswagen's equity-accounted profit, not cash |
| Volkswagen's restructuring will restore value | VW Q3 2026 (2026-10-29): operating loss about EUR 5.8bn, special items EUR 7.8bn in the quarter including EUR 6.4bn of Porsche goodwill write-downs; nine-month operating profit about EUR 0.1bn vs EUR 5.4bn | Not yet - the numbers are going the other way |
| The stakes are worth far more than the share price | Look-through value at 2026-11-10 prices is about EUR 37.7 a share vs EUR 25.28 (see section 8) | True on paper; the gap is a long-standing holding discount, not a new mispricing |
| Screener margins (gross 100%, net 97%) and P/FCF 5.7x | These are artifacts of a holding company that reports equity income, not sales | Ignore; value it on its stakes |

Cash flow is the real test. The screener shows trailing free cash flow of only EUR 242m and a 3-year FCF trend down 56% a year. That cash is essentially dividends received minus interest and costs. Volkswagen's 2026 profit collapse makes a lower Volkswagen dividend for fiscal 2026 (paid in 2027) likely. That would squeeze Porsche SE's ability to pay interest and its own dividend from income.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining. Q1 2026 said the year started "as expected". The August report and the 2026-11-10 statement moved to urging Volkswagen to act. The chairman said the agreed competitiveness and cost measures "must be implemented swiftly" and that delivering them is "the management's task and responsibility". This language puts responsibility on Volkswagen. Guidance precision fell: the adjusted-result range is EUR 2bn wide and now includes a loss.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium. Porsche SE's guidance just passes through Volkswagen's and Porsche AG's guidance, so it is only as good as theirs. Both cut during 2026 (Volkswagen's reported operating margin is now guided at up to about 1%, from 4.0-5.5% originally). Porsche SE cut its own range in September. The net-debt range has held all year, and that is the part management actually controls. The screener's "beat 5/5 quarters" is not meaningful for a holding company with thin analyst coverage.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- How big will the Volkswagen dividend for fiscal 2026 be, and can Porsche SE cover interest plus its own dividend without adding debt?
- Refinancing: about EUR 6.9bn of gross borrowings, with rates higher than when much of it was raised.
- Will the venture portfolio (EUR 0.67bn book value) ever be big enough to matter? Today it is about 4% of gross assets.
- Governance: the Porsche and Piech families control the votes. Ordinary shareholders of PAH3 hold non-voting preference shares, and there is no route to close the discount (no buyback programme of size, no break-up plan).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Four quarters in a row of write-downs on the Volkswagen stake (Q1, Q2 and the nine-month statement of 2026-11-10).
- 🔴 Volkswagen's Q3 2026 operating loss of about EUR 5.8bn and China deliveries down about 30% (reported 2026-10-29).
- 🔴 Full-year adjusted guidance now allows a loss (September 2026 cut).
- 🔴 Net debt is flat, not falling, while the assets behind it shrink.
- 🟢 Porsche AG's equity contribution doubled to EUR 0.2bn in the nine months, and Porsche AG shares (EUR 46.19) are near the top of their 52-week range.
- 🟢 Venture stakes are being marked up (Quantum Systems), with a EUR 135m contribution.
- 🟢 The net-debt range has been met all year, and no covenant or liquidity stress has been disclosed.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The wording has moved from "investment platform" to "calls for swift action at Volkswagen". That is a large shareholder admitting it has to push its main asset. Splitting out the Quantum Systems mark-up as a highlight suggests management wants good news to show beside the write-downs. That mark-up is a valuation estimate, not cash.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: DETERIORATING.

Look-through value at 2026-11-10 prices: about 157.3m Volkswagen ordinary shares x EUR 68.20 = EUR 10.73bn; about 113.9m Porsche AG ordinary shares valued at the listed preference price of EUR 46.19 = EUR 5.26bn; venture stakes EUR 0.67bn book; gross about EUR 16.66bn, minus EUR 5.10bn net debt (ex-lease, 2026-09-30) = about EUR 11.56bn, or about EUR 37.7 a share across 306.25m shares. At EUR 25.28 the stock trades at about a 33% discount to that value. That is near the middle of its usual range for a family-controlled, indebted holding company. It is not an extreme.

The single most important point for the director: the discount is not the opportunity. The underlying Volkswagen stake (about 64% of gross assets) is losing earnings power, and Porsche SE's debt makes its equity a geared bet on Volkswagen. A cheap holding company on a shrinking asset base is a value trap until Volkswagen's earnings turn.

Moat: as a holding company it has no operating moat of its own. Looking through to its assets, Volkswagen's scale and brands are a narrow moat that is being eroded (operating margin guided to about 1% reported in 2026, China volume collapsing under local electric-vehicle competition). Moat: ERODING, trend ERODING. Secular threat: material. The electric-vehicle and China shift is structurally eating into the core asset's terminal value, but it is not terminal for a company of Volkswagen's scale.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

Operations are top tier (Widerøe 93.5% on time, Norwegian top 5 in Europe in August and September), which supports corporate share gains and loyalty (net promoter score above 50, Reward above 10 million members, Spenn scaling with REMA 1000). Fare increases have failed twice ('didn't stick' in Q2; 'customers were not willing to pay' in Q3), and rivals are 'very aggressive on pricing' in Norway, so fuel costs do not pass through. Emissions costs (the NOK 733 million ETS loss in Q2 2026 and a rising ETS bill) are a structural headwind. The NLTG deal issues 300 million new shares (about 28% dilution) plus SEK 3.5 billion in cash for a business whose summer trading management could not describe ('We don't know'), and EU approval is 'challenging' with 'absolutely no guarantee'. The CFO has left, pilot talks are open, and a fuel spike or a winter fare war could cut 2027 EBIT to NOK 2-2.5 billion, worth NOK 9 or less per share.
picks.consensus_delta: The market swings between pricing Norwegian as a permanent fuel victim (it fell to NOK 11.675 on 2026-11-02) and pricing a quick fuel normalisation (NOK 13.29 on 2026-11-09, up 14% in a week as Brent fell to about $92). About 75% of 2027 fuel is unhedged, so a renewed Brent spike (the 52-week high was about $119) would flow straight to earnings. # Norwegian Air Shuttle (NAS.OL): a deep dive on management and the setup

Updated 2026-11-09. Prices in Norwegian kroner (NOK), Oslo listing. Based on five earnings calls (Q1 2025 on 2025-05-08, Q3 2025 on 2025-10-22, Q4 2025 on 2026-02-13, Q2 2026 on 2026-07-14, Q3 2026 on 2026-10-28) checked against the screener's financials.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Over the past two years the story has moved from repairing the balance sheet to running an efficient, cash-generating Nordic airline group, and now to a broader travel company.

- **2025 (balance-sheet repair).** In May 2025 management focused on buying leased aircraft. It bought 10 aircraft and booked a NOK 590 million gain, which it said would cut ownership costs by "approximately NOK200 million a year". It also repaid corporate debt and started paying a dividend.
- **February 2026 (peak confidence).** Full-year 2025 operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and tax) was about NOK 3.7 billion across Norwegian (NOK 3.16 billion) and Widerøe (NOK 585 million), described as "historically strong". Management proposed a NOK 0.80 dividend, a 31% payout ratio. Bookings were "ahead of the curve", and the weaker US dollar was presented as a tailwind.
- **July 2026 (setback, then expansion).** Management called the quarter "a little bit weaker than what we expected". Underlying EBIT was NOK 213 million, a lost EU emissions-trading (ETS) case cost NOK 733 million, and fare increases after the Iran fuel spike "didn't stick". In the same call the company announced the purchase of Nordic Leisure Travel Group (NLTG) for SEK 3.5 billion in cash plus 300 million new shares. That moves the group into package tours and hotels.
- **October 2026 (recovery, with a new risk).** Q3 EBIT of NOK 2.7 billion, a 21.4% margin, was "more or less in line with the underlying result" a year earlier. Cash rose to NOK 11.2 billion and the flat unit-cost guidance held. The new risk is that 2027 is only about 25% hedged at fuel of "$1,500, $1,600 a ton", so winter capacity is being cut 25-40% from October levels and Q1 2027 capacity about 5-6% year on year. Yield (revenue per passenger-kilometre) is "under pressure".

The NLTG deal changes the thesis. The company is no longer only a cost-and-network airline; it is also betting on owning the whole holiday.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Historically strong" 2025 | Net income NOK 2.71 billion (from NOK 1.36 billion in 2024); EPS NOK 2.49, up 107% | Matches, but part of it is aircraft-purchase gains and delivery compensation, which management itself later excluded |
| Unit cost under control ("flat CASK", cost per available seat-kilometre) | Gross margin 16.3% and falling; the Q2 2026 cost cut of 5% was 2-3 points currency (CFO, 2026-07-14) | Partly matches. Program X is real, but currency did much of the work |
| Strong balance sheet | Cash NOK 11.2 billion (Q3 2026), equity ratio 20.6%; but Altman-Z (a bankruptcy-risk score) is 1.3 and net debt is NOK 9.49 billion including leases (fiscal year) | Better than any time since restructuring, but still an indebted airline |
| Cash generation | P/FCF (price to free cash flow) 7.4x; but FCF fell 67% in the latest year and FCF margin is only 5.2% | Weaker than the story. Aircraft purchases absorb the cash |
| Returns | ROE (return on equity) 33%, but ROIC (return on invested capital) is about 0.4% on the screener's definition | The high return on equity comes from a thin equity base and leverage, not from high returns on capital |
| Revenue growth | 3-year CAGR +24.6% (Widerøe consolidated in 2023), latest year only +3.5% | The growth phase is over. Organic growth is low single digits |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a shift toward caution.** In February 2026 management was confident ("it's looking promising for the months to come"). By July it was openly apologetic ("weaker than what we expected"). In October it was confident on demand ("there's nothing wrong with the demand", tickets sold up 15% on capacity up 3%) but defensive on price ("there is a pressure on yields... That is also the case going forward") and on competitors ("I should be a little bit careful"). Guidance has become less specific: management declined to give a 2027 unit-cost number ("we'll come back to the guiding for 2027 later").

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium.** Management delivered the flat-cost guidance for 2025 and is holding it for 2026, and the beat rate is 5 of the last 7 quarters (71%). Two misses matter, though:
- In July 2026 management said "we will most likely put on more hedges for 2027 shortly". By October the 2027 hedge ratio was about 25%, below the company's own 50% rolling policy, and the CEO said hedging at current prices is "not very attractive". The promise was not kept, and the most important cost line for 2027 is now largely unhedged.
- In February 2026 the outlook said bookings "look promising" into Q2. Q2 then came in below management's own expectations.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Fuel hedging** (Nordea, October 2026; Barclays, July 2026). Management does not want to lock in high prices. This is defensible, but it leaves 2027 profits exposed to the fuel price in both directions.
- **Yield and competition** (ABG, DNB Carnegie). Management is reluctant to comment on aggressive pricing by rivals, "maybe especially here in Norway".
- **NLTG regulatory risk** (Barclays). "There's absolutely no guarantee", a "challenging process with a lot of documentation". Asked how NLTG traded over the summer, the answer was "We don't know". A buyer that cannot comment on its target's peak season is a soft red flag.
- **Labour.** Pilot negotiations in Denmark and Norway are under way, and technician talks were tense in July 2026 for the second year running.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Fuel exposure for 2027: about 25% hedged at very high prices (October 2026).
- 🔴 Fare increases do not stick. They failed in Q2 2026 and again after the Iran spike ("customers were not willing to pay", October 2026).
- 🔴 The NLTG deal brings 300 million new shares (about 28% dilution) plus SEK 3.5 billion in cash, the regulatory outcome is uncertain, and management offered no view on how the target is trading.
- 🔴 The lost ETS case (NOK 733 million, July 2026), and ETS costs are becoming "a significant portion" of the fuel line.
- 🔴 The CFO, Hans-Jørgen Wibstad, gave his last presentation on 2026-10-28, so the finance chair changes during the NLTG integration.
- 🟢 Operations are strong: Widerøe punctuality 93.5% and Norwegian 80.7% in Q3 2026, close to zero cancellations, and the NPS (net promoter score, a loyalty measure) is above 50.
- 🟢 Cash of NOK 11.2 billion after repaying the retained-claim bonds; the equity ratio rose to 20.6%.
- 🟢 Loyalty ecosystem: Spenn grew with Reitan/REMA 1000 (weekly sign-ups up 10x), and Norwegian Reward passed 10 million members.
- 🟢 The company keeps taking share in the corporate market (corporate revenue up 6-8%).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary has shifted from "cost program" to "performance program" and "synergies with NLTG". The cost-cutting phase is running out, and the next leg depends on an acquisition.
- Fleet strategy: the company is buying its own aircraft (80 Boeing MAX on order, a large share to be owned). This lowers long-run cost but turns operating leases into capital spending, which explains why FCF lags earnings.
- Capacity discipline in winter (cuts of 25-40% from October levels) shows the same rational behaviour as peers.
- The change of CFO coincides with the integration of an acquisition. This is worth watching for changes in accounting presentation, for example separating fuel and ETS in the P&L "from 2027".

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** The core airline is earning a normal-cycle return, but the jump in reported earnings in 2025 overstates recurring earnings power because of one-off gains. The single most important thing to weigh is that 2027 profits now depend heavily on the jet fuel price, with only about a quarter hedged. Each move in fuel feeds almost directly into earnings, and that exposure is shared by every airline in the peer group.

**Moat.** The moat is narrow and comes from scale-cost and regulation. Norwegian has the densest direct Nordic-Europe network, and Widerøe holds government-subsidised regional (PSO) routes in Norway that competitors cannot easily enter. Gross margin of about 16% (contracting) and an ROIC near zero do not support anything wider. The moat is stable, not widening.

**Secular threat.** The threat is manageable. EU emissions costs (ETS, plus the phase-out of free allowances) are a structural cost headwind, but they hit every European carrier and can be partly passed through in fares over time. They do not threaten the airline's existence. The cheapness reflects fear and cyclical fuel risk, not a structurally shrinking business.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Proximus (PROX.BR) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-02. Price EUR 6.085 (Euronext Brussels, FMP quote). Calls read: Q4 2024 (2025-02-28), Q3 2025 (2025-11-07), Q1 2026 (2026-05-13), Q2 2026 (2026-07-31), Q3 2026 (2026-10-30).*

**Bottom line:** the Belgian home business is steady and has real pricing power, but it barely grows. The story is now about cash flow after a fiber-building peak in 2027, delivered by a management team that has rebuilt some credibility in 2026 after missing badly on the international unit (Proximus Global) in 2025. The latest quarter (Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-30) was better on cash and worse on home-market earnings: the 2026 organic free cash flow guide (cash after investment, before asset sales) doubled from about EUR 50 million to about EUR 100 million, the Global earnings guide was raised, but home-market EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) fell 1.4% and the southern fiber deal slipped again.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **Q4 2024 / Q3 2025:** the story was "Global is a growth engine" plus a domestic defense against Digi, the low-cost fourth mobile operator that launched in December 2024. In Q3 2025 Global EBITDA fell about 22% in one quarter, and the narrative shrank.
- **February 2026 Capital Markets Day (CMD):** a reset — the dividend was halved (EUR 0.30 on 2026 results, stepping to 0.40 and 0.50), a EUR 400 million organic free-cash-flow target for 2030 was set, capital spending was guided to peak in 2027, and the CEO said Global "does not belong" with the Belgian operations.
- **Q1–Q2 2026:** execution language. Flanders fiber collaboration with Wyre and Telenet approved by the Belgian Competition Authority (July 2026); 100% of Unifiber taken in Wallonia; new duct-access rules accepted ("we don't have a clue" whether rivals will use them — Q2 2026).
- **Q3 2026:** defensive framing appears for the first time — the CEO devoted slides to satellite connectivity and AI shopping agents because both "put pressure on Proximus share price in particular". Global is now framed as a turnaround ahead of plan ("direct margin growth ahead of expectations"), with "value crystallization" discussed "around 2028".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic is "resilient" | Customer service revenue +2.9% y/y, consumer revenue per customer +1.7%, convergent revenue +4.7% (Q3 2026); but domestic EBITDA −1.4% in Q3 after slight growth in Q1–Q2 | Top line holds; the profit line is flat-to-down. "Broadly stable" for 2026 reiterated. |
| Price increases stick | January 2026 inflation-linked price rise flowed through; revenue per customer up despite challenger-brand mix shift | Corroborated — this is the strongest evidence of pricing power. |
| Global turning around | Direct margin +0.8% y/y, +4.5% q/q; EBITDA EUR 35m in Q3; full-year guide raised to EUR 125–135m | Corroborated for one quarter; OpEx +5.8% and rising. |
| Cash flow rebuilding | 2026 organic FCF guide ~EUR 100m (from ~EUR 50m); nine-month organic FCF EUR 114m vs EUR 153m a year ago; reported nine-month FCF EUR 54m | Better than guided, still below last year; about half of the capital-spending saving is timing (CFO: "half is efficiency, half is cash CapEx"). |
| Financials overall | Revenue 5.54bn (2021) → 6.38bn (2024) → 6.25bn (2025); EPS 1.37 → 1.23 → 1.12 trailing; return on invested capital about 5.7% (scan), lower on a trailing basis | The earnings base is shrinking slowly while debt-funded fiber investment is still building. |
| Balance sheet | Net debt EUR 5.11bn including leases (EUR 4.73bn ex-leases) at 2026-06-30; net debt/EBITDA guided below 3x; first bond maturity 2028 | High for a EUR 2bn equity; no near-term wall. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable, with a new defensive edge. Q3 2025 was apologetic on Global; Q1–Q2 2026 confident and specific on fiber deals; Q3 2026 confident on cash and Global but defensive on structural fears (satellite, AI agents) and candid on B2B IT ("some delays ... revenue recognition kicks in in Q1 next year"). A new CFO (Fiona Lam, since September 2026) gave tight, numeric answers.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium, improving. Misses: Global 2025 (the "triple digit" synergy story turned into a 22% quarterly EBITDA drop); Flanders fiber timing (about a year late); Wallonia now "summer 2027" versus "end of Q1 27" three months ago. Deliveries: 2026 domestic guidance held three quarters running; Global and free-cash-flow guidance raised in Q3 2026; the screener shows earnings beats in 6 of 7 recent quarters. Some sandbagging is visible in the low 2026 cash guide set at the CMD.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Digi's distribution push (655 Bpost stores) and a "mini price war" in unlimited mobile plans (ING, UBS) — management calls its EUR 24–25 unlimited plans "value-based", while conceding they "prepare for potential new Digi moves".
- Whether free cash flow still grows through the 2027 peak (UBS) — answer: 2027 organic FCF "above EUR 100 million ... still the case".
- B2B service revenue −2.8% and IT delays (Berenberg, Deutsche Bank) — persistent and unresolved.
- Global separation (Berenberg) — deferred to "around 2028".

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: domestic EBITDA turned negative in Q3 2026 (−1.4%); B2B keeps shrinking; Wallonia deal slipped again (Q3 2026); returns on capital are low and falling; heavy leverage; CEO-addressed structural fears on the Q3 2026 call show the market is pricing a terminal story.
- Green: 2026 cash guide doubled (Q3 2026); Global back to margin growth earlier than planned; consumer pricing power intact; dividend policy reconfirmed for the next two years; no bond maturity before 2028.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The CEO now talks about "value crystallization" for Global rather than "strategic options", which points to a separation in 2028, not a near-term sale. The language on duct access has gone quiet since Q2. The Head of B2C also carries the AI title, a sign management sees AI-agent shopping as a churn risk worth a senior owner.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT
Trajectory: turning — from a growth-and-acquisition story to a cash-harvest-after-fiber story. The single most important thing for the director: the equity is a thin slice on top of about EUR 5.1 billion of debt, so small changes in post-2027 cash flow move the share value a lot; the 2026 guide raise helps but half of it is timing.

**Moat:** a narrow but real moat from regulatory licenses, owned ducts and network scale in a small dense country, plus switching costs from bundled fixed-plus-mobile customers. Width is narrow: returns on capital sit well below the cost of capital and have drifted down, largely because of fiber depreciation and the Global write-downs, while home-market pricing power is holding. **Secular threat:** manageable — the four-player Belgian market and duct-access overbuild are competitive (cyclical-structural) pressures, satellite is not a credible substitute in Belgium, and AI agents raise churn risk at the margin. The cheapness is mostly leverage plus a slow-growth incumbent, not a melting terminal value — but it is not a clear fear-print either.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: TORM plc (the London line 0RG4.L, quoted in Danish kroner; the same share trades as TRMD A in Copenhagen and TRMD in New York) is a product tanker owner-operator earning record money and handing most of it back.
