picks.bull_thesis: Burkhalter is the largest building-technology contractor in Switzerland and Liechtenstein (about 87 local electrical and heating/ventilation/air-conditioning/plumbing companies, 173 locations, 5,356 full-time staff at end-2025), and it compounds earnings per share (EPS) steadily: CHF 4.95 (2023), 5.39 (2024), 5.78 (2025, +7.2%), and CHF 2.44 in the first half of 2026 (+8.0%, interim report signed 4 September 2026). The engine is margin, not volume: the operating margin (EBIT, earnings before interest and tax, over sales) rose from 5.9% in 2024 to 6.1% in 2025, and third-party service costs fell from CHF 51.4M to 43.1M in the first half of 2026 as digitalisation and the HVACP ERP roll-out (completing in 2026) bite. Demand has firm, dated policy support: the Swiss federal building programme and the second-home tax change approved by voters on 28 September 2025, which pulls renovation work forward before deductions end (from 2028 at the earliest). The energy transition (heat-pump swaps, solar, EV charging, building automation) is a structural tailwind for exactly these trades. Capital allocation is disciplined and shareholder-first: a 90%+ payout (dividend raised to CHF 5.20 in May 2026, half from capital-contribution reserves and so tax-free for Swiss holders), negligible debt, year-end net cash of CHF 51M (31 December 2025), and a steady cadence of small, cheap bolt-on acquisitions. The stock has fallen 30% from its late-April 2026 high of about CHF 190 to CHF 133.40 even though management confirmed its outlook of a further moderate EPS rise for 2026. At about 22x 2026 EPS of roughly CHF 6.10, a 3.9% dividend yield and a 5-7% free-cash-flow yield, a holder earns roughly 10% a year (dividend plus 6-7% EPS growth) at a constant multiple, with upside if the market returns to the 25-27x the shares held for most of the first half. The business also held its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 14.1% to 13.6%, operating margin +0.8 points), so a reflationary backdrop is not a margin threat. Conditions: EPS keeps growing at 5%+, the dividend keeps rising, and Swiss construction and renovation activity stays at today's level.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that Burkhalter is a fully priced, no-growth contractor whose headline quality is partly an accounting artefact. First, volume growth has stopped: sales rose only 1.8% in 2025 including two acquisitions, and first-half 2026 sales were flat (CHF 587.3M vs 586.8M) despite five acquisitions adding roughly CHF 19M of annual sales, so organic sales fell slightly. The market read it that way: the shares dropped 8.4% on 8 September 2026, the first trading day after the half-year release, and touched CHF 118. Second, the screener's 37.7% return on equity and 24.2% return on invested capital are inflated by Swiss GAAP FER, which lets acquisition goodwill be written off straight against equity: CHF 447.9M of goodwill sits offset against only CHF 104.0M of reported equity at 30 June 2026. On capital that includes that goodwill the after-tax return is about 11%: good, not exceptional, and not worth a premium multiple. Third, EPS growth now depends on margin gains and bolt-ons; margin expansion in a labour-intensive business with a skilled-labour shortage cannot run forever, and wage inflation in a reflationary world could cap it. Fourth, the 90%+ payout is partly funded from capital reserves and, within the year, from short-term bank lines (CHF 34.2M drawn in the first half of 2026), so any downturn in Swiss construction would force a dividend cut and the yield-oriented shareholder base would leave. Fifth, at about 22x 2026 EPS and roughly 18x EV/EBIT (enterprise value over operating profit) it still trades at a premium to Nordic and French installers (Bravida, Instalco, SPIE at roughly 10-16x), so the multiple can keep compressing toward 17-18x without anything going wrong operationally. Disclosure is thin (two reports a year, no order backlog, no earnings call), which keeps it a low-coverage name prone to drift. What would confirm the bear: FY2026 results in April 2027 with EPS flat or down, a dividend held or cut, or another flat-sales print.
picks.consensus_delta: No sell-side price target or consensus could be found or verified for this listing (FMP holds none and none was citable), so this is judged against what the price implies. The question for a deep-value name is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power. It is not. At CHF 133.40 the market pays about 22x 2026 EPS, which prices in continued mid-single-digit growth, not decline. The market's real disagreement was with the April 2026 price: from about CHF 190 (roughly 33x trailing EPS) the stock has de-rated to a multiple that matches a company with flat organic sales and 6-8% EPS growth driven by margins and bolt-ons. Where we differ from the screener rather than the market: its fair value of CHF 66.89 (a -49% margin of safety) and its earnings-power and IV15 readings of -100% understate a business with near-zero capital needs and a 90%+ payout, while the TTM EPS of 11.41 and TTM free cash flow of 174M are data errors (half-years stacked as quarters; true trailing EPS is CHF 5.96 and free cash flow about CHF 102M). We see fair value near CHF 145, only about 9% above today's price, so there is no large mispricing for us to exploit at this level.
picks.valley_of_death: There is no liquidation event, debt wall or forced selling that could kill the thesis: total financial debt was CHF 36.6M at 30 June 2026 against cash of CHF 38.0M, and the Altman Z (a solvency score) is 5.0. The risk window to April 2027 is quieter but real: (1) no scheduled news until FY2026 results in mid-April 2027, so the shares can drift with Swiss small caps; (2) the December US rate decision and a reflationary tape can pull money out of yield stocks, and Burkhalter's shareholder base is yield-oriented; (3) if the second half of 2026 also shows flat sales, EPS growth relies entirely on margin, and a weak full-year sales figure could repeat the 8% drop seen on 8 September 2026; (4) a slowdown in Swiss construction permits would hit the order book, which the company does not disclose. None of these is a thesis-breaker; they are reasons the price could revisit the CHF 118-121 range seen from 9 September to 2 October 2026.
picks.positioning_washout: The shareholder base is mainly Swiss income and small-cap investors attracted by a 3.9% partly tax-free dividend. The forced-selling pressure that matters is softer: the stock is thinly traded (typically 10,000-40,000 shares a day), so a style rotation out of Swiss defensive yield or small caps can move it sharply, as it did in September 2026 (heavy volume of 98,896 shares on 18 September at about CHF 121). Conviction is moderate (3): the business case is sound and the moat is narrow but stable, while the discount is not yet there.

# Burkhalter Holding AG (BRKN.SW) - a deep dive on management and the setup

**As of 2026-11-09. Live price CHF 133.40 (SIX Swiss Exchange, FMP quote).**

**Sources and their limits.** Burkhalter is a Swiss small cap that reports only twice a year and does not publish earnings-call transcripts; FMP holds no transcript for this listing, and none could be found. This deep dive therefore treats management's written communications as "the words": the full-year 2025 ad-hoc release (13 April 2026), the Interim Report 2026 shareholders' letter (signed 4 September 2026, published 7 September 2026), the list of 2025-26 media releases on burkhalter.ch, and the reported income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow and equity statements in those documents (Swiss GAAP FER). No analyst Q&A exists to quote, so section 5 is reconstructed from what the documents leave unsaid. No sell-side price target could be found or verified; none is assumed.

A data warning up front: the screener's "trailing twelve months (TTM) diluted EPS 11.41" and "TTM FCF 174M" are wrong. Burkhalter reports half-years, and the data feed has stacked half-year figures as if they were quarters. The true trailing EPS (second half 2025 plus first half 2026) is CHF 3.52 + 2.44 = CHF 5.96; trailing free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) is roughly CHF 86.5M + 15.8M = about CHF 102M. Everything below uses the reported figures.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has barely changed in four years, which is the point of the company. Burkhalter is a federation of about 87 local building-technology contractors in Switzerland and Liechtenstein (51 electrical, 36 heating/ventilation/air-conditioning/plumbing, "HVACP"), 5,356 full-time staff at end-2025, run as one reporting segment with devolved responsibility. The 2023 merger with Poenina (an HVACP group) roughly doubled sales from CHF 758M (2022) to CHF 1.16B (2023); since then the narrative has been "integrate, digitalise, bolt on":

- **FY2024 (release 14 April 2025):** "excellent" results; dividend CHF 4.85.
- **FY2025 (13 April 2026):** "exceeds expectations once again"; EPS CHF 5.78 (+7.2%), EBIT CHF 73.8M (+6.0%), group profit CHF 61.3M (+7.3%), sales CHF 1,207.6M (+1.8%). Growth was attributed to "sustained high demand for its building technology services and further efficiency gains from optimising and digitalising its processes." Dividend raised to CHF 5.20, half paid out of capital-contribution reserves (tax-free for Swiss holders). New talking points: the second-home tax change approved by Swiss voters on 28 September 2025 will pull renovation demand forward "ahead of the abolition (from 2028 at the earliest)" of tax deductions, and the HVACP ERP roll-out completes in 2026.
- **H1 2026 (4/7 September 2026):** "Half-year results for 2026 show a further increase"; EPS CHF 2.44 (+8.0%), EBIT CHF 31.1M (+5.2%), group profit CHF 25.9M (+8.1%), but sales flat at CHF 587.3M versus CHF 586.8M. Outlook "confirmed": a "moderate increase in earnings per share" for 2026.

What quietly shifted: sales growth has disappeared from the headline. In 2023-24 management led with sales; by 2026 the lead metric is EPS, and the sales line is mentioned last. Acquisitions are now a steady drumbeat of very small deals (seven companies from January to October 2026, each CHF 0.6-8.5M of annual sales) rather than transformative moves.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Sustained high demand" / "strong demand for energy-efficient building technology" (FY25, H1 26) | Sales +1.8% in 2025 including two acquisitions; H1 2026 sales +0.1% including five acquisitions worth roughly CHF 19M of annual sales (about CHF 6-7M in the half). Organic sales were therefore roughly flat to slightly down in H1 2026. | Richer than the numbers. Demand is stable, not "high"-and-growing. |
| Efficiency gains from digitalisation | EBIT margin rose from 5.9% (2024) to 6.1% (2025); H1 EBIT margin on sales 5.3% vs 5.0%. Third-party services fell from CHF 51.4M to 43.1M in H1 while personnel costs rose only 1.5%. | Corroborated. Margin, not volume, is the earnings engine. |
| EPS +7-8% a year | 2021-2025 EPS 3.99 -> 5.78 (about +9.7% a year, flattered by the 2023 merger); 2024 +8.9%, 2025 +7.2%, H1 2026 +8.0%. | Corroborated. |
| "Moderate" EPS increase for 2026 | H1 +8% on CHF 2.44; second half is seasonally larger (H2 2025 EPS CHF 3.52). A 4-7% full-year rise implies CHF 6.0-6.2. | Plausible and probably conservative. |
| Shareholder-friendly capital returns | Dividends of CHF 51.5M (2025) and CHF 55.2M (2026) against group profit of CHF 57.2M and 61.3M: a 90%+ payout. Half the 2026 dividend came from capital reserves. | Corroborated, but leaves little room for error and is partly funded by short-term bank debt in the first half (CHF 34.2M drawn, 20.6M repaid in H1 2026). |
| High returns (screener ROE 37.7%, ROIC 24.2%) | Under Swiss GAAP FER, acquisition goodwill is written off directly against equity. The equity statement shows CHF 447.9M of goodwill offset at 30 June 2026 against reported equity of only CHF 104.0M. On capital that includes this goodwill (about CHF 550M), after-tax operating return is roughly 11%. | The headline returns are an accounting artefact; true returns are good, not exceptional. |
| June 2026 "capital increase" (release 23 June 2026) | Only 39,484 new shares (CHF 6.6M) issued to pay for the anplaq acquisition; share count 10,661,614. | Immaterial dilution (0.4%). Not a funding need. |

Cash flow: free cash flow is heavily seasonal and swings with work-in-progress. H1 is always weak (H1 2026 operating cash flow CHF 22.9M) and H2 strong (H2 2025 CHF 88.9M). Full-year 2025 free cash flow was about CHF 101M, flattered by a CHF 43M second-half working-capital release; a normalised figure closer to group profit plus depreciation minus capital spending (about CHF 65-75M) is the honest base. Receivables from work in progress jumped from CHF 146.9M to 183.9M over the first half, matched by higher prepayments and payables; nothing abnormal for the season, but worth watching at the full-year.

Balance sheet: net cash of only about CHF 1.5M at 30 June 2026 (cash 38.0M vs bank and financial debt 36.6M), seasonally low after the dividend; year-end net cash was CHF 51.4M at 31 December 2025.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable.** The language is consistently upbeat and formulaic: "excellent" (FY24), "exceeds expectations once again" and "exceptionally successful" (FY25), "a further increase" and "outlook confirmed" (H1 26). Guidance specificity has not changed: always a qualitative "moderate increase in earnings per share", never a sales or margin number. There is no shift to defensive language about costs or macro conditions; the only change is the quiet demotion of sales growth noted above.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management guides one metric, qualitatively, and has met it: EPS rose in 2024, 2025 and H1 2026 as promised. The screener's "beat 0/2" refers to sell-side estimates the data feed may not hold for this name and cannot be verified; the company's own guidance has been delivered. There is a mild sandbagging pattern ("moderate", then +7-8%). Reliability: **High** on the narrow metric it guides; **Medium** on the broader growth narrative, because "high demand" has not translated into organic sales growth.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

No call transcripts exist, so this is inferred from what the documents avoid:
- **Organic growth.** Neither release breaks out organic versus acquired sales. With H1 2026 sales flat despite five acquisitions, this is the question an analyst would press, and the market appears to have answered it itself: the shares fell 8.4% on 8 September 2026, the first trading day after the H1 release (CHF 133.20 to 122.00), and touched CHF 118 within a week.
- **Order backlog / intake.** Not disclosed in either release.
- **Payout sustainability.** A 90%+ payout partly from capital reserves, with first-half bank borrowing to bridge the dividend.
- **Valuation reset.** The stock ran from about CHF 140 in January to CHF 190 in late April 2026 (about 33x trailing EPS) on the FY25 release and has since given back the whole move.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: H1 2026 sales flat (CHF 587.3M vs 586.8M) despite five acquisitions, implying slightly negative organic growth.
- Red: headline ROE/ROIC inflated by the Swiss GAAP goodwill write-off against equity (CHF 448M offset vs CHF 104M book equity).
- Red: dividend partly funded from capital reserves and short-term bank lines in H1 2026; payout above 90% leaves little buffer if a downturn hits Swiss construction.
- Red: sales and order data are thin; no backlog disclosure.
- Green: EPS up +7.2% (FY25) and +8.0% (H1 26); EBIT margin expanding for a fourth year.
- Green: net cash at year-end (CHF 51M at end-2025), negligible debt, Altman Z of 5.0.
- Green: inflation resilience: gross margin held through 2021-22 (14.1% to 13.6%) with operating margin up 0.8 points; labour-heavy contracts re-price.
- Green: policy tailwinds named with dates: the Swiss building programme and the second-home tax change (voted 28 September 2025) supporting renovations until at least 2028.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The headline metric migrated from sales to EPS, which suggests management knows volume growth has stalled and is steering attention to the efficiency story.
- Acquisitions shrank in size and moved into mountain cantons (Valais, Graubunden) and adjacent niches (building automation, pipeline construction for energy and water). This is density-filling, not empire-building: low risk, low growth.
- Paying for anplaq partly in shares (June 2026) is new; small, but a sign management is willing to use its paper.
- Leadership is unchanged (Chairman Gaudenz F. Domenig, CEO Zeno Bohm); no management turnover signals.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** A well-run, cash-generative, high-payout Swiss contractor compounding EPS at about 6-8% a year through margins and small bolt-ons, with organic volume flat. The single most important thing to weigh: **this is a dividend compounder trading on its multiple, not a mispriced asset.** At CHF 133.40 it trades at about 22x 2026 EPS of about CHF 6.10, a 3.9% dividend yield and roughly a 5% normalised free-cash-flow yield. The April 2026 peak (33x) was the outlier; today's price is close to fair, and the screener's "fair value 66.89 / -49% margin of safety" and "DCF 157.7" bracket that fairly wide.

**Moat:** narrow, based on local scale and density (a contractor with 173 locations wins on proximity, apprentices and service contracts) plus switching costs in the service-and-maintenance book. Returns on true capital (about 11% after tax including written-off goodwill) and margins that have risen four years running point to a stable, not widening, moat. **Secular threat:** manageable. The energy transition is a tailwind (heat-pump replacement, solar, EV charging, retrofits), not a threat; the real structural risk is the skilled-labour shortage, which caps growth more than it threatens terminal value. The cheapness since April is a de-rating of an expensive multiple, not a shrinking base.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# 4imprint Group plc (FOUR.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-16. No earnings-call transcript is available from our data provider (FMP) for this London listing. This dossier is built from the company's own trading statements and results as reported on the dates shown (20 January 2026 full-year 2025 trading update, 20 May 2026 annual-meeting trading update, 5 August 2026 half-year results, 10 November 2026 ten-month trading update), FMP's reported half-year statements, and the screener's multi-year figures. No management quotes are reproduced because no transcript was read; paraphrases are attributed to the dated statement they come from.

4imprint is a US-centred direct marketer of promotional products (branded pens, drinkware, apparel and bags for businesses). It reports in US dollars and its shares trade in pence in London (live price 4,110p on 2026-11-16, about $54.2 at $1.319 to the pound). The screener files it under advertising agencies; it is really a catalogue-and-online distributor whose edge is a marketing machine and fulfilment network.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- 2021-2024 was a post-pandemic recovery and share-gain story: revenue rose from $787m (2021) to about $1.37bn (2024), and earnings per share from about $0.80 to $4.15. Management's story then was market-share gain from a fragmented distributor base and operating leverage on a brand-marketing (TV, "brand awareness") spend.
- 2025 turned defensive. Revenue slipped to about $1.35bn (20 January 2026 trading update) as US small-business customers ordered less; new-customer orders were down about 13% in the ten months to October 2025 (November 2025 update). The narrative shifted from growth to "resilience" and margin protection.
- 2026 is a stabilisation story with a tariff overlay. Four-month orders were down about 2%, new-customer orders down about 7% (20 May 2026). At the half (5 August 2026) revenue was up about 1% to $666m but adjusted profit before tax fell about 12% to $64.8m as gross margin fell from 32.8% to 31.5% on tariff-related product costs. Management nonetheless raised full-year guidance to revenue slightly above $1.35bn and adjusted profit before tax of about $130m. On 10 November 2026 it reaffirmed that guidance: ten-month revenue up 2%, order intake down 1%, average order value up 3%, new-customer orders down 5% year to date with the decline narrowing every quarter (minus 9% in the first quarter, minus 5% in the second, minus 3% in the third).

The arc is: growth compounder (2021-24), demand stall (2025), tariff-squeezed stabilisation with improving order momentum (2026).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (dated statement) | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue "slightly above $1.35bn" in 2026 (5 Aug, reaffirmed 10 Nov) | H1 revenue $661-666m, ten months +2% | Matches. |
| Adjusted profit before tax about $130m (5 Aug, reaffirmed 10 Nov) | H1 adjusted $64.8m (reported $59.6m); ten-month operating margin just above 9% | Achievable; implies a second half of about $65m, similar to the first. Note it is down from about $149m+ in 2025 (20 Jan 2026 update) - a 12-13% profit decline. |
| Gross margin pressure is tariff-driven and manageable | Gross margin 32.8% (H1 2025) to 31.5% (H1 2026) to "just above 31%" (ten months) | Consistent; the squeeze is real and still building into the second half. |
| Strong cash generation | Cash $152m at end-October 2026 after $68m of dividends and a ~$10m office project; FMP shows half-year free cash flow of $51.6m (H1 2026) and $54.4m (H2 2025) | Matches. Trailing free cash flow is about $106m, not the $229m in the screener's trailing block. |
| Screener trailing earnings per share $7.78, free cash flow $229m | FMP half-years: earnings per share $2.07 (H2 2025) + $1.53 (H1 2026) = $3.60 | The screener's trailing figures double-count half-yearly reports. True trailing earnings per share is about $3.60. The headline 69% margin of safety is a data artefact. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable. The tone through 2025 was cautious (demand softness among small US businesses, tariff uncertainty). In 2026 it firmed: a guidance raise at the half (5 August) despite lower margins, and a clean reaffirmation with improving new-customer trends on 10 November. Guidance remained specific (revenue level plus a profit-before-tax number), which is a sign of confidence rather than hedging.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High. The 2025 full-year outcome (about $1.35bn revenue, profit before tax of at least $149m) was flagged early and delivered. The 2026 guidance was raised at the half and held at ten months. The screener shows earnings beats in three of the last three reported periods. No sandbagging pattern of note; management tends to guide once and hit it.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- How far tariffs compress gross margin in the second half of 2026 and in 2027, and how much can be passed on (average order value up about 3% suggests partial pass-through).
- Whether the brand-marketing spend still buys new customers efficiently: new-customer orders fell about 13% in 2025 and about 5% in 2026 to date.
- Capital allocation: a large net cash pile (about $152m) and whether special dividends continue (2025 included a large payout; $119.9m of dividends in H1 2025 per FMP).
- Broker coverage is thin (about five analysts). Published targets found range from about 3,500p (Deutsche Bank, March 2026) to 5,140p (Berenberg, March 2026) and about 5,300p (Peel Hunt, undated); consensus averages of roughly 4,650-4,950p were reported by aggregators around mid-2026. None was found dated after the 10 November update.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: profit before tax down about 12-13% in 2026 on flat revenue; gross margin down about 1.5 points since H1 2025 (tariffs); operating margin fallen from about 10.8% (2024-25) to just above 9% (ten months 2026); new-customer acquisition shrinking two years running.
- Red (data, not company): the screener's trailing earnings and cash-flow figures are inflated roughly 2x, which is what made the stock screen as deep value.
- Green: net cash about $152m (end-October 2026), essentially no debt; return on invested capital above 50%; free cash flow about $106m trailing; new-customer decline narrowing each quarter of 2026; average order value rising; guidance raised (5 August) and reaffirmed (10 November).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The emphasis has moved from "share gain" to "average order value" and "existing customers" - a defensive, retention-led framing typical of a mature franchise.
- A roughly $10m office relocation in Oshkosh, Wisconsin is being treated as an adjusting item; the gap between adjusted and reported profit (H1: $64.8m vs $59.6m) should be watched so that recurring costs do not migrate into adjustments.
- The interim dividend was held at 80.0 cents (5 August 2026) rather than raised - consistent with a flat-earnings year.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. This is a high-quality, cash-generative, debt-free business going through a flat year with tariff margin pressure and improving order trends. The single most important thing to weigh: the cheapness the screen reported is not real. On true trailing earnings of about $3.60 per share (about 273p) the shares trade at about 15 times earnings, or about 13.5 times after stripping out net cash of about 411p a share - a fair, not a cheap, price for a no-growth year.

Moat: scale-cost and marketing-machine (customer-acquisition engine plus supplier scale in a fragmented industry). Width is narrow but real: returns on capital remain above 50%, but operating margin has fallen about 1.5-2 points since 2025 and new-customer acquisition has weakened two years running, so the trend is softening rather than widening; part of that is tariffs (policy, potentially cyclical) rather than structural. Secular threat: manageable - marketplace and online competition and changes in how small businesses find suppliers (search and AI-assisted buying) could raise acquisition costs, but promotional products remain a physical, fragmented, relationship-light category where 4imprint is the scale leader. The price is not a fear-print; it is roughly fair value for a stable base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

Wait for a better price: we buy near $7.50, which a sector sell-off in small-cap biotech could deliver.

The thesis holds, and the third-quarter report on 2026-11-04 confirms it without changing our answer, so we inherit it. ORLADEYO sold $174.8 million, up 20% on a comparable basis, and the company made $86.5 million of non-GAAP operating profit while cutting its cost guidance again. But roughly $17-19 million of that quarter was the new pharmacy filling its shelves, and management kept the drug's full-year range at $625-645 million, so underlying growth is a high-single-digit rate and the fourth quarter will look softer.

Valued by its parts (sum-of-the-parts, valuing each business line separately) BioCryst is worth about $10.60 a share: $9.50 for ORLADEYO at seven times segment operating profit, $2.26 for navenibart, $0.57 for the Netherton program and royalties, less $1.71 of net obligations (about $453 million at 2026-09-30, counting the royalty financing). The adverse case is $6.40 and the favourable case $16.20.

At $7.63 the base case is about 39% above the price, but the upside beyond it depends on a trial a year away, a one-time gene-editing rival faces its FDA decision on 2027-03-10, and the moat is narrow and narrowing. We hold to the level we named, about 2% below today: at $7.50 the discount to fair value is about 41% and the adverse case is $1.10 away. Value conviction stays at 4 because the discount, while real, is not wide enough to pay for a single-product franchise facing a cure; overall conviction stays at 3.
picks.forcing_function: The navenibart pivotal readout in Q3 2027 is the true forcing function; before it, 2027 guidance (likely with Q4 results in late February 2027) showing growth on a lower cost base, and the year-end 2026 Netherton data, are the nearer checks.

# BioCryst Pharmaceuticals (BCRX) — Forensic Interrogator Dossier

**Transcripts reviewed:** 2025-11-03 (Q3 2025) · 2026-02-26 (Q4/FY 2025) · 2026-05-06 (Q1 2026) · 2026-08-05 (Q2 2026) · 2026-11-04 (Q3 2026)
**Price used:** $7.64 (close, 2026-11-09), US dollars, Nasdaq listing
**Prepared:** 2026-11-10

---

## 1. Narrative arc

Over five quarters BioCryst has stopped being a one-drug growth story and become something closer to a leveraged specialty-pharma roll-up. The change is deliberate and management says so openly, but the shape of the story has moved a long way.

**November 2025 — the self-funding growth story.** The pitch was simple and confident: ORLADEYO, the only oral once-daily preventive treatment for hereditary angioedema (HAE, a rare genetic disease causing dangerous swelling attacks), was "well on our way to $1 billion at peak," the European business had just been sold, the Pharmakon debt was repaid, and the company had crossed into operating profit. Competition from two newly launched monthly injectables was dismissed on the strength of in-house market simulation: "our market simulation works consistently predicted that the growth of ORLADEYO would not be affected by new competition."

**February 2026 — the target gets a formula.** Full-year 2025 ORLADEYO revenue came in at $601 million, slightly ahead of the raised $590–600 million guidance. Management then did something unusually checkable: it published the arithmetic behind the $1 billion peak — "what we need is 150 patients net patient growth average per year for this year and 3 more years to hit $1 billion in 2029." That is a falsifiable commitment, and it is the single most useful sentence in the whole transcript set. Alongside it, navenibart (the long-acting injectable acquired with Astria Therapeutics) was introduced with unusual confidence: the earlier mid-stage data gave management "high confidence that the pivotal trial will be successful."

**May–August 2026 — the pivot.** Three things happened in quick succession. Internal drug discovery was shut down and the Birmingham research site closed. The company declared an "external innovation" model — buy or license assets rather than invent them. And the leadership bench turned over: Jon Stonehouse, the long-tenured chief executive, is gone; Charlie Gayer (previously the commercial head) now runs the company, with Dr. Sandeep Menon as chief research and development officer. By Q2 2026 the phrase "financial discipline" had replaced "momentum" as the organising idea, and the cost guidance was cut twice in a year (from $450–470 million to $420–440 million, then to $415–425 million).

**November 2026 — execution, with a thinner engine.** The Q3 2026 call is competent and unflashy. Pellet formulations for children (launched August 2026) and for adults and adolescents (approved 2026-10-21) are genuinely encouraging and management now thinks the paediatric pool is bigger than the 500 patients it had guided to. But the growth drivers quietly dropped along the way are telling: the $1 billion-in-2029 target is no longer mentioned at all on the Q3 2026 call, and the "150 net adds a year" arithmetic has vanished with it, replaced by the softer "net patient adds in the third quarter were quite healthy." Internal discovery, once a reason to own the stock, is gone. What remains is one commercial drug, one late-stage acquired asset, one early skin-disease programme, and $828 million of debt.

---

## 2. Claims versus financials (forensic)

| Management claim | Quarter said | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| "ORLADEYO revenue increased 20% year-over-year" | 2026-11-04 | True as stated, but $17–19 million of the $174.8 million was the new pharmacy, CareMed, building channel inventory. Strip it and the quarter is roughly $157 million, about +7–8% — and **below** Q2 2026's $158.2 million sequentially | Technically true, materially flattered |
| Growth is not affected by new competition | 2025-11-03, repeated 2026-11-04 | Comparable ORLADEYO growth: **+21% (Q1 2026) → +10% (Q2 2026) → ~+8% underlying (Q3 2026)**. Patient demand is holding; the growth *rate* is not | Diverges — the claim is about patients, the number is about revenue, and only one of them is intact |
| "$1 billion at peak" in 2029, needing 150 net adds a year | 2025-11-03, formalised 2026-02-26 | From a 2026 base of $625–645 million, $1 billion by 2029 needs about +16% a year. The underlying run-rate is roughly half that. The target was **not repeated** on the Q3 2026 call | Not supported by the current trajectory; quietly retired |
| 2026 ORLADEYO guidance of $625–645 million is "still the right guidance" | 2026-11-04 | Nine-month actual is $481.0 million ($148.0 + $158.2 + $174.8). Guidance implies Q4 of **$144–164 million**, i.e. a midpoint *below* Q3's $174.8 million. An analyst pressed explicitly on whether $650–655 million was now the right number; management declined | Honest, and the honesty is the bad news: the stocking benefit was absorbed, not added |
| Strong profitability and cash generation | every quarter | Real but lumpy. Q3 2026 operating profit $53.3 million, net income $37.9 million, operating cash flow **$32.98 million** — the cash lagged the earnings by roughly $20 million because channel stocking is a receivable, not cash | Match, with a working-capital caveat |
| "Our balance sheet has never been in a stronger position" | 2026-08-05 | Cash and investments $375.0 million at 2026-09-30, up from ~$354 million. But total debt went from **$477.3 million (Q4 2025) to $858.1 million (Q1 2026)** to fund Astria, and shareholders' equity is **negative $397.4 million**. Net obligations are about $453 million | Diverges sharply — the *cash* is stronger, the *balance sheet* is far weaker |
| Scan-level "deep value": price-to-free-cash-flow of 5.1x, 30% net margin, revenue +94%, earnings per share $1.21 | screener, FY2025 | **Artifact.** Q4 2025 alone carried $406.6 million of revenue, $245.9 million of net income and $292.0 million of operating cash flow — the European divestiture. The FY2025 segment split shows $244 million of "License" revenue, which is that sale, not a business line. Trailing free cash flow of $350 million is $292 million of divestiture plus a $55.7 million licensing upfront | The headline cheapness is one-off receipts, not earnings power |
| Cost discipline is structural | 2026-08-05, 2026-11-04 | Corroborated. Operating-cost guidance cut twice; $30–35 million of annualised savings from the Birmingham closure, of which only $10 million of the $19 million Q3 charge was cash; stock compensation down from $18–24 million a quarter in 2025 to ~$14 million | Match — this is the most credible part of the story |

Two numbers deserve separate emphasis because they are the ones most likely to mislead.

**Return on invested capital of 1.3% against return on equity of 20.6%.** Both are arithmetic consequences of negative book equity and a $718 million acquired-research write-off, not statements about the business. Ignore both.

**Altman-Z of −3.1.** This is the leverage and the negative equity, not operating distress: the company covers its roughly $34 million of annual cash interest several times over. But it is not nothing either — $828 million of debt against a single marketed drug is a real constraint on what management can do next.

---

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory

**Declining, then stabilising at a lower and more honest level.**

- *2025-11-03 — offensive, almost promotional.* "Yet another strong quarter," "well on our way to $1 billion at peak," "we are extremely excited." Competition answered with modelling rather than data.
- *2026-02-26 — peak specificity.* The 150-net-adds formula, and on navenibart "high confidence that the pivotal trial will be successful." This is the most forward-leaning the company gets.
- *2026-05-06 — first defensive notes.* A manufacturing delay on the paediatric pellets is disclosed, paired immediately with "we do not expect this delay to affect our revenue guidance."
- *2026-08-05 — the language flips to efficiency.* "Financial discipline," "leaner, more focused operating model," "disciplined data-driven approach to capital allocation." Growth language recedes.
- *2026-11-04 — measured and careful.* "Strong execution during a time of strategic evolution." The $1 billion target is absent. On the early skin-disease data, the framing is hedged twice over: "we will review the data in totality," "to inform potential next steps." That is pre-positioning for a mediocre readout.

The shift from offensive to defensive vocabulary is unambiguous and it tracks the revenue deceleration quarter for quarter. Guidance has become *less* specific over time on the thing that matters most (the long-term peak) while becoming *more* specific on costs — a classic substitution.

---

## 4. Guidance credibility

**Reliability: High on the near term, Low on the long term.**

What they said versus what they delivered:

- FY2025 ORLADEYO guidance was raised to $590–600 million in November 2025; the company delivered **$601 million**. Over-delivered, narrowly.
- FY2026 operating-cost guidance was cut twice ($450–470 million → $420–440 million → $415–425 million) and each cut was explained by a named, verifiable action (Birmingham closure, discovery wind-down). Delivered.
- FY2026 ORLADEYO guidance of $625–645 million was set in February 2026 and **held unchanged at all four opportunities** — including Q3 2026, when roughly $18 million of channel stocking landed in the quarter and was *not* added to the year. Management could have raised and chose not to. That is either genuine conservatism or an admission that the underlying was running slightly behind plan. The Q4 implied midpoint of about $154 million, versus $174.8 million reported in Q3, says it is closer to the latter.
- The paediatric pellet launch slipped on manufacturing (disclosed 2026-05-06) but landed in August 2026 without damaging the year.
- The earnings-beat record in the screener is 4 of 7 quarters (57%) — no sandbagging pattern, which is consistent with guidance that is set once and defended rather than walked up.

The long-term number is where credibility fails. The $1 billion-in-2029 peak was given a formula in February 2026 and then dropped from the script by November 2026 without ever being formally withdrawn. A target that quietly disappears is a target that was missed.

---

## 5. Analyst pressure points

Three questions recur, and management's handling of them is instructive.

**The quality of the Q3 2026 revenue beat.** The sharpest exchange in the whole set. Sylvia (for Jessica Fye, JPMorgan) asked directly whether investors should now expect $650–655 million for the year — guidance midpoint plus the stocking benefit. Gayer's answer: "we see the range of $625 million to $645 million is still the right guidance for the year." He did not dispute the arithmetic; he declined the conclusion. The clear implication is that underlying demand is running below the level that would let the windfall drop through.

**Competition, asked every single quarter.** Brian Abrahams (RBC) has asked about competitive encroachment on essentially every call. The Q3 2026 answer is the most useful one yet because it is specific and not entirely flattering: when a patient fails ORLADEYO, "instead of moving preferentially to TAKHZYRO, more of those patients are going either to HAEGARDA or DAWNZERA." Management frames this as neutral. It is also evidence that the switching market now has more exits than it did.

**The paid-patient rate.** Asked repeatedly; answered consistently and plausibly (82–83% exiting Q3 2026, down from 84% in Q2, with the seasonal explanation that second-half rates drift down as new patients enter). The long-term 85% goal is reaffirmed. This is management's strongest ground.

**What analysts are not asking, and should be.** No analyst on the Q3 2026 call raised Intellia's one-time gene-editing treatment for HAE, which has a fixed US regulatory decision date of **2027-03-10**. That is the largest single threat to the terminal value of every chronic HAE preventive therapy, including both ORLADEYO and navenibart, and it went unmentioned. Nor did anyone press on the economics of the $828 million debt load or on what "external innovation" will cost. The silence is the risk.

---

## 6. Red flags and green flags

🔴 **Underlying growth has halved twice in three quarters** — comparable ORLADEYO growth of +21% (Q1 2026), +10% (Q2 2026), roughly +8% ex-stocking (Q3 2026).

🔴 **The headline quarter was flattered by a one-off.** Roughly $17–19 million of the $174.8 million was CareMed building channel inventory (2026-11-04). It is revenue, it is legitimate, and it does not repeat.

🔴 **The $1 billion-in-2029 target has been quietly dropped** between 2026-02-26 and 2026-11-04 without being withdrawn.

🔴 **Shareholders' equity is negative $397.4 million** and debt nearly doubled to fund Astria ($477.3 million at Q4 2025 → $858.1 million at Q1 2026 → $828.2 million at Q3 2026).

🔴 **Insider selling is one-sided:** zero open-market purchases against 11 sales totalling 557,876 shares. The screener's buy ratio is inflated by grants; the open-market record is the real signal.

🔴 **Operating cash flow of $32.98 million lagged $53.3 million of operating profit in Q3 2026** — the stocking revenue is a receivable, not cash.

🔴 **Street coverage has thinned and the freshest view is the lowest.** Only one price target in the last quarter: RBC at $11.00 on 2026-09-10, cut from $14.00 on 2026-07-07. The $19.00 consensus is stale and is dragged up by a $29.00 Cantor target from June 2026.

🔴 **Single-product concentration is now total.** Internal discovery is shut; everything rests on ORLADEYO plus one acquired asset.

🟢 **Cost discipline is real and verified.** Two guidance cuts, $30–35 million of annualised savings, stock compensation down roughly 30% a quarter year on year.

🟢 **Gross margin of 97.8% is stable and was resilient through the 2021–22 inflation** (91.6% to 95.4%, +3.8 percentage points). Specialty-pharma pricing power is intact.

🟢 **The paediatric opportunity is being revised upward.** Children across the full 2–11 age range have started on pellets, the switch mix is balanced, and "there is likely a lot more opportunity than the 500 diagnosed and treated patients that we have previously described" (2026-11-04). The 150 mg adult and adolescent formulation was approved 2026-10-21.

🟢 **navenibart is on schedule and over-enrolled.** The largest blinded HAE trial ever run completed enrolment ahead of plan in June 2026; management says it is "already overpowered"; 12-month top-line data is guided to Q3 2027.

🟢 **Guidance has been defended, not walked up,** and the one slip (paediatric manufacturing) was disclosed early and absorbed.

🟢 **A pharmacy transition of this size went through without disruption** — days to first shipment improved. This was a named execution risk and it cleared.

---

## 7. Hidden signals

**"Strategic evolution" is doing a lot of work.** The Q3 2026 opener calls the year "a time of strategic evolution." Translated: a new chief executive, a new research head, research shut down, a site closed, a business sold, a company bought, and a pharmacy switched — all in twelve months. Each step is defensible; together they describe a company that concluded its old plan would not get there.

**The scientific advisory board announcement is a tell about the new model's credibility gap.** Gayer's defence of it on 2026-11-04 — these advisers "did not join us just for the honor of being on the board" — is a response to a question nobody asked. A company confident in its ability to source external assets does not need to argue that its advisers are sincere.

**Competitive language has shifted from denial to segmentation.** In 2025 the answer was "our market simulation predicted growth would not be affected." By late 2026 it is "new injectable therapies primarily compete with existing injectable therapies" — a narrower, more defensible, and smaller claim. The moat is being redrawn around the oral niche rather than the HAE market.

**The early skin-disease readout is being de-risked in advance.** "Review the data in totality," "inform potential next steps," and a stated willingness to spin out or partner the diabetic macular oedema programme rather than fund it. Management is signalling it will walk away from anything that does not clear a high bar. That is good capital allocation and a low expectation for the readout.

**The new chief financial officer speaks in cash, not in revenue.** Babar Ghias's prepared remarks lead with cost base, savings, and balance sheet in every quarter of 2026. The revenue line is handled by the chief executive. The division of labour says where management thinks the 2027 story is: margin, not growth.

---

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)

**Trajectory: PIVOTING.** This is not a deteriorating business — it is a profitable, high-gross-margin rare-disease franchise with improving costs. But it is explicitly being re-engineered mid-flight: one growth engine (internal discovery) switched off, another (acquired late-stage assets) switched on at the cost of roughly $380 million of incremental debt and $718 million of written-off purchase price, with the first proof point still ten months away.

**Moat: NARROW, and the trend is ERODING.** The moat type is a blend of regulatory licence (orphan-drug exclusivity, patents into the late 2030s) and switching costs (a chronic daily oral therapy with 82–85% paid coverage and established physician trust). The width evidence is mixed in a specific way: gross margin of 97.8% is stable and pricing power survived the 2021–22 inflation, which argues the moat is real — but the growth rate of the protected revenue base has halved twice in three quarters, two injectable competitors launched in 2025, an oral on-demand rival has been on the market over a year, and when patients leave ORLADEYO they now leave to more destinations than before. A franchise whose margin holds while its growth rate compresses toward the market's is narrow and narrowing, not wide.

**Secular threat: MATERIAL, not terminal — but it is the one thing that could make it terminal.** The structural force here is reimbursement compression in high-cost specialty pharmacy, and it arrives in a particularly sharp form: Intellia's lonvoguran ziclumeran, a one-time in-vivo gene-editing treatment for HAE, has US regulatory acceptance with priority review and a **fixed decision date of 2027-03-10** (announced 2026-09-08, reaffirmed in Intellia's 2026-11-05 quarterly release). A single curative administration does not compete with a daily pill on convenience; it competes on the payer's lifetime cost, and it attacks the terminal value of every chronic preventive therapy in the disease — ORLADEYO *and* navenibart, the asset BioCryst just paid roughly $700 million for. It is rated material rather than terminal because gene-editing uptake in a serious but non-fatal, well-managed disease has historically been slow, costly and limited to the most severe patients, and because a 2027 approval does not become meaningful revenue erosion for several years. But the direction is one-way.

**Is the cheapness a fear-print or a shrinking base?** Mostly a fear-print, with a real asterisk. The screener's 5.1x free cash flow is not a valuation — it is a divestiture. On clean 2027 earnings power the stock trades around 10–13x with a 98% gross margin and a funded late-stage asset, which is modestly cheap against profitable specialty-pharma comparables but far from a deep discount. The base is not shrinking today; it is growing at high single digits. The risk is not that the discount is fake, it is that the discount is small enough that the gene-editing overhang can eat it.

**The single most important thing to weigh before sizing.** Not the quarter, and not the debt. It is this: the committee is being asked to pay for two things it cannot yet see — that navenibart works and differentiates when 12-month data lands in Q3 2027, and that a one-time cure approved in March 2027 does not reprice the whole category before navenibart ever launches. Those two unknowns resolve in the wrong order. Strip navenibart out entirely and the residual ORLADEYO franchise, net of $453 million of obligations, is worth roughly $6 a share — which is to say the market price already embeds a meaningful part of the pipeline. Size this as a leveraged single-asset franchise with embedded optionality, not as a cash-flow compounder, and do not let the 97.8% gross margin stand in for durability.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

# Trustpilot Group plc (TRST.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-09. Source material: the first-half 2026 results call (2026-09-15), the screener's financial trajectory (fiscal 2021-2025, reported in US dollars), FMP half-year statements, and dated press coverage of the results day. Only one call transcript was available, so the "arc" below compares this call with the multi-year numbers and the dated news rather than with earlier calls.*

**Bottom line:** Trustpilot is a review platform that makes money by selling software subscriptions to the businesses being reviewed. The operating story is corroborated by the numbers: revenue has compounded about 21% a year since 2021 (from $131M to $267M in 2025), the business swung from a $26M loss in 2021 to steady profit, and first-half 2026 bookings grew 18% in constant currency (stripping out exchange-rate moves) with adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, after the company's own adjustments) up 46%. What keeps the credibility score from the top is housekeeping, not demand: the same results day disclosed a US sales-tax processing error, a restatement, and a mistake in how distributable reserves were determined for the share buyback, alongside a change of finance chief. The shares fell about 16% that day.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved in three steps. In 2021-2022 Trustpilot was a growth-at-a-loss listing (net losses of $26M and $15M). From 2023 the message became "profitable growth", and the numbers followed: small but positive net income every year since ($7M, $6M, $8M). The first-half 2026 call adds a third layer: artificial-intelligence search. The chief executive, Adrian Blair, now leads with the claim that Trustpilot is "the number one cited review platform globally" and that ChatGPT citations grew "more than 400%" year on year (H1 2026). The pitch to large customers has shifted from "collect reviews for your website" to "make sure language models recommend you" - what management calls answer-engine optimisation.

Enterprise is the second growth driver that has become central. Customers paying over $20,000 a year now make up 47% of bookings, against 27% in the first half of 2023. North America is the engine (bookings up 27% in constant currency, new-business sales up 76%), while the UK slowed to 11%, partly because multinational contracts such as Expedia are now billed from the US.

Quietly de-emphasised: net dollar retention (how much existing customers spend this year versus last), which slipped from 103% to 101% as earlier price-package migrations annualised.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (H1 2026 call) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Bookings grew 18% in constant currency" | FMP half-year revenue $148.4M vs $122.8M a year earlier, up about 21% reported; the 2025 annual revenue was up 26.5% | Matches |
| Adjusted EBITDA up 46% to $26.3M, margin 17.4% | Reported half-year EBITDA (FMP, before adjustments) was only $10.6M; operating income $4.4M; net result a $1.1M loss after a $5.3M tax charge | The adjusted figure is real but adds back a lot - mainly share-based pay (employee stock awards). Statutory profit is thin |
| "Inherent operating leverage" | Gross margin fell to about 78.8% in H1 2026 from about 82.2% in H1 2025 (FMP); the scan flags gross margin as contracting | Diverges: the leverage is in sales and overheads, not at the gross line |
| $16M adjusted free cash flow in H1 | Screener: free-cash-flow margin 22.5% for 2025, price-to-free-cash-flow 25.6x | Cash generation is real; the trailing figure includes stock pay as a non-cash add-back |
| Gross retention at a record 87% | No independent check possible; consistent with steady revenue growth | Plausible |
| Strong balance sheet | Net cash only about $4M at 2026-06-30 (cash $23M vs debt including leases $18M), after heavy buybacks and employee-trust funding | The cash cushion has been spent on buybacks |

The pattern: the demand claims are corroborated; the profit claims lean heavily on adjustments. Return on invested capital of 2.5% and a 3% net margin are what a shareholder actually owns today.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising.** The call is offensive, not defensive: "excellent first half", "enterprise momentum is excellent", "we're constantly choosing between attractive options". There is no retreat to cost or macro language. Guidance is specific and was reiterated (high-teens constant-currency revenue growth, mid-teens bookings growth, a 2-3 percentage point adjusted-margin improvement). The one defensive note is on the sales reorganisation in the US: an analyst (Investec) asked why new-business generation was partly outsourced, and the answer leaned on "a mixed model" rather than numbers.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The screener shows earnings beats in 5 of the last 7 quarters (71%) and revenue growing every year since listing. The first-half 2026 adjusted margin landed "at the top end of our guidance". There is no sign of a big miss. Reliability: **Medium-High** on operations. It is marked down because the 2026-09-15 disclosures (sales-tax error, restatement of the prior year, buyback reserves error requiring a shareholder circular for retrospective approval) show the finance function was behind the growth curve - the kind of issue that is usually fixed, but that the new chief financial officer has to prove.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Second-half deceleration** (Chris Luyckx): first-half revenue grew 19% against a full-year high-teens guide. Management said this reflects last year's bookings, not slowing momentum. Watch the January 2027 trading update.
- **Is AI paying?** Asked whether citation growth shows up in price or win rates, the answer was "all of the above" with no hard number. The claim is directional, not yet quantified.
- **US margin**: management declined to give a North America contribution margin, saying fast new-business growth delays margin expansion.
- **UK slowdown**: explained by billing relocation (1-2 points of growth), which is reasonable but convenient.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red flag (H1 2026): US sales-tax error, a $1M historic provision and a restatement of prior-year figures, disclosed 2026-09-15.
- Red flag (H1 2026): a technical error on distributable reserves affecting the buyback and employee-trust funding; needs a shareholder circular.
- Red flag (H1 2026): finance-chief change on results day - Hanno Damm leaves after 11 years; Marcus Roy (ex-Economist Group) joined the day before.
- Red flag: gross margin contracting about 3.4 points year on year; net dollar retention down to 101% from 103%.
- Green flag: insider buying after the sell-off - the chair (about £99,000 at 215-223p), the chief executive and the new finance chief all bought (press reports after 2026-09-15).
- Green flag: enterprise share of bookings up to 47%; customers paying over $20,000 up 29% by count and 35% by recurring revenue.
- Green flag: North America new-business sales up 76%; Germany now the third-largest country.
- Green flag: steady capital return - an ongoing buyback with daily "transaction in own shares" notices.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary has moved from "reviews" to "AI influence" and "answer engines". That is both the bull case and the risk: if language models summarise reviews well enough, consumers may stop visiting Trustpilot pages at all.
- The shift to outsourcing part of US new-business selling is a cost-efficiency move dressed as scale.
- A new finance chief from a subscription media business (The Economist) suggests the board wants a tighter controls culture after the errors.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Growth is broad, profitable on an adjusted basis, and accelerating in the largest market.

The single most important thing to weigh: the gap between adjusted and statutory profit. At about 257p the market values the company at roughly £0.98bn (about $1.32bn), about 5.3 times expected 2026 gross profit and about 24 times adjusted EBITDA - fair for an 18%-growth subscription business only if the adjusted margin keeps rising and stock-based pay is offset by the buyback.

**Moat:** a network effect (more reviews attract more readers, which makes businesses pay to engage, which drives more reviews), plus a scale advantage in the open review dataset (400 million-plus reviews). It is real but **narrow**: returns on capital are still thin (2.5%) and gross margin is slipping, so the evidence does not yet show a wide moat. Trend: stable.

**Secular threat:** AI is a double-edged force. Today language models cite Trustpilot and that helps sales; tomorrow they could absorb the reader traffic that makes businesses pay. This is a material, not terminal, threat - the dataset becomes more valuable as a source even if page visits fall, and management is already selling the AI angle. The current price is not a fear-print on a shrinking base; it is a modest discount on a growing one, widened by a self-inflicted accounting scare.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

# NRC Group ASA (NRC.OL): a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16. No earnings-call transcript was available from our data provider. This dossier is built from the company's published quarterly releases and result summaries (Q2 2025 to Q3 2026, the latest dated 5 November 2026), the quarterly statements in our data feed (FMP, through 30 September 2026) and the screener's multi-year figures. Where a quote would need a transcript, we describe the message instead of inventing words.*

**Bottom line:** NRC is a Nordic rail-infrastructure contractor (Norway, Sweden, Finland, plus the Kept, Gunnar Knutsen and Machines units) partway through a margin repair that is now real in the numbers. The third quarter of 2026 brought an operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and tax) of NOK 91 million, its best quarter since the restart. On the same day, 5 November 2026, management cut its 2026 revenue guidance from about NOK 7.5 billion to about NOK 6.5 billion, dropped the 2028 revenue target of more than NOK 10 billion, and admitted a below-target win rate on tenders. The repair is working on margins; the growth leg has gone soft.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **2024 (rescue):** large project write-downs and impairments (net loss of about NOK 1.0 billion for the year) and an equity raise in Q3 2024. The story was survival and restructuring.
- **2025 (restart):** the message became "profitability over volume": disciplined project selection, a return to profit (Q2 2025) and a record order backlog in Q1 2025. In Q3 2025 the headline profit measure changed from adjusted EBIT to reported EBIT. Targets: revenue of more than NOK 7 billion and an EBIT margin above 3% in 2026, with more than NOK 10 billion of revenue and a margin above 5% by 2028.
- **H1 2026 (growth promised):** Q1 2026 was a loss (EBIT of minus NOK 29 million on NOK 1.14 billion revenue) with growth promised for the second half. Q2 2026 lifted the 2026 revenue guide to about NOK 7.5 billion, reported a book-to-bill (orders won divided by revenue billed) of 1.2x and a NOK 8.9 billion backlog, and submitted a NOK 566 million final claim to Bane NOR on the ETM project.
- **Q3 2026 / Capital Markets Update (5 Nov 2026):** the story shrank. Revenue guidance for 2026 fell to about NOK 6.5 billion. The 2028 revenue target was replaced by order-intake targets (more than NOK 10 billion in 2027, more than NOK 12 billion in 2028) "because of project timing uncertainty". Margin targets were kept and extended: adjusted EBIT margin above 3.5% in 2027 and above 5.0% in 2028. Management described commercial performance as weak, with tender delays and cancellations (especially in Norway) and a win rate below target.

The arc runs from survival, to margin repair, to a growth promise that was withdrawn within one quarter.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Profitability over volume; margins recovering | Q3 2026 EBIT NOK 91m vs NOK 65m a year earlier (about 4.9-5.0% margin); year-to-date EBIT NOK 123m vs NOK 98m, after a NOK 71m one-off Swedish legal charge in Q2 | Corroborated |
| 2026 revenue about NOK 7.5bn (Q2 2026 guide) | Year-to-date revenue NOK 4.68bn vs NOK 4.85bn in 2025; guide cut to about NOK 6.5bn on 5 Nov 2026 | Missed: cut by about 13% within one quarter |
| Strong backlog, book-to-bill above 1.0x on a twelve-month basis after Q2 | Backlog NOK 7.88bn at Q3 2026 vs NOK 8.93bn at Q2 2026 and NOK 8.54bn a year earlier; Q3 book-to-bill 0.7x | Diverges: the backlog is shrinking |
| Cash flow improving | Operating cash flow: Q4 2025 +NOK 247m, Q1 2026 -NOK 173m, Q2 2026 +NOK 163-180m, Q3 2026 -NOK 27m to -NOK 39m (sources differ); year-to-date roughly zero. Net debt including leases NOK 823m at 30 Sep 2026 vs NOK 781m at 30 Jun 2026 | Mixed: seasonal and lumpy, no clear trend yet |
| More than 30% of profit to be paid as dividends | No dividend paid in 2026; reported retained earnings still negative (minus NOK 124m) | Not yet tested |
| Swedish turnaround | Sweden EBIT NOK 10m in Q3 2026 vs NOK 1m a year earlier | Corroborated, from a very low base |

The screener's 96.7% "gross margin" and the jumpy quarterly cost-of-revenue lines in our data feed are a data-mapping artifact (Q4 2025 shows a negative cost of revenue). Ignore them; contractor margins are judged at the EBIT line.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Rating: Declining on growth, rising on margins.** From Q1 2025 to Q2 2026 the releases leaned on the record backlog and a strong tender pipeline, and the 2026 revenue guide went up. By Q3 2026 the tone had turned defensive on the commercial side: management named tender delays, cancellations, a weak win rate, and switched from revenue targets to order-intake targets. On execution the tone stayed confident ("strongest quarter since the restart"). The shift from a revenue promise to an order-intake promise is the clearest sign of lower confidence about the top line.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
- Margin guidance: delivered. The 2025 margin improvement happened, and above 3% for 2026 is on track (year-to-date 2.6% after a NOK 71m one-off, with Q4 seasonally strong).
- Revenue guidance: poor. The about NOK 7.5bn 2026 figure set in mid-2026 was cut to about NOK 6.5bn by November, and the 2028 revenue target was dropped. Part of the gap is the weaker Swedish krona and euro, but the guide was stated at constant currency.
- The screener's earnings-beat rate is 4 of 7 quarters (57%); Q3 2026 beat the consensus EPS of about NOK 0.30 with NOK 0.33.
- **Reliability: Medium** (high on cost and margin, low on volume and timing).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
With no transcript we cannot quote the Q&A. The obvious pressure points from the releases: (a) why order intake and the win rate are below target while the tender pipeline is said to be NOK 43-44bn; (b) the status of the NOK 566m Bane NOR ETM claim, where negotiations were scheduled for Q3 2026 and the Q3 summaries say nothing about the result; (c) how a 5% margin in 2028 is reached on a shrinking backlog; (d) why diluted shares rose to about 184m in Q3 2026 against about 173m basic.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: 2026 revenue guide cut about 13% and the 2028 revenue target withdrawn (5 Nov 2026).
- Red: backlog down about 8% year on year and about 12% in one quarter; Q3 book-to-bill 0.7x.
- Red: management itself calls commercial performance weak, with Norwegian tender cancellations.
- Red: leverage is not trivial for a contractor. Net debt NOK 823m including leases (NOK 491m excluding leases), no reported cash at 30 Sep 2026, goodwill NOK 1.74bn against equity of NOK 1.70bn, Altman Z of 1.9.
- Red: the Bane NOR claim outcome is undisclosed after the negotiation window it named.
- Green: Q3 2026 EBIT up about 40% year on year, with Norway, Sweden and Kept all improving.
- Green: Finland revenue up 37%, and a second wave of Finnish light-rail contracts is secured, with production mainly from 2027.
- Green: margin targets extended (above 3.5% in 2027, above 5.0% in 2028) rather than cut.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- Replacing revenue targets with order-intake targets is a quiet admission that the top line is not under management's control; it also makes the 2027 test easy to observe (order intake above NOK 10bn).
- The 2025 switch from adjusted EBIT to reported EBIT, followed by a 2027-2028 target framed as adjusted EBIT, gives management room to exclude one-offs again. Watch for that.
- The tender pipeline is large, but the timing depends on public clients (Bane NOR, Trafikverket, Finnish cities). That is budget timing, not lost demand, but it moves the payoff to the right.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
**Trajectory: turning.** The business is moving from a volume story to a margin story, and only the margin part is proven. The single most important thing to weigh is whether order intake recovers by the Q4 2026 report on 17 February 2027. A contractor with improving margins but a shrinking backlog is a contractor whose 2027-28 revenue, and therefore profit, shrinks with it.

**Moat:** none of real width. Rail contracting is won by tender; the defensible parts are specialist rail skills, safety approvals and framework agreements with national rail owners, but returns have been negative (return on invested capital minus 6%) and margins of 3-5% leave no pricing power. Trend: stable. **Secular threat:** none in a structural sense. Nordic rail investment is a long-term tailwind; the risk is cyclical public-budget timing and project execution, not a force that shrinks the market. The cheapness is a mix of genuine execution risk and a fear print on order timing, not a value trap from a melting base.

Over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 it produced about $262M of free cash flow (cash from operations minus capital spending) against a market value of about $1.06B at $19.58 - roughly 4x free cash flow - with about $23M of net cash after its $75M revolver draw and $22M of leases. Management has beaten the top of its own profit range by $13-17M in every one of the last five quarters and cut stock-based pay to 6% of revenue a year ahead of plan, so the cash numbers are dependable. The ad decline is shallow: services advertising, about two-thirds of ad revenue, fell only 2% in Q3 2026 while cost per click still rose 2%, and Request-a-Quote projects grew about 10%, so consumer intent is still arriving. The new engine is real and fast: Other revenue rose 82% to a record $34M (a $136M run rate), with Hatch at a ~$37M run rate (+55%), Yelp Host handling a 2.5 million-call annual run rate (up 15x in a year) and data-licensing deals with OpenAI and Meta that turn the AI threat into a customer. Management targets a $250M run rate for Other revenue by end-2028; if it gets there, Other revenue offsets the ad decline and total revenue grows again. Capital return restarts in 2027 at more than 50% of free cash flow; at today's price that would retire roughly a tenth of the shares each year, after a 15% cut in the diluted share count over the past year. Conditions: services advertising declines stay in the low single digits, Other revenue keeps compounding above 50%, and the buyback restarts on schedule.
picks.bear_thesis: The core is now shrinking and the decline is accelerating, not stabilizing. Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $320-325M is about 11% below 2025, and Q3 net income fell 12% - EPS rose only because the share count fell 15%. Capital allocation was pro-cyclical: $200M of buybacks in 2026 at prices around $26, financed partly with a revolver, then paused near $19 to repay it, and management now flags acquisitions 'through a combination of cash and financing'. AI assistants and Google's AI answers can capture local search intent before it reaches Yelp, so the fall in clicks may be structural rather than a consumer slowdown. Insiders only sell (35 open-market sales, no buys; the CFO sold at $20.00 on 2026-10-15). Other revenue is only about 9% of sales, much of its growth is the acquired Hatch, and it is being run for growth at lower margins. If services advertising slides to -5% or worse in 2027, free cash flow after stock pay falls toward $120M and a 7x multiple is fair, putting the stock in the mid-teens. Confirmation: a services print worse than -4% or a 2027 revenue outlook below 2026.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the street is pricing Yelp as a terminally declining ad business - about 4x free cash flow and under 1x gross profit, with the newest targets cut to $17 (Morgan Stanley, 2026-10-13) and $23 (2026-11-06). picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure is visible. picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the Q4 2026 results show services advertising down no more than 2% and a 2027 revenue outlook at or above 2026, due about 2027-02-12.
