# BONESUPPORT Holding (BONEX.ST) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 26 October 2026 from five earnings calls (Q3 2025, 23 October 2025, through Q3 2026, 22 October 2026) and the screener's financial trajectory. All figures in Swedish krona (SEK).*

The short version: this is a credible management team running a genuinely scaling, cash-generative franchise, and the Q3 2026 report (22 October 2026) was the cleanest quarter yet. The numbers back the story. What the numbers do not back is today's share price, which has run about 41% in two weeks to SEK 339 and now discounts several more years of this pace.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The core story has been remarkably stable: CERAMENT G, an antibiotic-loaded injectable bone graft substitute, is the only product the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved in a category it created in 2022, and the company is converting US surgeons one segment at a time - foot and ankle first, then trauma, now revision joint replacement ("arthroplasty") and infection.

What has changed is the supporting evidence and the pipeline route:
- **Q3 2025 (23 October 2025):** a new CEO, Torbjorn Skold (from 1 September 2025), with "SEK 294 million" of sales, up 34% at constant exchange rates, and a 27% adjusted operating margin. Currency was the dominant optical drag.
- **Q4 2025 (24 February 2026):** the CERAMENT V filing (a vancomycin-loaded version) was moved by the FDA from the faster 510(k) route to the slower De Novo route (a review for an entirely new product category). Management reframed the delay as positioning "for a stronger long-term market entry". Spine was introduced via an early CERAMENT BVF launch.
- **Q1 2026 (22 April 2026):** US sales SEK 267 million, up 35% at constant currency; the SOLARIO trial (shorter systemic antibiotics when local antibiotics are used) was pitched as a coming "paradigm shift".
- **Q2 2026 (16 July 2026):** the first soft quarter. US CERAMENT G growth was "slightly lower than expected" because a handful of hospitals imposed usage pre-approvals ("go-stop-go", a cost-driven pause by hospital administrators). Growth eased to 30% at constant currency.
- **Q3 2026 (22 October 2026):** re-acceleration. Sales SEK 409 million, up 38% at constant currency; US CERAMENT G SEK 288 million against SEK 192 million a year earlier (about +50% reported); adjusted operating margin 34%; SOLARIO published in the New England Journal of Medicine; Medicare's improved payment for CERAMENT G infection cases in force from 1 October 2026; the CERAMENT V supplemental data package filed in September.

The thesis has expanded (infection, reimbursement, SOLARIO evidence) without any driver being quietly dropped. The one thing that contracted is the CERAMENT V timeline, which has slipped from a 510(k) clearance expected in 2025 to a De Novo reply now guided for "Q4 or in Q1".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Scalability of our business model" (Q2 and Q3 2026) | Adjusted operating margin 27% (Q3 2025) -> 26% (Q4 2025) -> 29% (Q2 2026) -> 34% (Q3 2026); trailing free cash flow (FCF, cash from operations less capital spending) SEK 329 million to 30 September 2026, up from SEK 263 million at June | Matches |
| Growth is real, currency only hides it | Revenue SEK 213 million (2021) -> SEK 1.17 billion (2025), a 3-year compound rate of about 53%; trailing twelve months (TTM) to September 2026 about SEK 1.40 billion | Matches |
| Self-funding, "We don't need any more capital" (Q3 2026) | Cash SEK 511 million against SEK 11 million of total debt at 30 September 2026, after buybacks; Altman-Z (a solvency score) 76 | Matches |
| Gross margin is durable | Gross margin 92.6%, stable; the CFO flagged some tariff and manufacturing cost pressure in Q3 2026 but called the reported US margin "a good indication of a sustained gross margin" | Matches, minor watch item |
| Earnings power | Reported EPS (earnings per share) 3.74 (2023, flattered by a tax-asset recognition) -> 2.01 (2024) -> 2.13 (2025) -> TTM diluted EPS 4.08; latest-quarter EPS up 167% | Matches the operating story; 2023 is a one-off, not a peak |
| Returns | Return on equity 4.4% and return on invested capital -1.7% in the screener are fiscal-year artefacts of a large cash pile and tax-asset effects; on operating profit the business is now earning well above its cost of capital | Story richer than the screener's return metrics, but justified |

Where the story runs ahead of the numbers: CERAMENT V. Management called it incremental worth "20%, 25% of total sales" (Q3 2026 Q&A), yet it has no approval and no fixed decision date.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising, with a dip in Q2 2026.**
- Q3 2025: "another strong quarter with solid execution".
- Q4 2025: defensive on CERAMENT V, upbeat on commercial traction ("exceptionally strong").
- Q1 2026: confident on SOLARIO ("a good and positive outlook").
- Q2 2026: the most defensive call - explaining pre-approvals as a known pattern ("We've seen this pattern before").
- Q3 2026: confident but disciplined. The CFO refused to extrapolate the record US quarter: "I do not think that you should see this as a sustained acceleration." That restraint is a credibility positive.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The company gave a full-year 2026 expectation in January 2026 of sales growth above 35% at constant currency. Delivery through nine months has been 35% (Q1), 30% (Q2) and 38% (Q3) at constant currency, so the year is tracking roughly at the bar, after the Q2 softness forced an outlook trim. The screener's earnings-beat rate is weak (2 of 6 quarters, 33%), but that reflects sell-side estimates swung by currency rather than missed company guidance. # AJ Bell plc (AJB.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Debate run 2026-10-26. Price used: 593p (FMP quote, London listing, pence sterling).*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript is available for AJ Bell from FMP, and the web-search budget for this run was exhausted, so this deep dive is built from primary company material fetched directly from AJ Bell's investor-relations site (the year-end trading update of 22 October 2026, the results calendar, and the company-hosted analyst consensus compiled 20 October 2026), plus FMP's reported half-year statements (six months to 31 March 2026) and the screener's multi-year financials. Quotes are limited to the 22 October 2026 trading update. Where a fact could not be verified it is said so.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story has been the same for three years and has only become louder: AJ Bell is a two-sided UK investment platform (one side serves financial advisers, the other serves do-it-yourself investors, called direct-to-consumer or D2C), and management has chosen to reinvest the scale benefits of a growing asset base into brand, marketing and pricing rather than bank them as margin. The FY26 year-end update (22 October 2026) frames the year as proof of that approach: the CEO calls the "record growth during the year" "clear evidence of the success of that approach", and the update stresses "underlying operational gearing" - the idea that each extra pound of assets costs little to serve.

What has shifted is the mix. The D2C side is now the growth engine: D2C customers rose 30% in FY26 to 602,000 against 7% growth on the advised side (194,000). Advised net inflows were only £1.9bn of the £9.7bn platform total. The narrative has quietly moved from "balanced two-sided platform" towards "a consumer brand that also serves advisers". The company also tidied the edges: it sold the Platinum SIPP and SSAS (self-invested pension) book, with £3.3bn of assets transferred to InvestAcc Group on 3 November 2025, booked a £13.8m exceptional gain in the first half of FY26, and is winding down the last third-party SIPP arrangement in the first quarter of FY27.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Record customer growth | Platform customers 796,000 at 30 Sep 2026, up 152,000 (24%) in the year; Q4 net adds 34,000, up 42% on the prior-year quarter | Corroborated |
| Accelerating flows | Platform net inflows £9.7bn in FY26, up 37% (FY25 £7.1bn); Q4 £2.5bn, up 47%. Gross inflows £21.5bn, up 36% | Corroborated |
| Scale converts to profit (operational gearing) | Revenue £146m (FY21) to £318m (FY25); net income £44m to £105m; net margin 33%. H1 FY26 revenue £183.0m vs £153.2m (+19%); reported pre-tax profit £92.8m includes the £13.8m disposal gain, so underlying is about £79m vs £68.8m (+15%) | Corroborated, but note underlying profit grew slower than revenue in H1 because of reinvestment |
| Assets growing on their own merit | Total assets under administration £127.6bn vs £108.2bn opening. Of the £19.4bn rise, about £13.0bn (13% of opening assets) came from favourable markets and only about £6.2bn from total net inflows after the SIPP transfer out | Partly - two-thirds of the asset growth in FY26 was the market, not the company |
| Capital-light, cash-generative | Net cash £155m at 31 Mar 2026 (cash £168m, only lease debt of £12m); ROE about 40%; buybacks ongoing (transaction-in-own-shares notices through 20 Oct 2026); share count down from about 413m (2024) to about 401m (H1 FY26) | Corroborated |

The screener's "TTM EPS 0.52" figure looks like a data artefact (it double-counts half-year periods); the consensus underlying diluted EPS for FY26 is 29.4p, which we use instead.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Rising, but deliberately measured. The year-end update is offensive in tone - it leads with record customers and flows, and says "as we enter the new financial year, we are continuing to invest in the business" and "our long-term growth opportunity remains significant". There is no defensive language about costs, macro or competition, and equally no new numerical guidance: revenue, profit and margin are held back for the 3 December 2026 results. That is consistent with the company's normal disclosure rhythm, not a red flag in itself.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
The company does not give hard profit guidance; the useful check is its record against the consensus it publishes. The screener shows 4 of the last 7 periods beating expectations (57%) - an average, not a sandbagger's, record. Multi-year delivery has been strong: EPS compounded about 24% a year over five years. The company's own consensus (compiled 20 Oct 2026, 14 contributing firms) has FY26 revenue £376.9m, underlying pre-tax profit £159.6m (a margin of about 42%) and underlying diluted EPS 29.42p, rising to £421.3m, £178.8m and 34.13p in FY27. H1 FY26 (revenue £183.0m, underlying profit about £79m) leaves a second half of roughly £194m revenue and £81m profit to hit FY26 consensus - achievable given the record Q4 flows and a 13% market tailwind. Reliability: Medium-High.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Without a transcript we cannot quote the Q&A. The questions that matter, and that the trading update does not answer, are: (1) how much revenue depends on interest earned on customer cash, and how much that falls if the Bank of England cuts; (2) whether the D2C growth is being bought with price cuts and marketing spend that compress revenue per pound of assets; (3) how the low-cost app competitors are affecting new-customer economics; (4) what the regulatory capital requirement is, i.e. how much of the £155m net cash is genuinely surplus. None is a known problem; all are unaddressed in the material available.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- 🟢 FY26 (to 30 Sep 2026): platform net inflows +37%, Q4 +47%, customers +24% - growth accelerating off a larger base.
- 🟢 Assets under management in its own funds a record £12.1bn, up 36% - a higher-margin product line gaining share of the platform.
- 🟢 Balance sheet: net cash, no borrowings, continuing buybacks; Altman-Z of 21.7 (a solvency score; anything above about 3 is safe).
- 🔴 About two-thirds of FY26 asset growth was market movement (£13.0bn), which reverses in a sell-off.
- 🔴 H1 FY26 underlying profit growth (about +15%) lagged revenue growth (+19%) - the reinvestment is real and is being paid for out of margin.
- 🔴 Advised side growing only 7% in customers and £1.9bn in net flows - the slower, stickier half of the business is the weaker half.
- 🔴 Free cash flow fell 10% in FY25 even as earnings rose - worth checking at the December results.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The language has moved from "margin" to "investment" and "operational gearing" - management is pre-positioning investors for a year in which costs rise with growth. The quiet exit from third-party and bespoke pension administration (Platinum SIPP sale, third-party SIPP wind-down) narrows the business to the two platforms, which simplifies it and should lift reported margins once the dis-synergies are gone. No management change is visible; Michael Summersgill (CEO) and Peter Birch (CFO) front the results.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: strengthening. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: at about 20 times FY26 and 17 times FY27 consensus earnings, the price already pays for the growth that the trading update just confirmed; what the director is underwriting is the durability of revenue per pound of assets (interest income on cash plus platform fees) as rates and competition move, not the customer count.

Moat: a narrow but real moat built on scale-cost advantages (a low cost to serve each extra pound of assets) and switching costs (moving a pension or ISA between platforms is slow and tedious, so customers rarely leave). Returns are high and still rising (ROE and ROIC near 40%, net margin widening every year since 2022), so the moat is not eroding. It is not wide either: retail platform pricing is competitive and the low-cost apps keep pressure on fees. The secular threat is fee compression from low-cost digital platforms - manageable, not terminal: AJ Bell is itself a low-cost platform taking share. The valuation is not a fear-print; it is a fully priced quality compounder.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Games Workshop Group (GAW.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. No earnings-call transcript exists for this name: Games Workshop does not hold analyst calls and publishes only regulatory statements (trading updates, half-year and annual reports). The paid data feed (FMP) had no transcript and no stock news for GAW.L, so this deep dive works from the company's dated statements as reported by the press and by Edison Investment Research, cross-checked against our screener's financials. Live price used: 16,890p (London listing, pence), FMP quote 2026-11-16.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story has barely changed in years, which is itself the point. Management describes one business: make Warhammer miniatures in-house in Nottingham, sell them through its own stores, independent stockists and online, and let others (video games, the Amazon screen deal) license the intellectual property. What has shifted across the last four reporting points is the emphasis on costs:
- **Half-year to 30 Nov 2025 (trading update 2025-11-20, results Jan 2026):** core revenue at least £310m versus £269.4m, licensing at least £16m versus £30.1m (the prior year had the Space Marine 2 game), profit before tax at least £135m. Reported later as revenue +10.9% to £332.1m and pre-tax profit £140.8m.
- **Full-year trading update (2026-05-22):** core revenue at least £625m, licensing at least £30m.
- **Full-year results (2026-07-28):** core revenue +10.9% to £626.8m; total revenue about £660m; pre-tax profit a record £275.7m (+4.9%). New language on costs: about £13m of new US tariffs expected in the year to May 2027 (after reclaiming £7.8m of the earlier £12m once the US Supreme Court struck the earlier duties down), higher plastic input costs linked to the Middle East conflict, and stepped-up investment. The cash buffer the board keeps before declaring dividends rose to £120m from £100m. Shares fell as much as 6.5% that day.
- **September 2026 AGM-season trading update (2026-09-16, per our own prior record):** in line with expectations. We could not retrieve the text again this week.

The arc runs from "growth plus a licensing windfall" (FY25) to "core growth, licensing normalising, margins under modest cost pressure" (FY27).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence in our financials | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The core hobby keeps growing | Revenue £415m (FY22) to £660m (FY26); 3-year compound growth about 12%; FY26 +6.8% total, +10.9% core | Matches |
| A high-margin, capital-light model | Gross margin 72.5% (stable); net margin 31%; free-cash-flow margin 33%; return on invested capital about 51% | Matches |
| Conservative balance sheet | Net cash £127m including £44m of lease liabilities (2026-05-31); Altman-Z 30 | Matches |
| Shareholders get the surplus cash | Dividend policy pays out cash above the £120m buffer; FY26 earnings per share about 623p | Matches; buffer raised, a minor tightening |
| Licensing is a growing second engine | FY25 licensing £30.1m H1 alone; H1 FY26 only £16m; Edison models no licensing growth in FY27 | Lumpy, not a steady engine |

One data caution: the screener's "TTM diluted EPS 12.15" is inconsistent with every reported figure (FY26 EPS about 623p; Edison FY27 forecast 611p). We treat it as a feed error and do not use it.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable. Chief executive Kevin Rountree's July 2026 line was that the company and the hobby are in good shape. The tone is the usual sparse, numbers-first style; it did not turn defensive, but for the first time in several years the outlook led with cost items (tariffs, plastic, investment) rather than with growth.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
High. The company guides with "not less than" floors and then clears them: H1 FY26 pre-tax profit guided at least £135m, delivered £140.8m; FY26 core revenue guided at least £625m, delivered £626.8m; FY26 pre-tax profit came in about £276m against an indicated £265m floor (Edison, 2026-07-29). The screener shows earnings beats in 2 of the last 2 periods. A mild sandbagging pattern is visible and consistent.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
There are no calls, so pressure shows up in broker notes and the share price: (a) whether core growth slows to mid-single digits now that the FY24-FY25 surge has passed; (b) licensing timing, which is lumpy and depends on third-party game launches; (c) the cost stack - tariffs, plastic, wages - against a very high starting margin; (d) valuation - Edison noted on 2026-07-29 that the price was "clearly discounting further upgrades" at about 33x forecast earnings. A shareholder revolt was reported ahead of the 2026 AGM (pay-related), a governance irritant rather than a business issue.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- 🔴 FY27 consensus (Edison) has pre-tax profit slightly down (£270m versus £276m) and earnings per share down to about 611p: the first flat-to-down year in a while.
- 🔴 Licensing fell by about half in H1 FY26; no near-term replacement of the Space Marine 2 windfall is in our evidence.
- 🔴 Cost headwinds (about £13m tariffs, higher plastic) in FY27.
- 🟢 Core revenue +10.9% in FY26 despite a high base.
- 🟢 Gross margin held through the 2021-22 inflation (67.5% to 67.9%) - real pricing power.
- 🟢 Net cash, no adjusted earnings, consistent guidance beats.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
Raising the dividend cash buffer to £120m is a small signal that management wants more room for investment and cost volatility. The new emphasis on "investment in infrastructure, geographic expansion and customer engagement" (per Edison's read of the FY26 report) suggests operating margin is being deliberately traded for reach. No management changes of note in our evidence.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: stable. The franchise is intact and the balance sheet is clean; what has changed in 2026 is that the earnings line has flattened (FY27 forecast roughly flat) while the stock still trades on a premium multiple. The single most important thing to weigh: at 16,890p the shares cost about 27-28x forecast FY27 earnings for a year in which earnings are expected to be flat - so the return depends on growth resuming in FY28 and beyond, not on today's numbers.

Moat: intangible brand plus scale and vertical integration (a 40-year intellectual property universe, its own factory and stores). Width: wide - return on invested capital about 51% and gross margin stable at 72%; operating margin dipping slightly in FY27 on costs is not erosion of the franchise. Secular threat: manageable - 3D printing of miniatures and digital alternatives are long-standing risks that have not shown up in the numbers; AI-generated content does not replace the physical hobby. The cheapness question does not arise: the stock is not cheap, it is a premium compounder that has de-rated from about 23,500p to 16,890p.

Management credibility 5 of 5 · trajectory steady · a wide, durable moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Dave Inc. (DAVE) - Deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-09. Sources: five earnings calls (Q3 2025 on 2025-11-04 through Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04), the Q3 2026 press release (2026-11-04), the screener's financial trajectory, and FMP prices. Live price $282.65 (Nasdaq, USD, 2026-11-09).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Dave is a US consumer neobank whose economic engine is ExtraCash, a small-dollar, single-pay cash advance (average size about $218-225) underwritten from the member's linked bank account, plus a monthly subscription and, from 2026, the Dave Flex card.

- **Q3 2025 to Q4 2025 (2025-11-04, 2026-03-03):** the story was "underwriting is our moat". CashAI v5 drove credit improvements, guidance was raised every quarter, and management announced the move of ExtraCash receivables to Coastal Community Bank in an off-balance-sheet structure (the bank holds the receivables, Dave keeps the full economic exposure) to free up liquidity and lower funding costs. Management noted 2025 opened with $415-435M revenue guidance and closed about 30% above that midpoint.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-05-06):** Dave Flex is introduced as the next growth leg, explicitly kept out of guidance. The pricing story begins: the $15 fee cap is removed for new members.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-08-05):** the fee cap is removed for most grandfathered members and raised to $20 for the rest from late August; Coastal funding begins. The stock gapped down on an earnings miss the next day (from $430 to about $386).
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-04):** revenue growth accelerated to 31%, a record 1.1M new members, and the third guidance raise of the year. But the tone now carries more explanation: a higher-than-planned provision for credit losses, a sequential gross-margin step-down, and an admission that collections improvements "pulled forward" recoveries rather than lowering ultimate losses.

The arc is expansion, then monetization (pricing), now scale (marketing up about 50%). The story has not shrunk; what has changed is that the earnings leverage is now being spent on growth and on credit, so adjusted EPS flattened year on year.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Revenue growth accelerating" (Q3 2026) | Q3 revenue $197.7M, +31% y/y (from $150.8M); FY2025 revenue $554M, +60% | Matches |
| "Strong credit performance" (Q3 2026) | 28-day past-due rate (share of advances unpaid 28 days after due) 2.09% vs 2.15% a year ago, below 2% in September; but provision for credit losses rose 22% y/y to $36.6M, or 18.5% of revenue, up 1.7 points sequentially | Partly. Early delinquency is improving; the loss provision, which is what hits earnings, is rising faster than the early-delinquency metric implies |
| "Adjusted EBITDA growing faster than revenue" | Adj. EBITDA $81.5M, +39%, 41% margin | Matches |
| Earnings per share momentum | Adjusted diluted EPS $4.39 vs $4.45 a year ago (-1%), missed consensus of $4.45; GAAP diluted EPS $3.30 vs $6.34 (the prior year carried a large warrant gain) | Diverges. EBITDA growth is not reaching EPS this year (marketing, tax, Coastal funding cost) |
| "Coastal frees up liquidity" | Cash and investments $315M (from $254M at June 30); the $75M Victory Park facility was repaid in early October 2026; Coastal-funded receivables $159M (from $93M) | Matches, but Coastal funding costs took about 100 basis points off gross margin |
| Capital return | About $20M of repurchases in Q3, $88M authorization left | Modest relative to a $3.2B market value |
| FCF quality | Screener: FCF margin 52%, P/FCF 13.9x | Lender cash-flow accounting flatters FCF (advances flow through investing); treat as indicative only |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a defensive edge emerging.** Through Q1 2026 the language was offensive ("eighth consecutive quarter of increasing guidance on all metrics"). By Q3 2026 management spent prepared remarks explaining provision and gross-margin drivers, and the CFO conceded on collections: "in hindsight, we did not really change much around the decisioning process... to really expect meaningful loss rate impact". The CEO steered investors to September's sub-2% delinquency as "what I would be using to assess credit performance". That is a reasonable point but also a choice of the most flattering metric.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High for the company's own guidance: 2025 finished about 30% above the original revenue midpoint and near double the original EBITDA guidance; 2026 guidance has been raised every quarter, most recently to revenue $746-750M (from $725-735M), adjusted EBITDA $327-330M (from $315-325M) and adjusted EPS $17.45-17.65 (from $17.00-17.50). Management describes a deliberately conservative philosophy ("numbers that we have very high confidence in delivering upon"). The weak spot is versus the street: Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 both missed consensus EPS, so the street is now running ahead of management on quarterly earnings timing. Reliability: High on the company's guide, Medium against consensus.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Why not push credit harder?** Analysts on 2026-11-04 asked why the improving delinquency is not used to lend more; management pointed to testing limits above $600 and up to $1,000.
- **Collections pull-forward:** the loss benefit analysts expected did not carry through; management called it "a learning".
- **Coastal economics:** whether Dave will balance-sheet more of the book; answer: Coastal will fund "the vast majority".
- **DOJ matter:** each call repeats "no updates and continue to vigorously defend our position" since the case entered discovery. No analyst pushed on settlement scenarios in the transcripts, which is itself a gap.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: provision rose to 18.5% of revenue in Q3 2026 (+1.7 points sequentially) and the collections gain proved to be timing, not lower losses (2026-11-04).
- Red: two straight adjusted-EPS misses against consensus (2026-08-05, 2026-11-04), with adjusted EPS down 1% y/y in Q3 2026 despite 31% revenue growth.
- Red: the Justice Department lawsuit (originally an FTC matter over fees and disclosures) is still in discovery; meanwhile the company removed the fee cap through 2026, i.e. raised the effective price of the very product under scrutiny.
- Red: securities-law-firm "investigations" announced 2026-11-05/06 after the 18% one-day drop; these are routine after a sharp fall and carry little information on their own.
- Green: revenue re-accelerated to 31% with a record 1.1M new members, and customer acquisition cost rose only 14% while marketing spend rose about 50% (2026-11-04).
- Green: net monetization rate (revenue per dollar advanced after credit losses) 5.2%, the highest in five years; September 28-day delinquency below 2% after CashAI v6.
- Green: balance sheet de-risked; the Victory Park facility repaid in October 2026, cash up to $315M.

- The member count was redefined in Q3 2026 (low-engagement savings-only users excluded, prior periods recast). Harmless if recast as stated, but definition changes deserve watching.
- "Invest to maximize gross profit dollars rather than minimize CAC" signals management will keep trading near-term EPS for growth while returns hold above the cost of capital.
- Pricing language moved from "fee cap" to "all customers roughly on the same fee structure" via a 5% additional-draw fee: a quiet price harmonization upward.
- Dave Flex is consistently framed as a 2027 second-half contributor, not 2026: this keeps the 2027 estimate dependent on ExtraCash.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** The business is still growing fast and profitably, guidance keeps rising, and the balance sheet is cleaner than a year ago. What changed on 2026-11-04 is the cost of that growth: credit provisions and funding costs are absorbing the operating leverage, so earnings per share stalled this year.

The single most important thing to weigh: the credit-loss rate. If provisions settle back toward 17% of revenue as CashAI v6 seasons (September's sub-2% delinquency is the early sign), the 2027 earnings path near $20 per share is intact; if they keep rising with larger advance sizes, the business is a fast-growing lender whose returns are being competed or regulated away.

**Moat:** narrow. The edge is underwriting data (CashAI on linked-account cash flows) and scale in small-dollar advances, visible in record net monetization and stable delinquency while advance sizes grow. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Universal Health Services (UHS) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Coverage window: five earnings calls, 2025-10-28 (Q3 2025) through 2026-10-28 (Q3 2026). Live price used: $180.65 (NYSE, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

Takeaway first: UHS is a well-financed, buyback-heavy hospital operator whose reported growth over the last two years leaned heavily on state Medicaid supplemental payments (extra funding states route to hospitals), and whose underlying operating results have now fallen short of management's own internal expectations for three quarters running. The business is not breaking, but the earnings base for 2027 is flat-to-down, and the 2028+ Medicaid cuts are a known, quantified-in-part headwind.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-28)** - offense. Adjusted EPS of $5.69 up 53% year on year; 2025 EPS guidance midpoint raised 6% to $21.80, helped by $90M from the newly approved Washington, D.C. supplemental Medicaid program. The story: acute-care demand strong, new hospitals (Cedar Hill in D.C., West Henderson in Nevada) ramping, Palm Beach Gardens opening spring 2026, outpatient build-out in both segments.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-26)** - adjusted EPS $5.88; acute same-facility adjusted admissions flat in the quarter. 2026 guidance issued.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-28)** - steady: behavioral wage inflation moderating from ~8% (2025) to 6-7%; turnover "improving meaningfully".
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-28)** - the turn to defense. Adjusted EPS $5.98 (+12%), but only because of a $100M out-of-period Florida payment not in guidance; ex that, EBITDA "fell short of our internal expectations" by ~$63M (liability reserves $28M, the San Antonio behavioral facility $20M, Cedar Hill ramp $15M). Volume guidance trimmed 50bp; 2026 adjusted EBITDA net of minority interests guided to $2.61-2.72B.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-28)** - adjusted EPS $5.22, down 8%. Underlying EBITDA again "below our internal expectations despite modest sequential improvement". Full-year guidance reiterated but now "towards the lower end". Talkspace (acquired 2026-08-17) becomes a featured growth pillar. The vocabulary has moved from "growth" to "offsets": revenue-cycle consulting, AI-driven length-of-stay control, payer-mix shift away from Medicaid.

Growth drivers quietly de-emphasized: big de novo hospitals ("not having any of these big de novo projects in the pipeline over the next several years"; capex trending to ~$800M from ~$1B). Introduced: Talkspace virtual outpatient care, an explicit Medicaid-cut defense narrative.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (quarter) | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Earnings power compounding (2025 calls) | EPS 9.14 (2022) -> 10.23 -> 16.82 -> 23.10 (2025); TTM diluted EPS 23.86; latest-quarter EPS down 9% year on year | True through 2025, but much of the 2024-25 lift is supplemental Medicaid money, some of it out-of-period (one-time catch-ups). 2026 is flat. |
| Acute-care demand is strong (Q3 2026) | Same-facility adjusted admissions +4.9%, ED visits +4.6%; but surgeries -0.7% and revenue per adjusted admission -1.7% reported | Volume claim holds; mix is shifting to lower-paying medical admissions as procedures move to surgery centers and offices - a structural, not cyclical, drift. |
| Costs well managed (every call) | Acute wages per adjusted admission +2.1%, supplies -2.3% (Q3 2026); behavioral wages per patient day +3.6% vs revenue per day +2.1% | Acute: true. Behavioral: wages still outrunning price - margin squeeze, though moderating. |
| De novo hospitals ramping (Q3 2025: Cedar Hill to "exit this year at breakeven or better") | Cedar Hill break-even now first half 2027, after Q4 2026 previously; still loss-making a year after Q3 2025's promise | Repeatedly missed. The $80-100M of 2026 losses at de novos plus San Antonio is the recovery lever management is now leaning on. |
| Shareholder returns (all calls) | $690M of buybacks year to date 2026; 1.35M shares bought in Q3 for $242M (~$179/share); $735M authorization left; leverage 2.17x | True and the strongest corroborated claim. Share count falls ~5-8% a year. |
| Cash generation | Q3 operating cash flow $637M vs $381M; FY2025 FCF -24% on heavy capex; TTM FCF $1.12B | Improving as capex steps down from ~$1B toward ~$800M. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Rating: **Declining, then stabilizing.** Q3 2025 was confident ("increasing the midpoint of our 2025 adjusted EPS guidance by 6%"). By Q2 2026 the prepared remarks itemized shortfalls; by Q3 2026 management structured its remarks around "reported results and unusual items" and pre-announced 2027 headwinds: $175-200M of non-repeating Medicaid supplemental money, at least $15M from health-insurance exchange losses, and unquantifiable Medicaid work-requirement effects. The language is now explicitly defensive ("offset opportunities", "challenges that will come, especially from OB-3"), but specific and candid rather than evasive.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- 2025: raised and delivered (EPS $23.10 vs the raised $21.80 midpoint) - but the beat came from supplemental programs, not operations.
- 2026: EBITDA guidance cut in July to $2.61-2.72B; volume guidance trimmed; now pointed to the low end. Each of Q2 and Q3 underlying results missed internal plans; out-of-period Medicaid payments masked the misses in reported numbers.
- The screener shows 6 of 7 quarterly beats (86%), which flatters the record: several beats were supplemental-payment windfalls not in guidance.
- De novo timelines: missed twice (Cedar Hill).
- No sign of sandbagging; if anything, operating plans have been a touch optimistic.
**Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- 2027 supplemental-payment cliff (AJ Rice, UBS, Q3 2026) - now answered with a number, $175-200M, which is roughly 7% of 2026 EBITDA.
- Slow de novo ramps (Ann Hynes, Mizuho, Q3 2026: "I do not remember a time where the acute care hospitals are ramping below expectations").
- Medicaid work requirements: management declines to estimate; gives exposure instead (expansion-state Medicaid ~15% of acute adjusted admissions, ~30% of behavioral patient days) and leans on medical-frailty exemptions.
- Surgical softness: attributed to procedures leaving the hospital - an honest answer that concedes a structural drift.
- Professional and general liability reserves: recurring additions every quarter ($28M Q2, $26M Q3 for the Cumberland, Virginia settlement) - analysts have stopped treating these as one-offs.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: underlying EBITDA below internal plan in Q2 and Q3 2026.
- Red: 2027 faces a known $175-200M Medicaid supplemental headwind before the larger 2028+ provider-tax cuts under the 2025 budget law (OB-3).
- Red: recurring liability reserve top-ups and behavioral-health litigation; the San Antonio (Laurel Ridge) facility lost Medicare certification and recertification is only "expected during 2027".
- Red: open-market insider activity is all selling (0 buys, 5 sells, 5,456 shares) - small, but no insider is buying at these prices.
- Red: Talkspace bought at roughly 74 times its FY2025 EBITDA (prior check, 2026 filings) - a richly priced bet with benefits "over the next 12-24 months".
- Green: acute volumes accelerating (+2.9% Q2 to +4.9% Q3 2026); capacity additions working.
- Green: acute labor and supply costs under control; contract labor falling.
- Green: aggressive, well-funded buybacks with leverage still at 2.17x, inside the 2-3x target.
- Green: capex falling toward ~$800M frees roughly $150-200M a year of extra free cash flow.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The reporting vocabulary changed from "same-facility EBITDA growth" to "excluding out-of-period benefit from both periods" - management itself now separates windfall from run-rate, which is honest and tells you the run-rate is the softer number.
- Payer-mix strategy has become a Medicaid-avoidance strategy: outpatient behavioral (Talkspace, Thousand Branches) is framed as shifting volume to commercial and Medicare.
- "AI" appears for the first time as a cost lever (length-of-stay control, revenue cycle) - defensive use, not growth.
- Capex framing ("not having any of these big de novo projects in the pipeline") signals a shift from building to harvesting - supportive of buybacks.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: **STABLE** - the operating base is flat, not shrinking; volumes are improving while price and mix soften and government funding steps down. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly (buybacks near $180, falling capex) with one questionable outlier (Talkspace).

The single most important thing to weigh: the 2027 earnings base. With 2026 adjusted EBITDA near $2.61B, a $175-200M supplemental headwind, ~$15M of exchange losses and only a partial recovery of $80-100M de novo/San Antonio losses, 2027 EBITDA is roughly flat to slightly down - so per-share growth will come almost entirely from buybacks. The stock at ~$181 already prices that.

Moat: regulatory-license plus local scale (certificate-of-need licensing in several states, dense local networks in Las Vegas, D.C. and elsewhere, and the largest US behavioral-health footprint). Returns are modest (ROIC 9%, ROE 15.4%) and stable rather than falling - a **narrow** moat with a **stable** trend. Secular threat: reimbursement compression (Medicaid supplemental and provider-tax cuts from 2028, exchange disenrollment, work requirements) plus the steady migration of procedures out of hospitals. That is **material** but not terminal: hospitals remain essential, and roughly 85% of acute admissions and 70% of behavioral days sit outside expansion-state Medicaid. The cheapness is mostly a fair price for a flat-earnings, policy-exposed business plus a buyback, not a deep mispricing.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

# Sezzle (SEZL) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*Five earnings calls reviewed: Q2 2025 (9 Aug 2025) through Q3 2026 (4 Nov 2026). Prices in US dollars, Nasdaq listing; live price $150.84 on 9 Nov 2026.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across five calls the core story has stayed remarkably constant: Sezzle is a "buy now, pay later" (BNPL — splitting a purchase into a few interest-free instalments) provider that makes most of its money from consumer subscriptions rather than from merchant fees, and it sells itself as a profitable growth company. What has changed is the engine underneath.

- **Q2 2025 (Aug 2025):** the story was marketing reinvestment and the new pay-per-use product, On-Demand. Marketing jumped from $1.0M to $8.8M a year earlier, with a stated "6-month payback period on our CAC" (customer acquisition cost). Monthly On-Demand and Subscribers (the company's headline user metric) rose 62% year on year.
- **Q3 2025 (Nov 2025):** the first candid course correction. Management admitted On-Demand "didn't deliver like we hoped on conversions at the point of sale or over to subscription", that subscribers had shrunk from 529,000 to 484,000 as On-Demand cannibalised them, and pivoted marketing back to subscriptions (568,000 by quarter end). Small subscription price rises ($1-2 a month) were described as "an inflationary type increase". The antitrust suit against Shopify and a refinancing of the expensive credit line (SOFR plus 6.75 percentage points) were flagged as side projects.
- **Q4 2025 (Feb 2026):** a new CFO (Lee Brading, previously head of investor relations), a 6-for-1 stock split, a $50M buyback completed plus a further $100M authorised, and first talk of a bank charter ("industrial loan company"). 2026 guidance: 25-30% revenue growth, $170M adjusted net income, adjusted earnings per share raised from $4.35 to $4.70.
- **Q1-Q2 2026:** product proliferation — Pay-in-5, a Canadian virtual card, longer-term lending, SezzleCash (cash advances to subscribers, launched June) and Sezzle Send (person-to-person payments). Guidance raised twice more, to $5.25 by August.
- **Q3 2026 (4 Nov 2026):** the story has matured into "the pieces of our strategy work together". Subscribers reached 955,000 (+68% year on year), transaction frequency 7.8 a quarter versus 6.5, revenue +42.6%, net income +79%. Guidance raised a fourth time (adjusted EPS $5.45-5.50) and a first look at 2027 ($7.20, about +31%). The bank-charter ambition has hardened into an actual application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (filed 22 Oct 2026).

The thesis has expanded (from a checkout product to a "financial companion" with cash, transfers and a bank charter) without dropping the core.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Profitable growth company" (every call) | Net income went from a $75M loss (2021) to $133M profit (2025); trailing-twelve-month (TTM) diluted EPS $5.21; quarterly net income $26.7M (Q3 2025) to $47.8M (Q3 2026) | Matches |
| Revenue growth outruns volume because of subscriptions | Q3 2026 revenue +42.6% vs transaction volume +34.9% (7.7 points faster) | Matches |
| Margin target "near the upper end" of range | Revenue less transaction costs at 64.7% of revenue in Q3 2026; gross margin 85% in the screener | Matches, with a caveat: Q4 2025 cost of revenue was booked as a negative $7.8M, which flatters that quarter's gross profit — accounting noise to watch |
| Disciplined marketing, 6-month payback | Marketing rose to $19.4M in Q2 2026 as a declared test, then cut to $15.9M in Q3 while still adding 101,000 subscribers | Matches; management did what it said |
| Credit is controllable ("we can reduce limits across the board") | Q3 2026 press coverage notes credit losses fell as a share of volume; Piotroski 9/9; Altman-Z 18.9 | Matches so far — but untested in a real consumer recession |
| Capital returns | $50M buyback done, $100M authorised Dec 2025; diluted share count fell from about 36.2M (Q3 2025) to 34.8M (Q3 2026) | Matches |
| Insider alignment ("we're all investors in the company") | Open-market insider record: 2 buys of 379 shares vs 67 sells of 155,461 shares | Diverges — insiders are steady net sellers |

Cash flow is real: TTM free cash flow of about $381M on a $5.1B market value. Net debt is small, about $32M (borrowings $102M less cash $70M, excluding leases).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising, but more measured.** In Q2 2025 the tone was combative ("we are upsetting the traditional norm", the Rule of 100 scoreboard at 165). Q3 2025 was the most self-critical call, owning the On-Demand misfire. By Q3 2026 the tone is calmer and more specific: management is giving honest early reads on weaker products ("Sezzle Send... still needs some fine-tuning"), calling the Q2 marketing push "a test, not necessarily a new run rate", and closing on "character" in lending rather than a growth brag. Guidance has become more specific over time (now a full-year 2027 EPS figure two months before 2026 ends), which is a confidence signal.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

| Given | Target | Delivered / now |
|---|---|---|
| Aug 2025 | 2025 adjusted net income +85% | Beaten — 2025 net income $133M, guidance exceeded on top and bottom line (Feb 2026) |
| Nov 2025 | Preliminary 2026 adjusted EPS $4.35 | Raised to $4.70 (Feb), then $5.25 (Aug), now $5.45-5.50 (Nov 2026) |
| Feb 2026 | 2026 revenue growth 25-30% | Now about 42.5% |

Seven of seven quarters beat (100%). The pattern is classic sandbagging: conservative opening guides, raised every quarter. **Reliability: High.** The risk this creates is that the 2027 figure of $7.20 will also be read by the market as a floor, not a midpoint.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Gross-margin durability:** TD Cowen asked in Q3 2026 whether the 65% level is the new norm; management would not commit, citing lower-margin new products (Send, Cash) with higher early loss rates. That is an honest non-answer, and it is the main forward-margin risk.
- **Marketing efficiency:** asked twice (Q2 and Q3 2026). Answered with specifics.
- **Take-rate volatility:** Q2 2025 (B. Riley) — explained by seasonal revenue recognition; Q1 should not be annualised.
- **Competition:** answered every call as "more of the same"; Klarna's higher-priced subscription noted. Analysts have not pressed on Affirm or Apple-style entrants, and management does not volunteer.
- **Shopify antitrust suit:** "no update"; timeline "upwards of 3 to 5 years". Treat as an option, not a catalyst.
- **Not addressed:** consumer-credit sensitivity in a slowdown with sticky inflation, and the regulatory path for cash advances (SezzleCash is a product type that has drawn regulatory scrutiny in the wider industry).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Persistent insider selling (67 open-market sells vs 2 buys).
- 🔴 The On-Demand misstep (Q3 2025) shows product bets can cannibalise the core.
- 🔴 New products (SezzleCash, Send) carry lower margins and higher early loss rates (CFO, Q3 2026).
- 🔴 Funding is still an expensive credit line; the bank charter that would fix it is an application, not an approval.
- 🔴 Q4 2025 negative cost-of-revenue line — an accounting oddity to watch.
- 🟢 Subscribers +68% to 955,000; transaction frequency at a record 7.8 a quarter (Q3 2026).
- 🟢 Fourth guidance raise in a year; first 2027 outlook at +31% EPS growth.
- 🟢 Marketing cut quarter on quarter while subscriber growth continued (Q3 2026).
- 🟢 Share count shrinking through buybacks; tiny net debt; strong free cash flow.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The headline metric keeps being redefined: "MODS" (Q4 2024), then subscribers, now "total transaction volume" including cash advances and transfers. Each redefinition flatters the growth line slightly; the underlying trend is still strong.
- "Industrial loan company" (Feb 2026) became a full national bank charter (Oct 2026) — a more ambitious, more regulated path. Management now says the process leans toward holding cash, which mutes buybacks for a while.
- A President (co-founder Paul Paradis) joined the Q3 2026 call — deeper bench on show ahead of a regulator review.
- AI language moved from customer-service cost savings (2025) to distribution through AI shopping assistants via the Anywhere card (Q3 2026).

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: strengthening.** The business is executing ahead of its own plan, and management has been candid about what is not working.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** this is a consumer lender priced as a compounder. At $150.84 the stock trades at about 27 times 2026 guided EPS and about 21 times the 2027 figure. Those are fair-to-full multiples for a business whose earnings depend on short-duration consumer credit that has never been through a real recession at this scale, run by insiders who sell steadily. The quality is real; the discount is not.

**Moat:** narrow. Sources are a subscription relationship with switching costs, eight-plus years of repayment data, and a lean cost base (very high return on equity, rising). The screener's 1.7% return on invested capital is not meaningful for a lender funded by receivables debt; margins are expanding, not falling, so the moat is stable to widening, not eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Sezzle is the disrupter in payments, not the disrupted; the structural risks are regulatory (BNPL rules, cash-advance scrutiny) and competitive (Affirm, Klarna, card issuers' instalment features), not a terminal decline of its base. The current price is not a fear print.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

First-quarter revenue grew 17.4% at constant exchange rates (30 April 2026); the first half grew 10.4% to CHF 646.2 million (28 August), with operating profit before depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) up 13.8% at constant rates to CHF 120.1 million and that margin up to 18.6% from 18.1%; net profit attributable to shareholders rose 22.5% at constant rates to CHF 79.1 million. And on 5 November 2026 the third quarter came in at CHF 310.2 million, up 10.2% at constant rates, taking nine months to CHF 956.5 million, up 10.3%. The worry that growth had faded to mid single digits in the second quarter did not survive the next print.

The longer record supports the claim: diluted earnings per share went from CHF 8.48 in 2021 to CHF 16.73 in 2025, close to 18.5% a year, on revenue up from CHF 876 million to CHF 1.12 billion, with return on equity around 22%. The balance sheet is an asset: CHF 181.6 million of company-stated net cash at 30 June 2026 (CHF 265.8 million including the share of joint-venture cash), almost no goodwill (CHF 51 million on a CHF 1.66 billion balance sheet), and solvency scores that agree.

The currency drag is easing. The franc's strength cost CHF 9.5 million of EBITDA in the first half alone, but the dollar has since recovered to about CHF 0.819 (9 November 2026) from a 52-week low near CHF 0.760, and the yen is also above its 200-day average against the franc. If that holds, the second half will translate less badly, and reported growth will start to look like underlying growth.

The environment helps the business operationally. Interdealer brokers are paid on volume and on disagreement, and a reflationary backdrop - growth up, inflation sticky, positive real interest rates - keeps rates and currency markets busy. This thesis does not need a rate cut. Capital returns are rising: the dividend has gone CHF 6.15 to 6.80 to 7.50 over three payment years, and a new buyback of up to 300,000 shares runs from 2 June 2026 to 1 June 2029, larger than the 251,574 shares retired under the 2023 programme. Finally, the data and analytics arm grows at a double-digit rate and has never been sized; at TP ICAP the equivalent business is the most valuable part of the group.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case is mostly arithmetic.

First, the stock is not cheap, and the screening data that said it was is broken. The company reports twice a year, and our vendor files the half-year statements under quarterly labels, so the trailing earnings of CHF 33.53 a share and trailing free cash flow of CHF 253 million in our input both add up two years. True trailing diluted earnings are CHF 17.88 a share. At CHF 244.50 the stock is on about 13.7 times trailing earnings and about 12.9 times our CHF 18.91 estimate for 2026 - not the 7.3 times the raw input implies. The reported +21.5% free-cash-flow growth is the same kind of artefact; like-for-like, first-half free cash flow fell about 12%.

Second, once the earnings figure is right, the company is dearer than its closest peers. On 9 November 2026 TP ICAP trades at 309.8 pence, about 12.3 times trailing diluted earnings of 25.18 pence, with a yield near 5%; BGC Group at USD 10.97 is roughly 8 times 2026 earnings. Only Marex is dearer. Tradition yields about 3%.

Third, earnings quality in the first half was weaker than the headline. Reported operating profit was CHF 88.0 million against CHF 88.2 million and the reported operating margin fell to 14.7% from 15.2%. Reported net profit still rose 12.6%, but about 71% of the increase came from below the operating line: about CHF 4.0 million more from associates and joint ventures (the Japanese affiliate Gaitame absorbing Money Partners Group) and about CHF 2.3 million from a tax rate that fell to 23.4% from 26.1%. Neither repeats at that rate.

Fourth, the whole re-rating case rests on one variable the company does not control: the Swiss franc. The gap between 22.5% constant-currency and 12.6% reported profit growth is the currency, and the third-quarter release headlines only the constant-currency figure. A risk-off episode that bids the franc would reopen the gap.

Fifth, nothing forces the market to close any gap that does exist. The company is controlled by Financiere Vermeer NV, has no analyst coverage, holds no earnings calls, issues no guidance, and trades a few thousand shares a day (3,361 on 9 November 2026) against a CHF 1.86 billion market value. Discounts on securities like this can last for years.
picks.consensus_delta:
There is no sell-side consensus to argue with: no analyst price targets or ratings for this listing in our data services, no earnings calls and no guidance, and turnover of a few thousand shares a day. What the market prices is the reported Swiss-franc numbers rather than the constant-currency ones - revenue up 2.2% and operating profit flat in the first half. The bull position is that this misses an underlying business growing about 10%, a rate the 5 November 2026 third-quarter release (+10.2% at constant rates) reconfirmed. Our view is that the market is not obviously wrong: a franc shareholder receives francs, and until the currency stops working against the company constant-currency growth is an explanation, not a cash flow.

The disagreement we do hold is with our own screening data, which made two false claims pointing the same way. The first is that the stock trades at roughly 7.3 times trailing earnings; it trades at about 13.7 times, because the CHF 33.53 figure sums four half-year statements. The second is that it is cheap against its peers; it is not - TP ICAP is on about 12.3 times trailing with a yield near 5% and BGC on roughly 8 times 2026 earnings. Correcting both removes most of the case for buying today.

The one thing we think the tape under-prices cuts against the bulls: about 71% of the first-half reported profit growth came from associates and a lower tax rate, while reported core operating profit was flat.
picks.valley_of_death:
There is no solvency risk in the months just ahead: no cash burn, no maturity wall, no covenant. The company holds CHF 328 million of cash and short-term investments against CHF 245 million of total debt including CHF 52 million of leases, generated roughly CHF 70 million of free cash flow in the first half and paid CHF 57 million of dividends from it, with a payout around 45% of earnings.

The risk over the next three to nine months is to the share price, in three parts. First, the franc: a risk-off episode that strengthens the franc against the dollar and the yen would again make reported second-half results look stagnant, even though the dollar has recovered to about CHF 0.819 from a 52-week low near CHF 0.760. Second, earnings quality: the 23.4% tax rate and the step-up in associate income flattered the first half; if either normalises while reported revenue is flat, full-year 2026 earnings per share can land below the roughly CHF 18.91 we model when the full-year results arrive around late March 2027. Third, illiquidity: with a few thousand shares trading a day, modest selling moves the price several percent, which is likely much of why the stock is about 12% below its 200-day average of CHF 277.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is close to absent, and that is a problem for the entry case rather than a comfort. This is a controlled company (Financiere Vermeer NV is the parent) with a small float, a long tail of patient Swiss holders, no index membership of consequence, no dividend cut in prospect to push out yield holders, no leverage to unwind and no fast-money position to liquidate - 3,361 shares traded on 9 November 2026 against a CHF 1.86 billion market value. The realistic route to CHF 210 is therefore not forced selling but a sector-wide sell-off in brokers and financial intermediaries - the peers have already slipped from their highs (TP ICAP at 309.8 pence against a 50-day average of 326 pence; BGC at USD 10.97 against a 52-week high of USD 12.89) - or a franc-driven de-rating of Swiss mid-caps, either of which would hit this thinly traded name harder than its fundamentals warrant. For sizing: building or exiting a position takes weeks at this volume, so any size given should be one that can be held through the full 18-month horizon.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Compagnie Financiere Tradition (CFT.SW) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-09. Price used: CHF 244.50 on the SIX Swiss Exchange (live quote, 9 November 2026; 52-week range CHF 236-323, 50-day average CHF 253.3, 200-day average CHF 277.3).*

**Source note.** Compagnie Financiere Tradition holds no earnings calls and publishes no guidance, so there are no transcripts to read. This deep dive is built from the company's own dated announcements (the 20 March 2026 full-year 2025 results, the 30 April first-quarter revenue release, the 29 May buyback announcement, the 6 August half-year revenue release, the 28 August half-year results and the 5 November 2026 third-quarter revenue release), the financial trajectory in our screening data, and live market quotes. Where a figure could not be verified it is said so. The full text of the 5 November release could not be retrieved (the document timed out); only its headline figures, taken from the company's news page, are used.

One correction to our own inputs comes first, because it changes everything downstream. Our screening file carries trailing earnings of CHF 33.53 a share and trailing free cash flow of CHF 253 million. Both double count. The company reports twice a year, and our data vendor files the half-year statements under quarterly labels, so adding four "quarters" adds two years. True trailing-twelve-month (TTM) diluted earnings are CHF 17.88 a share (first half 2026 CHF 9.95 plus second half 2025 CHF 7.93). At CHF 244.50 the stock trades on about 13.7 times trailing earnings, not 7.3 times.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story management tells has been steady for five years: a leading interdealer broker (the intermediary that matches banks and professional traders in interest-rate, currency, credit, equity and commodity instruments) that grows by adding brokers and desks, widens its margin through operating leverage, sells the data its trades generate, and returns most of its earnings through a rising dividend and buybacks. The 2026 releases added one emphasis: currency. Every 2026 announcement leads with constant-currency growth (growth measured as if exchange rates had not moved) because the Swiss franc's strength against the dollar, the pound and the yen has cut the reported figures. The first quarter was the high point (+17.4% at constant currency, 30 April); the half was +10.4% (6 and 28 August), which implied a second quarter growing only in the mid single digits. The third quarter, released 5 November 2026, came in at CHF 310.2 million, up 10.2% at constant currency, with nine-month revenue of CHF 956.5 million, up 10.3%. The second-quarter dip now looks like a soft patch, not a trend.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Underlying growth near 10% | Q1 +17.4%, H1 +10.4%, Q3 +10.2%, nine months +10.3% (all constant currency) | Corroborated |
| Margin expansion | Operating profit before depreciation (EBITDA) margin on the joint-venture-inclusive measure 18.6% vs 18.1% in H1 2026 | Corroborated on that measure; reported operating margin fell to 14.7% from 15.2% and reported operating profit was flat (CHF 88.0m vs 88.2m) |
| Earnings compounding | Diluted EPS CHF 8.48 (2021), 11.64, 12.26, 14.40, 16.73 (2025): roughly 18.5% a year | Corroborated |
| H1 2026 profit growth is operating | Net profit +12.6% reported, but about 71% of the increase came from a larger share of associates (the Japanese affiliate Gaitame after absorbing Money Partners Group) and a lower tax rate (23.4% vs 26.1%) | Weaker than the headline |
| Strong balance sheet | Company-stated net cash CHF 181.6m (CHF 265.8m including joint-venture cash) at 30 June 2026; on the strictest reading (leases as debt) CHF 83m; goodwill and intangibles only CHF 51m | Corroborated |
| Capital returns | Dividend CHF 6.15, 6.80, 7.50 over three payment years; new buyback of up to 300,000 shares from 2 June 2026 to 1 June 2029 | Corroborated |
| Free cash flow growth +21.5% | Artefact of vendor line inconsistency; like-for-like H1 free cash flow fell about 12% | Not corroborated |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable. The releases are short, factual and consistent in format. Management quantifies the currency drag to the franc rather than hiding it, and the third-quarter headline repeats the same constant-currency framing. There is no shift to defensive language and no new excuses.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
There is no guidance to test. What can be tested is consistency: every revenue release in 2026 has reconciled to the subsequent results release (the 6 August revenue figure of CHF 646.2m matched the 28 August accounts exactly). Reliability: High on disclosure, not scoreable on forecasting.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
There are no analysts and no calls. The questions an analyst would press, and that the releases leave unanswered: (1) what share of earnings growth is operating rather than from associates and tax; (2) what the data and analytics business earns (never sized); (3) the hedging policy on franc translation; (4) why reported operating profit has stalled while constant-currency revenue grows 10%.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: H1 2026 reported operating profit flat (-0.2%) with margin down 50 basis points; most of the net-profit gain came from below the operating line.
- Red: the investment case depends on a currency the company neither controls nor (as far as disclosed) hedges.
- Red: extreme illiquidity (a few thousand shares a day against a CHF 1.86 billion market value) and a controlling shareholder (Financiere Vermeer NV) foreclose any outside catalyst.
- Green: Q3 2026 constant-currency growth of 10.2% (5 November) undoes the worry that the business decelerated to mid single digits.
- Green: net cash, almost no goodwill, a 45% payout and a buyback that was enlarged, not withdrawn.
- Green: the currency backdrop eased in the second half - the dollar trades at about CHF 0.819 against a 200-day average near 0.800 and a 52-week low of 0.760 - so the translation drag should shrink.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The 29 May release was headlined as the end of the 2023 buyback; the substance was a larger new programme (300,000 shares over three years versus 251,574 shares retired under the old one). The growing reliance on associate income from Japan shifts part of the earnings mix into a volatile, tightly regulated retail currency-trading business. Data and analytics is mentioned as double-digit growth and never quantified.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: strengthening, at a steady pace. The operating business compounds; the reported numbers lag because of the franc. The single most important thing to weigh: at about 13.7 times true trailing earnings the stock is a fairly priced good business, not a discounted one - TP ICAP trades at about 12.3 times on the same basis (309.8 pence against 25.18 pence of trailing diluted earnings) and BGC at roughly 8 times 2026 earnings. The screening data's apparent cheapness was a data error.

Moat: a narrow scale-and-network moat. Interdealer broking is a liquidity business where the largest pools attract the most flow; Tradition is one of three global firms of scale. Returns are high and stable (return on equity about 22%, return on invested capital about 15%) and margins on the joint-venture-inclusive measure are widening, so the moat is not eroding. The secular threat - slow migration of voice broking to electronic venues - is manageable: it has run for two decades, and the hybrid voice-plus-electronic model and the data business have absorbed it. The low share price is neither a fear-print nor a value trap; it is a fair price for a steady franchise.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Management has a clean record: seven beats in seven quarters, Investor Day three-year targets met two years early, and a habit of guiding low (Coach first-quarter growth guided to mid-single digits, delivered 16%). The engine is customer acquisition rather than discounting - 2.6 million new customers in the quarter, about 35% Gen Z - which builds a base that keeps buying. Capital return is generous ($2 billion in fiscal 2027 including the new $350 million buyback lift), and at about 17 times fiscal 2027 consensus earnings of roughly $8.0 the stock still trades below Ralph Lauren and well below the European luxury houses on price-to-free-cash-flow (15.4 times versus about 31 times for Ralph Lauren per the peer file). If Coach keeps compounding at high single digits with modest margin gains, fiscal 2028 earnings per share of about $9 to $9.5 at 18 to 20 times supports $165 to $185 within 18 months. picks.bear_thesis: The good news is now in the price, and the shape of growth is getting more fragile. The stock moved from about $110 in late October to $136.11 on the 2026-11-05 beat-and-raise, so the discount to a reasonable fair value has shrunk to single digits. Underneath, handbag units decelerated from low double digits in fiscal 2026 to roughly flat in the fourth quarter and low single digits in the first quarter of fiscal 2027, while average selling price rose at a low double-digit rate - growth is increasingly price-led, which is how Coach's own 2013-2015 fade and Michael Kors's decline began. Management's reframing of a 'planned unit decline below $200' is plausible but is also exactly the language a brand uses as entry-level demand softens. Kate Spade is still shrinking (revenue -10% in the quarter) after years of 'phased' turnaround language. The reported earnings jump (+787% in fiscal 2026) is a base effect from one-off charges in fiscal 2025 and must not be extrapolated; the honest comparison is earnings per share of $3.50 in fiscal 2024 to $7.75 trailing, already a doubling. Return on equity of 69.8% is flattered by a book value that has fallen about 21% a year as buybacks outrun free cash flow; net debt is $3.45 billion including leases. Insiders sold 12 times on the open market (134,701 shares) with zero buys. Marketing has risen to about 12% of sales and cannot be cut without hurting acquisition. If brand heat cools and the market pays 13 times a fiscal 2027 earnings figure of about $7.6, the stock is worth about $100. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Tapestry (TPR) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-09 from five quarterly calls (2025-11-06 to 2026-11-05) cross-checked against the screener financials. Price used: $136.11 (NYSE, USD, live quote 2026-11-09).*

The short version: Tapestry is now essentially one brand, Coach, and Coach is having the best run in its modern history. Management has under-promised and over-delivered for five straight calls, the numbers corroborate the story, and the latest quarter (reported 2026-11-05) beat and raised again. The two things that keep this from being a clean story are a Kate Spade turnaround that has still not turned, and steady open-market selling by insiders while they talk up the future.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q1 FY26 (2025-11-06) to Q2 FY26 (2026-02-05):** the story was "Coach is acquiring young customers without discounting." The Q2 call was largely about defending gross margin against tariffs; the chief financial officer (CFO) Scott Roe said the company "just took up our outlook for gross margin year over year this year, fully offsetting the impact of tariffs on a full-year basis," and flagged that the lion's share of tariff mitigation lands in fiscal 2027.
- **Q3 FY26 (2026-05-07) to Q4 FY26 (2026-08-13):** the arc moved from defence to victory lap. In August the chief executive (CEO) Joanne Crevoiserat said the company hit "the 3-year revenue, operating margin and earnings per share commitments we established at our Investor Day 2 years ahead of plan": revenue of $8.0 billion (+17% on a pro forma constant-currency basis), operating margin up 340 basis points to over 23%, and adjusted earnings per share (EPS) up 38% to $7.05. The "$10 billion Coach" ambition entered the vocabulary.
- **Q1 FY27 (2026-11-05):** "a powerful start to the year": revenue +12% pro forma to $1.9 billion, operating margin +230 basis points to over 23%, EPS +32% to $1.82 (versus a $1.56 consensus estimate), and a raised full-year outlook. The emphasis shifted again, subtly: from unit growth to price. Coach handbag average unit retail (AUR, the average selling price per item) rose at a low double-digit rate while units grew only low single digits, with a "planned unit decline below $200."

What was quietly dropped: Stuart Weitzman (sold; it is now $15 million of residual revenue) and, increasingly, any near-term top-line promise for Kate Spade. What was added: footwear (+20% in Q1 FY27), China (+41%), Europe (+27%), and AI/data talk (a first AI patent, mentioned in August).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Durable growth" driven by Coach | Revenue 6.68B (FY22) -> 6.67B (FY24) flat, then 7.01B (FY25) -> 8.00B (FY26, +14%); Q1 FY27 +12% pro forma | Corroborated - but note the three flat years before; the growth is two years old |
| Margin expansion from pricing, not promotions | Gross margin 77.8% and expanding; net margin 19.1%; operating margin over 23% | Corroborated |
| Earnings power step-change | EPS 3.17 (FY22) -> 3.50 (FY24) -> 0.82 (FY25) -> 7.27 (FY26); trailing twelve months (TTM) EPS 7.75 | Corroborated, but the +787% FY26 jump is a base effect: FY25 net income of $183M was crushed by one-off charges (the Stuart Weitzman exit and the failed Capri merger costs). The honest comparison is FY24 3.50 -> TTM 7.75, roughly a doubling in two years |
| Strong cash generation funds buybacks | TTM free cash flow (FCF) $1.88B (FCF margin ~23%); FY27 FCF guide ~$1.7B; $2B returned to holders in FY27 after a $350M buyback lift | Corroborated, though the company is returning more than its FCF, so net debt is not falling |
| Strong balance sheet | Net debt $3.45B including $1.67B of capitalized leases (ex-lease ~$1.77B); Altman-Z 4.1 (comfortably solvent) | Healthy, but shrinking book value (book value per share down 21% a year over 5 years) shows the buyback is financed partly with leverage; the 69.8% return on equity is flattered by that thin equity base. Return on invested capital (ROIC) of 15% is the cleaner quality read |
| Kate Spade "phased" turnaround | Q1 FY27 Kate Spade revenue -10%, "consistent with guidance"; gross margin +190 bp | Not yet corroborated on revenue - margins only |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising.** In February the tone was technical and defensive (tariff timing, "quarter by quarter timing that's gonna be a little noisy"). By August it was celebratory ("Fiscal 2026 was a defining year"), and in November confident with numbers attached: the CFO closed by pointing to the buyback lift as evidence of "our conviction that we have a long-term durable growth model." Guidance specificity has, if anything, increased (the full-year guide of about 100 basis points of operating margin expansion, including about 20 basis points from overhead leverage, was laid out precisely in Q1 FY27). There is no shift toward defensive cost or macro language.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High.** The screener records 7 of 7 quarterly beats. Investor Day three-year targets were met two years early. In August the company guided Coach's first quarter to grow "mid-single digits"; Coach delivered 16% constant-currency growth. That is a consistent sandbagging pattern (guiding low and beating), which is the good kind for a holder but means the street has learned to expect beats; future beats will move the stock less. Kate Spade's revenue decline came in "consistent with guidance," so management is not over-promising there either.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Is the price gap to European luxury closing?** (Q1 FY27) An analyst asked whether European houses chasing aspirational buyers could compress Coach's value gap. Todd Kahn answered firmly that "$200 to $500 is our sweet spot" and "the delta is material," but did not quantify share or cross-shopping.
- **Kate Spade cadence** (Baird, Telsey, Q1 FY27) - repeatedly asked; answers are process words ("streamline", "solidify", "green shoots", 500,000 new handbag customers) with no revenue inflection date beyond "progress as we move into the back half."
- **Units vs price.** Units decelerated from low double digits (FY26) to roughly flat (Q4 FY26) to low single digits (Q1 FY27) while AUR carries the growth. Analysts have not yet pushed hard on how long price can do the lifting; this is the question the street is not asking loudly enough.
- **Marketing intensity** - spend is about 12% of sales, roughly four times five years ago. Analysts asked about leverage; management will not cut it.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Green: Coach growth broad by region in Q1 FY27 (North America +7%, Greater China +41%, Europe +27%, Japan +5%).
- Green: gross margin expanded through the tariff shock (guided up in Q2 FY26, delivered).
- Green: customer acquisition engine - 2.6 million new customers in Q1 FY27, about 35% Gen Z.
- Green: full-year outlook raised on 2026-11-05 and buyback lifted by $350M to $2B total shareholder return.
- Red: insiders sold on the open market 12 times (134,701 shares) with zero open-market buys in the window - management's wallets are not echoing the call's confidence.
- Red: unit growth in handbags has slowed to low single digits; growth is now price-led. Price-led growth in an accessible-luxury brand is the historical prelude to fatigue (Coach itself in 2013-2015, Michael Kors after).
- Red: Kate Spade revenue -10% in Q1 FY27; a multi-year turnaround without a revenue turn.
- Red: book value shrinking as buybacks outrun FCF; leverage is the funding source at the margin.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary moved from "units and AUR together" (FY26) to "AUR and strong unit growth within our $200 to $500 sweet spot" with a "planned unit decline below $200" (Q1 FY27). This is a careful reframing of decelerating total units as a deliberate choice. It may be true, but it is the sentence to watch next quarter.
- "Expressive luxury" stores and the remodel of about 80% of traffic by FY30 imply a step-up in capital spending; the CFO acknowledged "we have stepped up a bit our CapEx" (August).
- Leadership is stable (same CEO, CFO and Coach brand president across all five calls); a new creative director at Kate Spade (Jonathan Saunders) is the only senior creative change.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: strengthening.** The single most important thing to weigh: the stock has already re-rated on the news. It traded about $116 at our last look (2026-10-12) and $136 today, after a 2026-11-05 beat-and-raise. The business is better than it was a month ago; the price has caught up with most of that improvement. At roughly 17 times the fiscal 2027 consensus EPS of about $8.0, you are paying a fair, not a cheap, price for a brand at peak momentum.

**Moat.** An intangible-brand moat: Coach owns the $200-$500 leather-goods price band globally, with 85 years of heritage, a direct-to-consumer model and a proven youth-acquisition engine. It is narrow rather than wide - fashion brands can fall out of favour within a few years, as Coach itself did a decade ago - but the current evidence (gross margin at a record 77.8% and expanding, ROIC 15% and rising off the FY25 trough) says it is widening, not eroding.

**Secular threat.** Manageable. The relevant structural risks are a retail channel shift (Tapestry is already majority direct-to-consumer, which neutralizes most of it) and luxury down-trading/up-trading cycles, which are cyclical rather than terminal. The cheapness, where it exists, is not a structurally shrinking base; this is not a value trap. The risk is the ordinary one of brand heat cooling.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend widening · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Booking is the world's largest online travel platform, and the third quarter of 2026 (reported 2026-11-03) showed the business still working through a war and an AI scare: room nights up 7%, gross bookings up 10% to $54.5B, adjusted EPS up 17% to $4.66 against $4.49 expected, the seventh beat in seven quarters.
