# Comcast (CMCSA) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*Debate run 2026-11-09. Transcripts: Q3 2025 (2025-10-30) through Q3 2026 (2026-10-22). Live price $24.51 (Nasdaq, USD, 2026-11-09).*

**The short version:** Comcast is a cash machine whose core business, home broadband, is slowly shrinking under attack from fixed wireless (home internet sold by mobile carriers) and fiber overbuilders. Management has been unusually candid about that, and it is spending heavily — price cuts, a five-year price guarantee, free mobile lines — to stop the bleeding. The content side (parks, studios, Peacock, Sky) is in better shape and is being split off into a separate public company by the middle of 2027. The numbers corroborate the candor but not yet the turnaround: free cash flow is real (about $17.1B over the trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30), but connectivity profit is still falling every quarter.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-30):** the story was "a deliberate investment phase." Mike Cavanagh said broadband would end up as a market of "2 multi-gig symmetrical providers," conceded "most of our footprint will eventually be overbuilt," and guided that the decline in Connectivity & Platforms EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization — a cash-profit proxy) would "build slightly over the next several quarters." Leadership change: Steve Croney named head of connectivity.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-01-29):** the theme became execution of "the most significant go-to-market shift in our company's history" — four national speed tiers, a five-year price guarantee, a 12-month free mobile line. Management promised that "a meaningful portion" of free lines would convert to paid in the second half of 2026 and that connectivity profit would improve in the back half. The Versant cable-network spin was completed.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-23):** the high-water mark of the story — broadband net losses "improved by more than 100,000 year-over-year, the first year-over-year improvement since the fourth quarter of 2020," record wireless adds, record Olympic/Super Bowl advertising.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-23):** the narrative pivoted to structure. Three weeks earlier the company had announced the separation of NBCUniversal and Sky into a standalone company, targeted in "approximately 1 year," and the return of Michael Angelakis as the future Comcast chief executive. Peacock reached profitability.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-22):** tone turned defensive on connectivity. Management described fixed wireless as "aggressive," fiber pricing as having "pockets of irrational pricing," flagged an unusually large wave of two-year promotional roll-offs, and announced "the most significant operating and cost transformation in our company's history" with a roughly $1B fourth-quarter restructuring charge (reported 2026-10-22). Connectivity revenue fell about 2.6% and connectivity EBITDA about 4.4% year over year. Parks: Orlando softness guided to persist "at least next quarter and in the first half of next year."

The arc runs from "invest, then grow" to "split the company and cut costs." The growth promise for connectivity has been pushed out; the value-creation promise has shifted toward the separation.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Connectivity decline will "build slightly," then improve in the second half of 2026 (Q3 2025, Q4 2025 calls) | Connectivity EBITDA fell ~3.7% in Q3 2025, ~5.8% in Q2 2026, ~4.4% in Q3 2026 — it did build, and the Q3 2026 narrowing is the first sign of the promised improvement, but it is still falling | Partly delivered |
| Broadband losses turning (Q1 2026: first year-over-year improvement since Q4 2020) | The Q1 improvement did not become a trend; Q3 2026 was hurt by promotional roll-offs and aggressive competitor pricing | Not yet corroborated |
| Free lines will convert to paid in the second half of 2026 (Q4 2025) | Q2 2026: "positive early traction"; no conversion percentage has ever been disclosed | Unverified — a recurring non-number |
| Peacock will approach profitability (Q1 2026) | Peacock reached profitability in Q2 2026 and stayed profitable in Q3 2026 | Delivered |
| Cash generation is durable | Revenue flat for three years (3-year CAGR +0.6%; 2025 revenue $123.7B vs $123.7B in 2024); free cash flow $17.1B trailing twelve months, up ~25% in fiscal 2025 | Corroborated |
| Earnings growth | Fiscal 2025 EPS $5.39 (+30%) is flattered by one-offs and by the post-Versant comparison; trailing twelve-month diluted EPS is $3.16, and consensus forward EPS growth is only ~1% | The headline EPS growth overstates the earning power |

Net debt is about $79.8B (borrowings $87.4B less cash $7.6B at 2026-09-30, excluding leases), roughly 2.3-2.5 times EBITDA on our estimate — manageable, but it limits buybacks, which press coverage on 2026-11-08 described as on hold.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining on connectivity, rising on content.** Q3 2025: "intensely competitive environment, which we do not expect to change anytime soon" — candid but confident. Q1 2026: "early signs that the strategic pivot ... is underway" — the most offensive language of the run. Q3 2026: "near-term financial pressure," "pockets of irrational pricing," and a shift to cost and efficiency language ("structurally improve our cost base"). Guidance specificity has fallen: in Q4 2025 the chief financial officer said "I will stop short of giving a full EBITDA guide," and no connectivity framework has been offered since. On content, the tone is steadily more confident (Peacock profitable, The Odyssey, NBA ratings).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management gives directional rather than numerical guidance, which makes it hard to catch them out — and that is itself the point. Directional calls on the trough (the decline would "build") were accurate; calls on the recovery (broadband turning, back-half improvement) have been only partly delivered. Peacock guidance was met. The screener's 7-of-7 quarterly earnings-per-share beats reflects low consensus bars and cost control more than operating momentum. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- The free-line conversion rate: asked repeatedly (Q1 2026, Q2 2026), never quantified.
- Post-separation leverage, dividend policy and exchange ratio: asked in Q2 2026; answer was "nothing to add." The dividend split between the two companies is the largest unanswered question for the yield-holder base.
- Orlando parks softness and Epic Universe capacity: management now guides softness into the first half of 2027.
- Promotional roll-offs in the legacy base (Q3 2026): management admits it is "a pain point."

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

**Red flags**
- Q3 2026: a new round of the "most significant" transformation, with a ~$1B charge, one year after the last "most significant" go-to-market shift — the fixes keep getting bigger.
- Q3 2026: competitive language escalated ("irrational pricing"); peer Charter reported wider internet losses on 2026-11-06, so the pressure is industry-wide, not easing.
- Q2/Q3 2026: no capital-return framework for the two companies; buybacks reported paused.
- Insiders: 3 open-market sales (about 70,700 shares) and zero open-market buys.

**Green flags**
- Q2-Q3 2026: Peacock profitable two quarters running.
- Q3 2026: connectivity EBITDA decline narrowed to ~4.4% from ~5.8% in Q2.
- Business services generates "nearly $6 billion annually in EBITDA" with enterprise growth.
- Wireless: record line additions through 2026; over 10 million lines.
- The separation creates two cleaner stories and a potential sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) unlock.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Satellite is not yet a material factor" (Q3 2026) is the first time management has named satellite as a future competitor — a widening of the threat set.
- The language moved from "return to growth" to "position the business for return to growth over the long term" — a quiet extension of the timeline.
- Leadership churn: Croney (connectivity, 2026), Cavanagh co-CEO (2026), Angelakis returning as Comcast CEO (2027), a new NBCUniversal chief financial officer (Chris Halpin). The new voices emphasise cost and agility rather than growth.
- The proposed ITV acquisition for Sky signals the media company will be acquisitive, adding execution risk on the content side.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: PIVOTING.** The company is turning from a conglomerate defending cable into two separate companies, with an aggressive cost program on the connectivity side.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** the cash is real (about $4.80 of free cash flow per share against a $24.51 price), but the cash comes from a connectivity business whose profit is still falling about 4% a year. The investment works if that decline flattens; it is a slow value trap if it does not. The fourth-quarter 2026 results (late January 2027) are the next clean read.

**Moat:** scale-cost and network (a sunk, capital-efficient hybrid fiber-coax network) plus switching costs from bundling broadband with mobile. It is real but narrow, and the evidence says it is eroding: return on invested capital is only 6.8%, connectivity revenue and profit are falling, and management itself expects most of its footprint to be overbuilt. **Secular threat:** fixed-wireless and fiber overbuild (cord-cutting/broadband overbuild) is a material, not terminal, threat — the business still earns large cash margins and can defend share with price, and the content half is not exposed in the same way. The cheapness is partly a fear-print and partly a fair price for a shrinking core; at roughly 5 times free cash flow, the market is pricing more decline than the latest numbers show, but the burden of proof sits with management.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

picks.bull_thesis: Husqvarna is a cash-generative market leader priced as if its cost programme will never reach the margin. North America grew across all three divisions in Q2 and Q3 2026, professional robotics is building a defensible position in golf (just over 2,000 of about 38,000 courses, 99% retention per the 2026-10-21 call), and the Construction aftermarket has grown 15 quarters in a row. An EU anti-dumping duty on Chinese robotic mowers, if imposed, would ease the price pressure in Husqvarna's most important growth category. Gross margin is contracting (Q3 2026 about 25.6% vs 28.5%), robotics prices are falling (average cuts of about 5% on older Automower models, Gardena robotics 'margin decretive'), and management concedes price increases in Construction have cost volume for two to three years. Return on invested capital is about 7%, the Altman Z solvency score is about 1.6, and the CFO, a division head and several executives turned over in 2026. If the full-year 2026 underlying margin comes in below 5.5% ex-refund, the cost story is not working and the right multiple is 8-9 times a lower earnings base: SEK 20-24 a share.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrow. At about 10 times trailing free cash flow and roughly 25% below our base value, the market is pricing a company whose savings never reach the margin. We think that is too pessimistic on cash - the deleveraging is real and continuing - but we do not have evidence that the market is wrong on margins: three quarters of 2026 show savings absorbed by inflation, currency, price cuts and volume. Consensus expects strong forward earnings growth (about +33% per the screener), which mostly reflects the depressed 2025 base and cost savings; that expectation is exactly what the full-year 2026 report will test. We found no dated analyst price targets to cite.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window, the months just ahead, is seasonally the worst: Q4 is Husqvarna's smallest quarter and historically loss-making (Q4 2025 operating loss of SEK 846 million) and the quarter in which inventory is built, so cash flow turns negative (about SEK 1.3 billion outflow in Q4 2025). Trade inventory of robotics is 'slightly higher than we would like leaving the season' (2026-10-21), which could weaken the early-2027 sell-in. Items affecting comparability of about SEK 300 million more are expected in Q4 to reach about SEK 750 million for 2026. The Powered Garden decision in early 2027 could bring write-downs. There is no liquidation or maturity event in our inputs; the balance sheet is improving, though the Altman Z score of about 1.6 means the margin for error is thin.
picks.positioning_washout: We see no forced-selling pressure. The dividend was raised to SEK 1.25 for 2025 and there is no sign of a cut that would push income holders out; there is no index event, lock-up or spin-off in our inputs. The smart-money score (6 of 100) and a price about 14% below its 200-day average reflect ordinary disappointment after the Q2 and Q3 reports, not mechanical selling - so there is no named seller to wait for at a lower price, which is another reason the wait is for proof, not for a level.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the full-year 2026 report, due about 4 February 2027, shows an underlying operating margin of at least 7% excluding the one-off tariff refund. Nothing dated has changed since our late-October look, so the answer stands and only the price moves, to SEK 32.76. Husqvarna is a real value case on cash - about SEK 2.1 billion of free cash flow over the last twelve months, net debt falling every quarter, a cost programme running ahead of plan - and the share sits about 25% below our SEK 44 fair value (adverse SEK 22, favourable SEK 66). But the thesis is in doubt until the margin test passes: the third quarter of 2026 turned a year-earlier profit into a SEK 230 million operating loss despite about SEK 300 million of savings, and the second quarter's strong margin leaned on a one-off SEK 240 million tariff refund. A price below roughly SEK 24 alongside a full-year margin under 5.5% would mean the thesis has broken. The macro backdrop rewards cash generation but punishes consumer-discretionary demand and input inflation, so it neither helps nor hurts the call. Conviction stays at three: a decent business at a real discount, with the one piece of evidence that matters not yet in.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst that forces a re-rating is the full-year 2026 report, expected about 2027-02-04: the first full-year read on the underlying operating margin ex the tariff refund, plus the 2027 savings and IAC guidance. Close behind it is the Powered Garden strategic-review decision promised for early 2027 - a sale or closure of a loss-making unit would lift group margins directly. A possible EU anti-dumping duty on Chinese robotic mowers is an optional extra with no date. None of these is contractual.

# Husqvarna Group (HUSQ-B.ST) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16 from five earnings calls (Q3 2025 on 2025-10-21 through Q3 2026 on 2026-10-21) and the screener financials. All figures in Swedish kronor (SEK).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from "defend the balance sheet" to "transform the cost base", while the top line has gone nowhere.

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-21), new CEO Glen Instone's first call.** The emphasis was cash and inventory: "we've continued to reduce inventory... That has enabled us to reduce net debt". Growth claims were narrow - professional robotics and handheld - and the Gardena division was already shrinking (minus 7% that quarter). The Brastad plant closure (about SEK 100 million of savings) introduced the "asset-light" vocabulary.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-04).** The December 2025 Capital Markets Day reset the plan: a SEK 4 billion cost-out programme, a 3-5% sales-growth target "applicable immediately", an operating margin of 10% within two to three years, and "business portfolio units" sorted into growth, profit-improvement and turnaround buckets with a 24-month clock on turnarounds. The quarter itself was a SEK 841 million operating loss, and the CFO (Terry Burke) announced his departure.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-23).** The high point: 2% organic growth, growth "in all of our regions", a 12.3% operating margin and SEK 245 million of savings in a single quarter.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-17).** Demand rolled over (organic sales minus 4%, Gardena minus 11%) but the reported 13.6% margin was flattered by a one-off SEK 240 million US tariff refund. Management pulled the savings timetable forward (SEK 3 billion effective by end-2028) and put Gardena's Powered Garden unit under formal strategic review, with a decision promised in early 2027. A new cost headwind appeared: SEK 300-350 million from the Middle East crisis (two-thirds raw materials, one-third logistics).
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-21), new CFO Patrik Johnson.** Europe weak (consumer sentiment plus drought), North America growing in all three divisions, a reported operating loss of SEK 230 million (Q3 2025: a SEK 151 million profit), strong cash flow of about SEK 2.4 billion and net debt down to about SEK 9.4 billion. Savings above SEK 900 million year to date; items affecting comparability (one-off restructuring charges) of about SEK 450 million so far, about SEK 750 million expected for 2026.

The thread: what management controls (costs, inventory, cash, portfolio pruning) is going well; what it does not control (European consumer demand, weather, input inflation, Chinese robotic-mower price competition) keeps eating the savings.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence in the numbers | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "We must get this company back to growth" - 3-5% target, applicable immediately (2026-02-04) | FY revenue 54.0B (2022) -> 53.3B -> 48.4B -> 46.6B (2025); trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30 about 44.8B (Q4-25 7.43B + Q1 13.96B + Q2 14.38B + Q3 9.01B). Organic +2% Q1, -4% Q2, roughly flat Q3 | Not delivered. Reported sales are still shrinking, with currency adding to the organic weakness. |
| Cost-out ahead of plan (SEK 630m run rate by Q2, >900m by Q3) | Gross margin contracting (30.4%, flagged contracting); Q3 2026 gross profit 2.31B on 9.01B sales (25.6%) vs 2.62B on 9.20B (28.5%) a year earlier | Savings are real but being absorbed by volume deleverage, inflation, price cuts on older robotics and currency. The P&L has not yet shown the net benefit. |
| Margin expansion (Q1 12.3%, Q2 13.6%) | Q2 contained a SEK 240m one-off tariff refund (about 1.7 points of Q2 margin). Trailing reported operating income about 2.65B (5.9% margin) | The headline margins overstate the underlying run rate. Our test excludes the refund for that reason. |
| Strong cash and deleveraging | Trailing free cash flow 2.08B; net debt 7.72B incl. leases (ex-lease about 6.42B) at 2026-09-30, company-quoted figure about 9.4B (includes pensions); interest cost 160-210m a quarter | Corroborated. This is the cleanest part of the story. |
| Professional robotics as the growth engine (2,000+ golf courses of about 38,000; 99% retention) | No segment disclosure in our inputs; robotics plus battery at 22% of sales (up from 20%) | Plausible and directionally supported, but too small to move group numbers yet. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining on demand, rising on self-help.** Q1 2026 was the most confident ("off to a very solid start"). Q2 opened defensively ("Q2 has been somewhat difficult") and Q3 more so ("a very challenging market environment"). Guidance has become narrower and more about inputs management controls: savings of "SEK 1 billion" per year, IAC budgets, footprint moves. No sales or margin guidance for 2027 was offered. The language has shifted from offence (growth targets, marketing step-up from 3% to 5% of sales) to defence (inflation offset, "price elasticity", "too much assets supporting that business" in Gardena).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- Cost savings: guided SEK 800m for 2026 in Q1, then beaten (over SEK 900m after three quarters, over SEK 1bn for the year). **Delivered.**
- Tariffs: guided half-offset by price for H1 2026; broadly delivered, plus an unplanned refund. **Delivered.**
- Growth: 3-5% "applicable immediately" in February 2026; the year will end negative organically in all likelihood. **Missed.**
- The screener's 4-of-7 quarterly beat rate (57%) matches this mixed picture.

**Reliability: Medium.** Management hits the levers it controls and misses on the market.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Robotics margins and Chinese competition** (Eliason, Q3 2025 and Q1 2026; webcast Q4 2025): management conceded the entry segment (about 15% of robotic sales) is "not margin accretive", Gardena robotics is "margin decretive", and Automower profitability was "slightly down" in H1 2026 after average price cuts of about 5% on older models.
- **Tariff durability** (Tubic, Q2 2026): "I wouldn't factor in too much more of a tariff refund."
- **Gardena's logic** (Hagéus, Q3 2025; Eliason, Q3 2026): repeatedly asked whether Gardena belongs in the group; the answer in 2026 was a Powered Garden review and "too large an asset base".
- **Construction pricing vs volume** (webcast Q3 2026): "We have seen a volume decline in the past 2 or 3 years in Construction because of the price increases" - an admission that pricing is now costing share.
- **Trade inventory**: robotics "slightly higher than we would like leaving the season" (Q3 2026), which risks a softer 2027 sell-in.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Q3 2026 reported operating loss of SEK 230m vs a profit of SEK 151m a year earlier despite SEK 300m of savings in the quarter.
- 🔴 Q2 2026 margin flattered by a SEK 240m tariff refund; underlying margin trend is weaker than reported.
- 🔴 Both the CFO and a division head left in 2026; new CFO, procurement chief and construction head joined in H2 2026 - a lot of new people at once.
- 🔴 Altman Z about 1.6 (a solvency score in the caution zone), ROIC about 6.8%, gross margin contracting.
- 🔴 Volume losses in Construction attributed to price increases; robotics prices falling under competition.
- 🟢 Free cash flow of about SEK 2.1bn trailing; Q3 2026 cash flow of about SEK 2.4bn matched a year earlier; net debt falling every quarter.
- 🟢 Savings ahead of plan; SEK 3bn target by 2028 is credible on the run rate so far.
- 🟢 North America growing across all three divisions in Q2 and Q3 2026.
- 🟢 Portfolio pruning is happening (stone diamond tools exit, Powered Garden review, Brastad closure, battery outsourcing).
- 🟢 The EU Commission's disclosure in its anti-dumping investigation into Chinese robotic mowers (company notice of 2026-10-23; content confidential, no comment from Husqvarna) could, if duties follow, ease European price pressure - not verifiable today.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary has moved from "growth" to "portfolio management" and "asset-light". That is the language of a company preparing to shrink to a better core.
- Creating a Chief Procurement Officer seat signals that sourcing, not volume, is the main profit lever management believes in.
- "We'll keep a very, very close eye on it to make sure we remain competitive" (Construction, Q3 2026) is the first explicit admission that pricing power is near its limit.
- The new CFO's first comment on Gardena ("being negative in quarter 3 is unfortunately normal") lowers the bar rather than raising it.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: PIVOTING** - a credible self-help programme running against a shrinking, inflation-squeezed top line.

The single most important thing to weigh: **whether the SEK 1bn a year of savings reaches the operating margin.** So far it has not - year-to-date savings above SEK 900m coincide with a lower Q3 and a flat-to-down underlying margin. The full-year 2026 report (expected about 2027-02-04) is the first clean read of the whole year excluding the tariff refund.

**Moat:** narrow, built on brand and the professional dealer network (scale-cost and intangible-brand). It is not widening: returns are low (ROIC about 7%), gross margin is contracting, and residential robotics is being commoditised by lower-priced vision-based entrants. Professional robotics (golf, landscaping) and the Construction aftermarket (15 consecutive quarters of growth) are the parts with real switching costs.

**Secular threat:** manageable. Outdoor power equipment is not a structurally dying market, and electrification/robotics is a shift Husqvarna leads in the premium and professional tiers. The threat is margin pressure from Chinese robotic-mower makers in the residential tier, not a terminal-value problem. The cheapness looks more like a cyclical and execution fear-print than a value trap - provided the cost programme shows up in the margin.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Drägerwerk (DRW3.DE, preference shares, Xetra, EUR) — deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-02. Transcripts read: Q2-2025 (2025-07-29), Q3-2025 (2025-10-29), FY-2025 (2026-03-24), Q2-2026 (2026-07-30), Q3-2026 (2026-10-29). Live price used: EUR 102.20 for the preference line (DRW3.DE); the ordinary shares (DRW8.DE) trade at EUR 75.00.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story across five quarters is one sentence repeated with growing confidence: "profit before growth." Management set a goal in 2024 to lift the EBIT margin (operating profit over sales) by about one percentage point a year, reaching 10% by 2030. In mid-2025 the narrative was defensive — a weak first half (H1-2025 EBIT margin 1.3%) explained away by missing prior-year one-offs, a strong euro and US tariffs, with management leaning on a record order book and "back-end loading" of profit. Q3-2025 delivered the turn (Q3 EBIT more than doubled to about EUR 57M, 6.8% margin), and FY-2025 closed at a 6.7% margin and record sales of about EUR 3.5B, the second consecutive one-point step.

2026 introduced a new and awkward ingredient: refunds of US customs duties. In Q2-2026 (2026-07-30) refunds helped lift guidance twice, to an EBIT margin of 6-8%, with the CEO adding that "even without any refunds ... we are going to perform well in 2026." By Q3-2026 (2026-10-29) the emphasis shifted to the top line ("excellent net sales development") while profit growth was attributed "mainly" to the refunds. Newer threads: defense (target to triple to more than EUR 300M by 2028), the lifting of a roughly seven-year-old FDA (US Food and Drug Administration) warning letter, Chinese competitors pushing into Latin America and Africa, and a Capital Markets Day on 2026-11-18 to "sharpen our equity story."

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| One point of margin a year | EBIT margin about 4.8% (2024 reported 5.8% incl. one-offs) to 6.7% (FY-2025) | Delivered for 2024-25 |
| "Even without refunds we perform well" (2026-07-30) | 9M-2026 EBIT EUR 112M includes EUR 27.9M refunds; underlying about EUR 84M, 3.4% of about EUR 2.5B sales vs 3.3% (EUR 77M) in 9M-2025 | Underlying improvement is only about EUR 11M — real but tiny |
| Q3 strength | Q3-2026 EBIT EUR 48M includes EUR 20.1M refunds; underlying about EUR 28M vs EUR 57M a year earlier | Underlying Q3 profit roughly halved |
| Cost discipline ("expense growth below sales growth") | 9M functional costs +6.1% vs sales +5.3%; Q3 costs +8.7% vs sales +1% | Promise currently being missed; Q4 must hold costs flat with Q3 |
| Cash generation | 9M free cash flow about EUR 114M vs EUR 16M; net financial debt down to about EUR 106M; year-end guide now net cash of EUR 0-50M | Strong, partly refund-driven, partly working capital |
| Medical division turnaround | 9M Medical EBIT margin -0.7% (from -1.7%); Q3 1.0% vs 2.3% | Still loss-making over nine months; Safety (11% margin) carries the group |

Screener data agree: ROIC about 4.7%, net margin 4.0%, TTM diluted EPS 9.04 (refund-inflated), latest-quarter EPS down 5% year on year.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Confident and consistent on strategy, but notably more hedged on numbers in Q3-2026. The CFO answered the key Q4 cost question with "there's not much more that I can add at this point" and could not reconcile the implied Q4 free cash flow on the call. The CEO's framing of China moved from "stabilization ... perhaps even pickup" (2025-07-29) to "below our expectations and no growth for us" (2026-10-29). Tone: steady family-company optimism with less operating detail than a year ago.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

2025 guidance was met and beaten (margin at the top half, sales slightly above forecast). The 2026 6-8% EBIT margin guidance is flattered by refunds of about EUR 28M (roughly 0.8 points). To reach the committee's test of at least 6.7% excluding refunds on about EUR 3.6B sales, FY underlying EBIT must be about EUR 240M, i.e. Q4 underlying EBIT about EUR 155-160M — matching the record Q4-2025 (about EUR 156M) despite Q3 costs running 8.7% higher. Possible given Dräger's heavy Q4 seasonality, but not the base case; the guidance midpoint implies roughly 6.2% underlying.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts (Kepler Cheuvreux, MWB Research, JMS Invest, AlphaValue, Hauck Aufhäuser) keep pressing on: (a) the arithmetic of Q4 costs, (b) underlying versus refund-driven profit, (c) China, (d) defense order size (the Q3 German defense order is "low double-digit million", delivered over two to three years), and (e) 2027 headwinds — management flagged AI-driven component shortages and currency. No FMP analyst price-target coverage for this listing; none cited here.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red: underlying Q3-2026 EBIT roughly halved; cost growth outrunning sales; Medical still barely profitable after a decade of "profit before growth"; Chinese rivals redeploying into emerging markets; one-off accruals for share-price-linked management pay; logistics costs from Middle East tensions.
Green: record order intake (9M about EUR 2.7B, Safety orders +13%); net cash balance sheet; FDA warning letter lifted (confirmed on the 2026-10-29 call) freeing US approvals and compliance resources; defense optionality; dividend policy of at least 30% of net income; family control with long horizon.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The changed net-debt guidance (to net cash EUR 0-50M at year-end) implies Q4 free cash flow of EUR 56-106M; management did not confirm the math — either a strong Q4 is expected or the guide is loose.
- Hiring the North American head of sales from a Chinese competitor signals the competitive threat is taken seriously.
- The Capital Markets Day (2026-11-18) is likely to restate the 10%-by-2030 target; a new mid-term framework could re-anchor expectations, but it is a presentation, not a payout.
- Share-class gap: the preference line trades at about 36% over the ordinary line for the same economics (plus a small extra dividend); that premium is a risk if index or liquidity flows reverse.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

A sound, conservatively financed franchise whose margin story is real for 2024-25 but whose 2026 progress is mostly one-off refunds. The proof point is the FY-2026 preliminary release (expected about 2027-01-15): an underlying margin at or above 6.7% keeps the one-point-a-year path alive; below 5.5% breaks it. Until then, this is a wait-for-proof name, and the ordinary shares are the cheaper way to own the same company.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: The home business is steadier than the price implies and the cash recovery has started to show up ahead of plan. In Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-30) consumer customer service revenue grew 2.9% year on year, revenue per consumer customer rose 1.7% thanks to a January 2026 inflation-linked price rise that stuck, convergent (fixed-plus-mobile bundle) revenue grew 4.7%, and Proximus added 18,000 mobile postpaid and 38,000 fiber customers in a market the CEO called highly promotional. Global, the international unit that collapsed in 2025, returned to margin growth three quarters into an eight-quarter turnaround, and its 2026 EBITDA guide was raised to EUR 125-135 million. The 2026 organic free cash flow guide doubled to about EUR 100 million, 2027 is guided above EUR 100 million despite peak capital spending, and management targets EUR 400 million by 2030 - against a market value of about EUR 1.97 billion. The fiber path is largely defined: Flanders approved (July 2026), Unifiber consolidated in Wallonia, the Orange partnership expected by summer 2027. There is no bond maturity before 2028 and net debt is guided below 3x EBITDA. If even 80% of the 2030 target arrives, the equity trades on about a 16% free-cash-flow yield on 2030 cash, and a Global separation around 2028 could crystallize value the market gives no credit for today. Conditions: domestic EBITDA stays broadly flat, capital spending falls after 2027 as promised, and Digi's price moves stay contained.
picks.bear_thesis: This is still a leveraged bet on cash flow that mostly does not exist yet. Net debt was EUR 5.11 billion including leases (EUR 4.73 billion excluding) at 2026-06-30, about 2.6 times the market value, with a hybrid bond ranking ahead of shareholders; the Altman Z-score (a bankruptcy-risk gauge) is 0.9 and the Piotroski score (a nine-point financial-health check) is 4 of 9. The Q3 2026 cash beat is half timing - the CFO said half the capital-spending saving is cash paid later - and nine-month organic free cash flow of EUR 114 million is still below last year's EUR 153 million. The earnings base is shrinking: revenue fell 2.0% in 2025, EPS went from 1.39 (2024) to 1.23 (2025) to 1.12 trailing, consensus expects forward EPS about 14% lower, and domestic EBITDA turned negative in Q3 2026 (-1.4%) as wage indexation, Unifiber costs and B2B decline (business service revenue -2.8%) bit. Return on invested capital is about 5.7% on the scan and lower on a trailing basis, well below the cost of capital. Competitive pressure is building: Digi now sells through 655 Bpost stores, unlimited mobile plans have dropped to EUR 24-25, and duct-access rules let rivals overbuild dense areas. Management's timing record is weak - Global's 2025 miss, Flanders a year late, and Wallonia slipping again on 2026-10-30. In a market where European long yields are high, a leveraged, slow-growth telecom is the kind of bond-like equity that de-rates. What would confirm the bear: a 2027 guide in February 2027 with flat-to-down EBITDA and a later capital-spending decline.
picks.consensus_delta: The deep-value question is whether the market prices terminal decline into a company with stable earnings power. Partly. At EUR 6.085 the market value of about EUR 1.97 billion values the EUR 400 million 2030 cash target at well under half its face value, and the CEO felt obliged on 2026-10-30 to rebut satellite and AI-agent fears that he said put pressure on Proximus share price in particular. Where we disagree with the market: Belgian density makes satellite irrelevant as a substitute, consumer pricing power is visible in the numbers, and cash is arriving earlier than guided. Where we agree: the 2026 cash improvement is half timing, domestic EBITDA just turned down, B2B keeps shrinking, leverage is high and management's timing record does not earn full credit for a 2030 promise. No dated analyst price targets could be verified, so we do not claim the street is wrong on a specific number. The discount is real but not wide enough to pay for the leverage at today's price.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) runs through the 2027 capital-spending peak. No liquidation risk: the plan is described as fully financed and the first bond matures in 2028, though management will likely issue new bonds before then at higher coupons. Pressure points: (1) Q4 2026 and the February 2027 full-year results with 2027 guidance - the capital-spending timing that flattered 2026 cash reverses into 2027, and domestic EBITDA must be shown to hold after the September 2026 wage indexation. (2) Digi's wider distribution and a possible unlimited-plan move could force another round of price cuts. (3) High European long yields keep bond-like telecoms under pressure. (4) Any rating-agency warning on leverage near 3x EBITDA would hit the stock before the 2028 recovery.
picks.positioning_washout: Most forced selling has already happened: the dividend halving at the February 2026 Capital Markets Day pushed out yield holders, and the stock slid from a one-year high of EUR 8.55 to a low of about EUR 5.46 in late October 2026 before bouncing to EUR 6.085 on the results. The screener shows low smart-money interest (12 of 100) and neutral institutional flow, consistent with a sold-down stock. The Belgian state is the controlling, long-term holder, so there is no large-seller overhang, but it also limits takeover upside. A further leg down, if it comes, is most likely a sector-wide or style-wide sell-off of European telecoms on rising yields or on satellite and AI fears, not company-specific forced selling.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near EUR 5.60, which a sector-wide sell-off of European telecoms on rising yields or satellite and AI fears could deliver. The thesis holds: the Belgian business keeps its pricing power, and Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-30) doubled the 2026 cash-flow guide and raised the Global outlook. Our fair value edges up from EUR 7.49 to EUR 7.60, about 25% above today's EUR 6.085. That clears the minimum bar, but not by enough for this balance sheet: the equity is a thin layer on about EUR 5.1 billion of net debt, half of the cash beat is timing, home-market EBITDA just fell 1.4%, and the southern fiber deal slipped again, to summer 2027. The adverse case of EUR 4.50 sits about 26% below the price, roughly equal to the upside to fair value. We keep the committee's EUR 5.60 level, about a 36% discount to fair value, which pays for the leverage. The stock briefly traded through that level around 2026-10-26 before the results bounce; we do not chase the 11% rebound. We would move to buy at today's price if the February 2027 guidance shows domestic EBITDA holding and capital spending set to fall from 2028 on schedule.

(1) Full-year 2026 results and 2027 guidance, around February 2027 - the most important date: capital spending peak size, 2027 cash above EUR 100 million, domestic EBITDA path. (2) Wallonia partnership finalization with Orange Belgium, now guided for summer 2027 (not binding). (3) Visible capital-spending decline in 2028 plus the dividend step-ups to EUR 0.40 and EUR 0.50. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Proximus (PROX.BR) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-02. Price EUR 6.085 (Euronext Brussels, FMP quote). Calls read: Q4 2024 (2025-02-28), Q3 2025 (2025-11-07), Q1 2026 (2026-05-13), Q2 2026 (2026-07-31), Q3 2026 (2026-10-30).*

**Bottom line:** the Belgian home business is steady and has real pricing power, but it barely grows. The story is now about cash flow after a fiber-building peak in 2027, delivered by a management team that has rebuilt some credibility in 2026 after missing badly on the international unit (Proximus Global) in 2025. The latest quarter (Q3 2026, reported 2026-10-30) was better on cash and worse on home-market earnings: the 2026 organic free cash flow guide (cash after investment, before asset sales) doubled from about EUR 50 million to about EUR 100 million, the Global earnings guide was raised, but home-market EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) fell 1.4% and the southern fiber deal slipped again.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **Q4 2024 / Q3 2025:** the story was "Global is a growth engine" plus a domestic defense against Digi, the low-cost fourth mobile operator that launched in December 2024. In Q3 2025 Global EBITDA fell about 22% in one quarter, and the narrative shrank.
- **February 2026 Capital Markets Day (CMD):** a reset — the dividend was halved (EUR 0.30 on 2026 results, stepping to 0.40 and 0.50), a EUR 400 million organic free-cash-flow target for 2030 was set, capital spending was guided to peak in 2027, and the CEO said Global "does not belong" with the Belgian operations.
- **Q1–Q2 2026:** execution language. Flanders fiber collaboration with Wyre and Telenet approved by the Belgian Competition Authority (July 2026); 100% of Unifiber taken in Wallonia; new duct-access rules accepted ("we don't have a clue" whether rivals will use them — Q2 2026).
- **Q3 2026:** defensive framing appears for the first time — the CEO devoted slides to satellite connectivity and AI shopping agents because both "put pressure on Proximus share price in particular". Global is now framed as a turnaround ahead of plan ("direct margin growth ahead of expectations"), with "value crystallization" discussed "around 2028".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Domestic is "resilient" | Customer service revenue +2.9% y/y, consumer revenue per customer +1.7%, convergent revenue +4.7% (Q3 2026); but domestic EBITDA −1.4% in Q3 after slight growth in Q1–Q2 | Top line holds; the profit line is flat-to-down. "Broadly stable" for 2026 reiterated. |
| Price increases stick | January 2026 inflation-linked price rise flowed through; revenue per customer up despite challenger-brand mix shift | Corroborated — this is the strongest evidence of pricing power. |
| Global turning around | Direct margin +0.8% y/y, +4.5% q/q; EBITDA EUR 35m in Q3; full-year guide raised to EUR 125–135m | Corroborated for one quarter; OpEx +5.8% and rising. |
| Cash flow rebuilding | 2026 organic FCF guide ~EUR 100m (from ~EUR 50m); nine-month organic FCF EUR 114m vs EUR 153m a year ago; reported nine-month FCF EUR 54m | Better than guided, still below last year; about half of the capital-spending saving is timing (CFO: "half is efficiency, half is cash CapEx"). |
| Financials overall | Revenue 5.54bn (2021) → 6.38bn (2024) → 6.25bn (2025); EPS 1.37 → 1.23 → 1.12 trailing; return on invested capital about 5.7% (scan), lower on a trailing basis | The earnings base is shrinking slowly while debt-funded fiber investment is still building. |
| Balance sheet | Net debt EUR 5.11bn including leases (EUR 4.73bn ex-leases) at 2026-06-30; net debt/EBITDA guided below 3x; first bond maturity 2028 | High for a EUR 2bn equity; no near-term wall. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable, with a new defensive edge. Q3 2025 was apologetic on Global; Q1–Q2 2026 confident and specific on fiber deals; Q3 2026 confident on cash and Global but defensive on structural fears (satellite, AI agents) and candid on B2B IT ("some delays ... revenue recognition kicks in in Q1 next year"). A new CFO (Fiona Lam, since September 2026) gave tight, numeric answers.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium, improving. Misses: Global 2025 (the "triple digit" synergy story turned into a 22% quarterly EBITDA drop); Flanders fiber timing (about a year late); Wallonia now "summer 2027" versus "end of Q1 27" three months ago. Deliveries: 2026 domestic guidance held three quarters running; Global and free-cash-flow guidance raised in Q3 2026; the screener shows earnings beats in 6 of 7 recent quarters. Some sandbagging is visible in the low 2026 cash guide set at the CMD.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Digi's distribution push (655 Bpost stores) and a "mini price war" in unlimited mobile plans (ING, UBS) — management calls its EUR 24–25 unlimited plans "value-based", while conceding they "prepare for potential new Digi moves".
- Whether free cash flow still grows through the 2027 peak (UBS) — answer: 2027 organic FCF "above EUR 100 million ... still the case".
- B2B service revenue −2.8% and IT delays (Berenberg, Deutsche Bank) — persistent and unresolved.
- Global separation (Berenberg) — deferred to "around 2028".

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: domestic EBITDA turned negative in Q3 2026 (−1.4%); B2B keeps shrinking; Wallonia deal slipped again (Q3 2026); returns on capital are low and falling; heavy leverage; CEO-addressed structural fears on the Q3 2026 call show the market is pricing a terminal story.
- Green: 2026 cash guide doubled (Q3 2026); Global back to margin growth earlier than planned; consumer pricing power intact; dividend policy reconfirmed for the next two years; no bond maturity before 2028.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The CEO now talks about "value crystallization" for Global rather than "strategic options", which points to a separation in 2028, not a near-term sale. The language on duct access has gone quiet since Q2. The Head of B2C also carries the AI title, a sign management sees AI-agent shopping as a churn risk worth a senior owner.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT
Trajectory: turning — from a growth-and-acquisition story to a cash-harvest-after-fiber story. The single most important thing for the director: the equity is a thin slice on top of about EUR 5.1 billion of debt, so small changes in post-2027 cash flow move the share value a lot; the 2026 guide raise helps but half of it is timing.

**Moat:** a narrow but real moat from regulatory licenses, owned ducts and network scale in a small dense country, plus switching costs from bundled fixed-plus-mobile customers. Width is narrow: returns on capital sit well below the cost of capital and have drifted down, largely because of fiber depreciation and the Global write-downs, while home-market pricing power is holding. **Secular threat:** manageable — the four-player Belgian market and duct-access overbuild are competitive (cyclical-structural) pressures, satellite is not a credible substitute in Belgium, and AI agents raise churn risk at the margin. The cheapness is mostly leverage plus a slow-growth incumbent, not a melting terminal value — but it is not a clear fear-print either.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Genmab has turned a royalty company into an oncology company with three newly de-risked medicines, and the royalty still pays for the transition. In October 2026 three late-stage (Phase III) trials read out positive: EPCORE DLBCL-2 for Epkinly in first-line diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (hazard ratio 0.49, meaning roughly half the risk of progression versus standard R-CHOP), RAINFOL-02 for Rina-S in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer (progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.29, and overall survival also met, regardless of folate-receptor level), and LiGeR-HN1 for petosemtamab in first-line head and neck cancer (overall survival hazard ratio 0.50). Management reaffirmed peak-sales targets of more than $3B for Epkinly, more than $2B for Rina-S and multi-billion for petosemtamab on 2026-11-05, which analysts on the call called conservative. Meanwhile the existing business is growing: revenue up 22% in the first nine months of 2026, Epkinly sales $491M (+47%), full-year revenue guided to the upper part of the range, and trailing-twelve-month free cash flow of about $845M. Darzalex net sales at J&J were $4.24B in Q3 2026 alone, so the royalty stream that funds the launches is still near its peak. Management has committed to cutting gross leverage below 3x by the end of 2027, which a growing royalty plus launches should make achievable. If the three launches arrive on schedule from 2027, Genmab's own products replace the Darzalex royalty before it rolls off, and the market has to value it as a self-funding multi-product oncology company rather than a royalty with an expiry date. Conditions: approvals in 2027, a petosemtamab filing accepted on the interim survival data, and deleveraging on plan.
picks.bear_thesis: The stock has already roughly doubled in about three months (52-week range 1,512 to 3,947 DKK; 50-day average about 2,604 DKK) and now prices in most of the October good news. The single largest asset is still the Darzalex royalty, whose end-date was never quantified on any call and could not be verified from a primary source in this review; if it rolls off around the end of the decade the core of today's cash flow shrinks sharply just as three launches are still ramping. The Merus purchase left net debt of about $3.34B (2026-09-30), with Q3 interest expense of $111M against $25M of interest income, and adjusted operating profit grew only 9% against 22% revenue growth in the first nine months as launch and integration costs mount. The petosemtamab survival result is from a first interim analysis, so regulators may ask for more, and its combination partner Keytruda loses exclusivity late in the decade. Launch execution in three new indications at once is a new skill for a company that historically let partners sell. In today's backdrop of positive real interest rates, long-dated launch value is exactly what the market discounts hardest, and a broader biotech sell-off could push the shares back toward 2,400 to 2,800 DKK without any company-specific bad news.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrower than it was. Through mid-2026 the street priced Genmab as a Darzalex royalty with an expiry date plus an expensive acquisition (Merus) of unproven value; the October 2026 readouts disproved that, and the stock roughly doubled. Today's question is whether the market now over- or under-prices the three launches. Analysts on the 2026-11-05 call (TD Securities) already called the more than $3B Epkinly, more than $2B Rina-S and multi-billion petosemtamab targets conservative, so consensus is leaning optimistic on the products. Our edge, such as it is, is that the market still lumps Genmab with long-duration biotech that sells off on sector days, even though roughly a third of the value is a contractual royalty generating cash now. That is a modest, not a dramatic, disagreement.
picks.valley_of_death: In the next 3 to 9 months: no debt wall is visible in the materials, but Q3 2026 interest expense of $111M shows the cost of the Merus debt, and launch spending will keep operating profit growth below revenue growth into 2027. Regulatory risk: petosemtamab's filing rests on an interim survival analysis. Market risk: a further sector-wide biotech de-rating in a positive-real-rate environment, which is exactly what delivered today's price, could take the shares toward the high-2,000s without any company news. LiGeR-HN2 in Q1 2027 is a second binary for petosemtamab. None of these looks thesis-ending; they are the reason the downside case sits at about 2,420 DKK.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is low. There is no dividend to cut and no index event in the materials. Today's drop tracked a sector-wide biotech sell-off (XBI and IBB both down about 2% on 2026-11-10). After a doubling in three months, momentum and event-driven holders who bought for the October readouts are the likeliest sellers; their exit is a source of better prices, not a thesis risk.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds, and the price we said we would wait for has arrived. Yesterday (2026-11-09) we set a buying level near 3,600 DKK, expecting a sector-wide biotech sell-off could deliver it; today the shares traded at 3,581 DKK on exactly that kind of day, with biotech funds down about 2% and no Genmab-specific news. Nothing about the business changed overnight: revenue is up 22% this year, Epkinly is growing 47%, and three late-stage trials succeeded in October. Our sum-of-the-parts fair value (valuing each product and royalty separately and adding them up) remains about 4,340 DKK, about 21% above today's price, just clearing the 20% discount we require in the current environment. The adverse case of about 2,420 DKK, if the Darzalex royalty ends early and the launches disappoint, is about 32% below, so this is a moderate-conviction buy rather than a bargain: the upside depends on three 2027 launches and on debt coming down as promised. The margin is thin, so if the price rises back above about 3,615 DKK the discount no longer clears our bar and the code will treat it as a wait again.

# Genmab A/S (GMAB.CO) - a deep dive on management and the setup
As of 2026-11-10. Price used: 3,581 DKK (Copenhagen listing, FMP quote 2026-11-10, down 2.2% on the day). Transcripts covered: Q3 2025 (2025-11-08), full-year 2025 (2026-02-17), Q1 2026 (2026-05-14), first half 2026 (2026-08-06) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-05).

Takeaway: management promised a "catalyst-rich" 2026 and delivered it. Three positive late-stage (Phase III) trials landed in October 2026, revenue grew 22% over the first nine months, and the company kept its peak-sales targets. The open questions are not about credibility; they are about the balance sheet the Merus purchase created (net debt about $3.3B at 2026-09-30) and the eventual end of the Darzalex royalty, which still pays for everything.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **Late 2025:** the story was "transition" - from a royalty collector (Darzalex from J&J, Kesimpta from Novartis) to a company that sells its own medicines (Epkinly with AbbVie, Tivdak), plus the then-pending Merus acquisition (petosemtamab) and Rina-S from the 2024 ProfoundBio deal.
- **Full-year 2025 (2026-02-17):** guidance year; leverage commitment introduced ("below 3x gross leverage by the end of 2027").
- **Q1 2026 (2026-05-14):** revenue +25%; RAINFOL-02 (Rina-S, platinum-resistant ovarian cancer) completed enrollment early, pulling the readout into 2026. Management called 2026 "a very catalyst-rich year".
- **H1 2026 (2026-08-06):** revenue +25%; EPCORE DLBCL-4 positive in June; European approval of Epkinly plus R2 in second-line follicular lymphoma; two new Phase III colorectal trials for petosemtamab.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-05):** "October was a truly unprecedented month" - EPCORE DLBCL-2 (first-line diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, hazard ratio 0.49), RAINFOL-02 (progression-free survival hazard ratio 0.29, overall survival also met) and LiGeR-HN1 (first-line head and neck, overall survival hazard ratio 0.50 at the first interim analysis). The narrative has expanded; nothing was quietly dropped.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue growing 22-25% | Q1 +25%, H1 +25%, 9M +22% (calls); screener's -82% fiscal-2025 revenue figure is a data artifact of the reporting base, not a collapse (2024 rev 21.5B DKK) | Matches; ignore the -82% |
| "Growing operating profits" while investing | Adjusted operating profit +9% in 9M 2026; Q3 2026 operating income $441M (filed 2026-11-05) | Matches, but slower than revenue - margin dilution from Merus and launch build |
| Epkinly momentum | $491M 9M sales, +47% y/y | Matches |
| Tivdak "strong, stable" | $131M 9M, +9% | Modest; a supporting, not a driving, asset |
| Disciplined capital | Net debt $3.34B incl. $206M leases (2026-09-30); interest expense $111M vs $25M interest income in Q3 | Leverage is real and costs money; deleveraging promise is checkable by end-2027 |
| Profitability | TTM free cash flow about $845M, TTM diluted EPS 11.71; ROIC 12.6% | Still solidly cash-generative, though well below 2024 peak |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Rising. Q1 2026 was measured ("focused progress"); H1 2026 was "a really good place"; Q3 2026 was "a landmark stretch" and "unprecedented". Notably the confidence is backed by dated trial results rather than adjectives. The tone stays offensive (launch preparation, new Phase III starts, two to four new clinical programs a year) rather than defensive.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
High. The 2026 readout calendar was met or pulled forward (RAINFOL-02 accelerated into 2026). Full-year revenue now expected in the upper part of the guidance range (2026-11-05). The earnings-beat rate in the screener is 5 of 7 quarters (71%). Peak-sales targets (more than $3B Epkinly, more than $2B Rina-S, "multi-billion" petosemtamab) were reaffirmed, not raised, after positive data - if anything a mild sandbagging pattern.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Whether the peak-sales targets are now too low (TD Securities, 2026-11-05) - management declined to raise them.
- Filing strategy for petosemtamab on an interim overall-survival result; second-line data (LiGeR-HN2) due Q1 2027.
- Keytruda's loss of exclusivity late in the decade and its effect on the petosemtamab plus pembrolizumab combination (BNP Paribas) - not directly answered.
- Epkinly formulation patents possibly extending exclusivity (raised earlier in the year) - management declined to discuss IP on the call.
- The Darzalex royalty end-date is never quantified on the calls; it remains the single largest unverified input in any valuation.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: leverage from the Merus purchase (net debt about $3.3B; interest expense $111M in Q3 2026).
- Red: petosemtamab's overall-survival result is from a first interim analysis; regulators may want more.
- Red: adjusted operating profit (+9%) growing far slower than revenue (+22%) in 9M 2026.
- Red: Darzalex royalty dependence with an unquantified end-date.
- Green: three positive Phase III readouts in October 2026, each consistent with the Phase II data.
- Green: Epkinly +47% with the R2 combination now standard of care in second-line follicular lymphoma.
- Green: Rina-S worked regardless of folate receptor level or prior mirvetuximab - a broad label is plausible.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- "Winning programs" language (Q3 2026) signals capital will concentrate on the three late-stage assets; business development shifts to partnerships (Incyte) rather than new large acquisitions, consistent with the deleveraging promise.
- A Halozyme subcutaneous program for petosemtamab mirrors the Darzalex subcutaneous playbook that extended that franchise - a life-cycle signal, not yet in any number.
- Management now frames Genmab as a "commercialization engine across key markets" - the identity has shifted from royalty company to operating oncology company.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: STRENGTHENING. The pipeline bets (ProfoundBio 2024, Merus 2025) have each now produced a positive Phase III. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: how much of today's price is paid by the Darzalex royalty that ends around the end of the decade versus three launches that start in 2027 - the stock has roughly doubled in three months, so the remaining discount to fair value is modest and depends on launch execution and leverage falling as promised.

Moat: intangible (antibody engineering platforms - DuoBody, HexaBody, ADC know-how - plus patents and royalty contracts). Returns are good (ROIC 12.6%, 92% gross margin) but well below the 2024 peak as the company shifted from pure royalty income to funding its own launches, so the moat is narrow rather than wide; the trend is stable as the new medicines replace a royalty stream that is contractual and finite. Secular threat: manageable - the main risk is a product patent cliff and US drug-price negotiation, not a structural force that shrinks the whole base. The cheapness that existed earlier in 2026 was a fear-print, and much of it has already closed.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Enterprise value about $44B, less net debt of $3.34B (borrowings $4.99B plus $206M leases, minus $1.86B cash, 2026-09-30) gives equity of about $40.7B, about $661 per share, or about 4,340 DKK at the 6.56 DKK per dollar rate used on 2026-11-09. But the earlier consensus of about 7.8% forward growth was too high, and the new pessimism treats a cyclical trough as structural. Net margin held at 6.7% in Q3 on 10% lower sales, which a structurally broken franchise could not do. Where we disagree with the market is narrow: fair value is about HK$23.50, only about 11% above today's HK$21.20 after a 10% rally since 26 October. The disagreement is not wide enough to pay up for.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the next 3 to 9 months. Q4 2026 and Q1 2027 compare against strong subsidy-boosted quarters in China, so headline revenue declines are likely to continue. picks.positioning_washout: We see no forced-selling pressure in the shareholder base. Haier is not cutting its dividend, and there is no lock-up, index deletion or spin-off. Morgan cut Midea and Haier together) and on US air-conditioner inventory. The candidates are: full-year 2026 results (around March 2027, about 144 days away), which set the dividend and 2027 tone; continued buybacks across the H-, A- and D-share classes; and evidence that China appliance demand has bottomed after the subsidy. # Haier Smart Home (6690.HK) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 9 November 2026. Prices in Hong Kong dollars (HK$) for the H-share listing 6690.HK; financials reported in renminbi (RMB). HK$1 = RMB 0.8504 (FMP, 9 November 2026).*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript was bundled with this review, and FMP has none for this listing. A fresh web search was not available for this run, so the evidence here is: FMP's quarterly income, balance-sheet and cash-flow statements through 30 September 2026; the screener's multi-year trajectory; and dated Hong Kong news headlines (AASTOCKS) on the third-quarter results, broker target changes and buybacks. No management quotes appear below because none could be sourced. We have not made any up.

## 1. Narrative arc
Haier is the world's largest white-goods group (fridges, washers, air conditioners) across its own brand, GE Appliances in the US, Fisher & Paykel and Candy. From 2021 to 2025 it compounded steadily. Revenue grew from RMB 227.6 billion to RMB 302.4 billion (about 7.5% a year) and net income from RMB 13.1 billion to RMB 19.6 billion (about 10% a year). The story was "premiumisation plus global share gains plus digital cost cuts", and the numbers backed it.

2026 broke that rhythm. China's appliance trade-in subsidy, which pulled demand forward through 2025, has faded. US air-conditioner inventory is high. The story has moved from growth to defence: margin protection, buybacks and dividends.
- **Q1 2026:** revenue RMB 73.7 billion; net income RMB 4.65 billion.
- **Q2 2026:** revenue RMB 78.1 billion, about 1% higher than a year earlier; net income RMB 5.64 billion, about 14% lower.
- **Q3 2026 (reported at the end of October 2026):** revenue RMB 69.7 billion, about 10% lower than the RMB 77.5 billion a year earlier. Net income RMB 4.68 billion, about 12% lower than RMB 5.34 billion. Nine-month net profit was about RMB 15 billion, down 13.7%.

## 2. Claims vs financials (forensic)
| Claim (the committee's working thesis, management's stated strategy) | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Margins hold when sales fall | Gross margin was 27.1% in Q3 2026, against 27.9% in Q3 2025 and 29.0% in Q2 2026. Net margin was 6.7% in Q3 2026, against 6.9% a year earlier. BofA Securities says about RMB 0.5 billion of one-off expenses hit the quarter; excluding them, net profit fell only about 3% on 10% lower sales. | Mostly holds. Gross margin slipped, but operating cost control protected the bottom line. |
| Overseas growth offsets China | BofA: overseas revenue "broadly flat" in Q3. CLSA: weak China demand after the subsidy was withdrawn, plus high US air-conditioner inventory. | Not delivered this quarter. Both engines stalled together. |
| Cash generation funds dividends and buybacks | Trailing-twelve-month (TTM) free cash flow is RMB 10.2 billion. But Q3 2026 operating cash flow was only RMB 1.1 billion (Q3 2025: RMB 6.6 billion), and free cash flow was negative RMB 2.0 billion in a quarter that paid RMB 8.5 billion of dividends. | Annual cash generation is adequate; Q3 cash conversion was weak. |
| Shareholder returns | H-share buybacks continue. On 9 November 2026 the company bought 300,000 shares at HK$21.08-21.26; 5 million shares (0.18%) have been bought back under the current mandate. The company also bought back A-shares and D-shares (79 million D-shares for about EUR 148 million, undated on the page). | Real, but small against the share count. |
| Balance sheet is not a constraint | 30 September 2026: cash and short-term investments RMB 44.6 billion against borrowings of RMB 72.85 billion plus RMB 4.5 billion of leases. Net debt is RMB 32.8 billion including leases (RMB 28.3 billion excluding them), about 1.1x EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation). There is also RMB 44.8 billion of long-term investments. | Holds. |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory
No transcript is available, so we cannot rate tone from management's words. The actions read as defensive: steady small buybacks, a large dividend, and no growth acceleration. Brokers turned more cautious around the results. CLSA cut its target to HK$25, BofA to HK$24.5, Jefferies to HK$21, and J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs both cut. Rating from behaviour: **Declining (cyclical), not collapsing.**

## 4. Guidance credibility
Haier does not give hard numerical guidance. The screener records only 2 of 7 recent quarters as earnings beats (29%), and 2026 earnings are tracking down about 14% while consensus earlier assumed growth. Reliability: **Medium**. The long record is strong; the 2026 forecasts were too high.

## 5. Analyst pressure points
- How quickly does China demand normalise once the subsidy is gone, and how much channel destocking (dealers running down stock) is left?
- US air-conditioner inventory, and GE Appliances' margins if tariffs or price competition worsen.
- Whether Q3's weak cash conversion is timing (working capital) or a lasting change.
- Whether buybacks will be stepped up while the shares trade near 10x earnings.

## 6. Red flags / green flags
- Red flag: Q3 2026 revenue fell about 10% year on year, the first double-digit quarterly decline in the visible record.
- Red flag: Q3 2026 operating cash flow fell to RMB 1.1 billion from RMB 6.6 billion a year earlier.
- Red flag: Q3 2026 gross margin slipped about 0.8 percentage points year on year.
- Red flag: the screener's earnings-beat rate is low (2 of 7 quarters).
- Green flag: net margin was close to flat in Q3 (6.7% vs 6.9%) despite the sales drop; excluding one-offs, profit fell only about 3%.
- Green flag: five-year earnings per share growth was about 10.7% a year and book value per share growth about 10.8% a year. Return on equity is 16% and return on invested capital about 12%.
- Green flag: buybacks continue across all three share classes (9 November 2026 H-share purchase).
- Green flag: margins held through 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 29.8% in 2019, 31.2% in 2021).

## 7. Hidden signals
- The shares rallied about 10% in the ten trading days after the results (to HK$21.20 on 9 November from HK$19.30 on 26 October), even as every broker we saw cut its target. The market had already priced a bad quarter. The "worst is known" reflex is at work.
- Brokers cut their targets but none (in the headlines we saw) downgraded to sell. Their new targets cluster at HK$21-25, close to our fair value.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)
**Trajectory: deteriorating (cyclical).** Earnings are falling in 2026 because China's subsidy-driven demand has reversed and overseas growth has paused. The franchise itself is not shrinking structurally.

**The single most important point for sizing:** the stock trades at about 10x trailing earnings, below its own five-year earnings growth. The 2026 profit decline (down about 14% for the nine months) is the base the market now prices, so the question is whether 2027 stabilises. Q3 cash conversion is the item to watch.

**Moat:** scale and cost advantages plus brand and channel (global manufacturing and purchasing scale, the GE Appliances, Fisher & Paykel and Haier/Casarte brands, and a large Chinese dealer network). Return on invested capital of about 12% and return on equity of about 16% are solid but not exceptional. Gross margin is in the high 20s, edging down this year for cyclical reasons. **A narrow but real moat, stable in trend.**

**Secular threat:** manageable. Appliances are a replacement-cycle category, and no structural force (such as artificial-intelligence displacement or a channel shift) threatens Haier's terminal value. The cheapness reflects fear of a cyclical trough, not a structurally shrinking business.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Visteon (VC) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*Covers five earnings calls, 2025-10-23 to 2026-10-22, plus the 2026-10-27 CFO departure notice. Price used: $76.05 (Nasdaq, USD, 2026-11-02 close).*

**Takeaway.** Visteon still does what it says on the top line: sales keep beating a shrinking vehicle-production base, and the order book keeps filling. What changed in the most recent quarter is quality and cash. A $77 million warranty charge on its core product (instrument clusters), a cut to full-year profit and cash guidance, nine months of roughly zero free cash flow, and the chief financial officer's resignation five days after the call mean the "steady cash machine" story now needs to be proven again rather than assumed.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-23):** a defensive but confident call. Sales were "trending below the midpoint of guidance" on industry headwinds, but adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, excluding one-offs) of $119M at a 13% margin and adjusted free cash flow of $110M let management maintain full-year guidance. The new quarterly dividend had just been paid, "with more capital returns planned".
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-19):** the story shifted to 2026 as a reset year. Full-year 2025 sales of about $3.77B and adjusted EBITDA of $492M (roughly 13%); record bookings. Management flagged a "roughly 20% volume reduction" in battery-management systems (BMS) sold to GM, Ford program discontinuations, and memory-chip cost inflation it intended to pass to customers ("we are absolutely intending to recover the memory cost increases"). Capital allocation framework: dividend, tuck-in M&A, and "buyback ... in the $100-plus million".
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-23):** sales $954M (+2%), EBITDA $104M, free cash flow negative $23M "driven by normal seasonality and higher inventory". Net cash $385M. Guidance held "despite S&P cutting" its production forecast.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-23):** EBITDA $116M (12.1%), cash $650M, $2B of bookings, and a $200M accelerated share repurchase (a buyback where shares are retired up front). The new language is "AI-enabled cockpit computing" and high-performance compute (HPC) for Chinese domestic carmakers (Geely brands, Chery, SAIC).
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-22):** sales grew 6% to $970M, about 10 points ahead of customer production. But $77M of warranty charges on two cluster programs cut EBITDA to $46M (12.7% margin excluding the charge), free cash flow was neutral on a semiconductor inventory build, bookings slipped (just under $1B; "several significant sourcing decisions ... shifted into the fourth quarter"), and full-year EBITDA guidance fell to $370-410M with free cash flow guidance of $90-130M. Sales guidance was raised to $3.80-3.85B.

The arc: the growth story expanded (HPC, China domestic, India, two-wheelers, commercial vehicles) while the earnings and cash story contracted.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Market outperformance" — sales beat production | Q3 2026 sales +6% vs customer production about -5%; Europe +~20%; Asia ex-China +~14% | Corroborated |
| Underlying margin is stable around 12-13% | Q3 2026 12.7% ex-warranty; Q2 12.1%; FY2025 ~13% | Corroborated, but only by excluding the charge |
| Strong cash generation | FY2025 free cash flow ~$250M (scan P/FCF 7.3x); 9M 2026 adjusted free cash flow -$4M; TTM free cash flow $51M; FY2026 guide cut to $90-130M | Diverges — the cash claim is now the weak link |
| Memory costs will be recovered from customers | "good progress recovering higher memory costs" (Q3 2026); gross margin about 12% in Q1-Q2 2026 (11.8% and 12.3%) vs 14.3% in Q3 2025, 4.8% in Q3 2026 with warranty | Partly — recoveries lag the cost |
| $6B bookings target | $3.9B through nine months; Q4 needs ~$2.1B; management concedes "some final award decisions may extend into 2027" | At risk |
| Warranty is contained | Booked $77M; 10-Q discloses up to $20M more as "possible, but not probable" | Unproven until year-end |
| Capital returns | $200M accelerated buyback completed in Q3; diluted share count 27.9M (Q3 2025) to 26.0M (Q3 2026 weighted), ~24.7M now | Corroborated |

The balance sheet is sound but less cash-rich than the call implies: cash $466M against $330M of debt (management's $136M net cash), or roughly $5M of net cash once $129M of capitalized leases are counted.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable on growth, declining on profit.** Q2 2026 was offensive ("clear technology leadership", HPC "incremental" to Investor Day). Q3 2026 kept that tone on demand ("we have not seen a corresponding change in the underlying demand") but became defensive on costs and quality: the warranty charges "relate to previously delivered products"; "as additional cost could be possible, but not probable, we were required to disclose the top end of the range". The CFO's answer on 2027 repetition was garbled in the transcript ("we still anticipate additional charges for them"), which analysts should have pressed. Specificity on 2027 fell: management declined to update the Investor Day 2027 outlook until the Q4 call.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

FY2025: sales came in below the guidance midpoint, but EBITDA and cash held — a partial delivery. FY2026: sales guidance has been raised, but EBITDA guidance was cut, partly by the one-off warranty charge and partly by "cost pressures", and free cash flow guidance was cut on inventory. The scan shows earnings beats in 4 of 7 quarters (57%), and the Q3 2026 EPS of $0.19 missed the ~$2.25 consensus by a wide margin. **Reliability: Medium.** No sandbagging pattern; if anything, sales conservatism and cost optimism.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Warranty recurrence** (Barclays, Q3 2026): is $77M the end? The answer was "we believe that we are currently accrued at the right level", not a guarantee.
- **Memory-cost recovery** (Q4 2025): analysts calculated that guidance assumed very little recovery; management insisted on "the majority". Q3 2026's cost-pressure cut suggests the analysts were closer.
- **Insourcing and Chinese supplier durability** (Q2 and Q3 2026): Western carmakers moving software in-house and Chinese carmakers swapping suppliers quickly. Management's answer is that region-specific AI rules make it a long relationship — plausible, untested.
- **GM/Ford ramp-down** (Q2 2026): management called its Investor Day roll-off assumption "conservative" but gave no offset timing before 2027.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: $77M warranty charge on instrument clusters, which are 46% of revenue (Q3 2026).
- Red: CFO Jerome Rouquet's departure announced 2026-10-27, five days after the warranty charge and guidance cut; interim CFO named, no permanent successor.
- Red: nine-month 2026 adjusted free cash flow of -$4M; full-year cash guide cut (2026-10-22).
- Red: bookings slippage into Q4/2027 (2026-10-22).
- Red: open-market insider activity is 14 sales and zero buys.
- Green: sales outgrowth of about 10 points over production in Q3 2026; Europe and India strong.
- Green: HPC moved from awards into production (Chery, 2026-10-22); China domestic carmakers now about half of China sales, up from about a third.
- Green: $200M buyback completed at higher prices than today; share count down about 10% in a year.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The vocabulary has moved from "displays and clusters" to "AI-enabled cockpit computing" and "China speed". That is where the multiple expansion story lives, but it is still a small share of sales; the instrument cluster, the product with the warranty problem, remains the profit engine. The CFO change, coming right after a cash-guide cut and a buyback executed at higher prices, is the signal the director should weigh most.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: deteriorating.** Growth is real but cash conversion, product quality and finance leadership all worsened in a single quarter. **The single most important thing to weigh:** whether FY2026 free cash flow lands inside the $90-130M guide with no further warranty charge when Q4 results print (expected around 2027-02-19). If it does, the stock at about 4x normalized EBITDA is plainly cheap; if it does not, the "cheap on cash flow" label rests on 2025 numbers that are no longer current.

**Moat:** narrow, built on switching costs (multi-year programs designed into specific vehicles) and scale in sourcing semiconductors. Underlying EBITDA margins have been stable at 12-13% for three years, so the moat is not eroding on the evidence, but gross margin is contracting and return on invested capital (~9%) is modest. **Secular threat: material, not terminal** — carmaker insourcing of cockpit software and low-cost Chinese suppliers could compress share and pricing, but the shift to bigger displays and centralized compute adds content per vehicle. The cheapness looks like a fear print on a cyclical and execution stumble, not a melting base — with the caveat that cash must reappear to prove it.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.
