# SLVM (Sylvamo) - Forensic Dossier, 2026-11-09

Live price used: $38.00 (NYSE, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-09; prior close $39.38). Last committee look: 2026-10-12 at $32.24.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story has moved in four steps over the last year. In November 2025 (Q3 2025 call) Sylvamo was a steady uncoated-freesheet producer (the plain office and printing paper grade) earning about $150M of adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) a quarter, buying back stock near $45. In February 2026 a new CEO, John Sims, arrived with a "legendary" vision and stopped giving quarterly guidance. The first half of 2026 was a trough: $29M EBITDA in Q1 and $60M in Q2, hit by the end of the International Paper Riverdale supply deal, tariff-driven footprint changes, mill outages and Iran-war freight costs. On 2026-11-06 two things landed at once: Q3 adjusted EBITDA of $128M from continuing operations (a 20% margin) and a binding put-option offer from Midas Atlantic Partners / Najafi to take the loss-making European business (Saillat, France and Nymolla, Sweden). Europe is now a discontinued operation. As recently as the Q1 2026 call management said it had "the right strategy in Europe" - the exit is a reversal, but a rational one.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Claim (2026-08-07): the second half would show better price, mix and costs. Q3 delivered price/mix +$25M, operations +$6M and outages +$38M versus Q2; inputs and freight were -$6M. The claim held on the continuing basis.
- Reported figures are recast to exclude Europe, and about $6.5M a quarter of corporate cost formerly charged to Europe now sits in the Americas. Q2 continuing EBITDA was restated to $66M against $60M total, so Europe lost about $6M in Q2 even with green-energy credits. The recast flatters the comparison less than it might: the stranded cost is in the numbers.
- Free cash flow is thin: $16M in Q3, trailing twelve months $23M, against an $18M-a-quarter dividend. Diluted GAAP EPS for the trailing year is -$4.51 (Europe write-downs). Cash generation has not caught up with EBITDA.
- Balance sheet (2026-09-30): borrowings $1.00B, cash $93M, net debt $907M (no capitalised leases in the figure). Against roughly $345M of continuing trailing EBITDA (about $115M Q4-25 + $34M + $66M + $128M) that is about 2.6x, up from 1.6x at end-2025.
- The Europe exit is not a sale for cash: Sylvamo hands over the business with about EUR50M of working capital and about EUR35M of net cash, and receives only a 20% right to future distributions. It is paying roughly $100M (about $2.50 a share) to stop the losses.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Tone moved from defensive (Q1: "transition costs plus input cost inflation") to measured confidence (Q3: "solid execution on what we said we would do"). The CFO was candid that input and freight costs rise another $6M in Q4 and that 2026 costs run about $50M above 2025 and carry into 2027. No new guidance; the capital markets day was pushed to the second or third quarter of 2027.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Mixed but improving. Management abandoned annual guidance in 2024 and quarterly guidance in February 2026, which removes accountability. The Riverdale impact estimate was revised from -$85M to -$65M (better). The second-half recovery it described on 2026-08-07 arrived. Eastover paper-machine work is "60% through, on schedule and on budget"; the Sumter converting plan was enlarged by about $25M of extra 2027 capex with a claimed 30%+ return. Score: credible on operations, opaque on targets.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Cost inflation: George Staphos (BofA) pressed on whether the $6M quarterly cost step is cumulative - it is ($12M by Q4), and about $50M a year carried into 2027.
- Stranded overhead: the $6-7M a quarter previously allocated to Europe; management promises to cut it "over time", no number.
- Poison pill: the shareholder rights plan adopted November 2025 expired 2026-11-09 and was not renewed - relevant because Atlas Holdings pulled its directors in November 2025.
- Street targets are drifting down: RBC cut to $35 on 2026-10-16; the one-year average was $47.50.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: leverage rising to about 2.6x with thin free cash flow; paying to exit Europe; guidance withdrawn; insiders sold 12,980 shares in the open market with no buys; Piotroski 3/9; structurally shrinking end market (industry North America demand about -2% this year); imports rising again.
Green: Q3 passed the committee's proof test; Europe losses removed; owned Brazilian forest land (appraised near BRL 5B, about $0.9B) gives a cost edge; Riverdale conversion removed about 7% of North American supply; Colombia dropped anti-dumping duties on Brazilian paper (September 2026); poison pill allowed to lapse.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- Letting the poison pill lapse the same week as the Europe exit makes a cleaner Americas-only company easier to bid for; Atlas Holdings is a known interested party. This is optionality, not a thesis.
- The capex step-up at Sumter replaces Brazil-to-US cut-size imports that tariffs made uneconomic - management is building around tariffs staying.
- The 50-day Eastover outage runs into Q4, so Q4 EBITDA will dip again; the market may read that as a relapse.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Sound in direction (focus on the low-cost Americas mills, high-return Eastover/Sumter projects, exit a sub-scale European business) but expensive in the short run: buybacks paused, roughly $100M handed over with Europe, more capex in 2027, leverage near 2.6x. The dividend is not covered by trailing free cash flow. The test the committee set - Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA of at least $120M - was met on 2026-11-06 at $128M (continuing operations; Europe was running at a small loss, so the total is unlikely to be materially lower). The business case is back on track; the price has already moved 18% toward fair value.

picks.bull_thesis: Kia is a profitable, growing carmaker priced as if its earnings were about to halve again. At 97,000 won (FMP close 2026-11-09) the market value is about 37.7 trillion won, of which about 21.2 trillion is net cash (cash and short-term investments of 23.5 trillion against 2.25 trillion of debt including leases, balance sheet of 2026-06-30) - about 54,500 won per share, or 56% of the price. What remains, about 42,500 won per share, buys a car business that earned about 6.9 trillion won of net income over the last four reported quarters (roughly 17,800 won per share) and generated 6.44 trillion won of free cash flow in the twelve months to 2026-06-30. That is about 2.4 times trailing earnings for the operating business. The operating numbers have stabilised after the 2025 US tariff reset: revenue was higher than a year earlier in every 2026 quarter, and Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) brought revenue of 31.6 trillion won, up about 10%, and operating profit of 1.82 trillion, up about 24%, with the operating margin rising to 5.8% from 5.1%. The share price fall from 205,500 won (2026-02-27) is mostly the Korean market, not Kia: the KOSPI index is down about 47% from its high and sister company Hyundai Motor about 65%, against Kia's 53%. The dividend was raised in cash terms (2.64 trillion won paid in Q2 2026, about 6,800 won per share, a 7% yield at today's price). Kia also kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 16.1% to 18.5%), which matters in today's reflationary backdrop. Conditions: operating profit holds at roughly the 2026 run-rate of 1.5-2.8 trillion won a quarter, the cash pile is not spent on value-destroying projects, and the Korean market liquidation does not turn into a lasting earnings shock for exporters.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness may be a permanent Korea discount compounded by a cyclical peak. Net cash in a carmaker is working capital and a buffer for downturns, not money owners can take out; it has sat on the balance sheet for years without closing the gap. US tariffs on Korean cars are now a permanent cost under the Section 301 regime that took effect 2026-07-24, and gross margin was still about 1.7 points below a year earlier in Q2 2026 (18.3% vs 20.0%). The sell-side has been too optimistic for nearly two years - Kia beat estimates in 0 of the last 7 quarters - so the 2027 consensus of 19,663 won per share (range 14,806 to 24,296) should be haircut. Q3 2026 net income fell about 10% to 1.29 trillion won even as operating profit rose, because the usual interest and affiliate income vanished below the operating line, and that has not been explained. Share buybacks, about 0.3 trillion won a quarter through 2025, are absent from the first half of 2026. Higher-for-longer rates squeeze US auto-loan affordability, Chinese electric-vehicle makers compete on price in Europe and emerging markets, and the Korean market is still in a liquidation driven by foreign selling and the memory-chip unwind. A recession could take auto earnings back to 2021 levels (about 4.8 trillion won, roughly 12,000 won per share), and in a forced-selling tape the price can fall below any fundamental floor. What would confirm it: another quarter of falling net income, a cut to the shareholder-return plan, or an operating margin below 5%.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the price implies Kia's earnings are about to fall sharply again, and the numbers do not show it. At 97,000 won the operating car business is valued at roughly 42,500 won per share after net cash, about 2.4 times trailing earnings, while operating profit in the quarter ended 2026-09-30 rose about 24% on a year earlier. The sell-off is being driven by the Korean market as a whole (KOSPI down about 47% from its high) rather than by Kia-specific news. Where the street has been wrong in the other direction: consensus has been too high for nearly two years (beats in 0 of 7 quarters), so we haircut the 2027 consensus of 19,663 won per share rather than rely on it. Our fair value does not need the consensus to be right; it needs operating earnings to hold near the 2026 run-rate.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): the Korean market liquidation may not be over - foreign outflows and the memory-chip unwind have taken the KOSPI down about 47%, and Kia falls with it regardless of results (down 3.3% today while Toyota and GM rose about 4-5%). A weaker won helps exports but raises the dollar cost for foreign holders, which can keep them selling. US tariffs under the Section 301 regime in force since 2026-07-24 are a permanent cost, and rising real rates hurt US car affordability. There is no debt wall and no cash-burn hump: net cash is about 21.2 trillion won. Q4 2026 results (late January 2027) are the next checkpoint; another below-the-line surprise like Q3 would hurt sentiment.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure: the selling so far looks like a sector-wide and market-wide liquidation rather than Kia-specific forced selling - Korean equities lost about 22% in July 2026 alone, a large levered fund was margin-called and liquidated in late July according to the regime log, and foreign investors have been de-risking Korea. Kia is a large, liquid index weight and so gets sold with the market. The shareholder base is not yield-focused enough for a dividend cut to trigger mechanical selling, and none has been announced; the dividend was raised in cash terms in Q2 2026.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds: Kia is still growing (revenue up about 10% and operating profit up about 24% in the quarter ended 2026-09-30) and sits on about 21.2 trillion won of net cash, more than half of its 37.7 trillion won market value. At 97,000 won the stock trades well below our base fair value of 135,000 won, a discount that clears the 20% entry bar for the current reflationary backdrop. The fall from 205,500 won since late February is mostly a Korean market liquidation (KOSPI down about 47% from its high, Hyundai Motor down about 65%), not a Kia earnings collapse. We hold conviction at a middling level rather than higher for three reasons: no earnings-call transcript or Q3 release could be read, so management's guidance and the cause of the Q3 net-income drop are unverified; the street's numbers have been too high for nearly two years; and the Korean market tape could keep pushing the price down in the near term. The moat is narrow - scale and a brand that has moved up-market - and tariffs are now a permanent cost, which is why the value case stops short of the top grade. Size it as a position that can sit through further market-driven weakness; the balance sheet means there is no solvency risk on the way.

picks.bull_thesis: The bull case is that a large, state-backed Chinese drug distributor and manufacturer trades at about half of book value while its underlying profit is recovering. Prices are for the Hong Kong H-share at HK$11.05 (FMP live quote, 2026-11-09); company figures are in renminbi (RMB). Third-quarter 2026 attributable profit was RMB 1.08B against RMB 0.69B a year earlier (up 57%) on revenue of RMB 75.48B (up 2.8%), driven by operating costs falling to RMB 5.27B from RMB 6.02B. That follows a first half in which recurring profit rose 18% to RMB 2.48B and operating cash flow rose 350% to RMB 4.45B. Operating cash flow stayed positive in the third quarter (RMB 1.17B), short-term debt was cut by RMB 2.4B and RMB 1.96B of dividends were paid. Trailing free cash flow is about RMB 7.2B, a high cash yield against a market value near RMB 30B-35B at the H-share price. Book value attributable to shareholders is RMB 79.3B (about RMB 21.4 per share). The manufacturing arm, with a 59.7% gross margin in the first half and 49 innovative drugs in clinic, is valued by the market as if it were part of a low-margin distributor. For the bull case to work: recurring profit keeps growing high single digits, receivables stop outgrowing revenue, and the market starts giving the manufacturing arm a pharma multiple. The resolution driver is Chinese domestic healthcare policy, independent of the rates and AI-capex factors that dominate the global tape.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that this is a low-return, working-capital-heavy distributor that is cheap for good reason and not cheap against its own peers. Return on invested capital is 5.4% and return on equity 7.6%; earnings per share fell from RMB 1.79 in 2021 to RMB 1.54 in 2025 while book value compounded about 4% a year. Accounts receivable reached RMB 97.7B at 2026-09-30, up about 4.5% from roughly RMB 93.5B three months earlier, still outgrowing revenue and worth well over the whole H-share-implied market value; operating cash flow fell to RMB 1.17B in the third quarter from RMB 5.52B in the second. Third-quarter gross margin slipped to 9.5% from 10.2% a year earlier, the lowest of the last five quarters, so the profit gain came from cost cuts rather than pricing, under continuing medical-insurance cost control and volume-based procurement (national bulk-tender price cuts). Reported profit is repeatedly moved by one-off gains and year-end charges (fourth-quarter 2025 attributable profit only RMB 0.58B), so the fourth quarter of 2026 could again disappoint. Net debt is about RMB 15.4B excluding leases (RMB 16.9B including). Against live Hong Kong peers the stock is roughly in line, and the roughly 40% H-share discount to the A-share is structural. What would confirm the bear case: another year-end impairment, receivables outgrowing revenue again in the full-year 2026 report, or new procurement cuts hitting the manufacturing portfolio.
picks.consensus_delta: The market prices Shanghai Pharmaceuticals as one more low-return Chinese distributor at about half of book. Our variant view is modest: the manufacturing arm deserves a pharma multiple and the 2026 cash-flow recovery is better than the headline profit history suggests, but the third quarter's falling gross margin and rising receivables show why the market is not yet willing to pay for it.
picks.valley_of_death: The four months to the full-year 2026 results (around late March 2027) carry the usual year-end risk: an impairment on receivables or goodwill, or a fresh procurement round, could push reported profit down and the share toward the HK$9-10 range even with the franchise intact.
picks.positioning_washout: No forced seller is visible today. Smart-money score is 11 of 100 and institutional flow neutral; the stock sits at HK$11.05, below its 200-day average of about HK$11.60 and near the low end of its HK$10.70-12.39 52-week range. A wash-out, a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers, would most plausibly come from a sector-wide de-rating of Hong Kong-listed Chinese healthcare (policy headlines on medical-insurance payments or procurement), which could deliver HK$9.6.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near HK$9.6, which a sector-wide sell-off in Hong Kong-listed Chinese healthcare could deliver. The thesis holds: Shanghai Pharmaceuticals is a sound, state-backed franchise whose profit rose 57% in the third quarter of 2026 and whose cash generation stayed positive, but at HK$11.05 it is priced in line with its Hong Kong distributor peers, and our base fair value of about HK$12.3 offers too little upside against an adverse case near HK$8.3. Nothing dated has changed since the committee's 2026-11-02 review, so we keep that answer. The third quarter only half-passed our earlier test: profit grew strongly and operating cash flow stayed positive, but receivables still grew faster than revenue and gross margin fell, so the gain came from cost cuts. The resolution driver is Chinese healthcare policy, independent of the rates and AI-capex factors in the global tape, a plus for diversification but not a reason to pay up. At HK$9.6 the discount to fair value is about 28%, enough to clear the entry bar with a margin for the receivables risk.
picks.forcing_function: No binding, dated forcing event. Ongoing pharmacy disposals and gradual debt reduction are slow, soft levers; the full-year 2026 results around late March 2027 are the next data point.

- Balance sheet: borrowings RMB 57.6B against cash and short-term investments RMB 42.2B; net debt about RMB 15.4B excluding leases (RMB 16.9B including RMB 1.5B of leases). No transcript, so tone cannot be scored from management's own words. The filing pattern is steady: no profit warning, no new impairment flagged in the quarter, dividend paid on schedule.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
The company gives no numeric profit guidance. Record against consensus is middling: beat in 3 of the last 7 quarters (43%). Reported profit has repeatedly been moved by one-off gains (RMB 2.95B consolidation gain in the first half of 2025) and year-end charges (fourth-quarter 2025 attributable profit only RMB 0.58B), so a year-end charge in the fourth quarter of 2026 is a live risk to the reported number.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Would be: receivables growth and collection from public hospitals under medical-insurance cost control; distribution margin erosion from volume-based procurement (national bulk-tender price cuts); how much of the pipeline is valued; why the H-share trades about 40% below the A-share. Red: receivables (RMB 97.7B) are about 1.7 times the H-share-implied market value of the whole group and still outgrow revenue; return on invested capital 5.4%; recurring year-end charges; Altman-Z 2.1 (grey zone, normal for a leveraged distributor).
Green: third-quarter profit up 57% with lower costs; Piotroski 7 of 9; operating cash flow positive for a third straight quarter in 2026; debt being paid down; state ownership limits tail risk.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The third quarter's gross margin dipped while operating costs fell by about RMB 0.75B year on year: the profit gain is cost discipline, which is less durable than pricing power. The 9.5% gross margin is the lowest of the last five quarters, consistent with continuing procurement pressure on distribution.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A credible, conservatively run but low-return franchise. Profit is improving and cash generation is acceptable, but working capital keeps absorbing growth and the third quarter did not cleanly pass the committee's earlier test (receivables did not slow to revenue's pace). Fair to buy only at a clear discount.

picks.bull_thesis: Upbound (Rent-A-Center stores, Acima at retailers' checkouts, and the Brigit cash-advance app) has been through a year-long credit clean-up, and the results now show it. Lease charge-offs at Acima fell from about 10% at the Q4 2025 peak to 8.7% in Q3 2026, the lowest since 2021, and management called that path three quarters in advance. Q3 2026 (reported 2026-10-29) beat the top of every guided range: non-GAAP EPS of $1.01 against a $0.85-0.95 guide, and adjusted EBITDA of $123M against $105-115M. Acima's EBITDA rose 15% with margin up about 270 basis points. Brigit's revenue grew 37% and its EBITDA 59%, and its paying users reached 1.84M (up 27%). Rent-A-Center posted its fourth straight quarter of same-store sales growth (+1.8%). Net leverage fell to 2.4x on the way to a 2x target. Management announced a $50M buyback for this quarter, about 4% of the $1.33B market cap, on top of a $1.56 annual dividend (a 6.8% yield at $22.84). Insiders bought on the open market 8 times and sold once. At $22.84 the stock trades at about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint of roughly $4.2 and about 4.9x EV/EBITDA (enterprise value, meaning market cap plus net debt, divided by operating cash earnings), with EV of about $2.55B (ex-lease net debt of $1.22B) against about $520M of adjusted EBITDA. That multiple prices in a credit recession that the loss data does not show. Volume should turn soon: Q4 GMV (the dollar value of new leases written) is guided to roughly flat after three quarters of decline, and management now has margin room to loosen underwriting. New distribution through Boost Mobile (~5,000 stores), Experian for Brigit, and Amazon pickup at about 1,500 Rent-A-Center stores (~50 extra visits per store per week) gives that recovery a base. Conditions: charge-offs stay at or below about 9%, GMV stabilizes in Q4 2026 to Q1 2027, and the attorney-general settlement is absorbed within the FY2026 free-cash-flow guide of about $250M.
picks.bear_thesis: This is a subprime consumer lender with a flat-to-shrinking top line. Acima GMV fell 11% year over year in Q3 2026 and consolidated revenue fell 1.6% ($1.146B vs $1.165B). The $481M of trailing free cash flow is inflated by that shrinkage: the CFO said cash was strong 'partly due to some of the softness that we've seen on the top line and a reduction of overall working capital.' When volume returns, inventory reinvestment absorbs it. The FY2026 free-cash-flow guide is only about $250M, after 'substantial legal payments' to settle a multi-state attorney-general investigation whose size has not been disclosed. GAAP earnings are far below the non-GAAP figures: Q3 GAAP diluted EPS was $0.58 vs $1.01 non-GAAP, and TTM GAAP EPS is $1.90 vs a $4.00-4.35 non-GAAP guide. Return on invested capital is about 4.6%, below the cost of capital. Net debt is $1.51B including leases, against a $1.33B market cap, so the equity is a leveraged claim on a consumer cycle. The customer is squeezed by groceries, rent, utilities and gas (CEO, 2026-10-29), and the macro backdrop is reflation: CPI up 3.7% year over year with positive real rates. That is the environment in which subprime losses tend to rise and gas-price shocks hit discretionary durable purchases. Other overhangs: the 2026-10-01 data-breach claims investigation, a ~$13M fraud loss at Acima in Q2 2026, possible federal or state regulation of earned-wage access (Brigit's core product), and the long-term shift of retail toward buy-now-pay-later and e-commerce, which pressures the store-based Rent-A-Center. If charge-offs rise back above 10% while GMV is still shrinking, earnings power falls toward $2.50-3.00 per share, and the market will pay 5x for that.
picks.consensus_delta: Is the market pricing a terminal decline into a company with stable earnings power? Partly. At about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide and a 6.8% dividend yield, the price implies either a sharp credit downturn or a melting earnings base. The latest numbers show neither: charge-offs are at a 2021 low, three of three brands are growing EBITDA, and leverage is falling. Coverage is very thin, with one price target ($28 from Vincent Caintic, 2026-07-31) and none printed last quarter. That means the Q3 beat and the buyback have had little sell-side follow-through, which is typical of an orphaned small cap. Where the street is right to be wary: the revenue line is shrinking (Acima GMV down 11%), the free-cash-flow headline overstates the run-rate because of working-capital release, and non-GAAP earnings exclude real costs. Our disagreement with the market is modest. Earnings power is closer to $3.50 than the roughly $2-2.50 a sub-7x price implies, and that is worth about $28, not $22.84.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead), roughly November 2026 to May 2027. (1) The attorney-general settlement: the CFO flagged 'substantial legal payments' as the reason operating cash flow of $400M becomes free cash flow of $250M for FY2026. The headline amount, plus any conduct remedies on lease pricing or disclosures, could land as a negative surprise. (2) The holiday season: management is 'banking on a nice holiday season' with Q4 GMV guided flat. A weak holiday quarter with GMV still down would revive the shrinking-book worry when Q4 results print in late February 2027. (3) Consumer credit: the subprime customer faces sticky 3.7% CPI and elevated gas prices. If management loosens underwriting to chase volume just as the consumer weakens, losses could reverse up from 8.7%. (4) The data-breach litigation from 2026-10-01 is a cost and headline overhang. There is no near-term debt maturity wall in the materials, and leverage of 2.4x and falling is manageable. The near-term risk is to the valuation multiple, not a liquidity event.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is low. The holder base has a high-yield income bias (Upbound appears on high-yield small-cap dividend screens, Seeking Alpha 2026-10-31), and the dividend is covered by the ~$250M FY2026 free-cash-flow guide (about $91M a year in dividends on ~58M shares), so a dividend-cut liquidation is unlikely. Institutional additions are visible: Bank of America opened a 0.51% stake per a 2026-09-28 13F report, and Venture Visionary Partners raised its stake 72.8%. The stock is now up about 43% from the 2026-09-23 low of $15.99 and up 10.3% on 2026-11-02 alone, close to its 52-week high of $23.98. The near-term risk is profit-taking after a sharp short-term run, not forced selling. The ~$50M buyback in Q4 2026 is a modest steady buyer, about 2 days of average dollar volume per month.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds: the credit clean-up management promised a year ago has arrived. Lease charge-offs are at their lowest since 2021, Q3 2026 beat every guided range, leverage is down to 2.4x, and the company is buying back stock while paying a 6.8% dividend. At $22.84 the stock trades at about 5.4x guided non-GAAP earnings. Our more conservative earnings-power estimate of about $3.50 per share, at a through-cycle 8x, gives a fair value of about $28 over roughly 18 months. That is about 23% above today's price, just over the 20% margin of safety this book requires in the current reflationary backdrop. This is not a high-conviction call (conviction 3, value conviction 3), for four reasons. First, the margin of safety is thin after a 43% run off the September low, including 10% on the day of this review. Second, the lease book is shrinking (Acima volume down 11%), and part of the strong free cash flow comes from that shrinkage, not from durable earnings. Third, a multi-state attorney-general settlement of undisclosed size is coming, and non-GAAP earnings exclude real recurring costs. Fourth, the customer is a subprime consumer under real inflation pressure. The moat is narrow and stable: underwriting data and an embedded merchant network, earning a low but recovering return on capital. It is not a value trap. Sizing should be small, and the position should be revisited at Q4 2026 results (late February 2027), when the volume turn and the settlement size become visible. If charge-offs rise back above 10% while volume still falls, the thesis is in trouble.
picks.forcing_function: The re-rating has been under way since the 2026-10-29 Q3 beat. Three things keep it going. (1) The $50M open-market buyback in Q4 2026, the first meaningful repurchase since the Brigit acquisition. (2) Q4 2026 results in late February 2027, which show whether Acima GMV turned flat as guided and whether full-year non-GAAP EPS lands at the top of the $4.00-4.35 range. (3) Reaching the 2x leverage target, likely in 2027, which frees capital for larger buybacks or a dividend increase. A resolved attorney-general investigation would remove the main legal overhang. None of these has a contractual payout. The re-rate needs only continued delivery, not a single binary event.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Upbound Group (UPBD): a deep dive on management and the setup
*Five earnings calls, Q3 2025 (2025-10-30) to Q3 2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: $22.84 (NASDAQ, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

Upbound is the parent of Rent-A-Center (about 1,500+ corporate stores that rent furniture, appliances and electronics on a lease-to-own basis), Acima (the same lease-to-own product embedded at third-party retailers' checkouts and online) and Brigit (a subscription app that offers small cash advances, called earned-wage access, plus credit-building tools). The screener tags it as software. It is not software. It is a lender to subprime consumers, and its economics are driven by the losses it takes on leases. Read it that way.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

**The story shrank from growth to underwriting discipline, and that change worked.**

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-30):** management said Acima was "on track to deliver high single digits to low double-digit GMV growth" (GMV is gross merchandise volume, the dollar value of new leases written). The same call conceded that some 2025 lease cohorts were going bad. Lease charge-offs rose 50 basis points, the company tightened approvals "each month", and it warned that losses would peak in Q4 2025.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-19):** the framing became about getting back to normal. Management guided Acima losses to "that 9.5% range" for 2026 and said the most recent cohorts were "much more in line with historical years".
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-30):** charge-offs fell to about 8.8%, a 130 basis-point improvement from Q4. GMV came in "below our expectations", lower than a year earlier. Growth was now explicitly second to portfolio health.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-30):** management said it was "trading risk-adjusted margin for volume". The loss guide was cut to "around 9%, if not below 9%" and Acima's EBITDA margin passed 16%. The quarter also included a disclosed ~$13M fraud loss at Acima.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-29):** the story is now about profit and cash. Charge-offs were 8.7%, "the lowest level since stimulus in 2021". Acima GMV was down 11% year over year. Free cash flow was $121M in the quarter and net leverage was 2.4x. The company announced a $50M buyback "this quarter" and created a new chief operating officer role. It also guided Q4 GMV to "relatively flat", which would end three quarters of decline.

The growth drivers the company added along the way have held up: Brigit (paying users up 27% to 1.84M, revenue up 37%), an Experian distribution deal for Brigit, a Boost Mobile point-of-sale integration across about 5,000 stores, and an Amazon pickup partnership adding about 50 visits per store per week at Rent-A-Center. The Acima growth claim of 2025 was quietly dropped.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Losses would peak in Q4 2025 and normalize | Charge-offs went from ~10% (Q4 2025) to 8.8% (Q1), 8.8% (Q2) and 8.7% (Q3 2026) | Delivered |
| Q3 2026 beat guidance | Non-GAAP EPS $1.01 against a $0.85-0.95 guide; adjusted EBITDA $123M against $105-115M; revenue $1.15B at the top of the $1.05-1.15B range | Delivered (beat 7 of 7 quarters per the screener) |
| "Significant free cash flow" | TTM free cash flow $481M; Q3 FCF $121M, more than double the prior year | True, but flattered (see below) |
| Deleveraging toward the 2x target | Net leverage 2.4x; balance-sheet net debt $1.51B including leases, about $1.22B excluding leases | Delivered |
| Profit growth | GAAP diluted EPS: Q3 2026 $0.58 vs $0.22 a year earlier; TTM $1.90 vs FY2025 $1.25 | Real recovery from a weak base |
| Growth | Revenue down 1.6% y/y in Q3 ($1.146B vs $1.165B); Acima GMV down 11% | Revenue is flat to shrinking |

**Two forensic cautions.**
1. **Cash flow is flattered by shrinkage.** The CFO said cash flow was strong "partly due to some of the softness that we've seen on the top line and a reduction of overall working capital." A lease-to-own company buys inventory to lease out, so writing fewer leases releases cash. The $481M TTM free cash flow is not a run-rate. The FY2026 free-cash-flow guide is about $250M, after "substantial legal payments" tied to a multi-state attorney-general investigation. When GMV grows again, the company has to reinvest in inventory, and free cash flow will fall back toward its reported earnings.
2. **Non-GAAP and GAAP earnings are far apart.** Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $1.01 and GAAP was $0.58. The FY2026 non-GAAP guide is $4.00-4.35, while TTM GAAP EPS is $1.90. The gap is mostly amortization of intangibles from the Acima and Brigit acquisitions, which is a real non-cash charge to exclude. But it also removes stock compensation and recurring legal and regulatory charges, which are real costs in this industry. Our estimate of earnings power sits between the two: about $3.50 per share.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Rising, from defensive to confident.**
- Q3 2025: on the back foot, explaining bad cohorts ("softness in recent vintages").
- Q4 2025 and Q1 2026: steadier. "Validates the data-driven approach."
- Q2 2026: confident on credit and frank about volume ("trading risk-adjusted margin for volume").
- Q3 2026: offensive again. "Bullish on the holiday season", a buyback, new hires in leadership, and "flexibility to adjust that lever" (loosening underwriting). It is still careful about the consumer: "cautious around where the consumer is going to spend."

Guidance has become more specific over time, with quarterly ranges and named loss-rate targets. That is a good sign.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The loss-rate path was called correctly three quarters ahead. Q3 2026 beat the top of every range. Full-year non-GAAP EPS of $4.00-4.35 was reaffirmed on 2026-07-30, and the free-cash-flow guide was raised to about $250M. The one large miss was the Acima volume promise from 2025 (high single to low double-digit growth), which turned into an 11% decline. That miss was a choice made for credit reasons, not a forecasting failure. The guidance ranges have been wide enough to beat, which looks like mild sandbagging (setting targets low enough to clear). **Reliability: High on profit and credit, Medium on volume.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Volume:** analysts keep asking when GMV turns. The answer has moved from "growth" (2025) to "flat in Q4" (2026-10-29). This is the open question.
- **Cash conversion:** Bank of America asked on 2026-10-29 about the gap between $400M of operating cash flow and $250M of free cash flow. The answer was the attorney-general legal payments, and no amount was given. The size of that settlement is a real, unquantified liability.
- **Capital allocation after Brigit:** management said it is "not being proactive at this point around M&A", which is reassuring.
- **What analysts are not pushing on:** regulation of earned-wage access at Brigit, and the 2026-10-01 data-breach class-action investigation (Ademi LLP). Neither came up on the call.
- **Coverage is thin:** one price target in the last year ($28, 2026-07-31).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Green: lease charge-offs at 8.7% in Q3 2026, the best since 2021, after a correctly forecast peak in Q4 2025.
- Green: Acima adjusted EBITDA up 15% in Q3 2026 with margin up ~270 basis points to 14.7%.
- Green: Brigit revenue up 37% and EBITDA up 59% in Q3 2026. This is the growth asset.
- Green: net leverage 2.4x heading to 2x. A $50M buyback (about 4% of market cap) was announced 2026-10-29. The $0.39 quarterly dividend was maintained (declared 2026-09-24). Insiders made 8 open-market buys against 1 sale.
- Red: Acima GMV down 11% (Q3 2026), and consolidated revenue is down year over year. The lease book is shrinking.
- Red: an attorney-general investigation with "substantial" payments of undisclosed size (2026-10-29), plus a data-breach claims investigation (2026-10-01).
- Red: a ~$13M fraud loss at Acima in Q2 2026.
- Red: the core customer is squeezed by groceries, rent, utilities and gas (CEO, 2026-10-29). Gross margin has fallen from 61.6% (2019) to about 48-51% today, partly because Acima's business mix carries lower margins.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Underwriting capabilities are our core strength" (Q3 2026) shows the company now presents itself as a credit-risk manager rather than a retailer, which fits the peer set.
- A newly created chief operating officer role "unify[ing] business segments under a single leader" (2026-09-22) points to cost and integration work across the three brands. Overlap between the brands is only 10-15% today.
- AI comes up more often (about half of code changes "involve AI assistance"). This is efficiency talk, not a revenue claim.
- The buyback "coming out of blackout" signals that management thinks the stock is cheap at around $20.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Credit, margins, leverage and cash returns have all improved for three straight quarters, and management has delivered on its guidance.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing:** the stock is cheap on earnings (about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint, a 6.8% dividend yield) and expensive on growth (the lease book is shrinking). Today's free cash flow partly comes from that shrinkage, and it is reduced by an unquantified attorney-general settlement. Underwrite earnings power of about $3.50 per share, not the $481M TTM free cash flow.

**Moat:** narrow. It rests on scale and cost, plus underwriting data built from decades of subprime lease outcomes and an embedded merchant network (Acima at checkout, Boost Mobile, Amazon pickup). Returns are low (ROIC about 4.6%, ROE about 11.6%) but recovering, not falling, so the moat is stable rather than eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Buy-now-pay-later lenders and the shift of retail to e-commerce pressure the store-based Rent-A-Center, but Acima already sits on the e-commerce and virtual channel and Rent-A-Center same-store sales have grown for four quarters. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear of subprime credit plus a regulatory overhang, not a structurally shrinking base. The risk is consumer-cycle risk, not terminal risk.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# CECONOMY AG (CEC.DE, Xetra, EUR) - forensic dossier, 2026-11-09

Price used: EUR 4.53 on Xetra (FMP live quote, 9 November 2026; 52-week range EUR 3.51-4.59; market value about EUR 2.20 billion on about 485 million shares). Latest call transcript: second fiscal quarter, 13 May 2026.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
CECONOMY runs MediaMarkt and Saturn, Europe's largest consumer-electronics chain (about 1,000 stores, 11 countries, roughly EUR 24 billion of sales). The story management tells has moved from "turnaround retailer" to "platform": retail media (selling advertising to suppliers against store and app traffic), services, a third-party marketplace and rented floor space, now about 40% of gross profit. Since late 2025 the story has been overtaken by ownership: JD.com's 2025 tender at EUR 4.60 left JD.com and partner Convergenta with 85.2% on completion. The European Commission conditionally approved the purchase under the foreign-subsidies rules on 3 November 2026, and closing is expected by 12 November 2026, inside the 10 November-area long-stop the chief financial officer flagged on 13 May 2026.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Claim: twelve-plus straight quarters of adjusted operating profit growth. Preliminary fiscal 2025/26 figures reported in October 2026 put adjusted operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and tax) at about EUR 515 million versus a EUR 500 million target and EUR 406 million restated a year earlier; sales about EUR 23.9 billion, up about 5%. Final figures are due 14 December 2026. Corroborated, though from trade press, not the company release.
- Reported profit does not match adjusted profit: net income was negative in fiscal 2023 (EUR -39 million) and 2025 (EUR -35 million); trailing earnings per share EUR -0.03 at 30 June 2026. The gap of roughly EUR 300 million a year between adjusted and reported profit recurs with a differently named one-off each year.
- The screen's 3.2 times price to free cash flow counts trailing free cash flow of EUR 731 million before about EUR 524 million a year of store rent, which lease accounting books in financing. After rent, owner free cash flow is about EUR 200 million, in line with management's own guide: about 11 times at today's price.
- Return on invested capital 1.8%; gross margin 15.1% and contracting. Net debt EUR 1.51 billion at 30 June 2026 (borrowings EUR 2.60 billion less cash EUR 1.09 billion), a seasonal high; near nil at the December peak.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Confident on operations, deliberately vague on the minority. On 13 May 2026 the finance chief confirmed closing "in the second half of the calendar year" before the November long-stop and declined to give a precise delisting date. Tone on Germany and Austria, the core markets, was guarded across both reported 2026 quarters.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Good on the adjusted line: the EUR 500 million target was met and beaten (about EUR 515 million, preliminary, October 2026). Weaker on reported profit, where guidance is not given and one-offs recur. Credibility on deal timing was adequate: the timetable slipped from first half to second half of calendar 2026, but the regulatory path closed before the long-stop.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Analysts pressed on deal timing and delisting mechanics (13 May 2026), not on the adjusted-versus-reported gap or rent-adjusted cash flow. No current analyst price targets could be found with a dated source; the stock is effectively a controlled company with thin coverage.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: recurring one-offs; 1.8% return on capital; contracting gross margin; JD.com committed in its 2025 offer to no domination or profit-transfer agreement (a contract that would force an appraised cash exit) for at least three years; a German delisting offer must only meet the six-month average price (about EUR 4.15-4.30 on the 200- and 50-day averages) and the bidder's qualifying pre-acquisitions; free float about 14.8% and thin.
Green: adjusted profit beat (October 2026); mix shift to higher-margin income; supplier-funded working capital; no refinancing pressure; EU approval obtained 3 November 2026.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The share price (EUR 4.53, 94% up its range) has converged to within 1.5% of JD.com's EUR 4.60 tender price, above the statutory six-month-average floor. The market is pricing a delisting offer struck at or near EUR 4.60, not the business. Volume is low (about 5,000 shares on the quote day), so the marginal buyer is an event trader.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A better business than its reputation, held inside a security whose payout is set by the controlling shareholder's delisting decision. Today's price already discounts the most likely minority exit; the upside case (an appraised exit under a domination agreement) is contractually ruled out for about three years. Nothing here for a value book.

picks.bull_thesis: The bull case is that Jungheinrich, the number-two European maker of forklifts and warehouse equipment, is being priced as if a cyclical trough were permanent. The nine-month statement of 10 November 2026 shows the bottom forming rather than deepening: orders rose 6.0% to 4,323 million euros, the reported operating margin recovered to 5.9% from 4.0% a year earlier as one-off costs fell from 162.9 million to 36.5 million, and management confirmed its 2026 forecast of 340-400 million euros of operating profit for the second time instead of cutting again. Gross margin has held near 32% for years and rose through the 2021-22 inflation (29.1% to 30.9%), which says the product still carries pricing power. The balance sheet is roughly neutral (cash of 723 million against debt of 701 million at 30 June 2026), so there is no financing threat. The new 2030 target of an 8-9% margin, though lower than before, is what a recovery from today's 6-7% looks like, and Bernstein's Philippe Lorrain called the reset a de-risking step that could bring in long-term holders (10 November 2026). At 23.24 euros the shares trade near book value and at roughly 9-10 times a normalised 2.40-2.60 euros of earnings; if the margin returns to around 8% on about 5.9 billion euros of revenue, sum-of-the-parts value is near 35 euros. picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the screen is cheap for reasons that do not survive inspection, and that 10 November 2026 made two of them worse. First, cash: nine-month free cash flow was minus 106 million euros against plus 151 million a year earlier, so the 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow multiple rests on 2025 cash the business is not repeating; the full-year guide of above 50 million now needs roughly 156 million or more in the fourth quarter alone. Second, ambition: management cut its 2030 margin target to 8-9% from about 10%, which confirms the margin erosion visible in the numbers (adjusted 6.8% for nine months against 8.1% a year earlier; the third quarter on reported figures derives to about 5.4%, about 76 million on about 1.40 billion, using FMP's half-year operating profit of 165.8 million; one press report gives about 97 million for the quarter, which we cannot reconcile and may be adjusted). Third-quarter orders grew only 2.6%, slightly below expectations, and growth is concentrated in the smaller, lumpier automation business while the core truck business saw revenue fall 1.8% under Chinese price competition and high rates. Return on invested capital of about 5.8% is below the cost of capital. The effective tax rate was about 45% in the first half (59.0 million on 132.2 million of pre-tax profit). The German financial regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts, opened 21 July 2026 and tied to the Russia disposal, is still open with no timetable; a finding would undercut the argument that recent charges were one-off. The March 2026 forecast lasted four months, and only two of the last five quarters beat. The listed preference shares carry no vote, so no activist or bid can force value out. What would confirm it: a fourth quarter that misses the forecast or the cash guide (full-year results, late March 2027), a regulator finding, or a dividend cut that pushes income holders out.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrow. The street is pricing a long trough in European forklifts (Bank of America's 8 October 2026 underperform call, target 21 euros) and the shares sit about a third below where they started 2026. We think the market is roughly right on timing but slightly too pessimistic on the mid-cycle margin: the confirmed 2026 forecast, the 6.8% adjusted nine-month margin and management's own 8-9% 2030 target all point to a mid-cycle near or above 7%, which supports about 26 euros of value. But the gap is not large at 23.24 euros, and the market has a point on cash: a 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow screen is built on 2025, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow is minus 106 million euros. Nothing here is a terminal-decline pricing error large enough to buy today.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) runs to the full-year results in late March 2027. Three things can hurt before value converges: (1) the fourth quarter must deliver roughly 98-158 million euros of operating profit and about 156 million or more of free cash flow to meet the guide - a miss on cash would expose the low price-to-cash-flow screen as an artifact; (2) the regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts can publish a finding at any time with no notice; (3) European capital-spending demand under positive real rates and Chinese price competition in standard trucks can keep the core truck business shrinking (nine-month revenue there down 1.8%). There is no debt wall: cash of 723 million roughly matches debt of 701 million at 30 June 2026.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is modest. The preference shares carry no vote, so the holder base is income and value funds plus index holders (the shares are in the SDAX). A dividend cut in spring 2027 after a year of reported earnings well below 2024 could push income holders out, and the sector-wide selling seen in October 2026 (Bank of America's call covering KION too) is the most likely route to our 19.00 euro level. We see no index deletion, lock-up or spin-off dumping in prospect.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 19.00 euros, which a renewed sector-wide sell-off in European forklift makers could deliver.

The thesis holds. Today's nine-month statement (10 November 2026) confirmed the 2026 forecast instead of cutting it again, orders are up 6% and one-off costs have fallen sharply, so this still looks like a decent business in a cyclical trough rather than a broken one. But the statement did not deliver what we said would make us buy earlier: the adjusted margin was 6.8%, not above 7%, free cash flow was minus 106 million euros for nine months against plus 151 million a year earlier, and management lowered its 2030 margin goal to 8-9% from about 10%.

We trim fair value to 26.08 euros from 26.57: the core business at a mid-cycle 7.25% margin and eight times operating profit, the leasing arm near its estimated equity, less about 270 million euros of net debt once this year's cash outflow is counted. At 23.24 euros (Xetra, 10 November 2026) the discount is only about a tenth, short of the one-fifth this book requires, and the downside to our 16.53 euro adverse case is larger than the upside. At 19.00 euros the discount to fair value is well over a third and the remaining downside small, which is the asymmetry we want.

Conviction stays at a moderate 3, inherited from our last answer because no dated fact cleared an upgrade or broke the thesis: a narrow-moat number-two franchise whose margins and returns are eroding, with an open regulator review, a 45% tax rate and a guidance record that needed a cut in July. The value case alone also rates 3, capped by the eroding moat. We would move before 19.00 euros only on a dated fact: a fourth quarter that meets the forecast and the cash guide (late March 2027), or a clean close of the regulator's review.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard dated event that forces a re-rating. The candidates are routine: full-year 2026 results in late March 2027 (proof of fourth-quarter cash and the 2026 forecast met), and the close of the regulator's review (no date). The founding families control the vote, so no activist, tender or buyback campaign can be forced. The re-rating, if it comes, is a slow margin and cash recovery.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Jungheinrich AG (preference shares, Xetra JUN3.DE) - deep dive on management and the setup

As of 10 November 2026. No earnings-call transcript was available from FMP for this listing, and none could be found on the web for the nine-month statement published today. This dossier therefore reasons from the company's dated releases (first quarter, 23 July 2026 forecast cut, half-year report of 11 August 2026, nine-month statement of 10 November 2026, as reported in the press), the FMP quarterly statements and our screener figures. No management quotes are given because none could be sourced; where we derive a figure, we say so.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from growth ambition to damage control and back to a cautious "trough, then recovery" message.

- Early 2026: the company opened the year with a forecast it had to cut four months later. The first quarter was weak: operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and taxes) fell to 56.5 million euros from 104.5 million a year earlier, hit by a strike at the Lueneburg plant and price competition.
- 23 July 2026: an ad-hoc notice (a mandatory market announcement) revised the full-year forecast for the Industrial Trucks and Services segment and the group to EBIT of 340 to 400 million euros (a 6.2% to 7.0% margin, including about 40 million euros of one-off costs).
- 11 August 2026: the half-year report showed orders up about 8%, revenue flat at 2,669 million euros, and a group margin near 6.2%.
- 10 November 2026: the nine-month statement held the 2026 forecast, showed orders up 6.0% to 4,323 million euros, revenue up 1.5% to 4,068 million euros, and reported EBIT of 241.8 million euros (5.9% margin, against 4.0% a year earlier when one-offs were far larger). Adjusted for 36.5 million euros of one-offs, EBIT was 278.3 million euros, a 6.8% margin, down from 8.1% a year earlier. At the same time the company reset its long-term plan: the 2030 targets are now 7 to 8 billion euros of revenue and an 8% to 9% EBIT margin, down from roughly 10 billion euros and about 10% per a German trade report.

The quiet change is the long-term ambition. A 10% margin business has become an 8-9% margin business by the end of the decade, which matters more for the upside than for the downside.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / implied claim | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 forecast (EBIT 340-400m) is achievable | Nine-month reported EBIT 241.8m; Q4 must deliver about 98-158m. Q4 2025 delivered 131.6m reported (FMP). | Plausible at the low-to-mid end. |
| Margins recover from the trough | Adjusted nine-month margin 6.8% vs 8.1% a year earlier. Reported third quarter derived at about 76m on about 1.40bn (about 5.4%), using FMP's 165.8m half-year EBIT; one press report gives about 97m for the quarter, which may be an adjusted figure - we could not reconcile the two. | No clear recovery yet; flat at best. |
| Orders signal demand turning | Orders +6.0% for nine months, but the third quarter alone only +2.6% to just under 1.4bn, slightly below expectations. Automation orders +19.9% to 878m; core trucks +3.5%. | Real but slowing; growth comes from the smaller automation arm. |
| Cash generation (free cash flow above 50m for the year) | Nine-month free cash flow minus 106m euros vs plus 151m a year earlier. Q4 must produce roughly 156m+ to hit the guide. | The weakest link. The screener's 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow rests on 2025 cash that 2026 is not repeating. |
| Gross margin stability | Gross margin about 32.6% in the first half (870m on 2,669m); screen shows 32.2% stable; held through the 2021-22 inflation (29.1% to 30.9%). | Corroborated - pricing power on the product is intact. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining through July, stabilising since. The 23 July cut was defensive; the November release is cautious-steady (forecast held, long-term targets lowered to something believable). Bernstein's Philippe Lorrain called the lower targets a risk-reduction step that could attract long-term investors (as reported 10 November 2026). We rate the trajectory as still deteriorating on substance (lower long-term margins, negative cash flow) even as the tone has steadied.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-low. The March 2026 forecast lasted four months. The screener shows beats in only 2 of the last 5 quarters and earnings per share down 64% in 2025. The revised July forecast has now been confirmed once (10 November). The 2030 reset is a second admission that earlier ambition was too high. Reliability: Low-to-Medium, improving only if Q4 lands inside the range and cash turns positive.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without a transcript we can only infer the questions: (a) why free cash flow swung to minus 106m and whether the full-year cash guide is still realistic; (b) how much of the margin gap is Chinese price competition (structural) versus volume (cyclical); (c) the German financial regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts tied to the Russia disposal, opened 21 July 2026, for which we found no update; (d) the 45%-plus effective tax rate in the first half (59.0m of tax on 132.2m of pre-tax profit, FMP).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: nine-month free cash flow minus 106m (10 Nov 2026) against a full-year guide above 50m.
- Red: 2030 margin target cut to 8-9% from about 10% (10 Nov 2026).
- Red: adjusted margin 6.8% vs 8.1% a year earlier; third-quarter orders slightly below expectations.
- Red: regulator review of the June 2025 accounts still open (since 21 July 2026, no result found).
- Red: effective tax rate near 45% in the first half of 2026.
- Green: 2026 forecast confirmed on 10 November 2026, no second cut.
- Green: orders up 6% for nine months; automation orders up about 20%.
- Green: one-off costs fell to 36.5m from 162.9m a year earlier; reported margin up to 5.9% from 4.0%.
- Green: gross margin steady near 32%; balance sheet roughly neutral (cash 723m vs debt 701m at 30 June 2026 per FMP).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The target reset is the main signal: management is now anchoring the market to a lower, more achievable margin path, which removes a source of future disappointment but also caps the long-term upside the bull case used to lean on. Growth is migrating to automation, a more competitive and project-lumpy business. The listed preference shares carry no vote; control sits with the founding families, so no activist or bid can force value out.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT

Trajectory: DETERIORATING on substance (lower long-term margins, cash outflow this year), with a stabilising tone. The single most important thing for the director: whether the fourth quarter turns cash positive enough to meet the above-50m free-cash-flow guide - that decides whether the low price-to-cash-flow screen is real or a 2025 artifact.

Moat: a narrow but real moat from scale, a dense direct sales-and-service network and a large leasing and rental fleet that ties customers in (switching costs on service). Width is narrowing: return on invested capital about 5.8% is below the cost of capital, the margin has slid from about 8% to 6-7%, and management has cut its own end-of-decade margin target. That is an eroding moat trend, though from a cyclical trough rather than a collapse. Secular threat: Chinese low-price competition in standard trucks is a material but manageable pressure, not a terminal one - warehouse automation is a growth adjacency the company is winning in. The cheapness is mostly a cyclical fear print, with a real structural element on margins.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

The 7.25% sits above the 6.8% adjusted nine-month margin and below the 8-9% management now targets for 2030, so it is a mid-cycle figure, not a recovery bet. 2) Leasing arm: about 240 million of estimated equity at 1.2 times, about 290 million (about 2.84 a share). 3) Balance-sheet overlay: about minus 270 million (about minus 2.65 a share): the company's net-debt line of about 220 million at 30 June 2026 plus about 50 million for the nine-month free-cash-flow outflow of 106 million; we do not count the 241 million of short-term investments as free cash because the leasing arm's funding sits inside the group. picks.bull_thesis: Solvay sells essential chemistry - soda ash and bicarbonate for glass, food, feed and flue-gas cleaning, hydrogen peroxide including electronic grade for chips, highly dispersible silica for fuel-efficient tyres, rare earths and fluorine specialties, plus Coatis in Brazil - mostly local-for-local (over 80% of sales), with a low-cost US natural soda ash base at Green River. The 2026 earnings are depressed by identifiable, partly temporary hits: the Middle East conflict cost about EUR 20 million of EBITDA in Q2 and about EUR 25 million in Q3 2026 (mostly the Jubail peroxide shutdown, whose joint-venture contract has mechanisms to recover lost profitability, not included in guidance), on top of a seaborne soda-ash price trough driven by Chinese overcapacity that management says has many players 'selling below their cash costs' (Nov 2025 call). Under the trough, the rest of the portfolio is doing well: bicarbonate and electronic-grade peroxide at record sales (Jul 2026 call), silica sales +9.2% and Coatis +19.1% in Q3 2026, and EUR 283 million of structural cost savings banked by Q3 2026 against a EUR 300 million end-2026 target. Transformation cash costs fall from about EUR 90 million in 2026 to about EUR 50 million in 2027 (CFO, Jul 2026), which lifts free cash flow by about EUR 40 million almost mechanically. At EUR 24.40 the stock trades at roughly 6.4x price to free cash flow on the trailing EUR 316 million (through 2026-09-30). The upside path: Jubail restarts (or Sadara compensates), China's anti-involution policy finally closes old synthetic soda-ash capacity, the rare-earths joint venture crystallises a strategic value for a unit that is the only non-Chinese separator of all 17 elements, and the EU emissions-trading reform (draft July 2026) keeps free allowances. On normalised EBITDA of about EUR 900 million or more, at a European-chemicals multiple, the equity is worth well above today's price. Conditions: Jubail back or compensated within 2027, leverage held around investment grade, and no further leg down in domestic soda-ash pricing.
picks.bear_thesis: Earnings have fallen every year since the 2023 spin-off - underlying EBITDA from about EUR 1.0 billion (2024) to EUR 881 million (2025) to EUR 720-740 million guided for 2026 - and management has cut mid-year guidance two years running (July 2025, October 2026). Free cash flow, which funded the roughly EUR 257 million dividend in 2024 and 2025, is guided at only EUR 120-150 million for 2026, and only EUR 70 million had come in after nine months; the CFO's March 2025 assurance that the dividend would 'always' be covered by cash has failed. Leverage rose to 2.4x at September 2026 against a BBB- rating (one notch above junk) confirmed by S&P in June, so paying the full dividend from debt is not sustainable; a Belgian investor-test publication (2026-10-21) put a sustainable payout at about EUR 1.28 and rated the stock a sell. Seaborne soda-ash prices were still falling in Q3 2026, China has shown no capacity closures ('not yet', Feb 2026), the Torrelavega cut shows European synthetic soda ash is losing competitiveness under energy and carbon costs, and with Brent above USD 110 in late October 2026 European energy costs are a fresh headwind. Return on invested capital is 6.9% and Altman-Z (a solvency score) is 1.3, in the distress zone. Reported EPS is near zero (EUR 0.28 for 2025, EUR 0.32 trailing). If Jubail stays shut, soda ash stays weak and the multiple compresses to a stressed level, the equity, which is a thin slice above EUR 1.84 billion of net debt, falls sharply. What would confirm it: FY2026 free cash flow below EUR 120 million, leverage above 2.5x at year-end, or a rating downgrade to junk.
picks.consensus_delta: The market prices Solvay as a leveraged, structurally challenged European commodity-chemicals stock whose dividend is about to be cut - and on the dividend the market is probably right: 2026 free cash flow of EUR 120-150 million cannot fund a roughly EUR 257 million payout at 2.4x leverage. Where we disagree is on terminal decline: the end markets (glass, food, feed, chips, tyres, magnets) are not shrinking, Green River is a low-cost soda-ash source, and about EUR 45 million of the 2026 EBITDA loss so far is a plant shutdown with a contractual recovery mechanism. We do not think the street is badly wrong at EUR 24.40, which sits close to our EUR 26.0 base value; the disagreement only pays if a dividend cut forces yield holders out at a materially lower price.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): Q4 2026 cash must be back-ended to hit even the reduced EUR 120-150 million free-cash-flow guide (only EUR 70 million after nine months); year-end leverage around 2.4-2.5x tests the BBB- rating; Jubail has no restart date while the Middle East conflict and Brent above USD 100 persist; and the FY2026 results in late February 2027 will set the final dividend. A dividend cut and any rating-outlook change would likely cluster in that window. Soda-ash seaborne pricing gives no sign of turning before China closes capacity.
picks.positioning_washout: Solvay's shareholder base has historically been income-oriented (a long Belgian dividend record, the Solvac family holding company as anchor shareholder), and the EUR 2.43 dividend is about a 10% yield at EUR 24.40. A cut at the February 2027 results is the obvious trigger for forced selling by holders who own it for the yield and must sell regardless of value - income funds and dividend screens. That forced-selling pressure is the seller we name for our EUR 21.5 level; the 52-week low of EUR 22.58 shows the stock has already traded close to it without a cut.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near EUR 21.5, which forced selling by yield-focused holders after a dividend cut could deliver. The thesis holds - Solvay remains an essential, mostly local-for-local chemicals business whose 2026 profit fall is explained by a seaborne soda-ash trough and a temporary shutdown of its Saudi peroxide plant, while silica, Coatis, bicarbonate and electronic-grade peroxide are doing well and cost savings are on plan. But the 2026-10-19 guidance cut (EBITDA EUR 720-740 million, free cash flow EUR 120-150 million) leaves the roughly EUR 257 million dividend uncovered at 2.4x leverage, and the November 4 results did nothing to change that. At EUR 24.40 the stock sits only about 7% below our EUR 26.0 base-case fair value (normalised EBITDA about EUR 800 million at 6x, less EUR 1.84 billion of net debt), well short of the 20% discount we require in today's reflation backdrop, while the adverse case of about EUR 15 shows how thin the equity slice is above the debt. We keep the committee's answer from 2026-10-12 - wait for a better price, conviction 3 - and lower the entry level slightly from EUR 22.0 to EUR 21.5 to match the trimmed fair value. The firmly dated decision point is the final dividend at the FY2026 results in late February 2027; a cut there is the most likely route to our price. We would revisit the thesis itself if the rating fell to junk or FY2026 free cash flow missed the reduced guide.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating - is a combination with no fixed date: Jubail restart or contractual compensation from Sadara; signature of the rare-earths joint venture with OneIM (talks ongoing at 2026-11-04); Chinese closure of old synthetic soda-ash plants; and, mechanically, the drop in transformation cash costs from about EUR 90 million (2026) to about EUR 50 million (2027). The nearest firmly dated event is the FY2026 results and dividend decision in late February 2027, which is more likely to produce the entry price than the re-rating.

# Solvay (SOLB.BR) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-10. Live price EUR 24.40 (Euronext Brussels, FMP quote). Sources: five earnings calls (2025-03-06, 2025-07-30, 2025-11-06, 2026-02-24, 2026-07-29), the screener's financial block, Solvay's preliminary Q3 release and guidance update of 2026-10-19 and its full Q3 release of 2026-11-04.*

**Bottom line:** Solvay is a real, essential-chemicals business (soda ash and bicarbonate, hydrogen peroxide, tyre silica, rare earths and fluorine specialties, and the Brazilian phenol/solvents unit Coatis) being run with genuine cost discipline, but its earnings have fallen every year since the 2023 Syensqo spin-off and management's cash promises have now slipped. The 2026-10-19 guidance cut took full-year underlying EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) to EUR 720-740 million (from a range implying roughly EUR 765-845 million) and free cash flow to EUR 120-150 million (from "at least EUR 200 million"), against a dividend that costs about EUR 257 million a year. The single most important fact for sizing: the dividend is no longer covered by cash, and the next scheduled decision on it is the full-year results in late February 2027.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **March 2025 (FY2024 call): "resilience" and the post-split story.** Philippe Kehren framed 2024 as "a pivotal chapter" in which "the spinoff has unlocked significant value", raised the cost-savings target from EUR 300 million to EUR 350 million by 2028, and positioned Solvay's products as "not commodities, but they are not specialties neither". Soda ash was described as at "the low end of the cycle".
- **July 2025 (H1 2025): first guidance cut, Coatis and seaborne soda ash.** The tone shifted to tariffs, a "progressive reduction of demand" and Chinese competition. Coatis was hit by Asian imports redirected to Brazil; seaborne soda ash prices fell. Rare earths entered the story as a strategic option (La Rochelle, permanent magnets) but explicitly conditioned on customer or state price floors.
- **November 2025 (Q3 2025): self-help and asset monetisation.** A EUR 40 million EBITDA gain from selling CO2 emission rights was presented as "definitely not a one-off" but "a business decision"; the Chief Operations Officer was put on the call to evidence the savings programme; Torrelavega (Spain) soda-ash capacity was cut by a third. China's "anti-involution" policy was introduced as the hoped-for fix for soda ash ("if and when").
- **February 2026 (FY2025): "we deliver" plus defend the footprint.** EBITDA EUR 881 million (-13%), free cash flow EUR 350 million. The narrative widened to European climate policy (emissions-trading reform, free allowances) and a promise of "a stable growing dividend and an investment-grade rating".
- **July 2026 (H1 2026): exogenous shock.** The Middle East conflict shut the Jubail (Saudi Arabia) peroxide plant; EBITDA fell 20% in Q2. Bicarbonate and electronic-grade peroxide were at "record sales levels"; restart was guided to "the second part of Q3". An analyst stated plainly that "the dividend won't be covered in '26".
- **After the last call (dated facts):** Jubail did not restart; on 2026-10-19 guidance was cut; on 2026-11-04 Q3 EBITDA printed EUR 173 million (-26.6% organically, 16.8% margin), leverage reached 2.4x, the interim dividend was held at EUR 0.97, and talks continued to contribute the rare-earths business (about EUR 80 million of EBITDA) to a joint venture with OneIM in which Solvay keeps a significant minority.

The arc runs from "we are resilient and the cycle is at the bottom" to "we are controlling what we can while the cycle and geopolitics keep moving against us".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Soda ash is at "the low end of the cycle" (Mar 2025) | Seaborne prices fell further in every subsequent quarter through Q3 2026; Soda Ash & Derivatives sales -6.8% in Q3 2026 | Wrong on timing; the trough kept deepening |
| "We are cash flow covering the dividend... Yes, always" (CFO, Mar 2025) | FCF EUR 361m (2024), EUR 350m (2025) covered the ~EUR 257m dividend; 2026 guide EUR 120-150m does not | Held for two years, broken for 2026 |
| Cost savings EUR 350m by 2028, EUR 300m by end-2026 | EUR 283m delivered by Q3 2026 | Delivered — the most credible claim on record |
| Healthy ~21% EBITDA margin through the trough | ~21% in 2025; 18.1% Q2 2026; 16.8% Q3 2026 | Eroding, partly temporary (Jubail, ~EUR 45m in Q2+Q3) |
| Balance sheet "healthy", leverage back to ~2x by year-end (Jul 2026) | Underlying net debt EUR 1.79bn, leverage 2.4x at Sept 2026; S&P BBB- (one notch above junk) | Missed so far; year-end test pending |
| Group EPS trajectory | EPS 19.85 (2023, spin-distorted) -> 2.10 (2024) -> 0.28 (2025); TTM 0.32 | Reported earnings near zero; cash flow is the better gauge |

Revenue: EUR 4.75bn (2025) per the screener; underlying EUR 4.3bn, -6% organically. The 3-year revenue decline (-33%) is mostly the Syensqo spin restatement, not organic collapse. Free cash flow: TTM EUR 316m (screener, through 2026-09-30), but 9M-2026 FCF to shareholders was only EUR 70m, so the trailing figure overstates the run-rate.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** March 2025 was offensive ("our ambition is clear... be the best"). July 2025 turned defensive ("clearly, this is not what we expected"). November 2025 leaned on self-help and one-time levers (CO2 sales, footprint cuts). February 2026 added a policy-lobbying layer ("we need the support of the authorities"). July 2026 was frank about unpredictability ("volatility is the name of the game") and declined to discuss 2027 ("very early to say anything about '27"). Guidance specificity has stayed decent, but the confidence behind it has fallen each year.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- 2025 EBITDA guidance: cut in July 2025, then delivered inside the revised range (EUR 881m).
- 2025 FCF: delivered (EUR 350m, above the ~EUR 300m guide).
- 2026 EBITDA: given in February 2026 as a 4-13% decline, confirmed on 2026-07-29 (with Jubail restart assumed in late Q3), cut on 2026-10-19 to EUR 720-740m (-16% to -18%).
- 2026 FCF: "at least EUR 200m" -> EUR 120-150m.

Two consecutive years of mid-year guidance cuts; cost targets met; cash conversion good until 2026. The earnings-beat rate of 4 of 7 quarters (57%) matches a management that is honest about what it controls but has repeatedly underestimated the external hits. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Dividend cover** (Barclays, Mar 2025; Berenberg, Jul 2026): answered with confidence in 2025, sidestepped in 2026 ("an important piece of the equation"). This is the question that turned into bad news.
- **Why invest so little if returns are high / why not monetise non-core units** (Barclays Mar 2025; JPMorgan Nov 2025 on fluorine at 12x EBITDA): "nothing is excluded" — and the rare-earths JV talks with OneIM (disclosed by 2026-11-04) suggest portfolio action is now real.
- **China soda-ash rationalisation**: asked every call; the answer since February 2026 has been "not yet".
- **2027 earnings path**: not answered.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: dividend uncovered in 2026 (FCF guide EUR 120-150m vs ~EUR 257m) after the "yes, always" promise of March 2025.
- Red: leverage 2.4x at Sept 2026 with a BBB- rating — little headroom to keep paying the dividend from debt.
- Red: two mid-year EBITDA guidance cuts in two years (Jul 2025, Oct 2026).
- Red: seaborne soda ash still falling (Q3 2026) with no Chinese capacity closures yet.
- Red: Jubail restart missed its "second part of Q3" guide; no new date.
- Green: EUR 283m of structural savings delivered (Q3 2026), ahead of plan.
- Green: bicarbonate and electronic-grade peroxide at record sales (Q2 2026); silica +9.2% and Coatis +19.1% sales in Q3 2026.
- Green: Jubail joint-venture contract has mechanisms to recover lost profitability (2026-10-19 release) — not in guidance.
- Green: rare-earths JV with OneIM would crystallise value for a ~EUR 80m-EBITDA unit while keeping exposure.
- Green: EU emissions-trading draft reform (Jul 2026) keeps free allowances — reduces the long-run carbon-cost threat to European plants.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The language moved from "resilience" (2025) to "transformation expenses" and "what we control" (2026) — a defensive register.
- One-time cash levers (CO2-rights sales, working-capital squeezes to "best-in-class" ~10% of sales) have been carrying free cash flow; they are finite.
- Portfolio language softened from "we will concentrate on" to "nothing is excluded", and now a partial disposal (rare earths) is in negotiation — a sign the board is willing to sell assets to protect the balance sheet and possibly the dividend.
- Holding the interim dividend at EUR 0.97 on 2026-11-04 while guiding FCF far below the payout signals the board wants to defer any cut to the February 2027 final-dividend decision.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: DETERIORATING.** The operational discipline is real, but the cash base no longer funds the dividend and leverage is rising toward the edge of investment grade. The single most important thing to weigh: the February 2027 final-dividend decision. A cut is the likeliest route for forced selling by yield-focused holders — which is also the most likely route to a genuinely cheap entry price.

**Moat:** a narrow, scale-and-cost moat — Green River (US) natural trona soda ash is among the world's lowest-cost sources, the hydrogen-peroxide "mega plant" technology is licensable, and ~80% of sales are local-for-local, which protects against freight and tariffs. But returns are falling (ROIC 6.9% today versus "almost 18%" cited by an analyst in March 2025) and margins have slid from ~21% to 16.8%, partly cyclical (Chinese overcapacity, Jubail) and partly structural (European synthetic soda ash under energy and carbon-cost pressure, hence the Torrelavega cut). The moat is real but eroding at the European edge.

**Secular threat:** manageable. The end markets (glass, food and feed, semiconductors, tyres, magnets) are not shrinking; the structural risk is European energy and carbon costs on the older synthetic soda-ash plants (an energy-transition cost burden), which management is addressing by shrinking and converting capacity. The cheapness looks more like a cyclical fear-print on a leveraged balance sheet than a structurally shrinking base — but it is not a clean franchise until cash covers the dividend again.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.
