picks.bull_thesis: China Tower owns roughly two million shared tower sites that the three state carriers handed over by decree. Nobody else may build a competing national grid, and the carriers cannot take the towers back. The capital cycle has turned: the company spends about RMB 30bn a year (RMB 29.8bn in 2024, RMB 30.5bn in 2025) against RMB 48-50bn of depreciation, so the depreciation charge keeps falling for years. That is why profit attributable to shareholders rose from RMB 7.3bn in 2021 to RMB 11.6bn in 2025, rose a further 30.1% in the first half of 2026 (RMB 7.49bn, interim results 2026-08-11), and rose 12.8% in the third quarter. Free cash flow before lease and interest payments was RMB 25.6bn in 2025 (operating cash flow RMB 56.1bn), against a market value of only about RMB 136bn (HK$157bn at HK$9.00). The dividend is growing: the RMB 0.191 interim (about 45% of profit) was paid on 2026-10-30. The two growth wings, rooftop sensing for government and battery swapping/backup power, still grow at double digits (Smart Tower +11% and Energy +13% over nine months of 2026) and make up 16.3% of revenue. If the fall in carrier revenue is a passing effect of 5G capex cuts, and the receivable balance owed by the carriers starts to come down, the market will pay at least the 4.1-4.2 times cash operating profit that brokers such as CICC have used. That is still a fraction of the 11-20 times paid for Western tower peers.
picks.bear_thesis: The core business is shrinking, and the profit growth is an accounting effect. Carrier (tower rental) revenue went from -0.7% in the first nine months of 2025 to -5.0% in the first half of 2026 and -8.0% in the third quarter. In that quarter group revenue fell 5.7% to RMB 23.3bn, nine-month EBITDA (cash operating profit before depreciation) fell 12% to RMB 44.8bn, and the tenancy ratio slipped from 1.79 to 1.77 (Light Reading, 2026-10-23). Reported profit is up only because depreciation is falling faster than cash profit. Meanwhile trade receivables owed by the three carriers, who are also the controlling shareholders, rose to RMB 103.5bn at 2026-06-30, roughly a year of sales. The company is borrowing to fund its own customers: net debt is about RMB 92bn including leases (the net-cash line in the input bundle is a data artifact of a stub balance sheet). A global bank cut the stock to Sell on 2026-06-26, citing weak deployment momentum, tax headwinds and an index removal, and CICC reportedly trimmed its 2026-27 profit forecasts in late October 2026. The pricing agreements run to the end of 2027, and the customers who set the price have every incentive to cut it. A Hong Kong minority holder has no lever over any of this. On that path, a low multiple on a slowly shrinking annuity is not cheap.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is pricing a low-growth state utility, not terminal decline, and broadly that is right. Where we disagree: brokers model profit off the falling depreciation charge and treat the dividend as covered. CICC's 2025-10-17 note expected about RMB 870m of 2025 depreciation relief from a longer useful life for indoor coverage assets, and consensus had earnings per share rising for years on little revenue growth. The numbers say the profit is not the cash. Reported profit rose about 30% in the first half of 2026 while nine-month cash operating profit fell 12%, and receivables owed by the controlling shareholders grew by about RMB 21.6bn in six months. The street is watching the income statement while the risk sits on the balance sheet. CICC's late-October 2026 cut (reportedly -5.2% to 2026 profit and -2.5% to 2027, target HK$11.0) is the first sign of that view shifting.
picks.valley_of_death: There is no maturity wall or liquidity risk: borrowings are onshore and come from friendly state banks, and net debt has held near RMB 92bn including leases. The near-term risks (3-9 months) are slower bleeds. First, the fourth quarter of 2026 is likely to show carrier revenue down again (-5% to -8%) as carriers keep sharing networks and cutting 5G spending. Second, the full-year receivable balance could rise again, which would confirm that the company is funding its customers. Third, the end-2027 pricing renewal will start to weigh on the stock during 2027. None of these forces a sale; each can grind the price lower.
picks.positioning_washout: Little forced selling is left to buy from. The state carriers and their parent hold about two-thirds of the shares and do not sell. The index removal and the Sell downgrade around 2026-06-26, plus a large international manager trimming in June 2026, already pushed the price from a 52-week high of HK$12.85 toward the HK$8.65 low. It now sits at HK$9.00, about 11% below its 200-day average. This stock bleeds rather than flushes, which is why the committee waits for proof rather than a price.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for proof: we buy once the 2026 full-year accounts show the carriers' unpaid bills coming down (receivables below about RMB 95bn, with operating cash flow near last year's), due around 2027-03-22.

# China Tower (0788.HK): a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-02. Live price HK$9.00 on the Hong Kong listing (FMP quote; previous close HK$8.955). Figures are in renminbi (RMB) unless marked HK$; one RMB is about HK$1.155, the rate implied by the October 2026 interim dividend (RMB 0.19122 = HK$0.220901). Share counts are post-consolidation, about 17.48 billion shares.*

**A note on the evidence.** The transcript bundle is old: the latest call is the 2023 annual results (2024-03-18). Everything since then comes from the screener's financial history, FMP's quarterly statements and dated news: the 2026 interim results (2026-08-11) and the third-quarter update (reported 2026-10-23). Where the transcripts and the newer numbers disagree, the numbers win.

**A data warning for the committee.** The input bundle's "live correction" says China Tower has net cash of RMB 9.6bn and zero debt. That is wrong. FMP's 2026-09-30 balance sheet is a stub: assets, debt and receivables are all blank, and only the cash line is filled in. The last complete balance sheet, at 2026-06-30, shows RMB 77.8bn of borrowings plus RMB 23.6bn of lease liabilities against RMB 9.6bn of cash. That is **net debt of about RMB 92bn including leases (about RMB 68bn excluding them)**, which matches the scan's RMB 92.2bn. Every valuation below uses net debt, not net cash.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

From 2022 to early 2024 management told one story, "One Core and Two Wings". The core is renting tower space to China's three state carriers (the carrier tower business). The two wings are growth businesses: Smart Tower, which rents tower tops to government and industry for cameras and sensors, and Energy, which covers battery swapping for e-bike couriers and backup power.

- **2022-08-08 (2022 interim):** the tone was expansionary. Revenue rose 6.6%, the two wings grew 46.5%, and 5G was "gradually becoming the main driving force" for the carrier business.
- **2023-03-02 (2022 annual):** revenue grew 6.5% to RMB 92.2bn and the tenancy ratio (tenants per tower) reached 1.74.
- **2024-03-18 (2023 annual):** this is the pivot call. Reported revenue grew only 2% to RMB 94.0bn because the 2023 pricing agreement with the carriers came with discounts. In management's words, "we have offered some discount as a result of the pricing agreement". Operating cash flow fell while the new billing system was rolled out. The emphasis moved from growth to asset longevity, cost control and "the reuse and longevity of assets".
- **2025 to 2026 (no transcripts, numbers only):** the arc has moved again. Profit growth now comes almost entirely from depreciation running off (capex around RMB 30bn a year against depreciation near RMB 48-50bn). Meanwhile the core business has started to shrink. In the 2026 interim results (2026-08-11), carrier revenue fell 5.0% and group revenue fell 1.8% to RMB 48.7bn. In the third quarter, carrier revenue fell 8.0% and group revenue fell 5.7% to RMB 23.3bn. The tenancy ratio slipped from 1.79 to 1.77 (Light Reading, 2026-10-23). The story has gone from "5G drives growth" to "earnings rise because we spend less".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Stable growth" in the carrier business (2022-2023 calls) | Carrier revenue -0.7% for 9M 2025 (CICC note, 2025-10-17), -5.0% in H1 2026, -8.0% in Q3 2026 | **Diverged.** Growth turned into decline, and the decline is speeding up |
| 2023 cash-flow dip "is just a temporary thing" (2024-03-18) | Operating cash flow RMB 49.5bn in FY2024 and RMB 56.1bn in FY2025 | **Delivered.** Cash collection did recover |
| Two Wings is a second growth engine | Two Wings reached 16.3% of revenue in H1 2026 (RMB 7.9bn); Smart Tower +11% and Energy +13% over 9M 2026 | **Partly true.** The wings keep growing, but they are too small to offset an 8% fall in a business four times their size |
| Profitability "continued to improve" | Net income rose from RMB 7.3bn (2021) to RMB 11.6bn (2025), and H1 2026 profit was +30.1% | **True on the income statement, but low quality.** The gain comes from lower depreciation, an earlier extension of the useful life of indoor-coverage assets, and lower financing costs. Nine-month 2026 EBITDA (operating cash earnings before depreciation) fell 12% to RMB 44.8bn |
| Capex discipline | Capex RMB 29.8bn in 2024 and RMB 30.5bn in 2025, against depreciation of RMB 48-50bn | **True.** This is the engine of the profit growth and of free cash flow (RMB 25.6bn in FY2025 before lease and interest payments) |

The most important divergence: **net profit is up about 30% while EBITDA is down about 12%.** These are two different businesses. The accounting business is improving. The cash-earning business is shrinking.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** In 2022 management spoke offensively: "seized the opportunities", "accelerated growth", 5G as "the main driving force". By 2024-03-18 it was defensive: discounts granted, cash flow to be "verified", "intensified efforts to reduce cost". Guidance was never numeric. Management gave direction ("strive to accomplish the full year CapEx plan") rather than targets, and that pattern has not changed. With no call transcript after March 2024 there is no direct tone read on the 2026 decline. A preview piece (2026-08-04) noted that the company gives "no numeric guidance".

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium.** Directional promises were kept: cash flow recovered after 2023, capex stayed near RMB 30bn, and the payout ratio rose (the 2026 interim payout was about 45% of profit). The screener's 4-of-6 quarterly beat rate (67%) fits a company that keeps its promises on cost and capex. The larger implied promise, that carrier tenancy would keep inching up, has not held. Tenancy fell from 1.79 to 1.77 in 2026, and carrier revenue is falling. Management controls costs well. It does not control demand, which is set by three state customers.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Pricing power.** On 2024-03-18 the first concern management raised itself was cash flow after the new pricing agreement. The agreement's discounts were the real story. The current agreements run to the end of 2027, and their renegotiation is the next pressure point.
- **Carrier capex and network sharing.** The carriers are cutting 5G capex and sharing networks. Every co-located tenant that leaves cuts revenue, which is what the 2026 tenancy drop shows.
- **Index and ownership.** A global bank downgraded the stock to Sell on 2026-06-26, citing weak network deployment momentum, tax headwinds and removal from a widely tracked index. A large international manager trimmed its holding in June 2026 (preview article, 2026-08-04).
- **Earnings quality.** CICC's 2025-10-17 note flagged the risks of "depreciation on existing assets" not meeting expectations and operating cash flow falling short. A later CICC note, from about late October 2026 (exact date unverified), reportedly cut 2026 and 2027 profit forecasts by 5.2% and 2.5% and set a HK$11.0 target, citing pressure on tower revenue as the depreciation benefit fades.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: carrier revenue went from -0.7% (9M 2025) to -5.0% (H1 2026) to -8.0% (Q3 2026). The decline is accelerating.
- Red: nine-month 2026 EBITDA is down 12%, while reported profit is up because depreciation fell. That is earnings quality moving the wrong way.
- Red: the tenancy ratio fell for the first time in the recorded history, from 1.79 to 1.77 (2026).
- Red: the input bundle's net-cash claim is a data artifact. The real balance sheet carries about RMB 92bn of net debt including leases.
- Red: index removal and a Sell downgrade (2026-06-26) leave the shareholder base thinner.
- Green: a regulatory near-monopoly over about two million sites that the carriers transferred by state decree. No listed competitor exists.
- Green: capex is RMB 18-20bn below depreciation each year. Free cash flow was RMB 25.6bn in FY2025 before leases and interest, versus a market value of about RMB 136bn.
- Green: the dividend is rising. The 2026 interim payment of RMB 0.191 per share was paid on 2026-10-30, a payout of about 45%.
- Green: the two growth wings are still growing at double digits.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary moved from "growth by sharing" (2022) to "asset life extension" and "longevity" (2024). A company that talks about extending asset lives is telling you that its profit growth is coming from the depreciation line.
- In the 2024 deck the discount was framed as "excluding the impact of the commercial pricing agreements", with growth shown on a comparable basis. That habit of presenting a carve-out of the headline number is worth watching when the 2027 renewal comes.
- The board reshuffle and the proposed new non-executive director in 2026 (TipRanks items, undated) look routine for a state-owned company. No signal can be read from them without dates.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: deteriorating.** Capital allocation itself is sensible: capex is down, payouts are up, and leverage is stable at about RMB 92bn of net debt including leases. But the business the capital supports is now shrinking at its core. The single most important question for the director: **is the 8% fall in carrier revenue a temporary effect of carrier 5G capex cuts, or the start of the carriers using their power as customers (network sharing and site decommissioning now, a harsher price at the end-2027 renewal)?** If it is the latter, the cheap multiple is pricing a declining annuity correctly.

**Moat.** This is a regulatory-licence and scale moat: in practice, no one else may build China's shared tower grid. But it is a moat against competitors, not against customers. The three state carriers are both the only tenants and the owners of the company, and they set the price. Returns are thin (ROIC 3.9%, ROE 4.9%), gross margin is contracting, and carrier revenue is now falling. That makes the moat **narrow, and eroding in its economics even though it is legally secure**. **Secular threat: manageable.** Towers are not being disrupted by technology. The pressure is a customer-concentration and pricing problem, not a terminal one. The cheapness is part fear (index removal, foreign selling) and part a correct read of a slowly shrinking core. It is not a clean case of mispricing.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.
picks.sop_fair_value: HK$11.10 per share (about RMB 9.6), about 23% above the HK$9.00 price.

That assumes carrier revenue falls 3-5% a year, offset by lower depreciation and growth in the Smart Tower and Energy lines. Capitalised at 13 times, that gives RMB 9.6 (HK$11.10). As an enterprise-value cross-check, about 3.9 times a RMB 60bn run-rate cash operating profit (the peer-adjusted level brokers have used; CICC's late-October 2026 target of HK$11.0 sits close) gives about RMB 234bn of enterprise value. Less net debt including leases of about RMB 92bn (2026-06-30), that leaves RMB 142bn, or RMB 8.1 per share, so the cash-flow lens reaches the top of the range only if receivables stop growing. There is no special-situation overlay: no net cash, no asset sale, no tender. The interim dividend of RMB 0.191 was already paid on 2026-10-30 and is not added.

Equity owner earnings (free cash flow after leases and interest, about RMB 13-14bn in 2025) recover to RMB 0.85 per share as receivables are collected and carrier revenue stabilises; at 15 times that is RMB 12.75, about HK$14.70. picks.bull_thesis: Verallia is Europe's largest glass-container maker, and glass is a regional business: furnaces are expensive, run continuously, and bottles are too heavy to ship far, so each region is served by a handful of producers. That structure let Verallia pass through the 2021-22 energy shock with its gross margin intact (21.0% in 2019 to 21.4% in 2021). The bull case is that 2024-2026 is the trough of a de-stocking cycle in wine and spirits, not a permanent decline. The third quarter of 2026 (reported 27 October) showed the margin holding near 21% even with lower volumes, guidance of about 700 million euros of adjusted operating cash profit and about 220 million euros of free cash flow was confirmed for the third time, and debt fell to 2.5 times operating cash profit. The footprint plan, now described as implemented, should lift 2027 margins as German capacity cuts flow through. On analyst-style 2027 numbers near 770 million euros of operating cash profit and a 6.5 times multiple, with net debt down to about 1.6 billion euros, the equity is worth about 26.50 euros. At roughly 9-10% free-cash-flow yield on guided cash (220 million against a 2.23 billion euro market value), the stock pays an investor to wait, and a controlling shareholder at 77% could one day bid for the rest. Conditions: volumes stabilise in 2027, energy costs do not spike again, and the Capital Markets Day on 18 November 2026 lays out credible savings.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that this is a levered company on a slowly shrinking base. Revenue has fallen from 3.90 billion euros in 2023 to 3.33 billion in 2025 and fell again in the third quarter of 2026 (down 3.1% organically); EPS fell 62% in 2025 to 0.77 euros; the gross margin is contracting; and return on invested capital, at 11.5%, is well off its peak. European wine and spirits consumption is in structural decline, so weather-related explanations for weak volumes (as offered on 27 October 2026) may be masking a trend. With 1.76 billion euros of net debt in front of a 2.23 billion euro market value, a modest miss is magnified: if operating cash profit settles at 650 million euros and the market pays 5.5 times, as it does for stressed packaging names, the equity is worth about 10.50 euros. The Altman Z-score of 1.7 sits in the caution zone, the free float is only about 12% so there is little natural buying, and the new controlling owner may prefer debt paydown or a lowball squeeze-out to dividends. What would confirm it: 2027 guidance at the 18 November Capital Markets Day below 700 million euros, or another quarter of volume declines.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is not obviously looking the wrong way. At 17.86 euros it prices Verallia at about 5.8 times operating cash profit, which is roughly what the confirmed 2026 guidance and a mid-cycle multiple justify. Where we disagree mildly is on direction: analyst-style 2027 forecasts near 770 million euros of operating cash profit require the margin to climb toward 23% on flat or falling revenue, and the third quarter of 2026 moved the other way (margin 20.8% versus 21.3%, volumes down). We credit only part of the footprint savings. The deep-value screen signal (owner-earnings and discounted-cash-flow models showing 45-63% upside) leans on peak-era cash flows and ignores the debt; our balance-sheet-aware valuation shows a single-digit discount, not a deep one. No live analyst price targets could be verified this run, so none are cited.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the next three to nine months: the 18 November 2026 Capital Markets Day, where a new controlling owner may reset mid-term targets; the fourth-quarter volume trend in wine and spirits; European energy prices into the winter; and full-year 2026 results in late February 2027. There is no visible refinancing wall in the materials and liquidity is 1,048 million euros, so a liquidity event is unlikely, but with net debt of about 1.75 billion euros a 50 million euro shortfall in operating cash profit removes roughly 2.50 euros of equity value per share at 6 times. That leverage is why the adverse case sits near 10.50 euros.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited because there are few marginal holders left: after the 2025 tender offer the controlling shareholder holds 77.3%, employees about 4.4%, Bpifrance about 3.8% and treasury about 2.3%, leaving a free float near 12%. Thin float means index weights are small, so an index reweighting or a deletion from a mid-cap benchmark could force some selling, and sector-wide packaging or consumer de-ratings move a thin stock disproportionately. Insider buying is nil per the screen. The path to our entry level is most likely a sector-wide sell-off in European packaging and consumer staples rather than mechanical forced selling.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 14.00 euros, which a sector-wide sell-off in European packaging and consumer names could deliver.

The thesis holds. The third-quarter results on 27 October 2026 did what the committee needed: the 2026 targets of about 700 million euros of adjusted operating cash profit and about 220 million euros of free cash flow were confirmed, the margin stayed near 21% over nine months, and debt fell to 2.5 times operating cash profit. Volumes slipped and the quarter's margin dipped half a point, which keeps us cautious but does not break the case. Nothing dated has changed the committee's answer from 26 October, so we inherit it.

Valuing the business by its pieces gives about 20 euros a share: the glass operation on about 715 million euros of operating cash profit at 6 times, less about 1.70 billion euros of net borrowings, minorities and restructuring cash. At 17.86 euros that is about a 12% discount, short of the 20% margin of safety this book requires in the current reflation backdrop. The adverse case, on 650 million euros of operating cash profit at 5.5 times with no further debt paydown, is about 10.50 euros, so the downside is far larger than the upside. At 14.00 euros the discount to fair value is over 40%, the adverse case is substantially paid for, and the cash yield on guided free cash flow would exceed 12%.

Conviction stays low at 2 out of 5. The moat is real but narrow and eroding at the margin, wine and spirits volumes face a slow structural decline, and leverage magnifies every miss. The value case alone also scores 2: a modest discount on a levered, slowly shrinking base. Watch the 18 November 2026 Capital Markets Day for the new owner's mid-term targets and capital-allocation policy.
picks.forcing_function: No binding re-rating event exists. The change of control has already happened. The nearest scheduled events are the Capital Markets Day on 18 November 2026 (mid-term targets, capital allocation, possibly the dividend and debt policy) and full-year 2026 results in late February 2027. A squeeze-out by the controlling shareholder would be a genuine forcing event but is unannounced and requires about ten more points of capital; it is given no value. Re-rating otherwise depends on steady deleveraging, which moves value from lenders to shareholders at about 1 euro a share per year.

# Verallia (VRLA.PA) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-03. Prices in euros, Paris listing.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript was available for this run: the bundled inputs carry none, FMP returned no transcript, news or press releases for this listing, and the Quartr transcript service was not accessible. The primary source used is the company's own third-quarter 2026 release, dated 27 October 2026 and read from Verallia's website, together with the screener's financial history, the FMP live quote (17.86 euros on 2026-11-03) and this committee's own prior records (2026-09-07 and 2026-10-26). No quotation below is invented; where management's words are paraphrased, they are paraphrases of the 27 October release.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Verallia, Europe's largest maker of glass bottles and jars (about 3.3 billion euros of revenue in 2025, 34 glass plants in 12 countries), has moved from a boom story to a repair story. In 2022-2023 the narrative was pricing power: energy-driven price increases lifted revenue from 2.67 billion euros (2021) to 3.90 billion (2023) and net profit from 243 million to 470 million euros. Since then the story has been one of normalisation and defence: wine and spirits customers de-stocked, prices were given back, and revenue fell to 3.46 billion (2024) and 3.33 billion (2025), with net profit collapsing to 91 million euros in 2025 (EPS 0.77).

The 2026 narrative, as framed in the third-quarter release, rests on three pillars: holding the margin (adjusted operating cash profit, or EBITDA — earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation — near 21% of sales), executing an "industrial footprint adaptation plan" (closing or resizing furnaces, notably in Germany), and paying down debt. The change of control in 2025, when BWGI (the Moreira Salles family's investment arm) took a 77% stake through a tender offer, sits behind all of it. The next chapter is a Capital Markets Day on 18 November 2026, where management has said it will present mid-term strategic priorities.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (27 Oct 2026 release) | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Profitability "in line with H1 despite lower activity" | Q3 adjusted EBITDA 172m euros at a 20.8% margin vs 181m / 21.3% a year earlier; nine months 523m / 20.7% vs 531m | Broadly true, but the third-quarter margin did slip half a point year on year. "In line" is a fair, slightly generous description. |
| 2026 outlook confirmed: EBITDA around 700m, free cash flow around 220m (before restructuring cash) | Nine-month EBITDA 523m implies a fourth quarter of about 177m, close to Q3's 172m | Achievable without heroics. This is now the third time the 700m figure has been confirmed. |
| "Continued strong cash generation" and deleveraging | Net debt fell to 2.5 times trailing EBITDA at 30 September 2026, from 2.6 times at June and 2.7 times at December 2025; liquidity 1,048m euros | Corroborated, though the pace is slow — about a tenth of a turn per quarter. |
| Footprint plan "now implemented" and delivering, especially in Germany | No savings figure is quantified in the release | Directionally plausible (Germany volume decline was described as expected), but unmeasurable from what has been published. |
| Volumes down in Q3 on an "unfavorable summer in Europe" | Q3 revenue 829m, down 2.1% reported and 3.1% at constant scope and currency (3.9% excluding Argentina) | Weather is a convenient explanation; the multi-year decline in wine and spirits consumption is the deeper one. |

The screener's longer-term figures sharpen the picture: gross margin 17.4% and contracting, revenue growth -3.6% in the latest year, EPS down 62%, and a three-year revenue growth rate near zero. Return on equity of 30.5% flatters because equity is thin relative to the 1.76 billion euros of net debt; return on invested capital of 11.5% is the better guide and is well below the 2023 peak.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable to slightly defensive. The language across 2026 has shifted from growth to discipline: "strict cost discipline", footprint adaptation, cash generation and deleveraging. Guidance has been repeated rather than raised. The absence of any 2027 commentary, deferred to the 18 November Capital Markets Day, reads as caution rather than concealment. Trajectory rating: Stable.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The 700m euro EBITDA and 220m euro free-cash-flow targets have been held through the first half and the third quarter, and the nine-month run rate supports them. The weakness is that the guidance was set low after the 2024-2025 earnings collapse, so meeting it is not proof of recovery. Reliability: Medium-to-High on the near-term numbers; Low visibility beyond 2026 until the Capital Markets Day.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without a transcript, specific questions cannot be cited. The obvious pressure points visible from the numbers are: (1) whether volume declines in wine and spirits are cyclical or structural; (2) how much of the footprint-plan savings fall into 2027; (3) whether the controlling shareholder intends to take the company private (it holds 77.3% of the capital, short of the 90% French squeeze-out threshold); and (4) the dividend and capital-allocation policy at 2.5 times leverage.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Q3 2026 volumes fell after a stable first half; organic revenue down 3.1%.
- Red: Q3 2026 margin slipped to 20.8% from 21.3%, with the release citing inflationary energy and input costs.
- Red: gross margin contracting and EPS down 62% in the latest fiscal year; Altman Z-score of 1.7 (a solvency gauge where under about 1.8 is the caution zone).
- Red: very thin free float (about 12%) after the 2025 tender offer, which limits liquidity and index demand.
- Green: 2026 guidance confirmed for the third time (27 Oct 2026).
- Green: leverage down steadily, 2.7 to 2.5 times over nine months; liquidity above 1 billion euros.
- Green: margins held through the 2021-22 inflation shock (gross margin 21.0% to 21.4%), evidence of real pricing pass-through in a supply-tight industry.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The release headline leans on "profitability" rather than growth, and the footprint plan is now described in the past tense ("implemented"), which positions 2027 as the year of savings. Holding back all mid-term targets for the 18 November Capital Markets Day under a new controlling shareholder is the main thing to watch: new owners often reset targets lower and then beat them, or use the event to reframe capital allocation (dividend versus debt paydown).

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: PIVOTING — from post-boom earnings decline to a cost-and-debt repair under a new controlling owner. The single most important thing for the director to weigh is the balance sheet: 1.76 billion euros of net debt (including about 29 million of leases; about 1.73 billion excluding them) against a market value of about 2.23 billion euros means small changes in operating profit swing the equity value sharply.

Moat: scale-cost. Glass containers are heavy and travel badly, so regional plant networks with high-temperature furnaces create local oligopolies; Verallia is the European leader. The moat is real but narrow, and the evidence says it is eroding at the margin: returns and margins have fallen from the 2023 peak and the latest-year gross margin is contracting. Secular threat: material, not terminal — falling alcohol consumption in Europe and lightweighting/substitution pressure erode the volume base slowly, but glass remains the default for wine, spirits and premium food. The cheapness is partly a fear-print and partly a slowly shrinking base; at 2.5 times leverage, the second matters more than it would for an unlevered company.

# JD Logistics (2618.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-16. Transcripts read: Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), Q4/FY 2025 (2026-03-05), Q2 2026 (2026-08-13). Figures in RMB unless stated; the stock trades in Hong Kong dollars (HK$10.26 on 2026-11-16, FMP quote). Third-quarter 2026 results are due 2026-11-17 (FMP earnings calendar).*

**Takeaway:** JD Logistics is a fast-growing, thin-margin logistics network whose profits are now rising again after a soft 2025, and management has broadly done what it said it would on profit. The two things to watch are the quality of the growth (much of the 2026 revenue jump is a consolidated, low-margin on-demand delivery business, not the higher-value supply-chain work) and cash conversion, which the latest data feed reports as roughly zero over the trailing twelve months.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-13):** the story was integrated supply chain (ISC - running a customer's warehousing, inventory and delivery end to end) growth of 45.8% to RMB 13.1B, "targeted investments" in overseas and timeliness, and the new full-time food-delivery rider force. Profit was the soft spot: non-IFRS (adjusted, excluding items like share-based pay) net profit RMB 2.02B, attributable profit down about 8% year on year.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-03-05):** the CEO framed 2025 around three differentiators - ISC, customer experience, and automation/AI. Overseas warehouse space was doubled as promised (nearly 200 bonded/overseas warehouses, about 2 million square metres) and the JoyExpress delivery brand launched in Saudi Arabia and Europe. Deppon (the freight subsidiary) was conceded as a 2025 margin drag with "positive improvement" promised for 2026.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-08-13):** the CFO led with profit, not growth: revenue RMB 64.1B (+24.3%), adjusted operating profit +11.6% for the quarter and +39.9% for the half. The emphasis has shifted from "capacity building" to "operating leverage", with overseas now called "an important second growth curve" and the Joybuy European retail venture of the parent JD.com a named driver.

The arc is from investment to harvest - but the headline growth has quietly changed composition: ISC revenue growth slowed to 12.1% in Q2 2026, while "other customers" (express, freight and the newly consolidated on-demand riders) grew 37.6%.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "High-quality revenue growth" (every call) | Revenue RMB 104.7B (2021) to 217.2B (2025); H1 2026 RMB 124.7B, +26.5% | Corroborated on volume. Quality is mixed: Q2 2026 gross margin 9.7%, down 0.9pp year on year; outsourcing costs +40.5% to 37% of revenue on the on-demand consolidation. |
| 2026 profit would show "positive improvement" (2026-03-05) | IFRS net income Q1 2026 RMB 0.88B, Q2 RMB 2.41B; H1 adjusted operating profit +39.9% | Delivered. Trailing-twelve-month IFRS net income about RMB 7.4B (Q3 25 2.03 + Q4 25 2.04 + Q1 26 0.88 + Q2 26 2.41). |
| Core business margins rising, Deppon the drag (2026-08-13) | Group gross margin fell; management says the "original core business" margin rose | Plausible but unaudited in the transcript - no segment margin given. Cannot verify the split. |
| Overseas warehouse doubling by end-2025 (2025-11-13) | Confirmed achieved on 2026-03-05 | Delivered. |
| Strong cash generation (implied by the cheap price-to-free-cash-flow) | FY 2025 price/FCF about 5x; FMP trailing FCF reported as 0; FCF growth -26.7% in 2025 | Unclear. A "0" trailing figure may be a data gap, but the falling 2025 FCF is real. Lease payments (RMB 18.7B of lease liabilities) sit below operating cash flow and make FCF look better than owner cash. |
| Balance sheet strength | Cash RMB 22.47B vs borrowings RMB 5.17B (2026-06-30) | Corroborated: about RMB 17.3B net cash before leases; about RMB 1.4B net debt once RMB 18.7B of leases are counted. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, edging up.** Q3 2025 was defensive on profit ("lay the foundation for long-term business growth"; "In 2026, still I'm not in the right time to make the forecast"). Q4 2025 was more assertive on 2026 profit but vague on numbers. Q2 2026 is the most confident: "The operating margin will be further improved in the second half" and express growth "more than double the industry average". The shift is from offensive investment language to an operating-leverage message - a healthy direction - but specifics remain thin: no margin targets, no capex number, and no Deppon figures.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management gives qualitative, not numeric, guidance. What they promised, they delivered: the overseas-warehouse doubling (promised 2025-11-13, confirmed 2026-03-05) and the 2026 profit recovery (promised 2026-03-05, H1 operating profit +39.9%). The screener records 4 of the last 5 quarters beating estimates. Because the targets are soft, sandbagging is hard to detect. **Reliability: Medium-High.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Deppon's profitability** (asked 2026-03-05 and 2026-08-13): answered only with "on the track of recovery", never numbers.
- **Automation capex and returns** (2025-11-13, 2026-03-05): management says investment will be "higher than that of 2025" but gives no figure or payback.
- **Express industry slowdown** (2026-08-13): answered with relative growth claims, not unit pricing.
- **2026 revenue outlook** (2025-11-13): explicitly declined.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: gross margin down 0.9pp in Q2 2026 even as revenue grew 24%.
- Red: growth mix shifting toward consolidated, low-margin on-demand delivery (outsourcing costs +40.5%, Q2 2026).
- Red: free cash flow fell 26.7% in 2025 and the latest trailing figure is reported as zero; lease burden is large.
- Red: external ISC growth slowed to 12.5% in Q2 2026 from much higher rates in 2025.
- Green: profit recovery delivered on schedule (H1 2026 adjusted operating profit +39.9%).
- Green: cost ratios improving - staff costs 34.2% of revenue (-1.0pp), rent 5.3% (-1.1pp), operating expenses 6.4% (-0.5pp) in Q2 2026.
- Green: about RMB 17.3B of net cash before leases - roughly a third of the market value.
- Green: overseas build-out delivered to target.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The CFO, not the CEO, opened the Q2 2026 call and led with operating profit - a sign the investor message is now about margins.
- "Technology exports" appeared on 2026-08-13: the company now talks of selling its warehouse robots to outside customers - early, unquantified.
- The dependence on the parent is rising, not falling: JD Group ISC revenue RMB 19.88B of RMB 30.17B in Q2 2026, with Joybuy (JD's European retail) named as a driver. Related-party pricing is a governance lever worth watching.
- Energy-cost language ("fluctuation of the energy industry", 2026-08-13) shows management expects input-cost pressure; vehicle costs nonetheless fell 0.2pp as a share of revenue.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** Growth is robust and profit is recovering, but margins are not structurally widening yet, and the mix shift toward on-demand delivery offsets the core ISC improvement.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** whether the cheapness is in the earnings or in the cash. On earnings the stock is about 7.6 times trailing profit with a third of its value in pre-lease net cash; on owner cash (after lease payments and rising automation capex) the case is much thinner. The 2026-11-17 third-quarter results are the next read on both.

**Moat:** scale-cost and network (the densest self-operated warehouse network in China, about 1,600 warehouses and 34 million square metres, plus the JD.com anchor volume). Returns are low (ROIC about 1%, net margin about 3%), so the moat protects volume more than pricing - narrow, stable. **Secular threat:** manageable - automation and autonomous delivery are being adopted by the company itself rather than used against it, and e-commerce channel shift is a tailwind for a logistics provider. The cheapness reads as a fear print on China and thin margins, not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Meanwhile the parts are weakening: Studios margin has slid from 15% (2019) to 13.9% (2025) to 11% in H1 2026 and is guided to the bottom of a lowered 13-15% range; cash conversion was 65% and then 63% against an 80% target; group earnings per share roughly halved from 0.11 pounds (2022) to 0.058 (2025), and free cash flow fell 38% last year. UK linear advertising is soft (Q3 2026 guided down about 5%, Q4 'very little visibility'), and every month the deal is delayed ITV still owns that business. If the deal fails, shareholders hold a narrow-moat, hit-driven studio plus a structurally declining broadcaster, and the screener's own earnings-based fair value (48p) shows how low the market can go on a combined, ex-deal view. The 2026 buyback also pre-spends part of the return before the regulator has spoken.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrow. The market prices ITV close to an ex-deal, whole-group value: at 66.9p, the group is worth about 2.4B pounds, which is roughly Studios at a modest multiple plus a heavily discounted cash return. The street's working assumption appears to be that UK linear advertising keeps shrinking and that the Sky deal faces a long, uncertain review; since 2026-11-04 that second assumption is factually correct, so the market is not looking the wrong way on timing. Where the market may be too harsh is the residual studio: a business with 59% international revenue, about 30% from streamers and a format library that travels (Love Island in 28 markets) should not trade at 5-6x EBITA once separated. That disagreement only pays once the sale completes, and the market will not credit it ahead of the regulatory decision. No analyst price targets were available from FMP for this listing, and none were verified by web search, so we do not cite a consensus target.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) runs to the 2027-01-27 regulator reports and the ministerial decision after them. In that period: Q3 advertising was guided down about 5% and Q4 has 'very little visibility' (2026-07-31), so the business ITV still owns is weakening; Studios must deliver a heavy fourth-quarter slate to reach even the bottom of its 13-15% margin range after an 11% first half; cash conversion has run at 63-65% against an 80% target; and the buyback is lifting net debt before any proceeds arrive. If the minister refers the deal to a second-phase probe, completion slips toward late 2027 and the cash return's present value falls; a block would leave the stock trading on the combined-group view, around the mid-50s. There is no debt wall or liquidity risk: leverage is about 1x and the balance sheet is investment grade.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure looks limited. The shareholder base is largely UK income and value funds; the ordinary 5p dividend is being held, not cut, so there is no dividend-cut trigger for yield holders. The main mechanical risk is merger-arbitrage and event-driven holders exiting on a second-phase referral, which could push the stock toward the high-50s quickly. The stock already trades near the bottom of its 52-week range (61.5p to 87.35p) and about 12% below its 200-day average, so much of the post-announcement disappointment is in the price. Smart-money and insider-buying signals are weak (smart-money score 9 of 100, no insider buying).
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for the event: we buy once the Culture Secretary, after the competition and media regulators report on 27 January 2027, decides not to send the Sky deal to a deeper investigation. The thesis holds: ITV is selling its UK broadcaster to Sky for 1.6B pounds, will return about 950M pounds (about 25p a share) to shareholders, and keeps a narrow-moat global studio that the market prices cheaply once that cash is set aside. Our parts add to about 78p against 66.9p today, a discount too small to buy ahead of a decision that, since the 4 November 2026 intervention notice, has a fixed report date but an uncertain outcome and timing. The favourable case is about 100p and the adverse case, where the deal stalls and ITV keeps both businesses, is about 54p, so at today's price the downside is about as large as the base-case upside. Management credibility is good (a long record of hitting advertising guidance and cutting costs), but Studios margins and cash conversion have slipped and must recover in the fourth quarter. This is continued coverage: the committee's last answer (wait, conviction 3) is inherited, with only the event re-dated from a quick first-phase clearance, which the intervention notice has made impossible, to the post-January ministerial decision. The value case on its own is also a 3: the discount to fair value is about 15% and depends on a regulatory outcome we cannot underwrite today.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst, what forces the re-rating, is the regulatory decision on the Sky sale: the CMA and Ofcom reports due by 5pm on 2027-01-27, followed by the Culture Secretary's decision whether to refer the deal for a deeper second-phase probe. A decision not to refer (or acceptance of undertakings) would put the 950M-pound return and the standalone studio story on a firm path, with the H1-2027 Capital Markets Day as the follow-on event that sets the studio's growth and payout plan. Secondary dates: the full-year 2026 results (around early March 2027) for proof that Studios hit its margin guidance.

# ITV plc (ITV.L): a deep dive on management and the setup (as of 2026-11-09)

Sources: earnings calls dated 2019-07-27, 2020-08-06, 2021-03-09, 2026-03-05 (full-year 2025) and 2026-07-31 (2026 interims), the screener's financial trajectory, and dated news through 2026-11-04. The live price used is 66.9p (FMP quote, London listing, pence sterling, 2026-11-09).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from "a broadcaster defending its audience" to "a global content studio that is selling its broadcaster".

- 2019-2021: ITV was a UK advertising business with a production arm attached. Management talked about "scaled mass audiences", total advertising revenue (TAR, the money advertisers spend across ITV's channels and streaming) and cost savings, with Studios targeted at "at least 5% revenue growth" and a 14-16% margin (2019-07-27). Covid turned the 2020 calls into a cost-and-survival exercise (Q2 2020 advertising down 43%, "the most severe decline in the history of ITV", 2020-08-06).
- 2026-03-05 (full-year 2025): the language is "two attractive and resilient businesses". Two-thirds of revenue now comes from Studios and digital. Studios grew 5% to GBP 2.13B with GBP 297M adjusted EBITA (earnings before interest, tax and amortisation); digital advertising grew 12% to GBP 540M while linear advertising fell by double digits. Management confirmed "preliminary discussions with Sky" about selling the Media & Entertainment (M&E) arm.
- 2026-07-31 (interims): the sale is agreed. Sky (Comcast) pays GBP 1.6B plus up to GBP 200M contingent, enabling a "GBP 950 million net cash return, excluding any contingent consideration", with a GBP 100M buyback started as an early slice. ITV Studios becomes the whole company; a Capital Markets Day is promised for H1 2027.

Dropped along the way: BritBox UK as a growth pillar, the 14-16% Studios margin target (now 13-15%, and 2026 at "the lower end").

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence in the numbers | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Studios consistently outgrows the market" (2026-03-05) | Studios revenue +5% in 2025, +2% in H1 2026 (3% organic); market growing 1.5-2.5% | Holds, but the gap is narrowing in 2026 |
| Studios margins "industry-leading" | 13.9% in 2025 vs 15% in 2019; H1 2026 at 11%, guided to the low end of 13-15% | Weaker than the words: margins have drifted down |
| "Strong levels of cash" | Profit-to-cash conversion 65% (2025) and 63% rolling (H1 2026) vs ~80% three-year average; screener FCF -38% year on year | Cash is softer than the language; working-capital build cited |
| Group earnings resilient | Revenue flat for five years (GBP 3.45B in 2021 to 3.51B in 2025); EPS 0.11 (2022) to 0.058 (2025); 3-year EPS CAGR -19% | The group earnings base has not grown; digital only offsets linear decline |
| Investment-grade balance sheet | Net debt GBP 566M end-2025, GBP 652M June 2026, about 1x leverage | Holds |
| M&E cost discipline | M&E margin held at 11.8% in 2025 despite TAR -5% | Holds; the cost-cutting record (GBP 253M cumulative savings since 2019) is real |

Net: management's operational claims are mostly corroborated; the profit and cash trajectory is poorer than the confident tone.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable, shifting toward defensive on advertising and offensive on Studios. In 2026-03-05 the tone is upbeat ("outperforming market expectations"). By 2026-07-31 advertising language is guarded: Q3 TAR "expected to be down around 5%", "we have very little visibility of Q4", and macro is invoked ("a change of prime minister", "macro effects from the Iran war ... cost of living, inflation"). Studios language stays confident ("good visibility on revenue") but leans on a heavy fourth-quarter delivery slate.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High-to-medium. Advertising guidance has generally been met or beaten (2019 H1 advertising -5% vs -6% guided; 2025 TAR -5% "better than guidance"); the screener shows earnings beats in 5 of 7 quarters (71%). The Studios margin target has, however, been quietly lowered twice and 2026 is guided to the bottom of the reduced range. Reliability: Medium-High.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- How weak is Q3/Q4 advertising and does the World Cup pull spend forward (Deutsche Bank, 2026-07-31). Management could not give Q4 visibility.
- The Studios "growth algorithm" (mix, price, volume) was deferred to the 2027 Capital Markets Day: the standalone equity story is not yet fully specified.
- AI as a cost lever and as a threat to how linear inventory is bought (Barclays, 2026-03-05): answered with generalities.
- Regulatory path for the Sky sale was not a focus in the calls but has since become the dominant issue (see below).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Studios margin slide: 15% (2019) to 13.9% (2025) to 11% in H1 2026, with the full year resting on Q4 deliveries.
- Cash conversion below target two reporting periods running (65%, then 63%).
- Group earnings per share roughly halved since 2022.
- 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-04: the Culture Secretary first said she was minded to intervene, then issued a public interest intervention notice on the Sky deal, with Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) and Ofcom reports due 2027-01-27 and a possible referral to a deeper second-phase probe after that. The cash return is now further away and less certain.

Green flags:
- Binding sale agreement for M&E at GBP 1.6B, with a GBP 950M net return committed (2026-07-31) and a GBP 100M buyback already running.
- Digital growth is real: digital revenue +13% in H1 2026, ITVX viewing +27%, first month over 20M monthly active users (June 2026).
- Studios customer mix pivoted from about 5% streamer revenue to about 30% over five years; 59% of revenue international.
- Long cost-discipline record (GBP 273M cumulative permanent savings targeted by end-2026).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary has shifted from "audiences" to "IP library", "Zoo 55" (ITV's digital distribution arm) and "creator, owner, producer, and distributor of IP": management is already speaking as a pure studio.
- "Mindful of the macroeconomic climate" (2026-07-31) is new hedging language on advertising.
- The interims say the buyback will run "nine and 12 months ... as fast as we can with liquidity": the cash return is being pre-funded before completion, a sign of confidence in the deal but also a modest leverage step-up while the regulatory review runs.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning (pivoting). ITV is converting itself from a UK advertising company into a standalone global production company, with a cash return as the bridge.

The single most important thing to weigh: the value case leans on roughly 25p a share of cash that only arrives if the Sky deal completes, and since 2026-11-04 that completion runs through a politically supervised review (CMA plus Ofcom, reports due 2027-01-27, then a ministerial decision on whether to refer to a deeper probe). Without the deal, the shareholder owns a narrow-moat studio plus a shrinking linear broadcaster.

Moat: the moat type is intangible (a library of returnable formats such as Love Island in 28 markets, Line of Duty, Hell's Kitchen) plus scale in distribution. It is narrow rather than wide: returns are respectable (ROIC 12.6%, ROE 19.1%) but Studios margins have drifted down and the business is hit-driven. The trend is stable rather than eroding at the Studios level. The secular threat is material, not terminal: linear advertising is in structural decline, but that business is being sold, and the residual studio sells to the streamers that drive the decline. The cheapness is therefore partly a fear print (regulatory delay and UK advertising cyclicality) rather than a structurally shrinking base, provided the sale completes.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

picks.bull_thesis: TF1 is France's dominant commercial broadcaster, reaching about half the country every day, with an all-time-high 36.9% audience share among women under 50 in September 2026 and a 2-point gain in linear advertising market share after the World Cup. The Netflix distribution deal (live since late June 2026) re-accelerated TF1+ advertising growth to 20.5% in the third quarter, and management says the Netflix contribution will rise in the fourth quarter and in 2027 as ad load and pricing close the gap. Earnings per share has fallen from EUR 0.97 (2024) to about EUR 0.59 on a trailing basis, and free cash flow after working capital was EUR 16M over nine months (negative about EUR 41M in the third quarter) against a EUR 132M dividend, so the 'growing dividend' is being funded from the cash pile. If the margin settles near 6% and earnings drift to about EUR 0.40 a share at a 7x multiple, plus a reduced cash pile of about EUR 1.5 a share, the shares are worth about EUR 4.3.
picks.consensus_delta: Little disagreement with the market. The shares at EUR 6.09 already price a shrinking business; our fair value of EUR 6.75 is only about 11% higher. Where the market may be too generous is dividend safety: at nine months free cash flow after working capital covered about one-eighth of the dividend, so the 'growing dividend' depends on running down net cash.
picks.valley_of_death: Next 3-9 months: fourth-quarter 2026 advertising (management says October improved only slightly), the full-year results and dividend decision around February 2027, and a 2027 presidential campaign that shifts prime time to lower-yielding news. A flat or cut dividend would hit the yield-holder base.
picks.positioning_washout: Some forced-selling pressure is possible if the dividend is held flat or cut in February 2027, since part of the holder base owns TF1 for its yield; parent Bouygues holds a controlling stake, so free float is limited. No identified index deletion or lock-up.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. The thesis has broken: the case needed TF1's earnings to stabilise, and the nine-month results on 29 October 2026 show they are still falling - margin from activities 7.6% against 10.9% a year ago, advertising revenue down 9%, and free cash flow of only EUR 16M over nine months against a EUR 132M dividend. TF1+ streaming growth re-accelerated to about 20% on the Netflix partnership and the balance sheet holds EUR 382M of net cash (about EUR 1.82 a share), which is why the downside is not catastrophic, but management sees no improvement in 2027. At EUR 6.09 the shares sit only about 11% below our EUR 6.75 fair value, against roughly 29% downside to EUR 4.30, and the discount to peers is shared sector exposure rather than a company-specific edge. This continues the committee's earlier answer; nothing dated has changed it.
picks.forcing_function: No firm re-rating trigger. The next dated checkpoints are the full-year 2026 results and dividend proposal (about mid-February 2027) and the pace of Netflix monetisation through 2027.

# TF1 Group (TFI.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup
*Transcripts reviewed: 9M-2025 (2025-10-30), FY-2025 (2026-02-12), H1-2026 (2026-07-30), 9M-2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: EUR 6.09 (Euronext Paris, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
A year ago (2025-10-30) the story was "resilience": revenue stable, operating margin held near 11%, market-share gains in a falling linear advertising market, and TF1+ (the free streaming platform) growing advertising revenue about 41%. By the full-year call (2026-02-12) the frame was "the second phase of the strategic plan" - micro-payments, the Netflix distribution deal, and French-speaking international expansion - while advertising revenue was already down 4% for 2025. By H1-2026 (2026-07-30) the story had turned defensive: the margin target was cut to "mid- to high single-digit", and net profit roughly halved. The 9M-2026 call (2026-10-29) is a "we are on the road map" call: margin from activities (current operating profit before one-offs, divided by revenue) of 7.6% versus 10.9% a year earlier, advertising revenue down 9%, and the growth vocabulary now leans almost entirely on the Netflix partnership, the small-business ad platform and micro-payments.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong double-digit digital growth" | TF1+ ad revenue +19% over 9M-2026 (EUR 160M), +20.5% in Q3; total digital EUR 198M (+17%) | Delivered, but growth has halved from ~40% in 2025 |
| Digital offsets linear decline | Group advertising revenue EUR 1.0B, down 9% (about EUR 100M lost) versus roughly EUR 30M digital gain | Not true - the gap widened |
| Cost discipline protects margin | Programming costs down EUR 44M; margin still 7.6% vs 10.9% | Partial - costs cut, margin still fell about 3.3 points |
| "Very solid" balance sheet | Net cash EUR 382M at 2026-09-30 (EUR 587M cash vs EUR 207M debt at 2026-06-30) | True - the one clean pillar |
| "Growing dividend policy" | Dividend EUR 132M paid April 2026; free cash flow after working capital only EUR 16M over 9M-2026 (EUR 57M in H1, so Q3 was about minus EUR 41M) | Dividend is being paid out of the cash pile, not out of earnings |
| Earnings trajectory | EPS 0.97 (2024) to 0.72 (2025) to trailing 0.59; latest quarter EPS down 27% y/y | Decline is accelerating, not stabilising |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Declining. 2025-10-30: "successfully managed to mitigate" ad headwinds. 2026-02-12: offensive, with return-on-investment slides for advertisers. 2026-07-30: defensive, margin guidance cut. 2026-10-29: "visibility remaining limited", the market forecast of minus 6% "now seems slightly optimistic", and for 2027 "we see no near-term prospects for improvement in the macroeconomic and political environment or any reduction in the regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms." That last sentence is the most candid management has been in two years.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium. 2025 margin guidance was cut in October 2025 (from "broadly stable" to 10.5-11.5%) and then met at 11%. 2026 guidance was cut at H1 to mid- to high single-digit and is being met (7.6% at nine months). Management meets reset guidance; it does not forecast the down-leg well. The 9M-2026 results came in slightly above company-compiled consensus on revenue and margin.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Very thin coverage on the calls - the 9M-2026 call had only written questions from one broker (CIC). The questions were October/Q4 ad trends, 2027 visibility, the presidential election, Netflix monetisation, and programming costs. Management declined to give a programming-cost range and said Netflix revenue is ramping "more gradually than the audience" because ad load and CPM (price per thousand ad views) on Netflix are below TF1+ levels. Nobody asked about dividend cover, which is the real pressure point.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: dividend (EUR 132M) is about eight times nine-month free cash flow after working capital (EUR 16M) - 9M-2026.
- Red: advertising revenue down 9% with management saying the market has "deteriorated further" since May - 9M-2026.
- Red: no improvement seen for 2027; the 2027 presidential election likely reduces prime-time ad inventory - 9M-2026.
- Red: Studio TF1 operating profit down EUR 14M over nine months - 9M-2026.
- Green: audience share at an all-time high of 36.9% among women under 50 in September 2026, and linear ad market share up about 2 points in August-September - 9M-2026.
- Green: Netflix partnership "ahead of our expectations" on audience; TF1+ growth re-accelerated to 20.5% in Q3 - 9M-2026.
- Green: net cash of EUR 382M is roughly 30% of the market value.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The language moved from "gain market share" (a sign of strength in a stable market) to "regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms" - an admission that the problem is structural, not cyclical. Disclosure has shifted toward audience and usage metrics (streamers, transactions) and away from digital revenue per user. The micro-payment figures (about 2 million transactions year to date) are small in euros; their prominence on the call is a sign of how few growth levers remain.

## 8. BOTTOM LINE
A well-run, market-leading broadcaster in a shrinking market. Management executes against reset targets, keeps a strong net cash position, and is honest about 2027. But the earnings base is still falling, digital growth is not filling the linear hole, and the dividend now relies on the balance sheet.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory declining · a moat that is being eroded.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Imperial Brands (IMB.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Prices are in pence (GBp) on the London listing. Sources: the earnings-call transcripts bundled for this run (half-year and full-year calls of May 2021, November 2021, May 2022, November 2025 and the half-year call of 12 May 2026), the screener's financial block, the company's pre-close trading update of 8 October 2026 (verified through secondary reports), the half-year results announcement of 12 May 2026 and the total-voting-rights notice of 3 August 2026 (as checked by our independent reviewer), and the live quote of 2,977p (16 November 2026, paid market-data feed). Full-year results for the year to 30 September 2026 are due tomorrow, 17 November 2026 (company earnings calendar via the paid data feed; also reported by Boerse-Global).*

**Takeaway.** Imperial is a cash machine on a slowly shrinking volume base that has, for five years, done what it said it would do on profit, cash and returns. The story has narrowed from "transform the company" to "price, cut costs and buy back stock", which is less exciting but more credible. Nothing new about the business has been published since our last look on 19 October 2026; the shares have simply kept rising, from 2,826p then to 2,977p today (up about 5%, and about 22% above the 2,443p of 2 October). The setup is now almost entirely about price.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **2021-2022 (Stefan Bomhard's five-year plan).** A turnaround story: stop losing share in the five priority markets (the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Spain and Australia), and rebuild next-generation products (heated tobacco, vapes and nicotine pouches). In May 2022 he said the plan "to transform Imperial is fully on track" and that targeted investment had "improved aggregate market share in our top 5 markets".
- **November 2025 (new chief executive Lukas Paravicini, previously the finance chief).** Results slightly ahead of guidance: adjusted operating profit up 4.6%, free cash flow of about 2.7 billion pounds, leverage (net debt divided by cash earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) of 2.0 times, and more than 2.7 billion pounds of capital returns promised for the 2026 financial year. The new frame is Evolve 2030: at least 320 million pounds of savings by 2030 and disciplined spending on new products.
- **12 May 2026 (half-year).** Defensive. Group adjusted operating profit grew only 0.6%. Paravicini conceded that aggregate share in the five priority markets "is lower", calling it "a deliberate choice to prioritize value over low return volume"; growth in new products ran below the double-digit full-year guide because of United States promotion timing; Australian volumes fell about 50% after an excise change; the company exited United States vapes. Finance chief Murray McGowan stressed 2.6 billion pounds of rolling twelve-month free cash flow and a second-half weighting.
- **8 October 2026 (pre-close trading update).** On track for every full-year metric (operating profit growth of 3-5%, high-single-digit adjusted earnings-per-share growth, free cash flow of at least 2.2 billion pounds), tobacco revenue up a sixth straight year, new products back to double-digit growth, the 1.45 billion pound buyback completed and a 1.5 billion pound programme announced for the 2027 financial year.

The arc: the grand transformation has contracted into a self-help-and-capital-returns story. A smaller ambition, but the one the numbers support.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Stabilised the core" (2021-2022) | Revenue 32.79bn (2021) to 32.17bn (2025), about -0.4% a year over three years; gross margin steady near 22% | Holds: flat, not growing, but steady |
| Pricing outruns volume (every call) | Half-year 2026 pricing of 6% in Europe and 5.7% in the United States against low-single-digit volume declines; tobacco revenue up a sixth year (8 Oct 2026) | Holds |
| Strong cash, 90-100% conversion | 2025 free cash flow about 2.7bn; company rolling figure 2.6bn at March 2026; 2026 guide at least 2.2bn. The scan's "trailing free cash flow 5.70bn" and "trailing earnings per share 6.65" conflict with the company's own figures and look like data artefacts | Holds on the company's figures |
| Earnings growth "high single digit" | Reported earnings per share swings (2.99 in 2021, 1.65 in 2022, 2.49 in 2025) on impairments and one-offs; adjusted earnings compound via the buyback | Holds on an adjusted basis; reported earnings are noisy |
| Leverage at the low end of 2.0-2.5 times | 2.0 times at September 2025; 2.4 times at March 2026 (seasonal). Adjusted net debt 10.52bn and reported net debt 10.94bn at 31 March 2026 (half-year announcement); our scan's 10.73bn including leases sits between the two | Holds, but capital returns exceed free cash flow |
| New products will grow double digits | Below guide at the half; back to double digits per 8 Oct 2026 | Delivered late, still loss-making outside Europe |

The widest gap between story and numbers remains new products: years of investment have produced growth but not group-level profit.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a defensive dip in May 2026 and a recovery in October.** In 2021-2022 the language was offensive ("acceleration", "rebooting" new products). By November 2025 it was confident but financial. In May 2026 it turned defensive: one-off slides, "we are on track" repeated, and the market-share decline pre-empted ("I recognize that at the half year point, the 2 numbers on the left will be a focus"). The October 2026 update restored a confident register without new promises.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High.** Each full year in the transcripts was delivered in line or slightly ahead (2021, 2022, and 2025 at 4.6% profit growth against a 3-5% guide). The 2026 guide was reaffirmed in May and again on 8 October despite a 0.6% first half; the screener shows 5 of the last 7 periods beating estimates. There is a mild pattern of setting guides where the pricing lever can hit them. The final test is tomorrow's results (17 November 2026), where the consensus earnings estimate for the second half is about 1.94 pounds a share (paid data feed).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Priority-market share.** Repeatedly questioned; management argues it trades share for price. The first-half 2026 decline (16 basis points in aggregate, per the half-year announcement) is small but is the clearest sign the moat is narrowing.
- **New-product economics.** Analysts push on when it turns profitable; answers stay qualitative beyond Europe's first profitable half.
- **Cash versus returns.** 2026 returns (more than 2.7bn) exceed guided free cash flow (at least 2.2bn), and the 2027 buyback repeats the pattern; management answers with "evergreen" buyback language rather than a leverage bridge.
- **Australia.** Volumes down about 50%; management stresses it is a small share of revenue and will annualise.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Share loss in the five priority markets in the first half of 2026 after years of "stabilisation" claims (12 May 2026).
- 🔴 Capital returns above free cash flow, funded from the balance sheet, while UK long gilt yields are high and income stocks compete with them.
- 🔴 New products still loss-making at group level after five years of investment (every call); exit from United States vapes (May 2026).
- 🔴 Reported earnings are noisy (2022 fell to 1.65 from 2.99) - investors must rely on adjusted figures.
- 🟢 Pricing outran volume in every region outside Australia (May 2026) and tobacco revenue grew for a sixth year (October 2026).
- 🟢 Guidance met or beaten every year in the record, and reaffirmed into the year-end (8 October 2026).
- 🟢 Buyback renewed and enlarged to 1.5bn for the 2027 financial year (8 October 2026), about 7% of today's market value.
- 🟢 Litigation with R J Reynolds settled (half-year 2026: 150 million pounds paid, 162 million pounds over three years) - immaterial and already sunk.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary moved from "transformation" and "acceleration" (2021-2022) to "savings", "discipline", "value over volume" and "evergreen buyback" (2025-2026): a company now run for cash.
- The new chief executive was the long-standing finance chief and the new finance chief speaks almost only in cash and leverage terms; the refusal to chase pouch economics at any price signals restraint, not ambition.
- The decision to exit United States vapes and focus on "modern oral" (pouches) narrows the new-product bet to where Imperial is a small player against Philip Morris's Zyn.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning** - from a growth narrative to a harvest-and-return model under a new leadership team, now credible after the October update.

The single most important thing to weigh: **the price has run ahead of the evidence.** The shares are up about 22% since 2 October 2026 on an update that confirmed what was already guided; at 2,977p they sit only about 4% below our fair value of about 3,100p. Tomorrow's results should confirm the year; the open questions are the 2027 outlook, priority-market share and where leverage lands.

**Moat.** Intangible brands plus regulatory licence and scale in distribution (it consolidates 50.01% of Logista, the Spanish-listed distributor). Returns are solid (return on invested capital 14.2%, return on equity 41% on a thin equity base) and gross margin is stable, but priority-market share slipped in the first half of 2026 and volumes decline every year. That is a narrow moat whose trend is eroding slowly, not a wide one.

**Secular threat.** The shift of nicotine consumption to reduced-risk products, where Imperial is the weakest of the four majors. That is a material, slow threat to terminal value rather than a terminal one: combustible pricing has outrun volume decline for decades and the cash is real. The cheapness is mostly a fear-print about rates and the category, not a melting base - but the base is shrinking, which is why part of the discount to peers is deserved.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.
