# Upbound Group (UPBD): a deep dive on management and the setup
*Five earnings calls, Q3 2025 (2025-10-30) to Q3 2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: $22.84 (NASDAQ, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

Upbound is the parent of Rent-A-Center (about 1,500+ corporate stores that rent furniture, appliances and electronics on a lease-to-own basis), Acima (the same lease-to-own product embedded at third-party retailers' checkouts and online) and Brigit (a subscription app that offers small cash advances, called earned-wage access, plus credit-building tools). The screener tags it as software. It is not software. It is a lender to subprime consumers, and its economics are driven by the losses it takes on leases. Read it that way.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

**The story shrank from growth to underwriting discipline, and that change worked.**

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-30):** management said Acima was "on track to deliver high single digits to low double-digit GMV growth" (GMV is gross merchandise volume, the dollar value of new leases written). The same call conceded that some 2025 lease cohorts were going bad. Lease charge-offs rose 50 basis points, the company tightened approvals "each month", and it warned that losses would peak in Q4 2025.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-19):** the framing became about getting back to normal. Management guided Acima losses to "that 9.5% range" for 2026 and said the most recent cohorts were "much more in line with historical years".
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-30):** charge-offs fell to about 8.8%, a 130 basis-point improvement from Q4. GMV came in "below our expectations", lower than a year earlier. Growth was now explicitly second to portfolio health.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-30):** management said it was "trading risk-adjusted margin for volume". The loss guide was cut to "around 9%, if not below 9%" and Acima's EBITDA margin passed 16%. The quarter also included a disclosed ~$13M fraud loss at Acima.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-29):** the story is now about profit and cash. Charge-offs were 8.7%, "the lowest level since stimulus in 2021". Acima GMV was down 11% year over year. Free cash flow was $121M in the quarter and net leverage was 2.4x. The company announced a $50M buyback "this quarter" and created a new chief operating officer role. It also guided Q4 GMV to "relatively flat", which would end three quarters of decline.

The growth drivers the company added along the way have held up: Brigit (paying users up 27% to 1.84M, revenue up 37%), an Experian distribution deal for Brigit, a Boost Mobile point-of-sale integration across about 5,000 stores, and an Amazon pickup partnership adding about 50 visits per store per week at Rent-A-Center. The Acima growth claim of 2025 was quietly dropped.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Losses would peak in Q4 2025 and normalize | Charge-offs went from ~10% (Q4 2025) to 8.8% (Q1), 8.8% (Q2) and 8.7% (Q3 2026) | Delivered |
| Q3 2026 beat guidance | Non-GAAP EPS $1.01 against a $0.85-0.95 guide; adjusted EBITDA $123M against $105-115M; revenue $1.15B at the top of the $1.05-1.15B range | Delivered (beat 7 of 7 quarters per the screener) |
| "Significant free cash flow" | TTM free cash flow $481M; Q3 FCF $121M, more than double the prior year | True, but flattered (see below) |
| Deleveraging toward the 2x target | Net leverage 2.4x; balance-sheet net debt $1.51B including leases, about $1.22B excluding leases | Delivered |
| Profit growth | GAAP diluted EPS: Q3 2026 $0.58 vs $0.22 a year earlier; TTM $1.90 vs FY2025 $1.25 | Real recovery from a weak base |
| Growth | Revenue down 1.6% y/y in Q3 ($1.146B vs $1.165B); Acima GMV down 11% | Revenue is flat to shrinking |

**Two forensic cautions.**
1. **Cash flow is flattered by shrinkage.** The CFO said cash flow was strong "partly due to some of the softness that we've seen on the top line and a reduction of overall working capital." A lease-to-own company buys inventory to lease out, so writing fewer leases releases cash. The $481M TTM free cash flow is not a run-rate. The FY2026 free-cash-flow guide is about $250M, after "substantial legal payments" tied to a multi-state attorney-general investigation. When GMV grows again, the company has to reinvest in inventory, and free cash flow will fall back toward its reported earnings.
2. **Non-GAAP and GAAP earnings are far apart.** Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $1.01 and GAAP was $0.58. The FY2026 non-GAAP guide is $4.00-4.35, while TTM GAAP EPS is $1.90. The gap is mostly amortization of intangibles from the Acima and Brigit acquisitions, which is a real non-cash charge to exclude. But it also removes stock compensation and recurring legal and regulatory charges, which are real costs in this industry. Our estimate of earnings power sits between the two: about $3.50 per share.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Rising, from defensive to confident.**
- Q3 2025: on the back foot, explaining bad cohorts ("softness in recent vintages").
- Q4 2025 and Q1 2026: steadier. "Validates the data-driven approach."
- Q2 2026: confident on credit and frank about volume ("trading risk-adjusted margin for volume").
- Q3 2026: offensive again. "Bullish on the holiday season", a buyback, new hires in leadership, and "flexibility to adjust that lever" (loosening underwriting). It is still careful about the consumer: "cautious around where the consumer is going to spend."

Guidance has become more specific over time, with quarterly ranges and named loss-rate targets. That is a good sign.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The loss-rate path was called correctly three quarters ahead. Q3 2026 beat the top of every range. Full-year non-GAAP EPS of $4.00-4.35 was reaffirmed on 2026-07-30, and the free-cash-flow guide was raised to about $250M. The one large miss was the Acima volume promise from 2025 (high single to low double-digit growth), which turned into an 11% decline. That miss was a choice made for credit reasons, not a forecasting failure. The guidance ranges have been wide enough to beat, which looks like mild sandbagging (setting targets low enough to clear). **Reliability: High on profit and credit, Medium on volume.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Volume:** analysts keep asking when GMV turns. The answer has moved from "growth" (2025) to "flat in Q4" (2026-10-29). This is the open question.
- **Cash conversion:** Bank of America asked on 2026-10-29 about the gap between $400M of operating cash flow and $250M of free cash flow. The answer was the attorney-general legal payments, and no amount was given. The size of that settlement is a real, unquantified liability.
- **Capital allocation after Brigit:** management said it is "not being proactive at this point around M&A", which is reassuring.
- **What analysts are not pushing on:** regulation of earned-wage access at Brigit, and the 2026-10-01 data-breach class-action investigation (Ademi LLP). Neither came up on the call.
- **Coverage is thin:** one price target in the last year ($28, 2026-07-31).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Green: lease charge-offs at 8.7% in Q3 2026, the best since 2021, after a correctly forecast peak in Q4 2025.
- Green: Acima adjusted EBITDA up 15% in Q3 2026 with margin up ~270 basis points to 14.7%.
- Green: Brigit revenue up 37% and EBITDA up 59% in Q3 2026. This is the growth asset.
- Green: net leverage 2.4x heading to 2x. A $50M buyback (about 4% of market cap) was announced 2026-10-29. The $0.39 quarterly dividend was maintained (declared 2026-09-24). Insiders made 8 open-market buys against 1 sale.
- Red: Acima GMV down 11% (Q3 2026), and consolidated revenue is down year over year. The lease book is shrinking.
- Red: an attorney-general investigation with "substantial" payments of undisclosed size (2026-10-29), plus a data-breach claims investigation (2026-10-01).
- Red: a ~$13M fraud loss at Acima in Q2 2026.
- Red: the core customer is squeezed by groceries, rent, utilities and gas (CEO, 2026-10-29). Gross margin has fallen from 61.6% (2019) to about 48-51% today, partly because Acima's business mix carries lower margins.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Underwriting capabilities are our core strength" (Q3 2026) shows the company now presents itself as a credit-risk manager rather than a retailer, which fits the peer set.
- A newly created chief operating officer role "unify[ing] business segments under a single leader" (2026-09-22) points to cost and integration work across the three brands. Overlap between the brands is only 10-15% today.
- AI comes up more often (about half of code changes "involve AI assistance"). This is efficiency talk, not a revenue claim.
- The buyback "coming out of blackout" signals that management thinks the stock is cheap at around $20.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Credit, margins, leverage and cash returns have all improved for three straight quarters, and management has delivered on its guidance.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing:** the stock is cheap on earnings (about 5.4x the FY2026 non-GAAP EPS guide midpoint, a 6.8% dividend yield) and expensive on growth (the lease book is shrinking). Today's free cash flow partly comes from that shrinkage, and it is reduced by an unquantified attorney-general settlement. Underwrite earnings power of about $3.50 per share, not the $481M TTM free cash flow.

**Moat:** narrow. It rests on scale and cost, plus underwriting data built from decades of subprime lease outcomes and an embedded merchant network (Acima at checkout, Boost Mobile, Amazon pickup). Returns are low (ROIC about 4.6%, ROE about 11.6%) but recovering, not falling, so the moat is stable rather than eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Buy-now-pay-later lenders and the shift of retail to e-commerce pressure the store-based Rent-A-Center, but Acima already sits on the e-commerce and virtual channel and Rent-A-Center same-store sales have grown for four quarters. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear of subprime credit plus a regulatory overhang, not a structurally shrinking base. The risk is consumer-cycle risk, not terminal risk.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: The bull case is that Jungheinrich, the number-two European maker of forklifts and warehouse equipment, is being priced as if a cyclical trough were permanent. The nine-month statement of 10 November 2026 shows the bottom forming rather than deepening: orders rose 6.0% to 4,323 million euros, the reported operating margin recovered to 5.9% from 4.0% a year earlier as one-off costs fell from 162.9 million to 36.5 million, and management confirmed its 2026 forecast of 340-400 million euros of operating profit for the second time instead of cutting again. Growth is coming from the right place: automation orders rose about 20% to 878 million euros, a structurally growing business. Gross margin has held near 32% for years and rose through the 2021-22 inflation (29.1% to 30.9%), which says the product still carries pricing power. The balance sheet is roughly neutral (cash of 723 million against debt of 701 million at 30 June 2026), so there is no financing threat. The new 2030 target of an 8-9% margin, though lower than before, is what a recovery from today's 6-7% looks like, and Bernstein's Philippe Lorrain called the reset a de-risking step that could bring in long-term holders (10 November 2026). At 23.24 euros the shares trade near book value and at roughly 9-10 times a normalised 2.40-2.60 euros of earnings; if the margin returns to around 8% on about 5.9 billion euros of revenue, sum-of-the-parts value is near 35 euros. Conditions: the fourth quarter delivers the forecast and turns cash positive, European demand stops falling, and the regulator's review closes without a finding.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the screen is cheap for reasons that do not survive inspection, and that 10 November 2026 made two of them worse. First, cash: nine-month free cash flow was minus 106 million euros against plus 151 million a year earlier, so the 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow multiple rests on 2025 cash the business is not repeating; the full-year guide of above 50 million now needs roughly 156 million or more in the fourth quarter alone. Second, ambition: management cut its 2030 margin target to 8-9% from about 10%, which confirms the margin erosion visible in the numbers (adjusted 6.8% for nine months against 8.1% a year earlier; the third quarter on reported figures derives to about 5.4%, about 76 million on about 1.40 billion, using FMP's half-year operating profit of 165.8 million; one press report gives about 97 million for the quarter, which we cannot reconcile and may be adjusted). Third-quarter orders grew only 2.6%, slightly below expectations, and growth is concentrated in the smaller, lumpier automation business while the core truck business saw revenue fall 1.8% under Chinese price competition and high rates. Return on invested capital of about 5.8% is below the cost of capital. The effective tax rate was about 45% in the first half (59.0 million on 132.2 million of pre-tax profit). The German financial regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts, opened 21 July 2026 and tied to the Russia disposal, is still open with no timetable; a finding would undercut the argument that recent charges were one-off. The March 2026 forecast lasted four months, and only two of the last five quarters beat. The listed preference shares carry no vote, so no activist or bid can force value out. What would confirm it: a fourth quarter that misses the forecast or the cash guide (full-year results, late March 2027), a regulator finding, or a dividend cut that pushes income holders out.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrow. The street is pricing a long trough in European forklifts (Bank of America's 8 October 2026 underperform call, target 21 euros) and the shares sit about a third below where they started 2026. We think the market is roughly right on timing but slightly too pessimistic on the mid-cycle margin: the confirmed 2026 forecast, the 6.8% adjusted nine-month margin and management's own 8-9% 2030 target all point to a mid-cycle near or above 7%, which supports about 26 euros of value. But the gap is not large at 23.24 euros, and the market has a point on cash: a 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow screen is built on 2025, and nine-month 2026 free cash flow is minus 106 million euros. Nothing here is a terminal-decline pricing error large enough to buy today.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) runs to the full-year results in late March 2027. Three things can hurt before value converges: (1) the fourth quarter must deliver roughly 98-158 million euros of operating profit and about 156 million or more of free cash flow to meet the guide - a miss on cash would expose the low price-to-cash-flow screen as an artifact; (2) the regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts can publish a finding at any time with no notice; (3) European capital-spending demand under positive real rates and Chinese price competition in standard trucks can keep the core truck business shrinking (nine-month revenue there down 1.8%). There is no debt wall: cash of 723 million roughly matches debt of 701 million at 30 June 2026.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is modest. The preference shares carry no vote, so the holder base is income and value funds plus index holders (the shares are in the SDAX). A dividend cut in spring 2027 after a year of reported earnings well below 2024 could push income holders out, and the sector-wide selling seen in October 2026 (Bank of America's call covering KION too) is the most likely route to our 19.00 euro level. We see no index deletion, lock-up or spin-off dumping in prospect.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 19.00 euros, which a renewed sector-wide sell-off in European forklift makers could deliver.

The thesis holds. Today's nine-month statement (10 November 2026) confirmed the 2026 forecast instead of cutting it again, orders are up 6% and one-off costs have fallen sharply, so this still looks like a decent business in a cyclical trough rather than a broken one. But the statement did not deliver what we said would make us buy earlier: the adjusted margin was 6.8%, not above 7%, free cash flow was minus 106 million euros for nine months against plus 151 million a year earlier, and management lowered its 2030 margin goal to 8-9% from about 10%.

We trim fair value to 26.08 euros from 26.57: the core business at a mid-cycle 7.25% margin and eight times operating profit, the leasing arm near its estimated equity, less about 270 million euros of net debt once this year's cash outflow is counted. At 23.24 euros (Xetra, 10 November 2026) the discount is only about a tenth, short of the one-fifth this book requires, and the downside to our 16.53 euro adverse case is larger than the upside. At 19.00 euros the discount to fair value is well over a third and the remaining downside small, which is the asymmetry we want.

Conviction stays at a moderate 3, inherited from our last answer because no dated fact cleared an upgrade or broke the thesis: a narrow-moat number-two franchise whose margins and returns are eroding, with an open regulator review, a 45% tax rate and a guidance record that needed a cut in July. The value case alone also rates 3, capped by the eroding moat. We would move before 19.00 euros only on a dated fact: a fourth quarter that meets the forecast and the cash guide (late March 2027), or a clean close of the regulator's review.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard dated event that forces a re-rating. The candidates are routine: full-year 2026 results in late March 2027 (proof of fourth-quarter cash and the 2026 forecast met), and the close of the regulator's review (no date). The founding families control the vote, so no activist, tender or buyback campaign can be forced. The re-rating, if it comes, is a slow margin and cash recovery.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Jungheinrich AG (preference shares, Xetra JUN3.DE) - deep dive on management and the setup

As of 10 November 2026. No earnings-call transcript was available from FMP for this listing, and none could be found on the web for the nine-month statement published today. This dossier therefore reasons from the company's dated releases (first quarter, 23 July 2026 forecast cut, half-year report of 11 August 2026, nine-month statement of 10 November 2026, as reported in the press), the FMP quarterly statements and our screener figures. No management quotes are given because none could be sourced; where we derive a figure, we say so.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from growth ambition to damage control and back to a cautious "trough, then recovery" message.

- Early 2026: the company opened the year with a forecast it had to cut four months later. The first quarter was weak: operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and taxes) fell to 56.5 million euros from 104.5 million a year earlier, hit by a strike at the Lueneburg plant and price competition.
- 23 July 2026: an ad-hoc notice (a mandatory market announcement) revised the full-year forecast for the Industrial Trucks and Services segment and the group to EBIT of 340 to 400 million euros (a 6.2% to 7.0% margin, including about 40 million euros of one-off costs).
- 11 August 2026: the half-year report showed orders up about 8%, revenue flat at 2,669 million euros, and a group margin near 6.2%.
- 10 November 2026: the nine-month statement held the 2026 forecast, showed orders up 6.0% to 4,323 million euros, revenue up 1.5% to 4,068 million euros, and reported EBIT of 241.8 million euros (5.9% margin, against 4.0% a year earlier when one-offs were far larger). Adjusted for 36.5 million euros of one-offs, EBIT was 278.3 million euros, a 6.8% margin, down from 8.1% a year earlier. At the same time the company reset its long-term plan: the 2030 targets are now 7 to 8 billion euros of revenue and an 8% to 9% EBIT margin, down from roughly 10 billion euros and about 10% per a German trade report.

The quiet change is the long-term ambition. A 10% margin business has become an 8-9% margin business by the end of the decade, which matters more for the upside than for the downside.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / implied claim | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 forecast (EBIT 340-400m) is achievable | Nine-month reported EBIT 241.8m; Q4 must deliver about 98-158m. Q4 2025 delivered 131.6m reported (FMP). | Plausible at the low-to-mid end. |
| Margins recover from the trough | Adjusted nine-month margin 6.8% vs 8.1% a year earlier. Reported third quarter derived at about 76m on about 1.40bn (about 5.4%), using FMP's 165.8m half-year EBIT; one press report gives about 97m for the quarter, which may be an adjusted figure - we could not reconcile the two. | No clear recovery yet; flat at best. |
| Orders signal demand turning | Orders +6.0% for nine months, but the third quarter alone only +2.6% to just under 1.4bn, slightly below expectations. Automation orders +19.9% to 878m; core trucks +3.5%. | Real but slowing; growth comes from the smaller automation arm. |
| Cash generation (free cash flow above 50m for the year) | Nine-month free cash flow minus 106m euros vs plus 151m a year earlier. Q4 must produce roughly 156m+ to hit the guide. | The weakest link. The screener's 6.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow rests on 2025 cash that 2026 is not repeating. |
| Gross margin stability | Gross margin about 32.6% in the first half (870m on 2,669m); screen shows 32.2% stable; held through the 2021-22 inflation (29.1% to 30.9%). | Corroborated - pricing power on the product is intact. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining through July, stabilising since. The 23 July cut was defensive; the November release is cautious-steady (forecast held, long-term targets lowered to something believable). Bernstein's Philippe Lorrain called the lower targets a risk-reduction step that could attract long-term investors (as reported 10 November 2026). We rate the trajectory as still deteriorating on substance (lower long-term margins, negative cash flow) even as the tone has steadied.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-low. The March 2026 forecast lasted four months. The screener shows beats in only 2 of the last 5 quarters and earnings per share down 64% in 2025. The revised July forecast has now been confirmed once (10 November). The 2030 reset is a second admission that earlier ambition was too high. Reliability: Low-to-Medium, improving only if Q4 lands inside the range and cash turns positive.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without a transcript we can only infer the questions: (a) why free cash flow swung to minus 106m and whether the full-year cash guide is still realistic; (b) how much of the margin gap is Chinese price competition (structural) versus volume (cyclical); (c) the German financial regulator's review of the 30 June 2025 accounts tied to the Russia disposal, opened 21 July 2026, for which we found no update; (d) the 45%-plus effective tax rate in the first half (59.0m of tax on 132.2m of pre-tax profit, FMP).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: nine-month free cash flow minus 106m (10 Nov 2026) against a full-year guide above 50m.
- Red: 2030 margin target cut to 8-9% from about 10% (10 Nov 2026).
- Red: adjusted margin 6.8% vs 8.1% a year earlier; third-quarter orders slightly below expectations.
- Red: regulator review of the June 2025 accounts still open (since 21 July 2026, no result found).
- Red: effective tax rate near 45% in the first half of 2026.
- Green: 2026 forecast confirmed on 10 November 2026, no second cut.
- Green: orders up 6% for nine months; automation orders up about 20%.
- Green: one-off costs fell to 36.5m from 162.9m a year earlier; reported margin up to 5.9% from 4.0%.
- Green: gross margin steady near 32%; balance sheet roughly neutral (cash 723m vs debt 701m at 30 June 2026 per FMP).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The target reset is the main signal: management is now anchoring the market to a lower, more achievable margin path, which removes a source of future disappointment but also caps the long-term upside the bull case used to lean on. Growth is migrating to automation, a more competitive and project-lumpy business. The listed preference shares carry no vote; control sits with the founding families, so no activist or bid can force value out.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT

Trajectory: DETERIORATING on substance (lower long-term margins, cash outflow this year), with a stabilising tone. The single most important thing for the director: whether the fourth quarter turns cash positive enough to meet the above-50m free-cash-flow guide - that decides whether the low price-to-cash-flow screen is real or a 2025 artifact.

Moat: a narrow but real moat from scale, a dense direct sales-and-service network and a large leasing and rental fleet that ties customers in (switching costs on service). Width is narrowing: return on invested capital about 5.8% is below the cost of capital, the margin has slid from about 8% to 6-7%, and management has cut its own end-of-decade margin target. That is an eroding moat trend, though from a cyclical trough rather than a collapse. Secular threat: Chinese low-price competition in standard trucks is a material but manageable pressure, not a terminal one - warehouse automation is a growth adjacency the company is winning in. The cheapness is mostly a cyclical fear print, with a real structural element on margins.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Centrica is Britain's largest household energy supplier, trading in London at 156.20 pence on 16 November 2026, about 12% below its 200-day average and in the lower quarter of its 52-week range (144p to 220p), with net cash (about 709 million pounds adjusted, 30 June 2026). The anchor is the 9 July 2026 Sizewell B agreement: a 20-year regulated contract at 70.50 pounds per megawatt-hour in 2025 money, rising with inflation and extending the plant to 2055, for a small capital share funded from the nuclear partnership's own cash. That turns a merchant cash stream with a hard stop into a long inflation-linked annuity, which is worth more while inflation runs above 3%. The older nuclear fleet was extended to 2030 (22 July 2026), and the company has bought the flexible assets a renewables-heavy grid lacks: the Severn gas plant, half of the Grain LNG terminal, batteries and solar. Earnings beat estimates in 6 of the last 7 quarters, and gross margin is 38.7% and rising. picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is not that Centrica is a bad company; it is that the balance-sheet strength the value argument rests on is being spent, and the earnings the low multiple is built on are not backed by cash. The company's own interim release (23 July 2026) shows a 570 million pound free cash outflow in the first half of 2026 and adjusted net cash down to 709 million pounds, from 1.5 billion at the end of 2025 and about 2.5 billion a year earlier, while the interim dividend was raised to 2.0 pence (paid 22 September 2026) and large nuclear equity commitments remain to be funded. The screener's 328 million pounds of trailing free cash flow, and the 24 times price-to-free-cash-flow multiple built on it, do not reconcile with that statement. Retail is guided to the lower end of its 500 to 800 million pound core-profit range, the 2027 trading outlook was lowered to about 250 million pounds, and household bad debt runs above the regulator's allowance (above 4% of revenue against 3.8%, per Jefferies, 3 November 2026). picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is narrow and runs opposite to the sell side. Post-interim targets (late July 2026, about 200p to 215p) and Jefferies' 200p (3 November 2026) imply roughly 28% to 38% upside from 156.20 pence. Jefferies' case rests on 'visible' retail and infrastructure earnings growing about 17% a year to 2030 and on Centrica trading at about 11 times 2027 earnings against about 17 times for peers. What those targets do not address is cash: the company reported a 570 million pound free cash outflow in the first half of 2026 and net cash fell to 709 million pounds, with nuclear equity still to fund and the buyback off. A 200p target needs either a dated cash-flow turn nobody has given or a regulated-network multiple for a business that is not yet a regulated network. Under the deep-value lens, the question is whether the street is pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power. It is not: the market is pricing a smaller, more capital-hungry business roughly correctly, and the recent rise to about 156p has already closed most of the gap to our fair value.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window, the months just ahead, is shaped by cash. Over the next three to nine months Centrica must fund phased Sizewell C equity, the cash costs of the 1,300-job restructuring before its savings land, and household bad debt running above the regulator's allowance, while earnings are guided to be weighted to the first half. There is no liquidation event or debt wall: the company is solvent with net cash. The likely bad outcome is slow rather than sudden: net cash below about 400 million pounds at the February 2027 full-year results with the buyback still paused. A Rough closure decision without a support regime would bring clean-up costs forward.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited. The base is income-oriented and index-heavy (a FTSE 100 member with low beta), the dividend was raised rather than cut and paid on 22 September 2026, so there is no mechanical trigger for yield funds to sell. The slide from about 220p to a 144p low was orderly, and the shares have since recovered to about 156p. There has been no wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers) to buy into, and with the buyback paused the marginal buyer of 2024 and 2025 is absent.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. This is the same committee continuing coverage, and nothing dated in the business has changed since our last look on 19 October 2026: no trading update, no buyback restart and no Rough decision were announced. What changed is the price, up from about 149 pence to 156.20 pence today, helped by a broker upgrade (Jefferies, buy, 200p, 3 November 2026), and that narrows the gap to our 160 pence fair value to about 2%. Centrica is a competently run, solvent company swapping a volatile trading windfall for contracted infrastructure cash flow, and the 9 July 2026 Sizewell B contract is a genuinely good piece of work. But valued by its parts the business is worth about 160 pence in the base case, against 206 pence if everything goes right and 105 pence if the current cash trend simply continues. Our reason to pass is not the price alone: the company's own interim release shows a 570 million pound free cash outflow in the first half of 2026, net cash has fallen to about 709 million pounds while a rising dividend and new nuclear equity are funded from it, the buyback is paused, and returns are falling from their peak, so the moat is eroding. A low multiple on a shrinking, more capital-hungry base is not a value position. The thesis holds in that nothing has disproven the pivot; what would change our answer is dated evidence of cash cover: positive free cash flow and a buyback restart at the February 2027 full-year results, or a Rough support decision. The macro backdrop, which rewards cash flow now, is a headwind but did not move this answer.
picks.forcing_function: There is no firmly dated event that forces a re-rating. The real decision point is the full-year results in February 2027, where the company either restarts the buyback and shows free cash flow covering the dividend and capital spending, or does not. A government storage support regime for Rough has no published date and depends on a third party. Under the deep-value lens, a buyback reauthorisation or an asset sale (Spirit Energy, or a stake in the nuclear portfolio) would be the re-rating events; none is announced as of 16 November 2026.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Centrica plc (CNA.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 16 November 2026. Price used: 156.20 pence (London listing, GBp; live quote from the paid data feed, FMP, 16 November 2026: previous close 160.65p, day range 156.20p to 159.85p, 52-week range 144p to 220.30p, 50-day average 150.3p, 200-day average 176.9p). Shares in issue are about 4,530 million (market value of about 7.07 billion pounds divided by the price). No earnings-call transcript was bundled and the paid feed has no transcripts or news for this London listing, so this deep dive is built from the screener fundamentals, the company's dated disclosures (2025 full-year results of 19 February 2026, interim results of 23 July 2026), and a fresh web search for anything new since this committee's last full look on 19 October 2026. That search found no new company announcement dated after 19 October 2026: no trading update, no buyback restart, and no decision on Rough. The one dated item is a broker view, not a company fact: Jefferies upgraded the shares to buy with a 200p target on 3 November 2026. No management quotes are reproduced, because we did not have a transcript in hand, and we will not invent them.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved in three stages over roughly two years.

- 2023 to 2024: the windfall. Centrica earned net income of 3.93 billion pounds in 2023 on 26.5 billion pounds of revenue, an exceptional year driven by gas trading and upstream profits during the European energy crisis. Management used it to rebuild the balance sheet (net cash of about 2.7 billion pounds at the end of 2024) and to run a large share buyback.
- 2025: the normalisation. Revenue fell to 19.5 billion pounds and the company reported a statutory loss of 72 million pounds for 2025 (results of 19 February 2026). On that day the buyback was paused to fund investment, and guidance for the trading arm (Centrica Energy, the optimisation business) was cut to about 250 million pounds of core profit (EBITDA, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) for 2026.
- 2026: the pivot to contracted infrastructure. The narrative is "swap volatile trading profit for long-dated, inflation-linked cash flow": a 20-year regulated contract for Sizewell B (9 July 2026, 70.50 pounds per megawatt-hour in 2025 money, inflation-linked, plant life extended to 2055), the older nuclear fleet extended to 2030 (22 July 2026), the Severn gas plant (May 2026), half of the Grain LNG import terminal, and equity committed to the new Sizewell C station. A 1,300-job cost programme accompanies it (23 July 2026).

What was dropped: the buyback as the central per-share lever. What was introduced: regulated and contracted assets as the valuation anchor. What remains unresolved: Rough, the offshore gas storage field, whose future depends on a government decision on storage support with no published date. Nothing in this arc has moved since 19 October 2026.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (dated) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Earnings are normalising, not collapsing (19 Feb 2026) | Net income 586m (2021), -782m (2022), 3.93bn (2023), 1.33bn (2024), -72m (2025). Trailing diluted earnings 0.11 pounds a share to 30 June 2026; latest-quarter earnings per share down 52% year on year. | Partly true. The base is falling. |
| Full-year 2026 expectations "largely unchanged", earnings weighted to the first half (23 Jul 2026) | Retail guided to the lower end of its 500 to 800 million pound EBITDA range; trading arm about 250m for 2026, and a 2027 trading outlook of about 250m against a market expectation nearer 320m. | Guidance held, but at the low end, and the trading outlook was lowered. |
| Capital discipline while investing | Interim release (23 Jul 2026): free cash outflow of 570 million pounds in the half; closing adjusted net cash 709 million pounds, down from 1.5 billion at end-2025 and about 2.5 billion a year earlier. Balance-sheet recomputation at 30 Jun 2026: cash 3.47bn against 2.74bn of debt including 206m of leases, net cash 730m. | Diverges. Cash is being consumed, not generated. |
| Dividend progression is affordable | Interim dividend raised to 2.0 pence, paid 22 Sep 2026, out of the cash balance rather than free cash flow. | Story richer than cash flow. |
| Balance sheet strength | Net cash, solvent. The screener now shows Altman-Z (a solvency score) of 3.1 and Piotroski (a nine-point accounting-health score) of 6/9, down from the 5.0 and 7/9 our last look used. | True on solvency, but the cushion is thinning. |

A data conflict the director must know about: the screener records trailing free cash flow of 328 million pounds and a price-to-free-cash-flow multiple of about 24 times. The company's own interim release shows a 570 million pound free cash outflow in the first half of 2026. The screener figure does not reconcile with the published cash flow and should not be used to support value.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Trajectory: declining on the near term, rising on the long-term asset story. Without a transcript we judge tone from the shape of the disclosures. February 2026 was defensive (buyback paused, trading guidance cut). July 2026 was offensive in capital allocation (nuclear, LNG, generation) but cautious on cash, with management ruling out a near-term buyback in favour of investment. That is a team confident about 2035 and visibly less specific about cash in 2026 and 2027. Nothing new has been said since.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The screener shows earnings beats in 6 of the last 7 quarters (86%), but the trading guidance that was beaten had itself been cut. No dated guidance on free cash flow or on a buyback restart has been given, which is the guidance that matters for value. Reliability: Medium.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- When the buyback returns, and what net cash level management will defend. Not answered with a date.
- Rough: whether the government grants a support regime, and what closure would cost. Third-party dependent, undated.
- The phasing of Sizewell C equity calls against a thinning cash balance.
- Household bad debt above the regulator's allowance: Jefferies (3 November 2026) put residential bad debt above 4% of revenue at the half year against Ofgem's 3.8% allowance, and expects it below the allowance only from 2028.
- Sell-side targets sit well above the price: post-interim targets of about 200p to 215p (late July 2026), and Jefferies at 200p (3 November 2026), resting on "visible" retail and infrastructure earnings of 7.8p a share in 2026 growing to 14.7p by 2030. That growth path is an analyst forecast, not company guidance, and it does not address the cash outflow.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags
- 🔴 Free cash outflow of 570 million pounds in H1 2026 (interim release, 23 July 2026) while the dividend was raised.
- 🔴 Adjusted net cash down from about 2.5 billion pounds (mid-2025) to 709 million (30 June 2026).
- 🔴 Buyback paused since 19 February 2026, with management ruling out a near-term restart on 23 July 2026.
- 🔴 Revenue down 2.1% last year and 6.4% a year over three years; net margin about -0.4% for 2025.
- 🔴 In the last inflation shock gross margin fell from 35.7% (2019) to 9.6% (2021): this business did not pass costs through.

Green flags
- 🟢 Sizewell B contract (9 July 2026): thirty years of inflation-linked revenue for a small, self-funded capital share.
- 🟢 Older nuclear fleet extended to 2030 (22 July 2026).
- 🟢 Solvent with net cash; return on invested capital of about 39% on the screener (flattered by the trading arm and a small capital base).
- 🟢 Gross margin 38.7% and expanding in the latest year.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The vocabulary has shifted from "returns to shareholders" to "investment" and "contracted". That is a genuine strategic pivot, but it moves the company from a cash-return story to a capital-intensive one exactly when long-dated borrowing costs are high and the market pays for cash now. The household supply arm is showing stress through bad debt above the regulator's allowance. The shares rose from about 149p (19 October) to 160.65p (13 November) and 156.20p today without any company announcement, which looks like a sector move and broker support (Jefferies, 3 November) rather than news.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning. Centrica is pivoting from a merchant trading and retail business to a part-contracted infrastructure owner. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: the company is funding a rising dividend and new nuclear equity out of a shrinking cash balance rather than out of free cash flow, and the next hard evidence on whether that turns is the full-year results in February 2027.

Moat. The retail book (British Gas) has scale and brand but sits under the regulator's price cap and competes on switching; the trading arm earns volatility, not a moat. Returns are high but falling from the 2023 peak, and the screener's free cash flow has fallen by about 28% a year over three years. That is an eroding moat, with the contracted nuclear stake the one widening piece. Secular threat: the energy transition is material rather than terminal. It shrinks gas supply, upstream gas and gas storage over time, but Centrica is reinvesting into assets a renewables-heavy grid needs (nuclear, flexible generation, batteries). The cheapness is mostly the market correctly pricing a smaller, more capital-hungry business, not a fear-driven mispricing.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.
picks.sop_fair_value: 160 pence per share, about 2% above the 156.20 pence live price on 16 November 2026. Unchanged from this committee's reconciliation: a probability-balanced blend of the two cases, tilted slightly above the midpoint because the Sizewell B contract is signed, and cross-checked against a mid-cycle earnings view (about 950 million pounds of adjusted operating profit, less about 100 million of corporate costs and interest, taxed at about 30%, gives about 600 million of earnings or 13.2 pence a share, which at 12.5 times is about 165 pence).
picks.sop_breakdown: Base case, millions of pounds, about 4,530 million shares (market value 7.07 billion pounds at 156.20p, 16 November 2026): Retail 2,640 (320 million at 8 times); Optimisation 1,460 (225 million at 6.5 times); Nuclear 1,530 (Sizewell B 1,050, older fleet 480); Spirit Energy 450; Rough 150 (midway between a support regime and closure); generation and flexible assets 525; Sizewell C at negative 50 net of equity still to pay; net cash 600 (haircut from 709 adjusted for trading collateral and provisions). Total 7,305 million pounds, about 161 pence, rounded to 160.
picks.sop_bull: Favourable sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately), in millions of pounds, against about 4,530 million shares. Retail (British Gas supply and services, Bord Gais in Ireland) on about 340 million of adjusted operating profit at 9 times: 3,060. Optimisation, the trading and LNG arm, on about 250 million at 8 times: 2,000. Nuclear: Sizewell B stake on its 20-year inflation-linked contract 1,200, plus the older fleet to 2030 550: 1,750. Spirit Energy upstream gas net of decommissioning: 650. Rough storage with a support regime: 400. Generation and flexible assets (Severn, batteries, solar): 650. Sizewell C contributed equity: 100. Net cash at 30 June 2026 in full: 730. Total about 9,340 million pounds, or about 206 pence per share.
picks.sop_bear: Adverse sum-of-the-parts, same share count. Retail on 300 million at 6 times as the price cap and bad debt bite: 1,800. Trading on 200 million at 5 times: 1,000. Nuclear: Sizewell B 800 and the older fleet 350: 1,150. Spirit Energy 250, with decommissioning consuming most of its value. Rough at negative 100 on closure with no support. Generation and flexible assets 400 as spark spreads compress. Sizewell C at negative 200, treating the remaining equity as a call on cash earning below its cost. Net cash credited at 450 rather than 730, because part of the cash is trading collateral and pension, decommissioning and other long-term liabilities sit against it, and the first half burned 570 million. Total about 4,750 million pounds, or about 105 pence per share.
picks.risk_reward: Poor at this price. The base fair value of 160 pence is barely above the 156.20 pence price, the favourable case is 206 pence and the adverse case is 105 pence, and the adverse case is an extension of what the cash flow statement is already doing rather than a tail. There is no structural floor: no deal terms or tender, and net cash is only about 16 pence a share and shrinking. The dividend yield is not a floor while it is paid from the cash balance. The pipeline computes the ratios from these levels.

picks.peer_comps_note: The peer file lists SSE, National Grid, Drax, Orsted, EDF, Engie, United Utilities and one further London name (SNG.L), and calls Centrica in line with them, cheap on earnings power but rich on price-to-free-cash-flow. But the gap is earned. picks.bull_thesis: Kunlun Energy is the only Chinese gas distributor with net cash: 48.06 billion yuan of cash and short-term investments against 21.30 billion of debt at 30 June 2026, or about HK$31.4 billion at today's 1.1747 exchange rate, close to half the HK$65.3 billion market value. Moody's raised the issuer to A1 on 11 August 2026. Strip the cash out and the operating business trades at roughly 3.6 times enterprise value to trailing earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EV/EBITDA), against roughly 5.0 to 5.5 times for ENN Energy and China Resources Gas. Volumes still grow (gas sales up 3.65% in the first half of 2026) because China is still switching from coal to gas, and the interim dividend rose about 18%. The bull case needs only two things: that the margin squeeze on gas sales finds a floor in the full-year 2026 results due around late March 2027, and that some of the idle cash is eventually returned through a higher payout, a buyback or a special dividend. Either would close the gap to fair value on its own. The driver is Chinese gas volume and provincial tariff policy, independent of interest-rate cuts and of the artificial-intelligence spending cycle, with a beta of about 0.55.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is in the balance sheet, not in what shareholders receive. Operating profit fell from 13.55 billion yuan in 2023 to 9.71 billion in 2025, about 28%, on rising revenue; return on equity is about 7.9% and return on invested capital about 5.8%, both below the cost of capital and falling. The 3.1% rise in attributable profit in the first half of 2026 came from minority shareholders taking a smaller share of a flat pre-tax result, not from a better business. The cash earns about 1.4% a year, has grown while dividends paid fell, partly belongs to minority holders in subsidiaries, and sits under a 54% state parent that no outside shareholder can pressure. On earnings and yield Kunlun is not cheap: about 10.3 times trailing earnings with a dividend yield of about 5.1%, the lowest in its group, at a premium to its own parent PetroChina. The winter heating season from November to February is where regulated residential prices lag imported LNG costs, and a Hong Kong dollar risk-free rate tied to US rates near 5% leaves a 5.1% no-growth yield with no cushion. The bear case is confirmed if full-year 2026 EBITDA falls again and the payout stays near half of earnings.
picks.consensus_delta: On this name the street is not looking the wrong way. The published consensus price target of about HK$8.47 from seven analysts, six rating it a buy (gathered 22 September 2026), sits essentially on our base case of HK$8.55. Where we differ is in emphasis. The bullish street view leans on the first-half 2026 rise in attributable profit and the dividend increase; we read the profit rise as a minority-share effect on a flat pre-tax result, and the true earnings trend as down. The deep-value question for this lens is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power. It is not: it prices a low-return franchise fairly and gives partial credit for cash it cannot reach. The mispricing exists only on the balance sheet, and unlocking it requires a decision by PetroChina that nobody can forecast.
picks.valley_of_death: There is no liquidation event, debt wall or covenant that could break the thesis before value converges. Short-term borrowings of about 7.03 billion yuan are covered nearly seven times by cash, and the issuer is rated A1. The pressures over the next three to nine months are slow ones. First, the winter heating season from November 2026 to February 2027, when regulated residential prices lag imported LNG costs; its result lands in the full-year figures around late March 2027, on top of a first half where EBITDA already fell. Second, the cost of imported LNG, which is linked to oil prices. Third, rates: the Hong Kong dollar is pegged to the US dollar, so local risk-free yields near 5% leave a 5.1% no-growth dividend with no premium, and that grinds the multiple down for as long as rates stay high. The realistic downside is a de-rating toward and possibly through the 52-week low of HK$6.34, driven by a sector and rate sell-off rather than by damage to the company. That is exactly the setting in which our entry level could be reached.
picks.positioning_washout: The shareholder base is concentrated and stable: PetroChina owns about 54%, and the free float is held largely by income and value investors. No dividend cut, index deletion or lock-up is in view, so forced selling by holders who must sell regardless of value is unlikely. The plausible route to a lower price is a sector-wide or style-wide sell-off: the Chinese city-gas group has already de-rated, with China Gas Holdings near its year low, and high US-linked yields pressure every yield stock in Hong Kong. If the winter results disappoint across the group, income funds rotating out of Chinese gas utilities could take Kunlun down with its peers, toward the HK$6.34 low last seen within the past year.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near HK$6.40, which a sector-wide or style-wide sell-off in Chinese gas utilities and high-yield Hong Kong shares could deliver.

Nothing has changed since this committee last ruled on 2 November 2026. No results, announcements or capital-return decisions have been published, and the share price is HK$7.57 against HK$7.575 a week ago, so the earlier answer stands.

The thesis holds. Kunlun is a sound business with the only net-cash balance sheet among Chinese gas distributors, 26.76 billion yuan at 30 June 2026, an A1 credit rating since 11 August 2026, and volumes still growing as China displaces coal. Its operating business trades at about 3.6 times EBITDA against 5.0 to 5.5 for its peers. But profitability has fallen for two years, returns sit below the cost of capital, the cash earns about 1.4% under a 54% parent that decides its use, and on earnings and dividend yield the shares are not cheap against their group. That is an eroding moat, which caps the value case at a middling score however low the multiple looks.

The arithmetic decides the timing. Our fair value is HK$8.55, about 13% above today's price, below the 20% discount this book requires in the current growth-and-inflation backdrop, and the adverse case of HK$5.80 sits further below than the fair value sits above. At HK$6.40, a retest of the 52-week low of HK$6.34, fair value is about 34% higher, the dividend yield rises to about 6.1%, and the operating business costs about 5 times earnings once the cash is set aside. That is where the asymmetry turns in our favour.

Two developments would justify entering without the price concession: full-year 2026 results around late March 2027 showing EBITDA flat or better, ending the slide, or a real capital-return decision on the cash. The fair value sits on the analyst consensus, so at today's price this is a consensus view, not an edge. The thesis needs no rate cuts and has a driver independent of the artificial-intelligence spending cycle, which is useful for the book, but there is no live catalyst for the market backdrop to amplify, so it does not move the call.

# Kunlun Energy Company Limited (0135.HK) — a deep dive on management and the setup

**Date of this review:** 9 November 2026 (continuing coverage; the committee last ruled on 2 November 2026, on a full debate dated 22 September 2026).
**Price used throughout:** HK$7.57 (live quote from the paid market-data service, 9 November 2026). Market value about HK$65.3 billion.
**Currency:** Kunlun reports in Chinese yuan and trades in Hong Kong dollars. At today's rate of 1 yuan = 1.1747 Hong Kong dollars, every accounting figure below has been converted before being compared with the share price.

**Limitation stated up front:** Kunlun holds no earnings call that any accessible source carries, and the paid market-data service has no transcript or company-specific news for this listing (both checked 9 November 2026). The web-search budget for this run was exhausted before any additional search could be made, so this review relies on the licensed financial statements, the live quote and peer quotes, and the verified findings of the 22 September review and its independent check. No management quote is invented to fill the gap. Kunlun reports half-yearly; no new financial period has been published since the half year to 30 June 2026.

---

## 1. Narrative arc

Kunlun is the natural-gas arm of PetroChina, which owns about 54% of it. It sells gas through city pipelines and to industrial users, runs liquefied-natural-gas (LNG) receiving terminals and processing plants, and holds a small oil and gas production arm abroad. The story the company tells is consistent and unexciting: steady volume growth as China switches from coal to gas, conservative finance, and a rising dividend. What has quietly changed over three years is profitability. Revenue kept rising (188.96 billion yuan in 2025, up about 1%), but operating profit fell from 13.55 billion yuan in 2023 to 9.71 billion in 2025, a drop of about 28%. The narrative has shifted from growth to resilience — volumes and the balance sheet — because the margin story stopped working.

Since the last look on 2 November 2026 nothing new has been published: no results, no trading update, no capital-return announcement.

## 2. Claims versus the financials

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Volumes are still growing | Gas sales volume 30,156 million cubic metres in the first half of 2026, up 3.65% (company results, 25-26 August 2026) | Holds |
| The balance sheet is exceptionally strong | Cash and short-term investments 48.06 billion yuan against total debt 21.30 billion at 30 June 2026: net cash 26.76 billion; Moody's raised the issuer to A1 on 11 August 2026 | Holds |
| Earnings are improving | Attributable profit rose 3.1% in the first half to 3.26 billion yuan, but profit before tax was flat (6.69 billion versus 6.74 billion) and the gain came from minority shareholders taking a smaller share of a smaller result; earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation fell about 7-10% year on year depending on the data source | Richer than the numbers |
| Shareholder returns are rising | Interim dividend 0.1916 yuan, about 18% above the prior interim; forward run-rate about HK$0.389 a share, a 5.1% yield at HK$7.57 | Holds, from a low base |

Two corrections from the independent check of 22 September remain in force: the dividend yield is about 5.1%, not 5.3%, and the 5.07 billion yuan cash-flow figure is a half-year number, not a full year. The screener's own fair value and margin of safety compare a yuan model output with a Hong Kong dollar price and should be ignored; its return-on-equity and return-on-capital figures are roughly double the true values of about 7.9% and 5.8%.

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory

No call exists to read tone from. Judged by actions: stable and defensive. Payout rising, no buyback, no special distribution, cash still accumulating. Trajectory: stable in posture, declining in profitability.

## 4. Guidance credibility

Kunlun does not publish numeric earnings guidance. The screener records 0 of 2 recent periods beating estimates, and earnings per share fell 13% in 2025. Volume targets have broadly been met. Reliability: medium — conservative on balance sheet, unreliable as a signal of margin direction.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

The questions analysts cannot get answered are the same as in September: when, if ever, the 26.76 billion yuan net cash pile is returned to shareholders; how far the regulated spread between imported gas cost and the residential selling price can fall; and whether the parent will let Kunlun distribute more than about half its earnings. The published consensus price target of about HK$8.47 from seven analysts (as gathered on 22 September) sits close to this committee's base case, so the street already sees roughly what we see.

## 6. Red flags and green flags

- Red: operating profit down 28% from 2023 to 2025 on rising revenue (annual reports).
- Red: the first-half 2026 earnings rise was a minority-share effect, not operational (results, August 2026).
- Red: cash earning about 1.4% a year while a 54% state owner decides its use.
- Green: net cash of 26.76 billion yuan, about 48% of market value (30 June 2026).
- Green: Moody's A1 upgrade on 11 August 2026.
- Green: interim dividend up about 18% (August 2026); the dividend goes to holders on 26 November 2026.

## 7. Hidden signals

The share price has gone nowhere for seven weeks: HK$7.55 on 22 September, HK$7.575 on 2 November, HK$7.57 today, with the 50-day average at HK$7.56. Peers have kept falling — China Gas Holdings is at HK$5.05 near its year low of HK$4.81, China Resources Gas at HK$16.57 and ENN Energy at HK$49.08, both below their 200-day averages. Kunlun's stillness while its group de-rates is the cash pile and the parent's ownership acting as ballast, not a re-rating.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict for the director

Trajectory: deteriorating. Profitability has fallen for two years, and returns on capital sit below the cost of capital. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: the discount is in the cash and the assets, not in the earnings or the dividend, and the cash has a 54% gatekeeper with no stated intention of releasing it.

Moat: a regulatory-licence and scale moat in pipeline gas distribution — real, but its returns are falling, so it is eroding rather than wide. Secular threat: manageable. Gas is the transition fuel in China, displacing coal; electrification is a decades-long threat to residential and industrial gas demand, not a near-term terminal one. The cheapness is neither a pure fear-print nor a value trap: it is a fair price for a low-return franchise with an idle cash pile, and becomes attractive only at a lower price or a capital-return decision.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

# TF1 Group (TFI.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup
*Transcripts reviewed: 9M-2025 (2025-10-30), FY-2025 (2026-02-12), H1-2026 (2026-07-30), 9M-2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: EUR 6.09 (Euronext Paris, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
A year ago (2025-10-30) the story was "resilience": revenue stable, operating margin held near 11%, market-share gains in a falling linear advertising market, and TF1+ (the free streaming platform) growing advertising revenue about 41%. By the full-year call (2026-02-12) the frame was "the second phase of the strategic plan" - micro-payments, the Netflix distribution deal, and French-speaking international expansion - while advertising revenue was already down 4% for 2025. By H1-2026 (2026-07-30) the story had turned defensive: the margin target was cut to "mid- to high single-digit", and net profit roughly halved. The 9M-2026 call (2026-10-29) is a "we are on the road map" call: margin from activities (current operating profit before one-offs, divided by revenue) of 7.6% versus 10.9% a year earlier, advertising revenue down 9%, and the growth vocabulary now leans almost entirely on the Netflix partnership, the small-business ad platform and micro-payments.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong double-digit digital growth" | TF1+ ad revenue +19% over 9M-2026 (EUR 160M), +20.5% in Q3; total digital EUR 198M (+17%) | Delivered, but growth has halved from ~40% in 2025 |
| Digital offsets linear decline | Group advertising revenue EUR 1.0B, down 9% (about EUR 100M lost) versus roughly EUR 30M digital gain | Not true - the gap widened |
| Cost discipline protects margin | Programming costs down EUR 44M; margin still 7.6% vs 10.9% | Partial - costs cut, margin still fell about 3.3 points |
| "Very solid" balance sheet | Net cash EUR 382M at 2026-09-30 (EUR 587M cash vs EUR 207M debt at 2026-06-30) | True - the one clean pillar |
| "Growing dividend policy" | Dividend EUR 132M paid April 2026; free cash flow after working capital only EUR 16M over 9M-2026 (EUR 57M in H1, so Q3 was about minus EUR 41M) | Dividend is being paid out of the cash pile, not out of earnings |
| Earnings trajectory | EPS 0.97 (2024) to 0.72 (2025) to trailing 0.59; latest quarter EPS down 27% y/y | Decline is accelerating, not stabilising |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Declining. 2025-10-30: "successfully managed to mitigate" ad headwinds. 2026-02-12: offensive, with return-on-investment slides for advertisers. 2026-07-30: defensive, margin guidance cut. 2026-10-29: "visibility remaining limited", the market forecast of minus 6% "now seems slightly optimistic", and for 2027 "we see no near-term prospects for improvement in the macroeconomic and political environment or any reduction in the regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms." That last sentence is the most candid management has been in two years.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium. 2025 margin guidance was cut in October 2025 (from "broadly stable" to 10.5-11.5%) and then met at 11%. 2026 guidance was cut at H1 to mid- to high single-digit and is being met (7.6% at nine months). Management meets reset guidance; it does not forecast the down-leg well. The 9M-2026 results came in slightly above company-compiled consensus on revenue and margin.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Very thin coverage on the calls - the 9M-2026 call had only written questions from one broker (CIC). The questions were October/Q4 ad trends, 2027 visibility, the presidential election, Netflix monetisation, and programming costs. Management declined to give a programming-cost range and said Netflix revenue is ramping "more gradually than the audience" because ad load and CPM (price per thousand ad views) on Netflix are below TF1+ levels. Nobody asked about dividend cover, which is the real pressure point.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: dividend (EUR 132M) is about eight times nine-month free cash flow after working capital (EUR 16M) - 9M-2026.
- Red: advertising revenue down 9% with management saying the market has "deteriorated further" since May - 9M-2026.
- Red: no improvement seen for 2027; the 2027 presidential election likely reduces prime-time ad inventory - 9M-2026.
- Red: Studio TF1 operating profit down EUR 14M over nine months - 9M-2026.
- Green: audience share at an all-time high of 36.9% among women under 50 in September 2026, and linear ad market share up about 2 points in August-September - 9M-2026.
- Green: Netflix partnership "ahead of our expectations" on audience; TF1+ growth re-accelerated to 20.5% in Q3 - 9M-2026.
- Green: net cash of EUR 382M is roughly 30% of the market value.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The language moved from "gain market share" (a sign of strength in a stable market) to "regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms" - an admission that the problem is structural, not cyclical. Disclosure has shifted toward audience and usage metrics (streamers, transactions) and away from digital revenue per user. The micro-payment figures (about 2 million transactions year to date) are small in euros; their prominence on the call is a sign of how few growth levers remain.

## 8. BOTTOM LINE
A well-run, market-leading broadcaster in a shrinking market. Management executes against reset targets, keeps a strong net cash position, and is honest about 2027. But the earnings base is still falling, digital growth is not filling the linear hole, and the dividend now relies on the balance sheet.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory declining · a moat that is being eroded.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# CECONOMY AG (CEC.DE, Xetra, EUR) - forensic dossier, 2026-11-09

Price used: EUR 4.53 on Xetra (FMP live quote, 9 November 2026; 52-week range EUR 3.51-4.59; market value about EUR 2.20 billion on about 485 million shares). Latest call transcript: second fiscal quarter, 13 May 2026.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
CECONOMY runs MediaMarkt and Saturn, Europe's largest consumer-electronics chain (about 1,000 stores, 11 countries, roughly EUR 24 billion of sales). The story management tells has moved from "turnaround retailer" to "platform": retail media (selling advertising to suppliers against store and app traffic), services, a third-party marketplace and rented floor space, now about 40% of gross profit. Since late 2025 the story has been overtaken by ownership: JD.com's 2025 tender at EUR 4.60 left JD.com and partner Convergenta with 85.2% on completion. The European Commission conditionally approved the purchase under the foreign-subsidies rules on 3 November 2026, and closing is expected by 12 November 2026, inside the 10 November-area long-stop the chief financial officer flagged on 13 May 2026.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Claim: twelve-plus straight quarters of adjusted operating profit growth. Preliminary fiscal 2025/26 figures reported in October 2026 put adjusted operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and tax) at about EUR 515 million versus a EUR 500 million target and EUR 406 million restated a year earlier; sales about EUR 23.9 billion, up about 5%. Final figures are due 14 December 2026. Corroborated, though from trade press, not the company release.
- Reported profit does not match adjusted profit: net income was negative in fiscal 2023 (EUR -39 million) and 2025 (EUR -35 million); trailing earnings per share EUR -0.03 at 30 June 2026. The gap of roughly EUR 300 million a year between adjusted and reported profit recurs with a differently named one-off each year.
- The screen's 3.2 times price to free cash flow counts trailing free cash flow of EUR 731 million before about EUR 524 million a year of store rent, which lease accounting books in financing. After rent, owner free cash flow is about EUR 200 million, in line with management's own guide: about 11 times at today's price.
- Return on invested capital 1.8%; gross margin 15.1% and contracting. Net debt EUR 1.51 billion at 30 June 2026 (borrowings EUR 2.60 billion less cash EUR 1.09 billion), a seasonal high; near nil at the December peak.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Confident on operations, deliberately vague on the minority. On 13 May 2026 the finance chief confirmed closing "in the second half of the calendar year" before the November long-stop and declined to give a precise delisting date. Tone on Germany and Austria, the core markets, was guarded across both reported 2026 quarters.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Good on the adjusted line: the EUR 500 million target was met and beaten (about EUR 515 million, preliminary, October 2026). Weaker on reported profit, where guidance is not given and one-offs recur. Credibility on deal timing was adequate: the timetable slipped from first half to second half of calendar 2026, but the regulatory path closed before the long-stop.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Analysts pressed on deal timing and delisting mechanics (13 May 2026), not on the adjusted-versus-reported gap or rent-adjusted cash flow. No current analyst price targets could be found with a dated source; the stock is effectively a controlled company with thin coverage.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: recurring one-offs; 1.8% return on capital; contracting gross margin; JD.com committed in its 2025 offer to no domination or profit-transfer agreement (a contract that would force an appraised cash exit) for at least three years; a German delisting offer must only meet the six-month average price (about EUR 4.15-4.30 on the 200- and 50-day averages) and the bidder's qualifying pre-acquisitions; free float about 14.8% and thin.
Green: adjusted profit beat (October 2026); mix shift to higher-margin income; supplier-funded working capital; no refinancing pressure; EU approval obtained 3 November 2026.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The share price (EUR 4.53, 94% up its range) has converged to within 1.5% of JD.com's EUR 4.60 tender price, above the statutory six-month-average floor. The market is pricing a delisting offer struck at or near EUR 4.60, not the business. Volume is low (about 5,000 shares on the quote day), so the marginal buyer is an event trader.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A better business than its reputation, held inside a security whose payout is set by the controlling shareholder's delisting decision. Today's price already discounts the most likely minority exit; the upside case (an appraised exit under a domination agreement) is contractually ruled out for about three years. Nothing here for a value book.
