picks.bull_thesis: JD Logistics is China's largest self-operated warehouse-and-delivery network (about 1,600 warehouses and more than 34 million square metres, end-2025), anchored by JD.com volume and growing fast with outside customers. Revenue rose from RMB 104.7B in 2021 to RMB 217.2B in 2025, and first-half 2026 revenue was RMB 124.7B, up 26.5%. Profit is now catching up. Management promised on 2026-03-05 that 2026 profit would improve, and it delivered: IFRS (reported) net income was RMB 0.88B in Q1 and RMB 2.41B in Q2 2026, and adjusted operating profit rose 39.9% in the half. Cost ratios are falling. In Q2 2026 staff costs were 34.2% of revenue (-1.0 point), rent 5.3% (-1.1 points) and operating expenses 6.4% (-0.5 points), as automation (more than 1,000 driverless delivery vehicles and robot-run warehouses) takes cost out. Deppon, the freight subsidiary that dragged on 2025, is 'on the track of recovery' (2026-08-13), and the CFO guided that operating margin 'will be further improved in the second half'. Overseas warehouses (doubled in 2025 to nearly 2 million square metres) and the JoyExpress delivery brand in Europe and Saudi Arabia add a second growth curve. At HK$10.26 the stock trades on about 7.6 times trailing earnings (about RMB 7.4B over the last twelve months), with about RMB 17.3B of net cash before leases, roughly a third of its RMB 53B market value. It sits near the bottom of its 52-week range (HK$9.51 to HK$16.76). Sell-side targets cluster around HK$18.4, though the snapshots date from mid-2026 and are stale. The case needs three things to hold: the second-half margin improvement shows up, Deppon stops dragging, and revenue growth holds in the high teens.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is in the earnings, not the cash or the returns. Return on invested capital is about 1% and the net margin about 3%, so a scale network that protects volume has not shown pricing power. Gross margin fell 0.9 points to 9.7% in Q2 2026 even as revenue grew 24%. More of the growth now comes from consolidated, low-margin on-demand riders, with outsourcing costs up 40.5% to 37% of revenue, rather than from integrated supply-chain work, where external revenue growth slowed to 12.5%. Free cash flow fell 26.7% in 2025, and the latest trailing figure in our data feed is zero. After about RMB 18.7B of lease liabilities, the 'net cash' becomes about RMB 1.4B of net debt, and automation spending will be 'higher than that of 2025' (2026-03-05) with no payback disclosed. Dependence on the parent is rising, not falling: JD Group supplied RMB 19.88B of RMB 30.17B integrated supply-chain revenue in Q2 2026. That means related-party pricing, not market pricing, sets much of the profit, and a parent pushing a European retail venture (Joybuy) can lean on its logistics arm. Chinese express pricing is competitive and the industry is maturing (management conceded the slowdown on 2026-08-13). Energy and wage costs are rising, and margins dipped in the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 6.9% to 5.5%). If the 2026-11-17 third-quarter results show margins stalling, the stock can stay a low-multiple, low-return logistics utility at 6 to 7 times earnings, with no discount closing.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the sell side is more bullish than we are. Mid-2026 snapshots show about 18 of 19 analysts at buy, with targets around HK$18.4 (JPMorgan HK$17 on 2026-07-22, Macquarie HK$16 on 2026-07-08, Nomura HK$20 and Citi HK$18 in May 2026). Those are stale and were set when the stock was HK$13-15. The tape has gone the other way: the stock fell from a HK$16.76 high to HK$10.26, 18% below its 200-day average. The market is now pricing JD Logistics as a low-return China utility at about 7.6 times earnings, with the pre-lease net cash barely credited. Our view sits between the two. Reported profit is recovering on schedule, so 7.6 times is too low for earnings growing in the mid-teens. But the street's HK$18 assumes margin expansion that the Q2 gross margin (-0.9 points) has not yet shown, and it ignores the lease burden. We underwrite HK$13.86, not HK$18.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) starts tomorrow with the Q3 2026 results (2026-11-17). If gross margin keeps slipping because of the on-demand consolidation, or Deppon's recovery stalls, the 'second-half margin improvement' guidance fails and the stock can retest the HK$9.51 low. Q4 is seasonally weak in our data: FMP shows a negative consensus EPS for the March 2027 print. That looks like a data artifact, but it is a reminder that Q4 is lumpy. Further risks are automation capex rising faster than savings, parent JD.com shifting costs onto its logistics arm to fund Joybuy in Europe, express price wars, and a Hong Kong or China equity de-rating unrelated to the company. There is no debt wall: borrowings are only RMB 5.17B against RMB 22.47B of cash.
picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure. JD.com holds the controlling stake and is not a forced seller. There is no dividend cut or index event in view, and the stock is not a yield name. Smart-money and insider-buy readings are weak (smart-money score 5/100, insider buy ratio 0), so there is no supportive accumulation signal either. The slide from HK$16.76 to HK$10.26 looks like a sector and China-style de-rating rather than mechanical liquidation.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds. JD Logistics is still growing revenue in the mid-twenties: Q2 2026 revenue was RMB 64.1B, up 24%, and reported profit recovered to RMB 2.41B in the quarter, as management promised in March. At HK$10.26 the stock trades at about 7.6 times trailing earnings, with about RMB 17B of net cash before leases, roughly a third of its market value. We cut our fair value from HK$15.0 to HK$13.86 after verifying corrections from an independent second opinion: a larger diluted share count (6.404B), the live exchange rate (1.1794 HKD per yuan), and stripping interest income from earnings so the cash is not credited twice. Even so, the fair value sits about 35% above today's price, comfortably clearing the 20% bar for the current reflation backdrop. The adverse case is about HK$7.78, with no hard floor because the group carries net debt once leases are counted. Conviction stays moderate (3 of 5) for three reasons. Returns on capital are about 1%. Gross margin fell 0.9 points in Q2 as low-margin on-demand delivery grew. And the cash flow after lease payments is much weaker than the earnings. The near-term check is the third-quarter 2026 report on 2026-11-17: if gross margin stops falling and the second-half margin improvement shows up, the case strengthens. A further margin slide would put the thesis in doubt. The macro backdrop is neutral for this name, and the catalyst is a soft margin recovery with no fixed date and no contractual payout.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard re-rating date. The checkpoints are the Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-17 and the FY2026 results in March 2027 (FMP calendar shows 2027-03-11). The re-rating needs the margin recovery to show up in two consecutive prints, plus clearer evidence on cash conversion. A buyback or a first dividend funded from the RMB 17B of pre-lease net cash would be the cleaner forcing event, but none has been announced, so we do not count on it.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# JD Logistics (2618.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-16. Transcripts read: Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), Q4/FY 2025 (2026-03-05), Q2 2026 (2026-08-13). Figures in RMB unless stated; the stock trades in Hong Kong dollars (HK$10.26 on 2026-11-16, FMP quote). Third-quarter 2026 results are due 2026-11-17 (FMP earnings calendar).*

**Takeaway:** JD Logistics is a fast-growing, thin-margin logistics network whose profits are now rising again after a soft 2025, and management has broadly done what it said it would on profit. The two things to watch are the quality of the growth (much of the 2026 revenue jump is a consolidated, low-margin on-demand delivery business, not the higher-value supply-chain work) and cash conversion, which the latest data feed reports as roughly zero over the trailing twelve months.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-13):** the story was integrated supply chain (ISC - running a customer's warehousing, inventory and delivery end to end) growth of 45.8% to RMB 13.1B, "targeted investments" in overseas and timeliness, and the new full-time food-delivery rider force. Profit was the soft spot: non-IFRS (adjusted, excluding items like share-based pay) net profit RMB 2.02B, attributable profit down about 8% year on year.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-03-05):** the CEO framed 2025 around three differentiators - ISC, customer experience, and automation/AI. Overseas warehouse space was doubled as promised (nearly 200 bonded/overseas warehouses, about 2 million square metres) and the JoyExpress delivery brand launched in Saudi Arabia and Europe. Deppon (the freight subsidiary) was conceded as a 2025 margin drag with "positive improvement" promised for 2026.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-08-13):** the CFO led with profit, not growth: revenue RMB 64.1B (+24.3%), adjusted operating profit +11.6% for the quarter and +39.9% for the half. The emphasis has shifted from "capacity building" to "operating leverage", with overseas now called "an important second growth curve" and the Joybuy European retail venture of the parent JD.com a named driver.

The arc is from investment to harvest - but the headline growth has quietly changed composition: ISC revenue growth slowed to 12.1% in Q2 2026, while "other customers" (express, freight and the newly consolidated on-demand riders) grew 37.6%.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "High-quality revenue growth" (every call) | Revenue RMB 104.7B (2021) to 217.2B (2025); H1 2026 RMB 124.7B, +26.5% | Corroborated on volume. Quality is mixed: Q2 2026 gross margin 9.7%, down 0.9pp year on year; outsourcing costs +40.5% to 37% of revenue on the on-demand consolidation. |
| 2026 profit would show "positive improvement" (2026-03-05) | IFRS net income Q1 2026 RMB 0.88B, Q2 RMB 2.41B; H1 adjusted operating profit +39.9% | Delivered. Trailing-twelve-month IFRS net income about RMB 7.4B (Q3 25 2.03 + Q4 25 2.04 + Q1 26 0.88 + Q2 26 2.41). |
| Core business margins rising, Deppon the drag (2026-08-13) | Group gross margin fell; management says the "original core business" margin rose | Plausible but unaudited in the transcript - no segment margin given. Cannot verify the split. |
| Overseas warehouse doubling by end-2025 (2025-11-13) | Confirmed achieved on 2026-03-05 | Delivered. |
| Strong cash generation (implied by the cheap price-to-free-cash-flow) | FY 2025 price/FCF about 5x; FMP trailing FCF reported as 0; FCF growth -26.7% in 2025 | Unclear. A "0" trailing figure may be a data gap, but the falling 2025 FCF is real. Lease payments (RMB 18.7B of lease liabilities) sit below operating cash flow and make FCF look better than owner cash. |
| Balance sheet strength | Cash RMB 22.47B vs borrowings RMB 5.17B (2026-06-30) | Corroborated: about RMB 17.3B net cash before leases; about RMB 1.4B net debt once RMB 18.7B of leases are counted. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, edging up.** Q3 2025 was defensive on profit ("lay the foundation for long-term business growth"; "In 2026, still I'm not in the right time to make the forecast"). Q4 2025 was more assertive on 2026 profit but vague on numbers. Q2 2026 is the most confident: "The operating margin will be further improved in the second half" and express growth "more than double the industry average". The shift is from offensive investment language to an operating-leverage message - a healthy direction - but specifics remain thin: no margin targets, no capex number, and no Deppon figures.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management gives qualitative, not numeric, guidance. What they promised, they delivered: the overseas-warehouse doubling (promised 2025-11-13, confirmed 2026-03-05) and the 2026 profit recovery (promised 2026-03-05, H1 operating profit +39.9%). The screener records 4 of the last 5 quarters beating estimates. Because the targets are soft, sandbagging is hard to detect. **Reliability: Medium-High.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Deppon's profitability** (asked 2026-03-05 and 2026-08-13): answered only with "on the track of recovery", never numbers.
- **Automation capex and returns** (2025-11-13, 2026-03-05): management says investment will be "higher than that of 2025" but gives no figure or payback.
- **Express industry slowdown** (2026-08-13): answered with relative growth claims, not unit pricing.
- **2026 revenue outlook** (2025-11-13): explicitly declined.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: gross margin down 0.9pp in Q2 2026 even as revenue grew 24%.
- Red: growth mix shifting toward consolidated, low-margin on-demand delivery (outsourcing costs +40.5%, Q2 2026).
- Red: free cash flow fell 26.7% in 2025 and the latest trailing figure is reported as zero; lease burden is large.
- Red: external ISC growth slowed to 12.5% in Q2 2026 from much higher rates in 2025.
- Green: profit recovery delivered on schedule (H1 2026 adjusted operating profit +39.9%).
- Green: cost ratios improving - staff costs 34.2% of revenue (-1.0pp), rent 5.3% (-1.1pp), operating expenses 6.4% (-0.5pp) in Q2 2026.
- Green: about RMB 17.3B of net cash before leases - roughly a third of the market value.
- Green: overseas build-out delivered to target.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The CFO, not the CEO, opened the Q2 2026 call and led with operating profit - a sign the investor message is now about margins.
- "Technology exports" appeared on 2026-08-13: the company now talks of selling its warehouse robots to outside customers - early, unquantified.
- The dependence on the parent is rising, not falling: JD Group ISC revenue RMB 19.88B of RMB 30.17B in Q2 2026, with Joybuy (JD's European retail) named as a driver. Related-party pricing is a governance lever worth watching.
- Energy-cost language ("fluctuation of the energy industry", 2026-08-13) shows management expects input-cost pressure; vehicle costs nonetheless fell 0.2pp as a share of revenue.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** Growth is robust and profit is recovering, but margins are not structurally widening yet, and the mix shift toward on-demand delivery offsets the core ISC improvement.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** whether the cheapness is in the earnings or in the cash. On earnings the stock is about 7.6 times trailing profit with a third of its value in pre-lease net cash; on owner cash (after lease payments and rising automation capex) the case is much thinner. The 2026-11-17 third-quarter results are the next read on both.

**Moat:** scale-cost and network (the densest self-operated warehouse network in China, about 1,600 warehouses and 34 million square metres, plus the JD.com anchor volume). Returns are low (ROIC about 1%, net margin about 3%), so the moat protects volume more than pricing - narrow, stable. **Secular threat:** manageable - automation and autonomous delivery are being adopted by the company itself rather than used against it, and e-commerce channel shift is a tailwind for a logistics provider. The cheapness reads as a fear print on China and thin margins, not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Kia is a profitable, growing carmaker priced as if its earnings were about to halve again. At 97,000 won (FMP close 2026-11-09) the market value is about 37.7 trillion won, of which about 21.2 trillion is net cash (cash and short-term investments of 23.5 trillion against 2.25 trillion of debt including leases, balance sheet of 2026-06-30) - about 54,500 won per share, or 56% of the price. What remains, about 42,500 won per share, buys a car business that earned about 6.9 trillion won of net income over the last four reported quarters (roughly 17,800 won per share) and generated 6.44 trillion won of free cash flow in the twelve months to 2026-06-30. That is about 2.4 times trailing earnings for the operating business. The operating numbers have stabilised after the 2025 US tariff reset: revenue was higher than a year earlier in every 2026 quarter, and Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) brought revenue of 31.6 trillion won, up about 10%, and operating profit of 1.82 trillion, up about 24%, with the operating margin rising to 5.8% from 5.1%. The share price fall from 205,500 won (2026-02-27) is mostly the Korean market, not Kia: the KOSPI index is down about 47% from its high and sister company Hyundai Motor about 65%, against Kia's 53%. The dividend was raised in cash terms (2.64 trillion won paid in Q2 2026, about 6,800 won per share, a 7% yield at today's price). Kia also kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 16.1% to 18.5%), which matters in today's reflationary backdrop. Conditions: operating profit holds at roughly the 2026 run-rate of 1.5-2.8 trillion won a quarter, the cash pile is not spent on value-destroying projects, and the Korean market liquidation does not turn into a lasting earnings shock for exporters.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness may be a permanent Korea discount compounded by a cyclical peak. Net cash in a carmaker is working capital and a buffer for downturns, not money owners can take out; it has sat on the balance sheet for years without closing the gap. US tariffs on Korean cars are now a permanent cost under the Section 301 regime that took effect 2026-07-24, and gross margin was still about 1.7 points below a year earlier in Q2 2026 (18.3% vs 20.0%). The sell-side has been too optimistic for nearly two years - Kia beat estimates in 0 of the last 7 quarters - so the 2027 consensus of 19,663 won per share (range 14,806 to 24,296) should be haircut. Q3 2026 net income fell about 10% to 1.29 trillion won even as operating profit rose, because the usual interest and affiliate income vanished below the operating line, and that has not been explained. Share buybacks, about 0.3 trillion won a quarter through 2025, are absent from the first half of 2026. Higher-for-longer rates squeeze US auto-loan affordability, Chinese electric-vehicle makers compete on price in Europe and emerging markets, and the Korean market is still in a liquidation driven by foreign selling and the memory-chip unwind. A recession could take auto earnings back to 2021 levels (about 4.8 trillion won, roughly 12,000 won per share), and in a forced-selling tape the price can fall below any fundamental floor. What would confirm it: another quarter of falling net income, a cut to the shareholder-return plan, or an operating margin below 5%.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the price implies Kia's earnings are about to fall sharply again, and the numbers do not show it. At 97,000 won the operating car business is valued at roughly 42,500 won per share after net cash, about 2.4 times trailing earnings, while operating profit in the quarter ended 2026-09-30 rose about 24% on a year earlier. The sell-off is being driven by the Korean market as a whole (KOSPI down about 47% from its high) rather than by Kia-specific news. Where the street has been wrong in the other direction: consensus has been too high for nearly two years (beats in 0 of 7 quarters), so we haircut the 2027 consensus of 19,663 won per share rather than rely on it. Our fair value does not need the consensus to be right; it needs operating earnings to hold near the 2026 run-rate.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): the Korean market liquidation may not be over - foreign outflows and the memory-chip unwind have taken the KOSPI down about 47%, and Kia falls with it regardless of results (down 3.3% today while Toyota and GM rose about 4-5%). A weaker won helps exports but raises the dollar cost for foreign holders, which can keep them selling. US tariffs under the Section 301 regime in force since 2026-07-24 are a permanent cost, and rising real rates hurt US car affordability. There is no debt wall and no cash-burn hump: net cash is about 21.2 trillion won. Q4 2026 results (late January 2027) are the next checkpoint; another below-the-line surprise like Q3 would hurt sentiment.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure: the selling so far looks like a sector-wide and market-wide liquidation rather than Kia-specific forced selling - Korean equities lost about 22% in July 2026 alone, a large levered fund was margin-called and liquidated in late July according to the regime log, and foreign investors have been de-risking Korea. Kia is a large, liquid index weight and so gets sold with the market. The shareholder base is not yield-focused enough for a dividend cut to trigger mechanical selling, and none has been announced; the dividend was raised in cash terms in Q2 2026.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds: Kia is still growing (revenue up about 10% and operating profit up about 24% in the quarter ended 2026-09-30) and sits on about 21.2 trillion won of net cash, more than half of its 37.7 trillion won market value. At 97,000 won the stock trades well below our base fair value of 135,000 won, a discount that clears the 20% entry bar for the current reflationary backdrop. The fall from 205,500 won since late February is mostly a Korean market liquidation (KOSPI down about 47% from its high, Hyundai Motor down about 65%), not a Kia earnings collapse. We hold conviction at a middling level rather than higher for three reasons: no earnings-call transcript or Q3 release could be read, so management's guidance and the cause of the Q3 net-income drop are unverified; the street's numbers have been too high for nearly two years; and the Korean market tape could keep pushing the price down in the near term. The moat is narrow - scale and a brand that has moved up-market - and tariffs are now a permanent cost, which is why the value case stops short of the top grade. Size it as a position that can sit through further market-driven weakness; the balance sheet means there is no solvency risk on the way.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating: there is no hard dated event. The re-rating would come from (1) the Korean market stabilising, (2) Q4 2026 results in late January 2027 confirming operating profit at or above the 2026 run-rate and clarifying the Q3 below-the-line loss, and (3) a resumption of share buybacks or a larger capital return, which with net cash at 56% of market value Kia can easily afford. picks.bull_thesis: The bull case rests on verified share gains, a funded digital transition and the cleanest balance sheet in European free-to-air television. Share: video advertising fell only 3.1% in 2025 against a market down about 8%, group advertising rose about 1% in the first half of 2026 against a market down about 9% excluding M6, and third-quarter 2026 video advertising rose 6.2% while the market kept falling (release 2026-11-03); group audience share among 25-to-49-year-olds reached 23.5%, up 2.3 points. Digital: M6+ streaming revenue grew 27% to 126 million euros in 2025 and 21.8% to 101.1 million in the first nine months of 2026, on track for the over-200-million target for 2028, helped by Amazon Prime Video and Disney distribution deals. Balance sheet: 130.1 million euros of net cash at 2026-09-30 after repaying a 75-million-euro loan. Costs: an 80-million-euro savings plan to 2030 (about 8% of the cost base, announced 2026-02-17) can rebuild margins once World Cup programme costs drop out in 2027, where consensus sees profit before depreciation of about 245 million euros against roughly 180 million for 2026. And in the background, the French legal bar on a sale of M6 lapses in May 2028, with TF1 on record (June 2026) as still interested. If the market stabilises and the savings land, earnings power near 1.20 euros a share at 11 to 12 times supports the mid-teens.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is arithmetic. Revenue has fallen four years running, from 1.39 billion euros in 2021 to 1.26 billion in 2025, and earnings per share compounded at about minus 18.5% over five years, from 2.22 to 0.98 euros. Share gains do not fix a shrinking pool: the first half of 2026 grew revenue 4.1% on the World Cup yet profit before depreciation fell 34.7%, management attributes half of that to the market, and the third quarter grew EBITA only 4.2% on 9.4% revenue growth with non-recurring cinema and tournament revenue doing much of the lifting (non-advertising revenue up 34.7%, other advertising down 9.8%, audio down 3.3 million). Nine-month EBITA sits at a 10.0% margin. The 1.25-euro dividend (about 157 million euros) exceeds 2026 earnings, was not reaffirmed, and is decided on 2027-02-23 by a finance chief who joined on 2026-10-05; a cut would push yield holders out of a thinly traded, controlled stock. Management concedes some fourth-quarter budgets were pulled into the World Cup, and the fourth quarter is the year's largest. After a 13.5% rise in four weeks the stock trades above any value we can build from declining earnings, and on enterprise value to profit before depreciation it is richer than TF1, which carries far more net cash.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing a recovery into a business whose earnings power is still falling. Consensus models 2027 profit before depreciation of about 245 million euros against about 180 million for 2026 and 214 million delivered in 2025 - roughly 15% above 2025. That needs the World Cup cost to fall away (it will), the 80-million-euro savings plan to deliver meaningfully in year two of five (possible, but progressive by management's own account), and the advertising market to stop falling at high single digits (no evidence: management stayed prudent on 2026-11-03 with no outlook). The 13.5% rally since 2026-10-12 moved the stock further toward that recovery case, not away from it.
picks.valley_of_death: No solvency question - 130.1 million euros of net cash at 2026-09-30. The tests are operational and capital-allocation: the fourth quarter, the largest advertising quarter, must be delivered after a World Cup that management conceded pulled some budgets forward (2026-07-28); and the dividend decision on 2027-02-23, where a fourth 1.25-euro payout costs about 157 million euros against 2026 earnings well below that, presented by a finance chief who joined on 2026-10-05.
picks.positioning_washout: A wash-out - a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers - has not happened and the stock is moving the other way, up about 13.5% in four weeks with the sector. At 11.28 euros the 1.25-euro dividend is an about 11% trailing yield held by income funds and French retail savers; a cut on 2027-02-23 would force them out of a thinly traded, controlled stock. That is the mechanism that could eventually create a buyable price, and it sits after the dividend decision, not before it.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. The one dated fact since our 12 October 2026 look - third-quarter revenue on 3 November 2026 - confirms the business case and does not change the answer: M6 keeps taking share (video advertising up 6.2% against a market down about 9%, streaming up 26.7%), and it now holds 130 million euros of net cash. But that quarter leaned on the July World Cup tail and one-off cinema revenue, nine-month profit margins are 10% against 17% in 2025, programme costs are up 23%, and management offered no fourth-quarter outlook. The thesis holds as a description of a good share-winner inside a structurally shrinking advertising pool, so earnings power is still falling - and a discount to a melting estimate is not a margin of safety, which is why we name no buying level either. Meanwhile the price has run from 9.94 to 11.28 euros in four weeks, alongside TF1, so the stock now sits about a fifth above our 9.30-euro base value; on enterprise value to profit before depreciation it is richer than TF1, ITV and ProSiebenSat.1. Catalysts are soft: the World Cup is spent and consolidation cannot legally happen before May 2028. The event that matters is the dividend decision on 23 February 2027; a cut that forces income holders out could create the price, and stabilising advertising would change the earnings arithmetic - either would bring us back.
picks.forcing_function: Full-year 2026 results and the dividend proposal on 2027-02-23 are the decisive dated event: hold 1.25 euros and income holders stay; cut it and they are forced sellers. Consolidation has a legal date, not a deal date - the bar on a sale of M6 lapses in May 2028 - and no transaction step is visible. A buyback in place of the high payout would be the most constructive trigger; none has been announced.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# MMT.PA - Groupe M6 (Metropole Television) - forensic dossier

As of 2026-11-09. Price used: 11.28 euros (Euronext Paris, MMT.PA, FMP live quote 2026-11-09). Sources: full-year 2025 call (2026-02-17), first-half 2026 call (2026-07-28), third-quarter 2026 revenue release (2026-11-03, as reported by abcbourse and Zonebourse/Bourse Direct), prior committee record dated 2026-10-12.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has been stable for a year: M6 is the share-winner in a shrinking French television advertising market, funding a streaming transition (M6+) and cutting costs (an 80-million-euro savings plan to 2030, announced 2026-02-17) while paying a 1.25-euro dividend. In February 2026 the emphasis was transformation and cost; in July 2026 it was the World Cup (sole French broadcaster of 54 matches, 11 June to 19 July 2026) and outperformance against a market down about 9%. The third-quarter release on 2026-11-03 extended the same arc: revenue up 9.4% to 294.5 million euros, video advertising up 6.2% to 199.2 million against a market Zonebourse puts at about minus 9%, streaming up 26.7% to 30.9 million. The narrative has not shifted toward a market recovery: management "remains prudent" on political, geopolitical and economic uncertainty and gave no fourth-quarter guidance.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

- Share gains: corroborated. 2025 video advertising minus 3.1% against a market about minus 8%; first half 2026 group advertising up about 1% against minus 9% excluding M6; third quarter 2026 video advertising up 6.2%. Part of the third quarter is the July World Cup tail, which management said would be roughly neutral to profit (28 July 2026).
- Profit: the claim of resilience is weaker than the revenue line. Nine-month operating profit before amortisation of acquired intangibles (EBITA) was 93.4 million euros, a 10.0% margin, with video programme costs up to 447.0 million from 362.5 million. First-half profit before depreciation fell 34.7%. The third quarter alone grew EBITA only 4.2% on 9.4% revenue growth.
- Non-advertising revenue jumped 34.7% to 65.3 million in the third quarter on cinema and World Cup items - non-recurring.
- Balance sheet: net cash of 130.1 million euros at 2026-09-30 versus 139.9 million at 2025-12-31, after repaying a 75-million-euro Schuldschein (German private-placement loan) in July. The third-quarter cash inflow of 166.7 million (versus 16.1 million a year earlier) is largely the collection of World Cup and seasonal receivables, so it should not be annualised. The 2026-06-30 position (about 65 million of net debt including leases, the prior committee's figure) was the post-dividend seasonal trough.
- Five-year record: revenue 1.39 billion (2021) to 1.26 billion (2025); earnings per share 2.22 to 0.98 euros. The screener's own fair value of 5.51 euros and the minus 51% margin of safety reflect that path.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Confident and promotional on audiences and the World Cup; candid and uncertain on the market. On 28 July 2026 the chief executive could not separate cyclical from structural decline ("difficult to answer") and called the drop "not justified" without predicting it would stop. The 2026-11-03 release keeps that prudence. The tone on the dividend is non-committal ("too early to say", 28 July 2026). Finance-chief change: Jerome Lefebure leaves end-November 2026; Emmanuelle Marti started 2026-10-05.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

M6 does not give numeric profit guidance, which limits the test. What it did say has held: World Cup July effect near zero, streaming growth around a quarter a year (21.8% for nine months), the savings plan ramping progressively. Streaming target of over 200 million euros by 2028 from 126 million in 2025 needs about 17% a year - on track. No credibility breach found.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts (Kepler Cheuvreux, Bernstein, Deutsche Bank on 28 July 2026) pressed on three points: whether fourth-quarter budgets were pulled into the World Cup (management conceded "some part"), the dividend after a margin drop (no answer), and whether the television advertising market has stepped down structurally (no answer). None was resolved by the third-quarter release, which carried no outlook.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red: earnings per share compounding at about minus 18.5% over five years; gross margin contracting; a 1.25-euro dividend (about 157 million euros) above 2026 earnings and not reaffirmed; programme costs up 23% for nine months; audio revenue falling (31.0 million in the third quarter, down 3.3 million); diversification (real-estate franchises) in decline; two Supervisory Board resignations replaced provisionally by RTL Group/Bertelsmann executives (2026-11-03) - governance is in the controlling holder's hands.
Green: real and repeated share gains; streaming growing about 22-27%; net cash of 130 million at 2026-09-30; Piotroski 8 of 9; the cleanest balance sheet among European free-to-air broadcasters; third-quarter EBITA up 4.2%.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The third-quarter beat came with non-advertising revenue up 34.7% and other advertising down 9.8%: the core is still a video-advertising business taking share in a falling pool.
- The share price moved from 9.94 euros (2026-10-12) to 11.28 euros (2026-11-09), up about 13.5%; TF1 moved from 5.78 to 6.48 euros, up about 12%, over the same window. The re-rating is mostly sector-wide, not a verdict on M6's own quarter.
- Bertelsmann/RTL Group placing its own executives on the board is consistent with the holder managing the asset ahead of the May 2028 end of the legal bar on a sale - speculative, no dated step.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

A well-run, low-debt share-winner in a structurally shrinking market. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly in form (high payout) but the payout exceeds current earnings and is undecided until full-year results on 2027-02-23. The latest dated numbers (2026-11-03) confirm the operating claims and do not change the earnings arithmetic. At 11.28 euros the price sits above any fair value this committee can build from declining earnings power.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning.

Enterprise value 1,101 million euros. I carry the adverse case at 5.50 euros on the judgement that a franchise still producing over 100 million euros of free cash flow with a net-cash balance sheet rarely holds a 3.5-times multiple for long; it sits on the screening model's own whole-company value of 5.51 euros. There is no structural floor: no tender, no deal terms, and net cash at its seasonal peak is only about 1 euro a share.
picks.risk_reward: At 11.28 euros the base value of 9.30 euros sits below the price and the adverse value of 5.50 euros well below it; only the favourable case (15.00 euros, which needs a market recovery and a consolidation premium) is above. The pipeline computes the ratios from these levels; qualitatively the downside to the base case outweighs the upside to the favourable case.

On enterprise value to profit before depreciation, which counts balance sheets, M6 is the richer name: at 11.28 euros its market value is about 1.42 billion euros less roughly 40 million euros of normalised net cash, about 7 times trailing profit before depreciation, while TF1 at 6.48 euros (2026-11-09) carries considerably more net cash against a larger profit base. ITV (66.9 pence) and ProSiebenSat.1 (3.23 euros) trade on lower multiples still. The rally since 2026-10-12 was shared - M6 up about 13.5%, TF1 up about 12% - so the whole group moves on the same French and European advertising driver; any gap between them is sector exposure, not name-specific edge. M6 deserves some premium for the cleanest balance sheet and the only visible share gains, but not enough to call it cheap against the cohort.
picks.thesis_evidence: The operating claims hold on the latest dated numbers. Third-quarter 2026 (released 2026-11-03): video advertising up 6.2% against a market estimated down about 9%, streaming up 26.7%, group audience share among 25-to-49-year-olds 23.5%, up 2.3 points; nine-month streaming revenue up 21.8% to 101.1 million euros; net cash 130.1 million euros at 2026-09-30. First half 2026 (2026-07-28): advertising up about 1% against minus 9% excluding M6. Nothing dated disproves the share-winner, streaming or balance-sheet claims. The thesis we hold is a description of a good business; the pass rests on earnings power still falling inside a shrinking pool (nine-month EBITA margin 10.0%, programme costs up 23%), not on a broken claim. The price rise from 9.94 euros (2026-10-12) to 11.28 euros (2026-11-09) came with TF1 up about 12% - a sector rebound, not company-specific forced buying or selling.
picks.macro_fit_note: The backdrop is reflation (growth up, real GDP about 3.4% annualised; inflation hot and sticky) in a debt-cycle phase where positive real long-term rates reward cash flow now and punish long-dated stories, with an expected horizon of about 18 months. M6 is a cash-now business at about 11 times free cash flow, which suits that phase, and it kept its margins through 2021-22 (gross margin 31.6% to 31.7%, operating margin up 4.8 points); but sticky inflation squeezes consumer brands' advertising budgets and programme costs, so on the net a mild headwind. No pass-through evidence in the transcript: on 2026-07-28 management described a falling advertising market and cost cutting, not price increases sticking.

picks.bull_thesis:
OPmobility, the renamed Plastic Omnium, is a family-controlled French car-parts maker whose shares, at EUR 9.62 on the Paris market (live quote, 10 November 2026), sit about 7% above a 52-week low after halving from EUR 18.16. The bullish case is that the 7 October guidance cut reset expectations to a level the business can beat, and the 21 October revenue release is the first sign it is holding that line.

First, the top line has stabilised. Third-quarter revenue rose 2.8% like-for-like to EUR 2,437 million, with Europe up 8.6% and the rest of Asia up 12.3%, and management confirmed every reduced target on 21 October, two weeks after cutting them.

Second, deleveraging survives. Net debt including leases was EUR 1.43 billion at 30 June 2026 and is promised lower at end-2026 even after EUR 120-130 million of restructuring. Free cash flow above EUR 220 million is about 16% of today's EUR 1.38 billion market value.

Third, self-help and consolidation. The 770-job European restructuring should save something like EUR 50-60 million a year from 2027-28; the fuel-tank franchise is gaining share (21% to 23%, aim 30% by 2030); and the Hyundai Mobis lighting business is being bought for about EUR 390 million, roughly 0.24 times its EUR 1.6 billion of sales, which could add scale cheaply if its margin holds.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bearish case is that the guidance cut confirmed the structural problem the numbers had been signalling for two years, and that the stock is still not cheap against its nearest peers.

First, pricing power is absent. Gross margin (sales less direct production costs) fell from 11.0% in 2023 to 10.9% in 2024, 9.4% in 2025 and 9.6% in the first half of 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier. On 22 July management called second-half resin cost recovery from customers 'really hard to anticipate'; on 7 October it cited cost swings and weaker customers. Oddo BHF read the cut as sector-wide: cost pressure, inability to pass on inflation, overcapacity and weak volumes.

Second, returns sit below the cost of capital and are falling. Return on invested capital peaked near 7.0% in 2025, was 6.4% in the year to June 2026, and an operating profit guided down about 10% takes it lower again. A business earning less than its capital costs does not deserve a premium multiple.

Third, credibility took a hit. The 2026 targets were confirmed on 22 July and cut eleven weeks later; the restructuring management said was 'not embedded in our figures' has arrived. The Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition is still unpriced and unfinanced in public, and the hydrogen projects that were part of the long-term story are being cancelled.

Fourth, leverage magnifies everything. Net debt of EUR 1.43 billion is about the same size as the EUR 1.35 billion market value, so each 1% change in operating earnings moves the equity value by roughly 2%. At EUR 9.46 the enterprise value (market value plus net debt) is about EUR 2.82 billion, or about 3.3 times the roughly EUR 850 million of operating cash earnings (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) the new guidance implies - still above Valeo and Forvia at about 2.4 and 2.7 times when last struck on 31 August, before the sector fell further on 8 October. And the screen's 'deep value' flag rests partly on a data error: the feed adds two years of half-yearly results into one 'trailing' year, doubling earnings per share (EUR 2.49 supplied versus about EUR 1.37 true) and free cash flow.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is small. At about 3.3 times this year's operating cash earnings and about 6 times guided free cash flow the stock looks cheap until set against Valeo and Forvia, which trade lower still. We agree with the market's doubt about the margin story: four years of falling gross margin and the October cut show the company cannot pass on input costs. Where we may differ is on cash discipline: management kept the net-debt promise through the cut and reconfirmed it on 21 October, and if EUR 220 million of free cash flow and lower year-end debt are delivered in February the stock could re-rate toward our EUR 11.15 base case. That is a wager on proof that has not arrived, and the newly priced EUR 390 million Hyundai Mobis deal means 2027 debt will rise again on completion.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the period when the thesis is most exposed before it can be proven) runs from now to the full-year results in late February 2027. Four hazards sit inside it. First, the second-half cash bridge: H1 operating cash flow was flattered by EUR 97 million of slower supplier payments that tend to reverse, and factoring (selling receivables early) is being reduced, so even the lowered EUR 220 million needs a decent second half. Second, the restructuring cash: EUR 120-130 million of charges this year, some of which will be paid in 2027. Third, the Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition: if it is priced and debt-funded inside this window it could push leverage back up just as the deleveraging story is all that is left. Fourth, European carmakers - Renault, Stellantis and Volkswagen were all named by analysts in October - are cutting production schedules, which could force a second cut. The dividend, already lower in H1 2026, could also be trimmed at the February results.
picks.positioning_washout: This was not a wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers). The 8 October fall came from company news - the 7 October guidance cut - and was amplified by a same-day sell-off across European car-parts suppliers. About 63% of the shares are held by the Burelle family and cannot be forced out, so the thin free float (about EUR 500 million) moves violently on news but has no mechanical seller behind it. Remaining sellers are income funds if the dividend is cut in February and holders who bought the deleveraging story and now see free cash flow down a quarter. Neither is a dated, forced event to wait for.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for proof: we buy once the full-year 2026 results show free cash flow of at least EUR 220 million and net debt below end-2025, due late February 2027.

Nothing since our 12 October debate changes that answer. On 21 October the company reported third-quarter revenue up 2.8% like-for-like and confirmed the targets it had cut two weeks earlier, which is what it needed to say but not yet proof: cash flow and debt are only reported with the full-year results. The thesis is in doubt until then. The same release priced the Hyundai Mobis lighting deal at about EUR 390 million, to close in the second half of 2027; we treat it as roughly value-neutral, but it will lift debt again after the year-end test.

At EUR 9.62 our base-case value of about EUR 11.15 a share is roughly 16% above the price - short of the 20% margin we require in today's environment of growth with sticky inflation - against an adverse case near EUR 5.15, and the stock is still priced above Valeo and Forvia on enterprise value to operating cash earnings. Conviction stays at 2: a low-return, leveraged supplier with falling margins, where the only clean support is the cash-and-debt promise we are waiting to see kept.
picks.forcing_function: The one dated event that settles the question is the full-year 2026 results, expected late February 2027 (the prior year's came on 25 February 2026), when the reduced free cash flow, year-end net debt, restructuring cash and 2027 outlook are reported together. The 21 October revenue release has passed without testing cash. Completion of the Hyundai Mobis lighting deal (second half of 2027) and the European Industrial Accelerator Act have no binding dates.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# OPmobility (OPM.PA) - Forensic Dossier (continuing coverage, 2026-11-10)

Live quote used throughout: EUR 9.62 on Euronext Paris (FMP, 10 November 2026; previous close EUR 9.51). The 52-week range is EUR 9.01 to EUR 18.16, so the stock sits about 7% above its low and well below its 50-day (EUR 10.89) and 200-day (EUR 13.78) averages. Primary sources: the full-year 2025 call (25 February 2026) and first-half 2026 call (22 July 2026) in the transcript file; the 7 October 2026 guidance cut (French financial press); and the third-quarter 2026 revenue release of 21 October 2026 (reported by Ideal Investisseur and Reuters syndication). This file updates the committee's 12 October 2026 dossier; the only new company disclosure since then is the 21 October revenue release.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Through 2025 and into mid-2026 management told a consistent story: a mature French car-parts maker (bumpers and exterior parts, lighting, fuel tanks, assembly modules) that keeps paying down debt whatever the car market does. On 7 October 2026 that story was cut back: 2026 operating profit guided to EUR 430-450 million (from an improvement on 2025's EUR 490 million), free cash flow (the cash left after investment) to "above EUR 220 million" (from EUR 250-300 million), and a European restructuring of about 770 jobs costing EUR 120-130 million. The shares fell about 20% on 8 October.

On 21 October 2026 management reported third-quarter revenue of EUR 2,437 million, up 2.8% on a like-for-like basis (same scope, constant currency), and confirmed every one of the lowered targets, including lower net debt at end-2026 than at end-2025. Nine-month revenue was EUR 7,639 million, up 1.1% like-for-like. The narrative is now one of holding the reduced line rather than recovering it.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Data-feed error, still present: OPmobility reports half-yearly and the feed files each half as a quarter, so the supplied trailing figures double-count. The trailing earnings per share of EUR 2.49 is really about EUR 1.37, and the trailing free cash flow of EUR 890 million is really about EUR 445 million. The screen's 3.0 times price-to-free-cash-flow is wrong; on the EUR 220 million guidance the shares trade at about 6.2 times this year's free cash flow at a EUR 1.38 billion market value.
- Gross margin (sales less direct production costs) has fallen every year: 11.0% in 2023, 10.9% in 2024, 9.4% in 2025, 9.6% in the first half of 2026 against 11.3% a year earlier. Pricing power is the weak point and nothing in the October revenue release addresses it (it carries no margin data).
- Third-quarter mix: Exterior and Lighting EUR 1,081 million (+4.1% like-for-like), Modules EUR 721 million (+3.2%), Powertrain EUR 635 million (+0.5%). Europe rose 8.6% like-for-like, led by Eastern Europe; North America fell 5.9% reported; China economic revenue (including joint ventures) fell 33.2% like-for-like to EUR 195 million, and joint-venture sales fell 19.0%. The consolidated top line is holding; the equity-accounted China income behind it is shrinking fast.
- Return on invested capital peaked near 7.0% in 2025 and was 6.4% for the year to June 2026; with operating profit guided down about 10%, 2026 will be lower - below a sensible cost of capital for a leveraged cyclical.
- Balance sheet at 30 June 2026: borrowings EUR 1.94 billion plus leases EUR 0.31 billion less cash EUR 0.815 billion = net debt EUR 1.43 billion including leases (about EUR 1.12 billion excluding leases). This file uses the lease-inclusive figure.
- Hyundai Mobis lighting acquisition, now priced: enterprise value 600 billion won (about EUR 390 million at the 29 September 2026 rate) for a business with about EUR 1.6 billion of 2025 revenue and a positive operating margin, completion targeted for the second half of 2027 subject to approvals. Management says it should not significantly affect deleveraging. At about 0.24 times sales it is not expensive, but it is roughly a quarter of today's net debt added on completion, and the margin of the acquired business is not disclosed.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
February 2026: confident, "improvement" on every line. July 2026: careful - resin unhedged, second-half cost recovery "really hard to anticipate", restructuring "not embedded in our figures". October 7: retreat on profit and cash. October 21: steady, factual confirmation of the reduced targets with a positive like-for-like quarter. The slide in tone has stopped for now, but there is no sign of a rebuild.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Damaged and not yet repaired. The 2025 free-cash-flow and deleveraging targets were met, but the 2026 targets were confirmed on 22 July and cut eleven weeks later. The 21 October reconfirmation is two weeks after the cut and carries little information about cash: the free-cash-flow and net-debt figures are only tested at the full-year results, expected late February 2027 (the prior year's were published 25 February 2026).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
July call: the second-half cash bridge (EUR 97 million of slower supplier payments that tend to reverse, less factoring - selling receivables early), the then-unpriced Hyundai Mobis deal, and the European Industrial Accelerator Act (no timetable). October: Deutsche Bank cut its target from EUR 14 to EUR 11; Oddo BHF from EUR 21 to EUR 15, calling the causes sector-wide. No newer dated target changes were found for November.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: guidance cut eleven weeks after reconfirmation; gross margin down four years in five; returns below cost of capital; China joint-venture revenue down a third; a EUR 390 million acquisition to be paid in 2027 on a balance sheet whose net debt roughly equals the market value; hydrogen projects cancelled.
Green: reduced targets reconfirmed on 21 October with a positive like-for-like quarter; Europe growing 8.6%; net debt promised lower at end-2026; fuel-tank global share rising (21% to 23%, aim 30% by 2030); Burelle family control (about 63%) rules out forced selling of most of the register; restructuring savings should help 2027-28.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The fall in China joint-venture income will not show in consolidated revenue but does reduce equity-accounted profit and dividends up from the joint ventures, which feed net income and cash.
- The Hyundai Mobis deal doubles the lighting exposure, a segment that has struggled with launch costs; it is a bet on scale in a low-margin line, priced cheaply for a reason.
- Free float is about 37% of shares (about EUR 510 million at today's price), so moves overshoot both ways on thin news.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A competent, honest-enough management running a structurally low-return, leveraged business in a weak cycle. Nothing since 12 October changes the committee's read: the 21 October release confirmed the reduced targets but cannot test them, and the newly priced Hyundai Mobis deal adds about EUR 390 million of commitments in 2027. The proof point is unchanged - full-year 2026 results in late February 2027, where the EUR 220 million free cash flow and the lower net debt are delivered or not.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening.

Margins were squeezed in the 2021-22 inflation, and higher real rates lower what infrastructure buyers pay for projects. Once the Centennial Flats cash is booked, the next leg needs fresh project sales that may not come quickly. What would confirm it: another impairment in Q3 or Q4 2026, a Q3 that shows the Centennial gain largely offset by write-downs, or no new sale before mid-2027.

Where we disagree mildly is on the next two quarters: the Q3 report (2026-11-13) and phase three of Centennial Flats should add about SEK 11-12 a share of pre-tax value from cash already received or contracted, so end-2026 book should be SEK 55-57 rather than the SEK 51.5 on screens. # Eolus AB (EOLU-B.ST) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-09. Prices in Swedish kronor (SEK), Stockholm B-share listing.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript was available: the paid data feed (FMP) holds none for this listing, the Quartr connector requires a subscription we do not have, and the web-search budget for this run was exhausted. This deep dive therefore rests on the company's own dated press releases and interim reports fetched from eolus.com (year-end report preliminary release 2026-01-27, capital-allocation update 2026-03-30, Q2 interim report 2026-08-27, Centennial Flats release 2026-08-14, offshore permit rejection 2026-07-16, U.S. project sale 2026-09-04) plus FMP quarterly statements. No transcript quotes are given because none were read; the short phrases quoted below come from those press releases.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Eolus is a wind, solar and battery project developer: it secures land and permits, often builds the project, then sells it to a long-term owner and keeps a fee-earning asset-management role (1,271 MW of turbines managed at 30 June 2026). Earnings therefore arrive in lumps when projects are handed over, and the balance sheet - project inventory plus cash - is the real measure of value.

The story has narrowed sharply in twelve months:
- **Late 2025:** a growth narrative built on a very large pipeline (26.2 GW at 30 June 2025, including 8.8 GW of offshore wind) and a target of at least SEK 1,400 million cumulative operating profit for 2025-2027.
- **2026-01-27:** the turn. About SEK 240 million of impairments (SEK 166 million offshore, SEK 74 million onshore in Sweden, Finland and the US), offshore cut from 8.8 GW to 1.0 GW, the 1,400 million target withdrawn and replaced by a return-on-equity goal above 15%, equity/assets above 30% and a 20-50% payout policy.
- **2026 so far:** a self-described "pure-play developer with a strong financial position" navigating "a hesitant market" (Q2 report, 2026-08-27). The growth that does show up is in the United States, mainly batteries: the Roccasecca 127 MW battery project sold all-cash to a large US power producer (2026-02-13), Centennial Flats milestone payments and a raised forecast (2026-08-14), and a mid-stage US solar-plus-battery project sold for up to USD 6.5 million (2026-09-04). On 2026-07-16 the Swedish government rejected the Västvind and Najaderna offshore permits, effectively closing the remaining offshore story.

The arc is a pivot from "large pipeline, big profit target" to "smaller, cash-generative developer that returns capital", with the US battery business doing the heavy lifting.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (source, date) | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong financial position" (Q2 report, 2026-08-27) | Net cash SEK 227m at 30 June 2026 vs net debt SEK 698m a year earlier; equity/assets 65%; SEK 71m of bonds repurchased 2026-06-02, SEK 479m nominal outstanding | Supported |
| Value sits in the project portfolio | Inventory (project rights and work in progress) SEK 1,091m at 30 June 2026, about SEK 44 per share; equity per share SEK 51.54 vs SEK 64.67 a year earlier | Partly supported - book value per share fell 20% in a year, mainly through the 2025 loss and impairments |
| Pipeline scale | 14,797 MW at 30 June 2026 vs 26,198 MW a year earlier; only 155 MW under construction (343 MW a year earlier) | Story poorer than before - the headline pipeline halved, and near-term handovers are thin |
| Profit delivery | FY2025 net loss SEK 346m (impairments about 240m); H1 2026 operating profit SEK 177m but Q2 alone SEK -64m on SEK 12m of sales | Lumpy; first-half profit came from the Q1 Roccasecca sale |
| Centennial Flats upside (2026-08-14) | About USD 25m received on two phases reaching commercial operation, about USD 20m net positive to Q3 operating profit and cash flow; about USD 12m more expected when phase three reaches commercial operation "before end of 2026" | Concrete and cash-backed; Q3 (reported 2026-11-13) should show it |
| Shareholder returns | No dividend for FY2025 - bond terms bar it after the 2025 loss (2026-03-30); buyback authorisation exercised from 2026-08-28 | Buyback is real but small relative to a SEK 1.24 billion market value |

The screener's "P/FCF 0.7x" and "revenue +360%" are artefacts of project-sale timing (a big 2025 handover year after a thin 2024) and should not be read as run-rate economics.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Stable to slightly defensive.** The January 2026 release was a reset: targets withdrawn, impairments taken. Since then the language is about balance-sheet strength and discipline ("well equipped to navigate a hesitant market") rather than growth targets. The reaction to the offshore rejection was measured ("We will now carefully analyze the decisions and their consequences", 2026-07-16). The tone moved from offensive (pipeline size, profit target) to defensive (capital strength, cash returns) - typical of a developer in a soft Nordic power-price market.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
**Low to Medium.** The 2025-2027 cumulative operating-profit target of SEK 1,400 million was withdrawn barely a year into its window (2026-01-27), after a full-year 2025 operating loss of about SEK 310 million. The screener records an earnings beat on only 1 of the last 7 quarters (14%). On the other side, the more granular, project-level forecasts have held or been raised: Centennial Flats remaining proceeds were raised on 2026-08-14 and the cash arrived. The pattern is that top-down targets fail while project-specific cash calls are reliable.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
No call transcript was available, so analyst questions cannot be quoted. The obvious pressure points from the record are: (a) what the Swedish and Finnish onshore pipeline is actually worth when Nordic power prices are weak and buyers are "hesitant"; (b) whether more of the SEK 1,091 million inventory needs writing down (the remaining SEK 48 million of Västvind costs after the 2026-07-16 rejection is the first candidate); (c) how many megawatts will be handed over in 2027 when only 155 MW is under construction; (d) when the bond terms allow a dividend again.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: Financial target withdrawn and about SEK 240m of impairments (2026-01-27).
- Red: Pipeline down from 26.2 GW to 14.8 GW in a year; under-construction volume more than halved (Q2 2026).
- Red: Offshore permits for Västvind and Najaderna rejected by the government (2026-07-16); about SEK 48m of Västvind capitalised costs exposed.
- Red: Book value per share down from SEK 64.67 to SEK 51.54 year on year (Q2 2026).
- Red: Margins were squeezed in the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 11.7% to 4.9%), so inflation is a known pressure point.
- Green: Net cash SEK 227m versus net debt SEK 698m a year earlier; bond repurchase 2026-06-02.
- Green: Roccasecca battery sale completed all-cash (2026-02-13); Centennial Flats milestones paid and forecast raised (2026-08-14).
- Green: Share buyback started (2026-08-28) after a bond-terms amendment, at roughly book value.
- Green: Asset-management fees on 1,271 MW provide a small recurring base.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The shift in the financial goals from an absolute profit number to return-on-equity and payout ratios signals a board now focused on capital returns rather than scale.
- The company is quietly recycling capital out of mid-stage US projects (2026-09-04 sale for up to USD 6.5m, mostly milestone-contingent) rather than carrying them to completion - consistent with conserving cash.
- Buying back stock at about book value is management's own signal that it sees the portfolio as worth at least what it is carried at.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
**Trajectory: pivoting.** Eolus is turning from a pipeline-growth story into a smaller, cash-rich developer leaning on US batteries and returning capital. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing is whether the SEK 1,091 million of project inventory (about SEK 44 of the SEK 51.5 per-share book value) can be sold at or above cost: the stock trades at roughly 0.95 times book, so the whole case is a bet that the book is real and that the cash keeps coming.

**Moat:** none in the economic sense. Project development is competitive, and returns on equity (5.3%) and on invested capital (4.3%) are below the cost of capital. The edge is local permitting know-how and the asset-management relationships, which are real but not a moat. **Secular threat:** manageable - the energy transition is a tailwind for demand, but Nordic onshore wind faces low capture prices and permitting politics; this is cyclical and political, not a terminal decline. The cheapness is a modest discount to book, not a deep fear print.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · no real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis:
Jet2 is the best-run leisure travel business in the United Kingdom, trading at roughly seven times its earnings and about six times its free cash flow. The bull case is that the market is pricing a cyclical squeeze as if it were permanent.

The evidence: revenue reached a record 7.48 billion pounds in the year to March 2026 (up 4.3%), passengers passed 20 million, and free cash flow was 495 million pounds - 2.6 billion pounds since the pandemic (FY26 results call, 8 July 2026). Management has a high-credibility record: it flagged its own small miss on flight-only pricing early (November 2025) and landed full-year operating profit inside its 435-440 million pound guide. The September 2026 trading statement showed booked passengers up 8.8% on capacity up 7.6%, with Gatwick ahead of plan.

Three drivers can lift profit from here. First, the newer bases (Bournemouth, Luton and from March 2026 Gatwick) carry start-up costs today and should mature into profit; Gatwick is guided to break even by the year to March 2029. Second, the A321neo fleet (232 seats against 189, lower cost per seat, about 22% of the summer 2026 fleet) lowers unit costs as it grows. Third, the buyback shrinks the share count: about 22 million shares were bought back in the year to March 2026 and a further 250 million pounds runs to 31 May 2027, roughly 9% of today's market value of about 2.7 billion pounds.

Consensus, as cited in the committee's prior record, expects earnings per share to recover toward 188p for the year to March 2028 and 243p for the year to March 2029. On those numbers the stock trades at about eight and six times earnings respectively, with a balance sheet that carries roughly break-even own net debt and an undrawn 500 million pound credit line. If flight-only pricing stabilises and Gatwick scales, a multiple of nine to ten times recovery earnings gives 1,700-2,150p.

Conditions: flight-only yields stop falling, hotel cost inflation moderates toward package price growth, and no large demand shock (conflict, recession) hits the 2027 summer booking season.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case is that Jet2's profit has stopped growing even as it adds capacity, and that the cheap multiple reflects a narrowing moat in a crowded market rather than a mispricing.

The evidence: net income fell from 447 million pounds (FY25) to 410 million pounds (FY26) while seat capacity grew about 8%. Flight-only ticket yield fell 7% in both the November 2025 and July 2026 calls; management calls this 'investing in price' and 'investing in load factor', which is another way of saying it cannot hold fares. Hotel costs, 45% of the cost base, rose about 6.5% while package prices rose 3%, of which about one point was customers trading up. Return on capital employed slipped from a 17% three-year average to 14.4%, and our scan's return on invested capital of 6.4% is near the cost of capital. Free cash flow fell about 25% year on year as bookings moved closer to departure.

The headline net cash of about 2.0 billion pounds is mostly customer deposits; the CFO himself put own cash at about 1.2 billion pounds, roughly equal to the 1.28 billion pounds of debt including leases. In a shock those deposits become a refund liability, not a cushion, and the new 2 times leverage target signals more borrowing to fund the Airbus order book. Consensus earnings for the year to March 2027 of about 136p (cited in the prior record) imply the stock is not cheap on this year's numbers at about 11 times.

What would confirm the bear case: the 18 November 2026 interim results showing summer 2026 profit flat or down despite higher passenger numbers, winter flight-only yields still falling, or capacity guidance for summer 2027 that again outruns the market. The business is also exposed to inflation: its gross margin fell from 13.8% to a loss through the 2021-22 period (largely pandemic-driven), and it has shown only partial pass-through of hotel cost increases.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is not pricing terminal decline; it is pricing a profit plateau. Seven brokers average a target of about 1,617p (MarketBeat aggregator, 3 November 2026), only about 6% above today's price, with five buys and two holds. Our base case of 1,720p sits a little above that, so the disagreement with the market is modest. Where we differ is on composition: the street leans on the headline 2.0 billion pounds of net cash, which we largely exclude because most of it is customer deposits, and on the recovery in earnings per share to about 188p by the year to March 2028, which we accept only in the base case. The street may also be too relaxed about flight-only yield, which has fallen 7% in two reporting periods running. We do not see a large expectations gap at 1,525p.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation risk, debt wall or forced dilution: own cash roughly matches debt, the 500 million pound facility is undrawn to October 2030, and the fleet is financed through long-dated asset-backed borrowing. The risk over the next three to nine months is earnings disappointment. The 18 November 2026 interim results could show summer 2026 profit flat despite more passengers, and the winter booking season (typically sold from January) has been late and price-led in each of the last two years. Hotel cost inflation, sustainable aviation fuel mandates (32 million pounds of extra premium in FY26) and employment-tax rises all pressure margins. A demand shock - renewed Middle East conflict hitting eastern Mediterranean bookings, as in spring 2026, or a UK consumer slowdown - would compress the customer-deposit float and free cash flow quickly. Any of these could take the shares back toward the 1,250p entry level.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-seller setup specific to Jet2: no index deletion, no lock-up, no dividend cut to drive out yield holders, and the company itself is a steady buyer through the 250 million pound buyback. The path to 1,250p is a sector-wide sell-off: European leisure and airline shares de-rate together on fuel spikes, geopolitical shocks or UK consumer weakness, as they did in March 2026 when Jet2 set a 12-month low near 980p. That is why the wait is tied to a sector or style sell-off rather than to mechanical selling.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 1,250p, which a sector-wide sell-off of UK consumer and airline shares could deliver.

The thesis holds. Jet2 is a well-run, cash-generative leisure travel business with credible management, a strong own-cash position and an aggressive buyback. Nothing dated has changed since the committee's last look on 19 October 2026; the price has moved only from 1,510p to 1,525p.

The issue remains the price, not the business. Our fair value is about 1,720p, only about 13% above today's 1,525p, which does not clear the 20% bar we require in a growth-with-sticky-inflation backdrop, while the adverse case of about 1,200p is about 21% below. At 1,250p the trade becomes attractive: about 38% upside to fair value against little downside to the adverse case. The shares were near 980p as recently as March 2026, so a sector-wide sell-off of that kind is not far-fetched.

We hold the value case at a middle rating. The moat is real but narrow and being tested: profit fell in FY26 while capacity grew about 8%, flight-only fares have been cut 7% two periods running, and return on capital has slipped from 17% to 14.4%. Until pricing stabilises, the low multiple partly reflects a business that is buying growth with price, which limits how much we will pay.

The interim results on 18 November 2026 are the next dated test. A clear profit increase with stable winter yields would strengthen the case; a profit fall with more price-cutting would argue for a lower fair value.
picks.forcing_function: No single event forces a re-rating. The nearest dated checkpoint is the interim results on 18 November 2026, which will show whether summer 2026 converted higher bookings into profit and give the first read on winter pricing. Beyond that, the forcing mechanism is slow: the buyback steadily retiring stock to May 2027, Gatwick progressing toward break-even by the year to March 2029, and the summer 2027 capacity and yield guidance, typically given in the new year. A re-rating needs evidence that flight-only pricing has stopped falling.
