# Jet2 plc (JET2.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

Debate date: 16 November 2026. Live price 1,525p (FMP quote, London listing, pence). Transcripts read: interim results call of 19 November 2025 (half year to 30 September 2025) and full-year results call of 8 July 2026 (year to 31 March 2026). The next dated release is the interim results for the half year to 30 September 2026, scheduled for 18 November 2026 (FMP earnings calendar), two days after this debate.

The short version: management is credible and conservative, the balance sheet is strong, and the cash returns are real. But the last eighteen months show a business that is growing passengers by giving away price, with profit flat to slightly down while capacity grows about 8% a year. That is a narrow moat that is being tested, not a widening one.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

In November 2025 the story was "record numbers" and expansion: passengers up 6%, the new bases at Bournemouth and Luton, and the launch of London Gatwick, described as "a once-in-a-generation opportunity to accelerate our growth" (H1 FY26 call). The Gatwick base was explicitly not expected to make money until the year to March 2029.

By July 2026 the emphasis had shifted from growth to resilience. The words used most were "resilient", "robust" and "controlled": operating profit "remained resilient even after absorbing Gatwick startup investment costs and wider industry cost pressures" (FY26 call). The growth story is still there (over 20 million passengers, up 5%), but the profit story has become one of absorbing costs. Capital returns moved to the centre: 363 million pounds returned in the year, "more than ever before", and a further 250 million pound buyback to run to 31 May 2027.

A new strand appeared in July 2026: a medium-term leverage target of 2 times net debt to EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) on an own-cash basis. That is a quiet signal that management intends to use more of the balance sheet over time, mainly to finance the Airbus fleet.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record revenue" (FY26) | Revenue 7.48 billion pounds, up 4.3%; three-year growth about 14% a year, flattered by the post-pandemic rebound from 1.23 billion in 2022 | True, but growth has slowed sharply |
| Operating profit "resilient" | Net income fell from 447 million pounds (FY25) to 410 million (FY26); FY26 operating profit guided at 435-440 million against 446.5 million the year before (29 April 2026 trading update) | Profit fell while capacity grew about 8%. "Resilient" is generous |
| Package price "resilient, up 3%" | About 1 point of the 3% came from customers trading up to four- and five-star hotels; hotel costs, 45% of the cost base, rose about 6.5% | Partial pass-through only; the cost of the holiday rose faster than its price |
| Flight-only demand strong (+15% passengers) | Flight-only ticket yield down 7% in both calls | Volume bought with price |
| "Over 2 billion pounds of net cash" | True on the headline basis, but most of it is customer deposits. The CFO himself split out "1.2 billion pounds of our own cash, excluding customer advances"; against about 1.28 billion pounds of debt including leases, own cash is roughly break-even | The headline overstates distributable cash |
| Free cash flow 495 million pounds; 2.6 billion since the pandemic | Consistent with the trailing figures; free cash flow fell about 25% year on year as customers booked later | True, but declining and timing-sensitive |
| Earnings per share "stable" | Earnings per share roughly 208-211p in both FY25 and FY26 - stable only because about 22 million shares were bought back | Per-share stability is buyback-supported |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Trajectory: stable, with a defensive tilt.

- November 2025: confident, expansionary - "Further growth in the first half across all our key metrics." The CFO was candid about uncertainty: "there's a lot of moving parts ... I'm not being evasive, but there are."
- July 2026: still upbeat ("I hope you're as excited about the future as we are"), but the vocabulary moved to cost absorption, "investing in price" and capital returns. On the Middle East conflict, management described later bookings and a bounce-back in eastern Mediterranean destinations rather than a lasting hit.

There is no sign of panic and no sign of rising ambition either. The language is that of a well-run operator in a tougher market.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Reliability: high.

- The November 2025 guide for flight-only pricing was "mid-single digits down"; the CFO volunteered that the outcome was "slightly worse" at minus 7%. Flagging a small miss early is a good sign.
- FY26 operating profit landed inside the 435-440 million pound range guided in April 2026.
- The beat rate in our data is 50% (one of two quarters), and FMP shows the November 2025 half-year earnings per share at 300p against a 281p estimate.
- The July 2026 capital spending cut of about 350 million pounds for the following year was explained as Airbus delivery timing, "timing only, it doesn't undermine any of our growth plans". That is plausible given industry-wide Airbus delays, but it also flatters near-term free cash flow.

No sandbagging pattern, and no pattern of over-promising.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Capacity versus price: analysts asked in both calls whether growing capacity 8-9% when competitors grow less would force further fare cuts. Management answered with flexibility ("we can make adjustments") rather than with yield guidance. This is the central unresolved question.
- Cost per seat: management repeatedly declined to give unit-cost guidance before Eurocontrol fees and slot declarations were known.
- Booking curve: later bookings came up in both calls; management treats them as a timing effect, but they reduce visibility and the customer-deposit float.
- AI distribution (July 2026): asked whether large language models would change how holidays are booked, management said "We've not seen a big impact from LLMs at the moment" and that direct bookings are steady at just under 80% for holidays. Honest, but untested.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Profit falling while capacity grows about 8% a year (April 2026 trading update; FY26 results, July 2026).
- Flight-only yield down 7% two reporting periods running (November 2025, July 2026).
- Return on capital employed down from 17% (three-year average quoted in November 2025) to 14.4% in FY26.
- Hotel cost inflation (about 6.5%) running ahead of package price (3%, of which 1 point is mix).
- Gatwick start-up costs, with profitability not expected until the year to March 2029.

Green flags:
- Strong own-cash position, an undrawn 500 million pound revolving credit facility extended to October 2030.
- Shareholder returns at record levels, with the share count falling: about 22 million shares bought back in FY26 and a further 250 million pounds under way to May 2027.
- Fleet renewal to the A321neo (232 seats against 189, lower seat cost; about 22% of the summer 2026 fleet).
- Industry-leading customer service and low cancellation rates, which support the package-holiday brand.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Investing in price" and "investing in load factor" have become standing phrases. When a company describes price cuts as investments, it is telling you that it does not have the pricing power to hold fares.
- The new 2 times leverage target signals a shift from a cash-rich to a more geared capital structure as the Airbus order book is financed.
- The CFO's own-cash framing (1.2 billion pounds excluding customer advances) is a welcome bit of honesty that the headline net-cash figure hides.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. Capital allocation is disciplined (buybacks at single-digit earnings multiples, fleet renewal, no acquisitions), and management is credible.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: Jet2's profit has stopped growing even as capacity grows. The investment case depends on Gatwick and the newer bases maturing into profit and on flight-only pricing stabilising. The interim results on 18 November 2026 are the next test of whether summer 2026 converted bookings into profit.

Moat: scale-cost plus brand (the integrated package-holiday model, about 80% direct distribution, customer-service reputation). It is real but narrow, and the evidence - return on capital falling from 17% to 14.4%, yields given away to fill seats - says it is being tested rather than widening. Our scan's return on invested capital of 6.4% sits near the cost of capital. Secular threat: manageable. AI-led travel search could change distribution over time, but management reports no impact so far and the direct-booking share is steady. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear-print on a competitive, cost-inflated leisure market, not a structurally shrinking base - but the moat needs proof that pricing can hold.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

The half-year of 23 September 2026 confirmed after-lease free cash flow guidance of £460m-£520m, net cash before leases of £168m (up almost £300m in a year), a 21% higher interim dividend and steady buybacks. The governance clean-up is done. Management is credible on cash and cost, and less so on growth.

Why we pass: profit has fallen three years running, like-for-like sales are negative, and about half the business still depends on Nike's product cycle, which the CEO admits is not creating heat. Our base-case fair value is about 95p, close to today's price, with a plausible downside to about 68p and an upside to about 130p only if the footwear cycle turns. That is no margin of safety. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# JD Sports Fashion (JD.L) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-09. Sources: half-year results calls of 2023-09-21, 2024-10-02, 2025-09-24 and 2026-09-23, plus the screener's fiscal-year financials. Prices are in pence on the London listing (JD.L); the live quote used is 96.28p (FMP, 2026-11-09).*

**Bottom line:** JD is a highly cash-generative retailer whose earnings have been sliding for three years while its balance sheet has been getting steadily stronger. Management is credible on cash and costs and less credible on the top line: each year the story of a "structural growth market" has been replaced by a little more "controlling the controllables". The cash is real; the growth is not, for now.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **September 2023 (H1 FY24):** a governance and expansion story. The chairman talks about a new CFO, CTO and legal counsel, disposing of the fashion brands, buying out minorities in Iberia, Germany and Central Europe, and the pending Courir acquisition in France. Growth is the theme.
- **October 2024 (H1 FY25):** still a growth story — revenue "breaking the £5 billion milestone", JD-brand organic growth of 9%, double-digit organic growth in North America and Europe, and the Hibbett acquisition just closed. Nike's "stumble" is acknowledged as a headwind but framed as diversifiable ("if Nike is a little bit off form, we have New Balance and Adidas").
- **September 2025 (H1 FY26):** the tone shifts to discipline. Priority three of the April 2025 strategy update is "cash generation and shareholder return". Like-for-like sales fall 2.5% and growth comes from acquisitions (Hibbett, Courir) and new space.
- **September 2026 (H1 FY27):** fully defensive. "Our response to a maturing market and challenging trading conditions is to control the controllables." Organic sales fall 0.7%, like-for-like sales (sales at stores open in both years) fall 2.8%, and the store count is 106 lower. The proud line is now cash: net cash before leases of £168m, up almost £300m year on year, and "cash is king and cash is real."

The growth drivers introduced in 2023-24 (US expansion through acquisitions, the "structural growth market") have quietly given way to store productivity, apparel mix and buybacks. The phrase "maturing market" appears for the first time in 2026.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Highly cash-generative business" (every call) | FCF margin 7.9%, FCF up 40% in the latest year; net cash before leases swung from £125m net debt to £168m net cash (Aug 2025 to Aug 2026) after returning £260m | Matches |
| Market-share gains in North America and Europe (2025) | Revenue grew from £10.5bn (FY24) to £12.7bn (FY26), but mostly acquired (Hibbett, Courir); like-for-like negative in 2025 and 2026 | Richer than the numbers |
| Gross margin "maintained through trading discipline" | Gross margin steady around 47-48% for years; the 2026 call admits a 50bp underlying hit from price investment, offset by supplier marketing money | Broadly matches |
| Operating discipline protecting profit | Net income fell from £539m (FY24) to £490m (FY25) to £436m (FY26); H1 FY27 operating profit fell 19.5% and margin 120bp | Diverges — costs are controlled, but margins are not |
| Buybacks create value per share | Adjusted EPS fell 13.7% in H1 FY27 against a steeper fall in pre-tax profit; the share count is shrinking | Matches |

The headline earnings trajectory (EPS 0.10 in FY24 to 0.085 in FY26, down 10% in the latest year) is poorer than a "resilient" narrative implies. The cash trajectory is better than the earnings trajectory, which is the core of the bull case.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining on growth, stable on cash.**
- 2023: expansive ("the pace at JD is quite extraordinary").
- 2024: confident but with caveats (the "legendary UK summer", Nike's stumble).
- 2025: defensive ("a tough couple of years", national insurance rises, governance clean-up).
- 2026: defensive and specific — guidance is given as a fixed range (£700m-£800m pre-tax profit before adjusting items, £460m-£520m free cash flow after leases) and language centres on cost, capital and cash. The CEO concedes "heat created by the market leader... is not today the case", a direct admission that the Nike product cycle still drives the business.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management held its full-year guidance range at the 2024 half year and kept the FY27 range "unchanged from the Q2 trading statement" in September 2026. That FY27 range sits well below the prior year's profit, so the expectation was reset during 2026 rather than met. The screener shows earnings beats in only 3 of the last 7 quarters (43%). There is no clear sandbagging pattern: guidance is reset downward when trading turns, then held. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The footwear cycle and Nike:** analysts asked in 2025 and again in 2026 what it takes for footwear to return to growth. The answer was qualitative (end promotions, wait for new franchises such as the Adidas Samba, On, Salomon). There is no dated recovery marker.
- **Inventory:** management says it is "comfortable" while noting the industry may be too heavy, which is why the market stays promotional.
- **Mexico franchise and US womenswear (2026):** management frames franchising as capital-light growth. It is real but small.
- **Dividend cover:** the CFO signals a progressive dividend toward a yield "around 2-plus percent". The interim dividend was raised 21% to 0.40p.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: like-for-like sales negative in both H1 FY26 (-2.5%) and H1 FY27 (-2.8%).
- Red: three years of falling net income despite revenue up about 20%, so acquisitions have bought revenue but not profit.
- Red: heavy dependence on Nike, about half of revenue by Barclays' estimate, where brand heat is still weak (CEO, 2026-09-23).
- Red: North America operating margin down 220bp in H1 FY27, with the standalone Finish Line business being wound down.
- Green: net cash before leases up almost £300m year on year to £168m (Aug 2026), even after £260m of shareholder returns.
- Green: online sales up 5.2%, apparel up 4% to 36% of the mix, and like-for-like operating costs flat (H1 FY27).
- Green: adjusting items have shrunk to mainly the amortisation of acquired intangibles, so statutory and adjusted profit are converging. This marks the governance clean-up as done.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Fewer, bigger, better stores" has replaced store-count growth as the space story. It signals saturation in mature markets.
- Capital-allocation language has moved from acquisitions (2023-24) to buybacks and dividends (2025-26). This is a classic sign that management sees fewer high-return reinvestment options.
- The CFO now quotes free cash flow after leases as a headline metric, a more conservative and more honest measure than in 2023.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** Earnings are drifting lower, but cash generation, the balance sheet and governance are all improving, and capital returns are rising.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** the stock has already re-rated from about 64p to 96p over the past year and now trades near the top of its 52-week range. At roughly 9 times this year's guided earnings and a free-cash-flow yield of about 10%, it is cheap in absolute terms. Most of the discount to peers is explained by negative like-for-like sales and the Nike dependence, and the recovery in the Nike product cycle has no date.

**Moat:** a narrow scale and brand moat. JD is the preferred wholesale partner of Nike and Adidas for premium allocations, with a multi-brand, multi-country store estate that brands need for reach. The width is modest: return on invested capital is 8%, gross margin is steady around 47-48%, and operating margin is under pressure. Gross margin is not eroding, so the moat is stable rather than shrinking. **Secular threat:** manageable. Brand direct-to-consumer selling (the retail channel shift) was the structural fear, but Nike's partial return to wholesale has eased it. The cheapness reflects a cyclical earnings trough plus supplier concentration, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# China Unicom (Hong Kong) Ltd (0762.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-09. Price used: HK$5.51 (FMP live quote, Hong Kong listing, 2026-11-09). Reported figures are in renminbi (RMB); we convert at about HK$1.17 per RMB, the same rate this committee used last time.*

**Source note.** FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing (transcript-dates lookup returned nothing on 2026-11-09), and this run's shared web-search budget was used up before this name, so no new call commentary could be pulled. This dossier rests on (a) the screener's multi-year financials, (b) FMP's half-year statements, and (c) the dated company disclosures already verified by this committee's reviewer on 2026-11-03: the interim results of 2026-08-18 (HKEX announcement a260818a, carried by Cision/AAP and The Standard) and the nine-month unaudited key data of 2026-10-29 (The Standard). Nothing below quotes a call we did not read.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

From 2021 to 2024 the story was steady, policy-friendly compounding: revenue rose from RMB327.9bn to RMB389.6bn and net profit from RMB14.4bn to RMB20.6bn, with management leaning on "computing power" (cloud, data centres) to offset a mature mobile and broadband base. FY2025 was the first stall - revenue slipped 1.9% to RMB382.1bn and profit was flat at RMB20.3bn.

2026 broke the arc. China reclassified basic telecom services from the 6% to the 9% value-added tax (VAT) band from 1 January 2026, which comes straight out of reported revenue and margin. The 2026-08-18 interim showed attributable profit of RMB9.47bn, down 34.6%, and the board declared no interim dividend (prior year RMB0.2841 per share). Management said the full-year profit contraction was "expected to narrow significantly" as a staff-cost timing effect reversed. The 2026-10-29 nine-month data did not show that narrowing yet: profit RMB13.28bn, down 33.6%, implying a third quarter of roughly RMB3.8bn, down about 31%. The growth engine is still computing power (+12.2% in nine months, data centres +10.4%) while core service revenue edged down 0.28% to RMB260.89bn.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (dated) | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Profit fall will "narrow significantly" in H2 (2026-08-18) | 9M profit -33.6% vs H1 -34.6% (2026-10-29); Q3 alone about -31% | Not yet delivered; the claim now rides entirely on Q4 |
| Computing power is the new growth leg | +12.2% in 9M 2026; data centres +10.4% | Matches, but it is too small to offset a shrinking core |
| Balance sheet is strong | Net cash RMB44.1bn on 2026-06-30 (cash RMB75.4bn vs debt RMB31.3bn incl. leases) | Matches - about RMB1.44 (HK$1.69) per share |
| Cash generation intact | Trailing free cash flow RMB25.0bn (to 2026-06-30); H1 operating cash flow a multi-year high | Matches - cash is far stronger than accounting profit |
| Shareholder returns a priority | Interim dividend cancelled 2026-08-18 | Diverges sharply - the single biggest credibility hit |

Two screener figures are unreliable and we set them aside: the 23.5% ROIC sits beside a 5.2% ROE and is almost certainly a data artefact, and the "TTM EPS 0.66" is still the FY2025 figure - on the 2026 run-rate (about RMB13.3-14bn of profit) earnings per share are nearer RMB0.44-0.46.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining. The 2024-25 language was offensive (computing-power investment, rising payouts). By August 2026 it had turned defensive: a tax explanation for the profit drop, a promise of narrowing, and a dividend withheld without a restoration timetable. We have no transcript to quote the tone directly; the actions speak for it.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-to-Low. The screener shows earnings beats in only 1 of the last 7 quarters (14%). The one explicit 2026 promise (a narrowing profit decline) has not shown up in the third quarter. Delivery on cash flow has been good; delivery on per-share profit and payout has not.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

What investors will push on (inferred from the disclosures, not from a call we read): (1) when and at what level the dividend returns; (2) whether the VAT hit can be priced through, given state-guided tariff discipline; (3) whether the staff-cost reversal is real or a re-labelled run-rate; (4) how much of the data-centre build-out is spending ahead of demand. No FMP analyst price-target coverage exists for this listing, and no dated consensus target could be fetched this run.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: interim dividend cancelled (2026-08-18) for a stock owned by income holders.
- Red: H2 narrowing promised but not visible in Q3 (2026-10-29).
- Red: core service revenue shrinking (-0.28% in 9M 2026) and gross margin contracting.
- Red: shares fell 12% on 2026-08-19 on about eleven times normal volume; price still about 18% below its 200-day average (HK$6.73).
- Green: net cash RMB44.1bn and free cash flow about RMB25bn a year - roughly 15% of the market value per year.
- Green: computing power and data centres growing double digits.
- Green: margins held through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 71.1% to 70.3% on the repo's resilience file), so the business is not an inflation victim; the 2026 hit is a tax change, not a cost spiral.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The shift from "dividend growth" to "no interim dividend" while the cash pile and cash flow both rose is the tell: cash is being retained for something - state-directed computing-power capex or the tax hit - rather than paid out. For a state-controlled operator, payout policy is set with the parent and the regulator, so a restoration is a policy decision, not an earnings outcome.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: deteriorating. The single most important thing to weigh: the cash is real, but owners do not control it - the dividend was withheld in a year when cash flow rose, so the net cash and free cash flow cannot be counted at full value until the payout returns.

Moat: regulatory licence plus scale (one of three national operators). It is narrow rather than wide - returns on equity are only about 5%, profit is down a third this year, and core service revenue is flat-to-down. The trend looks stable at the franchise level (the licence is not at risk) even as reported profit falls on tax. Secular threat: manageable - no structural force is dismantling telecom demand; the pressure is policy (tax, tariffs, directed capex). The cheapness is mostly a fear-print about payout and policy, not a shrinking-base value trap, but it is a low-return franchise whose value depends on what the state lets it distribute.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# OTEC.OL — Otello Corporation ASA: a deep dive on management and the setup (2026-11-03)

Prices: Otello 17.24 kroner (Oslo, FMP quote, 2026-11-02 close). Bemobi (BMOB3, São Paulo) R$23.51 (2026-10-30 close). FX: 1 BRL = 1.7095 NOK (FMP, USD/NOK 9.294 / USD/BRL 5.437). Otello reports in US dollars. No earnings-call transcript was found; this dossier rests on the FMP balance sheet, FMP price history, a Quartr summary of the first-half 2026 report and dated press coverage. The web-search budget ran out partway through, so Bemobi's third-quarter 2026 results date and any company filing behind the 26 October drop could not be checked.

## 1. What the company actually is
Otello, the former Opera Software, is now a holding company. Its only material asset is a stake of about 38.2% (Quartr H1-2026 summary; Investing.com lists 38.55%) in Bemobi Mobile Tech, a listed Brazilian company that collects recurring bills (utilities, telecoms, education) and processes payments. The 30 June 2026 balance sheet shows the Bemobi stake carried at USD 122.2M, cash of USD 10.6M, no debt, and USD 2.6M of other liabilities. The screener's zero revenue and negative ROIC (return on invested capital) are simply what a holding company that books Bemobi by the equity method looks like. They are not an operating failure.

## 2. Earnings quality
First-half 2026 net income was USD 2.2M, well below the first half of 2025, which had one-off gains (Quartr). Trailing free cash flow is about -USD 0.7M: the holding company burns a little cash on head-office costs. Reported earnings per share swing with one-off items, so we value Otello on what it holds, not on its earnings.

## 3. Balance sheet and solvency
The holding company has no debt. Net cash after other liabilities is about USD 8.0M (74 million kroner, roughly 1.09 kroner per share). The Altman Z-score of 29 (a measure of bankruptcy risk) is meaningless here except to confirm there is no solvency risk. Treasury shares of USD 9.6M show past buybacks.

## 4. The underlying asset (Bemobi)
- 3Q25 (reported 2025-11-13): adjusted revenue R$187.5M (+22.3%), adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) R$62.7M (33.4% margin), adjusted net income R$46.8M (+88.7%).
- 4Q25: net income about R$61M (+31%, Guia do Investidor).
- 1Q26: revenue +35% year on year, helped by the Paytime acquisition (Investing.com summary).
- Bemobi runs a share buyback and pays interest-on-capital distributions (ex-date 18 August 2026). Itaú BBA has a buy rating with a R$27 year-end-2026 target, but the source is undated, so we use it only as context.
- At R$23.51 Bemobi's market value is about R$1.96B. That is roughly 8x our estimate of 2026 earnings (about R$240-260M, run-rate from 4Q25 plus growth), which is cheap for a business growing 20%+.

## 5. What changed since 2026-10-12 (dated)
- Bemobi rallied to R$34.55 on 2026-10-09 and R$33.85 on 2026-10-23, then **fell 26.0% on 2026-10-26** (R$25.04) and closed at R$23.51 on 2026-10-30.
- Otello followed it down: 22.55 kroner on 2026-10-23, then 18.50 kroner on 10-26 and 17.10 kroner on 10-30.
- The only explanation we found (Ad-hoc-News, citing Valor International on 2026-10-28) calls it a broad sell-off in Brazilian small caps: traders unwound bets on lower interest rates as long-term yields rose. That article reports no company announcement, and says Leblon Equities bought after the fall. **Caveat:** a 26% one-day drop in a single stock is extreme for a sector move. With the search budget gone, we could not rule out a company-specific trigger.
- 2026-10-14: SPX Gestão cut its Bemobi holding to 0.28%. This is a small, routine filing.

## 6. The look-through discount (the gap between Otello's price and the value of what it owns)
Bemobi stake: 38.4% × R$1.961B = R$753M = 1,288 million kroner, or 18.83 kroner per Otello share (68.37M shares). Add net cash of 1.09 kroner and the look-through NAV (net asset value) is about **19.9 kroner**. At 17.24 kroner, Otello trades about 13% below its NAV. On 2026-10-12 the gap was about 32% (NAV 31.4 kroner against a 21.40 kroner price). The wrapper discount has largely closed, because the asset fell rather than because Otello rose. Running costs of about USD 2-2.5M a year, valued at roughly 2 kroner per share, take up most of the remaining 13%.

## 7. Governance and management
Management is a small team that has historically returned capital through buybacks and special distributions (the Opera-era asset sales). The board says it remains positive on Bemobi's shift to payments (H1-2026 report). There is no stated plan to sell or distribute the stake, and no dated monetisation event exists. Insider buying in the screen is zero.

## 8. Red flags and open questions
- Otello now holds a single asset that trades at the mercy of Brazilian interest rates and the Brazilian real.
- The cause of the 26% drop is unverified.
- The inflation-resilience label "exposed" is an artefact of the holding company's near-zero revenue (a -6,600% "gross margin"). It says nothing about the business.
- The analyst target could not be dated, and the Bemobi 3Q26 results date is unconfirmed (3Q25 was reported on 2025-11-13).
- The "38.2% vs 38.55%" stake figure differs by source.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady.

# Wilh. Wilhelmsen Holding ASA (WWI.OL, A shares) - deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-03. Prices in Norwegian kroner (NOK) for the Oslo A-share listing WWI.OL; the company reports in US dollars (USD). Live marks (FMP, 2026-11-03): WWI.OL NOK 855, WWIB.OL (the B shares) NOK 802, Wallenius Wilhelmsen (WAWI.OL) NOK 168.80, Hyundai Glovis KRW 204,500, USD/NOK 9.299, USD/KRW 1,344.6.

Source limits, stated plainly: FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing, the FMP news feed returned no company items since 1 October 2026, and this run's web-search budget was exhausted before any search could run. Nothing in this dossier is a management quote. The quarterly figures below are FMP's standardised statements; the capital-return facts (NOK 20.00 dividend paid 20 May 2026, authorisation for up to NOK 8.50 more, buyback executions to 13 May 2026, net cash and a 74% equity ratio at 30 June 2026) are carried from this committee's earlier records, which verified them against the 12 August 2026 second-quarter release. Third-quarter 2026 results are due 4 November 2026 - tomorrow - and are not in hand.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Wilh. Wilhelmsen Holding is a 165-year-old, family-controlled holding company. Its story has two halves. The first is a set of listed stakes: about 37.8% of Wallenius Wilhelmsen (the world's largest car-and-heavy-equipment ocean carrier) and roughly 11-12% of Hyundai Glovis (Hyundai-Kia's logistics and car-carrier arm). The second is an operating group - Maritime Services (ships' agency, ship-management, marine products) plus a small New Energy portfolio. The narrative over the last two years has shifted from "a cheap collection of shipping stakes" toward "an improving operating business plus a capital-return machine" (a rising dividend and a continuous buyback). What has not changed is the absence of any stated intention to close the holding-company discount (the gap between the share price and the value of the parts) by selling or distributing either stake.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence (FMP quarterly, USD) | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Operating half is improving | Operating income Q2-2026 41.2M vs 28.0M in Q2-2025; Q1-2026 32.9M; revenue flat-to-down (307.0M vs 316.0M) | Corroborated: margin-led, not volume-led |
| Earnings are high quality | Net margin ~53% on a ~23% gross margin; Q2-2026 pre-tax 153.5M of which ~112M is "other income" (associates, mainly Wallenius Wilhelmsen) | Headline earnings are mostly the share of a shipping company's profit, not cash the holding controls |
| Earnings growing | EPS Q2-2025 5.96 (incl. gains) -> Q2-2026 3.38, latest-quarter EPS -43% y/y; TTM EPS 12.54 vs fiscal-2025 15.52; consensus forward EPS -11.5% | Earnings are past their peak; driven by the car-carrier cycle |
| Balance sheet clean | Net cash USD 182M incl. leases at 30 June 2026 (cash 611M vs debt 428M); Altman-Z 3.5; Piotroski 7/9 | Corroborated |
| Shareholder-friendly | Weighted shares 41.96M (Q1-2026) -> 41.48M (Q2-2026) | Corroborated: buyback is real |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable. Without transcripts, tone is read from actions: dividends rising every year, buybacks running, no guidance changes, no profit warnings, no management turnover of note in the window. Rating: Stable.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
The company gives no numeric earnings guidance; its one explicit target is a dividend policy (a 3-5% yield band), which it has met. The screener shows earnings beat 3 of 7 quarters (43%), but with no formal guidance and thin analyst coverage that rate mostly measures the swings in associate income. Reliability: Medium-High on what it promises (capital return); the earnings line itself is not management's to steer.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
No transcript is available. The recurring question any holder must ask: is there any plan to realise value from the Wallenius Wilhelmsen or Hyundai Glovis stakes? Nothing dated answers it. The second open question is how much of Wallenius Wilhelmsen's earnings are cycle-high freight rates that will fade as the 2023-24 newbuild order book delivers.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- 🟢 Net cash and a 74% equity ratio (30 June 2026); no financing risk anywhere.
- 🟢 Operating income up about 47% year on year in Q2-2026 on flat revenue.
- 🟢 Share count down about 1.1% in one quarter via buybacks.
- 🔴 About three-quarters of the asset value rides one factor: car-carrier freight and vehicle trade flows.
- 🔴 The Wallenius Wilhelmsen stake is marked at NOK 168.80, more than double its 52-week low of NOK 75.40, while its earnings fell sharply year on year.
- 🔴 Earnings per share are falling (latest quarter -43% y/y; forward consensus -11.5%).
- 🔴 The A shares trade at NOK 855 versus NOK 802 for the B shares - a 6.6% premium for votes in a company the family controls anyway.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The capital-return mix tilts to buybacks when the shares are below asset value - sensible. The A/B spread is a quiet signal: the market prices the voting A shares at a premium even though control sits with the family vehicle (Tallyman AS), so an economic investor gains nothing from the premium. Hyundai Glovis jumped 11.3% on 3 November 2026 (FMP quote); no news item explaining it was available to this run, so it is treated as a price mark, not a fact about the thesis.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: STABLE. The single most important thing to weigh: you are buying a permanently discounted, thinly traded wrapper around two shipping-linked stakes that are marked near the top of their cycle, and in this share class you pay a further 6.6% premium over the identical economic claim in the B shares.
Moat: the operating business (Maritime Services) has a narrow scale-and-network moat - a global port-agency and marine-products network with recurring customers; returns are modest (group ROIC about 5%) but stable. The listed stakes carry the moat of their underlying businesses (Wallenius Wilhelmsen's scale in a concentrated car-carrier market). Secular threat: manageable - the energy transition shifts fuel and fleet costs and Chinese car exports change trade lanes, but neither threatens the terminal value; the cheapness is cyclical and structural (holding discount), not a melting base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Comcast (CMCSA) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*Debate run 2026-11-09. Transcripts: Q3 2025 (2025-10-30) through Q3 2026 (2026-10-22). Live price $24.51 (Nasdaq, USD, 2026-11-09).*

**The short version:** Comcast is a cash machine whose core business, home broadband, is slowly shrinking under attack from fixed wireless (home internet sold by mobile carriers) and fiber overbuilders. Management has been unusually candid about that, and it is spending heavily — price cuts, a five-year price guarantee, free mobile lines — to stop the bleeding. The content side (parks, studios, Peacock, Sky) is in better shape and is being split off into a separate public company by the middle of 2027. The numbers corroborate the candor but not yet the turnaround: free cash flow is real (about $17.1B over the trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30), but connectivity profit is still falling every quarter.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-30):** the story was "a deliberate investment phase." Mike Cavanagh said broadband would end up as a market of "2 multi-gig symmetrical providers," conceded "most of our footprint will eventually be overbuilt," and guided that the decline in Connectivity & Platforms EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization — a cash-profit proxy) would "build slightly over the next several quarters." Leadership change: Steve Croney named head of connectivity.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-01-29):** the theme became execution of "the most significant go-to-market shift in our company's history" — four national speed tiers, a five-year price guarantee, a 12-month free mobile line. Management promised that "a meaningful portion" of free lines would convert to paid in the second half of 2026 and that connectivity profit would improve in the back half. The Versant cable-network spin was completed.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-23):** the high-water mark of the story — broadband net losses "improved by more than 100,000 year-over-year, the first year-over-year improvement since the fourth quarter of 2020," record wireless adds, record Olympic/Super Bowl advertising.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-23):** the narrative pivoted to structure. Three weeks earlier the company had announced the separation of NBCUniversal and Sky into a standalone company, targeted in "approximately 1 year," and the return of Michael Angelakis as the future Comcast chief executive. Peacock reached profitability.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-22):** tone turned defensive on connectivity. Management described fixed wireless as "aggressive," fiber pricing as having "pockets of irrational pricing," flagged an unusually large wave of two-year promotional roll-offs, and announced "the most significant operating and cost transformation in our company's history" with a roughly $1B fourth-quarter restructuring charge (reported 2026-10-22). Connectivity revenue fell about 2.6% and connectivity EBITDA about 4.4% year over year. Parks: Orlando softness guided to persist "at least next quarter and in the first half of next year."

The arc runs from "invest, then grow" to "split the company and cut costs." The growth promise for connectivity has been pushed out; the value-creation promise has shifted toward the separation.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Connectivity decline will "build slightly," then improve in the second half of 2026 (Q3 2025, Q4 2025 calls) | Connectivity EBITDA fell ~3.7% in Q3 2025, ~5.8% in Q2 2026, ~4.4% in Q3 2026 — it did build, and the Q3 2026 narrowing is the first sign of the promised improvement, but it is still falling | Partly delivered |
| Broadband losses turning (Q1 2026: first year-over-year improvement since Q4 2020) | The Q1 improvement did not become a trend; Q3 2026 was hurt by promotional roll-offs and aggressive competitor pricing | Not yet corroborated |
| Free lines will convert to paid in the second half of 2026 (Q4 2025) | Q2 2026: "positive early traction"; no conversion percentage has ever been disclosed | Unverified — a recurring non-number |
| Peacock will approach profitability (Q1 2026) | Peacock reached profitability in Q2 2026 and stayed profitable in Q3 2026 | Delivered |
| Cash generation is durable | Revenue flat for three years (3-year CAGR +0.6%; 2025 revenue $123.7B vs $123.7B in 2024); free cash flow $17.1B trailing twelve months, up ~25% in fiscal 2025 | Corroborated |
| Earnings growth | Fiscal 2025 EPS $5.39 (+30%) is flattered by one-offs and by the post-Versant comparison; trailing twelve-month diluted EPS is $3.16, and consensus forward EPS growth is only ~1% | The headline EPS growth overstates the earning power |

Net debt is about $79.8B (borrowings $87.4B less cash $7.6B at 2026-09-30, excluding leases), roughly 2.3-2.5 times EBITDA on our estimate — manageable, but it limits buybacks, which press coverage on 2026-11-08 described as on hold.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining on connectivity, rising on content.** Q3 2025: "intensely competitive environment, which we do not expect to change anytime soon" — candid but confident. Q1 2026: "early signs that the strategic pivot ... is underway" — the most offensive language of the run. Q3 2026: "near-term financial pressure," "pockets of irrational pricing," and a shift to cost and efficiency language ("structurally improve our cost base"). Guidance specificity has fallen: in Q4 2025 the chief financial officer said "I will stop short of giving a full EBITDA guide," and no connectivity framework has been offered since. On content, the tone is steadily more confident (Peacock profitable, The Odyssey, NBA ratings).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management gives directional rather than numerical guidance, which makes it hard to catch them out — and that is itself the point. Directional calls on the trough (the decline would "build") were accurate; calls on the recovery (broadband turning, back-half improvement) have been only partly delivered. Peacock guidance was met. The screener's 7-of-7 quarterly earnings-per-share beats reflects low consensus bars and cost control more than operating momentum. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- The free-line conversion rate: asked repeatedly (Q1 2026, Q2 2026), never quantified.
- Post-separation leverage, dividend policy and exchange ratio: asked in Q2 2026; answer was "nothing to add." The dividend split between the two companies is the largest unanswered question for the yield-holder base.
- Orlando parks softness and Epic Universe capacity: management now guides softness into the first half of 2027.
- Promotional roll-offs in the legacy base (Q3 2026): management admits it is "a pain point."

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

**Red flags**
- Q3 2026: a new round of the "most significant" transformation, with a ~$1B charge, one year after the last "most significant" go-to-market shift — the fixes keep getting bigger.
- Q3 2026: competitive language escalated ("irrational pricing"); peer Charter reported wider internet losses on 2026-11-06, so the pressure is industry-wide, not easing.
- Q2/Q3 2026: no capital-return framework for the two companies; buybacks reported paused.
- Insiders: 3 open-market sales (about 70,700 shares) and zero open-market buys.

**Green flags**
- Q2-Q3 2026: Peacock profitable two quarters running.
- Q3 2026: connectivity EBITDA decline narrowed to ~4.4% from ~5.8% in Q2.
- Business services generates "nearly $6 billion annually in EBITDA" with enterprise growth.
- Wireless: record line additions through 2026; over 10 million lines.
- The separation creates two cleaner stories and a potential sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) unlock.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Satellite is not yet a material factor" (Q3 2026) is the first time management has named satellite as a future competitor — a widening of the threat set.
- The language moved from "return to growth" to "position the business for return to growth over the long term" — a quiet extension of the timeline.
- Leadership churn: Croney (connectivity, 2026), Cavanagh co-CEO (2026), Angelakis returning as Comcast CEO (2027), a new NBCUniversal chief financial officer (Chris Halpin). The new voices emphasise cost and agility rather than growth.
- The proposed ITV acquisition for Sky signals the media company will be acquisitive, adding execution risk on the content side.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: PIVOTING.** The company is turning from a conglomerate defending cable into two separate companies, with an aggressive cost program on the connectivity side.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** the cash is real (about $4.80 of free cash flow per share against a $24.51 price), but the cash comes from a connectivity business whose profit is still falling about 4% a year. The investment works if that decline flattens; it is a slow value trap if it does not. The fourth-quarter 2026 results (late January 2027) are the next clean read.

**Moat:** scale-cost and network (a sunk, capital-efficient hybrid fiber-coax network) plus switching costs from bundling broadband with mobile. It is real but narrow, and the evidence says it is eroding: return on invested capital is only 6.8%, connectivity revenue and profit are falling, and management itself expects most of its footprint to be overbuilt. **Secular threat:** fixed-wireless and fiber overbuild (cord-cutting/broadband overbuild) is a material, not terminal, threat — the business still earns large cash margins and can defend share with price, and the content half is not exposed in the same way. The cheapness is partly a fear-print and partly a fair price for a shrinking core; at roughly 5 times free cash flow, the market is pricing more decline than the latest numbers show, but the burden of proof sits with management.

picks.bull_thesis: Geely is one of the few mass-market Chinese carmakers that still makes real money in a price war. In H1 2026 (results call 2026-08-17) it earned close to RMB 10 billion attributable profit at about a 5.6% margin while management put the industry average at 1.6%, and it ranked first in China by retail sales. Two engines are offsetting a shrinking home market: exports (the annual target was hit by mid-year, raised from 640,000 to 920,000, and nine-month exports reached 797,670, up 169%, per CnEVPost on 2026-10-01) and the premium ZEEKR brand (+97% in H1 2026), which lifts revenue per car. The One Geely programme is cutting costs measurably (admin ratio 1.9% to 1.7%, R&D ratio 5.5% to 5.2%, model count down 20%). The balance sheet carries RMB 56.6 billion of net cash at 2026-06-30, roughly 40% of the HK$148 billion market value, and the company pays out 30% of profit. At HK$13.71 the stock trades at roughly 7x annualised core earnings and a low single-digit multiple of free cash flow. If margins merely hold near current levels and the market re-rates toward 10-11x earnings, fair value is in the mid-to-high HK$20s. Conditions: gross margin stays near 16-17%, exports keep growing despite trade barriers, and no large value-destroying acquisition consumes the cash.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness may be deserved. Returns on capital are poor (ROIC about 2.5%, ROE 11.6%), reported EPS was flat in 2025 at RMB 1.63, the 2024 jump was about half one-off gains (core profit RMB 8.5 billion vs reported RMB 16.6 billion, per the 2025-03-12 call), the screener shows 0 of 2 recent quarters beating consensus, and latest-quarter EPS fell 22% year on year. The home market shrank by double digits in H1 2026 and domestic sales fell about 25% in August 2026; all of Geely's growth now comes from exports, which are exposed to tariffs and anti-subsidy actions in Europe and elsewhere, and exports slipped 3% month on month in September 2026. Management itself flagged rising chip and raw-material costs on 2026-08-17 and admitted 'a lack of blockbuster product' in the mainstream segment. The headline free cash flow and net cash are flattered by supplier credit (car makers pay suppliers late), so a slowdown could reverse working capital and shrink the cash pile quickly. If net margin falls toward 3% and the market keeps a 6x multiple, the stock could trade near HK$11.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing Geely as if the Chinese price war will crush its margins the way it has crushed most rivals' profits. The numbers so far say otherwise: H1 2026 net margin about 5.6% against an industry average of 1.6% (2026-08-17), gross margin near 16-17%, and growth shifted to exports and the premium ZEEKR brand. At HK$13.71 the stock trades around 7x annualised core earnings with about 40% of its market value in net cash. Where we disagree with the market: we think it extrapolates the sector's losses onto the one large private carmaker that is still profitable. Where the market has a point: reported EPS is flat, the latest quarter fell 22%, and returns on capital are low; so our fair value assumes no margin expansion and a below-peer-leader multiple. No dated analyst consensus target could be verified via FMP (no coverage for this listing), so we cite none.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): Q4 2026 and Q1 2027. Domestic demand is shrinking (domestic sales -25% in August 2026), input costs (chips, raw materials) are rising, and Beijing's price-war curbs have not stopped discounting. Exports, now the only growth engine, slipped 3% month on month in September 2026 and face tariff and anti-subsidy risk in Europe and emerging markets. A weak October-December sales run or a second-half margin miss at the March 2027 full-year results could push the stock lower before any re-rating; supplier-credit unwinding could also shrink the reported cash pile. None of this threatens solvency given net cash.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure appears sector-driven rather than holder-specific: the stock is about 25% below its 200-day average and near its 52-week low (HK$13.15) after a China-auto de-rating, with low smart-money interest (score 4/100) and neutral institutional flow. There is no dividend cut, index deletion or lock-up that would force mechanical selling; the 30% payout policy keeps income holders in place. Further sector outflows could extend the drawdown, but that is a sector-wide sell-off, not forced selling by holders who must sell regardless of value.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds. Nothing company-specific and dated has changed since our 2026-11-10 look. The price is HK$13.58 on 2026-11-16, so the stock trades about 34% below our fair value of HK$20.50 (about 51% upside), well clear of our 20% bar. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Valaris (VAL) - a deep dive on management and the setup
Debate run 2026-11-09. Continuing coverage; the committee's last full look was 2026-10-26. Latest transcript on file: the third-quarter 2025 call of 2025-10-31 (no newer Valaris call transcript in the bundle). Price used: $78.55 (US dollars, New York listing VAL), live quote from the paid market-data feed on 2026-11-09; Transocean (RIG) $5.17 on the same feed.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Across the calls on file (October 2024 to October 2025) the story moved in three steps. Late 2024: "the up-cycle is intact, demand is only deferred into 2026", with rigs warm-stacked (idled with a skeleton crew) and buybacks running near $100m a quarter. Early 2025: retire weaker rigs and hold out for long contracts at mid-to-high $400,000 day rates. October 2025: all four drillships with near-term availability contracted for 2026 work, drillship use to bottom late 2025 or early 2026. Then the story stopped being Valaris's to tell: on 2026-02-09 the company agreed to be acquired by Transocean for 15.235 Transocean shares per Valaris share - all stock, fixed ratio, no collar (no price protection band), no cash. Since our 2026-10-26 look, the deal has moved from "pending regulators" to "regulators done, votes scheduled": both chief executives said on their third-quarter calls (2026-11-02/03) that all required regulatory approvals are in hand, including the US Department of Justice and Brazil's competition authority, with no conditions; shareholder votes at both companies are set for 2026-11-24, the Bermuda court hearing for 2026-11-26 and completion targeted for 2026-12-01.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| 2025 earnings of $13.86 a share | Pre-tax profit roughly $552m; the rest is a one-off release of a deferred tax asset (a past tax loss put back on the balance sheet) of about $427m | Artefact - taxed normally about $6 a share |
| Utilisation trough in early 2026, then recovery | Revenue: Q1 2026 $465m (small loss), Q2 $539m, Q3 $594m (filed 2026-11-03), +10% quarter on quarter | Corroborated on revenue |
| Recovery shows up in earnings | Q3 2026 earnings $0.66 a share against a $1.00 consensus estimate, versus $2.65 a year earlier; pre-tax profit $101m but tax of $55m (a 54% rate) | Operating recovery real, bottom line hit by an uneven tax charge |
| "Return all future free cash flow" | Trailing twelve-month free cash flow -$211m to 2026-09-30; buybacks halted in 2026 | Missed |

The screen's $178 fair value and 123% margin of safety rest on the tax-inflated 2025 earnings; the cash-flow and earnings-power methods read fully valued, and return on invested capital is negative (-3.6%). Net debt about $590m; solvency score (Altman-Z) 2.8 - not stressed.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable and disciplined, never promotional. Management separated "deferred" from "cancelled" and backed it with stacking and retirement decisions. The October 2025 tone ("day rates have troughed ... in the high 300s, low to mid-400 range") was more measured than 2024. The decision to sell for acquirer stock eleven weeks later is the clearest tonal signal: the board chose scale inside Transocean over riding its own recovery.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
High on operations: revenue efficiency of 95-98% quarter after quarter; the trough timing held and revenue has stepped up three quarters running. Low on capital return: the free-cash-flow return promise became zero buybacks. Earnings delivery mixed: 4 of 7 quarters beat (57%); Q2 2026 beat ($0.72 vs $0.46), Q3 2026 missed ($0.66 vs $1.00). Overall reliability: Medium.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Idle-rig strategy and stacking costs, the Saudi Aramco jack-up suspensions in the ARO joint venture, and capital return. Trajectory: PIVOTING - from a standalone recovery to a three-week conversion into Transocean stock. Operationally capable management with a sound fleet strategy, a mixed capital-return record, and the decisive allocation choice already made. picks.bull_thesis:
Kogeneracja supplies district heating - hot water piped to buildings - and electricity to Wroclaw, a Polish city of about 640,000 people, from plants that make both at once (combined heat and power). At 84.20 zloty the whole company is valued at about 1.25 billion zloty. Over the twelve months to 30 June 2026 it earned about 334 million zloty of net profit (about 22.4 zloty a share) and generated 401 million zloty of free cash flow (cash left after capital spending): about 3.8 times earnings, 3.1 times free cash flow and 0.45 times the 188 zloty of book value (accounting net assets) per share.

The earnings step-up has a specific, finished cause. The 179-megawatt Czechnica-2 gas unit, a roughly 1.4 billion zloty project, was launched on 29 May 2025. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA, a proxy for operating cash earnings) rose from 485 million zloty in 2024 to about 718 million over the twelve months to June 2026, while quarterly capital spending has run below depreciation for three reported quarters. On 29 June 2026 the company also won contracted cogeneration support for its EC Wroclaw gas engines, so part of its revenue is no longer exposed to the power market.

The reporting is clean: a Piotroski score of 8 out of 9 (a nine-point accounting-health checklist) and results pre-announced to the decimal four times running. The June 2026 dividend of 2.58 zloty, the first since the 2021 year, shows the payout channel is open. If PGE, the 58% parent, lifts the payout at the 2027 meeting - the argument for retaining cash to build the plant has expired - or buys out the 42% it does not own, the shares re-rate toward book value.
picks.bear_thesis:
The earnings are real; the problem is that a minority shareholder cannot reach them, and nothing since 12 October has changed that.

At 30 June 2026 Kogeneracja held 16.1 million zloty of cash and 1,349.9 million zloty of 'other receivables' - more than its whole market value - most plausibly a cash-pool balance swept to the parent and lent back on the group's terms. PGE owns 58.06% and decides. On 28 May 2026 a minority pension fund asked for 6.71 zloty a share; the 11 June meeting gave 2.58 zloty, about 14% of profit, and the fund fell below 5% on 2 July.

The earnings are also flattered by a good moment. The June 2026 quarter swung to a 6.2 million zloty loss with gross profit down from 37.1 to 20.8 million. The heat tariff is cost-plus, so a supplier whose winter gross margin rose from 21.7% to 28.0% will share that gain at the next reset; the remaining coal units face rising carbon costs, and the announced full exit from coal plus the boiler tenders now under way mean a second spending wave that competes with dividends.

And the price has done the work: the shares rose from 78.50 zloty on 12 October to 87.90 at the high and 84.20 now with no announcement at all. At 84.20 the stock sits slightly above our base-case fair value of 82, so a buyer today is paying for the favourable case. A thin float - about 19% - cuts both ways when the flows reverse.
picks.consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the question is whether the market prices terminal decline into a business with stable or growing earnings power. Here it does not: it prices a governance discount, and at 84.20 zloty it prices it about where we do. There is no published analyst coverage, so there is no consensus forecast to be wrong. Where we disagree is narrow. First, the market may treat the post-project earnings partly as a windfall; capital spending below depreciation says at least half is structural, because the regulator can reset a tariff but cannot un-spend the build or un-award the June 2026 cogeneration support. Second, book value per share keeps compounding (about 188 zloty at 30 June 2026). Where the market may now be ahead of us: the shares rose about 7% since 12 October, touching 87.90, with no new fact; at today's price the market is giving more credit for a payout change than PGE's conduct so far supports.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) holds one near-certain soft spot and two probable ones; none is a solvency event. First, the September 2026 quarter, due in late November 2026, is structurally loss-making for a heat supplier (minus 15.0 million zloty a year earlier), and the June quarter's trough ran weaker than last year. Buyers who arrived on a low trailing multiple during the October run-up will read two loss quarters in a row and can sell into a float this thin. Second, the next heat-tariff decision: a supplier whose winter gross margin rose from 21.7% to 28.0% invites a harder look, and the reset date could not be sourced. Third, carbon and fuel, plus the coal-exit spending now being tendered. Not a risk: refinancing - total debt including leases of about 385 million zloty against about 718 million of twelve-month EBITDA, and interest income exceeds interest expense.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure here is slow, structural and real. PGE holds 58.06%; most of the rest sits with Polish open pension funds, which are structural net sellers of Warsaw small caps as members near retirement and assets transfer out of the system, regardless of valuation - and Nationale-Nederlanden's fund already fell below 5% on 2 July 2026 after its dividend request was cut. With normal daily turnover of a few thousand shares, unwinding even 1% of the company (about 149,000 shares) takes weeks and cannot clear without a price concession. That is the seller that could take the price back to our 66 zloty level - a wash-out, a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers. The level is not hypothetical: the shares traded at 59.40 within the last year and around 67 in August 2026. The 2 November session (20,296 shares, closing 3.2% lower after touching 81.20) shows how fast flows move this float in both directions.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 66 zloty, which the forced selling of Polish pension funds - holders who must sell regardless of value - could deliver.

The thesis holds. A 1.4 billion zloty gas unit launched on 29 May 2025 lifted twelve-month EBITDA to about 718 million zloty by June 2026, capital spending has run below depreciation for three quarters, twelve-month free cash flow is 401 million zloty, and the accounts score 8 out of 9 on the Piotroski checklist. At 84.20 zloty you pay about 3.8 times earnings and 0.45 times book.

But the price already reflects what a minority holder can reach - and since our 12 October look it has risen further with no news. PGE owns 58.06%, approved a 2.58 zloty dividend on 11 June 2026 (about 14% of profit) against a 6.71 zloty request, and at 30 June 2026 the company held 16.1 million zloty of cash against 1.35 billion zloty of group receivables. Valuing the heat franchise and generation separately and deducting 369 million zloty of net debt gives about 118 zloty a share before access; a 30% discount for a controlled entity that keeps its cash gives a fair value of 82 zloty, an adverse case of 36 and a favourable case of 145. At 84.20 the stock trades slightly above fair value; the required entry discount is cleared near 66 zloty, a level it traded around as recently as August 2026.

Nothing dated has changed since 12 October 2026 - the company has published nothing since its 8 September half-year report - so the answer is unchanged: a real, cleanly reported business at a governance-shaped discount, a soft catalyst with no fixed date in the 2027 annual meeting, and a hard cap on position size from a 19% float. Conviction stays at 3.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating - has no hard date. The scheduled decision point is the 2027 annual meeting, expected around June 2027, where PGE votes 58.06% on the 2026 profit; with the main build finished, a payout of 5 zloty or more would change the story, while the coal-exit spending gives PGE a reason to keep retaining. Unscheduled possibilities: a buy-out offer from PGE for the minority (nothing announced), a heat-tariff decision that confirms rather than resets the improved margin, or disclosure that the group receivable is an interest-bearing loan being repaid. None depends on interest-rate cuts, oil or artificial-intelligence spending - good driver independence - but all depend on a third party choosing to act.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Kogeneracja (KGN.WA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2 November 2026. Price used: 84.20 zloty (PLN) on the Warsaw exchange (live quote from the paid data feed, 2 November 2026; previous close 87.00, 52-week range 59.40-87.90). All figures in zloty.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists in the paid data feed for this listing, and Kogeneracja - a Polish subsidiary of the state-controlled PGE group - does not hold English-language analyst calls. This dossier tests management's actions and public statements (results pre-announcements, the annual-meeting dividend decision, capital spending, regulatory filings) against the reported quarterly statements pulled from the paid feed on 2 November 2026. The paid news feed carries no item for this ticker since 1 October 2026. The company's own announcement list (bankier.pl, checked 2 November 2026) shows nothing after the half-year report of 8 September 2026, and the biznesradar.pl news page shows no company-specific item since then either. The web-search allowance for this run ran out after two searches, so a deeper Polish-language press check was not possible. No quotes are invented below.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story over the last two years has one spine: build gas-fired replacements for coal, switch them on, and harvest the cash. The 179-megawatt Czechnica-2 gas unit (roughly 1.4 billion zloty of investment) was launched on 29 May 2025. Through 2024 and the first half of 2025 the narrative was about spending; since the September 2025 quarter it has been about earnings. In the regulator's cogeneration-premium auction held 22-24 June 2026 the company entered its AK6-10 gas engines at EC Wroclaw (49.9 megawatts of electricity, 50 megawatts of heat) and won support (result announced 29 June 2026) - a correction to our earlier notes, which attached that premium to Czechnica-2. Company material also describes a full exit from coal across its three Wroclaw-area plants (418 megawatts of electricity and 1,080 megawatts of heat in total), and public tenders show gas- and electricity-fired water boilers being procured.

What has not changed is who decides where the cash goes. PGE owns 58.06%. The 11 June 2026 annual meeting approved a dividend of 2.58 zloty a share (about 14% of the 277 million zloty 2025 profit) - the first since the 2021 year - after a minority pension fund had asked for 6.71 zloty. For a minority shareholder the arc is: the earnings arrived, the cash mostly did not.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / action | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The new gas unit lifts earnings | Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) over the twelve months to 30 June 2026 were about 718 million zloty, against 485 million in 2024 | Matches |
| The capital programme is over | Quarterly capital spending of 39.2, 45.6 and 33.7 million in the last three reported quarters, below quarterly depreciation of 61-67 million | Matches - but the coal-exit plan and boiler tenders mean a second, smaller spending wave is coming |
| Results pre-announced accurately | Q1 2026 pre-announced at about 213 million, delivered 213.1 million; 2025 at about 277 million, delivered 277.0 million | Matches |
| Free cash flow is real | Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow 401 million zloty | Matches, but lumpy and seasonal |
| Cash belongs to shareholders | Cash of 16.1 million zloty at 30 June 2026 against 1,349.9 million of "other receivables" (most plausibly a group cash-pool balance with PGE) | Diverges |

The June 2026 quarter showed revenue of 471.6 million zloty (up 5.7%), gross profit down to 20.8 million from 37.1 million, EBITDA flat at 67.0 million and a net loss of 6.2 million zloty. That is the normal summer trough for a heat supplier, slightly weaker than last year. The September 2026 quarter, due in late November 2026, will also be seasonally weak (a 15.0 million zloty loss a year earlier).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable. Without calls, tone is read from conduct: management pre-announces winter-quarter results weeks early and to the decimal, and the June 2026 dividend - small as it is - was the first in four years. No guidance has been withdrawn and nothing defensive has been published since the half-year report of 8 September 2026.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High. The company does not issue forward guidance in the usual sense, but its results pre-announcements have matched the final numbers four times running. No evidence of sandbagging or misses.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

No sell-side price target exists in the paid feed for this listing, and none was found on Polish market-data sites. The pressure comes from shareholders: the pension fund that asked on 28 May 2026 for 6.71 zloty got 2.58 and cut its stake below 5% on 2 July 2026. The unanswered question remains what the 1.35 billion zloty receivable is, what rate it earns, and whether it is callable.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 (Q2 2026) net loss of 6.2 million zloty and negative operating cash flow in the summer quarter, worse than a year earlier at the gross-profit line.
- 🔴 (30 June 2026) 1,349.9 million zloty of other receivables against 16.1 million of cash - more than the company's market value, held where a minority holder cannot reach it.
- 🔴 (11 June 2026) a payout of about 14% of profit with the main build finished.
- 🔴 (October 2026) the shares rose from 78.50 to a 52-week high of 87.90 with no company announcement - the discount closed on flows, not news.
- 🟢 capital spending below depreciation for three straight reported quarters.
- 🟢 (29 June 2026) contracted cogeneration premium won for the EC Wroclaw gas engines.
- 🟢 Piotroski score of 8 out of 9 (a nine-point accounting-health checklist) and accurate pre-announcements.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

Book value per share keeps compounding - about 188 zloty at 30 June 2026 - so retained profit is kept, not lost. Interest income (13.9 million zloty in the June quarter) is double interest expense (6.7 million), consistent with the receivable being an interest-bearing group loan. Turnover on 2 November 2026 was 20,296 shares, roughly seven times the 2,845 shares of 12 October - unusually heavy for a 19% free float, and the day closed 3.2% lower after touching 81.20. The supply side drives this stock.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: strengthening at the operating level, unchanged at the shareholder level. The single thing to weigh: the value is real but controlled - PGE decides the payout and holds the cash. Size this as an access problem, not an earnings problem, and note that at 84.20 zloty the price already sits slightly above our base-case fair value.

Moat: a regulatory-licence moat - the licensed district-heating supplier to Wroclaw (about 640,000 people), with cost-plus tariffs. Narrow (returns on invested capital of about 6% on the screener's measure, about 11-12% on our post-project EBITDA basis - at or slightly above a Polish cost of capital) and stable. The secular threat is material, not terminal: the remaining coal units face rising carbon costs as free allowances for district heating phase down toward 2030, but dense-city district heat is not being displaced and the gas units are the transition answer. The cheapness is a governance and liquidity discount, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

Exports depend on decisions by foreign governments (Russian recycling fees and rebates, tariffs elsewhere). The interim dividend was skipped in 2026. Net cash is only RMB 2.44 billion once supplier bills and debt (RMB 52.7 billion) are netted against RMB 55.1 billion of cash. Domestic price competition intensified after BYD price cuts in November 2026. Any change in Russian recycling-fee or rebate policy hits the export story directly. Cash is not a solvency risk (RMB 55.1 billion of cash, RMB 2.44 billion net), but weak cash flow could keep the final dividend small or skipped, which removes support from yield-minded holders. # Great Wall Motor (2333.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16. Hong Kong H-share, quoted at HK$5.785 (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16). Company reports in renminbi (RMB); HK$1 = RMB 0.848 (FMP, 2026-11-16).*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript is bundled and FMP carries none for this listing. This dossier relies on the company's reported numbers (FMP quarterly statements through 2026-09-30), the third-quarter 2026 report released on 2026-10-30 as summarised by Chinese financial press (10jqka, 2026-11-03; ifeng, 2026-10-30), the first-half 2026 interim report, and dated broker actions found by web search. No management quotes are reproduced because none could be sourced verbatim; management's stated reasons are paraphrased from the press summaries.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story over the last four reports has narrowed from "a profitable SUV and pickup maker going global" to "an exporter whose profits are stuck in transit." In 2024 the business earned a record RMB 12.7 billion on RMB 199.6 billion of revenue. Through 2025 and 2026 the emphasis moved overseas: exports passed half of all sales in 2026 (476,000 of 920,300 units in the first nine months, up 42%), and management lifted the 2026 export target from 600,000 to 700,000 vehicles. Meanwhile the home market has been ceded: the Tank off-road brand fell 13.5% and Haval 2.5% in the first nine months, and new-energy volume fell 5.9% while the Chinese market moves steadily to electric. The explanation offered for weak profits has stayed the same for three quarters - delayed overseas tax subsidies (reported by Citi as Russian scrap-tax rebates), exchange-rate losses, and domestic price competition - which is either a consistent truth or a recurring excuse. Q3 2026 did not settle which.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Overseas growth is the engine | 9M 2026 overseas units +42%, now over 50% of volume | Matches |
| Profit is depressed by timing (delayed subsidies, currency), not by the franchise | Q3 2026 net profit to shareholders RMB 1.36B (-40.8% y/y); excluding one-offs RMB 0.98B (-48.3%). 9M net profit RMB 3.83B (-55.7%) | Partly: the gap is too wide and too persistent for timing alone |
| Pricing holds | Q3 gross margin about 17.3% (FMP: 9.98B / 57.76B), down about 1.1 points y/y, but up from 15.4% in Q2 | Stable-to-softer, not collapsing |
| The business is a cash machine (screen shows 1.5x price to free cash flow) | Q3 2026 operating cash flow -RMB 0.27B, free cash flow -RMB 2.44B; 9M operating cash flow RMB 6.22B, -70.9%. The trailing RMB 16.6B is propped up by Q4 2025 alone (RMB 14.4B) | Diverges - the cheapness on cash flow is a stale, seasonal figure |
| Balance sheet strength | Net cash only RMB 2.44B (cash 55.1B against 52.7B of debt incl. supplier bills); inventory RMB 40.2B, up 54% since year-end 2025 | Thinner than the headline cash suggests; inventory build is the red flag |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Declining. The confident export target raise (to 700,000) sits beside a skipped interim dividend in 2026, a first-half profit warning (net profit down 61%), and a third quarter in which the company again cited delayed subsidies. The language has shifted from growth to explanation.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium-to-low. The screen shows 3 of 7 recent quarters beating expectations (43%). Revenue delivery is real (9M revenue +4.1% despite flat units), but the profit recovery repeatedly promised as subsidies "catch up" has not arrived in Q1, Q2 or Q3 2026. Brokers have cut: Citi moved to sell with a HK$7.3 target after the first-half warning, and Morgan Stanley set HK$7.30 on 2026-11-05 (headline only; details unverified).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- When exactly the overseas subsidy receivable is collected, and how large it is (never quantified in the sources found).
- Why inventory is up RMB 14.7B in nine months - overseas stocking (management's explanation) versus unsold domestic product.
- Accelerated supplier payments (cited for weak cash flow) - a policy change, or the end of supplier-funded working capital that flattered past free cash flow.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red (Q3 2026): operating cash flow negative in a quarter with RMB 1.36B of profit.
- Red (9M 2026): inventory +54% to RMB 40.2B.
- Red (H1 2026): interim dividend skipped; profit -61%.
- Red (9M 2026): domestic volume down about a quarter (derived: about 444,000 units against about 589,000 a year earlier); new-energy volume down while the market electrifies.
- Green (Q3 2026): gross margin recovered to about 17.3% from 15.4% in Q2.
- Green (9M 2026): exports +42%; Ora +100%; Wey +4.7%.
- Green: still net cash, small buybacks continuing (about RMB 0.22B in Q2 2026).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
"Accelerated supplier payments" is the important phrase: Chinese automakers came under regulatory pressure in 2025 to pay suppliers within 60 days. If that is the cause, part of the historic free-cash-flow strength was supplier financing, and the 1.5x price-to-cash-flow screen overstates durable cash earnings. The receding Tank brand (the high-margin product) explains the mix-driven profit squeeze better than subsidies do.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: deteriorating. The single most important thing to weigh: the cheapness rests on cash flow and earnings that Q3 2026 did not reproduce. Until a quarter shows profit back near RMB 2 billion with inventory falling, the low multiple is on an earnings base that is still shrinking.

Moat: narrow, scale-cost plus a brand niche in off-road SUVs and pickups (Tank, Poer). Returns are modest (ROIC 6.9%) and the domestic niche is being eroded by price competition and the shift to electric vehicles, where Great Wall lags. The export franchise is real but exposed to tariff and subsidy decisions in Russia and other markets. Secular threat: material, not terminal - the energy-transition shift erodes the domestic combustion-SUV base, but exports and plug-in hybrids give a credible path. The discount is partly a fear print and partly a shrinking domestic base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.
