Gold-bar demand lifted nine-month 2026 revenue to 2,225 million zloty, against 1,232 million a year earlier, and operating profit to 372.7 million, against 91.4 million. The partner buy-out means future property profit increasingly belongs to Mennica's shareholders, and debt is already being repaid: 41.2 million zloty in the third quarter. Conditions for the bull case: property marks hold at book value, Polish long rates ease, bullion volume stays high, and management sells or refinances property to cut the new debt.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the screen's deep-value signal is an accounting artefact sitting on a newly leveraged, low-return business. Of the 9.77 zloty of 2025 earnings per share, about 8 zloty was the third-quarter 2025 non-cash property remeasurement: 409.6 million zloty of pre-tax profit taxed at only 2.8 million. The 2026 profits so far are one-off hand-overs of finished flats. The second quarter earned 1.73 zloty a share and the third 0.94, and the third quarter's gross margin of about 22% coincided with 230 million zloty of buyer deposits leaving the balance sheet. The clean quarters earned only 0.54 zloty (first quarter of 2026) and 0.31 zloty (fourth quarter of 2025). Free cash flow was about 40 million zloty for the first nine months of 2026, about 0.8 zloty a share, against a market value of 1.94 billion zloty. Net debt including leases is about 666 million zloty (borrowings 654 million plus 66 million of leases, less 54 million of cash), up from about 109 million at the end of March 2026, after a 483 million zloty partner buy-out. Minority holders still took 44% of third-quarter net profit. Return on invested capital fell from about 11% in 2023 to about 5% in 2025 as thin-margin bullion trading displaced mint work. The backdrop works against the company: positive real long rates are being imposed, which punishes long-dated property marks and leveraged balance sheets. What would confirm the bear case: further quarters of flat-free profit near 0.3-0.6 zloty a share, a property write-down, or debt not falling.
picks.consensus_delta: The question for a deep-value name is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a company with stable or growing earnings power. Here it is not: the market is, if anything, paying for property marks and one-off hand-over profit. The screen reads 9.77 zloty of earnings per share and a 6.7 times price to free cash flow. The filings show about 8 zloty of non-cash remeasurement, and free cash flow of about 0.8 zloty a share for the first nine months of 2026. No broker price target for this listing could be found, so there is no published street assumption to dispute. Our disagreement is with the screen, not with the market, and at 38 zloty the market already sits above our fair value of about 31.
picks.valley_of_death: In the next 3-9 months, three things could hurt. First, results for the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first quarter of 2027 without flat hand-overs could fall back to the 0.3-0.6 zloty-a-share run rate seen in the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026, so trailing earnings would collapse once the 2025 remeasurement rolls out of the trailing twelve months. Second, the year-end property valuation could cut marks if Polish long rates stay high. Third, the roughly 600 million zloty of borrowings (excluding leases) must be served from about 50 million zloty a year of free cash flow, which leaves little room for the dividend without property sales. There is no near-term maturity wall in the data we have, and the Altman Z-score (a solvency gauge) of 3.3 rules out distress.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced selling looks limited. The register is dominated by long-term holders around a dividend-paying mint; the smart-money score is 13 out of 100, and liquidity is thin (about 1,550 shares traded on 16 November 2026). A dividend cut to fund debt reduction could push yield-focused holders out. That would be selling against a business we already value below the current price, so it is not a setup to buy.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. Mennica Polska reached us as deep value on a margin of safety of several hundred percent. That signal is an accounting artefact: about 8 of the 9.77 zloty of 2025 earnings per share was a non-cash fair-value gain on the company's own property in the third quarter of 2025. The one new fact since our 26 October answer is the nine-month report of 28 October 2026, and it reinforces the read rather than reversing it. Valuing the business by its parts gives about 31 zloty a share, roughly 18% below today's 38.00 zloty. Those parts are the property that belongs to ordinary shareholders at a 15% discount to book, the mint, bullion and ticketing on clean profit at 12.5 times, and a small credit for remaining development, less the net debt. The adverse case is about 18 and the favourable case about 41, so the room below is much larger than the room above. Fairly stated, this is a sound, licensed business with real Warsaw property, a 1.50 zloty dividend and new foreign coin contracts, but the cheapness on the screen does not exist and the thesis has broken. We would look again if the shares fell into the low-to-mid twenties, if a property sale at book value paid down the new debt, or if profit excluding hand-overs rose clearly above 2 zloty a share a year.
picks.forcing_function: No hard date forces a re-rating up. Possible events, none of them binding or dated in a way that helps the value case: the Guatemala coin award (bid binding until 28 February 2027), the full-year 2026 report in spring 2027 with year-end property marks, and any property sale at book value used to pay down the new debt. # Mennica Polska (MNC.WA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-16. Price used: 38.00 zloty (PLN) on the Warsaw Stock Exchange, from the live FMP quote. Earlier committee review: 2026-10-26.

**Source note.** Mennica Polska does not publish earnings-call transcripts, and FMP holds none for this listing (checked 2026-11-16). This dossier therefore rests on the company's filed numbers: FMP quarterly income, balance-sheet and cash-flow statements through 30 September 2026, the consolidated nine-month report published on 28 October 2026 (headline table read through money.pl), the company's current reports noted at our 2026-10-26 review, and press coverage of earlier quarters. No management quote appears below because none could be sourced. Where we infer a cause from the statements, we say so.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Mennica Polska is the Polish state-licensed mint. Around that core it runs a bullion and coin trading business (Mennica Skarbowa), an electronic ticketing and payments arm, and a large Warsaw property estate built on the old mint site (Mennica Residence, Mennica Towers). Over the past five years the story has moved from "a mint with some property" to "a property holding company with a mint attached".

- **2021-2024:** steady revenue of 1.2-1.4 billion zloty, net profit of 34-92 million, earnings per share of 0.67-1.79 zloty. A thin-margin bullion business paid for by the mint licence and steady ticketing income.
- **2025:** revenue jumped to 1.83 billion zloty on gold-bar demand, but the headline profit of 498 million (9.77 zloty a share) was mostly a third-quarter 2025 non-cash fair-value gain on property: 409.6 million of pre-tax profit carried only 2.8 million of tax.
- **First half of 2026:** record profit (1.73 zloty a share in the second quarter) from handing over finished flats, then a 483 million zloty buy-out of the property partner, funded by about 568 million of new debt.
- **Third quarter of 2026 (reported 28 October 2026):** profit attributable to shareholders of 47.8 million zloty (0.94 zloty a share). Revenue of 634.7 million, gross profit of 139.9 million (a 22% gross margin against the usual 10-11%), and operating profit of 118.4 million.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim on the screen | What the filings show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Earnings per share of 9.77 zloty, margin of safety near 300% | About 8 zloty of it was the third-quarter 2025 property remeasurement, which is non-cash and taxed at almost nothing | Did not hold up |
| Net margin of 27% | One-off remeasurement. The underlying gross margin is 10-11% | Did not hold up |
| Net debt of 102 million zloty | 666 million including 66 million of leases (borrowings 654 million plus leases, less 54 million of cash), about 600 million excluding leases, at 30 September 2026 | Stale. Debt is six times higher |
| "Record" 2026 | Nine months: 2,225 million zloty of revenue and 372.7 million of operating profit, against 1,232 million and 91.4 million a year earlier. Profit to shareholders was 163.4 million (3.20 zloty a share) against 482.4 million | Real, but lumpy |
| Free-cash-flow yield of about 15% (price to free cash flow of 6.7) | Free cash flow was 19.1 million in the first quarter, 0.6 million in the second and 20.2 million in the third: about 40 million for nine months, or 0.8 zloty a share | Did not hold up |

The third-quarter detail matters. The 230 million zloty of deferred revenue on the 30 June balance sheet is gone at 30 September, and gross margin doubled. Our inference is that most of the third-quarter profit, like the second quarter's, came from handing over flats on which buyers had already paid deposits. That is real profit, but it does not recur. Minority holders took 37.7 million of the 85.5 million zloty of third-quarter net profit (44%), and minority equity rose from 167 to 205 million. This suggests the profitable development still sits in a vehicle with an outside partner, so less of the property profit belongs to Mennica's shareholders than the headline implies.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

No transcript is available, so tone cannot be rated from management's own words. The company's actions point to a shift from defence to offence: a raised 1.50 zloty dividend in 2026, a leveraged buy-out of the property partner, and foreign coin tenders (Bermuda and Mauritius in the first quarter of 2026, Colombia signed on 30 September 2026, a Guatemala bid on 19 October 2026). Trajectory: turning, toward property and leverage.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Mennica gives no numerical guidance. We cannot track promises against delivery. Reliability: not scorable. The accounts themselves are clean and audited, and the remeasurement was disclosed rather than hidden.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

No call transcript and no FMP analyst price-target coverage exist for this listing, and searches on 2026-11-16 found no dated broker target. The open questions an analyst would press:
1. What profit does the business earn excluding flat hand-overs and revaluations?
2. How will the new debt be repaid? Will it come from property sales at book value, or from a mint business that turned only about 40 million zloty of free cash flow in nine months?
3. How much of the remaining development profit belongs to minority holders?

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- In the third quarter of 2025, 409.6 million zloty of pre-tax profit was mostly a non-cash remeasurement, and that profit drives the screen's signal.
- In the second quarter of 2026, net debt rose from about 109 to 680.5 million zloty to fund the partner buy-out.
- Profit before tax for the first nine months of 2026 was 349.5 million zloty, against 503.3 million a year earlier.
- Free cash flow was about 40 million zloty in nine months, against a 1.94 billion market value.
- Return on invested capital fell from 11.0% in 2023 to about 4.7% in 2025, our earlier estimate. The screen shows 8.3%, inflated by the remeasurement.

Green flags:
- Net debt eased from 680.5 to about 666-673 million zloty in the third quarter of 2026, as 41.2 million of debt was repaid.
- The mint licence is real, and foreign coin contracts keep arriving (Colombia, 30 September 2026).
- The property is real Warsaw land and buildings, and Mennica Towers and Residence were fully let in the first quarter of 2026.
- The Piotroski score (a nine-point test of balance-sheet and profit health) is 8 of 9, and the Altman Z-score (a solvency gauge) is 3.3.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- Minority interest rising while the company was buying out a partner suggests there is a second partner vehicle, or a remaining stake. It caps how much hand-over profit reaches ordinary shareholders.
- Inventory of 521 million zloty (bullion and flats) against payables of only 102 million: the bullion book is funded more and more by debt rather than by suppliers.
- The weighted share count slipped from 50.998 million to 50.859 million in the third quarter of 2026. That is a small buyback or a treasury effect, not a capital-return signal.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning, from a cash-generating mint toward a leveraged Warsaw property holder.

The single most important thing to weigh is this: almost every profitable quarter since mid-2025 has been a revaluation or a flat hand-over. Recurring profit, on the clean quarters (0.54 zloty in the first quarter of 2026 and 0.31 in the fourth quarter of 2025), runs at roughly 1.5-2.5 zloty a share a year. At 38 zloty, that is a high-teens to mid-twenties earnings multiple for a business with 666 million zloty of net debt.

Moat: the minting licence and Mennica's role as the national mint are a narrow, regulatory moat. The bullion trading around it has none. Returns have fallen as low-margin bullion displaced mint work, so the trend is eroding. Secular threat: material but not terminal. Physical coins and cash minting face slow decline, and the property leg is rate-sensitive, but neither threatens the company's survival. The cheapness on the screen is an accounting print, not a fear-driven mispricing.

picks.bull_thesis:
Jet2 is the best-run leisure travel business in the United Kingdom, trading at roughly seven times its earnings and about six times its free cash flow. The bull case is that the market is pricing a cyclical squeeze as if it were permanent.

The evidence: revenue reached a record 7.48 billion pounds in the year to March 2026 (up 4.3%), passengers passed 20 million, and free cash flow was 495 million pounds - 2.6 billion pounds since the pandemic (FY26 results call, 8 July 2026). Management has a high-credibility record: it flagged its own small miss on flight-only pricing early (November 2025) and landed full-year operating profit inside its 435-440 million pound guide. The September 2026 trading statement showed booked passengers up 8.8% on capacity up 7.6%, with Gatwick ahead of plan.

Three drivers can lift profit from here. First, the newer bases (Bournemouth, Luton and from March 2026 Gatwick) carry start-up costs today and should mature into profit; Gatwick is guided to break even by the year to March 2029. Second, the A321neo fleet (232 seats against 189, lower cost per seat, about 22% of the summer 2026 fleet) lowers unit costs as it grows. Third, the buyback shrinks the share count: about 22 million shares were bought back in the year to March 2026 and a further 250 million pounds runs to 31 May 2027, roughly 9% of today's market value of about 2.7 billion pounds.

Consensus, as cited in the committee's prior record, expects earnings per share to recover toward 188p for the year to March 2028 and 243p for the year to March 2029. On those numbers the stock trades at about eight and six times earnings respectively, with a balance sheet that carries roughly break-even own net debt and an undrawn 500 million pound credit line. If flight-only pricing stabilises and Gatwick scales, a multiple of nine to ten times recovery earnings gives 1,700-2,150p.

Conditions: flight-only yields stop falling, hotel cost inflation moderates toward package price growth, and no large demand shock (conflict, recession) hits the 2027 summer booking season.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case is that Jet2's profit has stopped growing even as it adds capacity, and that the cheap multiple reflects a narrowing moat in a crowded market rather than a mispricing.

The evidence: net income fell from 447 million pounds (FY25) to 410 million pounds (FY26) while seat capacity grew about 8%. Flight-only ticket yield fell 7% in both the November 2025 and July 2026 calls; management calls this 'investing in price' and 'investing in load factor', which is another way of saying it cannot hold fares. Hotel costs, 45% of the cost base, rose about 6.5% while package prices rose 3%, of which about one point was customers trading up. Return on capital employed slipped from a 17% three-year average to 14.4%, and our scan's return on invested capital of 6.4% is near the cost of capital. Free cash flow fell about 25% year on year as bookings moved closer to departure.

The headline net cash of about 2.0 billion pounds is mostly customer deposits; the CFO himself put own cash at about 1.2 billion pounds, roughly equal to the 1.28 billion pounds of debt including leases. In a shock those deposits become a refund liability, not a cushion, and the new 2 times leverage target signals more borrowing to fund the Airbus order book. Consensus earnings for the year to March 2027 of about 136p (cited in the prior record) imply the stock is not cheap on this year's numbers at about 11 times.

What would confirm the bear case: the 18 November 2026 interim results showing summer 2026 profit flat or down despite higher passenger numbers, winter flight-only yields still falling, or capacity guidance for summer 2027 that again outruns the market. The business is also exposed to inflation: its gross margin fell from 13.8% to a loss through the 2021-22 period (largely pandemic-driven), and it has shown only partial pass-through of hotel cost increases.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is not pricing terminal decline; it is pricing a profit plateau. Seven brokers average a target of about 1,617p (MarketBeat aggregator, 3 November 2026), only about 6% above today's price, with five buys and two holds. Our base case of 1,720p sits a little above that, so the disagreement with the market is modest. Where we differ is on composition: the street leans on the headline 2.0 billion pounds of net cash, which we largely exclude because most of it is customer deposits, and on the recovery in earnings per share to about 188p by the year to March 2028, which we accept only in the base case. The street may also be too relaxed about flight-only yield, which has fallen 7% in two reporting periods running. We do not see a large expectations gap at 1,525p.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation risk, debt wall or forced dilution: own cash roughly matches debt, the 500 million pound facility is undrawn to October 2030, and the fleet is financed through long-dated asset-backed borrowing. The risk over the next three to nine months is earnings disappointment. The 18 November 2026 interim results could show summer 2026 profit flat despite more passengers, and the winter booking season (typically sold from January) has been late and price-led in each of the last two years. Hotel cost inflation, sustainable aviation fuel mandates (32 million pounds of extra premium in FY26) and employment-tax rises all pressure margins. A demand shock - renewed Middle East conflict hitting eastern Mediterranean bookings, as in spring 2026, or a UK consumer slowdown - would compress the customer-deposit float and free cash flow quickly. Any of these could take the shares back toward the 1,250p entry level.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-seller setup specific to Jet2: no index deletion, no lock-up, no dividend cut to drive out yield holders, and the company itself is a steady buyer through the 250 million pound buyback. The path to 1,250p is a sector-wide sell-off: European leisure and airline shares de-rate together on fuel spikes, geopolitical shocks or UK consumer weakness, as they did in March 2026 when Jet2 set a 12-month low near 980p. That is why the wait is tied to a sector or style sell-off rather than to mechanical selling.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 1,250p, which a sector-wide sell-off of UK consumer and airline shares could deliver.

The thesis holds. Jet2 is a well-run, cash-generative leisure travel business with credible management, a strong own-cash position and an aggressive buyback. Nothing dated has changed since the committee's last look on 19 October 2026; the price has moved only from 1,510p to 1,525p.

The issue remains the price, not the business. Our fair value is about 1,720p, only about 13% above today's 1,525p, which does not clear the 20% bar we require in a growth-with-sticky-inflation backdrop, while the adverse case of about 1,200p is about 21% below. At 1,250p the trade becomes attractive: about 38% upside to fair value against little downside to the adverse case. The shares were near 980p as recently as March 2026, so a sector-wide sell-off of that kind is not far-fetched.

We hold the value case at a middle rating. The moat is real but narrow and being tested: profit fell in FY26 while capacity grew about 8%, flight-only fares have been cut 7% two periods running, and return on capital has slipped from 17% to 14.4%. Until pricing stabilises, the low multiple partly reflects a business that is buying growth with price, which limits how much we will pay.

The interim results on 18 November 2026 are the next dated test. A clear profit increase with stable winter yields would strengthen the case; a profit fall with more price-cutting would argue for a lower fair value.
picks.forcing_function: No single event forces a re-rating. The nearest dated checkpoint is the interim results on 18 November 2026, which will show whether summer 2026 converted higher bookings into profit and give the first read on winter pricing. Beyond that, the forcing mechanism is slow: the buyback steadily retiring stock to May 2027, Gatwick progressing toward break-even by the year to March 2029, and the summer 2027 capacity and yield guidance, typically given in the new year. A re-rating needs evidence that flight-only pricing has stopped falling.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Jet2 plc (JET2.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

Debate date: 16 November 2026. Live price 1,525p (FMP quote, London listing, pence). Transcripts read: interim results call of 19 November 2025 (half year to 30 September 2025) and full-year results call of 8 July 2026 (year to 31 March 2026). The next dated release is the interim results for the half year to 30 September 2026, scheduled for 18 November 2026 (FMP earnings calendar), two days after this debate.

The short version: management is credible and conservative, the balance sheet is strong, and the cash returns are real. But the last eighteen months show a business that is growing passengers by giving away price, with profit flat to slightly down while capacity grows about 8% a year. That is a narrow moat that is being tested, not a widening one.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

In November 2025 the story was "record numbers" and expansion: passengers up 6%, the new bases at Bournemouth and Luton, and the launch of London Gatwick, described as "a once-in-a-generation opportunity to accelerate our growth" (H1 FY26 call). The Gatwick base was explicitly not expected to make money until the year to March 2029.

By July 2026 the emphasis had shifted from growth to resilience. The words used most were "resilient", "robust" and "controlled": operating profit "remained resilient even after absorbing Gatwick startup investment costs and wider industry cost pressures" (FY26 call). The growth story is still there (over 20 million passengers, up 5%), but the profit story has become one of absorbing costs. Capital returns moved to the centre: 363 million pounds returned in the year, "more than ever before", and a further 250 million pound buyback to run to 31 May 2027.

A new strand appeared in July 2026: a medium-term leverage target of 2 times net debt to EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) on an own-cash basis. That is a quiet signal that management intends to use more of the balance sheet over time, mainly to finance the Airbus fleet.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record revenue" (FY26) | Revenue 7.48 billion pounds, up 4.3%; three-year growth about 14% a year, flattered by the post-pandemic rebound from 1.23 billion in 2022 | True, but growth has slowed sharply |
| Operating profit "resilient" | Net income fell from 447 million pounds (FY25) to 410 million (FY26); FY26 operating profit guided at 435-440 million against 446.5 million the year before (29 April 2026 trading update) | Profit fell while capacity grew about 8%. "Resilient" is generous |
| Package price "resilient, up 3%" | About 1 point of the 3% came from customers trading up to four- and five-star hotels; hotel costs, 45% of the cost base, rose about 6.5% | Partial pass-through only; the cost of the holiday rose faster than its price |
| Flight-only demand strong (+15% passengers) | Flight-only ticket yield down 7% in both calls | Volume bought with price |
| "Over 2 billion pounds of net cash" | True on the headline basis, but most of it is customer deposits. The CFO himself split out "1.2 billion pounds of our own cash, excluding customer advances"; against about 1.28 billion pounds of debt including leases, own cash is roughly break-even | The headline overstates distributable cash |
| Free cash flow 495 million pounds; 2.6 billion since the pandemic | Consistent with the trailing figures; free cash flow fell about 25% year on year as customers booked later | True, but declining and timing-sensitive |
| Earnings per share "stable" | Earnings per share roughly 208-211p in both FY25 and FY26 - stable only because about 22 million shares were bought back | Per-share stability is buyback-supported |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Trajectory: stable, with a defensive tilt.

- November 2025: confident, expansionary - "Further growth in the first half across all our key metrics." The CFO was candid about uncertainty: "there's a lot of moving parts ... I'm not being evasive, but there are."
- July 2026: still upbeat ("I hope you're as excited about the future as we are"), but the vocabulary moved to cost absorption, "investing in price" and capital returns. On the Middle East conflict, management described later bookings and a bounce-back in eastern Mediterranean destinations rather than a lasting hit.

There is no sign of panic and no sign of rising ambition either. The language is that of a well-run operator in a tougher market.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Reliability: high.

- The November 2025 guide for flight-only pricing was "mid-single digits down"; the CFO volunteered that the outcome was "slightly worse" at minus 7%. Flagging a small miss early is a good sign.
- FY26 operating profit landed inside the 435-440 million pound range guided in April 2026.
- The beat rate in our data is 50% (one of two quarters), and FMP shows the November 2025 half-year earnings per share at 300p against a 281p estimate.
- The July 2026 capital spending cut of about 350 million pounds for the following year was explained as Airbus delivery timing, "timing only, it doesn't undermine any of our growth plans". That is plausible given industry-wide Airbus delays, but it also flatters near-term free cash flow.

No sandbagging pattern, and no pattern of over-promising.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Capacity versus price: analysts asked in both calls whether growing capacity 8-9% when competitors grow less would force further fare cuts. Management answered with flexibility ("we can make adjustments") rather than with yield guidance. This is the central unresolved question.
- Cost per seat: management repeatedly declined to give unit-cost guidance before Eurocontrol fees and slot declarations were known.
- Booking curve: later bookings came up in both calls; management treats them as a timing effect, but they reduce visibility and the customer-deposit float.
- AI distribution (July 2026): asked whether large language models would change how holidays are booked, management said "We've not seen a big impact from LLMs at the moment" and that direct bookings are steady at just under 80% for holidays. Honest, but untested.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Profit falling while capacity grows about 8% a year (April 2026 trading update; FY26 results, July 2026).
- Flight-only yield down 7% two reporting periods running (November 2025, July 2026).
- Return on capital employed down from 17% (three-year average quoted in November 2025) to 14.4% in FY26.
- Hotel cost inflation (about 6.5%) running ahead of package price (3%, of which 1 point is mix).
- Gatwick start-up costs, with profitability not expected until the year to March 2029.

Green flags:
- Strong own-cash position, an undrawn 500 million pound revolving credit facility extended to October 2030.
- Shareholder returns at record levels, with the share count falling: about 22 million shares bought back in FY26 and a further 250 million pounds under way to May 2027.
- Fleet renewal to the A321neo (232 seats against 189, lower seat cost; about 22% of the summer 2026 fleet).
- Industry-leading customer service and low cancellation rates, which support the package-holiday brand.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Investing in price" and "investing in load factor" have become standing phrases. When a company describes price cuts as investments, it is telling you that it does not have the pricing power to hold fares.
- The new 2 times leverage target signals a shift from a cash-rich to a more geared capital structure as the Airbus order book is financed.
- The CFO's own-cash framing (1.2 billion pounds excluding customer advances) is a welcome bit of honesty that the headline net-cash figure hides.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. Capital allocation is disciplined (buybacks at single-digit earnings multiples, fleet renewal, no acquisitions), and management is credible.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: Jet2's profit has stopped growing even as capacity grows. The investment case depends on Gatwick and the newer bases maturing into profit and on flight-only pricing stabilising. The interim results on 18 November 2026 are the next test of whether summer 2026 converted bookings into profit.

Moat: scale-cost plus brand (the integrated package-holiday model, about 80% direct distribution, customer-service reputation). It is real but narrow, and the evidence - return on capital falling from 17% to 14.4%, yields given away to fill seats - says it is being tested rather than widening. Our scan's return on invested capital of 6.4% sits near the cost of capital. Secular threat: manageable. AI-led travel search could change distribution over time, but management reports no impact so far and the direct-booking share is steady. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear-print on a competitive, cost-inflated leisure market, not a structurally shrinking base - but the moat needs proof that pricing can hold.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

# Boyd Gaming (NYSE: BYD) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*Covers five earnings calls: Q3 2025 (2025-10-23), Q4 2025 (2026-02-05), Q1 2026 (2026-04-23), Q2 2026 (2026-07-23) and Q3 2026 (2026-10-22), checked against the screener's financials and the FMP quarterly statements through 2026-09-30. Note: this is Boyd Gaming, the US regional and Las Vegas locals casino operator, not the Chinese carmaker BYD Co.*

**Bottom line:** Boyd is a steady, honestly run regional casino operator whose earnings have gone flat. Property margins have held near 38-40% for years and management delivers what it says. But since the July 2025 FanDuel stake sale, almost all per-share progress has come from buybacks, and from 2026 those buybacks are being paid for partly with new debt while free cash flow is squeezed by a heavy building program. The story is credible. The growth is mostly scheduled for 2027-2028.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-23):** The FanDuel transaction dominated. Management had just received about $1.8 billion for its FanDuel stake, cut leverage (debt divided by annual operating earnings) to about 1.5x, and spoke openly about what to do with that balance-sheet room: "could be M&A, could be other things, could tick back up." Core-customer play was "strengthening"; destination (out-of-town visitor) business was soft, mainly at the Orleans.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-05):** A victory lap on 2025: record revenue, roughly $1.4 billion of EBITDAR (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and rent), more than $800 million returned to shareholders and an 11% cut in the share count. The 2026 pitch was a list of projects: Cadence Crossing (opened end of Q1 2026), the Suncoast modernization, the St. Charles convention center, the Sky River expansion, and a tax-bill tailwind for consumers.
- **Q1-Q2 2026:** The message moved from "growth" to "steady." Midwest and South kept delivering; Las Vegas Locals stayed weighed down by the Orleans and Suncoast construction.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-22):** The language now leans on adjustments. Reported revenue and EBITDAR both fell about 1%; management pointed to the Tunica closure (November 2025), the Shreveport sale (2026-08-01), higher Kansas Star property taxes and a lower tax pass-through to say that, adjusted, revenue grew 2% and EBITDAR 1%. Destination softness in Las Vegas is now described as "increased softness," not improving. The growth story has moved out to Norfolk (opening November 2027), Par-A-Dice (construction late 2027) and the Sky River hotel (2028; it was "mid-2027" on the Q3 2025 call).

The arc: from a cash windfall and an open question about how to use it, to a flat operating base where buybacks and future openings carry the per-share story.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Margins consistent" (every call) | Midwest and South adjusted margin 38% in Q3 2026, "consistent with our third quarter margins over the last several years"; company EBITDAR $319.6M vs $321.8M a year earlier on revenue of $990M vs $1,004M | Holds |
| Core customer strength | Las Vegas Locals ex-Orleans/Suncoast revenue and EBITDAR +3% in Q3 2026; Midwest and South EBITDAR $201.6M, flat year on year | Holds, but growth is low single digits |
| Las Vegas Locals recovery | Segment EBITDAR $87.4M in Q3 2026 vs $92.1M (-5%); Downtown $12.9M vs $16.1M (-20%) | Weaker than the story; destination softness widened |
| Capital investments paying off | Sky River fees drive Managed & Other EBITDAR to $29.8M vs $26.3M (+13%); Treasure Chest and St. Charles cited | Holds where the projects have opened |
| "Robust free cash flow" (Q4 2025) | TTM (trailing twelve months) free cash flow to 2026-06-30 only $35M. Q2 2026 operating cash flow was -$24M because of the roughly $360M tax bill on the FanDuel gain (accrued expenses fell from $602M to $342M); capital spending runs about $140-155M a quarter | Distorted by the one-off tax; normalized free cash flow after all building is roughly $250-300M a year, not "robust" against a $600M+ buyback pace |
| Buybacks reduce share count | Diluted shares 73.0M in Q3 2026 vs 80.9M in Q3 2025 (-10%); $164M repurchased in Q3 2026, $387M authorization left | Holds |
| Balance sheet conservatism | Long-term debt rose from $2.27B (2026-03-31) to $2.61B (2026-06-30) to about $2.7B total debt (2026-09-30); cash $297M. Net debt including leases about $3.0B | Leverage is drifting back up from 1.5x as buybacks outrun free cash flow |
| EPS +264% (fiscal 2025) | Fiscal 2025 EPS $22.56 includes the FanDuel gain (Q3 2025 EPS $17.81 alone). Underlying EPS is about $6.6 TTM (Q4 2025 $1.79, Q1 2026 $1.37, Q2 $1.75, Q3 $1.71 GAAP; Q3 adjusted $1.67 vs $1.72 a year earlier) | The headline growth is a one-off; underlying EPS is flat to slightly down |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, drifting slightly defensive.** Q3 2025 was confident and forward-leaning ("customer trends ... have continued into October"). Q4 2025 was celebratory. By Q3 2026 the prepared remarks spend a full paragraph on adjustments before getting to growth, and the CFO declined to give sequential guidance on the fly: "I have tried to do it in past, and hopefully, I have learned to stop doing that." On M&A, management was disciplined rather than eager: "we are not gonna buy assets just because they are cheap." On online, it played down expectations for new licenses: "not anything that will be a tailwind for us." The tone is measured and candid, not promotional.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Boyd gives little formal guidance, which limits the test. Where it did guide, it delivered: the Online segment guide was raised to $60M of EBITDAR for 2025 and set at about $30M for 2026 after the FanDuel change; Cadence Crossing opened on schedule; Norfolk is "on time and on budget." The screener shows a beat in 6 of 7 recent quarters (86%), and Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $1.67 beat the $1.65 consensus. One timeline slipped: the Sky River hotel phase moved from "mid-2027" (2025-10-23) to "2028" (2026-10-22), though that is a managed property and a fee stream, not Boyd's own capital. **Reliability: High.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Leverage and capital use:** analysts asked repeatedly from Q3 2025 where leverage would settle after the windfall; management said leverage "could tick back up." It has: debt is rising while buybacks run near $150M+ a quarter.
- **Las Vegas destination softness:** raised every quarter since Q3 2025; management has called each bottom ("90-day booking pattern ... much more positive," 2025-10-23) and the softness has instead widened by Q3 2026.
- **Strip and mid-market M&A:** pressed in Q3 2026; management deflected with discipline language.
- **Online growth and new markets:** management answered that it is a small, well-run piece and will not "juice it."

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Las Vegas Locals EBITDAR -5% and Downtown -20% year on year in Q3 2026, after four quarters of being told destination business was close to turning.
- 🔴 Debt-funded buybacks: long-term debt up about $430M in the first nine months of 2026 while operating earnings were flat.
- 🔴 Insiders: 0 open-market buys against 23 sales (about 700,000 shares) in the screener's lookback.
- 🔴 Reported free cash flow is thin because the building program (Norfolk, Suncoast, Orleans, Par-A-Dice) is front-loaded; the payoff is 2027-2028.
- 🟢 Margins steady around 38% in Midwest and South for "the last several years."
- 🟢 Share count down about 10% in a year; dividend maintained at $0.20 a quarter (paid 2026-10-15).
- 🟢 Sky River management fees growing double digits; Online growing double digits on a clean comparison.
- 🟢 Kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 47.8% in 2019 to 56.0% in 2022).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The shift to "adjusted for these items" framing in Q3 2026 is new; earlier calls led with reported growth.
- "Destination business" has gone from a temporary drag (2025) to a standing caveat attached to every Las Vegas comment.
- Management now says plainly that it does not "have to do anything" on M&A; the excess capital is going to buybacks by default.
- The Sky River hotel slipping from mid-2027 to 2028 is small but is the first timeline slip in the set.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** The operating base is flat; the per-share result depends on buybacks and on the 2027-2028 openings. The single most important thing to weigh: the buyback is now partly funded with debt while operating earnings are not growing, so the equity is getting more levered on a flat base until Norfolk opens in November 2027.

**Moat:** a narrow but real regulatory-license moat. State gaming licenses limit new competition in most of Boyd's regional markets, and its Las Vegas locals network has scale and loyalty-program advantages. Returns are respectable (ROIC, return on invested capital, about 12%) and property margins are stable, though the scan flags gross margin as contracting; the evidence supports a stable, not widening, moat.

**Secular threat:** manageable. Online casino and sports-betting apps could pull some play away from physical casinos, but Boyd participates through Boyd Interactive and its retained FanDuel market-access fees. No terminal-value threat is visible; the cheapness looks like flat earnings plus rising leverage, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis:
Dürr is the world's largest maker of automotive paint shops, owns HOMAG (the world's largest woodworking-machinery maker) and owns Schenck, whose balancing machines handle, on the chief executive's account repeated on 12 November 2026, about nine out of ten aircraft engines. At 15.72 euros the equity is worth about 1.09 billion euros and the enterprise value (equity plus net borrowings) about 1.33 billion euros against roughly 4.1 billion euros of revenue: about 0.32 times revenue, below the nearest listed comparison Krones.

The third quarter of 2026 made the operating case more concrete. Automotive sales rose 15% and its margin beat an already high 8.2% prior-year base; group orders rose 5% and sales 3%; the group operating margin before one-off items reached 5.7%, the best of the year, and management expects Q4 to be stronger still, as it typically is. Orders in the Americas are up 10% over nine months as foreign carmakers build US plants behind tariffs, and China is up 17% on domestic customers. The demand mechanism the bull case has rested on since late 2024 held again: a global fleet of 500-plus paint shops, most of them inefficient, and a paint shop is about half of a car plant's energy use, so refurbishment and replacement spending continues whether the plant builds petrol or electric cars. HOMAG's margin is rising sequentially and its new Polish plant (inaugurated October 2026) brings efficiency gains from 2027. Schenck is growing on aerospace and on power-generation equipment for AI data centres.

The portfolio surgery is done, the cash-flow drag in 2026 is made of one-off items (a reversal of 2025 prepayments, tax on the disposal, restructuring cash, a tax-audit settlement), and the 9-10 December Capital Markets Day under an almost entirely new board is the venue for a new 2030 margin target. If 2027 shows operating cash flow covering spending, a business earning roughly 200 to 240 million euros of operating profit will not stay valued at about 1.3 billion euros of enterprise value.
picks.bear_thesis:
The screen calls Dürr extraordinarily cheap (4.3 times free cash flow, 2.92 euros of earnings per share), and both inputs are artifacts. The 2025 earnings came from the 227m euro after-tax gain on selling the environmental business; continuing operations lost about 50m euros that year. Trailing free cash flow included about 100m euros of customer payments the former finance chief said in March 2026 were pulled forward from 2026. That reversal is now in the numbers: FMP quarterly free cash flow fell from +103m in Q4 2025 to +46m, +13m and then -39m in Q3 2026, and the company itself said prepayments were lower because fewer large contracts were signed. Net debt rose from 218m to 240m euros in the quarter, and full-year guidance of -150m to 0 free cash flow implies more to come.

Reported Q3 net income was only 4.9m euros on 1.08 billion of sales once 32m of restructuring and a high tax charge are counted, so the improving operating margin is not yet reaching shareholders. The capital-allocation record is weak: three write-downs on BBS Automation in five quarters and a 25% cut to its 2030 revenue goal in August 2026; group return on invested capital is about 5%. The finance chief retired at end-September and the new one starts weeks before a Capital Markets Day whose first target revision, last time, went down. The big Q4 orders management is counting on may slip into 2027, as it openly allowed. And the macro tape since summer has rewarded companies whose cash flow covers their spending and punished those guiding to burn cash, which is exactly where Dürr sits until March 2027.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market runs both ways. Against the screens: the 4.3 times free cash flow and 2.92 euro earnings figures are a disposal gain and a one-off cash pull-forward; on corrected numbers the business earns roughly 1.10 to 1.25 euros a share and is guided to burn cash in 2026, so it is about half as cheap as advertised. The third quarter made that concrete, with free cash flow at -39m euros and net debt up 22m. In Dürr's favor: the market keeps reading European carmaker distress straight across to Dürr's order book, and the third quarter again contradicted that read. Automotive sales rose 15%, Americas orders are up 10% on foreign carmakers building US plants, China is up 17% on domestic customers, and the demand is driven by an inefficient installed fleet of 500-plus paint shops rather than by new capacity. At 15.72 euros, a new 52-week low reached on a day with no company news, the price is pricing the cash trough as if it were permanent.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window runs from now to the March 2027 full-year report. Q4 2026 must absorb the rest of the guided cash burn (full-year free cash flow -150m to 0 after roughly flat nine months), restructuring cash from Vector and HOMAG, tax on the 2025 disposal and the undisclosed tax-audit settlement; net debt, 240m euros at 30 September including leases, likely ends the year higher. A brand-new finance chief presents for the first time at the 9-10 December Capital Markets Day, where a cautious 2030 target would land on a stock already at its low. If the big Q4 automotive orders slip into 2027, as management allowed they might, the Q4 order number will compare against a very high prior-year base. None of this is a solvency risk; it is a sentiment risk in a tape that pays for cash flow now.
picks.positioning_washout: No forced-selling event is scheduled: the dividend (0.80 euros paid in Q2 2026) was described as sustainable, there is no index deletion, lock-up or spin-off flow in view, and the HOMAG minority is a small, court-fixed claim, not an overhang. What is happening is a slow sector-and-style de-rating: the stock fell 4.1% to 15.72 on 16 November 2026 on no company news, its new 52-week low, about 18% below its 200-day average (19.10) and 37% below the 52-week high of 25.10. The register is thin (about 1.09bn euros of market value), the smart-money score is 7 of 100 and there is no insider buying. The level we wait for, 15.00 euros, is about 4.6% below today's price and is the kind of price a continued sector sell-off into the December Capital Markets Day or a soft Q4 order print could deliver.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 15.00 euros, which the sector sell-off could deliver. The thesis holds, and the third quarter reported on 12 November 2026 supported it: orders up 5%, sales up 3%, Automotive sales up 15% with a margin above last year's strong 8.2%, the group margin before one-off items at 5.7% (the best of the year), and full-year guidance confirmed. Dürr remains a good automotive paint-shop franchise, a cyclical but improving woodworking-machinery leader and a growing balancing niche, valued at about 0.32 times revenue.

Our sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately, then netting off what the group owes) gives a fair value of about 23.75 euros, down slightly from 23.89 because net debt rose by 22m euros in the quarter; the adverse case is about 12.05 and the favorable case about 37.65. At 15.72 the discount to fair value comfortably clears our 20% entry bar, so price is not the reason we wait. The reason is the same one this committee gave on 10 November, and the third quarter confirmed it rather than retired it: free cash flow turned negative (-39m euros per FMP) as the 2025 prepayment pull-forward reverses, net debt is rising, and the full-year guide still allows up to 150m euros of cash burn, all landing before the March 2027 report can show a cleaner 2027. The screen's cheapness is roughly half real, the acquisition record is poor, and a new finance chief debuts at the December Capital Markets Day. With the price only about 4.6% above our level after a no-news 4.1% fall today, we keep the order where it is rather than chase it.

The independent second opinion (fair value 21.50, skeptic-revised 22.34) named no specific figure to check, so it does not move our numbers. Conviction stays at 3; on the value case alone (ignoring catalysts and macro) it is a 4, held back from a 5 by the accounting and cash-flow quality, not by the discount.
picks.forcing_function: Two dated moments and one undated condition. The Capital Markets Day on 9-10 December 2026 (date fixed) sets new 2030 targets under the new board; it is a presentation, two-sided in direction. The full-year 2026 report and 2027 guidance, due around March 2027, is the first chance to show the 2026 cash drag was one-off. The undated condition that actually forces a re-rating is free cash flow turning positive again through 2027: once operating cash covers spending, the funding-quality objection this market is applying disappears and a business earning about 200 to 240m euros of operating profit is hard to keep at about 1.3bn euros of enterprise value. Roughly 12 to 18 months away.

# Dürr AG (DUE.DE) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16 from five earnings calls (13 May 2025, 13 November 2025, 5 March 2026, 6 August 2026, 12 November 2026) and FMP quarterly statements through 30 September 2026. Prices in euros on the Frankfurt XETRA listing; live quote 15.72 euros on 16 November 2026.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Two years ago Dürr told a growth-through-automation story: buy BBS Automation, build "the second largest player in industrial automation", and run five divisions. Across the five calls in this file the story contracted, deliberately, into a simpler one: three divisions (Automotive, Woodworking/HOMAG, Industrial Automation), the environmental-technology business sold (closed 31 October 2025), and "profitability first" as the operating rule. The May 2025 call was still about portfolio reshaping and the held-for-sale process; November 2025 and March 2026 were about the disposal gain, the cash pull-forward and a negative 2026 free-cash-flow guide; August 2026 added the Vector restructuring at BBS Automation and a 25% cut to its 2030 revenue target; the 12 November 2026 call is the first that reads like a steady-state operating report: sales +3%, orders +5%, a 5.7% operating margin before one-off items, guidance confirmed, and a Capital Markets Day on 9-10 December 2026 to reset the 2030 targets.

The growth driver that has quietly grown in importance is Schenck balancing (equipment that balances rotating parts such as aircraft-engine and turbine rotors). In November 2026 management credited it with "high order intake, sales and earnings" on power-generation spending for AI data centres, and repeated that Dürr balances "9 out of 10 aircraft engines globally". The driver quietly dropped is battery-production automation, which no longer features as a growth pillar.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Management claim | Date | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paint-shop demand is replacement and efficiency spending that survives a capacity freeze ("a fleet of roughly 500-plus significant paint shops... at very low efficiency levels") | Nov 2024 to Nov 2026, repeated | Q2 2026 order intake +13%; Q3 2026 +5%; Automotive Q3 sales +15% with margin above the 8.2% prior-year base | Matches |
| Group margin recovers in the second half | 6 Aug 2026 | Q3 2026 operating margin before one-off items 5.7%, the best of the year; nine-month 4.7% | Matches so far; Q4 must carry the year into the 5.0-6.5% range |
| 2025 earnings per share of 2.92 (+107%) | FY2025 | Driven by the 227m euro after-tax disposal gain; continuing operations lost about 50m euros | Headline overstates the business |
| Trailing free cash flow of about 225m euros | to mid-2026 | Included about 100m euros of customer payments pulled into December 2025 (CFO, 5 Mar 2026). FMP quarterly free cash flow: Q4-25 +103m, Q1-26 +46m, Q2-26 +13m, Q3-26 -39m | Overstated; the reversal is now visible |
| "Strong balance sheet... sustainable dividends" | Aug 2026 presentation | FMP net debt (including leases) 218.1m at 30 Jun 2026 rose to 240.1m at 30 Sep 2026; borrowings 987m, cash 747m | Still comfortable, but moving the wrong way |
| BBS Automation "has passed the trough" | 12 Nov 2026 | Industrial Automation "virtually returned to breakeven" in Q3 after a clearly negative Q2; third write-down booked in Q2 2026 (Q2 net loss 89.5m euros) | Unproven; one quarter |

Reported Q3 2026 net income was only 4.9m euros on 1,079m of revenue: 32m of restructuring provisions (Vector plus 17m at HOMAG) and a high tax charge (9.9m on 15.1m pre-tax profit) swallow the operating improvement.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable, shifting from defensive to cautiously offensive. In March 2026 the tone was explanatory and defensive (the cash pull-forward, the disputed tax audit whose size "we don't want to mention"). In August 2026 it was candid about BBS ("our expectations in terms of volumes... did not turn out"). On 12 November 2026 the CEO called the performance "very solid" against "an altogether adverse environment", and pointed to Q4 as "the strongest quarter in terms of order intake", while hedging that big orders "which might not be signed in Q4 are highly appreciated also in Q1". On pricing, he was blunt: auto margins are "never good. It's only bad or worse", but "we defend our margins". Confidence is real but carefully bounded.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium-High. Delivered: the five-to-three portfolio reduction on schedule; the 2025 margin step-up (4.6% to 5.6%); the H2 2026 margin recovery so far; 2026 guidance confirmed after nine months (orders 3.8-4.2bn, sales 3.9-4.3bn, margin before one-offs 5.0-6.5%, free cash flow -150m to 0). Missed: the BBS Automation plan (three write-downs in five quarters, 2030 revenue target cut 25% on 6 Aug 2026). The screener's 1-of-7 quarterly beat rate reflects consensus models built on polluted earnings more than operating misses. No sandbagging pattern; the group margin is guided "toward the lower end", which it is tracking.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Recurring: pricing quality on new orders in a weak European auto market (Q3 2026, answered with a general margin-defence argument rather than numbers); the size of the disputed German tax audit (never disclosed); BBS Automation's path and whether M&A resumes (answered: "not... anything soon", a small life-science bolt-on eventually); the tax rate (Q3 2026, answered approximately). What analysts did not press hard: the second-half cash burn and the year-end net-debt figure, which is the single number most likely to disappoint in the March 2027 report.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- 🔴 Three goodwill write-downs on one acquisition (Q2 2025, Q4 2025, Q2 2026).
- 🔴 Free cash flow turned negative in Q3 2026 (-39m euros per FMP) as prepayments fell; net debt rose 22m in the quarter.
- 🔴 CFO Dietmar Heinrich retired end-September 2026; the CEO covered the Q3 call alone; new CFO Alexandra Dambeck starts mid-November, weeks before the Capital Markets Day.
- 🔴 Undisclosed tax-audit liability (March 2026).
- 🟢 Automotive Q3 2026 sales +15% with margin above the 8.2% prior-year base; Americas orders +10% and China +17% in nine months.
- 🟢 HOMAG margin rising sequentially and a new Polish plant inaugurated October 2026, with efficiency effects from 2027.
- 🟢 Schenck balancing growing on aerospace and power-generation demand.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The shift in vocabulary from "industrial automation leader" (2024) to "sustainable automation" and "profitability first" (2026) is a quiet admission that the BBS growth case failed. The board is almost entirely new (CEO plus three new members, including a new CFO), so the 9-10 December Capital Markets Day will be the first set of targets this team owns. Mercedes hosting part of that event at its Sindelfingen site, the "largest paint shop ever" for Dürr, is a customer-relationship signal, not a financial one. Management now stresses that the European/German news flow is not its whole business, repeated with numbers on regional orders.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: PIVOTING (turning). The portfolio surgery is done and the operating core is improving, but the acquisition record is poor and the 2026 cash line is negative by guidance. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: the cheapness on the screen (4.3 times free cash flow, 2.92 earnings per share) is built on a disposal gain and a one-off cash pull-forward; on corrected numbers the stock is about half as cheap as advertised, and the year-end 2026 net debt and the 2027 cash guide in March 2027 are what will decide whether the market pays for the rest.

Moat: scale-cost and switching costs in automotive paint shops (the largest supplier, an installed base it services, 40%+ return on capital employed in Automotive, prepayment-funded) and an intangible certification niche in Schenck balancing; diluted at group level by HOMAG's cyclicality and BBS Automation's losses. Group return on invested capital of about 5% keeps it narrow; Automotive margins are stable to rising, so not eroding. Secular threat: material but not terminal — the shift to electric cars does not change paint-shop demand, but a prolonged European auto capacity reduction and Chinese domestic competitors can compress pricing. The cheapness is mostly a fear-print on a cyclical, cash-timing trough, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.
picks.sop_fair_value: 23.75 EUR per share (base case; range 12.05 adverse to 37.65 favorable)
picks.sop_breakdown: Base case on 2026 guided earnings power (group margin before one-off items guided 5.0-6.5%, trending to the low end; Q3 2026 at 5.7%): Automotive 2,100m revenue at 7.5% (guided 7-8%) = 157.5m at 7.5 times = 1,181m; Woodworking/HOMAG 1,250m at 4.5% = 56m at 7 times = 394m; Schenck balancing about 30m of profit at 11 times = 330m; BBS Automation 114m (about 0.3 times revenue, loss-making, mid-restructuring); holding cost -160m. Enterprise value 1,859m. Less net financial debt excluding leases of about 100m at 30 September 2026 (77.7m reported net financial status at 30 June 2026 plus the 22m rise in FMP net debt from 218.1m to 240.1m in Q3; the FMP 240m figure includes lease liabilities inside borrowings), pension provisions 33.4m and the HOMAG minority claim about 80m (2.55m shares at the 31.58-euro court-set price). Equity about 1,646m over 69.2m shares = 23.78, stated as 23.75 euros. Cross-check: at 23.75 the enterprise value is about 0.45 times revenue, still below Krones on revenue and profit-before-depreciation multiples; the analyst consensus target of about 25.9 euros cited in the prior record was not re-verified today and is not used.
picks.sop_bull: Favorable sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately, then netting off what the group owes): about 37.65 euros a share. On 2027 recovery earnings and a normal capital-goods rating: Automotive about 2.15bn euros of revenue at 9% margin (195m) at 9 times = 1,755m; HOMAG about 1.3bn at 6% (78m) at 9 times = 702m; Schenck about 270m at 12.5% (34m) at 13 times = 442m; BBS Automation 220m, crediting the Vector plan; holding cost about 20m a year at 8 times = -160m. Enterprise value about 2,959m. Less net debt of 240.1m (FMP, 30 September 2026, leases included in borrowings; the conservative definition, since the favorable case should not also get the benefit of excluding leases), pension provisions of 33.4m and the HOMAG minority claim of about 80m. Equity about 2,606m over 69.2m shares = 37.65 euros a share.
picks.sop_bear: Adverse sum-of-the-parts: about 12.05 euros a share. On a European car-capital-spending air pocket and trough ratings: Automotive 2.0bn at 7% (140m, below the guided 7-8% band) at 6 times = 840m; HOMAG 1.2bn at 3.75% (45m) at 6 times = 270m; Schenck 28m at 9 times = 252m; BBS Automation 35m (little more than its remaining goodwill); holding cost -160m. Enterprise value about 1,237m. Less net debt marked to end-2026 on the worst end of the cash guide (about 290m), pensions of 33.4m and the HOMAG minority claim of about 80m. Equity about 834m over 69.2m shares = 12.05 euros a share, roughly 0.7 times book value of 1.23bn euros, a level European capital-goods cyclicals reach in real recessions.
picks.risk_reward: From 15.72 euros: the adverse case is about 12.05 and the base case about 23.75; the favorable case about 37.65. There is no structural floor: no deal terms, no tender, no net cash (the group carries net borrowings), and the dividend is a payout policy, not a floor. The setup is asymmetric on paper, but the next five months carry a known cash burn and rising net debt before the March 2027 report can show whether 2027 cash flow turns positive.
picks.catalyst_status_plain: already happened
picks.peer_comps_note: The peer file lists Krones, GEA, Fanuc, ABB, Kuka and Atlas Copco and rates Dürr cheap versus peers; it carries no live override multiple, so the anchors used are the dated ones checked in the prior full debate (24 August 2026): Krones about 0.61 times revenue and 5.7 times profit before depreciation, GEA 1.92 times and 11.9 times, Biesse 0.22 times and 6.4 times. Dürr at 15.72 trades at about 0.32 times revenue. GEA, Fanuc, ABB and Atlas Copco earn far higher returns on capital and are not fair anchors; Krones is the honest one, and against it the discount is roughly a third. Part of that gap is shared sector beta (all of these names move on the same European industrial and automotive capital-spending cycle), which we do not credit as name-specific edge. The idiosyncratic part is a rating below Krones despite Automotive's 40%-plus return on capital employed and the Schenck niche. The peer file's own rationale leans on earnings-based margins of safety computed from the polluted 2.92 euro earnings figure; only the revenue and profit-before-depreciation comparisons survive.
picks.thesis_evidence: The load-bearing claims held in the 2026-11-12 third-quarter report: order intake +5% and sales +3% year on year, Automotive sales +15% with margin above the 8.2% prior-year base, group operating margin before one-off items 5.7% (best of 2026), full-year 2026 guidance confirmed (orders 3.8-4.2bn, sales 3.9-4.3bn, margin 5.0-6.5%, free cash flow -150m to 0). The free-cash-flow reversal (FMP Q3 2026 -39.0m) and the rise in net debt to 240.1m at 2026-09-30 were guided, not new. The 2026-11-16 drop to 15.72 (-4.1%, new 52-week low) came with no company news in FMP for 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-16, so it reads as a sector or style sell-off rather than a company event.
picks.macro_fit_note: Quadrant REFLATION (growth up, inflation sticky; real GDP +3.37% annualized to 2026-07) and debt-cycle phase DISCIPLINE (18 weeks, expected horizon 18 months: positive real long rates, duration punished, cash flow rewarded); a German plant engineer guiding to negative 2026 free cash flow sits on the wrong side of that until its 2027 cash guide in March. Its margins held through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 21.4% to 21.8%), and on 2026-11-12 the CEO said auto pricing is under constant pressure but 'we defend our margins' through cost control and low-cost-country sourcing, with Automotive Q3 margin above the prior-year 8.2%.
picks.entry_plain: buy near 15 EUR, which a sector-wide or style-wide sell-off could deliver

picks.bull_thesis: A2A is turning itself into a more regulated, less weather-dependent utility, and the 2026 slowdown is a weather and policy air-pocket rather than a trend. Since January 2025 it has run the Milan and Brescia electricity grid bought from Enel (Duereti), it sold gas networks to Ascopiave for EUR 430m (cashed 2025-06-03), and grid capital spending was up 5% year on year in the first nine months of 2026. Regulated networks earn a return set by the energy regulator, so each euro invested there adds predictable profit. Even in the second-worst hydro year in a decade, nine-month 2026 adjusted EBITDA fell only about 3% to EUR 1,673m (2026-11-10), because wind, solar and gas plants filled the gap - proof that diversification works. Guidance has been confirmed at every print since November 2025. Two dated growth steps lie ahead: the Monfalcone gas plant (about EUR 10m of EBITDA a month, around mid-2027) and the Corteolona waste-to-energy plant (end-2028), plus a 100 MW solar extension in Friuli. A normal water year alone would add back roughly EUR 40m of EBITDA. If 2027 EBITDA reaches about EUR 2.3bn and the market pays peer multiples for the grid (about 9x) and waste (about 7.5x), equity value is around EUR 3.2 a share. Conditions: hydro normalises, concession renewals after 2029 keep today's economics (the CEO's arithmetic of about EUR 103 per megawatt hour sold against about EUR 35 of fee and EUR 50 of cost), and leverage stops rising.
picks.bear_thesis: Earnings are going sideways while debt climbs, and the state is taking a bigger slice. Net income peaked at EUR 864m in 2024, fell to EUR 750m in 2025 and is guided to only EUR 630-660m in 2026, with management pointing to the low end on 2026-11-10; trailing earnings per share are EUR 0.21 against EUR 0.28 in 2024. Net debt rose from about EUR 5.83bn in June to about EUR 6.0bn in September, taking leverage to 2.8x EBITDA from 2.4x at end-2025, because capital spending (over EUR 1bn in nine months) and the dividend run ahead of cash generation; trailing free cash flow is only EUR 161m. Return on invested capital of about 5% barely covers a utility's cost of capital, so growth spending adds little value per share. Policy risk is rising: hydro concession fees cost EUR 47m in nine months, a higher IRAP tax is coming, a windfall levy on fixed-price contracts is under discussion (about EUR 30m by the CEO's estimate) and all hydro concessions expire in 2029. In the 2021-22 inflation spike gross margin fell from 27.6% to 10.7%, so the business does not pass costs through well. If 2027 hydro is weak again and multiples compress with rising real rates, EBITDA of about EUR 2.1bn at lower multiples leaves equity near EUR 1.8 a share.
picks.consensus_delta: For a deep-value name the question is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power. It is not: at about 11x the low end of 2026 profit guidance and about 6.5x EV/EBITDA, the market prices A2A as an ordinary, fairly valued utility. If anything the street is slightly more optimistic than us - broker targets near EUR 2.80-2.86 (Equita, 2026-07-17; Investing.com average cited 2026-11-10) assume a quick return to earnings growth in 2027. We think those targets underweight three things the 2026-11-10 call made plain: leverage rising to 2.8x, a higher IRAP tax excluded from adjusted profit, and policy pressure on hydro (concession fees, a possible windfall levy, renewals in 2029). There is no consensus error large enough to exploit.
picks.valley_of_death: Over the next 3-9 months the risks are a weak start to 2027 if hydro stays low (management noted dry conditions could extend into early 2027), the 2027 bond refinancing at higher rates (CFO, 2026-11-10), a windfall levy on fixed-price power contracts (about EUR 30m by the CEO's own estimate) and the reported profit hit from the IRAP surcharge. None of these threatens solvency - leverage of 2.8x is manageable and there is no maturity wall in the materials - but together they could keep 2027 earnings flat and the shares range-bound.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no sign of forced-selling pressure. A2A is a FTSE MIB member with a stable dividend policy and a domestic yield-holder base anchored by its municipal shareholders (Milan and Brescia). No dividend cut, index deletion or lock-up is in view; the shares trade in the lower part of their 52-week range (EUR 2.13-2.62) on ordinary volume. A dividend cut would change that, but nothing in the 2026-11-10 call suggests one.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. The thesis holds: A2A is a well-run, diversified Italian utility that confirmed its 2026 targets again on 2026-11-10, and its regulated grid is growing. But the nine-month results made the case slightly thinner, not stronger: profit is guided to the low end, adjusted nine-month profit fell 14%, and debt rose to 2.8 times EBITDA. At EUR 2.265 our fair value of EUR 2.55 leaves only about 12-13% of upside, short of the 20% discount this market backdrop requires, and the adverse case near EUR 1.80 sits further below than fair value sits above. We see no forced seller who would hand us a materially better price, so we name no entry level; we would revisit if leverage stabilises in the March 2027 full-year results or the price falls far enough to clear the bar on a fair value we still believe. Conviction stays at 2. On value alone, setting the catalyst aside, the business deserves a middling 3: a narrow, regulator-backed moat and credible management, but no real discount.
picks.forcing_function: No hard-dated event forces a re-rating. The next scheduled print is the full-year 2026 results in March 2027, which should show whether the low end of guidance holds and whether leverage stabilises; Monfalcone's start-up around mid-2027 is the first new earnings step. A data-centre deal or a hydro-concession framework would be upside events, but neither is dated.

# A2A S.p.A. (A2A.MI) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16. Calls reviewed: H1 2024 (2024-07-30), FY 2024 (2025-03-20), Q1 2025 (2025-05-13), H1 2025 (2025-08-05) and nine months 2026 (2026-11-10). Price on the Milan listing: EUR 2.265 (FMP quote, 2026-11-16).*

**The takeaway.** A2A is a well-run Lombardy multi-utility (a company that runs power generation, electricity and gas networks, waste and recycling plants, district heating and an energy retail business under one roof). Management has delivered or confirmed its guidance at every print we can check, and the 2026 targets were confirmed again on 2026-11-10. But that latest confirmation came with a clear tilt to the low end of the range, net debt is rising faster than profit, and a higher regional business tax (IRAP) and much higher hydro concession fees are leaking value to the Italian state. The business is solid; it is not getting cheaper to own.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **2024 (H1 2024 call, 2024-07-30):** a "happy holiday" story. Rain filled the reservoirs, hydro plants ran above 99% availability, and hedged power prices were high. The CEO, Renato Mazzoncini, framed the year as proof of the plan, with a "positive hydro contribution" carrying the numbers.
- **2025 (FY 2024 and H1 2025 calls):** the story moved to regulated networks, meaning businesses whose returns are set by the energy regulator. A2A bought Enel's grid in Milan and Brescia provinces (Duereti, live from January 2025), sold part of its gas network to Ascopiave for EUR 430 million (cashed "exactly in the 3rd of June" 2025), and signed a 17-year liquefied-gas supply deal with BP. Management called this "business risk profile optimization": less weather and commodity risk, more regulated earnings.
- **2026 (nine-month call, 2026-11-10):** the tone turns defensive. The headline is resilience against "a challenging backdrop": the second-worst hydro year in a decade, "extreme weather conditions", price volatility and "higher hydroelectric concession fees". The pitch is now that the diversified model limits the damage, not that it compounds.
- **Dropped or deferred:** the data-centre opportunity (two sites with land secured) still has no dated monetisation step. Asset rotation is now "opportunistic" with "no specific plan" (CFO Luca Moroni, 2026-11-10).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Diversification limits shocks: adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) for nine months 2026 of EUR 1,673m, down only about 3% (2026-11-10) | Consistent. The hydro shortfall (about EUR 40m) and concession fees (EUR 47m) were partly offset by wind, solar, gas-fired plants (+EUR 20m) and grid growth. Generation and trading fell about 9%. | Matches |
| Earnings are growing under the plan (H1 2025: "the EBITDA is growing") | Net income went EUR 659m (2023) to EUR 864m (2024) to EUR 750m (2025); adjusted nine-month 2026 net profit of EUR 473m is down 14%. Trailing diluted earnings per share are EUR 0.21 against EUR 0.28 in 2024. | Richer than the numbers |
| Leverage is under control | Net debt rose from about EUR 5.83bn (2026-06-30) to about EUR 6.0bn at 2026-09-30 (bundle: borrowings EUR 7.70bn less cash EUR 1.62bn = EUR 6.08bn, no capitalized leases). Net debt to EBITDA went from 2.4x (end-2025) to 2.8x. | Holding, but trending the wrong way |
| Capital spending turns into future earnings | Nine-month capital spending exceeded EUR 1bn, about 70% for growth. Return on invested capital is about 5.2%, near the cost of capital for a regulated utility. Monfalcone gas plant (about EUR 10m of EBITDA a month) lands around mid-2027. | Plausible, slow |
| Free cash flow | Trailing free cash flow is only EUR 161m on a EUR 7.1bn market value; the 7.6x price-to-free-cash-flow figure in the scan uses the stronger fiscal 2025 year. The dividend plus capital spending is being partly debt funded. | Weaker than the headline multiple |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining, from confident to defensive.** In 2024 the CEO spoke of "the reason for being happy". In 2025 the tone was execution ("with a very clear punctuality"). On 2026-11-10 the opening word was resilience: the results show "how our diversified business model has helped us navigate a challenging environment" (investor relations, 2026-11-10). Management also spent a large part of the Q&A rebutting a politician's claim that hydro is sold at EUR 350 per megawatt hour and explaining a possible windfall levy on fixed-price contracts (the CEO estimated "EUR 30 million", stressing "it's difficult really to say a number"). That is a company playing defence on policy.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- 2026 guidance (adjusted EBITDA EUR 2.21-2.25bn, adjusted net profit EUR 630-660m) was set in November 2025 and confirmed on 2026-03-17, 2026-05-14, 2026-07-30 and again on 2026-11-10 (Il Sole 24 Ore and Teleborsa, 2026-11-10). On 2026-11-10 management pointed to the low end of the range because of weak hydro output.
- In 2025 they delivered roughly in line with plan; the H1 2025 call called the EUR 1.2bn first half "quite in line with our target".
- The screener's "beat 0 of 1 quarter" reading rests on a single quarter and is not informative.
- **Reliability: High** on headline delivery; the steering to the low end is honest disclosure rather than a miss. There is no sandbagging pattern (setting easy targets to beat): guidance has tended to be met, not beaten.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Hydro concessions after 2029:** analysts keep asking how renewals will work. The CEO argued the economics (about EUR 103 per megawatt hour sold for 2027, about EUR 35 of concession fee, about EUR 50 of operating cost) leave little room for the state to take more. This is the single largest policy exposure.
- **Windfall levy and IRAP:** the extra IRAP charge is excluded from the "adjusted" profit, so reported profit will be lower than the adjusted figure for the next years.
- **Leverage and refinancing:** the CFO said 2027 refinancing will come early in the year, with duration managed to avoid "deteriorating the average cost of debt" - an implicit admission that the cost of new debt is higher.
- **Hedging:** about 70-72% of 2027 output is hedged, normal for A2A, so 2027 earnings carry roughly 30% open exposure to power prices and water.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Net debt to EBITDA up from 2.4x to 2.8x in nine months (2026-11-10), with earnings flat to down.
- 🔴 Low end of 2026 guidance flagged (2026-11-10); adjusted nine-month profit down 14%.
- 🔴 State take rising: higher hydro concession fees (EUR 47m drag in nine months) and a new IRAP surcharge.
- 🔴 Gross margin fell from 27.6% (2019) to 10.7% (2022) in the last inflation spike; the business is classified as inflation-exposed.
- 🟢 Guidance met or confirmed at every print since November 2025.
- 🟢 Treatment-plant problems from the first half stabilised in Q3 2026; retail customer churn back near 2025 levels.
- 🟢 Grid capital spending up 5% year on year; regulated asset base growing.
- 🟢 Piotroski score 7 of 9 (a test of improving accounting quality) in the scan.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary moved from "growth" and "achievements" (2025) to "resilience", "balance" and "visibility" (2026). Visibility is what a management team sells when growth is not available this year.
- Asset rotation changed from a stated pillar to "no specific plan... opportunistic approach" (2026-11-10). One lever for de-leveraging is now off the table as a promise.
- The CFO's interest-rate swaps "when the interest rate were very high and peaked very high in the last week and month" show they feel the rate backdrop. Same management team throughout; no new voices.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: Stable.** The business is executing its plan, but earnings are flat in 2026 and debt is climbing while capital spending runs ahead of profit. The single most important thing to weigh: at about EUR 2.27 the shares trade at roughly 11x the low end of the 2026 profit guide with leverage rising - fairly priced for a utility, not a mispricing. The value case depends on Monfalcone and grid growth showing up in 2027-28 earnings, not on anything this year.

**Moat:** regulatory-licence and scale. Regulated networks and waste-to-energy permits are hard to replicate, and the hydro concessions are valuable. Width is narrow: return on invested capital of about 5% is roughly the allowed return, not an excess return, and is stable rather than rising or falling. **Secular threat:** manageable. The energy transition is a tailwind for grids and a mixed bag for gas plants; the real long-run risk is political (concession renewals in 2029, windfall levies), which caps upside but does not shrink the earnings base structurally. The cheapness is neither a fear-print nor a value trap; it is a fair price for a levered, policy-exposed utility.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
