picks.bull_thesis: The bull case is that OKEA has moved from investing to paying out on schedule, or ahead of it, and that the market has not yet fully priced a cash-paying, growing late-life producer. The 3 November 2026 third-quarter report delivered on every operating claim this committee was waiting for. Net production rose to 29.1 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day, with 89% production efficiency. Unit production cost fell to 29.5 dollars a barrel from 34.0. Cash and money-market funds reached 476 million dollars against 296 million of bonds. Bestla at Brage is now due before the end of 2026, ahead of schedule and cheaper. With 2027 production guided to 39,000-43,000 barrels a day, roughly 35% above 2026, and Draugen's life running to 2040, cash flow should step up just as the dividend restarts: 2.00 kroner in December 2026 and at least 1.00 krone a quarter in 2027. That is at least 6 kroner over about 13 months, roughly 13% of today's price, and it brings back Norwegian income investors who could not own a non-payer. The payout is small against the cash flow: about 11 million dollars a quarter against 182 million of operating cash flow in Q3 2026. Management can therefore raise it at today's oil prices. Valued field by field as streams of after-tax cash, the business is worth about 78 kroner a share if Brent holds near 95-100 dollars and Talisker West follows Bestla in 2027. Board members bought shares near 33.50 kroner in July 2026.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the good news is out and the stock is still a leveraged bet on an oil price that is already falling. Brent has dropped from about 115 dollars on 26 October to about 93 dollars on 16 November 2026 as the Hormuz premium begins to unwind. Aker BP and Var Energi have fallen 15-17% in that time, yet OKEA has barely moved, because the 3 November dividend news propped it up. If the sector keeps de-rating, OKEA has only postponed its share of the fall. Norway takes 78% of offshore profit at the margin, so 107 million dollars of pre-tax profit in Q3 2026 became 29 million of net profit. At a 65-70 dollar oil price, after-tax cash per barrel shrinks to roughly 5 dollars, against 2027 spending raised to as much as 320 million dollars. The at-least-1.00-krone quarterly dividend would then compete with spending and the large decommissioning bill (about 1.0 billion dollars gross, about 528 million net after tax relief) for a thin equity base. Quality issues remain: a fourth write-down on the acquired Statfjord stake (33 million dollars in Q3 after 94 million in Q2), 23 million dollars of exploration costs written off, a solvency score near 2.3, and a 2026 production guidance cut earlier in the year. Part of the jump in net cash came from the one-off Mistral licence sale and the timing of tax payments, not from repeatable cash flow. No structural floor sits under the price. What would confirm the bear case: Brent below 75 dollars, a Bestla start-up slipping into 2027 after all, another Statfjord write-down at the fourth-quarter report, or the 2027 dividend held at the 1.00-krone minimum while spending rises.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the screener still makes OKEA look 95% undervalued, but that is a reporting-currency artefact. Corrected, the stock at 46.55 kroner trades about 12% below our base value of 52. That is a modest discount for a depleting, oil-levered annuity. The market has rewarded the 3 November dividend restart by holding OKEA steady while Brent fell about 20% and Aker BP and Var Energi fell 15-17%. In effect, investors are treating the new payout of at least 6 kroner over 13 months as protection. It is not a floor. The 2027 minimum of 1.00 krone a quarter is easily covered at 90-plus dollar oil, but at 65-70 dollars it would compete with raised spending of up to 320 million dollars and a large decommissioning bill. Where the market may be too cautious: Bestla's earlier start and Draugen's lengthening life add barrels that a 5.4-dollar-a-barrel enterprise value does not fully credit. The net of the two views is a fair-ish price, not a mispricing.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window, the months just ahead, runs through the first quarter of 2027. The main risk is a further unwinding of the Hormuz oil premium: Brent has already fallen from about 115 to about 93 dollars since 26 October, and peers have de-rated. If OKEA's dividend support fades once the December payment goes ex-dividend, the shares could catch down to the sector. Company-specific risks are a Bestla start-up slipping past year-end 2026, another Statfjord write-down at the fourth-quarter report (early 2027), and hedging losses (20 million dollars in Q3). Liquidity is not a risk: 476 million dollars of cash and money-market funds against 296 million of bonds. The shares also drop by the 2.00-krone dividend on the ex-dividend date in December, which is mechanical, not a loss of value.
picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure exists. The shares are near the top of their 52-week range (19.58 to 50.70 kroner), above both the 50-day (43.31) and 200-day (37.15) averages. The dividend restart is more likely to attract income buyers than to force anyone out. The seller that could deliver our price is a sector-wide sell-off in Norwegian oil producers as the Hormuz premium unwinds, which has already taken peers down 9-17% in three weeks. A smaller technical effect is holders who bought only for the December dividend selling after the ex-dividend date.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near 40 kroner, which a sector-wide sell-off in Norwegian oil producers could deliver as the Hormuz oil premium keeps unwinding. The 3 November 2026 third-quarter report was good news on every count this committee was watching. The dividend resumes at 2.00 kroner in December and at least 1.00 krone a quarter through 2027. Bestla now starts before the end of 2026, ahead of schedule and cheaper. Net cash grew to 180 million dollars on the company's definition, or 98 million including leases. The thesis holds and has strengthened. Those facts lift our sum-of-the-parts fair value (each field cluster valued as a stream of after-tax cash, on a long-run oil price near 80 dollars) from 50 to 52 kroner. A fourth write-down on the Statfjord stake and higher 2027 spending trim the gain. But the price has not given us a margin. At 46.55 kroner the shares are only about 12% below fair value, well short of the 20% discount we require in today's reflation backdrop, while the adverse case of 28 kroner is about 40% lower with no structural floor. The dividend is not a floor. The shares have held steady while Brent fell from about 115 to 93 dollars and Aker BP and Var Energi dropped 15-17%, so the dividend news is already in the price relative to the group. The catalyst has already happened, so the edge is spent. In this book that is neither a plus nor a minus; we judge the remaining value, which is a fair-ish price for a well-run but moat-less, short-life annuity on oil. Because the fair value rose on dated facts, we raise our buy price from 37 to 40 kroner, about 30% below fair value. That is a wider cushion than the bare 20% bar, because the downside is deep and resolves entirely on Brent, the single shared factor the regime read warns against stacking. Conviction stays middling at 3, both overall and on value alone.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst that forces a re-rating, the dividend restart, already happened when it was announced on 3 November 2026, so the edge is spent. What remains: the first payment of 2.00 kroner in December 2026; Bestla first oil, guided before year-end 2026; the fourth-quarter 2026 report in early 2027, with the first 2027 dividend and the hedging and spending update; and any Talisker West investment decision. None of these is a binding, dated payout beyond the December dividend. From here the value case rests on cash generation at the prevailing oil price, not on an event.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# OKEA ASA (OKEA.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 16 November 2026. Price used: 46.55 Norwegian kroner (Oslo listing, live quote 16 November 2026). Company reports in US dollars; dollar-to-krone rate used: 9.64.*

**Sources.** The paid market-data feed has no earnings-call transcript and no news for this listing. This dossier rests on the third-quarter 2026 results release (published 3 November 2026), the quarterly statements in the paid feed (Q4 2025 to Q3 2026), and this committee's own dated record from 12 and 26 October 2026, which drew on the second-quarter release (16 July 2026) and the Pareto Securities energy conference (16 September 2026). No call transcript was read, so management tone is judged from release language, not from analyst questions. No quotation below comes from anywhere other than the 3 November release.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Over the past year the story has moved from "invest and protect the balance sheet" to "harvest and pay out".
- Through mid-2026 the message was a high-investment year: the dividend was suspended (since early 2024), the company sat just below the distribution thresholds in its bond terms, and 2026 production guidance had been cut.
- The 16 September 2026 conference turned the page: about 35% production growth from sanctioned projects, with Bestla (a tie-back, meaning a small field piped into an existing platform, at Brage) due in "early 2027".
- The 3 November 2026 third-quarter report closed the loop. Net cash (cash minus interest-bearing debt) jumped to 180 million dollars from 59 million, Bestla moved forward to "before year-end" 2026 "at a lower expected cost", and quarterly dividends resume: 2.00 kroner a share in December 2026, then "at least NOK 1.00 per share" every quarter through 2027.
- What has quietly faded is Statfjord, the late-life stake bought from Equinor. It has gone from growth asset to a source of recurring write-downs.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Strong operations in Q3 2026 | Net production 29.1 thousand barrels of oil equivalent a day (up from 27.0); production efficiency 89% (from 83%); unit production cost 29.5 dollars a barrel (from 34.0) | Matches. The rise came from fewer maintenance shutdowns, not new wells |
| Balance sheet now supports payouts | Cash and money-market funds 476 million dollars against 296 million of bonds. Including leases and other debt, our inputs show net cash of 98 million dollars at 30 September 2026 | Matches. Part of the jump came from the Mistral licence sale (a 28 million dollar gain) and part from timing of tax payments, so it is not all repeatable cash flow |
| Earnings recovery | Net profit 29 million dollars in Q3, against 14 million in Q2 and 36 million in Q1. Diluted earnings per share over the last twelve months were 0.60 dollars | Real but thin. Norway's 78% marginal tax on offshore profit takes most of the pre-tax gain: 107 million dollars before tax became 29 million after it |
| Bestla ahead of schedule | Now "before year-end" 2026, against "early 2027" since July 2025 | Positive, but a management target. The comparable Garn West-South well slipped from April to mid-August 2026 |
| Capital discipline | 2026 spending narrowed to 320-340 million dollars, but 2027 raised to 260-320 million (from 230-290) for an accelerated Draugen well | Mixed. The earlier promise of a roughly 20% drop in 2027 spending is now smaller |
| Statfjord | Write-downs of 33 million dollars in Q3 and 94 million in Q2 (7 million and 27 million after tax), from "lower volume estimates and higher capex" | Diverges. This acquired stake keeps disappointing |
| Screener cheapness | 93% revenue fall, a 4,091 discounted-cash-flow fair value, 95% margins of safety | Data artefacts: a switch in reporting currency and missing quarters. Ignore |

Overall the numbers now back the operating story. The exception is Statfjord, where the story has been richer than the results.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Rising. The July 2026 language was cautious ("high investment period", dividend on hold). By 3 November the chief executive, Svein J. Liknes, was "very pleased with the strong operational execution" and committed to a dated payout. Guidance became more specific, with a first dividend date and a quarterly minimum for 2027. The shift is from defensive to offensive. It is backed by cash, though it was made while realised liquids prices averaged 94.6 dollars a barrel in Q3.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium, and improving.
- Missed: 2026 production guidance was cut once, during 2026, and Statfjord volumes have been revised down repeatedly.
- Delivered: 2026 production guidance was narrowed toward the top (31-32, from 29-32), Bestla is early and cheaper, and the dividend arrived when the balance sheet allowed it.
- The screener records earnings beats in only 2 of 7 quarters, but per-share earnings here are dominated by write-downs and tax timing, so this is a weak signal of credibility.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
No transcript was available, so these are the obvious questions the record raises, not quotes:
- Statfjord: how many more write-downs? Three in the last four quarters.
- Payout sustainability: at least 1.00 krone a quarter is about 104 million kroner, roughly 11 million dollars a quarter. That looks easy at 90-plus dollar oil. The test is a 65-70 dollar oil price with 2027 spending of up to 320 million dollars.
- Decommissioning: the gross obligation is about 1.0 billion dollars (roughly 528 million net after tax relief), against thin book equity.
- Hedging cost 20 million dollars in Q3. What is the hedge book for 2027?
- Analyst targets: no target dated after the 3 November report could be found. The latest dated consensus found (Saxo, 3 June 2026) was 45.56 kroner, with 8 buy ratings and 1 hold. That predates the dividend news and is not used here.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red flags:
- Recurring Statfjord write-downs: 94 million dollars in Q2 2026 and 33 million in Q3 2026.
- 23 million dollars of exploration costs written off in Q3 2026 (Alpehumle and Prince).
- Spending guidance for 2027 rose by 30 million dollars (3 November 2026).
- The solvency score (Altman-Z) is about 2.3, in the grey zone, and book equity is thin against a large abandonment liability.
- Brent has fallen from about 115 to about 93 dollars since 26 October 2026, as the Hormuz premium begins to unwind.

Green flags:
- Net cash of 180 million dollars on the company's definition (Q3 2026).
- Dividend resumes in December 2026, with a 2027 minimum.
- Bestla is ahead of schedule and cheaper.
- Unit production cost fell to 29.5 dollars a barrel.
- Production efficiency was 89%.
- Board members bought shares near 33.50 kroner in late July 2026.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The 2027 minimum payout is framed as "at least" 1.00 krone, a floor management can only raise. That signals confidence in 2027 cash flow at the forward oil prices it can see.
- The Statfjord write-down now cites "higher forward prices" as a partial offset. Without them, the hit would have been larger.
- Accelerating the Springmus East well at Draugen shows management directing spare cash first to its lowest-cost, longest-life asset (Draugen runs to 2040), before raising the payout further. That is sensible capital allocation.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: strengthening. The single most important point for sizing is this: OKEA is a leveraged after-tax claim on the Brent oil price. About 22 cents of each extra dollar of revenue reaches shareholders. The good company news of 3 November (dividend, Bestla, net cash) landed in the same weeks that Brent fell about 20%. The shares held near 46-47 kroner while Norwegian peers fell 9-17%, so the company news has already been paid for in relative terms.

Moat: none. This is a price-taking commodity producer. Its edge is a cost and know-how specialisation in extending the life of mature fields (Brage to 2035, Draugen to 2040), which is a skill, not a moat. Returns on capital are low and volatile (return on invested capital 4.2%, return on equity -24.5% on the fiscal-year figures, distorted by write-downs). The trend is stable, not eroding: unit costs are falling and field lives are lengthening.

Secular threat: manageable. The energy transition limits terminal value, but these are 7-to-14-year depleting assets valued on cash before then, so the cheapness reflects fair pricing of a short-life annuity on a volatile commodity, not a fear-driven mispricing and not a value trap.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory improving · no real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: The market is paying close to nothing for two late-stage obesity drugs. At DKK 239.80 (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16) Zealand is valued at about DKK 15.9 billion, while at 2026-09-30 it held DKK 13.51 billion of cash and securities and DKK 4.19 billion of receivables (mostly Roche) against DKK 0.48 billion of debt - about DKK 15.3 billion, or DKK 231 a share, after current liabilities and the last tranche of the buyback. For an enterprise value (market value minus net cash) near zero, you own a 50/50 US and European profit share in petrelintide, an amylin analog (a copy of a gut hormone that makes people feel full) that Roche chose to take into a global three-trial Phase 3 program in September 2026 after seeing both Phase 2 trials, plus the same profit share on its combination with Roche's enicepatide (Phase 2 starting Q4 2026). Petrelintide's edge is tolerability: stomach-related dropouts of 1.5% versus 0% on placebo in ZUPREME-1 and 1.9% versus 1.7% in ZUPREME-2 - a profile management calls 'easy to start, and easy to stay on' (Q3 2026 call), in a market where, per the 2026-02-19 call, only a small fraction of patients exposed to GLP-1 drugs stay on them. Second, Zealand earns royalties and up to EUR 315 million of open milestones on Boehringer's survodutide, whose Phase 3 program is now complete: 16.6% weight loss in SYNCHRONIZE-1 (June 2026), up to 13.1% in diabetics (2026-10-01) and confirmed cardiovascular safety (2026-11-09), with filings in 2027 and liver-disease (MASH) data in 2027 that could widen its use. Third, management is disciplined with the cash: it bought back DKK 1.3 billion of stock at about DKK 295 (completed 2026-10-05) and guided 2026 costs to the low end of its range (2026-11-12). Conditions: Roche stays committed, Phase 3 pushes petrelintide toward the low-to-mid teens with placebo-like tolerability, survodutide is approved in 2027-28, and spending stays near DKK 2.5-3 billion a year.
picks.bear_thesis: The cash is spoken for, and the drugs are second-tier. The screener's 2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow, 70% net margin and DKK 522.8 discounted-cash-flow value capitalise one-off Roche payments: recurring revenue was DKK 4 million in Q3 2026, trailing free cash flow is minus DKK 1.53 billion and return on invested capital is about minus 25%. Petrelintide missed management's own 15-20% target twice - about 10.7% at 42 weeks in ZUPREME-1 and up to 9.2% at 28 weeks in diabetics - and the Q3 2026 call quietly replaced the target with 'double-digit weight loss'. Lilly's eloralintide is about a year ahead with stronger numbers and Novo is advancing amylin drugs of its own, so tolerability may be a feature of the class, not of Zealand's molecule. Survodutide passed its heart-safety test, but about one in five patients stopped treatment for stomach side effects (2026-11-09), so it enters a crowded GLP-1 market as a liver-focused niche product. Meanwhile management is widening the spending agenda - a Cambridge research hub, an AI-protein collaboration, small molecules, '10 clinical programs by 2030' - and has never quantified its share of Phase 3 costs. If spending runs at DKK 2.5-3 billion a year for four years and both drugs prove commercially marginal, the stock converges on spent-down cash of about DKK 135 a share. What would confirm it: Roche scaling back Phase 3, competitor amylin data that clearly beat petrelintide, a survodutide approval delay, or 2027 cost guidance above DKK 3.3 billion.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: after a slide from a 52-week high of DKK 556 to DKK 239.80, the market prices Zealand as if its pipeline were worth roughly nothing and its cash will simply be burned. We agree the petrelintide data were below management's own target and that Lilly leads the amylin class. But the street is underweighting three dated facts: Roche committed to a full global Phase 3 after seeing all the data; survodutide has cleared every Phase 3 hurdle including heart safety (2026-11-09) and heads to filing in 2027; and management returned DKK 1.3 billion through a buyback while guiding costs to the low end. The screener's own signals (2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow, DKK 522.8 discounted-cash-flow value) are wrong in the other direction - they capitalise one-off milestones - and we disregard them.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): there is no debt wall and no liquidity risk, so this is a valuation-drawdown risk, not a solvency one. The main hazards are competitor amylin data from Lilly (eloralintide) and Novo at medical meetings, which can re-rate the whole class; 2027 cost guidance (due with the full-year report around February 2027) if it rises above about DKK 3.3 billion as Phase 3 and the research expansion ramp; and any sign that Roche is slowing the petrelintide program. Survodutide's tolerability (about 19-21% dropping out for stomach effects in the outcomes trial) could trim regulators' or prescribers' enthusiasm, but its value is a small part of ours.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has largely played out: the stock is down about 57% from its 52-week high, sits about 20% below its 200-day average of DKK 298.6 and only about 9% above its 52-week low of DKK 220.6. Momentum and growth funds that held it as an obesity proxy have been leaving since the first Phase 2 readout in early 2026. There is no dividend base to liquidate and no index event identified; further selling would be fundamental (data or spending), not mechanical. The company's own buyback at about DKK 295 shows management saw value well above today's price.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds and the news since our last look on 10 November 2026 nudged it slightly in our favour: Boehringer's survodutide passed its heart-safety trial on 9 November and will be filed in 2027, and the 12 November quarterly report showed DKK 13.5 billion of cash and securities plus DKK 4.2 billion of receivables, with 2026 costs guided to the low end of the range - the spending scare we flagged did not happen. At DKK 239.80 you pay about DKK 15.9 billion for a company with roughly DKK 15.3 billion of net cash and receivables, and you get a half share of Roche's petrelintide program and a royalty on survodutide for very little. Correcting the share count for the October buyback (about 66.3 million shares) and lifting survodutide's odds roughly offset, so our base-case fair value is DKK 300 a share, about 25% above the price and clear of our 20% bar for buying in today's reflationary market. This is not a classic value floor: the cash is committed to an expensive Phase 3 and a widening research agenda, petrelintide's weight loss missed management's own target, and Lilly leads the class. So conviction stays moderate (3 of 5), the value case scores 3 of 5, and the debt-cycle backdrop, which punishes long-dated stories, is a headwind. Watch 2027 cost guidance and competitor amylin data.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating: no single hard date. Nearest items are the start of the petrelintide plus enicepatide Phase 2 (Q4 2026), the full-year report and 2027 guidance (around February 2027), Boehringer's survodutide filings and MASH data (2027), and petrelintide Phase 3 data (about 2028). A new buyback funded from surplus cash, a milestone payment, or a licensing deal for the rare-disease assets would also narrow the gap between price and net cash.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Zealand Pharma (ZEAL.CO) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Quote used: DKK 239.80 on the Copenhagen listing (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16). Transcripts read: Q1 2025 (2025-05-09), H1 2025 (2025-08-14), Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), full year 2025 (2026-02-19) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-12). The Q1 and H1 2026 calls were not in the bundle, so the 2026 readouts between February and November are reconstructed from the Q3 2026 call and the dated company announcements.*

**Bottom line.** Zealand is a clinical-stage peptide company whose stock is now worth less than the cash and partner receivables on its balance sheet net of near-term liabilities, plus a modest value for two late-stage obesity programs run with Roche and Boehringer Ingelheim. Management has hit nearly every timeline it set, but the clinical numbers have landed below the 15-20% weight-loss bar it set for its lead drug. The reported profits and the screener's 2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow are one-off milestone artifacts and should be ignored.

## 1. Narrative arc

- **Q1 2025 (2025-05-09):** the story was the newly signed Roche deal - "historic and transformative" - a 50/50 profit share on petrelintide (an amylin analog, a copy of a gut hormone that makes people feel full) in the US and Europe. The pitch: a better-tolerated alternative to GLP-1 drugs, targeting 15-20% weight loss.
- **H1 2025 (2025-08-14):** two leading programs (petrelintide and survodutide, Boehringer's glucagon/GLP-1 drug on which Zealand earns royalties). Amylin pitched as "the next major class". Rare-disease assets and dapiglutide still part of the story.
- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-13):** dapiglutide paused ("the GLP-1-based therapeutic space has become increasingly crowded"). The company narrowed to its two partnered obesity assets and talked of becoming "a generational biotech".
- **Full year 2025 (2026-02-19):** "the most defining and catalyst-rich year" in the company's history; a Boston research hub, AI-driven discovery, "more than 10 candidates into the clinic" in five years, and "5 product launches over the next 5 years".
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-12):** the language moved from weight-loss magnitude to "first-choice" and "easy to start, and easy to stay on". The research story widened again: a Cambridge (US) hub, a Generate Biomedicines AI-protein deal, small molecules via OTR, and a "multimodality metabolic health company". The rare-disease assets (dasiglucagon, glepaglutide) are now to be licensed out.

The arc is a pivot from a single-asset partnership story to a platform story, with the efficacy target quietly reframed from "15% to 20%" to "double-digit weight loss" with placebo-like tolerability.

## 2. Claims vs financials (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Secured enough capital to fund our journey towards profitability" (Q1 2025) | Cash and securities DKK 13.51bn and DKK 4.19bn of receivables against DKK 0.48bn of debt at 2026-09-30 (FMP statements). Down from DKK 15.11bn at end-2025, partly due to a roughly DKK 1.3bn share buyback completed 2026-10-05. | Holds. No financing risk for years. |
| Earnings strength (screener: net margin 70%, P/FCF 2.7x, EPS 90.22 in 2025) | 2025 revenue DKK 9.21bn and 2026 Q2 revenue DKK 4.49bn are Roche upfront and milestone payments. Recurring revenue was DKK 34m in Q1 2026 and DKK 4m in Q3 2026; TTM free cash flow is minus DKK 1.53bn; return on invested capital about minus 25%. | Does not hold. The cheapness on earnings is an artifact. |
| Cost discipline | 2026 operating-expense guidance DKK 2.7-3.3bn; on 2026-11-12 the CFO said guidance was narrowed "to the lower end". Q3 2026 net operating loss only DKK 54m after cost sharing. | Holds; burn is running below the feared DKK 3bn+. |
| Petrelintide 15-20% weight loss (Q3 2025, FY 2025) | ZUPREME-1: "up to 10.7% mean weight loss at week 42", GI discontinuation 1.5% vs 0% placebo. ZUPREME-2 (diabetics): up to 9.2% at week 28, A1c down up to 0.65 points (Q3 2026 call). | Missed the stated efficacy target; the tolerability claim held. |
| Survodutide competitive weight loss, comparable tolerability (Q3 2025) | SYNCHRONIZE-1 16.6% (June 2026), SYNCHRONIZE-2 up to 13.1% in diabetics (2026-10-01), SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT met cardiovascular safety (2026-11-09, AHA). Press reports put GI discontinuations around 19-21% in the outcomes trial. Boehringer confirmed global filings in 2027. | Efficacy and safety hold; tolerability is worse than management implied. |
| Five launches in five years | Glepaglutide received a positive opinion from the EU medicines committee (CHMP) in Q3 2026; survodutide filing 2027; petrelintide Phase 3 started 2026-09. | On track in part; rare-disease launches will be via out-licensing. |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory - Stable to slightly declining

- Q1 2025: "never been in a stronger position" - maximum confidence.
- H1 2025 and Q3 2025: still bold on targets ("We remain fully confident in the potential of petrelintide to deliver 15% to 20% weight loss in Phase III").
- FY 2025: "catalyst-rich year"; success defined as data reinforcing "approximately 15% to 20%".
- Q3 2026: no restatement of the 15-20% figure; replaced by "double-digit weight loss" and "a tolerability profile that is generally comparable to placebo". The CFO declined to say where cost savings came from.

Confidence on execution stays high; confidence on the efficacy number has been walked back. That is a defensive shift dressed in offensive language.

## 4. Guidance credibility - Medium

Delivered: ZUPREME-1 data in the first half of 2026 (guided Q1); Phase 3 start in the second half of 2026 (started 2026-09); ZUPREME-2 in the second half of 2026; combination Phase 2 (ZYNERGY, with Roche's enicepatide, formerly CT-388) now guided to Q4 2026 versus "first half of 2026" on 2026-02-19 - a slip of about two quarters. Operating expenses inside guidance. Missed: the efficacy target. Dasiglucagon manufacturing has been delayed repeatedly by a third-party facility. Timelines are reliable; outcome claims are not. The screener's 5-of-7 earnings beat rate is meaningless for a company whose revenue is milestone timing.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- Tolerability versus efficacy trade-off in amylins (Wells Fargo, Q3 2025; Danske, H1 2025 on the flat dose response in men). Management answered with the 480-patient Phase 2 - which then showed about 10.7%.
- Survodutide GI tolerability (UBS, Q3 2025): management promised "comparable" tolerability; the outcomes trial showed about one in five stopping for GI effects.
- Cost sharing with Roche and caps on spend (Goldman, Q1 2025): never quantified; "we are not yet providing clear guidance".
- Where cost savings came from (BNP Paribas, Q3 2026): not answered.
- Competitive position versus Lilly's eloralintide and Novo's amycretin and cagrilintide: always deflected with "best-in-class potential", never with head-to-head data.

## 6. Red flags / green flags

Red flags
- The 15-20% weight-loss target set in 2025 and reaffirmed on 2026-02-19 was not met in either Phase 2 trial; the Q3 2026 call no longer quotes it.
- Survodutide GI discontinuations of about 19-21% in the outcomes trial (reported 2026-11-09) contradict "comparable tolerability" (Q3 2025).
- Scope creep during the proof years: Boston/Cambridge hub, AI-protein collaboration, small molecules, "10 clinical programs by 2030" - spending that competes with returning cash.
- The combination Phase 2 slipped from the first half of 2026 to Q4 2026.
- Stock-page earnings, margins and DCF value are built on one-off milestone payments.

Green flags
- Roche - which saw all the Phase 2 data - started a roughly three-trial global Phase 3 program in 2026-09 and is co-funding it; a sophisticated partner voting with money.
- Survodutide's Phase 3 program is complete, cardiovascular safety is confirmed (2026-11-09) and Boehringer has committed to filing in 2027, which de-risks royalties and the remaining milestones.
- Placebo-like GI discontinuation for petrelintide in both Phase 2 trials (1.5% vs 0% and 1.9% vs 1.7%).
- Capital discipline: a DKK 1.3bn buyback at about DKK 295 (completed 2026-10-05) and 2026 costs guided to the low end.
- Positive EU committee opinion for glepaglutide in short bowel syndrome.

## 7. Hidden signals

- "End the weight loss Olympics" (Q3 2025) became the frame that pre-justified a sub-target result: the bar was moved before the data arrived.
- CT-388 is now called enicepatide - Roche is branding its own asset, a small sign the combination is a Roche priority.
- New voices: the Chief Scientific Officer (Utpal Singh, ex-Lilly) now speaks on every call and the platform narrative is his; investor relations changed hands (Eric Rojas replaced Adam Lange in 2026). The scientific voice talks of "polypharmacology" and China access - a broader, more expensive ambition.
- Management now says the rare-disease assets will be licensed, not commercialized - a quiet retreat from building a commercial organization.
- "Without relying on dilutive funding" was added to the Q3 2026 framing - reassurance that suggests investors have asked.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict

Trajectory: **PIVOTING** - from a partnership-milestone company to a platform research company, funded by a cash pile that today exceeds the market value of the equity net of liabilities. The single most important thing the director must weigh: the stock is a claim on about DKK 230 a share of net cash and receivables that management intends to spend, not return. The value case works only if (a) petrelintide earns a real share of the amylin market despite trailing Lilly on efficacy, or (b) management keeps returning surplus cash as it did in 2026. The buyback is the best evidence for (b).

**Moat.** Type: intangible (patented peptide molecules and 25 years of peptide know-how), validated by two big-pharma partners. Width: narrow - there are no product earnings, returns on capital are negative, and the tolerability edge looks like a property of the amylin class that Lilly and Novo share. Trend: stable - the patent estate and partner terms are unchanged; the competitive position neither widened nor collapsed in 2026.

**Secular threat.** None of the listed structural forces (AI displacement, disintermediation, reimbursement compression and so on) threatens the terminal value directly. The real risk is competitive and clinical - Lilly's and Novo's amylin programs and price competition in obesity - which is manageable, not terminal. The cheapness is a fear print around below-target data, not a structurally shrinking base, but the cash cushion is being consumed by design.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Solstad Offshore is a cash-generating holding company priced like a small shipowner. Its 27.3% stake in listed Solstad Maritime alone was worth about USD 380 million on 2026-09-30 (roughly NOK 43 a share), and it pays Solstad Offshore about USD 15 million a quarter in dividends - enough to fund most of the shareholder payout by itself. On top come four Brazilian anchor handlers on long Petrobras contracts, the hard-to-replace construction vessel Normand Maximus (bought for USD 125 million against a replacement cost management says is several times higher, and now firm with Saipem into 2029), 35.8% of a growing ROV (remotely operated vehicle) owner, Omega Subsea (about USD 100 million revenue and USD 32 million EBITDA over the last 12 months), and a 14-year SBM newbuild contract from 2029. Guidance has been met every period, debt is falling, book equity compounded from USD 375 million to USD 528 million in a year, and 85% of 2027 owned-fleet days are already firm. In the favorable case the vessels are valued nearer their asset value and the Solstad Maritime stake re-rates, giving about NOK 97 a share.
picks.bear_thesis: The owned fleet is not growing: operating EBITDA fell to USD 17 million in Q3-26 from USD 19 million, and the headline profit is flattered by a USD 24 million sale gain, an arbitration win and associates' earnings Solstad Offshore does not control. Roughly 60% of the equity value is one listed stake whose price moves with the offshore-vessel sector, and that sector is de-rating (Tidewater near USD 71 against a 50-day average of about USD 85 on 2026-11-09). 2027 brings a maintenance hump - about half the fleet in class renewal, Maximus out about 60 days, Normand Superior still without work - just as newbuild construction vessels arrive, while about USD 125 million of new bank debt buys Maximus. A weaker oil price or Petrobras cost-cutting would hit day rates and the Solstad Maritime stake at the same time. In that case the parts are worth about NOK 47.5 a share.
picks.consensus_delta: We disagree with the market less than the screen suggests. The screen's DCF of NOK 770 and 3.6x price-to-free-cash-flow treat sale gains, an arbitration recovery and associates' dividends as recurring cash, which they are not; on a sum-of-the-parts basis (valuing each piece separately) the stock is about 6% below our NOK 72 fair value, not 90%. Where the market may be wrong is in how it treats the holding-company structure: the 27.3% Solstad Maritime stake (about NOK 43 a share at its 2026-09-30 market value) plus a long-contracted Brazilian fleet and an in-the-money Maximus purchase are worth a little more than today's price, and the base dividend (USD 0.18 per quarter, about NOK 1.7) is covered by Solstad Maritime's own payouts. There are no published analyst price targets on FMP for this listing, and none could be checked by web search this session, so we do not cite a consensus.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the first half of 2027: about half the owned fleet in class renewal, Normand Maximus out roughly 60 days, Normand Superior idle after its survey unless new work is found, and capex not yet guided (due with 2027 guidance). At the same time newbuild construction vessels arrive over the next 18 months, Maximus is financed with about USD 125 million of bank debt (option delivery October 2027), and the USD 70 million term loan matures in November 2027. None of this threatens solvency - equity ratio 47%, Altman-Z 6.7 - but it can pull the dividend back to the base level and weigh on sentiment. The bigger swing factor is the Solstad Maritime share price, which carries most of the value and moves with the sector.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited. The 2026-11-06 ex-dividend date has passed, so yield holders who bought for the USD 0.30 payment may drift out as the run-rate dividend steps down to the base USD 0.18 - a small, mechanical source of supply. The more likely route to our level is a sector-wide sell-off in offshore-vessel and oil-service shares, already visible in Tidewater and DOF trading below their 50-day averages on 2026-11-09; that would also push down the Solstad Maritime stake and widen the holding-company discount.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near NOK 59.5, which a sector-wide sell-off in offshore-vessel and oil-service shares could deliver. The thesis holds: management has done what it said - guidance met every period, debt down, book equity up about 40% in a year, the Normand Maximus contract made firm with Saipem into 2029 and its purchase option declared, and a dividend covered by what Solstad Maritime pays in. But the business is a holding company with a flat-earning owned fleet, and about 60% of its value is one listed stake that moves with the sector. Our sum-of-the-parts gives a fair value of NOK 72 a share, only about 6% above today's NOK 67.70, after the USD 0.30 dividend left the company on 2026-11-06. In the current macro backdrop we require a 20% discount to fair value before buying, which points to about NOK 59.5; the seller we expect is a broad offshore-sector de-rating, which has already started at Tidewater and DOF. Our downside case is about NOK 47.5 and our upside case about NOK 97. Conviction stays at 2, unchanged from 2026-10-19: no new fact moved the business case, and the dividend and the Q3 numbers only reset the price levels.
picks.forcing_function: What forces a re-rating: the 2027 guidance (expected with the Q4-2026 report in February 2027) that sets the class-renewal capex and the dividend run-rate; a firm contract for Normand Superior; the Maximus financing agreement before the October 2027 delivery; and any move by Solstad Maritime (its dividend, share price or a corporate step), since it carries most of the value. None is a hard-dated payout, and in this lane that is neither a plus nor a minus.

# Solstad Offshore ASA (SOFF.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup
As of 2026-11-09. Price used: NOK 67.70 on the Oslo listing (FMP quote, 2026-11-09). Company reports in US dollars; USD/NOK 9.38 (FMP, 2026-11-09). About 82.4 million shares (FMP market cap NOK 5.57 billion / price; consistent with the USD 25 million dividend at USD 0.30 per share).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Two years after its 2024 restructuring, which moved most of the fleet into Solstad Maritime (SoMa), Solstad Offshore is a small owner-operator plus a holding company. It owns a handful of vessels (the large construction support vessel, or CSV, Normand Maximus, the CSV Normand Superior and four Brazilian-built anchor handlers), holds 27.3% of listed Solstad Maritime, 35.8% of the ROV (remotely operated vehicle) owner Omega Subsea, and two 50/50 joint ventures with SBM Offshore. It also acts as the Brazilian contract holder for SoMa vessels, passing the operating risk back to SoMa (back-to-back leases). The story has moved from "survive" (2025) to "lock in and pay out" (2026): long Petrobras contracts for the anchor handlers, a firm Saipem contract for Normand Maximus, the Maximus purchase option declared, Normand Tonjer sold, and the dividend raised every quarter (USD 0.05 in Q3-25 to USD 0.30 in Q3-26, of which 0.12 is a one-off from the Tonjer sale).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- "Solid quarter": Q3-26 (reported 2026-11-04) total adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) of USD 41 million against 29 million a year earlier - but operational adjusted EBITDA fell to USD 17 million from 19 million. All of the growth came from the share of results of SoMa, Omega and the joint ventures (USD 24 million against 10 million). Claim holds, but the owned fleet is flat; the growth is in the holdings.
- Net profit of USD 63 million in Q3-26 includes a USD 24 million accounting gain on the Tonjer sale. The scan's 48% net margin and 3.6x price-to-free-cash-flow are inflated by such gains, an arbitration recovery (USD 5 million in Q2-26) and dividends received from SoMa; they are not a repeatable operating margin.
- Book equity rose to USD 528 million (2026-09-30) from 478 million (2026-06-30) and 375 million a year earlier - corroborated.
- Debt: term loan USD 70 million (matures Nov-2027), BNDES (Brazil development bank) USD 40 million, Normand Maximus lease USD 144 million (USD 30 million remaining hire plus USD 114 million present value of the USD 125 million purchase option). Cash USD 151 million before the USD 25 million Q3 dividend. The company's "net cash of USD 39 million" excludes the Maximus option; including it, net debt is roughly USD 128 million after the dividend. The USD 223 million of SoMa-related leases are matched by Brazilian end-client contracts and are excluded from our valuation as pass-through.
- Owned-fleet backlog USD ~400 million at Q3-26, down from 432 million at Q2-26 - normal run-off; 85% of 2027 days firm.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Measured and confident. The CEO called the Maximus purchase option "a no-brainer" with replacement value "several times higher" than USD 125 million. On dividends the tone is more careful than in Q2: capital return is balanced against "about half the fleet going into class renewals in the first half of '27" (class renewal = the five-yearly regulatory dry-dock survey). Management also flagged newbuild CSVs entering the market over the next 1.5 years.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Strong. 2025 landed inside the original USD 120-150 million adjusted EBITDA range; operational guidance of USD 60-70 million for 2026 was kept every quarter (USD 51 million year-to-date after Q3). The Q2-26 promise to convert the Maximus letter of intent into a firm contract was delivered by Q3 (26 months with Saipem, into Q2-2029, plus 11 months of options). The Tonjer cash and arbitration cash were flagged in Q2 and arrived.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Questions on 2026-11-04 focused on (a) newbuild supply and employment for the uncommitted Normand Superior after its 1H27 class renewal (no firm work yet), (b) Normand Carioca's re-contracting in roughly a year, (c) Maximus dry-dock length (about 60 days in Q1-27; capex not guided until the 2027 guidance), (d) dividend sustainability, and (e) Maximus financing (bank debt). No FMP analyst price-target coverage exists for this listing, and a web search for a consensus target could not be run this session, so no target is used.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Green: guidance met, backlog long-dated with a strong client (Petrobras, Saipem), debt falling, equity compounding, dividends covered by SoMa dividends received (USD 15 million in Q3-26), Maximus option deep in the money.
Red: owned-fleet earnings flat; headline profit flattered by gains; 2027 has a capex and off-hire hump (Maximus about 60 days out, Superior idle risk); value depends heavily on a listed stake (SoMa) whose price moves with the offshore-vessel sector; re-leveraging of about USD 125 million to buy Maximus.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- SoMa's market value (USD ~380 million for the stake on 2026-09-30) is now above its USD 263 million book value; roughly 60% of Solstad Offshore's equity value sits in that one stake, so this stock behaves partly like a discounted proxy for Solstad Maritime.
- The extraordinary USD 0.12 dividend was paid rather than retained, despite the 2027 maintenance hump - a sign of confidence, but also a sign the base dividend (USD 0.18) is the run-rate to watch.
- Peer tape: Tidewater trades at USD 71, well below its 50-day average of about USD 85 (FMP, 2026-11-09) - an offshore-vessel sector de-rating is under way.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Disciplined and shareholder-friendly: debt paid down, non-core asset sold at a gain, cash returned, an in-the-money option exercised with debt rather than new shares, and limited equity into the SBM newbuild joint venture. Moat: narrow but real - a regulatory and local-content position in Brazil (Brazilian-built, Brazilian-flagged tonnage and the in-country contract-holder structure) plus one hard-to-replicate CSV. Returns are improving from a low base (ROIC about 6%), not falling, so the moat is stable. Secular threat: the energy transition is a long-dated, manageable risk for offshore oil-service demand; Petrobras and the Atlantic-basin deepwater pipeline give years of visible work. The cheapness is mostly holding-company and cyclical discount, not a shrinking-base trap.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: China Unicom is one of China's three licensed national telecom operators, trading at HK$5.51 (FMP live quote, 2026-11-09) - about 44% below its 52-week high of HK$9.92 and 18% below its 200-day average of HK$6.73. The bull case is that the market is pricing a permanent earnings and payout collapse into what is really a one-off tax reset. The 2026 profit drop (H1 attributable profit RMB9.47bn, down 34.6%, reported 2026-08-18; nine months RMB13.28bn, down 33.6%, reported 2026-10-29) stems mainly from the reclassification of basic telecom services from the 6% to the 9% value-added tax (VAT) band from 1 January 2026 - a level shift, not a recurring decline. Cash generation is untouched: trailing free cash flow is about RMB25bn (to 2026-06-30) and net cash was RMB44.1bn (cash RMB75.4bn against RMB31.3bn of debt including leases), about HK$1.69 per share, or 31% of the share price. Strip out that cash and investors pay roughly 7.4 times this year's depressed run-rate profit (about RMB13.6bn), against China Mobile on about 11.7 times trailing earnings (FMP earnings yield 8.5%, 2026-11-09). Computing power (+12.2% in nine months) and data centres (+10.4%) give a growth leg, and the business kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 71.1% to 70.3%). What must hold: the dividend returns at or near the prior level with the full-year results in March 2027, and the VAT hit stays a one-time step rather than the start of tariff erosion.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is the price of a franchise whose cash owners do not control. In a year when operating cash flow hit a multi-year high, the board cancelled the interim dividend (2026-08-18; prior year RMB0.2841 per share) - so neither the RMB44bn of net cash nor the RMB25bn of free cash flow can be counted at face value. Management's promise that the profit fall would narrow significantly in the second half has not shown up: the third quarter alone was down about 31% (implied from the 2026-10-29 nine-month data). Core service revenue is shrinking (-0.28% to RMB260.89bn in nine months), gross margin is contracting, earnings beat in only 1 of the last 7 quarters, and return on equity is about 5% - this is a low-return, state-directed utility, not a compounder. Retained cash is likely to flow into state-guided computing-power capex at uncertain returns. If the final dividend is also withheld or cut in March 2027, the income-holder base that already dumped the stock on 2026-08-19 (down 12% on about eleven times normal volume) has no reason to come back, and a 7-8x ex-cash multiple can persist for years.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing the stock as if the 2026 earnings and payout collapse were permanent: about 7.4x ex-cash run-rate profit and a share price near the bottom of its range (52-week low HK$5.11). Where we partly disagree: the profit hit is mostly a one-time tax reclassification, and cash generation is intact. Where we agree with the market: owners do not control the cash, the dividend was cancelled despite record operating cash flow, and the promised second-half narrowing has not appeared. No dated analyst price targets could be found (FMP has no coverage for this listing), so we cannot quote a specific street assumption that is wrong.
picks.valley_of_death: There is no debt wall (net cash RMB44bn) and no liquidation risk. The risky window is the next four months to the March 2027 full-year results: a fourth quarter that again fails to narrow the profit decline, or a final dividend that is cut or withheld, would confirm the payout shift as policy. Further state-guided tariff cuts or capex demands for computing power would absorb the cash that underpins the value case.
picks.positioning_washout: The forced-selling pressure already happened: income holders exited on 2026-08-19 when the shares fell 12% on about eleven times normal volume after the dividend was cancelled. The stock has since based near HK$5.1-5.6 (50-day average HK$5.56). A second wave is possible if the final dividend is also withheld in March 2027, as yield-mandated funds and Southbound income buyers would have no reason to return.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. China Unicom is a cash-rich, licensed national telecom operator that the market has marked down hard - HK$5.51 on 2026-11-09, near its 52-week low of HK$5.11 - after a one-time tax change cut 2026 profit by about a third and the board cancelled the interim dividend on 2026-08-18. On our numbers fair value is about HK$6.80 (roughly 9.5-10 times this year's run-rate profit plus RMB44bn of net cash, about HK$1.69 a share), so there is roughly 23% upside against about 16% downside to our adverse case of HK$4.62. That arithmetic looks fine, but the value rests on cash that owners do not control: the dividend was withheld in a year of record operating cash flow, and management's promise that the profit decline would narrow in the second half did not show up in the third quarter (2026-10-29). Until the board shows, at the March 2027 full-year results, that it will pay out again, we treat the discount as fair rather than a gift. Nothing dated has changed since this committee's 2026-11-02 pass - the move from HK$5.21 to HK$5.51 came with no company news - so we keep the same answer and the same low conviction. The dividend decision is the thing to watch; a restored payout would be a dated fact that reopens the case.
picks.forcing_function: The full-year 2026 results and final-dividend decision, normally in March 2027, are the event that forces a re-rating either way. A restored dividend near the prior level would re-open the income buyer base; a withheld one would anchor the stock at a low ex-cash multiple. There is no buyback, activist or asset sale in view.

# China Unicom (Hong Kong) Ltd (0762.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-09. Price used: HK$5.51 (FMP live quote, Hong Kong listing, 2026-11-09). Reported figures are in renminbi (RMB); we convert at about HK$1.17 per RMB, the same rate this committee used last time.*

**Source note.** FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing (transcript-dates lookup returned nothing on 2026-11-09), and this run's shared web-search budget was used up before this name, so no new call commentary could be pulled. This dossier rests on (a) the screener's multi-year financials, (b) FMP's half-year statements, and (c) the dated company disclosures already verified by this committee's reviewer on 2026-11-03: the interim results of 2026-08-18 (HKEX announcement a260818a, carried by Cision/AAP and The Standard) and the nine-month unaudited key data of 2026-10-29 (The Standard). Nothing below quotes a call we did not read.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

From 2021 to 2024 the story was steady, policy-friendly compounding: revenue rose from RMB327.9bn to RMB389.6bn and net profit from RMB14.4bn to RMB20.6bn, with management leaning on "computing power" (cloud, data centres) to offset a mature mobile and broadband base. FY2025 was the first stall - revenue slipped 1.9% to RMB382.1bn and profit was flat at RMB20.3bn.

2026 broke the arc. China reclassified basic telecom services from the 6% to the 9% value-added tax (VAT) band from 1 January 2026, which comes straight out of reported revenue and margin. The 2026-08-18 interim showed attributable profit of RMB9.47bn, down 34.6%, and the board declared no interim dividend (prior year RMB0.2841 per share). Management said the full-year profit contraction was "expected to narrow significantly" as a staff-cost timing effect reversed. The 2026-10-29 nine-month data did not show that narrowing yet: profit RMB13.28bn, down 33.6%, implying a third quarter of roughly RMB3.8bn, down about 31%. The growth engine is still computing power (+12.2% in nine months, data centres +10.4%) while core service revenue edged down 0.28% to RMB260.89bn.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (dated) | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Profit fall will "narrow significantly" in H2 (2026-08-18) | 9M profit -33.6% vs H1 -34.6% (2026-10-29); Q3 alone about -31% | Not yet delivered; the claim now rides entirely on Q4 |
| Computing power is the new growth leg | +12.2% in 9M 2026; data centres +10.4% | Matches, but it is too small to offset a shrinking core |
| Balance sheet is strong | Net cash RMB44.1bn on 2026-06-30 (cash RMB75.4bn vs debt RMB31.3bn incl. leases) | Matches - about RMB1.44 (HK$1.69) per share |
| Cash generation intact | Trailing free cash flow RMB25.0bn (to 2026-06-30); H1 operating cash flow a multi-year high | Matches - cash is far stronger than accounting profit |
| Shareholder returns a priority | Interim dividend cancelled 2026-08-18 | Diverges sharply - the single biggest credibility hit |

Two screener figures are unreliable and we set them aside: the 23.5% ROIC sits beside a 5.2% ROE and is almost certainly a data artefact, and the "TTM EPS 0.66" is still the FY2025 figure - on the 2026 run-rate (about RMB13.3-14bn of profit) earnings per share are nearer RMB0.44-0.46.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining. The 2024-25 language was offensive (computing-power investment, rising payouts). By August 2026 it had turned defensive: a tax explanation for the profit drop, a promise of narrowing, and a dividend withheld without a restoration timetable. We have no transcript to quote the tone directly; the actions speak for it.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-to-Low. The screener shows earnings beats in only 1 of the last 7 quarters (14%). The one explicit 2026 promise (a narrowing profit decline) has not shown up in the third quarter. Delivery on cash flow has been good; delivery on per-share profit and payout has not.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

What investors will push on (inferred from the disclosures, not from a call we read): (1) when and at what level the dividend returns; (2) whether the VAT hit can be priced through, given state-guided tariff discipline; (3) whether the staff-cost reversal is real or a re-labelled run-rate; (4) how much of the data-centre build-out is spending ahead of demand. No FMP analyst price-target coverage exists for this listing, and no dated consensus target could be fetched this run.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: interim dividend cancelled (2026-08-18) for a stock owned by income holders.
- Red: H2 narrowing promised but not visible in Q3 (2026-10-29).
- Red: core service revenue shrinking (-0.28% in 9M 2026) and gross margin contracting.
- Red: shares fell 12% on 2026-08-19 on about eleven times normal volume; price still about 18% below its 200-day average (HK$6.73).
- Green: net cash RMB44.1bn and free cash flow about RMB25bn a year - roughly 15% of the market value per year.
- Green: computing power and data centres growing double digits.
- Green: margins held through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 71.1% to 70.3% on the repo's resilience file), so the business is not an inflation victim; the 2026 hit is a tax change, not a cost spiral.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The shift from "dividend growth" to "no interim dividend" while the cash pile and cash flow both rose is the tell: cash is being retained for something - state-directed computing-power capex or the tax hit - rather than paid out. For a state-controlled operator, payout policy is set with the parent and the regulator, so a restoration is a policy decision, not an earnings outcome.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: deteriorating. The single most important thing to weigh: the cash is real, but owners do not control it - the dividend was withheld in a year when cash flow rose, so the net cash and free cash flow cannot be counted at full value until the payout returns.

Moat: regulatory licence plus scale (one of three national operators). It is narrow rather than wide - returns on equity are only about 5%, profit is down a third this year, and core service revenue is flat-to-down. The trend looks stable at the franchise level (the licence is not at risk) even as reported profit falls on tax. Secular threat: manageable - no structural force is dismantling telecom demand; the pressure is policy (tax, tariffs, directed capex). The cheapness is mostly a fear-print about payout and policy, not a shrinking-base value trap, but it is a low-return franchise whose value depends on what the state lets it distribute.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: PetroNor E&P (not Panoro Energy, as the peer file mislabels it) is a debt-free, low-cost minority partner in the PNGF Sud offshore licences in Congo that returns almost all the cash it lifts. The bull case: (1) Operations are improving - net output rose to 5,045 barrels a day in Q2 2026 from 4,712 in Q1 as infill wells from 2025 came on and production efficiency climbed to 93% from 86%; a further infill campaign of about USD 20M is planned for 2027. (4) Oil is high: Brent closed at USD 108.75 on 15 September and was about USD 100 on 21 September amid Gulf supply disruptions; if the May 2027 cargo sells anywhere near USD 90-100, it alone would bring in roughly USD 90-100M, over half the market value. (5) Optionality the market ignores: 9.6 million barrels of 2C (discovered, not yet sanctioned) resources could stretch field life from about 9 to 14-15 years, and a sale or farm-down of the 52.2% Aje interest in Nigeria (about 70 million barrels of oil equivalent of 2C resources), which management said could conceivably land in Q4 2026, would crystallise value that is carried at near zero in the share price. (6) If Hemla is acquitted or settles modestly after the trial that opens 23 November 2026, the legal discount unwinds. Conditions: oil holds above about USD 80, the May 2027 lifting happens on schedule, and the court case ends in a fine rather than asset confiscation or licence damage. Update 2026-11-09: Brent is still about USD 92 (FMP), comfortably above the USD 75-80 long-run deck in our base case, and the shares at NOK 10.82 now trade about 15% below our base fair value of about NOK 12.7.
picks.bear_thesis: The screener's cheapness is a peak artifact. The 4x price-to-free-cash-flow multiple and the NOK 41 discounted-cash-flow value rest on one April 2026 cargo sold at about USD 116 a barrel during an oil spike; PetroNor sells lumpy one-million-barrel cargoes, which is why 2025 revenue fell 58% and then the latest quarter's earnings jumped over 600% - timing, not trend. Four problems follow. (1) The cash is spoken for: the USD 85M of cash at 30 June sits against an overlift liability of about USD 41.5M (roughly 355,000 barrels owed to partners), and there is no further sale until about May 2027, so the remaining cash must fund around eleven months of costs, capex (about USD 10M in 2026, USD 20M in 2027) and overhead. There will be no distribution until after the May 2027 AGM. (2) The asset is depleting: net reserves are just under 16 million barrels, about nine years of output, and the year-end exit rate is guided at about 4,300 barrels a day net, below Q2's 5,045. Outside minority owners in the operating vehicle take a share (USD 10.3M of dividends in Q2). (3) Legal risk is real and dated: Norway's economic-crime prosecutor indicted the Congo-holding subsidiary Hemla in January 2026 for alleged grand corruption of senior Congolese officials; the trial opens 23 November 2026, a first ruling is expected around March 2027 and appeals could run to late 2028. Penalties could include fines and confiscation, and management has itself linked cash extraction from Congo to its duty to cooperate with the authorities - so payouts could be delayed. (4) Aje has become a forced seller's asset because the case blocked financing, weakening the negotiating position. As a non-operating minority partner, PetroNor controls neither the drilling programme nor the lifting calendar. At a normalized USD 75-80 oil price the barrels are worth roughly today's market value, leaving no margin of safety for the court case. Update 2026-11-09: Brent has already slipped from about USD 109 in mid-September to about USD 92, the shares are down about 10% since the last full review, and the trial opens on 23 November 2026, three days after the Q3 report (20 November) - the legal binary is now two weeks away rather than two months.
picks.consensus_delta: The screener - and any reader of trailing multiples - sees an energy producer at 4x free cash flow with discounted-cash-flow and earnings-power values 70% above the price. We disagree: those figures capitalise one April 2026 cargo sold at about USD 116 a barrel. The market is not pricing terminal decline into stable earnings power; it is pricing a nine-year, depleting, minority non-operated interest with no cargo until May 2027, cash largely earmarked for the overlift and eleven months of costs, and a corruption trial starting in November 2026. On normalized oil the price is close to fair value. At NOK 10.82 (2026-11-09) the gap has widened to about 15%, but that is still not the discount we require. Where the market could be wrong in our favour is narrower: it may be giving no credit to the Aje sale or the 2C resource extension, and it may be underpricing how much the Gulf supply shock keeps Brent near USD 90-100 into the May 2027 lifting. Neither is certain enough to lean on. No broker consensus or price target could be found to test directly.
picks.valley_of_death: The next three to six months remain the weakest part of PetroNor's calendar. The Q3 report lands on 20 November 2026 and the Hemla corruption trial opens on 23 November 2026, with a first ruling around March 2027 - both before the next cargo (about May 2027), with no revenue in between and part of output going to repay the overlift. There is no debt and no solvency risk: cash net of the overlift was about USD 44M at 30 June 2026. The risk is price: trial headlines, a further retreat in Brent (already down from about USD 109 to about USD 92 since mid-September) or a trimmed 2027 infill programme could take the shares to the NOK 9.65 52-week low. One shared driver, oil, dominates both paths.
picks.positioning_washout: Moderate. The income-driven holder base, drawn by the June 2026 repayment, faces a dry year with no payout before the May 2027 annual meeting, and the shares have already drifted from NOK 11.98 to NOK 10.82 since late September alongside softer oil. Insider buying is nil on the screener and smart-money interest is weak (22 of 100). There is no index deletion or covenant forcing sales; a sector-wide oil sell-off or trial-driven selling toward NOK 9.5-10 is the plausible route to our level.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near NOK 10.0, which a sector-wide sell-off in oil producers, or selling around the corruption trial that opens on 23 November, could deliver. The thesis holds: PetroNor is a debt-free, low-cost producer whose management has delivered on output and payouts, and nothing dated since our last look changes that. But the screener's cheapness still rests on one April 2026 cargo sold near USD 116 a barrel. On a normalized oil deck our sum-of-the-parts (valuing each piece separately) fair value is about NOK 12.7 - slightly lower than before only because the krone strengthened - against a NOK 10.82 price, a discount of about 15%, short of the roughly 20% we require on a nine-year depleting, minority, non-operated asset with no revenue until about May 2027. At about NOK 10.0 the discount clears that bar. Brent near USD 92 still helps, but the case hinges on a single factor, oil, so we do not chase it. Value case judged without any event: modest discount, no moat, a live legal question mark - a low score.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# PetroNor E&P ASA (PNOR.OL) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-09 (update of the 2026-09-29 review). Listing: Oslo Børs, PNOR.OL, quoted in Norwegian kroner: NOK 10.82 on FMP on 2026-11-09 (down 3.9% on the day, down about 10% since NOK 11.98 on 2026-09-29; 52-week range NOK 9.65-18.58). The company reports in US dollars; USD/NOK 9.37 (FMP, 2026-11-09) is used for conversions, so 142.36M shares give a market value of about NOK 1.54B, roughly USD 164M. Brent crude was about USD 92 a barrel on 2026-11-09 (FMP), down about USD 6 on the day and below the USD 100-109 of mid-to-late September.*

**Identity note.** The peer file for this ticker describes the company as Panoro Energy; that is wrong. PNOR.OL is PetroNor E&P, confirmed by FMP's quote record and the company's own filings. PetroNor's economic engine is a minority interest in the offshore PNGF Sud production licences in the Republic of Congo (held through its subsidiary Hemla and the operating vehicle HEPCO, which has outside minority owners), plus an interest in the Aje field (OML 113) in Nigeria — the Q4 2025 report states the New Age transaction completed in February 2026, giving a 52.2% project economic and voting interest — and exploration acreage in Guinea-Bissau and The Gambia.

**What changed since the last look (2026-09-29).** Little that is dated and verifiable. The company's press-release page lists one new item, a "Q3 2026 production update" dated 9 October 2026; its PDF could not be retrieved in this run, so no Q3 production figure is used here. The company's financial calendar shows the Q3 2026 quarterly report on 20 November 2026, three days before the Hemla corruption trial is due to open (23 November 2026). FMP carries no news or press items for the listing, and our web-search budget for this run was exhausted, so no news of an Aje sale, an infill-drilling decision or a trial postponement could be checked beyond the company's own release list (which shows none). The share price fell about 10% while Brent eased from the September spike and the krone strengthened against the dollar (USD/NOK 9.60 to 9.37), which trims the kroner value of dollar assets by about 2.4%. No balance-sheet data later than 30 June 2026 is available on FMP (cash USD 85.7M, no debt, other current liabilities USD 52.9M including the roughly USD 41.5M overlift).

**Source note.** FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing. This dossier draws on the Q2 2026 interim report and webinar of 28 August 2026, the Q2 production update, the company's press-release list (checked 2026-11-09), FMP quarterly statements, quote, Brent and USD/NOK data (2026-11-09), and the January 2026 Økokrim (Norway's economic-crime prosecutor) decision. Only one quarter of management commentary could be read in usable detail, so the tone and guidance sections are necessarily thinner than an eight-quarter review.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has narrowed to one simple proposition: a small, debt-free, low-cost producer that pays out almost everything it lifts. Earlier years were about growth — adding Nigeria's Aje field, West African exploration, and a bigger footprint. In 2026 the emphasis is on the Congo cash machine: infill drilling in 2025 lifted output, facilities uptime improved (production efficiency 93% in Q2 against 86% in Q1), and the April cargo turned into a large cash return.

Aje has quietly moved from a growth pillar to something to sell. Management now describes a farm-down or divestment, run through an adviser, because Norwegian legal obstacles have hampered project financing. That is a meaningful retreat: the asset carries around 70 million barrels of oil equivalent of contingent resources (2C — discovered but not yet commercially sanctioned volumes), but the company can no longer fund it itself.

The other thread running through the year is legal. In January 2026 Økokrim indicted Hemla Africa Holding, the subsidiary that holds the Congo interest, for alleged corruption of senior Congolese political figures from 2016 onward; market-manipulation suspicions against the parent were dropped. The trial starts on 23 November 2026, with a first ruling expected around March 2027.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (Q2 2026) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Production up on infill drilling and uptime | Net output 5,045 barrels a day in Q2 vs 4,712 in Q1; year-end gross exit rate guided above 25,500 barrels a day (about 4,300 net) — i.e. volumes are expected to drift down again | Matches, but the gain is not a new plateau |
| The April lifting delivered a large cash injection | 964,593 barrels sold at about USD 116 a barrel, roughly USD 112M; Q2 revenue USD 151.4M, operating cash flow USD 102M, cash up from USD 44M to USD 85M even after the payout | Matches |
| Strong balance sheet: USD 85M cash, no debt | Confirmed on FMP's 30 June balance sheet. But the company is in an overlift position (it lifted more than its share and must hand back about 355,000 barrels, a liability of about USD 41.5M) and there is no further sale until about May 2027 | Richer than reality: cash net of the overlift is closer to USD 44M, and it must carry the company for about eleven months without a cargo |
| Shareholder returns are a priority | NOK 3.25 a share (about USD 50M) repaid in June 2026; USD 30.7M returned in Q2 2025 | Matches — the distribution record is real |
| Headline growth figures | The screener shows revenue down 58% and earnings per share down 79% for 2025, then a latest-quarter earnings jump of over 600% | These swings are cargo timing, not business trends. PetroNor sells in lumpy one-million-barrel cargoes, so annual and quarterly numbers jump around the lifting schedule |

Reported profits also swing with tax treatment: in Congo production-sharing contracts much of the tax is settled in barrels, so the income-tax line (USD 29M in Q2) is partly an accounting presentation rather than a cash outflow.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable (no new call since 28 August 2026; the Q3 report is due 20 November 2026). The Q2 2026 webinar was confident on operations and cash, openly flagged a softer Q3 while key wells are worked over, and was careful to present a possible Aje transaction in Q4 as conditional rather than guidance. On the indictment, the tone is firmly defensive: the company "categorically contests the indictment" (Q2 2026). There is no shift from offence to defence on the core business; the defensive register is confined to Nigeria and the court case.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium. Production has improved as promised after the 2025 infill campaign, and the distributions announced were paid. But the company's guidance is thin (capex of about USD 10M for 2026 and about USD 20M for 2027, the latter still subject to the operating committee in November), key decisions sit with the operator and the Congolese state partner rather than with PetroNor, and the Aje development plan has been abandoned in favour of a sale. There is no analyst consensus to measure beats against — no dated broker price target could be found.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- How long the cash lasts with no cargo until May 2027 and an overlift still being repaid in barrels.
- Whether the indictment could hold up cash extraction from Congo. Management earlier noted that pulling funds out of the Congo operations could clash with its commitment to cooperate with the authorities — a direct link between the court case and the timing of payouts.
- What Aje will fetch and when; "multiple" parties are reported under confidentiality agreements, but no price or date.
- Reserve life: net reserves just under 16 million barrels (about nine years at current rates), extendable to 14–15 years only if the 9.6 million barrels of 2C resources are converted.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: a subsidiary indicted for what the prosecutor calls grand corruption in the host country (January 2026; trial 23 November 2026). Outcomes range from a fine to confiscation and, in the worst case, damage to the relationship with the Congolese state that grants the licence.
- Red: no revenue until about May 2027; the overlift means part of the coming production is already spent.
- Red: Aje shifted from growth project to forced sale because financing was blocked (Q2 2026).
- Red: minority owners in the operating vehicle took USD 10.3M of dividends in Q2 — a reminder that not every barrel belongs to PNOR shareholders.
- Green: no debt, operating costs of about USD 12 a barrel at PNGF Sud, production efficiency up to 93%.
- Green: a demonstrated habit of returning cash (USD 50M in June 2026, about 30% of today's market value).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The vocabulary on Nigeria changed from development to "farm-down/divestment", and the reason given — Norwegian legal obstacles to financing — ties the court case directly to capital allocation. The next distribution was framed as following the May 2027 AGM, which implicitly concedes there will be no payout before the next cargo. Management also framed 2027 infill drilling as depending on a November operating-committee decision, showing that PetroNor, as a non-operator, does not control its own capex.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. The Congo business is a steady, low-cost, depleting cash stream paid out almost in full; nothing in 2026 changed that. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: today's price is not as cheap as the screener suggests. The 4x price-to-free-cash-flow figure and the discounted-cash-flow value near NOK 41 are both built on a single April cargo sold at about USD 116 a barrel during an oil-price spike. At a normal oil price, a nine-year reserve life and cash that must fund eleven months without revenue, the stock trades close to what the barrels are worth — before any charge for the corruption trial.

Moat: none in the durable sense. A low-cost position in a depleting field is an advantage, not a moat; the company is a minority, non-operating partner selling a commodity. The trend is stable rather than eroding — returns are high on a small asset base, but they track the oil price and the cargo calendar, not a competitive edge. The secular threat from the energy transition is manageable over a nine-year reserve life. The cheapness is mostly neither a fear-print nor a value trap: it is a fair price for a short-lived asset with a legal overhang.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · no real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
