# China Coal Energy (1898.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16 from three management briefings (2025 annual results on 2026-04-01, first-half 2026 results on 2026-08-22, nine-month 2026 results on 2026-10-28) cross-checked against our screener's financial history and the 2026-09-30 balance sheet. Company figures are in Chinese yuan (CNY) under Chinese accounting standards unless noted; the share trades in Hong Kong dollars (HKD).*

**Bottom line:** management's story is modest and the numbers mostly back it. China Coal Energy is a state-controlled coal miner with chemical and power arms. Earnings fell for two years as coal prices came off their 2022-23 peak (net income CNY 19.5B in 2023, CNY 14.1B in 2025), and in 2026 they have stopped falling: nine-month net profit is CNY 12.7B, up 2.1%, on coal prices up 17.5%. The weak spot is volume. The company produced 93.4 million tonnes in nine months, and policy caps on monthly output mean the shortfall will not be made up in the fourth quarter. Costs per tonne are rising and management says more than 60% of them are fixed.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **April 2026 (2025 results, group-wide briefing).** The group pitch was scale and national duty: 310 million tonnes of capacity, "2 integrations and 2 hedges" (pairing coal with captive power so a price move hurts one arm and helps the other, and pairing coal power with renewables to offset carbon), and a 15th Five-Year Plan built around coal, power, chemicals and renewables. The tone was strategic and long-dated. There was little on the listed company's own volumes, and the questions about life after China's 2030 carbon peak got a broad answer about efficiency, green hydrogen and "explorations".
- **August 2026 (first half).** The story narrowed to price recovery against volume loss. Self-produced coal sold for CNY 524 a tonne, up 11.5%, which added CNY 3.3B to profit. Lower output (CNY 1.17B) and higher unit cost (CNY 1.36B) took much of it back. The new items were a tax back-payment and late fees (non-operating expenses of CNY 551M, up 788%), and moving outsourced mining teams onto the payroll.
- **October 2026 (nine months).** Same story, with a sharper edge on cost. Coal prices were up 17.5% (CNY 557 a tonne) and coking coal up 29.4%. Unit cost was CNY 299 a tonne, up CNY 41. The new growth item is the 900,000-tonne Yulin phase-two coal-to-olefins (plastics feedstock) plant: startup "in November", full production "Q1 next year". Management also said fourth-quarter output is capped at one twelfth of annual capacity per month, so the volume gap will not close.

**What was quietly dropped:** volume growth. The April deck boasted capacity "up by 22% versus 2020". By October the message was "make every effort to stabilize output and make up for the shortfall", and then that policy will not allow it.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Sound profitability and cash generation" (Aug and Oct 2026) | Nine-month operating cash flow CNY 22.5B, up 6.9%; net profit up 2.1% (Chinese standards) and up 15.3% under international standards (IFRS) | Holds. The gap between the two standards (tax and the safety reserve) is worth watching |
| Coal prices "rebounded" | Average price CNY 557 a tonne, up 17.5%; this price effect added CNY 7.7B to profit | Holds, but it is market-driven, not management-made |
| Costs are "within a reasonable range" | Unit coal cost rose from CNY 286 (first half) to CNY 299 (nine months), up CNY 41 a tonne year on year; third-quarter labour, admin and finance costs all rose | Weaker than claimed: cost is rising faster than management lets on, and "over 60%" of it is fixed |
| "Stable and orderly" production | 93.4 Mt in nine months; the third quarter was about 31.4 Mt; an analyst asked whether 34-35 Mt a quarter could come back and was told policy prevents it | Worse than claimed: volume is the structural soft spot |
| The tax one-off is "fully absorbed" (Aug 2026) | In October an analyst asked whether the third-quarter tax level is "the new norm"; the answer was about the use of the safety reserve pushing tax payable up | Not proven. The tax line is still moving |
| Coal and power integration "steadies margin" | Revenue fell from CNY 240B (2021) to CNY 144B (2025), down about 40%; net margin about 9.8%, gross margin 56.3% on the screener's basis | Partly true. Profit fell far less than revenue, and much of the revenue drop is lower-margin bought-in coal for trading |
| Financial screener feed: trailing-twelve-month (TTM) earnings per share 1.78 and TTM free cash flow 24.16B | Company-reported nine-month earnings of CNY 0.96 a share imply TTM earnings per share near CNY 1.09 (Chinese standards) or about CNY 1.19 (IFRS) | The feed is wrong and should not be used. The 1.78 looks like a period double count |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Stable, turning defensive

- April: offensive and long-range ("we're not just grounded. We also have high ambitions").
- August: defensive on cost and tax ("there might be some differences between the understanding of the actual rules and the execution").
- October: candid but defensive ("it's not so scientific to press down the cost all the way... the rigid part is over 60%"; fourth-quarter costs "may also increase").

Guidance is light, which is typical for Chinese state-owned firms: no profit guidance, little volume guidance, and specific answers only on plant timing.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - Medium

- The first-half interim dividend (CNY 0.184 a share, CNY 2.44B in total) was promised for payment "before the end of October 2026". We could not independently confirm payment in this run; nothing says it slipped.
- The tax one-off was called fully absorbed in August, and in October the tax line was still the analysts' first question. That counts as a soft miss on candour.
- The screener records earnings beats in 3 of 7 quarters (43%), consistent with a company that does not manage expectations.
- Plant timing: the Yulin phase-two units were "mechanically completed" by August, with startup guided for November and full production in the first quarter of 2027. That is the next checkable promise.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

1. **Cost and tax** (both 2026 calls): the August tax back-payment, the third-quarter tax rate, and labour costs. Management's answers were long and did not commit to a number.
2. **Volume recovery** (October): management deferred to policy. Monthly output capped at one twelfth of annual capacity means no catch-up.
3. **Chemicals and oil** (October): the chemicals margin is partly a gift from high oil prices driven by Middle East conflict. Management put breakeven against oil-based plants at about USD 70 a barrel of oil. If oil falls below that, the chemicals profit uplift (CNY 1.2B in nine months) is at risk.
4. **After 2030** (April): asked about the 16th Five-Year Plan, management called it "a very sharp question, tricky for us to answer".

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Coal output is down and capped by policy for the fourth quarter (October 2026).
- 🔴 Unit cost is up CNY 41 a tonne year on year, with more than 60% fixed (October 2026).
- 🔴 A tax inspection back-payment and late fees in the first half (non-operating expenses up 788%), with the tax rate still drifting in the third quarter.
- 🔴 The chemicals uplift depends on oil staying above about USD 70 (October 2026).
- 🔴 Our data feed's TTM earnings and free cash flow figures are corrupted (they do not reconcile with reported results), so any screen built on them overstates cheapness.
- 🟢 Profit grew again in 2026 after two years of decline (nine months up 2.1%; up 15.3% under IFRS).
- 🟢 Net cash of CNY 22.2B at 2026-09-30 (CNY 97.3B cash against CNY 75.1B debt including leases), on a consolidated basis.
- 🟢 The controlling shareholder bought more shares in the first half of 2026 (August call), and the company has paid an interim dividend three years running.
- 🟢 Yulin phase two (900,000 tonnes of plastics feedstock) is close to startup, a 2027 volume lever that is not coal.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The language moved from capacity ("310 million tonnes") to "efficiency from existing assets". Growth capital spending is shifting to chemicals and power (Yulin, Wuxuan coal-power, Liquid Sunshine), not mines.
- More coal is now sold through domestic distributors than traded directly. The CFO framed this as a compliance and revenue-recognition fix. It is benign but deserves watching.
- Independent directors answered the safety, tax and compliance questions in August. That suggests the board is building a paper trail after the tax inspection.
- The "market value management" wording echoes the SASAC (the state assets regulator) push for state firms to support their share prices. The parent's share buying is the visible proof of it.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** Earnings have stopped falling at a lower level, cash is building, and spending is steering toward chemicals and power.

**The one thing to weigh before sizing:** this is a coal-price and policy-cap business, not a compounder. The discount to book value (about 0.67 times equity per share) reflects a falling earnings base since 2023 and China's capped coal volumes, and the margin of safety rests on coal prices holding. Our feed's flattering TTM earnings figure (1.78) is wrong; on reported numbers the stock is about 7 to 8 times earnings, in line with Chinese coal peers rather than cheap against them.

**Moat:** narrow but real, from scale and cost (large, low-cost mines in Shanxi and Inner Mongolia with rail and port logistics) and from mining licences in a sector where the state limits new supply. Return on invested capital (ROIC) of about 11% and return on equity (ROE) of about 12% are cyclically lower than 2022-23, but the drop tracks the coal price, not lost competitive position. The moat trend is stable.

**Secular threat:** material, not terminal. China's carbon peak by 2030 and the renewables build-out will cap thermal coal demand over the 2030s. The policy role of coal as baseload "energy security", the long-term contract system and the move into chemicals soften this. The cheapness is a mix of a cyclical fear print and a slowly shrinking base. It is not a pure value trap, but it is also not a mispricing that will close fast.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

picks.bull_thesis: IAG owns the strongest network positions in European aviation: British Airways at Heathrow, Iberia at Madrid as Europe's gateway to Latin America, Aer Lingus at Dublin, Vueling at Barcelona, and the Avios loyalty programme sitting across all of them. The 2026 fuel shock is the stress test the bull case needed, and it passed. In the third quarter of 2026 (reported 2026-11-06) unit fuel cost rose about 31%, yet revenue hit a record, every airline earned a double-digit margin, the group margin was 17.7%, North Atlantic unit revenue rose 11% (British Airways up 12.6% at constant currency) and management expects to recover over 80% of the extra fuel cost across the group and over 100% at British Airways. Loyalty keeps compounding: core loyalty profit up 20% in the quarter, with a high-margin, capital-light cash stream that the market values at an airline multiple inside the group. The balance sheet is a genuine asset: net leverage under 1x and gross leverage down from 2.6x to 1.9x through 2025, funding a EUR 1.5bn buyback that shrinks the share count by roughly a tenth a year at about 6-7 times earnings, plus a dividend raised 10%. Hidden value is starting to surface: the Iberia engine business won one of only eight premier LEAP maintenance licences and now has an outside partner, which puts a market price on a part the group multiple ignores. If fuel normalises and Gulf capacity stays constrained, 2027 margins can return toward the 15% earned in 2025, earnings per share grows double digits on the shrinking share count, and a re-rating toward US network peers (8-9x earnings, per the former CFO on 2025-08-01) is plausible. Conditions: jet fuel stabilises, transatlantic premium demand holds, and cash returns continue at the full-year results in February 2027.
picks.bear_thesis: Airlines are cyclical, capital-hungry businesses with a long record of destroying value at the bottom of the cycle, and 2025 was a near-perfect year (cheap fuel, a weak dollar, strong premium leisure) that flatters every trailing multiple. The 2026 numbers already show the reversal: third-quarter operating profit fell 16% year on year, the nine-month margin is 13.5% against about 15% for 2025, capacity was flat against a planned 1% rise, and non-fuel unit costs rose 3.4% (2026-11-06). Free cash flow fell 13.1% in 2025 before the fuel shock. Short-haul Europe and Dublin face heavy competitor capacity (Ryanair, US carriers into Dublin and Madrid), Vueling is entering years of mixed-fleet inefficiency, and Aer Lingus expects a challenging 2027. The TAP privatisation went to Lufthansa, closing the obvious acquisition route in Portugal. The inflation backdrop is unhelpful: the macro read is reflation (growth up, inflation sticky), and airline margins are exposed to fuel and wage inflation. A recession, a renewed fuel spike or a transatlantic demand slowdown could take margins back to high single digits, at which point the stock's apparent cheapness evaporates; airline shares routinely fall 30-50% in such episodes. Finally, at 450.7p the stock already trades within 10% of a reasonable fair value, so the margin of safety that justified buying in the 330s is gone.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is not pricing terminal decline into IAG; it is pricing a normal airline-cycle discount. At 450.7p the stock trades on roughly 6-7 times earnings and about 8.5 times free cash flow, which looks low, but the consensus forward earnings growth of about 19% already assumes fuel normalises and margins return toward 2025 levels. Where we disagree with the market is narrow: we think the loyalty business deserves more credit than a single group multiple gives it, and that the fuel-shock quarter proved the margin floor is higher than past cycles. But that view is largely reflected after the move from the 330s low to 450.7p. There is no factually wrong street assumption we can point to that leaves a large gap; the debate is about the size of the cyclical discount, not its existence.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) is the winter season and the first half of 2027. Winter is seasonally the weakest period for airlines, management is cutting winter capacity, and if jet fuel stays elevated, unhedged exposure grows as older hedges roll off. There is no debt maturity wall (net leverage under 1x, gross leverage falling), so liquidation risk is low. The real risks are a renewed Middle East escalation lifting fuel again, a slowdown in transatlantic premium demand, and continued competitor capacity in Dublin, Madrid and short-haul Europe. Any of these could push the shares back toward the 395p area or below, which is exactly the setup our buying level waits for.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-selling pressure on the horizon: no index deletion, no lock-up, no dividend cut (the dividend was just raised 10%). The shareholder base is mainly long-only and value funds plus Qatar Airways as the largest holder. The plausible seller to our level is a sector-wide sell-off: airline shares trade as a group on fuel, recession fears and Middle East headlines, and a 12% drop from today is well within the stock's normal range (52-week range 332.7p to 492.9p).
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near 395p, which a sector-wide sell-off in airline shares could deliver. The thesis holds, and the third-quarter 2026 results (2026-11-06) strengthened it: record revenue, a 17.7% margin through a fuel shock, every airline in double digits, loyalty profit still growing and the dividend raised 10%. IAG remains the best-run large network airline group in Europe. What changed is the price, not the business: the shares rose to 450.7p on 2026-11-09, so our sum-of-the-parts (valuing loyalty and the airlines separately, then subtracting EUR 4.64bn of net debt including leases) fair value of about 490p is now only about 9% above the market, against an adverse case near 265p if margins fall to a downturn level. That is not enough margin of safety for an airline in a reflation backdrop with fuel as the swing factor. We keep the committee's level of 395p, where the discount to fair value is about 24%, and conviction of 3. The soft catalyst (further cash returns, likely discussed with full-year results in February 2027) has no fixed date and no contractual payout, and we neither add nor subtract for it.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst, what forces the re-rating, is earnings delivery plus cash returns. Next checkpoints: full-year 2026 results around late February 2027 (when further excess cash returns are normally announced, not confirmed) and the 2027 capacity and fuel outlook. A 2027 margin back near 14-15% with continued buybacks would support fair value; neither is dated or binding.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# IAG.L (International Airlines Group): a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-09. Five calls reviewed: half-year 2025 (2025-08-01), third quarter 2025 (2025-11-07), full year 2025 (2026-02-27), half-year 2026 (2026-07-31) and third quarter 2026 (2026-11-06). Prices are in pence on the London listing (IAG.L); company figures are in euros unless stated.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved from "record margins on cheap fuel" to "the portfolio holds up when fuel spikes."

- **2025 (Aug and Nov calls):** the pitch was strength on every front. Operating profit up 43.5% in the first half of 2025, an 11.8% half-year margin, net leverage (net debt divided by operating earnings before depreciation) of 0.7x, and a third quarter in which "every single one of our airlines has reported a margin over 20%" (2025-11-07). Management openly credited part of the gain to "favorable fuel price" and "favorable FX" (2025-08-01).
- **Full year 2025 (2026-02-27):** "record operating profit, operating margin and return on invested capital", a dividend increase and a step-up in cash returns from EUR 1.0bn to EUR 1.5bn, with "further excess cash returns in the future" promised.
- **2026 (Jul and Nov calls):** the Middle East conflict pushed jet fuel up and closed Gulf routes. The tone shifted to recovery and resilience: around 60% of the fuel increase recovered through pricing in the first half, rising to "over 80% across the group and over 100% at British Airways" for the full year (2026-11-06). The third quarter of 2026 was a record for revenue (+4.5%) but operating profit fell from EUR 2,053m to EUR 1,726m, a 17.7% margin.
- **New threads in 2026:** a Japanese partner (ITOCHU) investing in a new engine-maintenance business, IAG Engine Tech, built around a premier LEAP engine licence ("only 8 of them in the world"), and the loss of the TAP Air Portugal privatisation to Lufthansa. Leadership also changed: the CFO is now Jose Antonio Barrionuevo, replacing Nicholas Cadbury.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "World-class", sector-leading margins | 2025 revenue EUR 32.6bn, net income EUR 3.28bn (10.1% net margin); third-quarter 2026 operating margin of 17.7% even with a 30.7% rise in unit fuel cost | Holds |
| Earnings growth per share | Earnings per share of 0.69 in 2025, up 25.5%; the share count shrinks every year through buybacks | Holds. Part of the 2025 jump came from cheap fuel and currency, as management itself said |
| Strong cash generation | Price-to-free-cash-flow of 8.5x, free-cash-flow margin of 9.5%, but free cash flow fell 13.1% in 2025 (higher capex, a EUR 447m VAT payment to the UK tax authority) | Mostly holds; the decline is explained and dated |
| Strong balance sheet | Net leverage of 0.7-0.8x through 2025; gross leverage down from 2.6x to 1.9x (2025-11-07). The scanner's "net debt 495.73B" is a unit error, not a real figure | Holds |
| Loyalty is a growing, steady earner | Loyalty profit GBP 152m in the third quarter of 2026, GBP 171m before the disputed VAT treatment, core loyalty up 20% (2026-11-06) | Holds |
| Margin target of 12-15% | 2025 came in at about 15%; nine months of 2026 at 13.5%; full-year guidance of at least 12% kept | Holds, now in the lower half of the range |

The scanner's return on equity of -31.8% and Altman-Z (a solvency score) of 1.7 are artefacts of an airline balance sheet with negative or thin book equity after COVID losses and heavy lease liabilities. They are not signs of distress in the current numbers.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable. In 2025 the tone was offensive: "we are delivering what we are promising to you every quarter" (2025-08-01). In 2026 it turned defensive on costs and capacity ("we are taking out capacity in a disciplined way", 2026-11-06) but stayed confident on demand: "This has been a record quarter in terms of revenue" and British Airways "is seeing very strong bookings for the first quarter of next year." Guidance specificity has fallen slightly: management declined to give 2027 capacity plans until it sees "how the situation in Iran is going to evolve" (2026-07-31).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

High. 2025 capacity growth of 2.4% matched the guidance given at the third quarter. Non-fuel unit cost guidance was cut from 4% to 3% mid-2025 and delivered. In 2026 the misses are explained and largely external: capacity flat against a plan of about 1% growth (Middle East cancellations, UK air traffic control failures), and an underlying non-fuel unit cost rise of only about 0.5% once one-offs are stripped out. The financials show earnings beats in 5 of the last 7 quarters (71%). Some press coverage described the third quarter of 2026 as a profit shortfall versus expectations, but full-year guidance was held. No sign of sandbagging; the pattern is careful guidance that is met.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Fuel recovery quality:** analysts asked how much of the third quarter still carried tickets sold before the fuel spike (2026-11-06). The answer was not quantified in the material available.
- **Competitive capacity:** transatlantic growth into Dublin and Madrid by US carriers has been a recurring question since 2025; Aer Lingus said 2027 will "continue to be a challenging competitive environment."
- **Premium dilution:** whether more business-class seats across the industry will erode premium fares. British Airways argued its premium footprint is broadly the same as in 2018-19.
- **Mixed fleet at Vueling:** moving to Boeing 737s while flying Airbus aircraft adds cost for years (2025-08-01).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags
- Operating profit fell by EUR 327m year on year in the third quarter of 2026 as fuel rose; the 2025 record was partly a cheap-fuel year.
- Vueling and Aer Lingus face persistent competition in short-haul Europe and Dublin.
- The VAT dispute with the UK tax authority costs Loyalty about GBP 19m a quarter in reported profit while it is appealed.
- Lost TAP to Lufthansa (2026); the obvious external growth option in Portugal is gone.

Green flags
- North Atlantic unit revenue up 11% in the third quarter of 2026, British Airways up 12.6% at constant currency.
- Interim dividend raised 10% (2026-11-06); the final EUR 500m tranche of the EUR 1.5bn buyback has started.
- The Iberia engine business gained a premier LEAP licence and an outside investor, which puts a market value on a hidden asset.
- Every airline delivered a double-digit margin in a fuel-shock quarter.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The language moved from "transformation program" in 2025 toward "portfolio" in 2026: management is now selling IAG as a diversified group (loyalty, maintenance, holidays) rather than a set of airlines.
- Bringing in an outside partner for the engine business, despite a strong balance sheet, signals a willingness to put market prices on non-airline parts. That supports a sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) reading over time.
- The new CFO is giving more granular cost bridges (a four-part breakdown of the non-fuel cost rise), which is a credibility positive.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. Capital allocation is disciplined: leverage held under 1x, a dividend that grows modestly, and buybacks while the shares trade at about 6-7 times earnings.

The single most important thing to weigh: 2025 was a peak-ish year helped by cheap fuel and a weak dollar. The business has now shown it can earn a 13-14% margin through a fuel shock, which is the better base for valuation, and it is not the 15% of 2025.

Moat: narrow but real. It rests on regulatory and licence assets (Heathrow and Madrid slots, hub positions, transatlantic joint ventures) and on the Avios loyalty network. Returns are high for an airline (record return on invested capital in 2025) and the 2026 dip is fuel-driven and cyclical, not structural, so the moat is stable rather than eroding. Secular threat: manageable. Decarbonisation costs (sustainable aviation fuel mandates, emissions trading) and possible demand limits are real but long-dated and shared by every carrier. The cheapness is a cyclical, fuel-risk discount typical of airlines, not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Danieli is a profitable, cash-rich steel-plant builder priced as if its record order book will not convert. On 2026-09-25 it reported a backlog of EUR 6.04B at 30 June 2026, up 12% in a year and worth about 1.6 years of revenue, while revenue fell 9% to EUR 3.83B because orders are being executed on later schedules. EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) held at EUR 438.9M and the company's own adjusted net cash, which strips out customer prepayments, rose about 48% to EUR 1,019.7M. At EUR 52.15 for the ordinary shares (FMP quote, 2026-11-16) and EUR 36.42 for the savings shares, the whole company is worth about EUR 3.18B, so the operating business is valued at roughly EUR 2.16B, or about 4.9 times EBITDA. The listed engineering peers in our peer file (Andritz, Metso, Valmet) trade at 12-20 times earnings on steadier aftermarket mixes; even a large discount to them leaves room. The 2026/27 guide (EBITDA EUR 430-450M, revenue EUR 3.9-4.2B, net profit stable or improving) sits about 10% below the pre-results consensus, and Equita reads it as prudent, with its own EBITDA estimate at EUR 471M. If the 2025/26 write-downs in Plant Making (tied to project delays and the Fata unit) prove one-off, as Kepler Cheuvreux expects, operating profit rebounds from a depressed EUR 220.8M toward EUR 290-300M. Steel Making (the ABS mill) is guided to grow EBITDA 26-40% to EUR 90-100M as the new Digimelter furnace, due by end-2026, ramps toward doubled capacity. The shift from blast furnaces to electric-arc and lower-carbon steel is a structural tailwind for Danieli's core product line. The advance float, about EUR 1.65B on top of the adjusted cash, earns interest for as long as the order book stays full, which is why net profit (EUR 230.4M, +5%) beats operating profit. Conditions: write-downs do not recur in the half-year results due around late March 2027, the backlog stays at EUR 5.8-6.0B as guided, and European energy costs do not crush ABS margins.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is old and has reasons. Return on invested capital is about 5.5% and return on equity about 9%, poor for a business that holds this much cash; the controlling family has paid out under 10% of profit for years (dividend flat at EUR 0.3146 per ordinary share, approved 2026-10-28, below the roughly EUR 0.38 brokers expected), so minority holders cannot count on the cash ever reaching them. The headline net cash of EUR 2.67B is mostly customer prepayments owed back as work; the true figure is about EUR 1.0B and is guided flat next year while Steel Making's net debt rises to EUR 250-300M to fund a capacity expansion with commodity-steel returns. 2025/26 operating profit fell 27% on write-downs that management has explained thinly, and Plant Making's margin is guided down from about 13.2% to about 11-12% on higher revenue, which suggests newer orders are priced tighter or carry more risk. Profit growth leaned on financial income including a EUR 26.9M currency gain that management itself expects to fade. The business is cyclical: its customers are steelmakers whose capital budgets depend on steel prices, European demand is weak, and Chinese plant builders compete hard on price in emerging markets. The margin record in the last inflation wave was poor (gross margin from 29.4% in the year to June 2019 to 18.2% in the year to June 2022), and the macro backdrop today is inflationary. The screener's cheapness signals are flattered: price to free cash flow of 5.3x includes a EUR 386M working-capital inflow from advances, and normalized free cash flow is closer to EUR 200-250M, a 6-8% yield rather than 19%. The ordinary shares also carry a 43% premium to the economically near-identical savings shares; a narrowing of that gap would hurt ordinary holders even if the business performs. What would confirm the bear case: another write-down or a backlog below EUR 5.8B in the half-year results, or an EBITDA run-rate under EUR 430M.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing Danieli as a cyclical project house in an earnings downgrade, and on the near term it is broadly right: the 2026/27 EBITDA guide of EUR 430-450M sits about 10% below the roughly EUR 497M Bloomberg consensus that prevailed before 2026-09-25, and every broker we found cut its target on 2026-09-29. Where we disagree is on what the cheapness is resting on. The street focuses on the write-downs; we think the bigger mispricing risk runs both ways around the cash. Screens that read EUR 2.67B of net cash and a 5.3x price to free cash flow overstate the value, because most of that cash is customer prepayments; the company's adjusted figure is EUR 1.02B. On the other side, even with only EUR 1.02B credited, the operating business trades at about 4.9 times EBITDA on a record EUR 6.04B order book, which does not discount a structurally shrinking company. Our base fair value of EUR 61 is below every published broker target (EUR 68-81, 2026-09-29), because we discount the engineering business heavily for low returns and family control. The street is not looking the wrong way; it is looking at the right problems and pricing them a little too harshly.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation, maturity or refinancing risk exists: debt is EUR 874M against EUR 3.54B of cash, and adjusted net cash is about EUR 1.0B. The risky window is the next four to five months up to the half-year report (due around late March 2027, date unconfirmed). Risks inside it: further Plant Making write-downs or delays that push revenue below the EUR 3.9B floor; a slowdown in new orders that would shrink both project margin and the interest-earning advance float; European energy-price spikes that hit the ABS mill while its new furnace is still ramping; and steel-industry capital spending stalling if steel prices or tariffs turn. The ex-dividend date of 2026-11-23 will lower the price by about EUR 0.31 mechanically.
picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure is identifiable. The dividend was held flat, not cut, so yield holders have no trigger to sell. The ordinary float is thin (about 36.4M shares outstanding, family-controlled, roughly 31,000 shares traded on 2026-11-16) and the stock sits in Italian small- and mid-cap mandates, so any outflow from that segment or a European-cyclicals de-rating can move the price sharply in either direction, as the 15.4% one-day fall on 2026-09-28 showed. The more likely route to our entry level is that kind of sector or style sell-off, not a mechanical event. The stock has already traded at EUR 50 (2026-09-28) and as low as EUR 44.30 within the last year.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near EUR 50.8, which a sector-wide sell-off in European cyclicals or Italian small caps could deliver; the stock already traded at EUR 50 on 2026-09-28. The thesis holds: a record EUR 6.04B order book, flat EBITDA of EUR 438.9M and adjusted net cash up to EUR 1.02B (all at 30 June 2026) describe a healthy if lumpy business, and the 2025/26 profit hit came from write-downs rather than lost demand. We value the ordinary shares at about EUR 61 by their parts (Plant Making at 6.5 times guided EBITDA, the ABS mill at 4.5 times, plus EUR 1.02B of adjusted net cash), about 17% above today's EUR 52.15; that is just short of the 20% discount we require in the current inflationary backdrop, so we do not buy at today's price. The adverse case is about EUR 48 and the favorable case about EUR 84. Two cautions shape our conviction, which is moderate: the headline EUR 2.67B of net cash is mostly customer prepayments and should not be counted as owners' money, and the family has shown no sign of returning the real EUR 1B either, which keeps returns on capital near 5.5%. The engineering moat is narrow but real, and the shift to electric-arc steelmaking helps rather than threatens it. What would change our view: another write-down or a backlog under EUR 5.8B in the half-year report would put the thesis in doubt; a larger payout, buyback or savings-share conversion would lift the fair value.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard, dated re-rating event. The next checkpoints are the half-year report to 31 December 2026 (due around late March 2027; last year's came 2026-03-25), which will show whether the write-downs stopped and whether the guide is being beaten, and the Digimelter furnace start-up at ABS targeted by end-2026. Events that would force a faster re-rating and are not announced: a larger payout or buyback using the EUR 1B of adjusted net cash, a revived conversion of savings shares into ordinary shares (proposed in 2020 at 0.65 ordinary per savings share, not completed), or a large order announcement. None of these is promised, so we do not lean on them.

# Danieli & C. Officine Meccaniche (DAN.MI): a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Prices are for the Milan-listed ordinary (voting) shares, in euros. Danieli also lists non-voting savings shares (DANR.MI); both are discussed where the difference matters.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this name in our data provider, and Danieli does not hold a widely transcribed analyst call. This dossier is built from the dated company releases and press coverage of them instead: the full-year 2025/26 results approved on 2026-09-25 (fiscal year to 30 June 2026), the segment guidance published 2026-10-16, the shareholder meeting of 2026-10-28, and the broker notes reported on 2026-09-29. Where we would normally quote management on a call, we quote the release language as reported. No quote below is invented; where a figure could not be sourced, we say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Danieli is two businesses under one roof. Plant Making (about 72% of 2025/26 revenue, EUR 2.78B) designs and builds steel mills and rolling lines for customers worldwide, with SMS group and Primetals (both private) as its main Western rivals. Steel Making (about 28%, EUR 1.06B) is ABS, Danieli's own specialty-steel mill in northern Italy.

The story over the last two years has narrowed from growth to delivery. In 2023-24 revenue rose to a peak of EUR 4.35B (year to June 2024) on the post-pandemic wave of electric-arc-furnace and "green steel" orders. Since then revenue has fallen two years running (EUR 4.20B, then EUR 3.83B, down 9% in 2025/26), while the order book has kept growing: EUR 6.04B at 30 June 2026 against EUR 5.38B a year earlier. Management's message in the September 2026 release is that the revenue dip is timing, not demand: orders are being executed on later schedules.

What is new in 2025/26 is the cost of execution. Operating profit fell 27% to EUR 220.8M because of higher depreciation and write-downs in Plant Making, which brokers tied to the Fata subsidiary and to "project delays and technical problems" (Equita, as reported 2026-09-29). The ABS story has also shifted from margin defence to capacity growth: the "Digimelter" furnace at ABS is under construction with completion targeted by end-2026, part of a plan to double installed capacity.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (dated) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue decline is project timing, demand intact (2026-09-25) | Backlog up 12% to EUR 6.04B while revenue fell 9%; backlog now covers about 1.6 years of sales | Supported |
| EBITDA "in line" with last year (2026-09-25) | EUR 438.9M vs EUR 437.8M; but it missed a consensus of about EUR 456M | Supported, but below the street |
| Cash generation "more than sufficient" to fund investment and R&D (2026-09-25) | Operating cash flow EUR 880M, capex EUR 155M; adjusted net cash rose to EUR 1,019.7M from EUR 688.9M | Supported, with a caveat below |
| Net profit up 5% to EUR 230.4M | Includes EUR 83.4M of financial income, of which EUR 26.9M was a currency gain; operating profit fell 27% | Quality of the beat is weak: it came below the operating line |
| 2026/27 guide: revenue EUR 3.9-4.2B, EBITDA EUR 430-450M, adjusted net cash EUR 1.0-1.1B, net profit "stable or improving" (2026-09-25) | The EBITDA midpoint is flat on 2025/26 and about 10% below the roughly EUR 497M Bloomberg consensus cited in the press | Conservative; credibility hinges on the write-downs not recurring |

**The cash caveat that matters most.** The balance sheet shows EUR 3.54B of cash and short-term investments against EUR 874M of debt, so the headline net cash is about EUR 2.67B. But much of that cash is customer prepayments (advances) on projects in the order book: money Danieli holds but owes back in the form of work. The company's own "adjusted" net cash, which strips these advances out, is EUR 1,019.7M at June 2026 and guided to EUR 1.0-1.1B next year. Equity investors should anchor on about EUR 1.0B, not EUR 2.67B. The advances are not worthless (they earn interest as long as the order book stays full, which is part of why net profit beats operating profit), but they are a float, not owners' money.

The same caveat inflates the cash-flow figures. Free cash flow of EUR 725M in 2025/26 (FMP) includes a EUR 386M working-capital inflow, mostly advances. A normalized figure is closer to EUR 200-250M a year (EBITDA of about EUR 440M, less roughly EUR 90M of tax and EUR 155M of capex, plus interest on the adjusted cash). The screener's "price to free cash flow of 5.3x" overstates the cheapness for that reason.

**Data anomaly.** The screener input shows trailing diluted EPS of 4.69; the fiscal year ends on 30 June, so the trailing year to 2026-06-30 is the fiscal year itself, with reported EPS of EUR 3.22. We use 3.22 and treat 4.69 as a data error.

**Segment numbers (2026-10-16 release).**

| Segment | 2025/26 revenue | 2025/26 EBITDA (margin) | 2026/27 guide EBITDA | Net cash (debt) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plant Making | EUR 2,777M | EUR 368M (13.2%) | EUR 340-360M | Net cash EUR 1.25-1.4B guided |
| Steel Making (ABS) | EUR 1,056M | EUR 71M (6.8%) | EUR 90-100M | Net debt EUR 216M, guided to EUR 250-300M |

Plant Making's margin is guided down (to roughly 11-12%) on higher revenue, which tells you the newer orders were priced more tightly or carry more cost risk. Steel Making is guided up on volumes and efficiency.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, turning more defensive.** Without call transcripts we judge tone from the releases. The 2026-09-25 release leads with the backlog and the "good positive net financial position", and frames 2026/27 as "stable or improving" profit. The risk list has grown: energy costs, weak European demand and the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are all named. Guidance was given in specific ranges for every line, and three weeks later (2026-10-16) the company volunteered a segment split, which is more disclosure than Danieli usually gives. That reads as a response to the share-price fall, not as a change in confidence. Kepler Cheuvreux's complaint (2026-09-29) about "limited information on the write-downs" is the clearest sign that disclosure lags what investors want.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium.** Danieli's guidance has historically been cautious, and the order book supports the revenue range. But the 2025/26 year missed the street on revenue (3.9% below consensus, per Banca Akros) and on EBITDA, and the miss below EBITDA came from write-downs that were not flagged ahead of time. We could not find the September 2025 guidance figures to score last year's delivery line by line, so we do not claim a beat rate. Equita's reading (2026-09-28) is that the 2026/27 guide "contains prudence" and can be beaten; Equita's own estimates sit above it (EBITDA EUR 471M, net cash ex-advances about EUR 1.12B, backlog EUR 6.25B). That is a broker opinion, not evidence.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The write-downs.** Several brokers (Equita, Kepler, as reported 2026-09-29) traced the profit miss to write-downs in Plant Making tied to project delays and technical problems, and to Fata. Kepler cut 2026/27 and 2027/28 EBIT estimates by 20-22% and said better project execution is "essential". Management has not, in anything we found, quantified the write-downs or said they are finished.
- **The dividend.** EUR 0.3146 per ordinary share and EUR 0.3353 per savings share (approved 2026-10-28, paid from 25 November 2026, ex-date 23 November) were flat and below the roughly EUR 0.38 / 0.40 analysts expected. A payout under 10% of net profit, with EUR 1B of adjusted net cash, is a long-standing complaint.
- **Margin direction in Plant Making.** Guidance implies a lower margin on higher revenue.

Broker targets after the results (all dated 2026-09-29): Equita buy, EUR 81 ordinary / EUR 56 savings; Kepler Cheuvreux buy, cut from EUR 80 to EUR 68; Banca Akros accumulate, cut from EUR 75 to EUR 70. Every listed broker cut; none downgraded.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Operating profit down 27% in 2025/26 on write-downs that management has explained only thinly (2026-09-25 release; Kepler 2026-09-29).
- Red: Net profit growth of 5% leaned on financial income, including a EUR 26.9M currency gain that management says will be "more neutral" next year.
- Red: Plant Making margin guided down from about 13.2% to about 11-12% (2026-10-16).
- Red: Payout stays tiny and flat; the controlling family shows no sign of returning the cash pile.
- Red: Margins were badly squeezed by the last inflation wave (gross margin fell from 29.4% in the year to June 2019 to 18.2% in the year to June 2022 on our inflation screen).
- Green: Order book at a high of EUR 6.04B, up 12% (30 June 2026).
- Green: Adjusted net cash up about 48% to EUR 1,019.7M in one year.
- Green: Steel Making guided to grow EBITDA 26-40% (2026-10-16) as the new furnace ramps.
- Green: More disclosure (segment guidance) arrived three weeks after the sell-off.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The headline profit and the operating profit now move in opposite directions. The interest earned on the advance float is doing more of the work, which means a slowdown in new orders would hit profit twice: through lower project margin and lower interest on a shrinking float.
- Plant Making's net cash (guided EUR 1.25-1.4B) funds Steel Making's rising net debt (guided EUR 250-300M). The group is quietly using the engineering business's cash to double capacity at its own steel mill. That is a capital-allocation choice with commodity-steel returns.
- The ordinary shares trade about 43% above the non-voting savings shares (EUR 52.15 against EUR 36.42 on 2026-11-16), even though the savings shares receive a slightly higher dividend. The 2020 proposal to convert savings shares at 0.65 ordinary each did not proceed; the share count still shows both classes. Whoever buys the ordinary shares is paying for votes that, in practice, sit with the controlling family.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** Demand, measured by the order book, is healthy; execution, measured by operating profit, slipped; guidance resets expectations to flat.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** the cash pile is about EUR 1.0B, not EUR 2.67B, and the family has shown no intent to distribute it. The equity is cheap on an enterprise basis (about 4.9 times EBITDA once the adjusted net cash is subtracted, against listed engineering peers in the peer file trading at 12-20 times earnings), but the discount has persisted for years because returns on capital are low (about 5.5% return on invested capital) and minority holders have little say.

**Moat.** A narrow but real moat built on scale and know-how: Danieli is one of three Western suppliers able to deliver a full steel plant, and a leader in electric-arc-furnace mini-mills. The width is limited by low returns on capital, lumpy project risk and Chinese plant builders competing on price in emerging markets. Gross margin has expanded recently (53.5% on the provider's classification), but operating margin fell; we read the trend as stable, not widening.

**Secular threat.** Manageable. The move from blast furnaces to electric-arc and "green" steel is a tailwind for Danieli's order book, not a threat. The real risk is cyclical (steel-industry capital spending) and competitive (Chinese engineering), not terminal. The cheapness is mostly a long-standing governance and cyclicality discount plus a fresh execution scare, not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Cal-Maine is the largest US egg producer (roughly one in six eggs) bought at the bottom of an egg-price cycle, with about $768M of cash and investments and no debt (balance sheet dated 2026-08-29), so about $16.40 of the $67.43 share price is cash. The stock trades near 1.2x book value (about $55 per share), which a September 2026 analyst noted is the lowest price-to-book in at least 20 years. Supply is starting to turn: on the 2026-09-30 call management cited the American Egg Board's flock estimate cut by about 4M birds, August hatch down about 12% year on year and rising chick cancellations, and egg prices are notoriously convex - small supply changes move price a lot. Bird-flu season is starting, and every recent winter (2022, 2024-25) produced a supply shock that sent earnings to records (fiscal 2025 EPS $24.95). Demand is not the problem: retail volume +4% and specialty +6% calendar year to date through August 2026, exports +29%. Meanwhile the mix has structurally improved: specialty eggs and prepared foods were about 54% of Q1 fiscal 2027 sales, specialty earned about a 17% operating margin in fiscal 2026 ($182M on $1.07B) and prepared foods about 14% ($34M on $245M), with prepared-foods capacity set to rise more than 60% by the first half of fiscal 2028. A normalised year should therefore earn more than the pre-2022 cycle did. Conditions: conventional prices recover toward the USDA's projected ~$1.10 per dozen for 2027 within 12-18 months, cash burn stays below about $150M before the turn, and management keeps acquisitions small and egg-centric.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is less than it looks. The screener's 9.6x price-to-free-cash-flow and DCF fair value near $200 are built on fiscal 2025-2026 boom earnings; trailing twelve-month free cash flow is about -$30M and Q1 fiscal 2027 posted gross profit of only $403,000 on $539.6M of sales and a $1.26 loss per share. The conventional segment lost $71M in that single quarter (operating margin -35%), and management's hybrid and cost-plus pricing did little to cushion it. Cash fell from $924M to $768M in one quarter (operating cash flow -$101M, $25M acquisitions, $27M capital spending), and prepared-foods start-up costs will weigh again in Q2 fiscal 2027. Feed, fertilizer and fuel costs are rising (raised on the April and September 2026 calls) just as egg prices sit at historically low inflation-adjusted levels. The industry flock was rebuilt aggressively (the American Egg Board puts it at 336-343M hens, above USDA), so the oversupply could last several more quarters; if bird flu stays mild this winter, there is no shortcut. Before the bird-flu era (fiscal 2019-2021) Cal-Maine earned close to nothing, and the specialty premium is being competed down (analysts flagged rising specialty promotion in April 2026). Insiders sold about 1.31M shares on the open market against 2,800 bought. A stock that has fallen from $95 to the mid-$60s can easily revisit book value or tangible book (about $51) if Q2 fiscal 2027, due around early January 2027, shows another loss.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is not looking the wrong way so much as pricing the trough correctly. Analysts cut targets into the September-October 2026 lows (Goldman $60 on 2026-10-01 with the stock at $65.84; Stephens cut from $80 to $70 in nine days); consensus $81, median $75. Where we disagree: the screener's headline margin of safety (49%) and DCF value near $200 extrapolate peak bird-flu earnings and should be ignored, but equally, the market at about 1.2x book is pricing a long trough with little credit for the specialty and prepared-foods mix, which earned about $216M of operating profit in fiscal 2026. Our base value of $76 sits near the consensus target: there is modest, not large, disagreement with the market.
picks.valley_of_death: Fiscal Q2 2027 (quarter ending late November 2026, reported around early January 2027) will likely show another loss: conventional prices were still oversupplied at the September call and management warned of prepared-foods start-up costs in Q2. Cash and investments could fall from $768M toward $650-700M by early 2027 with operating losses, about $50-60M of maintenance capital spending a year plus about $54M of growth projects mostly in fiscal 2027. Rising feed, fertilizer and fuel costs add to the squeeze. There is no debt, so no maturity wall and no solvency risk; the risk is a 15-25% drawdown toward book or tangible book (about $51-55) if a mild bird-flu winter extends the oversupply into spring 2027.
picks.positioning_washout: The variable dividend (one-third of net income) has already gone to zero with the losses, so income-oriented holders have largely had their reason to leave; the stock fell from about $95 to a $60.13 low. Any further washout would be a sector-wide sell-off in egg and protein names on another loss print in January 2027, not forced selling specific to Cal-Maine.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near $63, which a sector-wide sell-off in egg and protein names on another loss-making quarter could deliver. The thesis holds: Cal-Maine is a debt-free market leader at the bottom of a commodity cycle, with about $16.40 per share in cash, demand still growing and early signs that the industry is cutting supply. On normal-cycle earnings by segment we value it at about $76 per share (range $50 to $104), about 13% above today's $67.43, which is short of the 20% discount we require in the current backdrop. The drivers are (1) the egg-supply turn - watch USDA layer-flock and hatch reports and the American Egg Board supply commentary monthly; (2) bird-flu layer outbreaks during the fall-winter 2026-27 migration season, which historically tighten supply sharply; (3) fiscal Q2 2027 results in early January 2027 and the management appearance at the Stephens conference on 2026-11-18; (4) buybacks - management said (2026-09-30) it sees 'a big value at these levels' and has a large cash pile but has bought only modestly ($5M in Q1 fiscal 2027).
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Cal-Maine Foods (CALM) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16 from five earnings calls (2025-10-01 through 2026-09-30), the screener's financial trajectory and FMP filings data (balance sheet and income statement through the quarter ended 2026-08-29). Live price used: $67.43 (Nasdaq, USD, 2026-11-16).*

**Bottom line:** Management is honest about the cycle and the balance sheet is genuinely strong (about $768M of cash and investments, no debt), but the story management tells - that Cal-Maine is becoming a "diversified consumer-driven food company" whose earnings no longer swing with the egg price - is still mostly an aspiration. The last two quarters lost money at the operating line, and the company burned about $128M of free cash flow (cash from operations minus capital spending) in the quarter to 2026-08-29. What you are buying is the largest US egg producer at the bottom of an egg-price cycle, with a cash cushion, not a de-risked branded-food company.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **October 2025 (first-ever earnings call, fiscal Q1 2026):** a record quarter - $922.6M of sales, $4.12 earnings per share. The framing was already "diversification": specialty eggs (cage-free, pasture-raised, organic and similar) plus prepared foods were "nearly 40% of net sales", and the company was described as "advancing as a diversified consumer-driven food company". A Chief Strategy Officer (Keira Lombardo) and a board member from Tyson were added - a deliberate signal of a consumer-food identity.
- **January 2026 (Q2):** egg prices falling; message became "a rare combination of both value and growth" and "This is a long-term investment story, not a short-term trade." First admission that prepared foods would see "temporary lower volume and higher costs" from plant rebuilds.
- **April 2026 (Q3):** sales down 53% year on year, conventional egg sales down 72%. The language shifted to "compound intrinsic value per share over time" and "normalized earnings power" - the vocabulary of a company preparing investors for a down-cycle. Q3 was called a prepared-foods "trough".
- **July 2026 (Q4 and fiscal 2026):** an operating loss of $58.8M on a 6.2% gross margin; prices at "historically low inflation-adjusted levels". New three-segment reporting (conventional, specialty, prepared foods) and a further $54M prepared-foods capacity investment. The trough was reframed as "a valuable stress case reference point".
- **September 2026 (fiscal Q1 2027):** gross profit of only $403,000 on $539.6M of sales and a $1.26 loss per share. The opening question became explicitly about timing: "when the conventional shell egg market begins to rebalance" and when prepared foods "translate into greater earnings contribution". The story has contracted from "growth engines" to "two timing questions".

The thesis has not been abandoned, but it has moved from "the mix shift already protects us" (October 2025) to "the mix shift will protect us once it scales" (September 2026).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Diversification makes earnings "durable and predictable" (Jan 2026) | Quarterly operating income went $249M -> $124M -> $36M -> -$59M -> -$84M across five quarters (FMP). Fiscal 2026 EPS $6.63, down 73% from $24.95. | **Not yet true.** Earnings are still dominated by the conventional egg price. |
| Specialty eggs have "structurally stronger margins" (Apr 2026) | Specialty segment: $1.07B of sales and $182M operating profit in fiscal 2026 (about 17% margin) - but specialty prices fell 16.9% in Q3 FY26 and analysts flagged rising specialty promotion. | **Partly true.** Better than conventional, but not immune. |
| Prepared foods is a "high-margin growth platform" (Apr 2026) | $245M of sales and $34M operating profit in fiscal 2026 (about 14%). Small: under 10% of sales. Margins expected to dip again in Q2 FY27 on start-up costs. | **Plausible, unproven at scale.** |
| "Financially we're operating from a position of strength" (Oct 2025) | Cash and investments $767.6M, zero debt, equity $2.57B (about $55 per share) at 2026-08-29. But cash fell from $924M at 2026-05-30 in one quarter. | **True**, with a visible burn rate. |
| No demand destruction (every call) | NielsenIQ retail volume +4% calendar-year-to-date through August 2026; specialty +6%; exports +29% (Sep 2026 call). | **Corroborated by third-party data management cited.** |
| Hybrid / cost-plus pricing protects the downside (Apr 2026) | Conventional segment still lost $71M in Q1 FY27 (operating margin -35%). | **Weak protection at the trough.** |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining, then stabilising.** October 2025 was celebratory ("the strongest first quarter in our history"). By April 2026 the tone was explanatory ("price softness can create noise"). July 2026 was defensive but candid ("one of the most difficult conventional egg pricing environments we've experienced"). September 2026 was the most measured: "These indicators do not establish that the market will turn." That honesty is a credibility positive. The shift from offensive (acquisitions, growth engines) to defensive language (timing, rebalancing, digestion) is clear; Lombardo in September 2026: "We need to digest and build at a pace that supports long-term success."

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Cal-Maine gives no numerical earnings guidance, so there is little to miss. Operational guidance has been delivered: prepared-foods projects (pancake line, scrambled-egg consolidation) are on the stated schedule; the "progressive recovery beginning in Q4" for prepared foods (April 2026) was partly met - an analyst called Q1 FY27 prepared-foods profitability "pleasantly surprised" (Sep 2026). The screener shows earnings beat only 3 of 7 quarters (43%), which mostly reflects analysts mis-modelling an egg price nobody can forecast rather than management over-promising. **Reliability: Medium-High** on operations, **not applicable** on earnings.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Why have egg prices fallen so far?** (Heather Jones, Oct 2025: demand destruction or USDA undercounting?). Management blamed seasonality - but prices kept falling for three more quarters. The July 2026 call conceded the American Egg Board estimates the flock "materially above USDA's published estimate". Jones's question turned out to be the right one.
- **Specialty competition and promotions** (Ben Mayhew, Apr 2026): answered with "the first step is having supply" - a non-answer on pricing.
- **Buybacks at record-low price-to-book** (Jones, Sep 2026): the company bought "200-and-some thousand shares" after quarter end but only $5M in Q1 FY27, against a $768M cash pile. Management did not commit to more.
- **Feed and input costs** (Mayhew Apr 2026; Klieve Sep 2026) are rising (grain, fertilizer, fuel) - a margin squeeze on top of low egg prices.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Gross margin of 0.07% in Q1 FY27 - the conventional business is selling at or below cost.
- Red: Free cash flow of -$128M in Q1 FY27 (operating cash flow -$101M); continued burn into Q2 is likely given management's warning of prepared-foods start-up costs.
- Red: Insider selling - 14 open-market sells of about 1.31M shares versus 5 buys of 2,800 shares (screener live correction). Much of this is likely the founding family over a long period, but it is not conviction buying at the low.
- Red: Variable dividend (one-third of net income) has gone to zero during losses; income holders have no reason to stay.
- Green: No debt, $768M of cash and investments (about $16.40 per share), equity of about $55 per share.
- Green: Supply indicators turning: August hatch down about 12% year on year, flock estimate cut by about 4M birds, chick cancellations rising (Sep 2026 call, citing the American Egg Board).
- Green: Bird-flu (high-path avian influenza) season is starting; historically it has tightened supply sharply.
- Green: Mix shift is real - specialty plus prepared foods about 54% of Q1 FY27 sales, including about 12% prepared foods.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The move to three reporting segments in July 2026 is a tell: management wants investors to value specialty and prepared foods separately from conventional eggs. It also exposes how unprofitable conventional is at the trough.
- New voices (Lombardo, prepared-foods CFO John Zoeller) now take a large share of the call. Zoeller is explicitly declining to give margin guidance - prudent, but it means the "high-margin platform" claim has no number attached.
- The word "egg-centric" appears repeatedly in M&A answers (Jul and Sep 2026) - a deliberate signal against a diversifying, value-destroying acquisition.
- "Percent produced to sold" hit 98.2% in Q1 FY27, up from about 90% in January 2026: Cal-Maine has rebuilt its own flock and is now fully exposed to its own production at a low price.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning (PIVOTING).** The business is genuinely moving its mix, but the earnings base remains a commodity cycle. The single most important thing to weigh: **this is a cyclical-trough purchase, not a franchise at a discount.** The price is about 1.2x book value with about a quarter of the market value covered by cash; the risk is the timing of the egg-price recovery and the cash spent waiting, not solvency.

**Moat:** scale-cost and vertical integration (feed mills to delivery, about one in six US eggs). It is narrow but real: it does not lift prices in an oversupplied market, but it keeps Cal-Maine the last producer standing when weaker producers are forced to cut flocks. Returns are high-but-falling, yet the fall is cyclical (egg price), not structural - previous troughs (fiscal 2019-2021) recovered. Moat trend stable.

**Secular threat:** manageable. Bird flu is a recurring cyclical shock, not a terminal one; egg demand is growing (protein, weight-loss drug users), and plant-based egg substitutes have not dented volumes. The cheapness is a cyclical fear-print, not a structurally shrinking base - but the "cheapness" itself is modest once earnings are normalised.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.consensus_delta: The market prices PDD as if its profits are in terminal decline and its cash belongs to someone else. We think the first view is wrong and the second is half right. Profits: the Street has cut targets (the average target is 16% below a year ago; newest targets are $90 on 2026-11-09 and $93 on 2026-09-07), but core operating profit has already stabilized. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# PDD Holdings (PDD) - deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-16. Calls read: Q2 2025 (2025-08-26), Q3 2025 (2025-11-18), Q4/FY 2025 (2026-03-25), Q1 2026 (2026-05-27), Q2 2026 (2026-08-24). Financials from FMP filings (reported in Chinese yuan, RMB); the American depositary share (ADS) trades in US dollars on Nasdaq at $78.21 (2026-11-16), with USD/CNY at 6.65.*

**Data warning up front.** The screener's "fair value 417.5" and "margin of safety 429%" are a currency artifact: they multiply PDD's earnings per ADS in yuan (RMB 65.24 for FY2025) as if they were dollars. In dollars FY2025 earnings were roughly $9.80 per ADS and trailing-twelve-month (TTM) diluted earnings about RMB 62.5, or $9.40. Ignore the 429%. Also, the FMP transcript of the Q1 2026 call says revenue was "RMB 16.2 billion"; the filing says RMB 106.2 billion. That is a transcription error, not a restatement.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story has stayed the same for five quarters, and it is not a shareholder story. In every call management describes PDD as a platform with "social responsibility" that is spending its profits on merchants, farmers and the supply chain: first the RMB 10 billion fee-reduction program (August 2024), then the RMB 100 billion merchant support program (2025), and in March 2026 a new first-party brand company with "an initial cash injection of RMB 15 billion and plan to invest RMB 100 billion over the next few years" (Q1 2026). The goal is to "build another PDD over the next 3 years" (Q2 2026).

What changed is how much is being spent and on what. In 2025 the money went to fee cuts and coupons. In 2026 it moves into physical assets and new businesses: transit warehouses, "free shipping to villages" pickup points, a subsidiary in the Xiong'an New Area with an office building purchase, and data and service centers for traditional manufacturers. Temu, the overseas marketplace, went from a growth engine (2023-24) to something management mostly mentions as a source of "unforeseeable risks" from "trade policies, tax rules, data security and product compliance" (Q3 2025). In Q2 2026 management said the first-party brand rollout was "slower than expected due to certain external factors."

What was dropped: any mention of capital return. In five calls there is no buyback, no dividend and no word on how the cash pile will be used for shareholders.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS
| Claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Delivered solid results" (Q2 2026) | Revenue RMB 112.4B, up 8%; net income RMB 27.2B, down 12%. Operating income RMB 27.8B, **up 7.6%** from RMB 25.8B a year earlier | Partly true: operating profit has stopped falling; the drop in net income came from non-operating items |
| Investment "will affect ... revenue and net profit" (Q3 2025) | FY2025 net income RMB 97.8B, down 13% from RMB 112.4B; Q1 2026 net income RMB 12.5B (down about 59%); FMP-adjusted earnings per share $1.38 against a $2.40 estimate | Delivered exactly as warned. Management was honest about the damage |
| Margins under pressure | Gross margin by quarter: 55.9% (Q2'25), 56.7%, 55.5%, 55.9%, 57.3% (Q2'26). Operating margin: 24.8% in Q2'25, 24.7% in Q2'26 | After the 2024-25 compression, margins **stabilized** in 2026. Q1 2026 (18.4% operating margin) was the low point |
| Program "beginning to yield tangible results" (Q2 2026) | Support is backed by anecdotes (pineapples, lighting makers), not metrics. Revenue growth went from 7% (Q2'25) to 9% (Q3'25), 12% (Q4'25), 11% (Q1'26) and 8% (Q2'26) | Not proven. Some revenue was regained, then slowed again |
| Fortress balance sheet | Cash and short-term investments RMB 456.4B (2026-06-30); total debt RMB 4.8B (all leases); about RMB 109.9B payable to merchants and RMB 76.9B in accrued liabilities | Real, but RMB 110B of it is merchant float (money owed to merchants), not owner cash |

TTM free cash flow is RMB 111.9B, about $16.8B, roughly $11.40 per diluted ADS. That is about 6.9 times FCF at $78.21. Part of it is growth in merchant float, so treat that figure as a ceiling.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Stable, deliberately defensive.** Every call carries the same disclaimer: "simple linear projection might not be a good way to projecting future performance" (Q3 2025), "our financial results of this quarter should not be considered as guidance" (Q3 2025), "we cannot rule out the possibility that the financial performance in the next few quarters will continue to fluctuate." Q2 2026 is a little more upbeat ("a new phase ... deeper execution", "overall momentum remains positive"), but the main topic shifted to platform governance: 150 trust and safety measures, a ban on freshly prepared food, and live-stream rules. That reads like a response to regulators.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Management gives no numerical guidance, so there is nothing to miss. The qualitative warnings were accurate: profits fell when they said they would. Against Street estimates the record is uneven: beats in Q2 and Q3 2025 ($3.08 vs $1.91; $2.96 vs $2.21), misses in Q4 2025 ($2.53 vs $2.98) and badly in Q1 2026 ($1.38 vs $2.40), then a beat in Q2 2026 ($2.85 vs $2.72). The screener's beat rate of 4 of 7 quarters (57%) fits. Reliability: **Medium.** The words are honest, but the numbers swing widely by design, and management says so.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- **Return on the investment.** Analysts asked in Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 how management thinks about "the investment and return cycle" and whether merchant health will lead to more ad spending. The answers were anecdotes and "over time ... the platform's intrinsic value will naturally follow." No timetable and no return target.
- **Quick commerce / instant retail.** Management declined to compete ("limited scope for synergies", Q2 2026). That is disciplined, but it leaves the fastest-growing part of Chinese retail to Meituan, Alibaba and JD.
- **Temu and regulation.** Analysts keep asking; management keeps describing a "complex global environment" without numbers. Temu's profitability is never disclosed.
- **Capital return.** None of the five calls includes a question or an answer on this, which says a lot about how analysts read the company.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: net income fell 13% in FY2025 and 59% in Q1 2026; the investment program is open-ended, with a second RMB 100B commitment (Q1 2026).
- Red: no buyback or dividend while the company holds about $68B of gross cash; minority owners have no lever to get at it.
- Red: the finance chief was on medical leave (Q3 2025). An independent director died (Q2 2026). There is a co-CEO/co-chair structure, and governance is opaque.
- Red: Temu regulatory exposure continues; the Texas data-privacy settlement on 2026-10-16 (Reuters) is one dated example.
- Red: insiders made 0 open-market buys and 3 small sales.
- Green: operating income rose 7.6% year on year in Q2 2026 and gross margin was the highest in five quarters (57.3%).
- Green: almost no debt, ROIC around 19% and ROE around 26% even after the investment program.
- Green: management avoids a cash-burning quick-commerce fight.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
Since the 10th anniversary the language has moved from "consumers" to "the industry", "society" and "traditional manufacturing", which fits Beijing's "common prosperity" and supply-chain-upgrade priorities. The Xiong'an subsidiary (a state-favored development zone) and the "data processing service center for traditional industries" look like policy alignment as much as commercial investment. In practice part of PDD's cash is going to purposes the state supports. That lowers regulatory risk but limits what the cash is worth to a foreign shareholder.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT
**Trajectory: PIVOTING**, from a high-margin consumer marketplace toward a capital-heavy supply-chain and first-party brand operator that spends its cash on policy-aligned goals. The core marketplace still earns about RMB 95-100B a year in operating profit.

**The most important thing for the director:** the stock trades at about 3 times enterprise value to operating profit (EV/EBIT) because the market gives little value to RMB 450B of cash that has never been returned and is now being committed to new programs. The value case depends on how much of that cash you count. If you count it at face value, PDD is very cheap. If you treat it as locked inside the company, the business at about 7 times operating profit is only modestly cheap.

**Moat.** A network and scale-cost moat: a two-sided marketplace with hundreds of millions of price-sensitive buyers, plus agricultural and industrial-belt supply relationships. Width is **narrow, but real**. Returns are high (ROIC about 19%), but they fell from the 2023-24 peak as margins compressed. In 2026 gross and operating margins stopped falling, so the trend is **stable**, not eroding. **Secular threat: manageable.** Douyin and Kuaishou live-commerce, instant retail and Temu tariff/de minimis rules are competitive and regulatory pressures, not a force that would shrink the business toward zero. The cheapness is mostly a governance and China-risk discount, not a shrinking-base value trap.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# COSCO SHIPPING Holdings (1919.HK) - deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16. Prices in Hong Kong dollars (H-share listing 1919.HK, HK$17.29 on 2026-11-16 per FMP); company accounts are in Chinese yuan (RMB). FX used: 1 HKD = 0.8492 RMB (FMP, 2026-11-16).*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript is bundled, FMP carries no transcript for this listing, and COSCO SHIPPING Holdings (China's state-controlled container line, which also owns most of Orient Overseas/OOCL and a stake in COSCO SHIPPING Ports) does not publish a full English call transcript. This deep dive therefore works from the company's dated results announcements as reported by the trade press (gCaptain 2026-10-29, FreightWaves, Baird Maritime), its HKEX dividend and buyback filings (2026-08-28 interim dividend announcement; spring-2026 H-share buyback returns), FMP statements (balance sheet at 2026-06-30), and the screener's financial trajectory. No management quotes are reproduced because none could be verified verbatim.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **2021-22 (pandemic windfall):** revenue peaked at RMB391B and net profit at RMB110B in 2022 as freight rates went vertical. Management built a very large cash pile and began paying out up to 50% of profits.
- **2023 (normalisation):** revenue halved to RMB175B, net profit fell 78% to RMB24B. The story shifted to "cost discipline, fleet renewal and shareholder returns".
- **2024 (Red Sea):** Houthi attacks forced Asia-Europe ships around the Cape of Good Hope, absorbing capacity; profit doubled to RMB49B.
- **2025 (fade):** rates eased, profit fell to RMB31B (Q3 2025 attributable RMB9.53B, down 55% year on year). Buybacks of H shares started under a May-2025 mandate.
- **2026 (a second shock):** after 2026-02-28 a Middle East war closed the Strait of Hormuz; Asia-US West Coast spot rates were 343% above their February level in October (Xeneta via FreightWaves, 2026-11-09). H1 2026 attributable profit was RMB13.39B (down from RMB17.53B), then Q3 2026 jumped 81% year on year to RMB17.23B (gCaptain 2026-10-29), nine-month profit RMB30.65B, up 13%. The narrative is once again "geopolitics supports rates", which is a borrowed tailwind, not a franchise change.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / storyline | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Strong balance sheet | Cash RMB141.6B vs debt RMB71.6B incl. RMB30.6B leases at 2026-06-30 = net cash RMB70B. But RMB51.5B of equity belongs to minorities (mainly OOIL), so roughly 82% of that cash is attributable (~RMB57B, ~HK$4.4/share) | Matches, with a minority haircut |
| Shareholder returns 30-50% of profit | Interim 2026 dividend RMB0.43/share, ~49% payout, paid 2026-10-23; H-share buybacks (14.45M shares by early May 2026, cancelled) | Matches; buybacks are token in size (~0.1% of shares) |
| Q3 rebound reflects operating strength | Q3 volumes +4.5% (7.21M TEU) but revenue +29% and EBIT +70%: the rebound is mostly price, i.e. war-driven rates | Narrative richer than the franchise justifies |
| Cheap on earnings | Trailing attributable EPS about RMB2.26 (HK$2.66) = ~6.5x; P/B about 0.96x on RMB15.31 book per share | True on trailing numbers, misleading on through-cycle numbers |
| Screener "beat 3 of 4 quarters" | Carriers give no numeric guidance; "beats" are against sell-side estimates that chase spot rates | Low information value |

FMP's quarterly line items for this name are internally inconsistent (e.g. the "Q2 2026" row shows H1 revenue and H1 profit; Q4 2025 cost of revenue duplicates Q1 2026). Use the company's half-year and quarterly announcements, not the FMP quarter split.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Stable.** Without transcripts, tone is read from disclosure behaviour: the company keeps paying at the top of its 30-50% range, kept a modest buyback running and sought a renewed 10% repurchase mandate at its 2026 AGM. That is the behaviour of a management that expects the cash to keep coming but does not want to commit to large structural returns - consistent with a state-controlled carrier that also funds a large newbuilding programme.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
COSCO gives no quantitative earnings guidance. The one dated commitment we can test, the 30-50% payout, was delivered (49% at the 2026 interim). Reliability: **Medium** - honest about policy, but the policy itself is discretionary and the controlling shareholder's priorities (fleet, national logistics) rank alongside minority returns.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- How much of 2026 profit is the Hormuz/Red Sea disruption, and what happens when capacity returns? Xeneta forecasts 2027 spot rates about 30% below Q3 2026 and contract rates about 5% lower, with fleet capacity growing 6.8% against demand of 2.5-4% (FreightWaves 2026-11-09).
- Orderbook and decarbonisation capex (dual-fuel newbuilds) versus the payout.
- Bunker fuel is up about 107% since February 2026; recovery via surcharges lags.
- US policy risk on Chinese-built/operated ships (port fees were suspended, per Lloyd's List, but can return).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: Q3 2026 profit growth is price, not volume (revenue +29% vs volume +4.5%).
- Red: the industry orderbook is large; a reopening of Hormuz and a full return to Suez would release capacity into a market already forecast to be in surplus in 2027.
- Red: minority interests take ~18% of equity and ~10% of profit; headline net cash overstates what H-shareholders own.
- Green: genuine net cash, no refinancing risk, dividend paid on schedule (2026-10-23).
- Green: shares trade around book value with a ~6.5x trailing P/E; downside in a normal down-cycle is cushioned by book and cash.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The H share (HK$17.29 = RMB14.68) trades only ~15% below the A share (RMB17.25), a narrower gap than COSCO's usual H discount; the H line is not unusually cheap on that measure.
- Buybacks are concentrated in H shares, a small signal that management sees the H line as the cheaper one.
- The stock is 74% up its 52-week range and 9% above its 200-day average: the market already pays for part of the war windfall.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
**Trajectory: STABLE** - a cyclical upswing on a geopolitical shock, not a structural improvement. The single most important thing to weigh: current earnings are inflated by a dated, reversible disruption (Hormuz closure from 2026-02-28 plus partial Red Sea avoidance); valuing the company on trailing profit is valuing the war.

**Moat:** liner shipping is a commodity service; COSCO's scale (top-4 carrier, OCEAN Alliance, terminal stakes) gives some cost benefit but no pricing power - returns swing from ~4% to 40%+ ROE purely with freight rates. Moat: none in the durable sense; trend stable (cyclical, not eroding). **Secular threat:** manageable - decarbonisation capex, tariff-driven trade shifts and US measures against Chinese shipping are real but do not impair terminal value. The cheapness is neither a fear-print nor a value trap: it is a fair price for a cyclical at a cyclical high.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · no real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
