| Growth recovers in the second half | Q3 2026 revenue RMB 97.9B (+34% year on year), attributable profit RMB 5.40B (+16%), operating profit RMB 5.99B, the best quarter on record. | Matches |
| Strong balance sheet, net cash | Cash plus short-term investments RMB 122.9B against borrowings and leases of RMB 13.0B at 2026-09-30, so net cash of about RMB 110B. But trade and bills payable alone are RMB 158.8B, and liabilities are 79% of assets. Receivables, inventory and prepayments total about RMB 117B against roughly RMB 226B of operating liabilities. | Partly - the cash is mostly supplier credit, not spare money |
| Free cash flow | FY2024 free cash flow (cash from operations minus capital spending) RMB 41.9B, inflated by a RMB 25.5B rise in payables; FY2025 RMB 12.9B. Our feed shows zero for the last four quarters, which is a missing-data gap, not a real zero. | Unverified for 2026 |

The pattern is the usual one for Chinese carmakers: the headline cash pile is funded by paying suppliers slowly. That float is stable while volumes grow, but it would shrink if volumes fell or if Beijing's 2025 push for carmakers to pay suppliers within 60 days is enforced harder.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable to rising. The interim report talks of the company continuing to "advance its global expansion" and that it "will expand its product lineup, strengthen brand positioning and increase investment" - offensive language, backed by research spending up 28% in the first half and up again in Q3 (RMB 4.37B). There is no defensive turn toward cost-cutting. Note that we cannot judge how management answers hard questions, because no call transcript is available.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Chery gives no formal profit guidance. The group set a 2025 export target and beat it, and in 2026 group exports to October (1.75M, up 65%) already exceeded the whole of 2025. Delivery on volume ambitions is good. Profit delivery is lumpier: earnings per share fell in H1 2026 on lower currency gains before recovering in Q3. Reliability: Medium.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without a transcript we infer them from broker notes and the numbers: (1) the domestic collapse - October domestic volume down close to 40% - and whether price cuts at home will follow; (2) the share of profit coming from currency gains, interest and joint ventures; (3) trade-policy risk on the export engine (tariffs, local-content rules, Russia's rising recycling fees, currency swings), which GF Securities lists first among its risks; (4) the payables float and supplier-payment rules.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: domestic sales down roughly 40% year on year in October 2026 (group data, 2026-11-01).
- Red: non-operating income was about RMB 7.4B of the last four quarters' RMB 18.5B net profit (Q4 2025 to Q3 2026), and the currency-gain part of that will not repeat.
- Red: liabilities at about 79% of assets; the net cash rests on RMB 159B of payables.
- Red: the 12-month IPO lock-up for pre-listing holders ended about 2026-09-25 (secondary source, not checked against the prospectus). The shares have since fallen to a 52-week low (HK$21.74).
- Green: gross margin up three points in a year on export mix, now 16.3% (Q3 2026).
- Green: Q3 2026 operating profit RMB 5.99B, up about 38% year on year; borrowings cut from RMB 15.9B to about RMB 9B during 2026.
- Green: exports up about 59% in October 2026, new-energy sales over 100,000 a month for seven months running.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The reporting emphasis has shifted from "five brands" and domestic share to overseas plants (three of twelve major bases are now abroad) and new-energy revenue mix. Petrol-car revenue is shrinking fast at home and being replaced abroad, which makes Chery a bet that emerging markets keep buying Chinese cars for longer than China itself does. Joint-venture income fell 38% in the first half, a quiet sign that the legacy partnerships matter less.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning, from a domestic carmaker to an export-led one. The single most important thing to weigh: the stock looks like it trades at about the value of its cash (market value about RMB 110B against net cash of about RMB 110B), but that cash is supplier credit. Value it on earnings, not on the cash pile. On earnings it costs about 6 times this year's expected profit, which is cheap but not free for a business whose profit depends on export trade policy.

Moat: narrow, from scale and cost. Chery is one of the lowest-cost car producers in the world, and returns are rising (gross margin up, return on equity high on a thin equity base, return on invested capital about 9%). It has no pricing power at home. Secular threat: manageable. The shift to electric cars is the force that could hurt a petrol-heavy maker, but Chery's new-energy share is rising fast (41% of revenue), so the cheapness looks more like fear of the Chinese car sector, export tariffs and share overhang than a shrinking business.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Trailing earnings per share of about 48,600 won puts the stock near 5 times earnings, against a book value of about 210,000 won per share. Backlog fills yard and engine slots through 2028, so profits over the next two years are largely locked in by ships already ordered at good prices; customer prepayments of 14.6 trillion won (2026-06-30) corroborate that. The engine and machinery business (Q3 margin 24.2%) and Marine Engine (record 28.5% margin) give a second earnings pillar that management is extending into onshore power generation (1.5 GW of capacity in 2028, 3 GW in 2029), partly independent of the ship cycle. Dividends are flowing up the chain: HD Hyundai Heavy's Q2 2026 dividend was 6,090 won per share, about 3.6 times a year earlier, and its policy targets at least 30% of standalone net income. The whole Korean shipbuilding sector has been cut roughly in half from its 2026 highs on fears that the order cycle has peaked and China is taking share, so sentiment is already washed out; any U.S. naval progress (the December conference version of the U.S. defense authorization bill, the HD Hyundai-Kiewit U.S. yard joint venture due to be finalized by year-end 2026) or continued Korean governance reform that narrows holding-company discounts could re-rate both the subsidiaries and the parent's discount at once. Conditions: subsidiary margins hold through 2027-2028 deliveries, the won does not strengthen sharply further, and the parent does not keep diverting cash into group expansion.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness has two durable reasons. First, Korean holding companies have traded at large discounts to the value of their stakes for decades, because cash and decisions sit in the subsidiaries and the parent serves the controlling group's needs; HD KSOE illustrated this in May 2026 by issuing a zero-coupon 1.55 billion dollar (about 2.37 trillion won) exchangeable bond backed by 4.32% of HD Hyundai Heavy to fund group expansion in India, the U.S. and the Philippines, rather than returning cash. Today's roughly 44% discount to the market value of its holdings is close to its historical range, so the stock may simply track the subsidiaries rather than re-rate. Second, the subsidiaries themselves may be near peak earnings: the screener flags margins about 2.1 standard deviations above their historical peak, Chinese yards won about 76% of global orders in January-September 2026 versus Korea's 15% (Clarksons), Chinese yards have won 32 LNG carriers this year in what was a Korean stronghold, LNG carrier prices have fallen, and Clarksons expects global orders to drop about 30% in 2027. Earnings from 2029 onward depend on orders being written now at lower prices. The company also proved in 2021 how fragile its margins are to cost inflation on fixed-price contracts: gross margin went from 6.5% in 2019 to minus 3.3% in 2021, and the current reflationary backdrop plus a fresh wage settlement (2026-10-27, about 41 million won of benefits per union member) and a stronger won (about 6% in Q3, costing roughly 70 billion won of operating profit) squeeze the margin from both sides. The free-cash-flow multiple of 3.2 times is inflated by customer prepayments that will be consumed as ships are built. The U.S. naval story that lifted the stock has produced no HD Hyundai order, and combat ships now need 'further discussion'. If HD Hyundai Heavy de-rates to 7-8 times peak-ish earnings and Samho to 6 times, while the holding discount widens to 50-55%, the stock could fall to about 160,000 won. What would confirm the bear case: further Chinese LNG carrier wins at lower prices, a falling backlog, Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 margins below 15%, or further parent-level capital raising.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing HD KSOE as if the shipbuilding up-cycle is over and the holding discount is permanent. Where we disagree: the next two years of earnings are largely contracted (backlog and engine slots through 2028, 14.6 trillion won of customer prepayments), and Q3 2026 operating profit still grew 37% year on year, so the de-rating is a bet on 2029-onward order prices, not on near-term earnings. At about 5 times trailing attributable earnings and below the value of its HD Hyundai Heavy stake alone, the stock already discounts a meaningful down-cycle. Where the market is probably right: the holding-company discount is structural in Korea and the parent is still being used to fund group expansion (the 2.37 trillion won exchangeable bond in May 2026), and China's push into LNG carriers is real. The disagreement is therefore modest in size: our base fair value of 285,000 won is about 19% above today's price, not a deep mispricing.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): Q4 2026 still carries the remaining 25-30% of the annual wage cost booked after the October settlement; a further strengthening of the won would hit both operating profit and the non-operating FX line (Q3 net income fell 51% from Q2 to 777 billion won largely on FX losses); 2027 order intake is forecast to drop about 30% globally and each Chinese LNG carrier win reinforces the peak narrative; a December 2026 U.S. defense bill without an overseas-construction provision would remove the last near-term sentiment support. There is no debt maturity or liquidity risk: the group has about 10 trillion won of net cash and the parent's exchangeable bond carries no interest. The risk is a further sector de-rating, not a solvency event.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is mostly spent but not absent. The sector was a crowded momentum and theme trade (U.S. naval cooperation, shipbuilding exchange-traded funds such as KODEX Shipbuilding TOP 10 and SOL Shipbuilding TOP 3 Plus), and those holders have already sold the stock down about 50% from its high, to within about 6% of its 52-week low of 224,500 won and about 35% below its 200-day average. Further theme-fund outflows on bad sector news could push it a little lower, which is a sector-wide sell-off rather than forced selling specific to this company. There is no yield-holder base to dump on a dividend cut; dividends are rising.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near 235,000 won, which the ongoing sector-wide sell-off in Korean shipbuilders could deliver. The thesis holds. HD KSOE is the holding company for the HD Hyundai shipbuilding group, its earnings are still rising on a backlog that runs through 2028 (Q3 2026 operating profit up 37% year on year; nine-month profit already above last year's record), and at 239,000 won its market value is below the value of its HD Hyundai Heavy stake alone. But two things keep this from being a buy at today's price. First, most of the apparent discount is the long-standing Korean holding-company discount, which tends to persist, and the parent is still raising money for group expansion rather than returning it. Second, the subsidiaries are earning near-peak margins while China takes order share and global orders are forecast to fall about 30% in 2027. Marking the subsidiaries at today's prices, valuing Samho on about 8.5 times earnings and applying a 35% holding discount gives a fair value near 285,000 won, about 19% above today's price, just short of the 20% margin we require in the current reflationary backdrop. The level we name is within about 2% of today's price, so this is close to actionable; the catalysts (the U.S. yard joint venture, the U.S. defense bill, a richer dividend) are real but soft, and none is needed for the value case. The business case scores a middling 3: real earnings and real cash, but cyclical peak risk and a structural discount that may never close.
picks.forcing_function: No single hard date. Candidates, all soft: finalization of the HD Hyundai-Kiewit U.S. yard joint venture by year-end 2026; the December 2026 conference text of the FY2027 U.S. defense authorization bill; Q4 2026 results and the year-end dividend decision (around late January to February 2027), where a higher payout from the parent would chip at the holding discount; any Korean governance measure that forces treasury-share cancellation or penalizes double listings. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (009540.KS) — a deep dive on management and the setup

Prepared 2026-11-16. Price used: 239,000 won (Korea Exchange, FMP live quote, 2026-11-16). Market value about 16.9 trillion won on roughly 70.8 million shares.

**Source note.** FMP has no earnings-call transcript for this listing. This dossier rests on the Q3 2026 results release (reported 2026-10-28 via Korea JoongAng Daily and BizWatch), a third-party summary of the Q3 2026 earnings call (Investing.com), FMP quarterly statements to 2026-09-30, and Korean press on the group's ownership and dividends. Only one quarter of call commentary was available, so the quarter-by-quarter tone tracking the template asks for is necessarily thin; where a claim cannot be dated to a quarter, it is flagged.

**What this company is.** HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE) is the intermediate holding company (a parent whose main assets are stakes in other companies) for the HD Hyundai shipbuilding group. It owns about 69.2% of HD Hyundai Heavy Industries (listed, and since December 2025 merged with HD Hyundai Mipo), about 96.7% of HD Hyundai Samho (unlisted), about 35% of HD Hyundai Marine Engine (listed) and a majority stake in HD Hyundai Energy Solution (listed). HD Hyundai, the group apex company, owns about 35% of HD KSOE. The screener's "industrials / aerospace" tag is a mislabel; this is a shipbuilding holding company.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has moved through three stages over the last two years:

- **2024 to 2025: the price-recovery story.** Ships ordered at much higher prices from 2022 onward began to reach the income statement. Net income went from a loss of 929 billion won (2021) to a profit of 2.17 trillion won (2025) on revenue that doubled from 15.5 to 31.2 trillion won.
- **2025 to early 2026: the U.S. naval and "MASGA" story** (the Korea-U.S. shipbuilding cooperation framework). This added a re-rating narrative on top of earnings: U.S. Navy repair and construction work, a U.S. shipyard, nuclear-powered submarines. The stock peaked near 488,000 won within the last year.
- **Mid-2026 to now: the "past the peak" fear.** Clarksons data show Chinese yards won about 76% of global orders in January-September 2026 versus Korea's 15%, and Chinese yards (Hudong, Jiangnan, Hengli) have won 32 liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers year to date, a Korean stronghold. The U.S. naval story has produced no HD Hyundai order yet. The stock has roughly halved (down 49.8% from the 2026 high as of 2026-10-28), alongside Hanwha Ocean (down about 65%) and Samsung Heavy (down about 52%).

What management now emphasizes (Q3 2026 call): record profitability, backlog that fills slots through 2028, the engine business as a second earnings pillar (engine utilization "already exceeded 110%"), and the Kiewit joint venture for a U.S. yard, with structure to be finalized by year-end 2026. What has quietly moved down the list: combat-vessel work for the U.S. Navy now "needs further discussion"; the initial U.S. targets are logistics ships.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Profitability is at record levels and still rising | Operating profit (profit from operations before interest and tax) for January-September 2026 was 4.45 trillion won, already above the record full-year 2025 figure of 3.9 trillion. Q3 2026 operating margin 17.5%, versus 13.9% a year earlier. | Matches |
| The quarter's dip was temporary (strong won, fewer working days, front-loaded wage costs) | Q3 operating profit fell 12% from Q2 to 1.447 trillion won. Management quantified about 70 billion won from the won and about 50 billion from 14 fewer working days; wage costs from the 2026-10-27 settlement (147 days of talks, 11 partial strikes) were mostly booked in Q3. These explain most of the gap. | Plausible, partly verified |
| Backlog is strong and orders beat target | Group yards booked 176 vessels worth $19.1 billion through Q3, above the full-year target. Customer prepayments (contract liabilities) on the balance sheet were 14.6 trillion won at 2026-06-30, up from 14.1 trillion at 2026-03-31, which corroborates a growing backlog. | Matches |
| Newbuild prices "continue to rise" | Not independently verified. Management conceded LNG carrier prices have fallen, partly due to Chinese competition. Clarksons expects 2027 global orders to fall about 30%. | Mixed: true for some ship types, not for LNG |
| Strong cash generation | Trailing twelve-month free cash flow (cash from operations minus capital spending) of about 5.2 trillion won is real, but shipbuilding cash flow is flattered by customer prepayments: cash arrives ahead of the work. A P/FCF (price to free cash flow) of 3.2x overstates the sustainable cash yield. | Overstated by the contract structure |
| Net cash of about 11 trillion won | Consolidated balance sheet at 2026-06-30: cash and short-term investments 13.59 trillion, total debt 3.48 trillion, so net cash about 10.1 trillion. But most of that cash sits inside subsidiaries with minority holders, and much of it is customer prepayments owed back as work. The parent itself issued a zero-coupon $1.55 billion (about 2.37 trillion won) exchangeable bond in May 2026, backed by 4.32% of HD Hyundai Heavy. | True at group level, much less at the parent |

Two screener figures are artifacts and should be ignored: the return on invested capital of minus 17.9% and the Altman Z-score (a bankruptcy-risk score) of 1.8. Both are distorted by the holding-company structure and by the large customer prepayments that sit as liabilities. Return on equity of 3.5% is likewise stale; trailing earnings per share is about 48,600 won against book value per share of about 210,000 won, which is a return on equity above 20%.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Rating: **Stable**, on thin evidence (one call summary). Management in the Q3 2026 call is confident about the backlog and the engine business and is specific with numbers (FX impact, working-day impact, engine capacity of 1.5 GW in 2028 and 3 GW in 2029 for onshore power generation). The tone on China is defensive rather than dismissive: they argue reliability, supply-chain stability and port access, not price. On the U.S. venture, the language is cautious: the ownership split (reported as about 60/40) and total investment are "not yet final."

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Orders through Q3 beat the full-year target, and nine-month profit already beat the prior record year. The screener records 4 earnings beats in the last 7 quarters (57%), and Q3 2026 was a small miss (earnings per share about 2% below consensus, revenue about 2% below). The pattern is delivery on the big picture with small quarter-to-quarter noise from currency and labor. Reliability: **Medium-High**.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **China in LNG carriers.** Analysts pressed on the 32 Chinese LNG carrier orders; management's answer was qualitative.
- **2027 order decline.** The Clarksons forecast of roughly 30% fewer orders in 2027 was raised; management said volumes would remain "well above historical averages" without a number.
- **U.S. naval timing.** No order, no final structure for the Kiewit venture; nuclear submarine legislation pending, with a first budget not expected before 2027.
- **Currency.** A roughly 6% stronger won in Q3 cut operating profit and produced a large non-operating FX loss (net income fell 51% from Q2 to 777 billion won).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: China's share of global orders (76% in January-September 2026) and its entry into LNG carriers threatens the highest-margin Korean product.
- Red: The screener flags margins 2.1 standard deviations above their historical peak. Some of today's profit is cycle-peak pricing on ships ordered in 2022-2024.
- Red: Holding-company structure. The parent's value depends on subsidiaries with their own minority shareholders; the parent raised a 2.37 trillion won exchangeable bond in May 2026 to fund overseas expansion rather than returning cash.
- Red: Inflation sensitivity. In 2021 the gross margin went from 6.5% (2019) to minus 3.3% as steel costs rose on fixed-price contracts.
- Green: Profit growth is broad-based in Q3 2026: Samho operating profit up 56% year on year to 479 billion won; engines and machinery margin 24.2%; Marine Engine margin a record 28.5%; offshore back to profit.
- Green: Dividends from HD Hyundai Heavy to the parent have scaled sharply (Q2 2026 HHI dividend of 6,090 won per share, about 3.6 times a year earlier), funding the parent's own dividend.
- Green: Labor settled on 2026-10-27, removing the strike overhang for 2026.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The engine business is now pitched as a power-generation and data-center supplier, not just a marine supplier, a deliberate attempt to decouple part of the earnings from the ship cycle.
- U.S. ambitions are framed around "local manufacturing footprint" with Kiewit, which implies capital commitment by the group before any orders.
- The parent is now a funding vehicle for group expansion (India, the U.S., the Philippines) via the exchangeable bond, which is the classic reason Korean holding companies trade at a discount.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: **STABLE**. Earnings are still rising on a backlog that runs through 2028, but the order cycle that will feed 2029-2030 is weakening and China is taking share.

The single most important thing to weigh: **the holding-company discount.** At 239,000 won, HD KSOE's market value of about 16.9 trillion won is below the market value of its stake in HD Hyundai Heavy alone (69.2% of about 28.3 trillion won, or about 19.6 trillion), before counting Samho (which earned 479 billion won of operating profit in Q3 alone), the engine stakes and the parent's other assets. The investor is buying the group's earnings at roughly 5 times trailing attributable profit. The question is whether that discount closes (Korean corporate-governance reforms, higher payouts) or merely persists while the cycle turns.

**Moat.** Scale-cost and technology in high-value ships (LNG carriers, dual-fuel container ships, gas carriers) and engines. Width: narrow. Margins and returns are rising, not falling, so this is not an eroding moat on the evidence, but China's LNG wins are the first real test of it. **Secular threat:** Chinese state-backed capacity is a material competitive threat to pricing and share, but not a terminal one: Korean yards still win most high-spec and U.S.-allied orders. The cheapness is mostly a fear-print about the cycle peak plus a structural holding-company discount, not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

# DBC.WA - Firma Oponiarska Debica S.A. (Tire Company Debica) - a deep dive on management and the setup
As of 2026-11-09. Price 88.90 PLN (FMP quote, Warsaw listing DBC.WA, 2026-11-09). Market value about PLN 1.23B on 13.8M shares.

Sources: FMP quarterly and annual statements (through Q2 2026, quarter ended 2026-06-30); Warsaw exchange current reports (ESPI) as carried by Bankier.pl: the 2026-09-16 loan agreement with Goodyear S.A., the 2026-10-29 preliminary nine-month 2026 estimate, the 2026-11-04 notice of articles-of-association changes, and the dividend calendar. No earnings-call transcript exists for this name (Polish majority-owned subsidiaries rarely hold calls) and the web-search budget for this run was exhausted, so there are no management quotes here - none are invented.

## 1. What the company actually is
Debica is Poland's largest tyre plant and an 87.25%-owned subsidiary of Goodyear S.A. (Luxembourg), itself owned by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company. In substance it is a captive contract manufacturer: the large majority of its output is sold to Goodyear group companies at prices Goodyear sets (transfer pricing, the internal prices one group company charges another). That is why gross margin is only about 5-7% of sales - the plant earns a cost-plus return, not a brand margin. Minority shareholders (12.75% free float, thin trading of about 2,500 shares a day) own a slice of a cash-rich factory whose profit is set by its parent.

## 2. Financial trajectory (PLN)
- Revenue: 2.34B (2021), 3.28B (2022), 2.99B (2023), 2.52B (2024), 2.91B (2025). Nine months of 2026: 2.13B (2026-10-29 estimate) vs about 2.28B a year earlier - down about 7%.
- Net income: 43M, 73M, 284M (2023, inflated by one-offs), 78M, 125M (2025, EPS 9.06). Nine months 2026: 67.2M estimate, implying Q3 2026 of only about 9.8M against 40.7M in Q3 2025 - a fall of roughly three-quarters.
- Quarterly gross margin: 6.5% (Q1 25), 6.5% (Q2 25), 6.5% (Q3 25), 2.0% (Q4 25), 5.9% (Q1 26), 3.9% (Q2 26). The trend is down in 2026.
- Free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) was negative in every year 2021-2025: -41M, -189M, -21M, -318M (2024, a heavy capacity programme of 538M capex), -33M.
- Balance sheet (2026-06-30): equity 1.40B (about 101 PLN per share, so the stock trades near 0.88 times book value), no bank debt, leases 6M. Cash 110M plus intercompany loans to Goodyear S.A.

## 3. Cross-check of the narrative against the numbers
Management's only stated reason for the 2026 slide (2026-10-29 estimate) is lower prices realised on sales to related parties and a difficult macro backdrop. That is consistent with the numbers: volumes and revenue fell only mid-single-digits, but profit fell much more, which is what a cut in the transfer price looks like. The point for an outside owner: the profit line is a parent decision, not a market outcome, and in 2026 the parent chose to keep more of the margin itself.

## 4. Capital allocation and related-party exposure
- Debica lends its spare cash to its parent. On 2026-09-16 it signed a new PLN 150M one-year loan to Goodyear S.A. (WIBOR 1Y + 0.45%, 4.37% at signing, matures 2027-09-17, guaranteed by The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company), rolling an earlier 150M loan; total loans to Goodyear are PLN 600M of principal - about 43 PLN per share, or roughly half the share price.
- These loans earn a thin margin over WIBOR and are an unsecured-in-practice exposure to a parent group whose credit is below investment grade, backed by the parent's own guarantee. They are liquid in name (early repayment can be requested) but in practice a minority cannot force recall.
- Dividends: 6.79 PLN per share for 2025 (about 94M, a 7.6% yield at today's price), payable 2026-12-17 per the exchange calendar. Equity fell from 1.47B to 1.40B in Q2 2026 despite a profit, consistent with the dividend already booked as a liability; it has not yet been paid.
- 2026-11-04: amendments to the articles of association were registered (content not verified in this run).

## 5. Forensic quality
Clean in the narrow sense: no debt, no dilution (share count 13.80M for years), timely preliminary estimates. The accounting quality concern is structural, not fraud: reported profit is set by intercompany pricing, and cash is recycled to the parent. Persistent negative free cash flow alongside a growing loan book to the parent means the cash on the balance sheet has been sustained by working-capital swings and earlier profits rather than by today's operations.

## 6. Governance and the minority
Goodyear controls the board and pricing. Goodyear is mid-way through its own cost and asset programme; a buy-out of the 12.75% minority would be cheap for it, but nothing has been announced and no date or terms exist. That possibility is a real but undated option, not a catalyst.

## 7. What would change the picture
- Full Q3 2026 report on 2026-11-19: confirms whether the Q3 collapse is pricing (recoverable when the parent resets) or volume (structural).
- FY2026 results (around March 2027) and any 2027 transfer-price reset.
- Any squeeze-out or tender by Goodyear.
- Any change in the size or terms of the parent loans.

## 8. Bottom line
A cash-backed, below-book tyre plant whose earnings and cash deployment are controlled by a stretched parent. Roughly 51 PLN per share of the 88.90 price is financial assets (loans to Goodyear plus cash, including the pending dividend); the remaining ~38 PLN buys a factory that is earning less each quarter in 2026. The value is real but the minority has no lever to unlock it.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · no real moat.

Conch is still profitable at the bottom while China Resources Building Materials has guided to a loss, which is exactly the positioning that wins a consolidation. Cash generation runs far above reported profit because depreciation is about CNY 8B a year: Q3 operating cash flow actually rose 11.8% to CNY 3.15B. China's cement demand has fallen five years running with property construction, so this is a shrinking base, not just a cyclical dip; 'intensifying competition' (interim report, 2026-08-26) means smaller kilns are undercutting price, the opposite of discipline. The company's margins were also squeezed in the last inflation (gross margin 33.3% in 2019 to 21.3% in 2022) and coal is up 30.6% again. picks.consensus_delta: The question for a deep-value name is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a business with stable earnings power. # Anhui Conch Cement (0914.HK) - deep dive on management and the setup

**Debate date:** 2026-11-16. **Quote used:** HK$17.20 (H share, Hong Kong listing, FMP quote 2026-11-16). The company reports in Chinese yuan (CNY); at the live rate of HK$1.1776 per yuan the H share is about CNY 14.61. The Shanghai A share (600585.SS) trades at CNY 18.38, so the H share sits about 20% below its own A-share twin.

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists in FMP for this listing, and Conch does not publish English call transcripts. This dossier is built from the company's own reported results (H1 2026 interim report, 2026-08-26; unaudited Q3 2026 report, 2026-10-28), a Guosen Securities results note on Q3 (around 2026-11-01), a Chinese financial-press write-up of the interim report, and the FMP balance sheet at 2026-09-30. Where management is paraphrased, it is the wording carried by those reports; no direct call quotes are invented.

**Data-integrity warning for the committee.** The screener block that fed this debate is wrong on the two numbers a reader would anchor on. It shows trailing-twelve-month (TTM) diluted earnings per share of 1.55 and "latest-quarter EPS +104% year on year". The FMP quarterly series is corrupted for this name (its "Q2 2026" line is the cumulative first half, its Q3 2025 revenue is negative). The real figures: Q3 2026 attributable profit CNY 0.216B, down 88.9% year on year; nine-month profit CNY 2.74B, down 56.9%; TTM attributable profit about CNY 4.55B, or about CNY 0.86 per share - roughly half what the scan shows. Every "cheap on earnings" signal in the scan (the Graham and EPV margins of safety, the P/FCF of 10.9x) is computed on stale or doubled earnings. The balance-sheet figures (net cash CNY 21.67B) do check out against the 2026-09-30 statement.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Through 2025 the story was "the lowest-cost producer earns through the property bust": revenue fell from CNY 168B (2021) to CNY 80B (2025), but 2025 profit actually rose about 7% to CNY 8.25B as coal got cheaper and the company cut cost per tonne. That narrative broke in 2026. The interim report (2026-08-26) shifted the explanation to "weak cement demand and intensifying competition": first-half revenue fell 10.9% to CNY 36.9B, attributable profit fell 42.8% to CNY 2.53B, and own-product volume fell about 4% to 121 million tonnes, with the profit drop blamed mainly on lower selling prices. The Q3 report (2026-10-28) added a second leg: prices and volumes both down and costs up. Guosen puts the national average cement price at CNY 322 per tonne in Q3, down 7.8% year on year, while thermal coal (Qinhuangdao 5,500 kcal) averaged CNY 875 per tonne, up 30.6%.

The growth story management now leans on is outside the domestic clinker business: overseas revenue up 21% in H1 with margins up 2.2 points, exports up 77%, and a build-out into aggregates (4 projects), ready-mix concrete (26 projects) and dry mortar. These are real but small next to a domestic cement base of roughly CNY 28.6B of half-year own-product revenue.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / story | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Lowest-cost leader earns through the trough | Still profitable when China Resources Building Materials (1313.HK) guided to a nine-month loss; but Q3 2026 gross margin 14.9% (down 7.5 points year on year), Q3 profit CNY 0.22B, profit decline widening every quarter (Q1 -19%, Q2 roughly -59%, Q3 -89%) | Relative claim holds, absolute claim is failing |
| Cost reduction (technology, logistics, alternative fuels) | H1 cost per tonne down 6.3%; Q3 coal up 30.6% wiped that out | Self-help was real but too small against coal |
| Shareholder returns are protected | 2025 payout 55.3% (final CNY 0.61); 2026 interim cut to CNY 0.13, only 26.9% of half-year profit; Guosen (2026-08-27) reports a CNY 0.90 per-share minimum for 2026, which we could not find in the company's own announcement text | Partly verified; the interim payout ratio fell |
| Balance sheet is a fortress | 2026-09-30: cash and short-term investments CNY 42.5B, total debt CNY 20.8B, net cash CNY 21.7B (about HK$4.84 per share, 28% of the share price); liabilities 19.7% of assets | Verified |
| Insiders back the value | Parent Conch Group bought 52.9 million A shares (about CNY 1.28B); company bought back and cancelled small A and H blocks | Verified, supportive but small versus a CNY 77B market value |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining. The 2025 annual message was cost leadership and resilience; by the 2026 interim it was "weak demand and intensifying competition"; by Q3 the company simply attributed the drop to price, volume and cost together. The forward-looking language has moved from domestic margin recovery to overseas growth and new building-materials lines - a classic defensive shift.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Conch gives no numeric profit guidance, so there is little to miss. The scan's 50% beat rate (3 of 6 quarters) is on the corrupted FMP series and should not be trusted. Street expectations, by contrast, have been badly wrong: Guosen cut its 2026/2027/2028 earnings-per-share forecasts from CNY 1.14/1.40/1.59 to 0.79/1.00/1.21 after Q3 - a 31% cut to this year. Reliability of management statements: Medium (factual, terse, not promotional); reliability of consensus: Low.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Can price discipline hold? Guosen notes coordinated staggered production lifting prices since September 2026 and regulators enforcing caps on over-production. That is the whole recovery case and it is a coordination outcome, not a contract.
- The dividend: whether a CNY 0.90 floor is a real commitment when 2026 earnings are tracking about CNY 0.79 per share.
- Coal: the cost line that turned a price problem into a profit collapse in Q3.
- Online consensus price targets (Simply Wall St, Investing.com, about HK$26-28, undated and from when the stock traded near HK$23-24) predate the Q3 collapse and are stale.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Q3 2026 profit down 88.9% and recurring profit down 93.9% (2026-10-28) - the trough is deeper than the market assumed in mid-year.
- Red: profit decline accelerating every quarter of 2026; operating cash flow for nine months down 31%.
- Red: 2026 interim dividend payout ratio cut to 26.9% from the 2025 full-year 55.3%.
- Red: input cost (coal +30.6%) passed through badly - margins were also squeezed in 2021-22 (gross margin 33.3% in 2019 to 21.3% in 2022).
- Green: CNY 21.7B net cash, low leverage; still profitable at the industry bottom while a large peer is loss-making.
- Green: parent buying about CNY 1.28B of A shares; overseas revenue up 21% with better margins.
- Green: Q3 operating cash flow up 11.8% year on year (CNY 3.15B) despite the profit collapse; depreciation of about CNY 8B a year keeps cash generation far above reported profit.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary moved from "cost leadership" to "competition", which in Chinese cement usually means smaller players undercutting price to keep kilns running - the opposite of the supply discipline the bull case needs.
- The pursuit of Wanwei High-tech's cement assets (described as removing potential competition) shows consolidation is the chosen lever; it adds capacity to a shrinking market rather than retiring it.
- Financial income fell as treasury money was moved out of structured deposits, and currency losses rose: the cash pile is earning less, so the "net cash cushions earnings" support is also thinning.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: deteriorating. The single most important thing to weigh: the stock looks cheap on the scan only because the scan carries about double the real trailing earnings. On real numbers the H share trades at about 17x trailing earnings, about 0.41x book value, and about 13x the operating business once net cash is stripped out on the broker's 2026 estimate. The cheapness is in the balance sheet (book value about HK$42 per share, net cash about HK$4.84 per share), not in current earnings, and the earnings are still falling.

Moat: scale and cost advantage (limestone reserves, the Yangtze river logistics network, the largest kiln fleet). It is narrow and, relative to peers, stable - Conch still earns money where weaker rivals lose it. But the returns evidence is falling hard (return on equity from above 20% in 2021 to about 2% annualized on 2026 estimates) because the whole industry pie is shrinking. The secular force is the structural decline in Chinese property and infrastructure construction, which has cut national cement demand for five straight years. That is a material threat to the size of the earnings base, not a terminal one: China will still consume well over a billion tonnes of cement a year, and the low-cost leader will keep the profitable share of it. Cheapness is therefore part fear-print and part shrinking base; the test is whether supply discipline restores domestic margins.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Equinor ASA (EQNR.OL) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-02. Quarters covered: Q2 2025 (call 2025-07-23), Q3 2025 (2025-10-29), Q4/FY 2025 (2026-02-04), Q2 2026 (2026-07-22), Q3 2026 (2026-10-28). Prices in Norwegian kroner (NOK) on the Oslo listing; Equinor reports in US dollars.*

**Bottom line:** Equinor is a disciplined, well-run producer whose management has delivered what it promised on production, costs and capital returns for five straight quarters. The numbers that look terrible in the annual history (earnings per share down 32% in fiscal 2025, a 3-year EPS decline of about 40% a year) are the tail of the 2022 gas-price windfall unwinding, not a broken business; the trailing-twelve-month (TTM) figures to 2026-09-30 have already swung back up (TTM EPS 4.81, TTM free cash flow about USD 11.2B) because Brent crude ran from about USD 72 in June to USD 113-117 in late October. The credibility question is therefore not management; it is the commodity price the market is capitalising.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Mid-2025 (Q2 2025):** the story was "control what we can control" in a weak price tape — flat costs, firm capital spending, Johan Castberg (a large new Barents Sea oil field) reaching 220,000 barrels a day in under three months, and a USD 955M write-down on US offshore wind (Empire Wind and the South Brooklyn terminal) after US policy turned against the industry.
- **Late 2025 to early 2026:** portfolio pruning (Peregrino in Brazil sold for USD 3.5B; Nigeria, Azerbaijan, Argentina exits), the growth story shifted to US onshore gas and Brazil (Bacalhau), and renewables were quietly shrunk to a smaller, project-financed book.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-28):** the tone is now a windfall quarter — adjusted operating income of USD 12.35B before tax, "almost twice the level from the same quarter last year", production guidance raised from about 3% to about 4% growth, record refining at Mongstad, and a new capital-return framework for 2027 (dividend growth above 5% a year plus USD 2-4B of buybacks at USD 60-80 oil). New growth avenues appear: a stake in the Lackawanna gas power plant in Pennsylvania (selling power to the data-centre build-out), Namibia entry, Bay du Nord in Canada with Shell as partner.
- **What was dropped:** the old "renewables as a growth pillar" language. What was added: gas-to-power in the US and a cautious, non-linear stance on buybacks above USD 80 oil.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| ~4% production growth in 2025, ~4% again 2026 | Q3 2026: "year to date ... almost 5%", guidance raised to ~4% | Matches |
| Flat / falling unit costs | Q3 2026: 10% underlying cost cut "somewhat behind" on FX and energy costs | Mostly matches, slipping at the margin |
| Strong balance sheet | Cash USD 24B; net debt ratio 3.8% at Q3 2026; recomputed net debt USD 5.67B incl. leases (ex-lease about 1.4B) | Matches — but management itself warns the year-end ratio is "somewhat above 10%" once the six-month Norwegian tax lag is adjusted for |
| Capital distribution of ~USD 9B in 2025, buybacks raised to USD 3B in 2026 | Dividends 0.37 then 0.39 per share per quarter; four buyback tranches | Matches |
| Earnings power | Fiscal 2025 EPS 2.0 (down 32%), net margin 4.8%, FCF margin 5.6%; TTM EPS 4.81 | The recovery is price-driven, not structural |
| Offshore wind "double-digit equity returns" | USD 955M impairment Q2 2025; Empire Wind first power slipped to H1 2027 | Weaker than claimed |

The scan's "Graham" and "Buffett" fair values (NOK 103) are artefacts of the depressed fiscal-2025 earnings; the cash-flow models sit near the price (DCF +11%, owner earnings +6%). EPS beat rate is only 2 of 7 quarters (29%), but that reflects commodity noise around consensus more than over-promising.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable.** Q2 2025 was defensive ("we continue to focus on what we are able to control"). Q3 2026 is confident but deliberately restrained: "while commodity prices are cyclical, it is important to focus on what we can control", and on buybacks above the band, "you should not expect a linear relationship ... we want to avoid being too cyclical". The CFO is using the windfall to build the balance sheet rather than to promise more — a sober signal.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High.** Production guidance has been met or raised every year in the window; the capital-spending guide (about USD 13B organic for 2026) is held; distributions were delivered exactly as set out at the February capital markets update. The one repeated miss is offshore wind timing and value (Empire Wind impairment, first power pushed into 2027).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Buybacks above USD 80 oil** (BNP, Barclays, Q3 2026): management refused to give a formula — upside to distributions in a spike is discretionary, not contractual.
- **Johan Sverdrup decline** (ABG, 2025): the giant field "will come off plateau"; no date given.
- **US gas-to-power strategy** (ABG, Q3 2026): an analyst said he "struggles to give investors a good answer" on why Equinor should own Pennsylvania power plants — a capital-allocation question that remains open.
- **Safety** (Barclays, Q3 2026): incident frequency has ticked up this year.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: six-month Norwegian tax lag means Q4 2026 and H1 2027 carry heavy tax cash outflows (USD 9.3B expected in Q4 2026 alone) — the headline balance sheet flatters.
- Red: board member Hilde Møllerstad sold 1,662 shares at NOK 442.50 on 2026-10-28 (small, but a sale at the top).
- Red: offshore wind write-downs (Q2 2025) and a 2027 slip at Empire Wind (Q3 2026).
- Red: diversification into US power (Lackawanna) at a cyclical high.
- Green: production delivery and the fast Castberg and Bacalhau ramp-ups.
- Green: dividend growth above 5% a year formally committed (Q3 2026).
- Green: exploration collaboration with Aker BP and Vår Energi (2026-10-26) supports the Norwegian shelf to 2035.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The language shifted from "renewables" to "power" and "the intersection between the gas markets and the power markets" — Equinor is repositioning from transition spending toward monetising its gas. The new quarterly buyback framing (no annual number) makes distributions explicitly price-linked; in a falling oil tape the buyback will shrink mechanically toward USD 2B a year.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** The business is executing well; the single most important thing to weigh is that the share price (NOK 427.90 on 2026-11-02, after hitting NOK 454.60) capitalises an oil price that already fell about 8% in a day on a Hormuz reopening plan. On mid-cycle prices (Brent about USD 75, European gas about USD 10/MMBtu) our fair value is near NOK 350.

**Moat:** narrow — a regulatory-licence and scale-cost position on the Norwegian shelf (low break-even, pipeline access to European gas buyers), with ROIC around 10.7% that is cyclical rather than structurally eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable — the energy transition caps long-term terminal growth, but long-term gas contracts with the UK and Germany and production held to 2035 make the shrinkage slow; cheapness here would be cyclical, not a value trap. The current price is not cheap.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Return on invested capital is a modest 9.3%, so the company earns little above its cost of capital through the cycle; a cyclical multiple of 4-4.5x EBITDA on a softer $780M is a fair bear anchor, implying about NOK 98.
picks.consensus_delta: Is the market pricing decline into stable or growing earnings power? Not really: at about 5x EV/EBITDA and 6.9x trailing earnings the market prices DOF as a generic cyclical vessel owner, which matches the peer file's in-line verdict. Where we differ modestly from the market is on duration: backlog has grown 40-50% in a year to about $7B, the Petrobras pipe-layers are approved to 2032, and 2028 rate step-ups are contracted, so earnings are more visible than a trough multiple implies. Where we agree with caution: analyst targets already sit at NOK 146-150 (aggregators, 2026-09 to 2026-11-02), roughly our fair value, so this is not a hidden mispricing - it is a fair-to-modestly-cheap cyclical with a high cash yield. The scan's headline margins of safety (EPV +67%, owner earnings +92%, 'fair value 1,417') are artifacts of the NOK-to-USD reporting switch and should not be relied on.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): (1) the oil price - Brent above $100 on a Hormuz disruption can unwind fast on a reopening deal, dragging offshore names as a group; (2) North Sea spot anchor-handling turned slow in November 2026, a small Q4 drag; (3) 2027 capex - Norseman final payment, 85% of a 250-ton newbuild late 2027 - lands while dividends run at about $394M a year against $135M of TTM free cash flow, so a delayed vessel sale or a weak quarter could force a pause in dividend growth; (4) the PLSV contracts slipping or being re-priced before signature. No debt wall is visible: leverage is about 1.6x and Altman-Z 10.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure looks limited. The holder base is yield-oriented after more than $500M of dividends since mid-2025, so the risk is a dividend disappointment, which management has no near-term reason to deliver while backlog grows. A sector-wide de-rating of offshore names if oil retreats is the more plausible seller, and is the one the entry level relies on. Smart-money score 31/100 and institutional flow 50/100 per the screener give no sign of crowding.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near NOK 126.5, which a sector sell-off in offshore names on a falling oil price could deliver - it is barely below today's NOK 127.2. The thesis holds: Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-12) showed revenue up 22%, underlying EBITDA up 13%, backlog up to about $7B from $4.7B a year earlier, and a dividend raised to $0.40 a quarter. Our base-case fair value is NOK 152 (5.5x 2027 EBITDA of $880M, plus the joint-venture stake at book, minus $1.24B of net debt including leases), with a bear value of NOK 98 and a bull value of NOK 207. That is about 19.5% upside, a touch short of the 20% margin our current reflation backdrop requires before buying at today's price, so the call is a near-trigger wait rather than a pass. The business case is solid but cyclical: return on invested capital is a modest 9.3%, dividends run well ahead of free cash flow, and the sector's fortunes ride one shared factor, offshore oil spending. The Petrobras pipe-laying contracts are approved but not signed, a soft catalyst with no fixed date; in this book it is neither a plus nor a penalty. Value conviction is three: a fair-to-modestly-cheap, well-financed cyclical with a high cash yield, not a deep discount.

# DOF Group ASA (DOFG.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16 from the Q3 2026 results call (2026-11-12; the bundle carries one quarter, with the middle of the call omitted), the screener metrics, FMP quarterly statements (Q3 2025 to Q3 2026, reported in US dollars) and dated trade-press checks. Shares quote in Norwegian kroner (NOK) on Oslo; the company reports in US dollars. Live quote used: NOK 127.2 (FMP, 2026-11-16) at USDNOK 9.635, so about $13.20 a share.*

**Data warning before anything else.** The screener's multi-year history mixes two reporting currencies. The 2021-2023 rows (revenue 6.34B / 9.26B / 11.93B) are the old DOF in NOK; 2024-2025 (1.39B / 1.87B) are the merged group in USD. The "3-year revenue CAGR -41%", "FCF 3-year CAGR -48%", the "net debt 12.11B" and the "Buffett fair value 1,417" are artifacts of that mix, not economics. The scan's per-method margins of safety (EPV +67%, owner earnings +92%, Graham -100%) inherit the same problem and are ignored here. The live balance sheet (2026-09-30) is what counts: borrowings $1.48B, leases $0.16B, cash $0.40B, so net debt is $1.24B including leases ($1.08B excluding them). Equity is $2.13B, about $8.66 (NOK 83) a share.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Only one call is in the bundle, so the arc is read from what management chose to stress on 2026-11-12, set against the reported quarters.

- **Backlog first, earnings second.** CEO Mons Aase opened on the backlog ($6.6B at quarter-end, "roughly $7 billion" including contracts released after the balance date) and spent most of his prepared remarks on contracts "nearing signature", saying the company should be "closer to $8 billion than $7 billion" once they land. The story is now one of visibility into 2027-2029 rather than of a cycle upturn.
- **The Petrobras pipe-layers (PLSVs, pipe-laying support vessels) are the centrepiece.** Petrobras has approved new four-year contracts (early 2028 to early 2032) for Skandi Recife, Skandi Olinda and Skandi Buzios, owned in the 50/50 joint venture with TechnipFMC (DOFCON). Management said the three boats are 8-9% of group EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) and the award is "more than $500 million in backlog for us", with a press release expected "within a week or two or three... if everything goes according to plan. Of course, no guarantees."
- **Fleet high-grading is the new capital-allocation theme.** The sale of Skandi Implementer, a high-end subsea vessel, was presented as opportunistic: "when you get an offer... with such a high price, you need to use your brain and sell the boat", at "between 7x and 8x" EBITDA by internal numbers. Sales and purchases are meant to be "cash neutral" over time.
- **Shareholder returns are rising.** The quarterly dividend goes to $0.40 a share (from $0.35 a year earlier), payable 2026-11-30.
- **A tilt toward SURF** (subsea umbilicals, risers and flowlines - installing the pipes and cables on the seabed) was flagged as a segment to grow, while a large Subsea7 vessel coming to market was waved off as "a bit too heavy for us".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (Q3 2026 call) | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Q3 EBITDA $240M, $219M excluding vessel-sale gains, "13% better than last year" | FMP Q3 2026 EBITDA $239M vs $201M in Q3 2025; ex-gain growth ~9-13% depending on last year's base | Matches |
| Revenue up strongly | Q3 2026 revenue $577M vs $472M a year earlier (+22%) | Matches |
| Earnings growth | Net income $115M (EPS $0.47) vs $109M ($0.44) in Q3 2025; trailing-twelve-month (TTM) EPS $1.92 | Matches, but per-share growth is modest (+7%) once gains are stripped |
| Leverage 1.6x | Consolidated net debt $1.24B against roughly $0.8B of consolidated TTM EBITDA is ~1.5x; the company's 1.6x likely includes its share of joint-venture debt | Consistent |
| Rising dividend is affordable | 2025 dividends paid $241M against 2025 free cash flow (FCF) of $244M; TTM FCF only $135M while the run-rate dividend is now ~$394M a year ($0.40 x 246M shares) | **Gap.** Dividends now run well ahead of FCF; the bridge is vessel-sale proceeds (Implementer) and newbuild capex rolling off. This is the main forensic caution |
| Backlog de-risks 2027 | 2027 backlog "close to $1.7 billion" vs 2025 revenue $1.87B and TTM revenue ~$2.24B | Supportive but not full coverage; spot exposure and project work fill the rest |
| Utilisation "room for improvement" at 86% | DOFCON utilisation hit by a long docking (Skandi Acu, Q1) and downtime on an older asset (Q3) | Candid; explains part of the gap |

The reported story and the reported numbers agree on operations. Where the story is richer than the evidence is cash: the dividend, the newbuild programme (Skandi Norseman 2027, two 250-ton vessels around year-end 2027 and early 2028, RSVs in Brazil) and the payout all compete for a TTM FCF of $135M.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising.** The language is offensive, not defensive: "one of those periods where we are really optimistic on building backlog", 2027 "better than... 2026", 2028 "better still" because "a few assets... will go on higher rates in 2028". The hedges ("no guarantees, of course") are specific to the unsigned PLSV contracts, which is honest framing. The one soft spot is the North Sea anchor-handling spot market: good in September and October, "slow now in November", with exposure deliberately cut to one or two boats.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

With one transcript in the bundle, guidance tracking relies on the reported record: the screener shows earnings beats in 6 of the last 7 quarters (86%), and the capital-markets-day guidance (2025 EBITDA $781M reported; backlog $7.2B at Q2 2026) is consistent with Q3 delivery. Management also reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance. When asked for PLSV capex, the CFO answered from memory ("if it was big amounts, I would have remembered it") - informal, but not evasive. **Reliability: High** for operations; **Medium** for the timing of contract signatures, which depend on Petrobras.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Cash trapped in DOFCON.** The joint venture's cash rose after the Skandi Acu refinancing; management said surplus cash "we do expect... to come out at some point" - undated.
- **Newbuild payments.** The CFO itemised them (Norseman final $12-13M in 2027, 85% of one 250-ton vessel late 2027, the second early 2028) but withheld the contract price. Capex is back-end-loaded into 2027-2028, the same window as the dividend increase.
- **Spot exposure.** Analysts pressed on the anchor-handling spot results; management conceded November was weak and "who has done the right thing... remains to be seen."
- **Utilisation at 86%** was pushed on twice; answers pointed to dockings, not demand.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: the run-rate dividend (~$394M a year) is about 2.9x TTM FCF ($135M) - it relies on asset sales and on capex falling away.
- Red: the PLSV award is approved but unsigned (Q3 call, 2026-11-12); management itself says "no guarantees".
- Red: part of the Q3 beat is a $21M vessel-sale gain; underlying EPS growth is closer to +7% year on year.
- Red: dependence on oil-and-gas offshore spending, now riding a Brent oil price above $100 on a Strait of Hormuz disruption (per the house regime read of 2026-11-02) - a shared macro factor that can reverse.
- Green: backlog of $6.6-7.0B (Q3 2026) against $4.7B at Q3 2025 - up roughly 40-50% in a year.
- Green: selling a high-end vessel at 7-8x EBITDA while the whole company trades near 5x shows the asset values sit above the share price's implied multiple.
- Green: balance sheet de-levered to ~1.6x, with dividends raised every few quarters since mid-2025 (over $500M returned per the 2026 capital markets day).
- Green: Altman-Z of 10 and Piotroski 7/9 per the screener.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Use your brain and sell the boat" plus "one or two boats that we are considering" signals management sees second-hand vessel prices above the value the market puts on the fleet - a quiet asset-value argument.
- The SURF ambition and the anchor-handler-with-services contract in Suriname show a shift from renting boats to selling services on top, which lifts margins but adds project-execution risk.
- The refusal to discuss Seven Borealis ("if it was an obvious target for DOF, I would not say it") is a reminder that M&A remains on the table.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING.** Earnings, backlog and leverage all improved over the past year, and the late-2027 to 2028 contract roll is to higher rates.

**The single thing to weigh:** this is a cyclical, asset-heavy vessel owner paying out more than its free cash flow while building ships. The value case is real (about 5x EV/EBITDA, NOK 83 a share of book equity, a 12% dividend yield) but it rests on the offshore cycle holding through 2028 and on asset sales filling the cash gap.

**Moat:** narrow. It is a scale-and-relationship moat - a top-five global ROV (remotely operated vehicle) fleet, a Brazilian PLSV franchise with Petrobras, and a full-service offering - but in a commodity-like vessel market where returns follow day rates. ROIC is 9.3% and margins have expanded with the cycle, so the trend is stable rather than widening or eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. The energy transition caps the very long-term demand for oil-and-gas subsea work, but deepwater Brazil, Guyana, Suriname and Africa have multi-decade field lives, and the vessels serve offshore wind as well. The cheapness is a cyclical-discount print, not a shrinking-base value trap.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# TF1 Group (TFI.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup
*Transcripts reviewed: 9M-2025 (2025-10-30), FY-2025 (2026-02-12), H1-2026 (2026-07-30), 9M-2026 (2026-10-29). Price used: EUR 6.09 (Euronext Paris, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
A year ago (2025-10-30) the story was "resilience": revenue stable, operating margin held near 11%, market-share gains in a falling linear advertising market, and TF1+ (the free streaming platform) growing advertising revenue about 41%. By the full-year call (2026-02-12) the frame was "the second phase of the strategic plan" - micro-payments, the Netflix distribution deal, and French-speaking international expansion - while advertising revenue was already down 4% for 2025. By H1-2026 (2026-07-30) the story had turned defensive: the margin target was cut to "mid- to high single-digit", and net profit roughly halved. The 9M-2026 call (2026-10-29) is a "we are on the road map" call: margin from activities (current operating profit before one-offs, divided by revenue) of 7.6% versus 10.9% a year earlier, advertising revenue down 9%, and the growth vocabulary now leans almost entirely on the Netflix partnership, the small-business ad platform and micro-payments.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Strong double-digit digital growth" | TF1+ ad revenue +19% over 9M-2026 (EUR 160M), +20.5% in Q3; total digital EUR 198M (+17%) | Delivered, but growth has halved from ~40% in 2025 |
| Digital offsets linear decline | Group advertising revenue EUR 1.0B, down 9% (about EUR 100M lost) versus roughly EUR 30M digital gain | Not true - the gap widened |
| Cost discipline protects margin | Programming costs down EUR 44M; margin still 7.6% vs 10.9% | Partial - costs cut, margin still fell about 3.3 points |
| "Very solid" balance sheet | Net cash EUR 382M at 2026-09-30 (EUR 587M cash vs EUR 207M debt at 2026-06-30) | True - the one clean pillar |
| "Growing dividend policy" | Dividend EUR 132M paid April 2026; free cash flow after working capital only EUR 16M over 9M-2026 (EUR 57M in H1, so Q3 was about minus EUR 41M) | Dividend is being paid out of the cash pile, not out of earnings |
| Earnings trajectory | EPS 0.97 (2024) to 0.72 (2025) to trailing 0.59; latest quarter EPS down 27% y/y | Decline is accelerating, not stabilising |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Declining. 2025-10-30: "successfully managed to mitigate" ad headwinds. 2026-02-12: offensive, with return-on-investment slides for advertisers. 2026-07-30: defensive, margin guidance cut. 2026-10-29: "visibility remaining limited", the market forecast of minus 6% "now seems slightly optimistic", and for 2027 "we see no near-term prospects for improvement in the macroeconomic and political environment or any reduction in the regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms." That last sentence is the most candid management has been in two years.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium. 2025 margin guidance was cut in October 2025 (from "broadly stable" to 10.5-11.5%) and then met at 11%. 2026 guidance was cut at H1 to mid- to high single-digit and is being met (7.6% at nine months). Management meets reset guidance; it does not forecast the down-leg well. The 9M-2026 results came in slightly above company-compiled consensus on revenue and margin.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Very thin coverage on the calls - the 9M-2026 call had only written questions from one broker (CIC). The questions were October/Q4 ad trends, 2027 visibility, the presidential election, Netflix monetisation, and programming costs. Management declined to give a programming-cost range and said Netflix revenue is ramping "more gradually than the audience" because ad load and CPM (price per thousand ad views) on Netflix are below TF1+ levels. Nobody asked about dividend cover, which is the real pressure point.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: dividend (EUR 132M) is about eight times nine-month free cash flow after working capital (EUR 16M) - 9M-2026.
- Red: advertising revenue down 9% with management saying the market has "deteriorated further" since May - 9M-2026.
- Red: no improvement seen for 2027; the 2027 presidential election likely reduces prime-time ad inventory - 9M-2026.
- Red: Studio TF1 operating profit down EUR 14M over nine months - 9M-2026.
- Green: audience share at an all-time high of 36.9% among women under 50 in September 2026, and linear ad market share up about 2 points in August-September - 9M-2026.
- Green: Netflix partnership "ahead of our expectations" on audience; TF1+ growth re-accelerated to 20.5% in Q3 - 9M-2026.
- Green: net cash of EUR 382M is roughly 30% of the market value.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The language moved from "gain market share" (a sign of strength in a stable market) to "regulatory asymmetries vis-a-vis global platforms" - an admission that the problem is structural, not cyclical. Disclosure has shifted toward audience and usage metrics (streamers, transactions) and away from digital revenue per user. The micro-payment figures (about 2 million transactions year to date) are small in euros; their prominence on the call is a sign of how few growth levers remain.

## 8. BOTTOM LINE
A well-run, market-leading broadcaster in a shrinking market. Management executes against reset targets, keeps a strong net cash position, and is honest about 2027. But the earnings base is still falling, digital growth is not filling the linear hole, and the dividend now relies on the balance sheet.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory declining · a moat that is being eroded.

picks.consensus_delta: Is the market pricing terminal decline into a business with stable or growing earnings power? No. The street is roughly where we are: analyst targets cluster near NOK 330-345 (Berenberg NOK 345 after its Q3 refresh; a 24-analyst average of NOK 331.50 around July 2026), against a NOK 325.90 price and our NOK 350 fair value. Where we differ is on the oil deck: some of the recent strength reflects Brent averaging above USD 100 over the last 50 days on Middle East supply disruption, and we value on USD 70. If anything the market is slightly too comfortable that today's prices persist; we do not see a mispricing to exploit at this level.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) is oil-led, not balance-sheet-led. There is no liquidation event or debt wall: net debt is USD 7.07B with about USD 6B of liquidity and investment-grade ratings. The risks over the next 3-9 months are (1) Brent continuing to slide from USD 93 as the supply disruption eases (it has already fallen from a USD 119 high), which compresses cash flow just as capex is still at its peak of about USD 1.8B a quarter; (2) winter installation and hook-up work on Hugin A and Valhall PWP, where any slip pushes first oil past summer 2027; (3) another unit-cost or capex revision at the full-year report in February 2027, when management also gives the long-range plan; (4) impairments on a lower price deck, as in Q4 2025.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited. The holder base is income-oriented (Aker group and BP are anchor owners) and the dividend of USD 0.6615 per quarter has been held; a cut is unlikely while operating cash flow exceeds USD 2B a quarter. The more probable seller is the sector itself: if oil falls back toward USD 75-80, generalist money that rotated into energy during the supply shock will leave Norwegian producers together. That sector-wide sell-off is what could deliver our NOK 290 level.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near NOK 290, which a sector-wide sell-off in Norwegian oil producers as crude prices normalise could deliver. The thesis holds. Aker BP is a well-run, low-cost, low-emission Norwegian producer that has done what it promised since 2022: the ten developments are two-thirds complete, both large hubs are on schedule for 2027 first oil after their topsides went in this autumn, and production should rise about 35% to above 500,000 barrels a day in 2028. Our entry needs a 20% discount to fair value, so we would buy near NOK 290, well above our adverse case of NOK 215. Conviction is a middling 3: good franchise, fair price, value that depends on the oil price and on the 2027 start-ups. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Aker BP (AKRBP.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup

Prepared 2026-11-16. Live price NOK 325.90 on Oslo (USD/NOK 9.64, so about USD 33.80 per share; the company reports in US dollars). Brent crude USD 93.35, down from a 50-day average near USD 104.

A note on the evidence: the transcript file carries five calls - the four quarterly calls of 2022 (Q1 on 2022-04-28, the half-year on 2022-07-20, Q3 on 2022-10-26, the full-year on 2023-02-10) and the Q2 2026 call of 2026-07-15. There is a three-year gap (2023 to mid-2026). Where this deep dive judges what happened in between, it relies on the screener's financial trajectory and on the Q3 2026 results release of 2026-10-29 (checked through public reporting), not on call commentary.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story has been unusually consistent for four years, and that is the main finding. In 2022 management sold three things: the Lundin Energy acquisition (closed 2022-06-30, "roughly doubled the size of Aker BP"), a wave of ten field developments rushed to approval inside Norway's temporary tax window (submitted December 2022), and the claim to be the lowest-cost, lowest-emission producer on the Norwegian shelf.

By the Q2 2026 call the same three pillars were still the script, now in the delivery phase: "we sanctioned 10 PDO projects, of which five subsea tiebacks have started production", the portfolio is "over two-thirds completed", and the two big hubs (Yggdrasil and Valhall PWP-Fenris) "remain on track for first production next summer" (summer 2027), lifting output "above 500,000 bpd in 2028", roughly 35% above 2026. A PDO (plan for development and operation) is the Norwegian approval filing for a new field.

What was added: an asset swap with Equinor (May 2026) giving a 90% position in the Ringvei Vest tie-back cluster, a UK licence next to Yggdrasil, and a cut in Wisting from 35% to 27.5% to reduce capital commitment. What was quietly dropped: the 2022 talk of carbon capture as a business, and the specific long-run production-cost target of USD 7 per barrel - cost now runs at USD 8.8 (Q2 2026) and guidance was raised to about USD 8.5 for 2026 at Q3.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (call, date) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Lundin synergies "closer to USD 250 million" (2022-07-20) | Revenue jumped from USD 5.6B (2021) to 12.9B (2022) and 13.6B (2023) on the doubled asset base; synergies are not separately disclosed later | Plausible, unverifiable in detail |
| All PDOs by year-end 2022 (2022-04-28) | Delivered: ten PDOs submitted December 2022 (2023-02-10 call) | Matches |
| Johan Sverdrup Phase 2 on time, Q4 2022 (2022-04-28) | Started mid-December 2022 (2023-02-10 call) | Matches |
| Projects on track for 2027, costs "around 6% above previous estimates" for Valhall PWP-Fenris (2026-07-15) | Q3 2026 release (2026-10-29) again says both hubs on track for 2027; capex runs about USD 1.8B per quarter through 2026 | Matches on schedule; a modest overrun is admitted |
| Production cost "laser-focused" at USD 7/bbl (2023-02-10) | USD 8.8 in Q2 2026; full-year guidance raised to about USD 8.5 at Q3 2026 | Story is richer than the numbers |
| "Robust financial position", "USD 6 billion in available liquidity" (2026-07-15) | Net debt USD 7.07B including leases at 2026-09-30 (USD 5.84B excluding leases), cash USD 2.6B; Altman-Z 1.1 reflects the heavy-tax, capital-heavy model more than distress | Matches, but leverage is up from USD 2.2B net debt in Q3 2022 |
| Earnings power | Net income USD 1.83B (2024) fell to 0.13B (2025, including a USD -145M Q4 2025 loss on impairments), then recovered to USD 2.26B in the first nine months of 2026 as oil rose; trailing-twelve-month (TTM) EPS USD 3.35 | Earnings are driven by the oil price and impairments, not by management narrative |
| Cash flow | Operating cash flow USD 9.1B over the last four quarters, capex about USD 7.4B, so free cash flow (cash after investment) about USD 1.67B TTM - below the dividend bill of about USD 1.67B (USD 0.6615 per share per quarter) | Dividend is just covered at USD 90-100 oil while capex is at peak |

Earnings beat rate is weak: 2 of the last 7 quarters (29%), with "just missed earnings" headlines around Q3 2026. The misses are mostly tax and impairment timing, but they show the reported earnings line is noisy.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable, with a shift from offence to delivery. 2022 was expansive ("fantastic cash flow potential", "the best team in the industry", 2022-07-20). By late 2022 inflation crept in: in an "environment with high predicted inflation" management moved from fixed-price procurement toward taking input-price risk itself through open-book alliance contracts (2022-07-20, 2022-10-26) - a more honest, but riskier, posture. The Q2 2026 call is confident but concrete: dated milestones (Hugin B topside lifted, Hugin A installation "towards the end of the year", Skarv Satellites "late August") rather than adjectives. One deflection: asked for future exploration spend, the CEO declined ("I'm not going to provide you with updated guidance", 2026-07-15), deferring to February.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-High. Delivered: every 2022 project milestone, the 2022 production range, the Sverdrup Phase 2 start, the 2026 production range (Q2 raised the low end; Q3 2026 at 374,000 boe/d with full-year 380,000-400,000 kept). Slipped: unit cost (USD 7 target now about 8.5) and project capex (+6% on Valhall PWP-Fenris). The 29% earnings beat rate reflects oil-price and tax noise more than operational misses. No sandbagging pattern; if anything cost targets were optimistic.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Cost inflation and execution risk on the 2022 project wave (Anish Kapadia 2022-04-28; James Hosie 2022-07-20) - partly came true as a 6% overrun and higher unit costs, not a schedule break.
- Whether all projects would be sanctioned after the tax changes (2022-10-26) - they were.
- Winter installation risk for the 29,000-tonne Hugin A topside (John Olaisen 2026-07-15) - answered with a specific technical case; installation of the Yggdrasil and Valhall topsides was reported done by late October 2026.
- Shelf-wide decline after 2030 (James Carmichael 2026-07-15) - the CEO conceded 2035 "might be more of a challenge". This is the real long-run question: reserve replacement after the 2028 peak.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Unit production cost drifting up (USD 7 target vs 8.8 in Q2 2026; guidance raised at Q3 2026).
- Net debt up to USD 7.07B (with leases) while the dividend is about equal to free cash flow at peak capex.
- Q4 2025 loss of USD 145M on impairments shows reserve or price-deck write-downs can hit.
- Earnings beat rate 29% over seven quarters.
- Long-run (post-2030) production depends on exploration and new tie-backs; the CEO admitted 2035 is harder.

Green flags:
- Project delivery: five tie-backs onstream, both hubs on schedule after topside installation (Q3 2026).
- Production efficiency 94% (Q2 2026) versus a shelf average of 87% (2021 benchmark cited on 2023-02-10).
- Emissions about 3.1 kg CO2 per barrel, roughly a quarter of the global industry average - a real cost advantage as carbon prices rise.
- Disciplined portfolio moves (Wisting stake cut, Ringvei Vest consolidation) rather than a large acquisition.
- Steady dividend (USD 0.6615 per quarter, about 7.8% yield at today's price).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- Language moved from "growth" to "OneTeam", "hub" and "infrastructure-near" exploration (80% of activity) - a tie-back and life-extension company, not a frontier explorer.
- Procurement risk was quietly shifted onto Aker BP's own balance sheet in 2022; the 2026 overrun is the bill for that choice.
- Management is the same core team (CEO Karl Johnny Hersvik, CFO David Tonne) since 2022, so the track record is attributable. The CEO joining the Orsted board (2026) is a personal role, not a strategy pivot.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: STABLE. The company is doing what it said in 2022, roughly on time and modestly over budget. The single most important thing to weigh: Aker BP's value is a function of the long-run oil price and of the capex roll-off after 2027. Today's price already assumes the 2028 production lift; the stock is not cheap on a mid-cycle oil price (USD 70 Brent), and current earnings are flattered by a supply-shock oil price (Brent averaged above USD 100 over the last 50 days, year high USD 119.40).

Moat: scale-cost and regulatory-licence (operated hub infrastructure on the Norwegian shelf, where tie-backs to existing platforms are cheaper than any new entrant can match; very low emissions per barrel). Width: narrow. Returns are cyclical (ROIC 4.1% on the depressed 2025 year; the gross margin of 65% is high but moves with price), not structurally falling. Trend: stable. Secular threat: the energy transition caps the very long-run value of oil, but Aker BP's low-cost, low-carbon barrels sit at the bottom of the global cost curve, and the 2028-2035 cash flows that drive value are inside the demand runway - manageable, not terminal. The cheapness, where it exists, is oil-price fear rather than a shrinking base; the issue here is that there is not much cheapness.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
