picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the single asset carrying the thesis has disappointed in three consecutive reports, and the rest of the company is a thin-margin thermal coal producer leaning on an energy shock that can reverse. Centurion was guided to 3.5Mt for 2026 as recently as February 2026 and called ahead of schedule; Q4 2026 sales are now guided at only 0.3-0.5Mt, the call admitted that elements of the longwall design were less effective than expected, and the next longwall move has slipped to Q3 2027. The seaborne steelmaking-coal segment earned just $5.2M of adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2026 at a $162.45/t cost against $164.83/t revenue, even with benchmark prices near two-year highs. GAAP results have been losses in every 2026 quarter (earnings per share -$0.27, -$0.74, -$0.27), Q3 free cash flow was about -$61M, revenue fell from $4.95B in 2023 to $3.86B in 2025, and the earnings-beat rate is one in seven quarters. About 72% of 2025 revenue is thermal coal, which faces long-run decline; US Powder River Basin volumes missed guidance in Q3 on cheap gas and strong renewables. Much of today's thermal price strength rests on the Strait of Hormuz disruption and LNG tightness; the regime read of 2026-11-02 already shows Brent giving back 7.6% on a reopening plan, and a deal would pull Newcastle back toward $110-120/t. Insiders sold about 53,500 shares and bought none, a securities class action covers October 2024 to May 2026, and the newest analyst target (2026-11-16) is the range low at $22. If Centurion stalls again and thermal prices normalise, earnings fall back toward breakeven and the stock trades on book value of coal assets the market does not want.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the street's targets ($22-36, consensus about $29, mostly set before the 2026-11-04 cut) still assume Centurion delivers a steep 2027 ramp, while the share price at $17.40 discounts something close to failure. The question is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into a business with recoverable earnings power. Partly yes: at about 6x trailing EBITDA with net cash, the price gives little credit for Centurion. But the bullish targets are not reliable anchors either - the newest one (2026-11-16, $22) is the lowest, and management's own Centurion guidance has missed three times. Our base case sits between the two at $22.5, which is the market price plus a modest Centurion recovery, not the street's full ramp.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) runs to the February 2027 report. Q4 2026 Centurion output depends on getting through about 110 metres of faulted ground, with further geological interruptions expected through the rest of the panel. There is no debt wall: the convertibles are being retired in cash this month and liquidity was $887M on 2026-09-30, so there is no solvency event. The risks are earnings and price: Q3 free cash flow was about -$61M, and if a Strait of Hormuz reopening deal lands, Newcastle and LNG prices could fall quickly, taking the seaborne thermal segment (the only segment earning real money today, $65.5M of Q3 EBITDA) down with them. A mild US winter with cheap gas would also weigh on Powder River Basin volumes, which already missed in Q3.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure looks largely spent. The stock is 36% below its 200-day average and 7% up its 52-week range after falling from $39.50 in March 2026; momentum and growth-at-a-reasonable-price holders who owned the Centurion story have likely exited. The $0.075 quarterly dividend is small, so there is no yield-holder base to liquidate on a cut. Insiders sold about 53,500 shares in five open-market sales with no buys, which is not a vote of confidence. We see no index deletion or lock-up that would force mechanical selling, so we do not name a price-wait level.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once Centurion's Q4 2026 sales and 2027 guidance show the ramp is back on track, due with Q4 2026 results around 2027-02-05. Peabody at $17.40 has a clean balance sheet (about $60M of net cash), positive earnings in every segment, and steelmaking-coal prices near two-year highs. Our sum-of-the-parts fair value is $22.5, about 29% above today's price, with a $10.5 adverse case and a $36 favourable case. The thesis is in doubt until the Centurion test passes. The mine was meant to be the company's lowest-cost steelmaking-coal operation and the reason the stock deserved a higher multiple, yet it has missed in each of the last three reports, and management's credibility on it is low. The downside is roughly as large as the upside, and today's thermal coal profits lean on the Strait of Hormuz energy shock, which is a shared risk across the book and can reverse on a headline. So the business is worth owning only once the next report shows the mine working. If the February guidance passes, the discount to fair value should still be there to buy; if it fails, the thesis has broken and we pass.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating - is Q4 2026 results with full 2027 guidance, expected around 2027-02-05. A credible 2027 Centurion plan (3Mt or more at $140/t or less) would re-rate the steelmaking-coal segment; another cut would confirm the bear case. Secondary: completion of the cash redemption of the 2028 convertibles in November 2026, any announced germanium offtake, and a resumption of buybacks once Centurion capital falls away. Seaborne thermal prices will swing with Strait of Hormuz diplomacy, which is a shared energy driver across the book, not a Peabody-specific event.

# Peabody Energy (BTU) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Calls reviewed: Q2 2025 (2025-07-31), Q3 2025 (2025-10-31), Q4 2025 (2026-02-05), Q1 2026 (2026-05-05) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-04). The Q2 2026 call (early August 2026) was not in the transcript bundle; its figures are taken from the filed quarterly statements. Live price used: $17.40 (NYSE, US dollars, FMP quote 2026-11-16).*

**Bottom line:** Peabody's story for 18 months has been one mine. Centurion, a new premium hard coking coal (the high-grade coal used to make steel) longwall mine in Queensland, was meant to lift the company from a thermal coal (power-station coal) producer with thin margins into a lower-cost steelmaking-coal franchise. Three straight quarters of operating trouble at that mine have broken management's delivery record, and the share price has fallen from about $39.50 in March to $17.40 today. The balance sheet is still clean (about $60M of net cash on 2026-09-30) and seaborne coal prices have turned up sharply, so the question for the director is whether Centurion is late or whether it is worse than the company says.

## 1. Narrative arc

- **Mid-2025: "controlling the controllables."** In the Q2 2025 call the chief executive, Jim Grech, raised full-year guidance on cost control and announced that Centurion's longwall start had been *accelerated* to February 2026. The US story was policy-led: executive orders and the federal royalty cut from 12.5% to 7% (worth an estimated $15-20M in the second half of 2025).
- **Late 2025: "an interesting inflection point."** In Q3 2025 management said Centurion shipments would rise sevenfold to 3.5 million tonnes in 2026, that Centurion would be the company's lowest-cost steelmaking-coal mine for 25-plus years, and that capital spending was tapering just as cash flow would expand "in both directions". The Anglo American steelmaking-coal acquisition had been terminated in August 2025 and was being wound down.
- **February 2026: peak confidence.** On the Q4 2025 call the last longwall shield was being installed "well ahead of its original schedule", with 3.5Mt guided for 2026 and 4.7Mt a year by 2028.
- **May 2026: the first crack.** The Q1 2026 call opened with "the notable exception of Centurion": mechanical and electrical commissioning problems slowed cutting, which let roof conditions deteriorate. The thermal story took over the narrative: the Iran conflict in late February lifted Newcastle thermal coal prices by more than $20 a tonne in March.
- **August 2026 (from the filings):** the second quarter was the worst of the year - a GAAP gross loss of $72M and a net loss of $90.6M. A securities class action covering 2024-10-14 to 2026-05-04 was filed (lead-plaintiff deadline 2026-08-24).
- **November 2026: "more complex than our mine plan assumed."** Centurion met its Q3 sales target, but faulting across the tailgate, face and headgate cut October output, and Q4 sales guidance for the mine is now only 0.3-0.5Mt. The next longwall move is now expected in Q3 2027. New side stories appeared - germanium, solar and storage on reclaimed land with RWE, and mine-mouth power for data centres - which is what management teams often add when the core story stalls.

## 2. Claims versus financials

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Centurion ships 3.5Mt in 2026 (Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 calls) | Q4 2026 guide alone is 0.3-0.5Mt; the year will fall far short of 3.5Mt | Missed badly |
| Centurion is the lowest-cost steelmaking-coal mine, about $105/t in 2024 dollars (repeated 2026-11-04) | Seaborne steelmaking-coal segment cost $162.45/t against revenue of $164.83/t in Q3 2026; segment adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) just $5.2M | Not yet shown in the numbers |
| Capital tapering means free cash flow expands (Q3 2025) | Q3 2026 operating cash flow about -$1.4M, capital spending $59.8M; free cash flow roughly -$61M. Trailing-twelve-month (TTM) free cash flow about $230M is flattered by Q2 working-capital and FX effects | Not delivered yet |
| "Pristine balance sheet" (Q3 2025) | Cash $434M against total debt $374M (including $78M of leases) on 2026-09-30 = about $60M net cash; liquidity $887M. Reclamation liabilities are largely pre-funded by restricted collateral | Holds |
| Seaborne prices improving | Premium hard coking coal averaged $248/t in Q3 2026 (+35% year on year); Newcastle thermal about $135/t, ending the quarter above $145/t; seaborne thermal segment EBITDA $65.5M | Holds - this is the bright spot |
| Returning capital | Dividend held at $0.075 a quarter; convertible notes repurchased (about 5.7 million share-equivalents retired in 2026); no open-market buyback of note | Modest, real |

Revenue fell from $4.95B (2023) to $3.86B (2025), and earnings per share from $8.31 (2022) to -$0.43 (2025). Three 2026 quarters have printed GAAP losses (-$0.27, -$0.74, -$0.27 per share).

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory - Declining

- Q2 2025: offensive - "a great first half", guidance raised, start-up accelerated.
- Q3 2025: expansive - "an interesting inflection point", "the intersection of some of the most significant themes going on in America".
- Q4 2025: proud - "well ahead of its original schedule".
- Q1 2026: defensive - "a longer-than-anticipated commissioning period", the emphasis moves to safety and "durable solutions".
- Q3 2026: explanatory and conditional - "more complex than our mine plan assumed", "give us another quarter here, and we will provide full guidance".

Specificity on Centurion fell call by call: from tonnage targets per year to a narrow quarterly range and a promise of guidance next time.

## 4. Guidance credibility - Low

Guidance on the legacy thermal mines and on costs has generally been met or beaten (Q2 2025 costs came in below plan; Q4 2026 seaborne thermal cost guide is $46-51/t versus $56.58/t in Q3). But on the single item that carries the thesis, every forward statement since mid-2025 has been missed: the accelerated start, the 3.5Mt year, the 80% steelmaking-coal price realisation. The screener records one earnings beat in seven quarters (14%), and Q3 2026 missed the consensus loss estimate (-$0.27 against -$0.08). US thermal volumes (the Powder River Basin, PRB) also came in below guidance in Q3 2026 on weather, cheap gas and a customer outage. Reliability score: Low on Centurion, Medium on the rest of the portfolio.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- **Will Centurion be a higher-cost mine than planned?** (Texas Capital, 2026-11-04). The answer - the fixes are "very modest capital" and long-run costs are unchanged - was confident, but it was followed by "we have got a lot to learn".
- **The next longwall move** (Nathan Martin, 2026-11-04): timing deferred to February guidance.
- **2027 contract coverage for US thermal**: not given; deferred to guidance.
- **Diversification side projects** (B. Riley): germanium deal "near", mine-mouth power "very early days". Analysts are probing them, which shows how little else there is to ask about.

## 6. Red flags and green flags

- Red: Centurion slippage in three consecutive reports (Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026) after it was called "ahead of schedule" in February 2026.
- Red: GAAP losses in every 2026 quarter; Q3 2026 free cash flow negative despite the best coking coal price since early 2024.
- Red: insiders sold about 53,500 shares in five open-market sales and bought none.
- Red: securities class action covering October 2024 to May 2026.
- Red: newest analyst target (2026-11-16) is $22, the low of the range; the bundle shows target velocity down 3% versus a year ago.
- Green: about $60M net cash and $887M of liquidity; no debt wall. The remaining $39.9M of 2028 convertible notes is being redeemed in cash in November 2026.
- Green: seaborne prices strong - premium coking coal $248/t and Newcastle above $145/t at end of Q3 2026, with China removing an estimated 70Mt of domestic steelmaking-coal supply this year.
- Green: every segment had positive adjusted EBITDA in Q3 2026 (total $97.5M); Q4 cost guides are lower than Q3 actuals.

## 7. Hidden signals

- The language moved from "accelerated" and "ahead of schedule" to "faulting", "ground pressure" and "elements of the current longwall design were less effective". That is a design admission, not just bad luck with the rock.
- The October 2026 output figure is unclear in the sources: the call transcript reads "just over 450 thousand tons" while the results release, as summarised, puts it nearer 45,000 tonnes; the Q4 sales guide of 0.3-0.5Mt fits the lower reading better.
- Investor-relations leadership changed in late 2025 (Vic Svec to Kala Finklang); the commercial lead's title changed to chief commercial officer.
- New growth vocabulary (germanium, data-centre power, reclamation-land solar) arrived just as the coal growth story stalled.
- Capital returns quietly shifted from buybacks to retiring convertible notes, which is sensible but slower.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict for the director

**Trajectory: Deteriorating** on execution, with a better price backdrop that partly offsets it.

The single most important thing to weigh: **this is a bet on Centurion reaching most of its 4.7Mt nameplate at roughly $125/t costs in 2027.** If it does, steelmaking-coal earnings alone could add several hundred million dollars of EBITDA a year and today's price looks cheap. If it keeps faulting, Peabody is a thermal coal producer with thin margins whose profits depend on an oil-and-gas price shock (the Strait of Hormuz disruption) that could reverse on a diplomatic headline. The proof arrives with Q4 2026 results and 2027 guidance in early February 2027.

**Moat:** none in the durable sense. Peabody is a price-taker in a commodity. Its cost position in the Powder River Basin and the quality of Centurion's coal give it a cost advantage, not pricing power, and returns have fallen with prices (earnings per share from $8.31 in 2022 to losses in 2026). **Secular threat:** material, not terminal - about 72% of 2025 revenue was thermal coal, which faces long-run decline as power systems move away from coal (US thermal especially), while Asian seaborne demand and steelmaking coal remain needed for years. The cheapness is part fear-print (an execution problem on one mine during a sector sell-off) and part structural (a shrinking thermal base), so the discount should not be treated as pure mispricing.

Management credibility 2 of 5 · trajectory weakening · no real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

picks.bull_thesis: Chalco is a state-controlled, integrated bauxite-alumina-aluminium producer. Its Hong Kong shares have fallen about 58%, from a 52-week high of HKD 15.55 to HKD 6.505 (FMP quote, 2026-11-16), while its reported profit kept rising: nine-month 2026 attributable net profit was RMB 17.92bn, up 64.8%, and Q3 alone was RMB 6.04bn, up 59% (results 2026-10-29). Corrected trailing-twelve-month attributable profit is about RMB 19.4bn, or RMB 1.13 (HKD 1.33) a share. That puts the stock at under 5 times trailing earnings and about 1.1 times attributable book value (RMB 85.8bn, or HKD 5.90 a share, at 2026-09-30). The balance sheet is now net cash (RMB 56.4bn of cash against RMB 47.2bn of debt including leases). Operating cash flow rose 84% in the first half, and the interim dividend was raised to RMB 0.276 a share, about 40% of profit, paid by 2026-10-23. The bull case does not need today's prices to hold. China's 45-million-tonne smelting cap limits domestic supply, and Chalco's Yunnan smelters run on hydro power. The buy-in of minority stakes in three Yunnan smelters, agreed 2025-11-25, lifts the share of group profit that reaches Chalco's own holders. If aluminium holds near Bank of America's RMB 21,000-23,000/t path (2026-07-14), 2027 attributable profit could stay near RMB 18-20bn, and at 8 times earnings the shares would be worth about HKD 11. The whole aluminium group (China Hongqiao, Alcoa, Norsk Hydro) has roughly halved, so this is a sector-wide de-rating rather than anything specific to Chalco.
picks.bear_thesis: The trailing numbers are a peak. The 2026 profit came from a war-related supply shock: disruption to Gulf smelters and shipping lifted the London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium price about 29%, to roughly USD 3,855/t on 2026-06-02. Since a preliminary peace agreement in mid-June the price has given back much of that gain, to about USD 3,110-3,135/t in early October (SMM, 2026-10-07), and analysts describe the move as an unwinding risk premium and a repricing toward a looser market. Q3 profit already slipped about 5% from Q2. Goldman Sachs (Sell, target HKD 7.5, 2026-06-16) expects the smelting margin to shrink from about RMB 8,879/t in the first half of 2026 to about RMB 4,250/t in 2027, and recurring profit to fall by about half. The alumina business lost RMB 0.82bn in the first half, so the benefit of owning the whole chain is thin when alumina is cheap. About 42% of group profit and of the group's net cash belongs to minority holders: consolidated Q3 profit was RMB 10.47bn against RMB 6.04bn attributable to Chalco's shareholders. The state parent's related-party dealings are a standing governance discount. If aluminium drops toward RMB 18,500/t and the margin falls back to 2023 levels, attributable profit could return to about RMB 7bn (2023 was RMB 6.7bn), or about HKD 0.48 a share. At 9 times earnings that is about HKD 4.3, and at a cyclical trough Chinese producers often trade below book value (0.8-0.85 times book is about HKD 4.7-5.0). The share price is at its 52-week low and still falling (down about 11% in the week to 2026-11-16), and the earnings downgrades have not yet found a bottom.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the market is not pricing terminal decline, it is pricing a deep cyclical drop, and we think that is only slightly too pessimistic. At HKD 6.505 the shares trade at about 1.1 times attributable book value. That price fits sustained profit of about RMB 10bn at 9 times earnings, roughly the bottom of the range brokers expect once the smelting margin shrinks. Goldman Sachs' Sell case (2026-06-16, target HKD 7.5) expects about half of recurring profit to disappear by 2027. Our base case already assumes that (RMB 12.5bn) and still finds a fair value of about HKD 7.95. Where the street may be wrong is the floor: China's smelting cap, falling alumina costs and a net-cash balance sheet make a 2015-style collapse in returns less likely. Where we may be wrong: the market has been right ahead of us so far, every aluminium peer has fallen in step, and the earnings downgrades are probably not finished.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the next few months. Q4 is seasonally Chalco's weakest quarter: Q4 2025 attributable profit was only about RMB 1.5bn after year-end write-downs. A soft Q4 2026, combined with a further fall in the Shanghai aluminium price as Gulf supply returns and new Indonesian capacity starts, could take the shares toward book value (about HKD 5.90) before the full-year results in late March 2027. There is no debt maturity wall (the company has net cash), no liquidity risk and no forced share issuance. The risk is a lower price for the metal and the shares, not the company's survival.
picks.positioning_washout: Most of the forced selling has already happened. The stock joined the Hang Seng Index on 2026-06-08 and fell 8% that day, followed by sustained selling. Momentum and commodity funds have left the whole sector since the metal peaked in June. The holder base now leans toward state-related and dividend investors, and the next dividend (the final 2026 payout, normally declared with the March results) is a reason to own the stock, not to sell it. We cannot name any remaining forced seller; a further fall would come from fundamentals, mainly the metal price.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now, at a modest size. The thesis holds. Chalco is a net-cash, state-controlled aluminium producer trading at about 1.1 times book value and under 5 times trailing earnings, after aluminium shares across the sector halved as the 2026 Middle East supply premium unwound. Our fair value of about HKD 7.95 assumes 2027 profit falls to roughly half the 2026 run rate, and it still sits about 22% above today's HKD 6.505. That only just clears our 20% entry bar for the current macro backdrop. Two cautions keep conviction at a middling 3. First, the cheapness on trailing numbers is a peak-earnings illusion, so the real margin of safety rests on the mid-cycle estimate. Second, about 42% of group profit belongs to minority holders, and capital allocation follows the state parent. The bear case of about HKD 4.6 assumes a 2023-style trough. No forced seller is left that we can name, but the metal price is still sliding, so expect volatility and size this as a cyclical holding, not a compounder.
picks.forcing_function: No firmly dated event forces a re-rating. The paths are: (1) the full-year 2026 results and final dividend around late March 2027, which should show net cash rising and a payout of about 40%; (2) the Shanghai aluminium price settling above roughly RMB 20,000/t, which would stop the earnings downgrades; and (3) further buy-ins of minority stakes inside the group. None of these is binding, so the case rests on the value itself, not on an event.

# Aluminum Corporation of China (Chalco), H-share 2600.HK: a deep dive on management and the setup
As of 2026-11-16. No earnings-call transcript was available: Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) has none for this listing, and the web search found no call transcript. This dossier therefore reasons from the filed numbers (FMP quarterly statements to 2026-09-30), the H1 2026 results release (2026-08-27, as reported by the Chinese financial press), the Q3 2026 results (2026-10-29) and dated broker and metals-market coverage. No management quote is invented. Figures are in Chinese yuan (RMB) unless marked HKD; the H-share trades in Hong Kong dollars.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The story over the last two years is a commodity upswing, not a strategic change. Chalco is the state-controlled integrated producer of bauxite, alumina (the refined powder that is smelted into aluminium) and primary aluminium, with a large trading arm. Management's framing in the H1 2026 release was that profit rose because of "higher aluminium prices, lower alumina prices and cost reduction", with an internal slogan about pushing operations to the limit to cut costs. The one structural move in the period was consolidation: on 2025-11-25 its subsidiary Yunnan Aluminium agreed to buy minority stakes in three smelting subsidiaries (Yunlv Yongxin, Runxin, Hongxin) from a sister company for cash, so that more of the group's hydro-powered smelting profit reaches Chalco's own shareholders. The 2026 narrative was then shaped by events outside the company: a Middle East conflict disrupted Gulf smelters and shipping, the London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium price rose about 29% in five months to about USD 3,855/t on 2026-06-02, and then gave back gains after a mid-June preliminary peace agreement, to about USD 3,110-3,135/t in early October (SMM, 2026-10-07).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / datum | Evidence | Read |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable. Without transcripts, tone can only be read from releases: they are formulaic state-company disclosures that credit prices and cost control and list generic risks (price volatility, overseas operations, safety and environment, foreign exchange, trade barriers). There is no shift to defensive language, and no forward guidance on prices, which management never gives.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Chalco gives profit alerts rather than guidance. The H1 2026 alert range of RMB 11.2-12.2bn was met at RMB 11.87bn. The screener shows beats in 5 of 6 quarters. Reliability: Medium-High for what it guides, but it guides very little; the important variable (the aluminium price) is outside its control.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
The debate is entirely about the cycle. Goldman Sachs downgraded the stock to Sell on 2026-06-16 with a HKD 7.5 target, arguing that supply growth in China and abroad would shrink the smelting spread from RMB 8,879/t in the first half to about RMB 4,250/t in 2027 and could cut recurring profit by about half. Citi cut its target to HKD 7.6 the same day but kept a Buy. Bank of America (2026-07-14) called the worries overdone, kept a Buy with a HKD 10.5 target and assumed RMB 23,000/t aluminium for 2026 and RMB 21,000/t for 2027; Morgan Stanley kept Overweight at HKD 11.2. A BOCI target cut was recorded on 2026-10-22 (target 10.46, currency not shown on the source page). The street therefore already prices a sharp earnings decline; the open question is the size of that decline.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: earnings are at a cyclical high driven by a war-related supply shock that is unwinding; Q3 profit already dipped from Q2 (2026-10-29).
- Red: the alumina business lost money in H1 2026; Chalco's integration advantage is weaker when alumina is cheap and abundant.
- Red: about 42% of group profit goes to minority holders; state-owned capital allocation (related-party deals with the parent, Chinalco Group, which owns about 30.5%).
- Red: the H-share has fallen about 58% from its 52-week high of HKD 15.55 and sits at its 52-week low of HKD 6.445 (FMP, 2026-11-16), together with every aluminium peer, so the market sees something in the cycle that trailing numbers do not show.
- Green: net cash of RMB 9.2bn, debt ratio falling, operating cash flow up 84% in H1 2026.
- Green: payout roughly doubled in rate (interim RMB 0.276).
- Green: China's 45-million-tonne smelting capacity cap limits domestic supply growth, which supports a better mid-cycle margin than in the 2010s.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The minority-buy-in deal in Yunnan (2025-11-25) and the higher payout point to a parent that wants Chalco's listed vehicle to capture more of the group's best smelting assets and return cash: a modest positive for governance. The sharp fall of the share price while reported profit kept growing means the market is valuing the stock on 2027 earnings, not on trailing ones.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: STABLE. The business is doing what a well-run commodity producer does at the top of the cycle: paying down debt, raising the dividend and buying in minorities. The single most important thing to weigh: on trailing numbers the stock looks absurdly cheap (about 4.9 times earnings), but that is a peak-earnings reading; the value case only holds if mid-cycle profit settles around RMB 11-13bn, roughly half of the 2026 run rate.
Moat: scale-cost and regulatory (China's capacity cap, integrated bauxite-to-metal chain, hydro-powered Yunnan smelters). It is narrow: returns swing with the metal price (ROIC 8.7% on the last fiscal year, ROE 12.6%), so there is no wide moat. Secular threat: none. Aluminium is a beneficiary of lighter vehicles, power grids and solar frames; the risk is cyclical, not terminal. The cheapness is a cyclical fear-print, not a structurally shrinking base, but part of it is honest discounting of peak earnings.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat none.

picks.bull_thesis:
Wise is one of the few payments businesses that turns scale into lower prices and is paid back in volume, and the newest quarter is the cleanest evidence yet. Between November 2023 and Q2 of the 2027 financial year management cut the take rate (the percentage Wise keeps on each cross-border transfer) from 0.67% to 0.49%. The customer response has been steady and broad: in the quarter to September 2026 cross-border volume rose 22% to 72 billion dollars, business volume rose 32%, active customers rose 20% to 12.5 million, card spend rose 30% to 14 billion dollars and customer balances rose 22% to 32 billion dollars. The chief financial officer said in November 2025 that 'we will see the real growth in the second half year when this pricing adjustment is not affecting anymore the comparison', and it happened: cross-border revenue growth went from about 5% to 16%, and total net revenue grew 21% to 739 million dollars. On 2026-10-15 management raised full-year guidance to the upper half of its 15% to 20% growth range.

The machinery underneath is concrete. Nine direct connections into national payment systems (Malaysia was added this quarter), about 65 financial licences, and a cost advantage that lets Wise charge less and still earn a profit margin in the low-to-mid twenties. Wise Platform, which rents those rails to banks such as Standard Chartered, Itau, Raiffeisen and UniCredit, earns about 0.40% per transfer with no customer-acquisition cost and, per management, no churn so far. Revenue is diversifying: transfers are now under half of net revenue once cards, investments and interest are counted.

The macro backdrop helps rather than hurts. The Fed and the European Central Bank have raised rates in recent months, and management has written that into second-half expectations; roughly a third of gross revenue is interest earned on customer balances, so higher-for-longer rates lift earnings mechanically. At 823 pence the shares trade at about 20 times the roughly 40 pence of earnings per share we expect for the year to March 2027 and about 17.5 times the roughly 47 pence for the year after, for a business compounding revenue at close to 20%. The independent sell-side check points the same way: UBS raised its target to 1,300 pence ahead of the results and JPMorgan, rated Overweight, lifted its Nasdaq target to 17.70 dollars (about 1,345 pence); both figures are from Yahoo Finance listings retrieved 2026-10-19 whose exact dates we could not confirm. The bull case needs three things to hold: the take rate keeps falling about one basis point a quarter rather than in large steps, the Brussels investigation ends in a fine rather than a licence restriction, and margins hold near the top of the guided range.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case starts with the reason this name reached the committee, which is a measurement error. The screener's 1.2 times free cash flow, 115% margin of safety and 24.1 billion pounds of net cash are customer money: at 31 March 2026 Wise held 24.5 billion pounds of cash and investments against 23.3 billion pounds owed back to customers, and shareholders' equity was about 1.46 billion pounds. The trailing earnings per share of 0.77 in the screener does not reconcile with 377 million pounds of profit on about 1.0 billion shares (0.37 pounds). Strip those out and Wise is a growth stock at about 20 times forward earnings - not deep value.

Second, earnings have not followed revenue. Statutory profit fell from 417 million to 377 million pounds in the year to March 2026 and earnings per share fell from 0.40 to 0.37 pounds, the first decline since listing, as the gross margin fell from 72.4% to 57.5% and marketing spend more than doubled. The 2026-10-15 update guided the half-year margin to about 23% including about 2 points of one-off costs (about 15 million dollars of dual-listing expense), and the market sold the shares 7.7% the next day while peers rose - a sign that investors expected more profit from the revenue beat.

Third, about a third of gross revenue is interest on customer balances, and that stream deserves a lower multiple than fees. The gross yield already fell from 3.1% to 2.9% in a year; management says it does not want to depend on rates and may pass the recent rate gains back to customers ('we might pass it, but that's a bit too early to say'). If policy rates turn down in 2027, or more of the yield is handed to customers, the largest single profit stream shrinks while transfer prices are still being cut.

Fourth, the regulatory record is the real tail. Belgian prosecutors are investigating whether about 500 million euros of criminal proceeds moved through Wise Europe and cited 'indications of non-compliance with anti-money laundering legislation' (reported 2026-06-01; the shares fell as much as 19% that day). The United States regulator refused Wise's trust-bank charter on 2026-07-23. United States securities class actions filed in August 2026 allege these risks were understated at the Nasdaq listing. None of this was discussed on the 2026-10-15 call. A licence restriction in the European hub, rather than a fine, would hit the business itself. Finally, the second half laps tougher comparisons; when asked whether that points to the lower half of the guided range, the chief financial officer did not answer.
picks.consensus_delta:
Where we disagree with the market splits three ways. First, with our own model: the screener valued customer money as shareholder value (24.1 billion pounds of net cash, 1.2 times free cash flow, a 13,087 pence cash-flow value). Corrected, Wise trades at about 20 times forward earnings. Any reader of the screener output should know that the deep-value label is false; the real case is a growth franchise at a fair-to-modest discount.

Second, with the market's reaction to the 2026-10-15 update. The shares fell 7.7% on 2026-10-16 to 833.2 pence while Remitly, PayPal and Adyen rose over the month. The selling focused on a one-basis-point take-rate cut, a lower yield on balances and about 2 points of one-off costs in the half-year margin. We think it over-weighted noise: the one-off costs are mostly the dual-listing expense that will not recur, the take-rate cut was smaller than the two basis points management had flagged, and the revenue guide went up. The re-acceleration the company promised in November 2025 has been delivered on schedule.

Third, with the sell side on how to value the interest stream. Published targets (UBS 1,300 pence; JPMorgan about 17.70 dollars on the Nasdaq line, roughly 1,345 pence; both from undated Yahoo Finance listings retrieved 2026-10-19) appear to value interest on customer balances at the fee multiple. We value it at about 10 times after-tax retained spread because it moves with policy rates and management keeps saying it may hand it back to customers. That is why our 1,000 pence fair value is well below the street, and why we treat the street targets as a bull case rather than a base case.
picks.valley_of_death:
There is no solvency risk here: about 366 million pounds of debt including leases, real operating profit, no dividend to cut, a 500 million dollar buyback under way. The risky window (the months just ahead) is about the multiple and the headlines.

First, the half-year results, confirmed scheduled for 2026-11-12 and still ahead as of this update. That print will show the full cost base, the one-off costs and any provision for the Belgian investigation or United States remediation. A provision, or a second-half outlook at the lower end of the range as the comparisons get tougher, could take the shares through the 754 pence 52-week low.

Second, regulatory and legal news on someone else's timetable: a development in the Belgian investigation, consolidation and amended complaints in the United States class actions, or a further statement from the United States regulator. Each arrives without warning.

Third, the rate path. About a third of gross revenue is interest on customer balances. The current backdrop is hikes, which helps; a pivot to cuts in 2027 would shrink the largest single profit stream while transfer prices are still being reduced. This is the one macro driver that matters, and it is shared with every float-earning payments company, so it is not independent of the rest of a payments-heavy book.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-selling pressure to harvest here, and the recent fall did not come from forced sellers. Wise pays no dividend, so there is no income holder base to flush. The one mechanical event, the move of the primary listing to Nasdaq in May 2026 and the index selling it triggered in London, is already behind us; the shares bottomed at 754 pence afterwards. The 7.7% fall on 2026-10-16 was a reaction to company news (the Q2 update) by discretionary holders, and it happened while the peer group rose, so it is neither a wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers) nor a sector-wide sell-off. The 500 million dollar buyback announced in June 2026 is a steady buyer under the price. The dual-class structure keeps control with the founder, so there is no activist route to force a sale or a change in pricing policy. The insider buy ratio is zero, which is a mild negative.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Buy now. The price has come to the level we said we would wait for, and the business delivered what it promised on the way down.

When we last looked on 2026-10-12, we said Wise was a good business at the wrong price and that we would buy below about 800 pence, roughly 20 times forward earnings and a 20% discount to our 1,000 pence fair value. Since then, net revenue grew 21%, cross-border volume grew 22%, cross-border revenue growth returned to 16% after a year depressed by its own price cuts, and full-year revenue guidance was raised (2026-10-15); the shares nonetheless fell 7.7% the next day while the rest of the cross-border payments group rose. They have since drifted back up to 833.0 pence (2026-11-09 close). Our fair value is unchanged at 1,000 pence, now about 20.0% above the price - still just clearing the 20% discount we require in today's backdrop, though the margin of comfort has narrowed from 23.4% two weeks ago. The thesis holds: the price cuts are buying durable volume, and the volume is turning back into revenue growth.

This is a buy on a fair-to-modest discount, not a deep-value bargain, and the size should say so. The screener's deep-value signal was false: its cash and cash-flow figures are customer money held against an equal liability, and on honest numbers Wise trades at about 20 times forward earnings. The downside to our adverse case of 640 pence is about 23%, slightly more than the upside to fair value, so the payoff still leans on the long right tail (our favourable case is 1,480 pence) and on a growing business compounding into its multiple, not on a cheap entry. Two risks set the size. The Belgian anti-money-laundering investigation, reported on 2026-06-01, is the real tail: a fine is in the price, a restriction on the European licence is not. And about a third of gross revenue is interest on customer balances; today's rising rates help, but a pivot to cuts would hurt.

The next checkpoint is the half-year results, confirmed for 2026-11-12, still a few days ahead. A provision for the investigation or a weak second-half outlook would be the reason to stop adding; a clean margin near 23% with the listing costs gone would confirm the case.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard-dated special situation, and in this book none is needed. The next dated checkpoint is the half-year results, confirmed for 2026-11-12, where the founder presents and the full margin, one-off costs and platform progress are disclosed. The 500 million dollar buyback is a steady support, not a re-rating trigger. The re-rating path is therefore the ordinary one for a compounder: earnings per share growing from about 0.37 pounds toward about 0.47 pounds over two years, with the multiple held near 22 times.

picks.bull_thesis: Seres builds the AITO range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing, and the bull case is that the shares now price a broken company while the accounts still describe a cyclical one. At HK$30.88 on 26 October 2026 the whole company, 1.742 billion shares, is worth about CNY 46 billion against roughly CNY 160 billion of trailing revenue, about 0.29 times revenue (enterprise value to revenue, the value of the business per yuan of sales) before any credit for cash, versus roughly 0.65 times for Li Auto and 0.55 times for Leapmotor on the 22 September 2026 pull. The first-half 2026 damage was price and cost, not customers: units fell only 1.02% while gross margin fell 4.7 points to 21.8% on a 132.2% year-on-year rise in battery-grade lithium carbonate and chip shortages, both named in the 19 August 2026 half-year report. The third-quarter volume slump (July down 45.65%, August down 43.96%, September down 34.48% in new-energy units) coincides with the largest product changeover in the brand's history, the M8 refresh that opened pre-sales on 30 September 2026 at CNY 389,800, CNY 30,000 above its predecessor, and with the 15 September handover of product, brand, retail and service from Huawei to Seres; a bull reads it as a transition gap rather than lost demand. The company has moved to fix its two biggest exposures: an 11 October 2026 long-term battery agreement with CATL to take capacity above 20 GWh, and a five-year agreement with Huawei signed 30 September 2026 that keeps AITO inside the alliance. Beyond the vehicle business sit CNY 73.13 billion of cash and short-term investments against about CNY 4.35 billion of borrowing, and a 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang intelligent-automotive unit carried at about CNY 13.5 billion, which alone is close to a third of the market value. If the 30 October 2026 third-quarter report shows gross margin stabilising near 22% and positive operating cash flow, the market is paying very little for a CNY 130 to 160 billion revenue franchise that now owns its customer relationship, with a 2027 European launch and the Aiva brand as free options.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the first-half story, steady demand and a passing cost shock, has been disproved by the third quarter, and that the apparent cheapness rests on cash that is not really spare. Seres's own monthly reports show new-energy sales down 45.65% in July, 43.96% in August and 34.48% in September 2026 (September report dated 8 October), and January-to-September sales down about 17% to roughly 283,200. That is worse than the Huawei alliance overall, down 29% in September, so AITO is losing share inside its own alliance in the very quarter Huawei handed the brand back. Huawei keeps running the other four alliance brands, and on 21 October 2026 it emerged that overseas AITO models will use Bosch systems instead of Huawei's, the partner's role narrowing again. Seres must now fund its own retail network, a European launch announced for 2027, a new Aiva brand and robotics projects, while selling and administrative expense was already CNY 5.37 billion in the second quarter, 17% of revenue. On the balance sheet, the CNY 73.13 billion cash pile is financed by CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables; operating cash flow was minus CNY 20.95 billion in the first quarter of 2026 alone, and trailing free cash flow is minus CNY 3.27 billion. A business whose volume falls 40% in a quarter releases that supplier float in reverse, so the third-quarter cash flow may well be negative again, and the defensible net cash could fall well below the CNY 30 billion we credit. Returns on invested capital are near zero, a CNY 1.75 billion write-down of capitalised development in the first half signals earlier aggressive capitalisation, and the screener's 1.7 times price-to-free-cash-flow and DCF value of 198.7 are computed from the 2025 peak and must be discarded. What would confirm the bear: a third-quarter gross margin below 18%, another large operating cash outflow, or October sales still down more than 30% year on year.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market has narrowed and now runs mainly against the sell side rather than the tape. The share price, 77% below the November 2025 listing price of HK$131.5, already treats Seres as a broken company; on the no-cash revenue multiple of about 0.29 times we think that is roughly fair for the vehicle business alone, and our edge, if any, is the 10% Yinwang stake and the part of the cash that is genuinely spare. Where we disagree with consensus is the earnings path: the 2026 consensus of about CNY 159 billion of revenue and CNY 0.44 of earnings per share that the earlier reviews cited needed a second half matching the record second half of 2025, roughly CNY 102 billion; with third-quarter sales down about 40% year on year that is now very unlikely, and the 2027 recovery estimate of about CNY 3.05 a share rests on volume and margin recovering together under a new retail model. We also continue to reject the company's balance-sheet framing (cash above CNY 73 billion, debt 3.2% of assets), treating CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes as debt.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the next one to two quarters. The 30 October 2026 third-quarter report will be the first set of accounts covering the post-handover quarter and a roughly 40% year-on-year volume drop. With supplier float unwinding as volume falls, a negative operating cash flow quarter is likely, and the cost of the self-run sales network will land in selling expense before any retail margin shows in gross profit. The full-year 2026 estimates will be cut. Beyond that, the first quarter of each year is this company's cash-flow trough (minus CNY 20.95 billion in the first quarter of 2026), so early 2027 will look alarming even if the business stabilises. There is no debt maturity wall; the risk is cash consumption by working capital, not insolvency.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure from the listing has largely played out: buyers of the November 2025 offering at HK$131.5 are down about 77%, and the price sits about 3% above the 52-week low of HK$29.88. The Hong Kong line is thin, about 109 million of 1.742 billion shares on the committee's count, so it overshoots both ways, and the gap to the Shanghai A-shares has no conversion mechanism to close it. Institutional interest is negligible (smart-money score 4 out of 100). I could not identify a dated mechanical seller, an index deletion or lock-up expiry, behind the October fall; it followed the September sales report, so it is company news, not a forced wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers).
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the third-quarter report, due 30 October 2026, shows gross margin at or above 22% with positive operating cash flow for the quarter. The answer is still to wait, at conviction 2, but the reason has changed. On 5 October the case was a cheap asset whose demand had held while price and cost fell; since then Seres's own monthly reports showed third-quarter new-energy sales down 45.65%, 43.96% and 34.48% year on year in July, August and September (the last reported 8 October 2026), worse than the Huawei alliance as a whole, in the first quarter after Huawei handed the brand back. That puts the thesis in doubt until the accounts show whether this is a changeover gap around the refreshed M8 or lost customers. The price has fallen 15% to HK$30.88, but we cut fair value too, from HK$46.50 to HK$41, by lowering vehicle revenue to CNY 130 billion, with an adverse case of HK$21 and a favorable case of HK$88. The cheapness is still mostly a balance-sheet add-back: CNY 73 billion of cash financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes, and a 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang unit carried near CNY 13.5 billion. October brought two useful supply-side steps, a CATL battery agreement on 11 October and a confirmed 2027 European launch, and one more sign of Huawei stepping back, Bosch systems for overseas models on 21 October. On the value case alone, ignoring catalysts and the macro backdrop, this remains a three: the discount to the parts is real, but near-zero returns on capital, an eroding brand position and an unverified share count (a quote page implies 2.75 billion shares against the 1.742 billion we use) cap how far that case can be pushed.
picks.forcing_function: There is no binding event that forces a re-rating. The nearest information event is the third-quarter 2026 report on 30 October 2026: gross margin at or above 22% with positive operating cash flow would show the slump is a transition gap, and that is the condition for buying. October and November monthly sales (early November and early December) are the next checks on whether the M8 refresh restores volume. The deeper driver, lithium prices rolling over, is a single shared sector factor and gets no credit here.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Forensic Dossier — Seres Group Co., Ltd (9927.HK / 601127.SS)

**Date of review:** 2026-10-26 (full re-debate; prior committee review 2026-10-05, earlier full review 2026-09-22) · **Price used:** HK$30.88 (Hong Kong listing 9927.HK, HKD, delayed close 26 October 2026, StockAnalysis; our licensed quote feed was not responding this session, and the screener scan carried HK$31.00) · Figures in Chinese yuan (CNY) unless stated

**What changed since the last look (dated, 6 to 26 October 2026).** The new facts are mostly about volume, and they cut against the single strongest pillar of the earlier bull case, that demand had held:

1. **8 October 2026 — Seres's own September production and sales report.** Seres sold 32,218 vehicles in September 2026 against 48,286 a year earlier, down about 33%; new-energy vehicle sales were down 34.48% year on year, after July (down 45.65%) and August (down 43.96%). January-to-September sales of about 283,200 are roughly 17% below the 340,650 of the same period of 2025 (CnEVPost Seres coverage). The first half fell only 1.02%; the third quarter fell roughly 40%. The earlier finding that "the franchise kept its customers and lost its price" was true of the first half and is no longer true of the third quarter.
2. **11 October 2026 — long-term strategic agreement with CATL** to expand AITO battery capacity above 20 GWh once a joint project completes. This secures supply in a lithium-cost shock; it does not by itself lower the cost. Terms undisclosed.
3. **12 October 2026 — AITO confirmed a 2027 European entry** at the Paris Motor Show, showing four sport-utility vehicles. Option value, with launch costs ahead of any revenue.
4. **21 October 2026 — report that overseas AITO models will use Bosch driver-assistance, cockpit and chassis systems** as Huawei steps back from the brand abroad. Consistent with the 15 September handover: Huawei's role in AITO keeps narrowing, and the brand is being re-engineered around a non-Huawei stack outside China.
5. **26 October 2026 — the price.** The Hong Kong line closed at HK$30.88, about 15% below the HK$36.48 of the 5 October review and roughly 3% above the 52-week low of HK$29.88. The decline coincides with the September sales report rather than any forced-selling event I can identify, so I read it as company news layered on a weak sector tape.
6. **The third-quarter report is due 30 October 2026** (StockAnalysis earnings calendar; our scan shows six days to the next report). It is the first set of accounts that covers the post-handover quarter and the volume slump.

**A data caution.** StockAnalysis shows a Hong Kong-listing market value of HK$84.86 billion, which implies about 2.75 billion shares rather than the 1.742 billion used in every prior review. I could not reconcile the two this session; I keep 1.742 billion (the count the committee verified on 22 September) and flag that a larger count would lower every per-share value in this file by roughly a third.

Net effect: the thesis has moved from "a margin event on steady demand" to "a margin event plus a volume event", and the volume event is company-specific (Huawei's alliance as a whole was down 29% in September; Seres was down 33-34% and much worse in July and August). Sections 1 to 8 below are carried from the 5 October review with these facts added where they change the reading.

**A note on sources before anything else.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this company in our licensed data feed, and Chinese A-share issuers with a Hong Kong secondary listing do not hold the quarterly analyst calls that American companies do. There is therefore no multi-quarter transcript arc to read. Everything below is built from the company's own filed numbers (eight quarters of income statement, balance sheet and cash flow), its 12 July 2026 profit warning, its 19 August 2026 half-year report, and dated trade-press coverage of the Huawei partnership. Where I quote, I quote the filed half-year report as relayed by CnEVPost on 19 August 2026. I have invented nothing, and where a fact could not be verified I say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Seres makes the AITO (Wenjie) range of premium electric and range-extended sport-utility vehicles in Chongqing. It is not really an ordinary carmaker. Until one week ago it was the manufacturing half of a partnership in which Huawei did almost everything that touches the customer — defined the product, designed the vehicle, built the brand, and sold the cars through its own retail network — while Seres built them. That arrangement is what turned a loss-making minivan maker into a company with CNY 165 billion of revenue.

The arc across the last three years is one of the steepest in the industry, in both directions.

**2021 to 2023 — the pre-Huawei company.** Revenue of CNY 16.7 billion in 2021 rising to CNY 35.8 billion in 2023, with losses every year: CNY 1.82 billion, CNY 3.83 billion, CNY 2.45 billion. This was a subscale manufacturer going nowhere.

**2024 to 2025 — the Huawei years.** Revenue quadrupled to CNY 145.2 billion in 2024 and CNY 165.1 billion in 2025, and the company made money for the first time: CNY 5.95 billion and CNY 5.96 billion of net income. Gross margin reached 29.1% in 2025 — extraordinary for a volume carmaker and a direct product of Huawei's brand pricing power. Management spent heavily to secure the relationship: CNY 2.5 billion in July 2024 for the AITO trademarks and design patents, and CNY 11.5 billion in August 2024 for a 10% stake in Shenzhen Yinwang, Huawei's intelligent-automotive unit (the deal completed in September 2025). On 5 November 2025 the company listed in Hong Kong at HK$131.5 a share, raising roughly CNY 12.9 billion.

**2026 — the unwind.** The story since has contracted on every axis. First-half revenue fell 7.87% to CNY 57.49 billion, gross margin fell 4.7 percentage points to 21.8%, and the company swung to a net loss of CNY 1.72 billion from a CNY 2.94 billion profit a year earlier. In June the company cut the entry price of the new M6 by CNY 50,000, from CNY 279,800 to CNY 229,800 — an 18% cut on the trim that sets the brand's price floor. Then on 15 September 2026 Huawei handed operational control of AITO back to Seres: product definition, vehicle design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations all transfer. AITO stays inside Huawei's HIMA alliance and keeps buying Huawei's driving software, but Seres must now build and fund its own sales network.

**What was quietly added.** While the core brand was shrinking, 2026 saw a remarkable burst of new initiatives: a premium-charging joint venture with BMW and Mercedes (17 April), a new vehicle brand connected to ByteDance (3 June), a second new brand called Aiva through affiliate Saidou (9 June), a humanoid robot (15 June), and a United Arab Emirates dealership (6 February). Five new directions in five months, from a company whose one profitable product line was losing share.

---

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

The company's explanation for the half-year loss is specific and testable. It blames input costs — battery-grade lithium carbonate up 132.2% year on year on an average daily price basis, plus "structural shortages and sharp price increases" in automotive-grade chips — and says it chose not to pass those costs to customers. It also took a CNY 1.75 billion write-down of intangible assets, attributed to "rapid technological iteration in the NEV industry."

| Management's claim | What the filed numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| The problem is input costs, not demand | Unit sales were 196,580, down only 1.02%; electric-vehicle units actually rose 3.87% to 178,777. Revenue fell 7.87%, so the average selling price fell about 7%. Gross margin fell 4.7 points. | **Largely supported.** Volume held; price and cost did the damage. This is genuinely a margin event, not a demand collapse. |
| "We declined to pass these costs to customers" | True in the sense that prices were not raised — but the company went the other way and *cut* the M6 entry price by CNY 50,000 in June. | **Poorer than the story.** This is not restraint; it is the absence of pricing power, described kindly. |
| Scale is still building | Half-year revenue of CNY 57.49 billion is below the CNY 62.40 billion of a year earlier; the second half of 2025 alone did CNY 102.6 billion. The business is running below its own recent peak. | **Diverges.** |
| The write-down reflects industry pace | The CNY 1.75 billion charge sits against CNY 12.3 billion of intangible assets carried on the balance sheet, much of it capitalised development spending. Writing off capitalised development because technology moved on is the textbook sign that the spending was capitalised too aggressively in the first place. | **Concerning.** The charge is honest; what it reveals about the earlier accounting is not flattering. |
| The balance sheet is a fortress — cash above CNY 73.15 billion, 57% of total assets, with interest-bearing debt only 3.2% of assets | Both figures are accurate. But the cash is funded by supplier credit: CNY 38.8 billion of notes payable to suppliers plus CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Net working capital is only CNY 3.84 billion. The company collects from customers in about 8 days and pays suppliers in about 61. | **Accurate but seriously misleading if read as spare cash.** See section 6. |

**The single most important forensic finding in this file** concerns that cash. In the first quarter of 2026, operating cash flow was *minus CNY 20.95 billion* in three months — the supplier float draining after the year-end volume push. The second quarter put CNY 8.47 billion back. Across the half, operating cash flow was minus CNY 12.38 billion. A cash balance that swings by twenty billion on working-capital timing is not a store of value the way an investor instinctively reads "57% of assets are cash." It is the float of a business that is paid instantly and pays late, and it shrinks when volumes shrink.

**Two numbers in our own screener file are wrong and must not be used.** The scan reports price-to-free-cash-flow of 2.0x and a discounted-cash-flow fair value of 198.1 — both computed from the 2025 peak-year cash flow. On a trailing twelve-month basis free cash flow is *minus* CNY 3.27 billion. The screener's net-debt field is also wrong; the corrected balance-sheet figure is in section 6.

---

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rating: Declining** (reinforced 2026-10-26 by the third-quarter volume slump), judged from disclosure behaviour rather than call transcripts, since none exist.

The sequence is telling. On **12 July 2026** the company issued a profit warning flagging a half-year net loss of CNY 1.5 billion to CNY 1.8 billion and naming the causes as rising material costs and asset write-downs. On **19 August 2026** it reported a loss of CNY 1.72 billion — inside its own range, and close to the middle of it. That is competent, unpanicked disclosure and it deserves credit.

But the *content* of the disclosure has shifted from offensive to defensive in one year. The 2025 language was about scale, premium positioning and a 29% gross margin. The 2026 language is about lithium prices, chip shortages, write-downs and "maintaining premium supply standards" — the vocabulary of a management team explaining a result rather than setting a direction. Research and development spending rose 27.4% to CNY 3.73 billion into a shrinking revenue base, which reads as commitment rather than retreat; but it sits alongside five new ventures launched in five months, which reads as a company casting about for the next story because the current one has stopped working.

---

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Score: Medium.**

The evidence that exists is good. The July warning was issued roughly five weeks before the result, gave a numerical range, named the causes, and the reported figure landed inside it. Chinese issuers are required to warn on large swings, so this is compliance rather than virtue — but plenty of companies warn late, warn vaguely, or warn low and then miss their own range. Seres did none of those.

Against that, the screener's earnings-beat record is 2 of the last 4 quarters, a 50% hit rate, which is coin-flip. And there is a structural pattern the director should hold in mind: this company's results are extremely back-half-weighted. The first half of 2025 was CNY 62.4 billion of revenue against CNY 102.6 billion in the second half. The same shape is embedded in the current consensus, which expects CNY 159.3 billion for full-year 2026 against CNY 57.5 billion delivered in the first half — implying a second half of roughly CNY 102 billion, essentially matching the prior year's record second half at a moment when the brand is losing share. That is a demanding number and it has not been de-risked.

---

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

With no calls, the pressure points must be inferred from what the company does and does not quantify. Three stand out.

**The Huawei dependency was never quantified, and now it is changing.** Seres has never disclosed what it pays Huawei — for the driving software, for the retail channel, for the brand. The 15 September restructuring changes all of those economics at once, and the company disclosed no new fee or equity arrangement alongside it. An investor is being asked to underwrite a transition whose cost is undisclosed.

**AITO's own volumes are not broken out.** The company reports total units. The alliance-level data that is public tells an uncomfortable story: Huawei's HIMA alliance delivered about 192,000 units from January to May 2026, up 26.5% year on year, while Seres's revenue fell 8% over the half. The alliance is growing; Seres's share of it is not. In August, HIMA deliveries themselves turned negative, down 5.52% year on year.

**Nobody has been made to explain the working-capital swing.** A negative CNY 20.95 billion operating quarter in a company that headlines its cash position is the question I would ask first, and there is no public forum in which it has been asked.

There is a further gap worth stating plainly: I could find no dated analyst price target for the Hong Kong line. Our data provider has no price-target coverage for this listing, and the web-search budget for this session was exhausted before a broker target could be sourced. I therefore use no target figure anywhere in this file.

---

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 **The cash is supplier float, not a war chest.** Cash and short-term investments of CNY 73.13 billion are financed by CNY 38.8 billion of supplier notes and CNY 19.9 billion of trade payables. Netting the supplier notes and the CNY 4.35 billion of genuine borrowings leaves roughly **CNY 30 billion of defensible net cash** — about CNY 17.2 a share, or HK$20.1. The company's own framing (debt is 3.2% of assets) implies nearly CNY 69 billion, which would be more than the entire Hong Kong-line market value. I do not accept that framing, and the first quarter's cash flow is the reason.

🔴 **Returns on capital have gone to nothing.** Trailing return on equity is 3.6% and return on invested capital 0.7%. The screener's full-year figures are worse still. A company earning less on its capital than it can earn on a bank deposit is not compounding.

🔴 **Capitalised development spending written off.** CNY 1.75 billion of intangibles impaired for "rapid technological iteration," against CNY 12.3 billion still carried. A further CNY 2.31 billion sits in "other gains and losses."

🔴 **The partner stepped back from this brand and only this brand.** Huawei retains operational leadership of the other four HIMA marques — Luxeed, Stelato, Maextro and Shangjie. It handed back the one it had built first. That ordering matters.

🔴 **Five new ventures in five months** while the core brand shrank: a charging joint venture, a ByteDance-linked brand, the Aiva brand, a humanoid robot, a Gulf dealership. Each is a call on management attention and capital.

🔴 **The listing itself was sold at a peak.** The November 2025 initial public offering priced at HK$131.5, valuing the whole company near CNY 196 billion on CNY 165 billion of revenue — roughly 1.2x revenue for a vehicle assembler, when the closest listed comparables trade around 0.55x to 0.65x. Much of the 73% decline since is the deflation of that price, not new information.

🟢 **Volume held — in the first half only.** Units fell only 1.02% and electric units rose 3.87% in the first half of 2026. 🔴 Superseded for the third quarter: July, August and September new-energy sales fell 45.65%, 43.96% and 34.48% year on year (company reports, 8 October 2026 for September), and year-to-date sales are down about 17%.

🟢 **The loss is smaller than it looks.** Strip the CNY 1.75 billion write-down and the half-year result is an operating stumble of a few percent on CNY 57.5 billion of revenue, not a structural cash loss.

🟢 **Seres now owns the customer.** Whatever the execution risk, product definition, design, brand and retail all move in-house from 15 September. The retail margin Huawei captured is now Seres's to capture — and Seres already owns the AITO trademarks outright.

🟢 **A real, under-recognised financial asset.** The 10% stake in Huawei's Yinwang unit, bought for CNY 11.5 billion and carried at about CNY 13.5 billion, is a minority interest in the supplier of driving software to the entire HIMA alliance and to third parties. It earns no line in the income statement that an investor would notice.

🟢 **Honest pre-announcement.** The July warning was specific, early and accurate.

---

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

**The language of the 15 September announcement is the signal.** Huawei transferred "product definition, product design, brand marketing, retail channels and service operations." That is not a delegation of tasks; it is the return of an entire commercial function. Read one way it is a promotion — Seres graduates from contract manufacturer to brand owner. Read the other way, the party that made the brand work has decided its time is better spent on four other brands, and the manufacturer now has to reproduce Huawei's retail machine from a standing start, with falling volumes, in a price war. Both readings are available from the same sentence. The second is the one the share price is pricing.

**The sequencing of the write-down.** The impairment of capitalised development landed in the same half as the loss of product-definition authority. Intangible assets are written down when the cash flows behind them shrink. It is hard not to read the charge as an early, quiet acknowledgement of the September change.

**A tell in the working capital.** Days of payables outstanding is about 61 against 8 days of receivables and 7 days of inventory — a cash conversion cycle of minus 47 days. That is a supplier-financed model. It works beautifully at scale and reverses violently on the way down, which is exactly what the first quarter showed.

**A new voice, and what it is selling.** The 2026 initiative list — robotics, an internet-company car brand, a charging network with German luxury marques — is the vocabulary of a company that wants to be valued as a technology platform rather than an assembler. That ambition is not yet visible anywhere in the returns on capital.

---

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: DETERIORATING**, with a genuine restructuring underway that could change the label but has not yet; the third-quarter volume data (8 October 2026) moves the label further in the wrong direction. The 30 October 2026 third-quarter report is the test: gross margin at or above 22% with positive operating cash flow would say the slump is a model-changeover and handover gap; gross margin below 18% or another large operating cash outflow would say the brand is losing customers, not just price.

Revenue is down 8%, gross margin down 4.7 points, the company has swung to a loss, operating cash flow ran minus CNY 12.38 billion in the half, and the brand is losing share inside an alliance that is growing. The Huawei handover is a real pivot and may prove to be the right one, but it is one week old and entirely unproven.

**The single thing the director must weigh before sizing this:** almost all of the apparent cheapness is a balance-sheet add-back, not an earnings discount. Value the whole company on revenue with no cash credit and the Hong Kong line trades at roughly 0.33x revenue against 0.65x for Li Auto and 0.55x for Leapmotor — a discount, but a defensible one for a brand losing relative share. Credit the CNY 30 billion of net cash and the operating business is being valued at almost nothing. The entire investment case turns on whether that cash is spare or is supplier float that a volume decline would consume. On the first quarter's evidence, it is a great deal more float than spare. Size the position to the version of the balance sheet you actually believe, not the version the company presents.

**Economic moat.** The moat here was never Seres's. It was Huawei's brand, Huawei's driving software and Huawei's retail network, rented to a manufacturer that supplied the factory. The type is best described as intangible-brand and channel access, held on loan. The evidence says it is narrowing on every measure the returns provide: gross margin from 29.1% in 2025 to 21.8% in the first half of 2026, return on invested capital down to 0.7%, pricing cut by CNY 50,000 on the entry trim, and the brand shrinking while its own alliance grew 26.5% through May. By the returns-and-margin test this is an eroding moat, not a wide one, and the 15 September transfer of channel and brand authority is the formal confirmation of that erosion rather than a cure for it.

**Terminal value.** The threat is real but not terminal. China's electric-vehicle market is growing, not shrinking, so this is not a melting base. The structural risk is different: in a vehicle built around someone else's driving software and sold through someone else's shops, the durable economics accrue to the software and channel owner, and the assembler is commoditised. Seres has partially hedged that — it owns 10% of Yinwang and it owns the AITO marks — but it has not escaped it. I judge the secular threat **material, not terminal**, and note that none of the eight named structural forces in our own controlled vocabulary describes this risk; forcing one on would be false precision.

**Fear-print or value trap?** Neither cleanly. It is a genuine de-rating from a genuinely absurd listing price, on top of a real margin shock, in a business whose competitive position got weaker in the same quarter. The cheapness is real on a revenue basis and overstated on a cash basis. That combination argues for patience and a small size, not for conviction in either direction.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a moat that is being eroded · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.
picks.sop_fair_value: Base case HK$41 a share for the Hong Kong line, down from HK$46.50 on 5 October 2026 because the vehicle-revenue assumption falls from CNY 160 billion to CNY 130 billion after the third-quarter volume slump; about a third above the HK$30.88 price of 26 October 2026, over eighteen months.
