# Clarkson PLC (CKN.L) - deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-09. Listing: London Stock Exchange, priced in pence (GBp). Live quote used: 4,550p (FMP, 9 November 2026; previous close 4,570p; 50-day average 5,078p; 52-week range 3,480p-5,485p). Update since the 26 October 2026 review: the shares have fallen about 10.7% from 5,095p with NO company news - FMP stock-news and press-release searches for 20 October-9 November 2026 returned nothing. The fall coincides with a shipping-sector de-rating (A.P. Moller-Maersk 19,865 DKK on 9 November vs a 50-day average of 23,143, about 14% below), so it reads as a sector move, not a company event.

Source note, stated plainly: FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing, FMP stock news and press-release searches for August-October 2026 returned nothing, and this run's web-search budget was again exhausted (9 November 2026) before any web lookup could be made. This deep dive therefore rests on FMP's half-yearly statements (to 30 June 2026), the screener metrics, and the committee's own record of 19 October 2026, which cited the 3 August 2026 interim results. No management quotes are reproduced because none could be sourced this week; none are invented.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Clarkson is the world's largest shipbroker, with a subscription research and data arm (Clarksons Research), a financial-services arm (Clarksons Securities) and a port-support business. The story has moved in a clean cycle: a 2021-2023 boom (revenue from 443m to 639m pounds), a plateau in 2024 (661m), a soft 2025 (631m, earnings per share down 22%), and then a sharp rebound in the first half of 2026 - revenue of 413.5m pounds, up 39% on the first half of 2025, the record half the committee noted on 19 October. The narrative has never been about a new growth driver; it is about being the biggest, best-informed intermediary in a cyclical market, and compounding a dividend through every phase.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / perception | Evidence (FMP statements) | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Record first half 2026 | H1-26 revenue 413.5m vs 297.8m (+39%); reported pre-tax profit 55.6m vs 37.5m; reported EPS 131p vs 93p | Corroborated |
| Strong balance sheet | Cash and deposits 339.5m vs total debt 59.4m (of which leases 48.9m) at 30 June 2026 | Corroborated, but see below |
| Cheap on trailing earnings (screener TTM EPS 4.94) | Half-year EPS: H2-25 120p + H1-26 131p = 251p reported trailing | The screener figure is a double count of a twice-yearly reporter. True trailing P/E (price to earnings) is about 20x reported, roughly 18x on an estimated underlying basis |
| Free cash flow 208m trailing | H2-25 +152.5m, H1-26 -28.5m = about 124m trailing; FY2025 about 64m | Overstated by the scan; cash flow is highly seasonal because staff bonuses accrue through the year and are paid in the first half |

The net cash is real but not all free. Payables of 335.6m at 30 June include accrued broker bonuses that are paid out each spring; the first halves of 2025 and 2026 both show large working-capital outflows (-139.5m and -76.9m). We credit roughly half of the 280m net cash (about 140m, roughly 450p a share) as genuinely surplus.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Not assessable from transcripts this week (none available). The capital-allocation actions speak instead: 24m pounds of buybacks and 23.9m of dividends in H1-26, plus 54.9m spent on acquisitions - a confident posture. Trajectory of the business itself: rising since the 2025 trough.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Clarkson does not give hard numeric guidance; it issues trading updates against market consensus. The screener's beat record (0 of 1) is too thin to judge. Medium reliability by default; the 2025 decline was a market softening, not a guidance failure we can document.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Without a transcript, the obvious pressure points are structural: how much of a record half is rate-driven (freight and tanker markets) versus repeatable volume; what share of the cash is owed to brokers; and how broking commissions hold up if newbuild ordering and sale-and-purchase activity cool.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: screener earnings and cash-flow figures are inflated by a twice-yearly reporting double count; the apparent cheapness is not real.
- Red: free cash flow fell 34.5% in FY2025 and has a 3-year compound rate of -25%; cash generation lags profit in the boom years because bonuses lag.
- Red: the multiple (about 20x reported trailing earnings) is the highest in the peer set at a point where the cycle is already strong.
- Green: revenue +39% and reported EPS +41% in H1-26; profit margins recovered (operating margin 13.4% vs 10.4%).
- Green: net cash, negligible debt, an Altman-Z of 4.1 (a solvency score; above 3 is safe), and a multi-decade record of rising dividends.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The 54.9m acquisition spend in H1-26 is new relative to 2025 (2.3m); its target could not be verified this week. Buybacks continued at a share price near the top of the range, which is a mild negative for allocation discipline.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: STABLE - a high-quality cyclical in an upswing, with the upswing visible in the numbers. The single most important thing to weigh: the stock is priced on strong-cycle earnings, not trough earnings, and the cheapness in the screen is an accounting double count. Moat: a narrow but real moat - scale and information advantage in broking (the biggest broker sees the most deal flow) plus a sticky data subscription franchise; returns on capital of about 14% are respectable rather than exceptional, and margins move with the cycle rather than eroding structurally. Secular threat: manageable - digital freight platforms and AI-assisted matching could chip at commodity broking, but large, bespoke shipping transactions still run on relationships and proprietary data. The price, not the business, is the problem: this is neither a fear-print nor a value trap; it is a good cyclical franchise fully priced.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

Total about 4,700p, which also matches the committee's 19 October 2026 fair value.

picks.bull_thesis: Danieli is a profitable, cash-rich steel-plant builder priced as if its record order book will not convert. On 2026-09-25 it reported a backlog of EUR 6.04B at 30 June 2026, up 12% in a year and worth about 1.6 years of revenue, while revenue fell 9% to EUR 3.83B because orders are being executed on later schedules. EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) held at EUR 438.9M and the company's own adjusted net cash, which strips out customer prepayments, rose about 48% to EUR 1,019.7M. At EUR 52.15 for the ordinary shares (FMP quote, 2026-11-16) and EUR 36.42 for the savings shares, the whole company is worth about EUR 3.18B, so the operating business is valued at roughly EUR 2.16B, or about 4.9 times EBITDA. The listed engineering peers in our peer file (Andritz, Metso, Valmet) trade at 12-20 times earnings on steadier aftermarket mixes; even a large discount to them leaves room. The 2026/27 guide (EBITDA EUR 430-450M, revenue EUR 3.9-4.2B, net profit stable or improving) sits about 10% below the pre-results consensus, and Equita reads it as prudent, with its own EBITDA estimate at EUR 471M. If the 2025/26 write-downs in Plant Making (tied to project delays and the Fata unit) prove one-off, as Kepler Cheuvreux expects, operating profit rebounds from a depressed EUR 220.8M toward EUR 290-300M. Steel Making (the ABS mill) is guided to grow EBITDA 26-40% to EUR 90-100M as the new Digimelter furnace, due by end-2026, ramps toward doubled capacity. The shift from blast furnaces to electric-arc and lower-carbon steel is a structural tailwind for Danieli's core product line. The advance float, about EUR 1.65B on top of the adjusted cash, earns interest for as long as the order book stays full, which is why net profit (EUR 230.4M, +5%) beats operating profit. Conditions: write-downs do not recur in the half-year results due around late March 2027, the backlog stays at EUR 5.8-6.0B as guided, and European energy costs do not crush ABS margins.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is old and has reasons. Return on invested capital is about 5.5% and return on equity about 9%, poor for a business that holds this much cash; the controlling family has paid out under 10% of profit for years (dividend flat at EUR 0.3146 per ordinary share, approved 2026-10-28, below the roughly EUR 0.38 brokers expected), so minority holders cannot count on the cash ever reaching them. The headline net cash of EUR 2.67B is mostly customer prepayments owed back as work; the true figure is about EUR 1.0B and is guided flat next year while Steel Making's net debt rises to EUR 250-300M to fund a capacity expansion with commodity-steel returns. 2025/26 operating profit fell 27% on write-downs that management has explained thinly, and Plant Making's margin is guided down from about 13.2% to about 11-12% on higher revenue, which suggests newer orders are priced tighter or carry more risk. Profit growth leaned on financial income including a EUR 26.9M currency gain that management itself expects to fade. The business is cyclical: its customers are steelmakers whose capital budgets depend on steel prices, European demand is weak, and Chinese plant builders compete hard on price in emerging markets. The margin record in the last inflation wave was poor (gross margin from 29.4% in the year to June 2019 to 18.2% in the year to June 2022), and the macro backdrop today is inflationary. The screener's cheapness signals are flattered: price to free cash flow of 5.3x includes a EUR 386M working-capital inflow from advances, and normalized free cash flow is closer to EUR 200-250M, a 6-8% yield rather than 19%. The ordinary shares also carry a 43% premium to the economically near-identical savings shares; a narrowing of that gap would hurt ordinary holders even if the business performs. What would confirm the bear case: another write-down or a backlog below EUR 5.8B in the half-year results, or an EBITDA run-rate under EUR 430M.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing Danieli as a cyclical project house in an earnings downgrade, and on the near term it is broadly right: the 2026/27 EBITDA guide of EUR 430-450M sits about 10% below the roughly EUR 497M Bloomberg consensus that prevailed before 2026-09-25, and every broker we found cut its target on 2026-09-29. Where we disagree is on what the cheapness is resting on. The street focuses on the write-downs; we think the bigger mispricing risk runs both ways around the cash. Screens that read EUR 2.67B of net cash and a 5.3x price to free cash flow overstate the value, because most of that cash is customer prepayments; the company's adjusted figure is EUR 1.02B. On the other side, even with only EUR 1.02B credited, the operating business trades at about 4.9 times EBITDA on a record EUR 6.04B order book, which does not discount a structurally shrinking company. Our base fair value of EUR 61 is below every published broker target (EUR 68-81, 2026-09-29), because we discount the engineering business heavily for low returns and family control. The street is not looking the wrong way; it is looking at the right problems and pricing them a little too harshly.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation, maturity or refinancing risk exists: debt is EUR 874M against EUR 3.54B of cash, and adjusted net cash is about EUR 1.0B. The risky window is the next four to five months up to the half-year report (due around late March 2027, date unconfirmed). Risks inside it: further Plant Making write-downs or delays that push revenue below the EUR 3.9B floor; a slowdown in new orders that would shrink both project margin and the interest-earning advance float; European energy-price spikes that hit the ABS mill while its new furnace is still ramping; and steel-industry capital spending stalling if steel prices or tariffs turn. The ex-dividend date of 2026-11-23 will lower the price by about EUR 0.31 mechanically.
picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure is identifiable. The dividend was held flat, not cut, so yield holders have no trigger to sell. The ordinary float is thin (about 36.4M shares outstanding, family-controlled, roughly 31,000 shares traded on 2026-11-16) and the stock sits in Italian small- and mid-cap mandates, so any outflow from that segment or a European-cyclicals de-rating can move the price sharply in either direction, as the 15.4% one-day fall on 2026-09-28 showed. The more likely route to our entry level is that kind of sector or style sell-off, not a mechanical event. The stock has already traded at EUR 50 (2026-09-28) and as low as EUR 44.30 within the last year.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near EUR 50.8, which a sector-wide sell-off in European cyclicals or Italian small caps could deliver; the stock already traded at EUR 50 on 2026-09-28. The thesis holds: a record EUR 6.04B order book, flat EBITDA of EUR 438.9M and adjusted net cash up to EUR 1.02B (all at 30 June 2026) describe a healthy if lumpy business, and the 2025/26 profit hit came from write-downs rather than lost demand. We value the ordinary shares at about EUR 61 by their parts (Plant Making at 6.5 times guided EBITDA, the ABS mill at 4.5 times, plus EUR 1.02B of adjusted net cash), about 17% above today's EUR 52.15; that is just short of the 20% discount we require in the current inflationary backdrop, so we do not buy at today's price. The adverse case is about EUR 48 and the favorable case about EUR 84. Two cautions shape our conviction, which is moderate: the headline EUR 2.67B of net cash is mostly customer prepayments and should not be counted as owners' money, and the family has shown no sign of returning the real EUR 1B either, which keeps returns on capital near 5.5%. The engineering moat is narrow but real, and the shift to electric-arc steelmaking helps rather than threatens it. What would change our view: another write-down or a backlog under EUR 5.8B in the half-year report would put the thesis in doubt; a larger payout, buyback or savings-share conversion would lift the fair value.
picks.forcing_function: There is no hard, dated re-rating event. The next checkpoints are the half-year report to 31 December 2026 (due around late March 2027; last year's came 2026-03-25), which will show whether the write-downs stopped and whether the guide is being beaten, and the Digimelter furnace start-up at ABS targeted by end-2026. Events that would force a faster re-rating and are not announced: a larger payout or buyback using the EUR 1B of adjusted net cash, a revived conversion of savings shares into ordinary shares (proposed in 2020 at 0.65 ordinary per savings share, not completed), or a large order announcement. None of these is promised, so we do not lean on them.

# Danieli & C. Officine Meccaniche (DAN.MI): a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Prices are for the Milan-listed ordinary (voting) shares, in euros. Danieli also lists non-voting savings shares (DANR.MI); both are discussed where the difference matters.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists for this name in our data provider, and Danieli does not hold a widely transcribed analyst call. This dossier is built from the dated company releases and press coverage of them instead: the full-year 2025/26 results approved on 2026-09-25 (fiscal year to 30 June 2026), the segment guidance published 2026-10-16, the shareholder meeting of 2026-10-28, and the broker notes reported on 2026-09-29. Where we would normally quote management on a call, we quote the release language as reported. No quote below is invented; where a figure could not be sourced, we say so.

---

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Danieli is two businesses under one roof. Plant Making (about 72% of 2025/26 revenue, EUR 2.78B) designs and builds steel mills and rolling lines for customers worldwide, with SMS group and Primetals (both private) as its main Western rivals. Steel Making (about 28%, EUR 1.06B) is ABS, Danieli's own specialty-steel mill in northern Italy.

The story over the last two years has narrowed from growth to delivery. In 2023-24 revenue rose to a peak of EUR 4.35B (year to June 2024) on the post-pandemic wave of electric-arc-furnace and "green steel" orders. Since then revenue has fallen two years running (EUR 4.20B, then EUR 3.83B, down 9% in 2025/26), while the order book has kept growing: EUR 6.04B at 30 June 2026 against EUR 5.38B a year earlier. Management's message in the September 2026 release is that the revenue dip is timing, not demand: orders are being executed on later schedules.

What is new in 2025/26 is the cost of execution. Operating profit fell 27% to EUR 220.8M because of higher depreciation and write-downs in Plant Making, which brokers tied to the Fata subsidiary and to "project delays and technical problems" (Equita, as reported 2026-09-29). The ABS story has also shifted from margin defence to capacity growth: the "Digimelter" furnace at ABS is under construction with completion targeted by end-2026, part of a plan to double installed capacity.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (dated) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue decline is project timing, demand intact (2026-09-25) | Backlog up 12% to EUR 6.04B while revenue fell 9%; backlog now covers about 1.6 years of sales | Supported |
| EBITDA "in line" with last year (2026-09-25) | EUR 438.9M vs EUR 437.8M; but it missed a consensus of about EUR 456M | Supported, but below the street |
| Cash generation "more than sufficient" to fund investment and R&D (2026-09-25) | Operating cash flow EUR 880M, capex EUR 155M; adjusted net cash rose to EUR 1,019.7M from EUR 688.9M | Supported, with a caveat below |
| Net profit up 5% to EUR 230.4M | Includes EUR 83.4M of financial income, of which EUR 26.9M was a currency gain; operating profit fell 27% | Quality of the beat is weak: it came below the operating line |
| 2026/27 guide: revenue EUR 3.9-4.2B, EBITDA EUR 430-450M, adjusted net cash EUR 1.0-1.1B, net profit "stable or improving" (2026-09-25) | The EBITDA midpoint is flat on 2025/26 and about 10% below the roughly EUR 497M Bloomberg consensus cited in the press | Conservative; credibility hinges on the write-downs not recurring |

**The cash caveat that matters most.** The balance sheet shows EUR 3.54B of cash and short-term investments against EUR 874M of debt, so the headline net cash is about EUR 2.67B. But much of that cash is customer prepayments (advances) on projects in the order book: money Danieli holds but owes back in the form of work. The company's own "adjusted" net cash, which strips these advances out, is EUR 1,019.7M at June 2026 and guided to EUR 1.0-1.1B next year. Equity investors should anchor on about EUR 1.0B, not EUR 2.67B. The advances are not worthless (they earn interest as long as the order book stays full, which is part of why net profit beats operating profit), but they are a float, not owners' money.

The same caveat inflates the cash-flow figures. Free cash flow of EUR 725M in 2025/26 (FMP) includes a EUR 386M working-capital inflow, mostly advances. A normalized figure is closer to EUR 200-250M a year (EBITDA of about EUR 440M, less roughly EUR 90M of tax and EUR 155M of capex, plus interest on the adjusted cash). The screener's "price to free cash flow of 5.3x" overstates the cheapness for that reason.

**Data anomaly.** The screener input shows trailing diluted EPS of 4.69; the fiscal year ends on 30 June, so the trailing year to 2026-06-30 is the fiscal year itself, with reported EPS of EUR 3.22. We use 3.22 and treat 4.69 as a data error.

**Segment numbers (2026-10-16 release).**

| Segment | 2025/26 revenue | 2025/26 EBITDA (margin) | 2026/27 guide EBITDA | Net cash (debt) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plant Making | EUR 2,777M | EUR 368M (13.2%) | EUR 340-360M | Net cash EUR 1.25-1.4B guided |
| Steel Making (ABS) | EUR 1,056M | EUR 71M (6.8%) | EUR 90-100M | Net debt EUR 216M, guided to EUR 250-300M |

Plant Making's margin is guided down (to roughly 11-12%) on higher revenue, which tells you the newer orders were priced more tightly or carry more cost risk. Steel Making is guided up on volumes and efficiency.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, turning more defensive.** Without call transcripts we judge tone from the releases. The 2026-09-25 release leads with the backlog and the "good positive net financial position", and frames 2026/27 as "stable or improving" profit. The risk list has grown: energy costs, weak European demand and the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran are all named. Guidance was given in specific ranges for every line, and three weeks later (2026-10-16) the company volunteered a segment split, which is more disclosure than Danieli usually gives. That reads as a response to the share-price fall, not as a change in confidence. Kepler Cheuvreux's complaint (2026-09-29) about "limited information on the write-downs" is the clearest sign that disclosure lags what investors want.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium.** Danieli's guidance has historically been cautious, and the order book supports the revenue range. But the 2025/26 year missed the street on revenue (3.9% below consensus, per Banca Akros) and on EBITDA, and the miss below EBITDA came from write-downs that were not flagged ahead of time. We could not find the September 2025 guidance figures to score last year's delivery line by line, so we do not claim a beat rate. Equita's reading (2026-09-28) is that the 2026/27 guide "contains prudence" and can be beaten; Equita's own estimates sit above it (EBITDA EUR 471M, net cash ex-advances about EUR 1.12B, backlog EUR 6.25B). That is a broker opinion, not evidence.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The write-downs.** Several brokers (Equita, Kepler, as reported 2026-09-29) traced the profit miss to write-downs in Plant Making tied to project delays and technical problems, and to Fata. Kepler cut 2026/27 and 2027/28 EBIT estimates by 20-22% and said better project execution is "essential". Management has not, in anything we found, quantified the write-downs or said they are finished.
- **The dividend.** EUR 0.3146 per ordinary share and EUR 0.3353 per savings share (approved 2026-10-28, paid from 25 November 2026, ex-date 23 November) were flat and below the roughly EUR 0.38 / 0.40 analysts expected. A payout under 10% of net profit, with EUR 1B of adjusted net cash, is a long-standing complaint.
- **Margin direction in Plant Making.** Guidance implies a lower margin on higher revenue.

Broker targets after the results (all dated 2026-09-29): Equita buy, EUR 81 ordinary / EUR 56 savings; Kepler Cheuvreux buy, cut from EUR 80 to EUR 68; Banca Akros accumulate, cut from EUR 75 to EUR 70. Every listed broker cut; none downgraded.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Operating profit down 27% in 2025/26 on write-downs that management has explained only thinly (2026-09-25 release; Kepler 2026-09-29).
- Red: Net profit growth of 5% leaned on financial income, including a EUR 26.9M currency gain that management says will be "more neutral" next year.
- Red: Plant Making margin guided down from about 13.2% to about 11-12% (2026-10-16).
- Red: Payout stays tiny and flat; the controlling family shows no sign of returning the cash pile.
- Red: Margins were badly squeezed by the last inflation wave (gross margin fell from 29.4% in the year to June 2019 to 18.2% in the year to June 2022 on our inflation screen).
- Green: Order book at a high of EUR 6.04B, up 12% (30 June 2026).
- Green: Adjusted net cash up about 48% to EUR 1,019.7M in one year.
- Green: Steel Making guided to grow EBITDA 26-40% (2026-10-16) as the new furnace ramps.
- Green: More disclosure (segment guidance) arrived three weeks after the sell-off.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The headline profit and the operating profit now move in opposite directions. The interest earned on the advance float is doing more of the work, which means a slowdown in new orders would hit profit twice: through lower project margin and lower interest on a shrinking float.
- Plant Making's net cash (guided EUR 1.25-1.4B) funds Steel Making's rising net debt (guided EUR 250-300M). The group is quietly using the engineering business's cash to double capacity at its own steel mill. That is a capital-allocation choice with commodity-steel returns.
- The ordinary shares trade about 43% above the non-voting savings shares (EUR 52.15 against EUR 36.42 on 2026-11-16), even though the savings shares receive a slightly higher dividend. The 2020 proposal to convert savings shares at 0.65 ordinary each did not proceed; the share count still shows both classes. Whoever buys the ordinary shares is paying for votes that, in practice, sit with the controlling family.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** Demand, measured by the order book, is healthy; execution, measured by operating profit, slipped; guidance resets expectations to flat.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** the cash pile is about EUR 1.0B, not EUR 2.67B, and the family has shown no intent to distribute it. The equity is cheap on an enterprise basis (about 4.9 times EBITDA once the adjusted net cash is subtracted, against listed engineering peers in the peer file trading at 12-20 times earnings), but the discount has persisted for years because returns on capital are low (about 5.5% return on invested capital) and minority holders have little say.

**Moat.** A narrow but real moat built on scale and know-how: Danieli is one of three Western suppliers able to deliver a full steel plant, and a leader in electric-arc-furnace mini-mills. The width is limited by low returns on capital, lumpy project risk and Chinese plant builders competing on price in emerging markets. Gross margin has expanded recently (53.5% on the provider's classification), but operating margin fell; we read the trend as stable, not widening.

**Secular threat.** Manageable. The move from blast furnaces to electric-arc and "green" steel is a tailwind for Danieli's order book, not a threat. The real risk is cyclical (steel-industry capital spending) and competitive (Chinese engineering), not terminal. The cheapness is mostly a long-standing governance and cyclicality discount plus a fresh execution scare, not a shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
picks.sop_breakdown: Base case, per ordinary share (EUR): Plant Making EUR 350M EBITDA (midpoint of the 2026-10-16 guide) x 6.5 = EUR 2,275M (about 37.3/share); Steel Making EUR 95M EBITDA (guide midpoint) x 4.5 = EUR 428M (about 7.0/share); adjusted net cash EUR 1,020M at 2026-06-30 (about 16.7/share). Equity EUR 3,723M over 60.95M ordinary-equivalent shares (36.37M ordinary plus 35.20M savings at the current 1.43x price ratio) = about EUR 61. The 6.5x engineering multiple is a deliberate discount to the listed peers (12-20x earnings in the peer file) for lumpy project risk, low returns on capital and family control. No credit for the advance float in the base case.
picks.sop_bull: Favorable parts, per ordinary share. Plant Making: EUR 380M EBITDA (above the EUR 340-360M guide as write-downs normalize) x 8.0 = EUR 3,040M. Steel Making (ABS): EUR 100M EBITDA (top of guide) x 5.5 = EUR 550M. Overlays: adjusted net cash EUR 1,020M (company figure at 2026-06-30) plus EUR 500M of credit for the structural advance float (about 30% of the roughly EUR 1.65B of prepayment cash, which earns interest while the order book is stable). Equity EUR 5,110M. Share count: 36.37M ordinary and 35.20M savings shares outstanding after 9.73M treasury shares (30 June 2026); savings shares converted to ordinary equivalents at today's 1.43x price ratio gives 60.95M ordinary-equivalent shares. Value about EUR 84 per ordinary share. No pending special distribution: the EUR 0.3146 dividend goes ex on 2026-11-23 and is ordinary.
picks.sop_bear: Adverse parts, per ordinary share. Plant Making: EUR 320M EBITDA (below guide on further write-downs and weak European demand) x 5.0 = EUR 1,600M. Steel Making (ABS): EUR 80M EBITDA (energy costs offset the new furnace) x 4.0 = EUR 320M. Overlay: adjusted net cash EUR 1,000M (low end of guide), no credit for the advance float. Equity EUR 2,920M over 60.95M ordinary-equivalent shares = about EUR 48 per ordinary share. A wider ordinary-to-savings premium compression would push this lower; we hold the ratio constant.
picks.risk_reward: From EUR 52.15: downside to the adverse case of EUR 48 is about 8%; upside to the base fair value of EUR 61 is about 17%; the favorable case of EUR 84 is about 61% higher. The pipeline computes the ratios from these levels.
picks.catalyst_status_plain: already happened
picks.peer_comps_note: Danieli is cheap against the listed engineering peers in its peer file. At EUR 52.15 (ordinary) and EUR 36.42 (savings) the combined equity is about EUR 3.18B; subtracting the company's adjusted net cash of EUR 1.02B leaves an operating value of about EUR 2.16B, or about 4.9 times 2025/26 EBITDA of EUR 438.9M and about 7.4 times a normalized operating profit of roughly EUR 290M. The peer file places Andritz and Metso at 12-20 times earnings on steadier aftermarket mixes; the two closest rivals (SMS group and Primetals) are private, so the listed set is a proxy. Most of the gap is justified: project-based, lumpy earnings, about 5.5% return on invested capital, a write-down-hit year and family control with a tiny payout. We apply 6.5x to Plant Making and 4.5x to the ABS steel mill, well below peers, and still find about 17% upside. The peer file carries no live override multiple and no shared-regulatory flag, so the residual discount is name-specific, not sector beta.
picks.thesis_evidence: The load-bearing claims hold on the latest dated numbers. 2026-09-25 (results to 2026-06-30): order backlog EUR 6,038M vs EUR 5,384M a year earlier; EBITDA EUR 438.9M vs EUR 437.8M; adjusted net cash EUR 1,019.7M vs EUR 688.9M; net profit EUR 230.4M (+5%). 2026-10-16 segment guidance: Plant Making EBITDA EUR 340-360M with net cash EUR 1.25-1.4B, Steel Making EBITDA EUR 90-100M. The blemish is execution: operating profit fell 27% to EUR 220.8M on Plant Making write-downs (project delays, Fata), which brokers expect to normalize but management has not quantified. That is a risk to watch in the half-year report, not a disproven claim.
picks.macro_fit_note: The backdrop is reflation (growth up, inflation sticky) in a debt-cycle phase of positive real rates that rewards cash today over long-dated stories; Danieli is a cash-now business and earns interest on about EUR 3.5B of gross cash, which helps. Against that, its margins were squeezed in the last inflation wave (gross margin 29.4% to 18.2%, year to June 2019 vs year to June 2022) and there is no pass-through evidence in the transcript (none exists); the 2026-10-16 guide instead shows Plant Making margin falling to about 11-12% and the company flags energy costs as a risk.
picks.entry_plain: buy near 50.8 EUR, which a sector-wide or style-wide sell-off could deliver

picks.bull_thesis: The bull case is a margin repair that the market is not yet paying for. NRC has turned from a NOK 1.0 billion loss in 2024 into its best quarter since the restart: third-quarter 2026 EBIT of NOK 91 million on NOK 1.84 billion of revenue (about a 5% margin), up roughly 40% year on year, with Norway (NOK 15 million vs NOK 5 million), Sweden (NOK 10 million vs NOK 1 million) and the Kept unit (5.3% margin vs a loss) all improving. Year to date EBIT is NOK 123 million even after a NOK 71 million one-off legal charge in Sweden, so the underlying run-rate is closer to NOK 190-200 million for nine months. Management kept and extended its margin path: adjusted EBIT margin above 3.5% in 2027 and above 5.0% in 2028. Nordic rail investment is a long-term public commitment, the tender pipeline is NOK 43-44 billion, and Finland (revenue up 37% in Q3 2026) has secured a second wave of light-rail projects with production mainly from 2027. If order intake reaches the NOK 10 billion 2027 target, 2028 revenue of NOK 8-9 billion at a 5% margin gives EBIT of NOK 400-450 million, against an enterprise value (market value plus net debt including leases) of about NOK 2.37 billion today, under 6x. Two free options sit on top: the NOK 566 million final claim submitted to Bane NOR on the ETM project, and the stated ambition to pay out at least 30% of profit as dividends once retained earnings turn positive. Conditions: order intake must recover in the next two to three quarters, the margin gains must hold on lower volume, and the Bane NOR claim must settle for something.
picks.bear_thesis: The bear case is that the repair arrived just as the volume left. On 5 November 2026 management cut 2026 revenue guidance by about 13% (to about NOK 6.5 billion from about NOK 7.5 billion), withdrew the 2028 revenue target, and replaced it with order-intake targets because it can no longer forecast project timing. The backlog fell to NOK 7.88 billion, down about 12% in one quarter and about 8% in a year, and the third-quarter book-to-bill was 0.7x. Management itself called commercial performance weak, with Norwegian tender cancellations and a below-target win rate. A contractor's revenue follows its backlog with a lag, so 2027 revenue may be flat to down, and operating leverage cuts both ways on a business earning 3-5% margins. The balance sheet leaves little room: net debt of NOK 823 million including leases (NOK 491 million excluding leases), no reported cash at 30 September 2026, goodwill of NOK 1.74 billion against equity of NOK 1.70 billion, Altman Z (a solvency score) of 1.9 and a five-year history of losses, write-downs and an equity raise in 2024. Cash flow is lumpy: operating cash flow was negative in Q1 and Q3 2026 and roughly zero for the year to date. Diluted shares rose to about 184 million against about 173 million basic in Q3 2026, an unexplained potential dilution. The NOK 566 million Bane NOR claim had negotiations scheduled for Q3 2026 and the results say nothing about the outcome. The inflation record is weak: gross margin fell about 4 points in 2021-22. What would confirm the bear case: another quarter of book-to-bill below 1.0x, a backlog under NOK 7 billion, or a 2026 EBIT margin below the 3% guide.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: little, and less than last time. Before 5 November 2026 the market was pricing a repaired contractor heading to more than NOK 10 billion of revenue at a 5% margin by 2028. The company has now withdrawn the revenue half of that. The few covering analysts we can find average NOK 10.83 (TradingView, accessed 2026-11-16), roughly our NOK 10.80 base case. For a deep-value name the question is whether the market is pricing terminal decline into stable or growing earnings power. It is not: at about 9.5x our 2027 operating profit, the shares price a modest recovery and no collapse. Our one disagreement is on margins. If the Q3 2026 margin of about 5% holds through 2027, consensus is too low on profit even with flat revenue. The order book has not yet earned that view.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the next three to nine months. First, the backlog has shrunk about 12% in a quarter, and with Q1 the seasonally weakest quarter (Q1 2026 was an EBIT loss of NOK 29 million), Q1 2027 could show falling revenue and a loss. Second, cash: operating cash flow was negative in Q1 and Q3 2026, there was no reported cash at 30 September 2026, and net debt including leases rose to NOK 823 million. A working-capital swing on a large project could press covenants on a company with an Altman Z of 1.9. Third, the NOK 566 million Bane NOR claim could settle low or go to litigation and a write-down. Fourth, Norwegian public tender timing is a budget decision NRC cannot control. We see no dated debt maturity wall in the materials we accessed.
picks.positioning_washout: We see no sign of forced selling. NRC pays no dividend, so there is no income-holder base to flee a cut, and it is not near an index event we can identify. The 10% fall after 5 November 2026 looks like ordinary repricing of the revenue guidance cut by active holders. Institutional flow (50 of 100) and smart-money (32 of 100) scores are neutral to weak, and insider buying is nil. Without a named forced seller, waiting for a lower price has no basis, which is why we wait for proof instead.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the Q4 2026 results show the order backlog holding at or above NOK 7.9 billion with a full-year 2026 operating margin of at least 3%, due 17 February 2027. NRC Group's margin repair is real. Third-quarter 2026 operating profit of NOK 91 million was its best since the restart, and Norway, Sweden and Kept all improved. But the same 5 November 2026 report cut 2026 revenue guidance by about 13%, dropped the 2028 revenue target, and showed the backlog falling to NOK 7.88 billion on a 0.7x book-to-bill. A contractor's revenue follows its backlog, so the thesis is in doubt until order intake recovers. We value the business on operating profit (the reported gross margin is a data artifact): about NOK 250 million of 2027 profit at 10.5x, plus a small risked value for the Bane NOR claim, minus NOK 823 million of net debt including leases, gives NOK 10.80 a share. That is about 21% above today's NOK 8.94, little more than our 20% bar for buying in this macro backdrop, and roughly in line with peers. The adverse case of NOK 4.60 sits much further below. With the balance sheet still stretched (no reported cash, an Altman Z of 1.9) and no moat to speak of, we lower conviction from 3 to 2 on the dated guidance cut and keep the value case at 2. The 10% share-price fall since our last look came from that company news, not from forced sellers or a sector-wide sell-off, so we no longer wait for a better price. If the February print shows the backlog stabilising, the margin story alone can carry the shares toward fair value; if the backlog drops below NOK 7 billion, the thesis has broken and we pass.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst, what forces the re-rating, is the Q4 2026 report on 17 February 2027. It is the first print after the new order-intake targets, it reports full-year margin against the above-3% guide, and it should state the Bane NOR claim outcome. A backlog held at or above NOK 7.9 billion and a margin of at least 3% would show the growth leg stabilising and reopen the case. A backlog below NOK 7 billion would turn the thesis from in doubt to broken. A first dividend under the at-least-30% payout ambition would be a later, secondary signal that the balance sheet is repaired.

# NRC Group ASA (NRC.OL): a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16. No earnings-call transcript was available from our data provider. This dossier is built from the company's published quarterly releases and result summaries (Q2 2025 to Q3 2026, the latest dated 5 November 2026), the quarterly statements in our data feed (FMP, through 30 September 2026) and the screener's multi-year figures. Where a quote would need a transcript, we describe the message instead of inventing words.*

**Bottom line:** NRC is a Nordic rail-infrastructure contractor (Norway, Sweden, Finland, plus the Kept, Gunnar Knutsen and Machines units) partway through a margin repair that is now real in the numbers. The third quarter of 2026 brought an operating profit (EBIT, earnings before interest and tax) of NOK 91 million, its best quarter since the restart. On the same day, 5 November 2026, management cut its 2026 revenue guidance from about NOK 7.5 billion to about NOK 6.5 billion, dropped the 2028 revenue target of more than NOK 10 billion, and admitted a below-target win rate on tenders. The repair is working on margins; the growth leg has gone soft.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **2024 (rescue):** large project write-downs and impairments (net loss of about NOK 1.0 billion for the year) and an equity raise in Q3 2024. The story was survival and restructuring.
- **2025 (restart):** the message became "profitability over volume": disciplined project selection, a return to profit (Q2 2025) and a record order backlog in Q1 2025. In Q3 2025 the headline profit measure changed from adjusted EBIT to reported EBIT. Targets: revenue of more than NOK 7 billion and an EBIT margin above 3% in 2026, with more than NOK 10 billion of revenue and a margin above 5% by 2028.
- **H1 2026 (growth promised):** Q1 2026 was a loss (EBIT of minus NOK 29 million on NOK 1.14 billion revenue) with growth promised for the second half. Q2 2026 lifted the 2026 revenue guide to about NOK 7.5 billion, reported a book-to-bill (orders won divided by revenue billed) of 1.2x and a NOK 8.9 billion backlog, and submitted a NOK 566 million final claim to Bane NOR on the ETM project.
- **Q3 2026 / Capital Markets Update (5 Nov 2026):** the story shrank. Revenue guidance for 2026 fell to about NOK 6.5 billion. The 2028 revenue target was replaced by order-intake targets (more than NOK 10 billion in 2027, more than NOK 12 billion in 2028) "because of project timing uncertainty". Margin targets were kept and extended: adjusted EBIT margin above 3.5% in 2027 and above 5.0% in 2028. Management described commercial performance as weak, with tender delays and cancellations (especially in Norway) and a win rate below target.

The arc runs from survival, to margin repair, to a growth promise that was withdrawn within one quarter.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Profitability over volume; margins recovering | Q3 2026 EBIT NOK 91m vs NOK 65m a year earlier (about 4.9-5.0% margin); year-to-date EBIT NOK 123m vs NOK 98m, after a NOK 71m one-off Swedish legal charge in Q2 | Corroborated |
| 2026 revenue about NOK 7.5bn (Q2 2026 guide) | Year-to-date revenue NOK 4.68bn vs NOK 4.85bn in 2025; guide cut to about NOK 6.5bn on 5 Nov 2026 | Missed: cut by about 13% within one quarter |
| Strong backlog, book-to-bill above 1.0x on a twelve-month basis after Q2 | Backlog NOK 7.88bn at Q3 2026 vs NOK 8.93bn at Q2 2026 and NOK 8.54bn a year earlier; Q3 book-to-bill 0.7x | Diverges: the backlog is shrinking |
| Cash flow improving | Operating cash flow: Q4 2025 +NOK 247m, Q1 2026 -NOK 173m, Q2 2026 +NOK 163-180m, Q3 2026 -NOK 27m to -NOK 39m (sources differ); year-to-date roughly zero. Net debt including leases NOK 823m at 30 Sep 2026 vs NOK 781m at 30 Jun 2026 | Mixed: seasonal and lumpy, no clear trend yet |
| More than 30% of profit to be paid as dividends | No dividend paid in 2026; reported retained earnings still negative (minus NOK 124m) | Not yet tested |
| Swedish turnaround | Sweden EBIT NOK 10m in Q3 2026 vs NOK 1m a year earlier | Corroborated, from a very low base |

The screener's 96.7% "gross margin" and the jumpy quarterly cost-of-revenue lines in our data feed are a data-mapping artifact (Q4 2025 shows a negative cost of revenue). Ignore them; contractor margins are judged at the EBIT line.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Rating: Declining on growth, rising on margins.** From Q1 2025 to Q2 2026 the releases leaned on the record backlog and a strong tender pipeline, and the 2026 revenue guide went up. By Q3 2026 the tone had turned defensive on the commercial side: management named tender delays, cancellations, a weak win rate, and switched from revenue targets to order-intake targets. On execution the tone stayed confident ("strongest quarter since the restart"). The shift from a revenue promise to an order-intake promise is the clearest sign of lower confidence about the top line.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
- Margin guidance: delivered. The 2025 margin improvement happened, and above 3% for 2026 is on track (year-to-date 2.6% after a NOK 71m one-off, with Q4 seasonally strong).
- Revenue guidance: poor. The about NOK 7.5bn 2026 figure set in mid-2026 was cut to about NOK 6.5bn by November, and the 2028 revenue target was dropped. Part of the gap is the weaker Swedish krona and euro, but the guide was stated at constant currency.
- The screener's earnings-beat rate is 4 of 7 quarters (57%); Q3 2026 beat the consensus EPS of about NOK 0.30 with NOK 0.33.
- **Reliability: Medium** (high on cost and margin, low on volume and timing).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
With no transcript we cannot quote the Q&A. The obvious pressure points from the releases: (a) why order intake and the win rate are below target while the tender pipeline is said to be NOK 43-44bn; (b) the status of the NOK 566m Bane NOR ETM claim, where negotiations were scheduled for Q3 2026 and the Q3 summaries say nothing about the result; (c) how a 5% margin in 2028 is reached on a shrinking backlog; (d) why diluted shares rose to about 184m in Q3 2026 against about 173m basic.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: 2026 revenue guide cut about 13% and the 2028 revenue target withdrawn (5 Nov 2026).
- Red: backlog down about 8% year on year and about 12% in one quarter; Q3 book-to-bill 0.7x.
- Red: management itself calls commercial performance weak, with Norwegian tender cancellations.
- Red: leverage is not trivial for a contractor. Net debt NOK 823m including leases (NOK 491m excluding leases), no reported cash at 30 Sep 2026, goodwill NOK 1.74bn against equity of NOK 1.70bn, Altman Z of 1.9.
- Red: the Bane NOR claim outcome is undisclosed after the negotiation window it named.
- Green: Q3 2026 EBIT up about 40% year on year, with Norway, Sweden and Kept all improving.
- Green: Finland revenue up 37%, and a second wave of Finnish light-rail contracts is secured, with production mainly from 2027.
- Green: margin targets extended (above 3.5% in 2027, above 5.0% in 2028) rather than cut.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- Replacing revenue targets with order-intake targets is a quiet admission that the top line is not under management's control; it also makes the 2027 test easy to observe (order intake above NOK 10bn).
- The 2025 switch from adjusted EBIT to reported EBIT, followed by a 2027-2028 target framed as adjusted EBIT, gives management room to exclude one-offs again. Watch for that.
- The tender pipeline is large, but the timing depends on public clients (Bane NOR, Trafikverket, Finnish cities). That is budget timing, not lost demand, but it moves the payoff to the right.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
**Trajectory: turning.** The business is moving from a volume story to a margin story, and only the margin part is proven. The single most important thing to weigh is whether order intake recovers by the Q4 2026 report on 17 February 2027. A contractor with improving margins but a shrinking backlog is a contractor whose 2027-28 revenue, and therefore profit, shrinks with it.

**Moat:** none of real width. Rail contracting is won by tender; the defensible parts are specialist rail skills, safety approvals and framework agreements with national rail owners, but returns have been negative (return on invested capital minus 6%) and margins of 3-5% leave no pricing power. Trend: stable. **Secular threat:** none in a structural sense. Nordic rail investment is a long-term tailwind; the risk is cyclical public-budget timing and project execution, not a force that shrinks the market. The cheapness is a mix of genuine execution risk and a fear print on order timing, not a value trap from a melting base.

picks.bull_thesis: The core business is getting more profitable while the market prices the whole group as if the 2025 food-delivery losses were permanent. JD Retail (the owned-inventory online store) earned a record RMB 15.0B of operating profit in Q1 2026 at a 5.6% margin, and 4.6% in Q2 2026 - a record for a peak promotional quarter - with retail gross margin up 1.3 points to 18.5%, management says the 17th straight year-on-year rise (Q2 2026 call, 2026-08-13). Trailing-twelve-month retail operating profit is roughly RMB 52-53B. The money-losing new businesses are shrinking fast: the segment loss fell from RMB 14.8B to RMB 9.85B year on year in Q2 2026 and food-delivery losses fell more than 50%; group operating income swung from a RMB 0.9B loss to a RMB 4.5B profit and non-GAAP profit rose 21% to RMB 8.9B. Beijing's campaign against cut-throat subsidy wars (echoed by management from Q1 2026: 'rational', 'full compliance') is a policy brake on a renewed price war. Advertising and commission revenue has grown double digits for six straight quarters, a high-margin mix shift that structurally lifts retail margins. Capital returns are real: USD 3.0B of buybacks in 2025 (6.3% of shares, cancelled), USD 631M more in Q1 2026, USD 1.4B authorisation left to August 2027, and a USD 1 per ADS dividend (about a 3.6% yield at HKD 108.1). Around the core sit listed stakes in JD Health (about two-thirds of a HKD 132B company) and JD Logistics (about 63% of a HKD 63B company) plus RMB 96B of long-term investments. At HKD 108.1 the group is valued around RMB 250-265B, roughly 11 times trailing non-GAAP profit and well under 10 times what the retail business alone earns after tax. Conditions: retail margin holds at 4.5% or better, new-business losses keep falling year on year (management guided a 'substantial narrowing' in the second half of 2026), and buybacks continue.
picks.bear_thesis: Profit is recovering but sales are not, and management has a habit of spending the core business's profits on the next venture. Group revenue fell 2.9% to RMB 346B in Q2 2026 and retail revenue fell to RMB 295B from RMB 310B as the trade-in subsidy base and rising electronics component prices hit the largest category (electronics down 8.4% in Q1 2026). The electronics recovery has been promised and pushed back twice (Q4 2025 call, then Q1 2026, then 'second half'). New businesses still lose about RMB 10B a quarter; Joybuy (Europe) and Jingxi stepped up spending in Q2 2026, and on 2026-11-12 JD closed a EUR 1,335M purchase of 59.8% of Ceconomy, a thin-margin European electronics chain now consolidated into JD's accounts. Group returns are poor - ROIC 3.9%, return on equity 7.9%, 2025 net margin 1.5%, 2025 free cash flow down 89% - so the 'high single-digit margin' target is still an aspiration with no date. The cash pile flatters: much of the RMB 235B is supplier float (payables RMB 229B vs inventory RMB 120B) or sits in listed subsidiaries with outside shareholders. China-specific risks stack on top: a contract-based ownership structure for foreign holders, an RMB 635M regulatory fine (April 2026), US-China tech tension that hit the whole sector (Alibaba fell 8% on 2026-11-12 on chip-access reports), and competition from Alibaba, PDD and Meituan that can reignite. If retail margin slips back under 4% and the new-business losses stall around RMB 30B a year, the stock is worth well under today's price.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the market prices JD on group earnings that still carry about RMB 40B a year of new-business losses, at about 11 times trailing non-GAAP profit, as if those losses were permanent and the China e-commerce price war never ends. The dated numbers say otherwise - the loss is down a third year on year and regulators are actively discouraging subsidy wars. Where the market is right: sales are shrinking in 2026, electronics recovery keeps slipping, and management has just added Ceconomy to the list of ventures, so a holding-company and reinvestment discount is deserved. We do not claim the market is wrong about the business; we claim it overprices the permanence of the drag.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the next three to nine months): Q3 2026 results tomorrow (2026-11-17) could show retail revenue still negative if the promised reacceleration fails; Ceconomy is consolidated from 2026-11-12, which will add low-margin revenue and integration noise to the next several quarters and make the numbers harder to read; Joybuy and Jingxi spending is rising; US-China technology and listing tensions can hit the whole sector overnight (the 2026-11-12 sell-off). No debt wall: consolidated debt is RMB 105B including leases against RMB 235B of cash and short-term investments. No liquidation risk.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited. JD is widely held through both the US ADS and the Hong Kong line; the dividend is small (about 3.6%) so there is no yield-holder base to flee a cut. The main mechanical risk is sector-wide: Chinese internet names sell off together on US policy headlines and on southbound-flow swings, which is a sector-wide sell-off rather than anything specific to JD.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds: JD's core retail business is earning record margins and the food-delivery losses that halved group profit in 2025 are shrinking quickly, yet at HKD 108.1 the market values the whole group at roughly what the retail business alone should be worth after a de-rating. Our sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) fair value is about HKD 160, roughly 48% above today's price and well clear of the 20% bar we require in the current macro backdrop; the adverse case is about HKD 78 and the favourable case about HKD 260. We hold conviction at a middling level rather than higher for three reasons. First, management keeps funding new loss-making ventures - Europe's Joybuy and, since 2026-11-12, the Ceconomy electronics chain - so part of the discount is a fair tax on capital allocation. Second, revenue is shrinking in 2026 and the electronics recovery has slipped twice. Third, much of the gap to fair value is shared with the whole China-platform sector (Alibaba, PDD and Meituan are all near their lows), so it is sector beta rather than a JD-specific edge. Results land tomorrow (2026-11-17); a print showing new-business losses still falling year on year and retail margin at or above 4.5% keeps the case on track, while a fresh step-up in losses would put the thesis in doubt.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating: no single binding event. The re-rating comes from successive quarterly prints showing new-business losses falling and retail profit rising; the next is Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-17, then Q4 2026 results around March 2027 (with the annual dividend decision). Ongoing buybacks (USD 1.4B left to August 2027) shrink the share count about 1.5-2% a quarter at the recent pace and act as a slow forcing mechanism. Ceconomy closing (2026-11-12) is already done.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# JD.com (9618.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16, the day before third-quarter 2026 results (due 2026-11-17, before the US open). Five earnings calls read: Q2 2025 (2025-08-14), Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), Q4 2025 (2026-03-05), Q1 2026 (2026-05-12), Q2 2026 (2026-08-13). All company figures are in Chinese yuan (RMB) unless stated; the Hong Kong share trades at HKD 108.1 (live quote, 2026-11-16).*

**Bottom line for the reader:** JD spent 2025 pouring the profits of its core online retail business into a food-delivery price war, and the group's earnings halved. Through 2026 management has been pulling that spending back exactly as promised, while the core retail business kept widening its margins. The story management tells has matched the numbers on profit; it has not matched them on sales growth, which turned negative in 2026. The real question is not whether the core business is good - it is - but whether management will stop opening new loss-making fronts (food delivery, Europe, the newly bought German electronics chain Ceconomy).

## 1. Narrative arc

- **Q2 2025 (offense):** Revenue up 22% to RMB 357B, helped by the government trade-in subsidy for appliances. The headline was user growth ("quarterly active customers... over 40% year-on-year") powered by the brand-new food-delivery business. Group non-GAAP profit (profit before stock pay and one-off items) halved to RMB 7.4B "as a result of the investment and rapid growth in our new businesses". The Ceconomy (MediaMarkt/Saturn) takeover was announced; Europe framed as a "long-term vision".
- **Q3 2025:** Revenue +15%, non-GAAP profit RMB 5.8B. First admission that the trade-in subsidy had created a "high base" for electronics. Food-delivery loss "narrowed... from the prior quarter". The AI roadmap appears (digital-human assistants, robot agents).
- **Q4 2025 (defense):** "Results in line with expectations as we navigated short-term challenges." Retail revenue fell 1.7%. Management stresses the full-year JD Retail operating margin of 4.6% (up 52 basis points) and that new-business spending fell nearly 20% quarter on quarter.
- **Q1 2026:** Group revenue +4.9%; JD Retail revenue only +1.8%, electronics -8.4%, but retail operating margin 5.6% and record retail operating profit of RMB 15.0B. New-business investment down "over 30% sequentially". Europe's Joybuy launched in March 2026.
- **Q2 2026 (harvest):** "Q2 marked a definitive turning point for our profitability trajectory." Non-GAAP profit +21% to RMB 8.9B; food-delivery losses down more than 50% year on year. But group revenue fell 2.9% to RMB 346B and retail revenue fell to RMB 295B from RMB 310B. Joybuy and Jingxi (the low-tier-city app) saw a "sequential step-up in strategic investment".

The arc is a full cycle: from a growth-at-any-cost land grab in mid-2025 to a profit-recovery story in mid-2026. Food delivery was quietly reframed from a growth engine ("exponential" orders, Q2 2025) to a "synergy" feature whose own profitability is a distant goal ("will eventually achieve profitability", Q1 2026). The growth emphasis moved to advertising, general merchandise and supermarket.

## 2. Claims vs financials

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Core retail margins keep expanding (every call) | Retail operating margin 3.9% (Q2 2025) to 4.5% to full-year 2025 4.6% to 5.6% (Q1 2026) to 4.6% (Q2 2026, vs 4.5% a year earlier). Retail gross margin 18.5% in Q2 2026, up 1.3 points; management says up year on year for 17 straight quarters. Scan shows group gross margin 16% and "expanding". | Matches |
| Food-delivery losses fall every quarter | New-businesses operating loss RMB 14.8B (Q2 2025) to RMB 9.85B (Q2 2026). Group operating income RMB 4.5B in Q2 2026 vs a RMB 0.9B loss a year earlier (company release, 2026-08-13). | Matches, but the segment still loses about RMB 10B a quarter |
| Healthy, sustained top-line growth | 2025 revenue RMB 1,275B (+10%), then Q1 2026 +4.9% and Q2 2026 -2.9%; retail revenue down about 4.7% in Q2 2026. | Poorer than the story |
| Shareholder returns are a priority | 2025 buybacks USD 3.0B (6.3% of shares, all cancelled); USD 1 per ADS dividend kept (USD 1.4B, paid April 2026); Q1 2026 buyback USD 631M (1.6%); USD 1.4B authorisation left to August 2027. Diluted ADS count fell from 1.485B (Q2 2025) to 1.408B (Q2 2026). | Matches |
| "Long-term high single-digit margin target" | Group net margin 1.5% (2025), ROIC 3.9%, return on equity 7.9%. 2025 EPS RMB 6.42, down 52%. | Unproven - an aspiration |
| Investing "with discipline... focus on ROI" | Food-delivery war cost tens of billions of RMB; the group then bought 59.8% of Ceconomy for EUR 1,335M (completed 2026-11-12) and stepped up Joybuy spend in Q2 2026. | Mixed |

Cash flow is the weak spot: free cash flow fell 89% in fiscal 2025 (FCF margin 0.4%), though trailing-twelve-month (TTM) free cash flow to June 2026 recovered to RMB 31.7B. The balance sheet is strong: RMB 235B of cash and short-term investments against RMB 105B of total debt including leases (2026-06-30), but much of that cash is supplier money (payables of RMB 229B against inventory of RMB 120B) and part of it sits in listed subsidiaries (JD Health, JD Logistics) with outside shareholders.

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory - Rising (from a low base)

- Q2 2025: expansive, user-metric heavy, profit-light. "Very productive quarter."
- Q3 2025: still upbeat, first hedge on electronics ("high base effect is expected to linger").
- Q4 2025: defensive. "Navigated short-term challenges"; leans on margins and full-year totals.
- Q1 2026: confident on profit ("strong start to the year"), explicit about "rational" competition and "full compliance" with regulators' stance against cut-throat subsidies.
- Q2 2026: most confident on profit ("definitive turning point", "accelerated profit growth at the group level" promised for the second half), while still hedging on sales ("we expect JD Retail to hit a turning point, reaccelerating into positive top line expansion" in Q3).

The language moved from offense (users, frequency, food delivery) to efficiency (unit economics, ROI, marketing-expense ratio). Guidance became more specific on profit and stayed vague on revenue.

## 4. Guidance credibility - Medium

- Delivered: food-delivery loss narrowing each quarter (promised Q3 2025, delivered through Q2 2026); new-business investment reductions (-20% in Q4 2025, -30% in Q1 2026); dividend and buybacks; Joybuy launch in March 2026 as announced.
- Missed or slipped: the electronics recovery. Q4 2025 said trade-in resumption would provide "a constructive backdrop"; Q1 2026 electronics -8.4%; Q2 2026 still "moderated", recovery pushed to the second half. Q3 2025 said general-merchandise strength would "sustain into Q4"; Q4 general merchandise slowed from 19% to 12%.
- The scan's beat rate (6 of 7 quarters on earnings) fits a pattern of conservative profit guidance and over-optimistic revenue talk. FMP shows Q2 2026 earnings USD 0.93 per ADS vs 0.86 expected, revenue slightly ahead; Q1 2026 USD 0.74 vs 0.57.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- Every call has a "profitability outlook / margin target" question (Joyce Ju, Thomas Chong). The answer is always the unchanged "high single-digit" long-term target with no date.
- Food-delivery end-state: asked repeatedly; management answers with "synergy" (advertising contribution of 2-3% in Q4 2025, 3% in Q1 2026) rather than a break-even date.
- Ceconomy logic (Q2 2025): answered in generalities ("brand strength, supply chain capabilities"). No return target given.
- Regulation (Q4 2025): answered with a compliance statement. In April 2026 the market regulator fined a JD affiliate about RMB 635M (reported alongside Q2 results).
- Not addressed: what the European build-out will cost in total, and how much of the consolidated cash belongs to minority holders of subsidiaries.

## 6. Red flags / green flags

- Red - **Revenue has turned negative** (Q2 2026 -2.9%) while management calls the business "resilient".
- Red - **Capital allocation keeps finding new fronts**: food delivery (2025), Joybuy and Jingxi step-up (Q2 2026), Ceconomy consolidated from 2026-11-12. Each one eats profits the core retail business earns.
- Red - **Return on invested capital is 3.9%**, well below any reasonable cost of capital, and 2025 free cash flow almost vanished.
- Red - Regulatory fine of about RMB 635M (April 2026) and an affiliate structure (the VIE, a contract-based ownership structure used by Chinese internet companies) that leaves foreign holders with indirect rights.
- Green - **Retail gross margin up for 17 straight quarters**; retail operating profit at a record RMB 15.0B in Q1 2026.
- Green - **New-business losses down by a third year on year** (RMB 14.8B to RMB 9.85B, Q2 2025 to Q2 2026).
- Green - Steady buybacks (diluted share count down about 5% in a year) plus a 3.6% dividend yield at today's price.
- Green - Advertising and commission revenue growing double digits for six straight quarters, a high-margin mix shift.

## 7. Hidden signals

- "Synergy" replaced "growth" as the justification for food delivery from Q4 2025; the business is now defended by its ad contribution to retail rather than its own economics. That is the classic language of a business that will be kept small.
- "Rational", "compliance" and "against involution (cut-throat competition)" appear from Q1 2026, matching Beijing's campaign against subsidy wars. This makes another expensive price war less likely - a real, policy-backed brake on the biggest bear risk.
- An unnamed executive (interpreted) took most Q&A in 2026 calls in place of the CFO; no change in the stated strategy.
- JD Logistics now books the on-demand delivery revenue (accounting change from Q1 2026), which flatters the new-businesses revenue decline (-47.6% in Q2 2026) and makes segment comparisons harder.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning** - from an investment phase back to profit harvesting. The single most important thing to weigh: the core retail business earns roughly RMB 50B+ a year of operating profit and is getting more profitable, but shareholders only see what is left after management's next strategic venture. The discount is partly a fair "reinvestment tax", not pure mispricing.

**Moat:** scale and cost advantage in owned inventory (first-party retail) plus a proprietary logistics network - a narrow but real moat. Evidence: gross margin rising for 17 quarters through a price war is the opposite of erosion; but group returns (ROIC 3.9%) are diluted by the new ventures, so the moat does not show up in group returns. Width is stable, not widening.

**Secular threat:** AI shopping agents could shift how shoppers find products, but JD's edge is physical (inventory, warehouses, delivery), which an AI front end does not replace. Competition from Alibaba, PDD and Meituan is intense and cyclical rather than terminal. The cheapness looks more like a fear print on China consumer platforms plus a reinvestment discount than a shrinking base: revenue is roughly flat-to-down this year but profit is rising.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: New Corteva is the world's number four or five crop-protection maker and was spun off from its seed business (now Vylor) on 2026-10-01. It trades at about $9.08, an equity value of about $6.1B on 667.3M shares, and roughly 7x this year's guided trough EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization) of $1.10-1.125B once net debt, pension and minority interests are added. About two-thirds of the portfolio is patented or otherwise differentiated, earning 10-15% higher margins, and management says nothing major loses patent protection before the end of 2028. The damage is concentrated in one place: Latin America organic sales fell 31%, which management attributes to Brazilian distributors working down inventory (its own product, sold in during 2025) while farmer applications held up. If that is a one-season destock, 2027 EBITDA should recover toward the roughly $1.3B base set out at the 2026-09-15 Investor Day, helped by more than $200M of net cost improvements planned for 2027-29 and a new CEO who says everything is on the table, including country and product exits. At 8-9.5x a recovered $1.25-1.45B, the shares are worth $12-17. The balance sheet is investment-grade-minded: net debt after the spin is roughly $0.7-1.0B, and the pension was largely funded during 2026 (the liability fell from $2.21B to $0.66B).
picks.bear_thesis: The guidance cut came only eight weeks after Investor Day, and management admitted that 'too much of the product we sold into the Brazil channel last year didn't go to ground.' Some 2025 sales, part of the base the 2029 targets build from, were pulled forward. The implied Q4 2026 EBITDA margin of about 7-9%, on high-single-digit price declines with flat volume, shows price erosion as well as a timing problem. Brazilian generic pricing from Chinese suppliers has been called temporary on every call since Q4 2025 and has not turned. Management said 'we've continued to see negative developments since then', so Q4 could miss again and the first 2027 guide could start near $1.0-1.1B. Cash is opaque: nine-month operating cash flow from continuing operations was -$1.24B, and the CFO deflected a direct question about roughly $800M of unexplained cash movement in Q3. Legacy DuPont-era PFAS ('forever chemical') liabilities stay with New Corteva through EIDP. They are shared and capped under the 2021 agreement with Chemours and DuPont, but they are a real tail, and state attorneys general tried to block the spin over them (2026-09-14). FMC, the closest US crop-protection peer, is down to about $5 with a market value of $0.65B after its own Brazil-driven miss, which shows how far this sector can de-rate. Returns on the remaining asset base are thin, with heavy goodwill. At 6.5x a stuck $1.0B EBITDA, less about $2.4B of debt, pension, minority-interest and legacy claims, the equity is worth about $6.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market. Street targets have collapsed from a one-year average of about $66.50 (combined company) to three targets in the last month averaging $13.33, with the newest at $13 and $11 (2026-11-13 and 2026-11-16). The market is now pricing New Corteva as though the Brazil damage is permanent and the business looks like FMC. Our view is narrower. The franchise outside Latin America is growing (new products +20%, North America volume +19%), and the balance sheet bears no resemblance to FMC's. But the street's 'temporary' framing of Brazil has been wrong on every call since Q4 2025, and management's own 2026-07-31 claim that the channel was 'not oversupplied' was contradicted three months later. We do not yet have the evidence to say the street is looking the wrong way. The disagreement is that the stock is cheap if, and only if, 2027 restarts from at least $1.2B of EBITDA.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead). Q4 2026 is guided to an EBITDA margin of about 7-9%, and management flagged continued deterioration in Brazil after the quarter ended, so another reset at the February print is possible. Brazilian farmers face high interest rates and El Nino weather, and Corteva's own barter and credit exposure in that market (near $1B of barter revenue disclosed in early 2026) carries collection risk. Cash is the second hazard. Nine-month operating cash flow was -$1.24B, the year-end cash target is about $1.5B, and Q3 cash movements are not fully explained. A weaker Q4 collection season could lift net debt toward $1.2B or more. There is no debt maturity wall, and the dividend is small, so this is not a liquidity threat. It is a risk of earnings reset and a lower multiple.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure. There was a mechanical seller at the spin: Corteva left the S&P 500 for the S&P MidCap 400 on 2026-10-01, which forced large-cap index funds out and brought mid-cap funds in. That rebalancing is complete. The 24% drop after 2026-11-11 was company news, not forced selling. Former holders of the combined company who wanted seed exposure may keep drifting out of the smaller crop-protection stub, and plaintiff-firm activity adds headline pressure, but neither is a level we can name with confidence. We therefore do not set a price-wait; we wait for proof instead.
