picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Corteva (CTVA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Debate date 2026-11-16. Live price $9.075 (NYSE, USD; FMP quote 2026-11-16, down about 4% on the day and about 24% since the 2026-11-11 results).*

**Read this first.** The Corteva that trades under CTVA today is not the company in most of the screener's numbers. On 2026-10-01 Corteva spun off its seed business as Vylor (VYLR, one Vylor share per Corteva share). What is left is a pure crop-protection company (herbicides, insecticides, fungicides and biologicals) with about $7.6B of 2025 pro forma sales and about $1.27B of 2025 adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization; 8-K pro forma filing). The screener's fiscal-year figures (revenue $17.4B, EPS $1.60, P/FCF 2.3x, DCF fair value $39, the $30.73 consensus target) describe the combined company before the spin, and none of them can be used to value the stock at $9. The same is true of the "live corrections" balance sheet (debt $7.45B, cash $3.93B at 2026-09-30): that is the consolidated pre-spin balance sheet. New Corteva's own carve-out balance sheet at 2026-09-30 (8-K) shows cash of $1.72B (plus $0.42B restricted), short-term borrowings of $0.84B, long-term debt of $2.37B and a pension and retiree-benefit liability of $0.66B. On 2026-10-01 Vylor paid New Corteva $761M, which went straight to repaying a $600M revolver and $161M of commercial paper, so net debt after the spin is roughly $0.7-1.0B before the seasonal cash swing. The share count at the spin was 667.3M.

## 1. Narrative arc

- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-05) to Q2 2026 (2026-07-31): the combined company was on a roll.** The October 2025 split announcement was framed as "not that we believe things aren't going well today. They are." Guidance went up twice: 2025 EBITDA to $3.8-3.9B, then 2026 to $4.1-4.3B on 2026-07-31. Crop protection was described as delivering "top and bottom line growth... in what I'd still describe as less than ideal market conditions" (Q4 2025).
- **Brazil was a known, recurring soft spot.** Every call from Q4 2025 onward mentions "competitive pricing dynamics" in Latin America from Chinese generics. On 2026-07-31 Chuck Magro said high-single-digit price declines in Brazil were "not the new normal" and the channel was "healthy... we would not say it is oversupplied."
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-12): first call as a stand-alone crop-protection company, under a new CEO (Luke Kissam) and a new CFO (Jeff Rudolph).** The tone changed completely. Latin America organic sales fell 31% in the quarter. Management said conditions "deteriorated sharply in the final weeks of the third quarter" and "we've continued to see negative developments since then." Full-year 2026 adjusted pro forma EBITDA guidance is now $1.100-1.125B, against the roughly $1.3B framed at the 2026-09-15 Investor Day, a cut of about 14% only eight weeks later.

## 2. Claims vs financials (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Differentiated" products drive the business (about two-thirds of the portfolio, 10-15% higher margins) | New-product volume +20% in Q3 2026 at stable price; Arylex and Pyraxalt each growing more than 20%, about $650M combined | **Holds.** This is the real asset. |
| The Brazil channel was healthy and not oversupplied (2026-07-31) | Q3 2026: "too much of the product we sold into the Brazil channel last year didn't go to ground" | **Contradicted.** Some 2025 sales were effectively pulled forward into the channel. Management owned this, which is the most important forensic finding here. |
| Investor Day 2026 EBITDA of about $1.3B; 2029 target $1.45-1.65B | Guidance cut to $1.10-1.125B on 2026-11-11; nine-month EBITDA $943M (flat), Q3 $222M (-17%), implied Q4 margin of about 7-9% | **Contradicted for 2026.** The 2029 bridge now starts from a lower base. |
| Cash on track for about $1.5B at year-end | Nine-month operating cash flow from continuing operations was -$1.24B (including large pension top-ups: the liability fell from $2.21B to $0.66B); the CFO deflected a direct question about roughly $800M of unexplained cash movement in Q3 | **Unverified.** A cash bridge is owed. |
| Little near-term patent exposure | "Nothing major that comes off... by the end of '28"; acetochlor (North America) and older Brazil molecules are already in their generic phase | **Plausible**, and consistent with pricing pressure being concentrated in named molecules. |

The scan's annual figures (EPS +23%, FCF +82%, gross margin 47%) belong to the combined seed-plus-crop-protection company. They do not describe this business. Seed carried the higher margins and the cash.

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory - Declining

Through H1 2026 the tone was confident ("the company is slightly ahead", 2026-07-31). In Q3 2026 it turned defensive and cost-led: "Everything is on the table... if you're not making it and you're not selling it, we're looking to see what we need to do to reduce our cost." The new CEO said Brazil is "a top priority for me" but gave no quantified recovery path. The prepared remarks lean on "the demand is there; what has changed is when people buy", which is a destocking framing rather than a demand-loss framing. That may well be correct, but nobody has proved it yet.

## 4. Guidance credibility - Medium for the old team, Low so far for the new one

The combined company raised and beat guidance through 2025 and H1 2026 (the screener records 5 of 7 quarters beaten). The stand-alone company's first guidance, given at the 2026-09-15 Investor Day, was cut within eight weeks. That guidance was also set when, by management's own account, Brazil channel inventory was already too high, which suggests the problem was underestimated rather than hidden. Two securities-fraud "investigations" by plaintiff firms (2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13) followed the roughly 24% one-day drop. These are routine after a large drop and are not evidence in themselves.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- **Cash** (KeyBanc, Q3 2026): where did about $800M go between pro forma Q2 and Q3? The answer was to refer to the filings.
- **Q4 implied margin** (KeyBanc): sales down only low-to-mid single digits but EBITDA margin around 7-9%. The answer was that pricing is down high single digits with flat volume, which signals that price, not just destocking, is the problem in Q4.
- **Brazil pricing** (Mizuho, every quarter): the "not the new normal" answer from 2026-07-31 did not hold up.
- **Patent cliffs** (JPMorgan): answered credibly.

## 6. Red and green flags

- Red (Q3 2026): channel overstock from 2025 sales admitted, and guidance cut eight weeks after Investor Day.
- Red (Q3 2026): Latin America organic sales -31%, and "negative developments since then" means Q4 risk remains open.
- Red (Q3 2026): the cash bridge was unexplained, and nine-month operating cash flow was -$1.24B.
- Red (2026-09-14): state attorneys general tried to block the separation over legacy PFAS ("forever chemical") liabilities. Those liabilities sit with New Corteva through EIDP, inside the 2021 cost-sharing agreement with Chemours and DuPont (Corteva's share is 29% above the first $300M, within a $2B combined DuPont-Corteva cap).
- Green (Q3 2026): new products +20% in volume at stable prices, North America volume +19%, EMEA organic +14%.
- Green (Q3 2026): productivity is ahead of plan, R&D spending went up while SG&A came down, and nothing major comes off patent before the end of 2028.
- Green (2026-10-23): first stand-alone dividend of $0.05 a quarter, a modest about 2% yield.

## 7. Hidden signals

- The vocabulary has shifted from "growth platforms" to "transformation office", "exit countries/products" and "sell straight through distribution". The new CEO is preparing a restructuring ($130-140M of 2026 restructuring charges for the manufacturing network).
- "We own that" on the Brazil inventory: candid, and it moves the blame to the 2025 commercial decisions of the prior regime.
- Robert King, the crop-protection head for four years, left with the Q2 2026 call. Every key voice is now new.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict

**Trajectory: deteriorating near term.** The single most important thing for the director: at about $9 the stock trades on roughly 7x 2026 trough EBITDA (enterprise value of about $8.0B including net debt, pension and minority interests), so the price already assumes a lot. The open question is whether the Brazil damage is a one-season channel destock, which would get EBITDA back toward $1.25-1.3B in 2027, or a structural reset of Latin American pricing from Chinese generics, which would leave EBITDA stuck near $1.0-1.1B. The Q4 2026 print and the first 2027 guide (expected early February 2027) settle it.

**Moat:** narrow but real. It rests on intangible and regulatory assets (patented actives and registrations; about two-thirds of the portfolio is differentiated, with a 12-active pipeline). Off-patent molecules erode on a schedule, and returns are thin: the combined company's ROIC was about 5% with heavy goodwill. The moat is stable, not widening. Generics replace actives as they age, and the pipeline replaces them in turn.

**Secular threat:** manageable. Chinese generic oversupply and the shift to biologicals are cyclical-to-structural pressures that the pipeline has historically offset. No terminal threat applies. The cheapness looks more like fear than a melting base, but the forensic flags above have to clear first.

Management credibility 2 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

The new engine is real and fast: Other revenue rose 82% to a record $34M (a $136M run rate), with Hatch at a ~$37M run rate (+55%), Yelp Host handling a 2.5 million-call annual run rate (up 15x in a year) and data-licensing deals with OpenAI and Meta that turn the AI threat into a customer. Management targets a $250M run rate for Other revenue by end-2028; if it gets there, Other revenue offsets the ad decline and total revenue grows again. Capital return restarts in 2027 at more than 50% of free cash flow; at today's price that would retire roughly a tenth of the shares each year, after a 15% cut in the diluted share count over the past year. Conditions: services advertising declines stay in the low single digits, Other revenue keeps compounding above 50%, and the buyback restarts on schedule.
picks.bear_thesis: The core is now shrinking and the decline is accelerating, not stabilizing. Services advertising went from +7% (Q3 2025) to +1%, flat, and now -2% (Q3 2026); RR&O advertising (restaurants, retail and other) fell 13%; ad clicks fell 8%; and management guides to 'increased pressure on advertising revenue across categories' in Q4 2026. Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $320-325M is about 11% below 2025, and Q3 net income fell 12% - EPS rose only because the share count fell 15%. Capital allocation was pro-cyclical: $200M of buybacks in 2026 at prices around $26, financed partly with a revolver, then paused near $19 to repay it, and management now flags acquisitions 'through a combination of cash and financing'. AI assistants and Google's AI answers can capture local search intent before it reaches Yelp, so the fall in clicks may be structural rather than a consumer slowdown. Insiders only sell (35 open-market sales, no buys; the CFO sold at $20.00 on 2026-10-15). Other revenue is only about 9% of sales, much of its growth is the acquired Hatch, and it is being run for growth at lower margins. If services advertising slides to -5% or worse in 2027, free cash flow after stock pay falls toward $120M and a 7x multiple is fair, putting the stock in the mid-teens. Confirmation: a services print worse than -4% or a 2027 revenue outlook below 2026.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the street is pricing Yelp as a terminally declining ad business - about 4x free cash flow and under 1x gross profit, with the newest targets cut to $17 (Morgan Stanley, 2026-10-13) and $23 (2026-11-06). We think that overstates the decline rate today: services advertising is down 2%, not collapsing, cost per click is still rising, project requests are up ~10%, and the AI licensing and Host/Hatch lines are growing 50-80%. But the market is right on direction - the core has shrunk for the first time, the Q4 guide points to more pressure, and adjusted EBITDA is falling about 11% this year. Our disagreement is about magnitude, not sign, and it can only be settled by the next two prints.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): Q4 2026 is guided to $347-352M with 'increased pressure on advertising revenue across categories', and there is no buyback support until 2027 while the revolver ($75M at 2026-09-30) is repaid. There is no debt wall or cash-burn hump - free cash flow stays positive at roughly $60M a quarter - so this is a slow-bleed risk, not a liquidation risk. The danger is a February 2027 outlook that shows 2027 revenue down, which would push the stock toward the $16 bear value; a new debt-funded acquisition would add goodwill risk on top of the $440M already on the balance sheet.
picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure is visible. The stock is down more than 30% this year and near the bottom of its 52-week range ($17.27-$31.72), so momentum and growth holders have largely left; it gapped from $20.52 to an $18.50 open on 2026-11-06 and recovered to $19.58. Insiders are steady sellers (35 open-market sales, no buys; the CFO sold 7,500 shares at $20.00 on 2026-10-15), which removes a confirming signal but is not a mechanical flush. No index deletion, lock-up or dividend cut is pending; at a ~$1.06B market value a small-cap index reshuffle is the only plausible mechanical seller.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the Q4 2026 results show services advertising down no more than 2% and a 2027 revenue outlook at or above 2026, due about 2027-02-12. The thesis is in doubt until that test. The test we set last week came back in between: on 2026-11-05 Yelp reported services advertising down 2% - not the flat-or-better we needed, but not the collapse that would break the case - and it guided to more advertising pressure in the fourth quarter. Our base fair value falls to $25.00 from $27.50 because the core is now shrinking; that is still well above today's $19.58, and the bear value is $16. We lower conviction to 2 and value conviction to 3 because the dated print showed a declining core and a narrow, eroding moat under real pressure from AI search. This is not a buy until the decline rate is shown to be shallow and Other revenue is shown to offset it.

None of these is contractually fixed.

# Yelp Inc. (YELP) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-09 from five earnings calls (Q3 2025, 2025-11-06 through Q3 2026, 2026-11-05), the screener's financial record, the 2026-09-30 balance sheet (filed 2026-11-06) and FMP news. Prices in US dollars, NYSE listing; live price $19.58 on 2026-11-09.*

**The takeaway:** Yelp is still a highly cash-generative business that keeps beating its own forecasts, but the core advertising engine has now tipped from slow growth into shrinkage. Services advertising, the larger and healthier half, went from +7% a year ago to -2% in Q3 2026, and management guides to "increased pressure on advertising revenue across categories" in Q4. The growth story has moved to a small, fast-growing "Other revenue" line built on AI products. The question for a buyer is no longer whether the core is stable; it is whether the cash it throws off, and the new AI lines, outrun its decline.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-06):** a growth-and-buyback story. Services revenue rose 7% to a quarterly record $244M; restaurants, retail and other (RR&O) fell 2%. Management cut the full-year 2025 revenue range to $1.460-1.465B on "heightened macroeconomic uncertainties" but raised profit guidance. Capital allocation: cash, acquisition capacity, buybacks.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-13):** a five-year victory lap on "product-led growth and disciplined expense management", plus the Hatch acquisition (an AI lead-management tool for service professionals). The tone shifted from harvesting to investing: "We plan to increase our investments in 2026."
- **Q1 2026 (2026-05-08) and Q2 2026 (2026-08-06):** services advertising slowed to +1%, then flat ($241M); RR&O fell 11% and more; net income fell 27% and 28% year over year as investment rose. Other revenue nearly doubled. Buybacks were paused "as we work to pay down our revolving credit facility".
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-05):** the language is now an "AI transformation". Net revenue fell 1% to $371M; services advertising fell 2% to $238M; RR&O advertising fell 13% to $99M; ad clicks fell 8%. Other revenue rose 82% to a record $34M, and management now sets a target of a $250M annual run rate for Other revenue by the end of 2028 (it is at $136M). Capital return is reframed as "more than 50% of free cash flow" through buybacks, resuming in 2027, alongside "strategic acquisitions through a combination of cash and financing".

The thesis has contracted: the core is now described as something to defend, and the growth narrative has moved to a line that is about 9% of revenue.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Disciplined, highly profitable business | Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, excluding stock pay) $92M, a 25% margin, $17M above the top of guidance; trailing-twelve-month (TTM) free cash flow $262M on ~$1.46B revenue | Holds. Cash generation is real. |
| Services advertising is resilient | +7% (Q3 2025) -> +1% (Q1 2026) -> flat (Q2 2026) -> -2% (Q3 2026) | Does not hold. Four quarters of steady deceleration into decline. |
| AI products are building a new engine | Other revenue $34M in Q3 2026, +82%; Hatch run rate ~$37M, +55%; data licensing with OpenAI and Meta | Holds, but small: about 9% of revenue, and much of the growth is the acquired Hatch. |
| Buybacks shrink the share count | Diluted shares down 15% year over year; $200M spent in 2026 at prices well above today (Q3 average $26.14) | Holds mechanically, but the money was spent high and the program was paused low, with $75M still drawn on the revolver at 2026-09-30 (down from $100M at 2026-06-30). |
| Earnings growth | Q3 2026 net income $35M, -12%; diluted EPS $0.63 vs $0.61 (+3%) only because of the buyback | Per-share growth is now entirely from the smaller share count. |
| Full-year 2026 outlook | Now $1.455-1.460B revenue and $320-325M adjusted EBITDA; Q4 guide $347-352M, roughly 1-2% below a year earlier | Revenue range updated (the prior range could not be verified from licensed sources); adjusted EBITDA is down roughly 11% from 2025's $360-365M guide level. |

Balance sheet (2026-09-30): cash $120M, revolver $75M, leases $22M, a net cash position of about $23M. Goodwill and intangibles of $440M reflect the Hatch deal.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining on the core, rising on the new lines.** In Q3 2025 the CFO talked about "quarterly record" services revenue. By Q3 2026 the opening line about the core is defensive: "consumers and local businesses continue to face a challenging economic environment, contributing to increased pressure on advertising revenue." On RR&O, the COO was blunt (2026-11-05): "I wouldn't read into anything in terms of really sunny days ahead." Language on Yelp Host, Hatch and licensing is confident and specific (2.5 million annual calls, food ordering up 6x from June to October). Guidance on the core has become more cautious and less specific.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Management beat the top of its own revenue range in every quarter covered (Q3 2025 +$6M, Q1 2026 +$6M, Q2 2026 +$8M, Q3 2026 +$1M) and beat the top of its adjusted EBITDA range by $13-17M each time. The screener records 7 of 7 quarterly EPS beats. This is a sandbagging pattern, especially on costs, which makes the profit guide dependable. The warning is that the revenue beat shrank to $1M in Q3 2026: the cushion they build into revenue guidance is being consumed by the ad decline. **Reliability: High on profit, Medium on revenue direction.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Why RR&O revenue fell 13% while paying RR&O locations rose 3% (2026-11-05). The answer: multi-location customers added locations without spending more per location - in plain terms, less revenue per advertiser.
- What it takes to stabilize advertising. Management answered about go-to-market for the new products and did not give a stabilization path for the core.
- The margin profile of Other revenue as it scales. The answer was qualitative; they are "certainly investing against growth opportunities" in the near term.
- No analyst got a direct answer on when buybacks resume beyond "2027, subject to market and economic conditions, as well as business requirements."

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: services advertising turned negative (-2%, Q3 2026), the first decline in the covered period.
- Red: ad clicks -8% and RR&O -13% (Q3 2026); Q4 guide flags "increased pressure... across categories".
- Red: buybacks of $200M executed at ~$26 average, then paused near $19 to pay down a revolver; capital return was pro-cyclical.
- Red: insider selling only - 35 open-market sales, no buys; the CFO sold 7,500 shares at $20.00 on 2026-10-15.
- Red: new language about acquisitions funded "through a combination of cash and financing" raises the risk of another goodwill-heavy deal.
- Green: profit beats every quarter; stock pay cut to 6% of revenue, a year ahead of plan.
- Green: Other revenue +82% to $34M, with licensing deals with OpenAI and Meta that monetize Yelp's review content inside AI assistants.
- Green: Request-a-Quote projects up about 10% (Q3 2026), with Yelp Assistant generating about 10% of them - consumer intent is still flowing through the platform.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The reporting vocabulary shifted from "Services revenue" (Q3 2025) to "Services ad revenue" (2026) as Hatch and other non-ad items were split out - the headline growth line is now Other revenue.
- "Paying advertising locations" is falling for services while multi-location RR&O accounts rise: the base is consolidating toward larger, more price-sensitive buyers.
- The cost per click rose 2% while clicks fell 8% (Q3 2026): Yelp can still lift price a little but volume is going the wrong way, which is the shape of a toll road with less traffic.
- Capital allocation priorities were reordered from "healthy cash balance, acquisitions, buybacks" (2025) to "invest in growth, acquisitions with financing, return more than 50% of free cash flow" (2026-11-05) - acquisitions moved up.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning.** Yelp is trying to rebuild growth around AI products while its core advertising business shrinks slowly. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing is the rate of decline in services advertising: at -2% a year the business is a cash machine worth far more than $19.58 a share (about $262M of free cash flow against a ~$1.06B market value); at -6% or worse, the cash flow falls fast enough that today's low multiple is fair.

**Moat:** a narrow but real network moat - two decades of local reviews (a content asset that AI companies now pay to license) and a two-sided base of ~509,000 paying advertising locations. Gross margin is steady at ~90%, but returns (ROIC about 9%) are modest and the moat is eroding: clicks, locations and services ad revenue are all falling. **Secular threat:** AI assistants and Google's AI answers can intercept local search intent before it reaches Yelp. This is material, not terminal: Yelp's content is being licensed into those assistants, and project requests are still growing. The cheapness is part fear and part a genuinely shrinking ad base - it is neither a clear mispricing nor a clear value trap until the decline rate settles.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

Returns are high (return on equity about 37%, return on invested capital about 20%) and the company historically pays out most of its profit. If margins hold at 5-5.5% on a growing backlog, earnings per share can reach NOK 14-15 within two years, and a 15 times multiple plus surplus cash supports about NOK 230. Conditions: margins hold through the next downturn in housing, the big infrastructure contracts are executed without the cost overruns that have historically plagued large fixed-price jobs, and Denmark and Sweden stop lagging.
picks.bear_thesis: The business is good but the share already prices it as permanently better. At NOK 222 (2026-11-10, a 52-week high, up from a NOK 159 low) Veidekke trades at about 18 times trailing earnings, or about 16 times after setting aside the surplus cash - a premium for a contractor, a business whose margins are thin (net margin 3.6% in 2025) and cyclical. The screener flags the margin at 1.27 standard deviations above its own history: this is what peak-cycle earnings look like, helped by full crews, a strong asphalt season and a lull in cost inflation. A single bad large contract can erase a year's margin gain, and the backlog now contains exactly the kind of very large infrastructure work (the Oslofjord Link) where contractors have historically lost money. The cash pile is partly customer prepayments that flow back out when volume slows, so treating all NOK 3.7B as surplus overstates value. The lost-time injury rate rose to 3.8 in Q2 2026 from 2.4 a year earlier, Danish construction revenue was flat, and the Norwegian housing market remains sensitive to interest rates. Our own earnings-power valuation is about 42% below the price. If the margin reverts to 4% and the market pays 12 times, value is about NOK 130 - roughly 40% below today. What confirms it: a third-quarter margin below last year's, order intake slowing, or a write-down on a large project.
picks.consensus_delta: On the deep-value question - is the market pricing terminal decline into a company with stable or growing earnings? - the answer is plainly no. Where we disagree with the market is only on durability: we think a 5% margin is closer to the top of a good cycle than a permanent level, because the screener shows it 1.27 standard deviations above its own history and because the gains now come from full crews and volume rather than repricing. picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) is mostly about expectations, not solvency. With NOK 3.7B of net cash there is no debt wall and no liquidity risk. picks.positioning_washout: Little forced-selling pressure is visible. Veidekke is a Norwegian mid-cap held largely by domestic institutions and dividend investors; no index deletion, lock-up or dividend cut is pending. The more likely seller is a sector-wide de-rating of Nordic contractors if housing or rates turn, which would be a buying opportunity rather than a thesis break. picks.moderator_conclusion: Pass for now. The thesis holds: Veidekke has delivered the 5% pre-tax margin it promised in 2020 (5.0% over the twelve months to June 2026), its order book is up about 12% to NOK 55.3B, and it sits on NOK 3.7B of net cash. # Veidekke ASA (VEI.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-10. Prices in Norwegian kroner (NOK), Oslo listing. No earnings-call transcript was available from our data provider (FMP) for this listing, so this dossier leans on the company's own dated releases (Q2 2026 results, published 2026-08-14), the financial calendar on the investor-relations site, the FMP quarterly statements, and our screener's multi-year numbers. No quotes below are invented; every quote is from the 2026-08-14 release.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story over the last several years has been one of deliberate discipline over growth. In 2020 Veidekke set itself a public goal of a 5% pre-tax profit margin (profit before tax divided by revenue) and chose to take on fewer, better-priced contracts to get there. Revenue has grown only modestly since (NOK 37.6B in 2021 to NOK 43.1B in 2025, about 3.7% a year), while earnings per share rose much faster (NOK 7.07 to NOK 11.50, about 13% a year). That gap between slow sales growth and fast profit growth is the narrative made real: margin, not volume.

In 2026 the tone shifted from "we are getting there" to "we are there and still winning work". The Q2 2026 release (2026-08-14) calls it "a strong second quarter, with solid revenue growth, higher profits and improved profitability", and leans on a record-looking order book: NOK 55.3B at 30 June 2026, up from NOK 49.2B a year earlier, helped by large Norwegian infrastructure wins including the Oslofjord Link. The margin target has moved from a goal to a delivered fact (5.0% over the twelve months to June 2026).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (source, date) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Improved profitability" (Q2 2026 release, 2026-08-14) | Q2 pre-tax margin 5.4% vs 4.7% a year earlier; trailing-twelve-month margin 5.0%; FMP shows Q2 2026 pre-tax profit NOK 669M on NOK 12.3B revenue | Matches |
| "Our order intake is very high" (2026-08-14) | Q2 intake NOK 17.9B vs NOK 14.3B; backlog NOK 55.3B vs NOK 49.2B, about 55% converting within 12 months | Matches |
| Margin discipline over growth (strategy since 2020) | Revenue CAGR ~3.7%, EPS CAGR ~12.9% (5-year); ROE 37%, ROIC ~20% | Matches |
| Cash generation | First-half 2026 operating cash flow NOK 1.7B vs NOK 146M; net interest-bearing assets NOK 3.7B at 30 June 2026 vs NOK 1.2B a year earlier; trailing free cash flow NOK 4.44B | Matches, with a caveat: a contractor's cash pile is partly customer prepayments that unwind when volume slows, so not all of it is surplus |
| Seasonality | Q1 is structurally weak (Q1 2026 pre-tax profit NOK 27M; Q1 2025 a small loss), so one strong quarter must not be annualised | Context, not a flaw |

Data note: the screener's 100% gross margin is an artefact (Veidekke reports no cost-of-sales line in several FMP quarters); ignore it. The share counts in the FMP quarterly file also wobble (105M to 137M) - a data artefact; the market capitalisation of about NOK 30.0B at NOK 222 implies roughly 135M shares, which we use.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Rating: Stable to Rising. The 2026-08-14 release is confident but not promotional - no formal guidance, just that the asphalt season "had a strong start" and that the project portfolio "continues to deliver good margins". There is no shift toward defensive cost or macro language. The one soft spot management itself flagged is Denmark, where construction revenue was flat while every other unit grew.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Veidekke gives targets, not quarterly guidance. The one target that matters - the 5% margin set in 2020 - was delivered on a trailing basis by mid-2026. The screener shows earnings beat estimates in 5 of the last 7 quarters (71%). Reliability: High.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Without a transcript we cannot quote analyst questions. The obvious pressure points are: (a) whether 5%+ margins are a new floor or the top of a good cycle, given that Norwegian infrastructure spending and a strong asphalt season flatter the current numbers; (b) whether the cash pile will be returned (Veidekke historically pays out most of its earnings) or is needed as working capital; (c) the Danish business and the Swedish construction market; (d) safety - the lost-time injury rate rose to 3.8 in Q2 2026 from 2.4 a year earlier.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Green: trailing pre-tax margin reached the 5.0% target (12 months to June 2026).
- Green: order backlog up about 12% year on year to NOK 55.3B (30 June 2026), much of it public infrastructure.
- Green: net cash of NOK 3.7B (30 June 2026) and a Piotroski score of 8 of 9.
- Red: lost-time injury rate 3.8 in Q2 2026 vs 2.4 in Q2 2025 - a culture signal worth watching in a contractor.
- Red: the stock sits at its 52-week high (NOK 222 on 2026-11-10, range NOK 159-222), so the good news is in the price.
- Red: margin is 1.27 standard deviations above its own history - the classic peak-earnings warning for a cyclical contractor.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The language has moved from "turnaround" to "capacity utilisation" - management now credits volume and full crews, not repricing, for the profit gains. That is healthy but it also means the next leg of margin needs volume to hold. The Oslofjord Link win shows Veidekke is again willing to take very large infrastructure contracts, a category where contractors historically lose money; the discipline story will be tested inside that contract over several years.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: STRENGTHENING. The single most important thing to weigh: the business case is real and proven, but the share price at NOK 222 already pays about 18 times trailing earnings (about 16 times after setting aside the cash), which prices the 5% margin as permanent. The next dated test is the Q3 2026 report on 2026-11-12.

Moat: narrow. Veidekke's edge is local scale and execution reputation in Norwegian civil engineering plus owned asphalt and aggregates assets, which give some cost advantage. Returns are rising (ROIC ~20%) and margins expanding, so the moat is not eroding. No structural (non-cyclical) force threatens terminal value; the risks are cyclical (housing, interest rates, public budgets). The current price is not a fear-print; it is a fair-to-full price for a good contractor.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat none.

# thyssenkrupp AG (TKA.DE) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-16. Live price EUR 11.815 on Xetra (FMP quote), market value about EUR 7.36 billion (about 622 million shares). Sources: five earnings calls (2025-05-15 half-year FY24/25, 2025-08-14 nine-month FY24/25, 2025-12-09 full-year FY24/25, 2026-02-12 Q1 FY25/26, 2026-08-13 nine-month FY25/26), the screener's financial trajectory, and dated news through mid-November 2026. thyssenkrupp's fiscal year ends 30 September.

**Bottom line:** management has done what it said on structure - two businesses listed in twelve months (the naval unit TKMS on 2025-10-20, the materials distributor tk accelis on 2026-10-28) - but it has not yet shown that the remaining businesses earn their cost of capital. Revenue has fallen three years running, free cash flow before acquisitions is guided negative for this fiscal year, and the steel unit's green-steel plant has slipped two years. The break-up story is real; the earnings story is still a promise.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Mid-2025 (H1 and 9M FY24/25):** the story was "resilience in weak markets" - the cost programme APEX 2.0, headcount cuts (2,600 fewer staff by Q2, 4,200 by Q3) and a debt-free balance sheet ("EUR4 billion in net cash... makes the group debt-free", 2025-05-15). The TKMS spin was the headline portfolio move; the steel unit was heading for a 50/50 joint venture with EPCG.
- **December 2025 (FY24/25):** the story widened into "ACES 2030" - turning thyssenkrupp into a "financial holding company" with stand-alone, separately listed businesses. TKMS was listed; Jindal Steel was negotiating to buy a majority of the steel unit; a union restructuring agreement was signed.
- **February 2026 (Q1 FY25/26):** confidence peaked. European steel stocks had re-rated about 50% on EU import quotas and tariffs, and the CEO said that sentiment would "get into an input" for the Jindal talks. The Salzgitter takeover of the HKM steelworks was agreed.
- **May to August 2026:** the Jindal talks were paused (reported around 2026-05, with management citing "significantly changed" assumptions). The steel unit is now to be made independent on its own, with thyssenkrupp eventually holding a minority. The 2026-08-13 call pivoted to tk accelis (the renamed Materials Services) as "the next visible proof point" and to a steel Capital Markets Day.
- **Autumn 2026:** tk accelis listed on 2026-10-28 (first price EUR 27.80; EUR 25.30 today). The steel unit set medium-term targets of at least EUR 1.2 billion adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) and an 11% margin, then in November moved the start-up of its Duisburg direct-reduction plant (the hydrogen-ready iron plant at the core of its green-steel plan) from 2027 to 2029.

What was quietly dropped: the steel sale to a strategic buyer (Jindal), and the early-2025 language about the green-energy business (Decarbon Technologies) growing; by August 2026 the CEO conceded clean-fuel markets had been "very hesitant" for three years and the group will only "exploit the technologies that we have right now on hand".

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Increasing underlying resilience": EBIT adjusted (operating profit before one-offs) held while sales fell | Sales fell from EUR 41.1bn (FY21/22) to EUR 32.8bn (FY24/25), down about 7% a year for three years; EBIT adjusted rose from EUR 568m to EUR 640m in FY24/25 | Matches - but only a ~2% margin on a much smaller base |
| "Third year in a row positive" free cash flow before M&A (FY24/25: EUR 363m) | FY24/25 was helped by a large TKMS customer prepayment; FY25/26 is guided at minus EUR 600m to minus EUR 300m, and trailing-twelve-month free cash flow (TTM, the last four quarters) is minus EUR 1.0bn at 2026-06-30 | The streak ends this year; the cash claim was richer than the underlying trend |
| Net cash is a strong cushion | Net cash fell from about EUR 5bn (2025-09-30) to EUR 3.2bn (Q1) and EUR 2.6bn (2026-06-30). Pension provisions are about EUR 5.2bn, half of them in steel | The cash is real but roughly halved, and it is smaller than the pension deficit |
| Net income turning positive | FY24/25 net income of EUR 465m depended on a EUR 902m Q4 revaluation of the TK Elevator stake; FY25/26 net income guidance is minus EUR 700m to minus EUR 40m | Accounting gains, not operating earnings |
| Steel self-help is working | Steel EBIT adjusted "more than doubled year-to-date" (2026-08-13), helped by lower raw material costs and an electricity price compensation; EUR 400m of steel write-ups were booked in Q3 FY25/26 after years of impairments (EUR 600m in FY24/25) | Improving from a very low base; part is input-cost luck |
| Portfolio value "crystallisation" | TKMS: 49% distributed 1-for-20 on 2025-10-20, now EUR 76 (thyssenkrupp's 51% is worth about EUR 2.46bn). tk accelis: 49% distributed 1-for-20, listed 2026-10-28, now EUR 25.30 (51% is worth about EUR 0.82bn) | Delivered as promised |

Return on equity is minus 4.1% and return on invested capital minus 2.0% on the latest fiscal year; earnings beat expectations in only 1 of the last 5 quarters.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a defensive tilt since spring 2026.** May 2025 was upbeat ("You can see we are delivering proof points"). February 2026 was the most confident ("there are really good things happening" on steel policy). August 2026 was measured: "staying realistic about the macro and demand environment" and "we are not yet seeing a broad-based market recovery". Guidance became less specific on cash: the CFO repeatedly declined to give the steel unit's starting balance sheet ("it's too early to talk about", 2026-08-13; "it's difficult to quantify", 2025-08-14).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- FY24/25: sales guidance cut in August 2025, EBIT adjusted moved to the low end of EUR 600m-1bn, delivered EUR 640m; free cash flow guidance met and slightly beaten.
- FY25/26: sales cut again in August 2026 (now minus 3% to minus 1%), EBIT adjusted range narrowed to EUR 600-900m, free cash flow confirmed at minus EUR 600m to minus EUR 300m with a heavy fourth-quarter reversal still needed (nine-month figure minus EUR 1.9bn).
- Pattern: top-line guidance is routinely cut; profit and cash ranges are wide enough to be met. The 1-in-5 beat rate fits that. **Reliability: Medium.** Results for FY25/26 (with the annual report) are due on 2026-12-08 and will show whether the fourth-quarter cash reversal arrived.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Pensions** (2026-08-13, Jason Fairclough): analysts want to know how much of the EUR 5.2bn deficit leaves with each carve-out; the CFO confirmed half sits with steel and that only a "low 3-digit million" amount went with HKM. The analyst concluded he may need to treat it "as 100% consolidated debt". This is the single biggest unresolved value question.
- **Steel's starting balance sheet and cash needs** were asked on 2025-08-14, 2025-12-09 and 2026-08-13 and never answered.
- **Further steel impairments** "cannot be excluded" (2025-12-09).
- **Materials Services working capital** (2026-02-12): management acknowledged it as part of "capital market readiness".
- **Decarbon Technologies** project delays and cost overruns at the cement unit (Polysius) recur in every 2026 call.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: free cash flow before M&A turns negative in FY25/26 (guided 2025-12-09) after three positive years; TTM minus EUR 1.0bn.
- Red: net cash roughly halved in nine months (EUR ~5bn to EUR 2.6bn, 2025-09-30 to 2026-06-30).
- Red: the Jindal steel sale was paused (around 2026-05); the steel exit now depends on a slower stand-alone route.
- Red: the Duisburg green-steel plant slipped from 2027 to 2029 (November 2026), extending capital spending and execution risk.
- Red: Decarbon Technologies sales fell 19% in Q1 FY25/26 with recurring legacy project charges.
- Green: two listings delivered on schedule (2025-10-20 and 2026-10-28).
- Green: steel profits rising on self-help, and the HKM exit (closed early July 2026) removes an expensive slab supply contract from 2028.
- Green: TKMS backlog above EUR 20bn (2026-08-13), giving a growing, visible defence business that thyssenkrupp still controls.
- Green: the 16.2% TK Elevator stake (booked around EUR 2bn) could be monetised if its owners pursue the IPO or sale reported through 2026.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The phrase "financial holding company" now does the work that "turnaround" used to. It shifts the investor's question from "will these businesses earn money?" to "what will a buyer or the market pay for each piece?" - which is a sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) story with a holding-company discount attached.
- The CFO changed in May 2025 (Jens Schulte to Axel Hamann); the new CFO is noticeably more guarded on balance-sheet allocation between units.
- On steel, the language moved from "sell the majority to Jindal" (February 2026) to "make it independent, keep a minority eventually" (May 2026). A business no one would buy at an acceptable price is being prepared for the market instead.
- Green-transformation language is now hedged on policy ("policy framework is not clear"), which matters for the EUR 2bn of public funding tied to the DRI plant.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning.** The group is being rebuilt as a holding company of listed stakes plus three unlisted, low-margin industrial businesses (steel, automotive parts, plant engineering). The most important thing to weigh: at EUR 11.815 the market already pays about EUR 7.4bn for a package whose listed and semi-liquid pieces (51% of TKMS, 51% of tk accelis, 16% of TK Elevator, 50% of nucera) are worth about EUR 5.8bn before any holding-company discount, so the remaining businesses plus net cash must be worth about EUR 1.6bn more than the pension deficit and head-office costs. That is roughly where they are - there is no large hidden discount left after two spin-offs.

**Moat:** narrow and concentrated in the parts - TKMS (a regulatory and technology position in non-nuclear submarines), the Rothe Erde bearings and Bilstein aftermarket niches. The steel unit and the distribution business have no durable moat. Group returns are negative (return on invested capital minus 2.0%), so the group-level moat is not widening; the trend is stable because the weak parts are being carved out rather than eroding further. **Secular threat: manageable** - European steel faces carbon costs and a costly green conversion, but the EU's carbon border tax and import quotas now shield it; the automotive parts business is exposed to slow car demand rather than a terminal shift. The cheapness that remains is a holding-company and pension discount, not a fear-print on a structurally shrinking franchise.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

That is about 2.4 times trailing earnings for the operating business. The operating numbers have stabilised after the 2025 US tariff reset: revenue was higher than a year earlier in every 2026 quarter, and Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) brought revenue of 31.6 trillion won, up about 10%, and operating profit of 1.82 trillion, up about 24%, with the operating margin rising to 5.8% from 5.1%. The dividend was raised in cash terms (2.64 trillion won paid in Q2 2026, about 6,800 won per share, a 7% yield at today's price). picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness may be a permanent Korea discount compounded by a cyclical peak. Net cash in a carmaker is working capital and a buffer for downturns, not money owners can take out; it has sat on the balance sheet for years without closing the gap. US tariffs on Korean cars are now a permanent cost under the Section 301 regime that took effect 2026-07-24, and gross margin was still about 1.7 points below a year earlier in Q2 2026 (18.3% vs 20.0%). The sell-side has been too optimistic for nearly two years - Kia beat estimates in 0 of the last 7 quarters - so the 2027 consensus of 19,663 won per share (range 14,806 to 24,296) should be haircut. Q3 2026 net income fell about 10% to 1.29 trillion won even as operating profit rose, because the usual interest and affiliate income vanished below the operating line, and that has not been explained. Share buybacks, about 0.3 trillion won a quarter through 2025, are absent from the first half of 2026. Higher-for-longer rates squeeze US auto-loan affordability, Chinese electric-vehicle makers compete on price in Europe and emerging markets, and the Korean market is still in a liquidation driven by foreign selling and the memory-chip unwind. A recession could take auto earnings back to 2021 levels (about 4.8 trillion won, roughly 12,000 won per share), and in a forced-selling tape the price can fall below any fundamental floor. What would confirm it: another quarter of falling net income, a cut to the shareholder-return plan, or an operating margin below 5%.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the price implies Kia's earnings are about to fall sharply again, and the numbers do not show it. The sell-off is being driven by the Korean market as a whole (KOSPI down about 47% from its high) rather than by Kia-specific news. Where the street has been wrong in the other direction: consensus has been too high for nearly two years (beats in 0 of 7 quarters), so we haircut the 2027 consensus of 19,663 won per share rather than rely on it. picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): the Korean market liquidation may not be over - foreign outflows and the memory-chip unwind have taken the KOSPI down about 47%, and Kia falls with it regardless of results (down 3.3% today while Toyota and GM rose about 4-5%). A weaker won helps exports but raises the dollar cost for foreign holders, which can keep them selling. US tariffs under the Section 301 regime in force since 2026-07-24 are a permanent cost, and rising real rates hurt US car affordability. There is no debt wall and no cash-burn hump: net cash is about 21.2 trillion won. Q4 2026 results (late January 2027) are the next checkpoint; another below-the-line surprise like Q3 would hurt sentiment.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure: the selling so far looks like a sector-wide and market-wide liquidation rather than Kia-specific forced selling - Korean equities lost about 22% in July 2026 alone, a large levered fund was margin-called and liquidated in late July according to the regime log, and foreign investors have been de-risking Korea. Kia is a large, liquid index weight and so gets sold with the market. The shareholder base is not yield-focused enough for a dividend cut to trigger mechanical selling, and none has been announced; the dividend was raised in cash terms in Q2 2026.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds: Kia is still growing (revenue up about 10% and operating profit up about 24% in the quarter ended 2026-09-30) and sits on about 21.2 trillion won of net cash, more than half of its 37.7 trillion won market value. The fall from 205,500 won since late February is mostly a Korean market liquidation (KOSPI down about 47% from its high, Hyundai Motor down about 65%), not a Kia earnings collapse. picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Webuild S.p.A. (WBD.MI, Borsa Italiana, EUR) - forensic dossier, 2026-11-09

Takeaway: a growing, margin-improving contractor whose earnings are real on paper but have not turned into cash, run by management that leads with an adjusted "net cash" figure the statutory balance sheet does not show. The Italian state funded more of the disputed rail overruns in the budget bill on 2026-11-01, which eases the worst liquidity fear, but sites are still slowing over unpaid work and the promised 2026-2029 plan remains undated. Live price EUR 2.176 (FMP quote, Milan listing, 2026-11-09).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
On the 2026-07-30 first-half call (the latest transcript), management told a story of scale turning into value: revenue held at a record EUR 6.7B despite two cancelled NEOM contracts in Saudi Arabia (about EUR 3.8B of backlog, more than EUR 550M of 2026 revenue), EBITDA up 14% to EUR 673M, a EUR 47B construction backlog, and a 2026-2029 business plan "at the end of September" built on vertical integration and "stable and predictable cash generation". The plan was then postponed on 2026-09-23 until after the Trevi takeover. Since our last review (2026-10-12) the story has moved to two fronts: winning Trevi (rival bidder ICOP withdrew on 2026-11-05; Webuild owns about 42% as of 2026-11-09 and the offer is now mandatory and unconditional, closing 2026-11-20, payment 2026-11-27) and getting paid by the state rail operator RFI.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- "Net cash of EUR 110M" (company definition) versus statutory net debt of about EUR 960M at 2026-06-30 (borrowings EUR 3.25B plus EUR 77M leases, minus EUR 2.37B cash). The gap is the company excluding project-level and Panama Canal debt and including items it treats as cash-like. We use the statutory figure.
- Trailing free cash flow is negative EUR 559M (to 2026-06-30) against EUR 240M of 2025 net income. Earnings are not converting.
- Financial expenses rose EUR 93M in the half, explained as interest waived on receivables in settlement deals plus "a genuine one-off write-down". Waiving interest to collect faster is a sign the receivables are hard to collect.
- Return on invested capital about 3.5%, below any reasonable cost of capital for a BB+ issuer paying 5.1% on debt.
- Altman Z about 0.8 (a solvency stress score; below 1.8 is the distress zone), though typical of contractors carrying large advances and receivables.
- Positive: S&P confirmed the BB+ rating on 2026-11-09, citing the order book and rising margins; 95% of debt is fixed rate and little matures before late 2028.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Confident and promotional on the call ("no single project or market can affect our ability to create value"). Since September the tone has turned defensive and public: a leaked letter to the government, a complaint to the market regulator Consob, RFI publicly contradicting Webuild (2026-09-18), "Works done, RFI must pay" (2026-10-22), and on 2026-11-06 press reports of Webuild pressing the government over accumulated receivables on the Brenner tunnel. Workers on several rail sites were put on short-time pay in October.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
2026 guidance was confirmed after the September headlines and the backlog does cover 2026 revenue, so the top-line guide is credible. The cash promise is not yet tested: capital spending of about EUR 700M this year was called "a peak", and the plan meant to set cash targets has slipped once already. The third-quarter update is still pending (date not confirmed in the sources we could reach).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Analysts pressed on Saudi exposure after NEOM, whether EUR 700M of capital spending is a peak (answer: yes), Trevi synergies (EUR 80-90M of EBITDA "from 2027", with no ramp detail) and Trevi's 60% emerging-market revenue, which runs against Webuild's stated low-risk-geography strategy. No analyst pushed on the net-cash definition or cash conversion, which is the real question. No current analyst price-target consensus could be verified for this listing.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: statutory net debt versus headline net cash; negative free cash flow; interest waived to collect receivables; public payment fight with its largest domestic client; rail sites slowing and short-time work (2026-10-16 to 2026-11-03); arsenic-bearing spoil raising Brenner disposal costs (2026-11-02 and 2026-11-09); Libyan Autostrada della Pace contract torn up by the Haftar administration (2026-10-07); a debt-funded acquisition (mandatory offer of about EUR 222M for the remainder of Trevi) while cash is negative; finance chief departure in September.
Green: record backlog with price-adjustment clauses; margins rising (EBITDA margin 10.1%); the 2026 budget bill adds about EUR 1.6B for the Terzo Valico rail line (2026-11-01/02), showing the state is funding overruns rather than refusing them; new orders (Genoa sub-port tunnel lot B, EUR 803M, signed 2026-10-15; Toronto Ontario Line, 2026-08-05); S&P BB+ confirmed with stable outlook (2026-11-09); bond maturities pushed to 2028+.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The rescue money is coming through the budget, not through settled claims: the state is paying more for the projects, but the receivable dispute itself is not closed, so cash timing still depends on RFI. Management's choice to spend on Trevi before publishing cash targets suggests growth and control rank ahead of cash return in their priorities. The share price recovered from EUR 1.81 to about EUR 2.18 into the budget news and the Trevi win, so some relief is already priced.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Operations are improving and the state is still paying for its rail program, but cash conversion is the unproven link and management is spending on an acquisition before proving it. Treat the stock as an earnings-cheap, cash-unproven contractor: worth owning only at a price that pays for the cash risk, or after a plan with statutory free-cash-flow targets is published and starts to be met.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
