picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is mostly an accounting artifact and a governance discount. The screener's 2.4x price-to-cash-flow and 75% discount to a DCF value come from adding back lease depreciation; strip out rent and the stock is a 6-7x cash-flow retailer with about EUR 1.04B of net borrowings at mid-year 2026 before EUR 1.19B of leases, an Altman Z of 1.5, return on invested capital of about 3% and an operating margin of about 2% in a weak French consumer market (management, 2026-02-25: 'a challenging consumption situation in France'). More importantly the shareholder base has changed: EP Group now owns 69.3% (AMF result, 2026-11-10), the offer reopens only until 2026-11-25, and EP Group has said it will not squeeze out remaining holders. After that date a buyer owns an illiquid minority stake (the latest session traded 6,388 shares) in a controlled company whose dividend, capital spending and related-party dealings are set by the controller. Controlled minority stubs commonly trade at 15-30% below the control price; the 52-week low was EUR 26.25. Repeated write-downs (Nature & Decouvertes, EUR 78M in 2025) and a capital-spending plan of about EUR 200M a year cap what reaches minority holders.
picks.consensus_delta: The screener and simple multiples see a 2.4x price-to-cash-flow stock with a 75% discount to discounted-cash-flow value. That is wrong: the cash flow includes the add-back of roughly EUR 300M a year of lease depreciation that is in substance rent. On real free cash flow of about EUR 145-160M the stock is 6-7x - cheap, not absurd. The market itself has priced the name off the EUR 35 offer, not off fundamentals, since January 2026. Where we disagree with the market is narrower: once the offer closes on 2026-11-25 the price support disappears, and the natural level for a controlled, illiquid stub is below the control price, not at it. We do not believe the street is pricing terminal decline into a stable earner; we believe it is still pricing the offer.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is late November 2026 to mid-2027. After 2026-11-25 the EUR 35 bid disappears; event-driven funds that did not tender become forced sellers into very thin volume. Free float falls to roughly 30%, which can trigger removal or down-weighting in mid-cap indices that screen on free float and liquidity. Operating risk sits in the first half (Fnac Darty loses money every first half; the 2026 H1 loss was EUR -34M) and in seasonal borrowing of about EUR 1.04B at mid-year against an Altman Z of 1.5. Bonds of EUR 550M due 2029 and EUR 300M due 2032 are covered by EUR 600M of undrawn credit lines, so there is no near-term maturity wall. Weak French consumption (flagged 2026-02-25) is the main fundamental risk to the 2026 margin guidance, reported around February 2027.
picks.positioning_washout: Yes, and it is the reason to wait. The holders of the remaining roughly 30% of shares are merger-arbitrage and event-driven funds, index trackers and retail holders. Arbitrage funds that did not tender by 2026-11-25 have no reason to keep a controlled stub; index funds may be forced out if free float drops below index thresholds. These are forced or non-fundamental sellers, and in a stock that trades a few thousand shares a day they can push the price well below the EUR 35 offer - the 52-week low was EUR 26.25. A wash-out (a sharp sell-off by forced or non-fundamental sellers) toward EUR 30 is the entry we want.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for a better price: we buy near EUR 30, which forced selling by arbitrage funds and index trackers after the offer closes on 2026-11-25 could deliver. The thesis holds: Fnac Darty is a flat-sales, low-margin but cash-generative retailer whose first-half 2026 loss narrowed and whose guidance for higher margin and cash flow is intact. But at EUR 34.90 the stock is pinned to EP Group's EUR 35 offer, and our base fair value of about EUR 36.5 (8.5x operating profit before lease accounting, less seasonal net borrowings and a modest discount for being a controlled minority) leaves only about 5% of upside, well short of the 20% discount this market requires. The screener's headline cheapness (2.4x price-to-cash-flow) is a lease-accounting artifact; on real free cash flow the stock is about 6-7x. With EP Group at 69.3% and no squeeze-out planned, a minority buyer after 2026-11-25 owns an illiquid stake with no exit mechanism, which is why the bear case of EUR 26 is real. At about EUR 30 the discount to fair value clears 20% and the price would sit near the level forced sellers typically leave behind; until then, pass on chasing the offer spread. For anyone already holding, tendering at EUR 35 before 2026-11-25 is close to full value.
picks.forcing_function: Near term: the reopened offer closes 2026-11-25 (EUR 35), and its final result fixes the free float. After that, the re-rating has to come from the business: full-year 2026 results (around late February 2027) confirming the guided increase in operating margin and free cash flow, Unieuro synergies of at least EUR 20M by end-2026, the dividend decision at the May 2027 shareholders' meeting (payout policy above 40%), and any sale of Nature & Decouvertes. A later move by EP Group to buy out the minority would be upside, but it has said it will not squeeze out, so we give it no weight.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Fnac Darty (FNAC.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Source material: the full-year 2025 results call (2026-02-25), the screener's financial trajectory, FMP quarterly statements through 2026-06-30, and the dated tender-offer releases of 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-10. Only one call transcript was available, so trend judgements lean on the financials.*

**The takeaway:** Fnac Darty is a low-margin, cash-generative French electronics and books retailer whose story in 2026 is no longer about its own plan - it is about its new owner. EP Group (Daniel Kretinsky's holding) now controls 69.3% of the shares after a cash tender offer at EUR 35 per share (EUR 36 before the EUR 1 dividend paid on 2026-06-05). The offer has been reopened until 2026-11-25 on the same terms, and EP Group has said it will not squeeze out the remaining holders. Management's operating claims are modest and mostly corroborated; the large risk for a minority shareholder is governance and liquidity after the offer closes, not the stores.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The February 2026 call had two stories running side by side. The first was the five-year "Beyond Everyday" plan (launched June 2025): grow subscription services (2.4 million subscribers at end-2025, target 4 million by 2030), second-life (refurbished) products, store renovation, and an operating margin of "at least 3% in 2030" with cumulative free cash flow (cash left after capital spending) of "at least EUR 1.2 billion over 2025-2030". The second was the EP Group cash offer at EUR 36, which the board "favorably received ... unanimously".

What quietly left the story: Nature & Decouvertes, the gift-and-nature chain, was moved to held-for-sale after a turnaround that "didn't come to fruition", with a EUR 78 million charge, mostly goodwill. What was added: the Unieuro (Italy) integration, which drove the reported revenue jump from EUR 8.25 billion (2024) to EUR 10.33 billion (2025) - an acquisition effect, not organic growth (like-for-like growth was +0.7%).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (2026-02-25) | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue "up 0.7%" like-for-like, outperforming the French market | Reported +25% in 2025 is Unieuro; H1 2026 revenue EUR 4.46B vs EUR 4.48B in H1 2025 (about -0.5%) | Matches: growth is flat, not a growth story |
| Current operating income EUR 203M, 2% margin, "up" | First-half operating loss narrowed to EUR -34M (H1 2026) from EUR -57M (H1 2025) on FMP's basis; the business earns almost all its profit in Q4 | Corroborated directionally |
| Free cash flow (excluding lease accounting) EUR 145M, down from EUR 210M in 2024 | 2024 included a EUR 93M warehouse sale; underlying FCF roughly stable | Honest - management flagged the one-off itself |
| "Sound" balance sheet, BB+ ratings | Year-end 2025: borrowings EUR 958M vs cash EUR 1.10B, so about EUR 146M net cash before leases. Mid-year 2026: borrowings EUR 1.56B vs cash EUR 516M, about EUR 1.04B net debt before leases, plus EUR 1.19B of lease liabilities. Altman Z (a bankruptcy-risk score) 1.5 | The year-end figure flatters; the average-year debt is much higher because suppliers fund the Christmas inventory. Sound but not strong |
| Screener's P/FCF of 2.4x and "+75% DCF margin of safety" | TTM cash flow of EUR 686M includes the add-back of lease depreciation; lease cash payments of roughly EUR 300M a year must come off. Real owner free cash flow is about EUR 145-180M, so the stock trades at roughly 6-7x real free cash flow on a EUR 1.03B market value - cheap, but before about EUR 0.45B of average-year net debt and EUR 0.12B of minority interests | The screener's cheapness signal is a lease-accounting artifact. Do not trust it |
| Net loss per share EUR -4.92 (2025) | Driven by non-cash items: EUR 96M non-recurring and the EUR 78M Nature & Decouvertes write-down; restated continuing net income was about +EUR 28M | The headline loss overstates the damage; the restated profit is still thin |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable, defensive. Management talked of a "challenging consumption situation in France, notably in Q4" and declined to confirm current trading ("I cannot confirm what the performance is today"). The guidance is qualitative - "an increase in our current operating margin and also our free cash flow" - with no numbers for 2026. The language is that of a company handing strategic direction to a controlling shareholder ("the support of a long-term stable shareholder is a great asset").

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The previous plan's targets were broadly met per management, and the 2025 cash flow came in "in line with our expectations". The EUR 20 million Unieuro synergy target by end-2026 is "confirmed". Guidance is modest and usually delivered; it is also vague enough to be hard to miss. Reliability: Medium.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts asked about the Nature & Decouvertes sale proceeds (management: "too soon to say"), French trading after weak Bank of France data (deflected), and capital spending (about EUR 200M a year on average to 2030 - a real claim on the cash flow). No question addressed what happens to minority holders after the offer - the most important question for anyone buying now.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: controlled company with no squeeze-out (2026-11-10 release) - remaining holders become a small, illiquid minority whose dividends and strategy are set by EP Group.
- Red: trading volume collapsed (6,388 shares on the latest session) and the price sits pinned just below the EUR 35 offer.
- Red: operating margin of about 2% leaves little room for error in a weak French consumer market; Altman Z of 1.5.
- Red: repeated write-downs (Nature & Decouvertes goodwill, 2025).
- Green: services now 27% of gross margin (up 200 basis points in 2025) - higher quality earnings.
- Green: first-half operating loss narrowed by about EUR 23M year on year (H1 2026).
- Green: dividend policy kept at a payout above 40%; EUR 1 paid 2026-06-05.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The CFO's vocabulary shifted to "rigorous management of our portfolio" (Nature & Decouvertes disposal) - a portfolio-pruning tone consistent with a new owner's priorities. The board's unanimous support and an independent expert (Ledouble) report preceded the offer; the expert's opinion that EUR 36 was fair is a useful anchor for what the controlling shareholder thinks the whole company is worth.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: Pivoting - from a widely held listed retailer to a Kretinsky-controlled subsidiary with a residual listing. The single most important thing to weigh: a buyer today is not buying Fnac Darty's plan, they are buying a minority stake in a controlled company at almost exactly the price the controller paid for control, with no exit mechanism after 2026-11-25.

Moat: narrow, scale-and-brand based (the Fnac cultural brand, Darty's after-sales "contrat de confiance", 9 million click-and-collect pickups a year, a 2.4 million-member subscription base). Returns do not show a wide moat: return on invested capital about 3%, operating margin about 2%. The margin is flat to slightly up, so the moat is narrow and stable rather than eroding. The secular force is the shift of electronics and books to online pure players and marketplaces; Fnac Darty has answered it partly (22% of sales online, half picked up in stores), so the threat is material but not terminal. The cheapness is largely an accounting artifact plus a controlled-minority discount, not a fear-print mispricing.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.
picks.sop_breakdown: Base case, valued as one company (no segment block): operating profit before lease accounting of about EUR 205M for 2026 (2025's EUR 203M current operating income plus modest guided improvement, less lease-accounting difference) x 8.5x = EUR 1.74B enterprise value; less about EUR 0.45B average-year net borrowings (stated definition: excluding leases, seasonal average of the 2025-12-31 net cash of EUR 0.15B and 2026-06-30 net debt of EUR 1.04B) and EUR 0.12B minority interests = EUR 1.17B equity, about EUR 39.5 per share on 29.7M shares. Cross-check: EUR 160M of 2026 free cash flow at a 13% yield = EUR 41. Blend about EUR 40, less a roughly 10% discount for being a controlled, illiquid minority with no squeeze-out = EUR 36.5. This sits just above the EUR 36 (cum-dividend) control price an independent expert judged fair, which is a sensible anchor. No special-situation overlay is added: the EUR 1 dividend was paid 2026-06-05, and Nature & Decouvertes sale proceeds are undisclosed.
picks.sop_bull: Whole-company intrinsic value (no segment revenue block). Operating profit before lease accounting of about EUR 250M by 2028 (2.4% margin on EUR 10.4B, halfway to the 2030 3% target) x 9x enterprise value to operating profit = EUR 2.25B enterprise value; less average-year net borrowings of about EUR 0.45B (year-end 2025 net cash EUR 0.15B, mid-2026 net debt EUR 1.04B - the seasonal average is used) and minority interests of EUR 0.12B = EUR 1.68B equity over 29.7M shares = about EUR 56; haircut 20% for controlled-minority status and execution = about EUR 45 per share. Leases are treated as an operating cost, not as debt.
picks.sop_bear: Operating profit before lease accounting of about EUR 180M (flat 2025 level less weaker French demand) x 6x = EUR 1.08B; less average-year net borrowings EUR 0.45B and minorities EUR 0.12B = EUR 0.51B, about EUR 17 per share on pure multiple; cross-checked against a 14% free-cash-flow yield on EUR 145M (EUR 1.04B, EUR 35 per share) and a 25% controlled-minority discount to that = about EUR 26. Bear value EUR 26 per share, close to the 52-week low of EUR 26.25.
picks.risk_reward: From EUR 34.90, the base fair value of EUR 36.5 is about 5% above and the bear value of EUR 26 about 25% below; the bull value of EUR 45 is about 29% above. The reward from today's price does not compensate for the downside once the offer closes on 2026-11-25. (Ratios are recomputed by the pipeline.)
picks.catalyst_status_plain: a deal-close arbitrage
picks.peer_comps_note: Against Currys, Ceconomy and Best Buy, Fnac Darty looks cheap on the screener's free-cash-flow multiple, but that multiple is inflated by lease accounting; on lease-adjusted cash flow (about 6-7x) and operating profit it is cheap but not dramatically so, and the discount is partly earned by its 2% operating margin, 3% return on capital, an Altman Z of 1.5 and now controlled-minority status. Ceconomy's own 2025 sale to JD.com is a reminder that European electronics retailers change hands near, not far above, their trading values. No live peer multiple file was provided, so no specific peer multiple is cited; the 8.5x operating-profit base multiple is within the usual range for low-margin European electronics retail. The gap is a mix of quality and governance, not clear name-specific mispricing.
picks.thesis_evidence: The business case (a flat-sales, slowly improving-margin, cash-generative retailer) is corroborated by the latest dated numbers: the first-half 2026 operating loss narrowed to about EUR -34M from EUR -57M (FMP, period ending 2026-06-30) on revenue of EUR 4.46B versus EUR 4.48B, consistent with the 2026-02-25 guidance of a higher operating margin and free cash flow. The 2026-11-10 offer result changes the ownership (EP Group 69.3%, no squeeze-out), which weighs on price and liquidity but does not disprove any operating claim.
picks.macro_fit_note: Reflation with a discipline-phase debt cycle (positive real rates, about an 18-month horizon) rewards cash now over long-dated stories, and Fnac Darty is a cash-now payback profile, but it is a discretionary retailer exposed to a weak French consumer and to higher refinancing costs on its seasonal borrowing, so the two roughly offset. It kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin moved only -0.4 points), but there is no pass-through evidence in the transcript.
picks.entry_plain: buy near 30 EUR, which forced selling by holders who must sell regardless of value could deliver

picks.bull_thesis: The market is pricing Kuaishou as if its earnings are in permanent decline, when most of the 2026 profit drop is a deliberate, front-loaded AI spending cycle on top of a still-profitable platform. At HK$25.30 (2026-11-16 close) the company is worth about HK$108.8 billion; about HK$49 billion of that is net cash (cash and short-term investments of RMB 80.6 billion against RMB 39.0 billion of debt at 2026-06-30, converted at 1.179 HK$ per yuan), and the company also holds RMB 44 billion of long-term investments not counted here. That leaves roughly HK$60 billion for an operating business that still earned RMB 3.1 billion of reported net profit and RMB 3.9 billion of adjusted profit in Q2 2026 alone, plus a 68% stake in Kling AI. Kling is real and fast-growing: revenue above RMB 850 million in Q2 2026, up over 200%, and outside investors (reportedly General Atlantic leading, with Tencent, Alibaba Cloud and Baidu) bought in during July 2026 at about US$15 billion before the new money, roughly US$18 billion after it. Even a heavy discount to that private price is a large share of today's market value, and a Hong Kong listing reportedly targeted for early 2027 would put a public price on it. The core is slowing, not collapsing: core commercial revenue (advertising, e-commerce services and Kling) still grew 7.4% in Q2 2026, daily users held at 412.5 million, and the drop in total growth to 1.4% is concentrated in live streaming (-13.5%), a business the company has been deliberately cleaning up after regulatory pressure. Capex was front-loaded in the first half; management says Q2 free cash flow was positive and it aims to keep it positive in the second half, while 2026 cash returns (HK$2 billion of buybacks and HK$3 billion of dividends by mid-August) are set to exceed 2025. For the bull case to work: Q3 2026 results (2026-11-19) must show advertising still growing and adjusted profit stabilising near Q2's level; depreciation from the 2026 compute build must start to be absorbed by Kling and ad-tech revenue in 2027; and the China internet sector sell-off (Tencent about 39% below its 52-week high, Alibaba about 48%, Bilibili about 64%) must at least stop deepening.
picks.bear_thesis: This is a shrinking core financing an expensive AI bet, and the trend is still down. Revenue growth fell from +11.8% in Q4 2025 to +1.4% in Q2 2026; gross margin fell from about 55.7% to 47.9%; reported net profit fell 36% year on year to RMB 3.13 billion. Brokers have cut hard: CMB International (2026-08-20) cut its 2026-2028 net profit forecasts to RMB 8.9 / 11.5 / 13.9 billion from 16.9 / 20.0 / 23.3 billion, and Daiwa downgraded to hold with a 2026 revenue decline of 3.5% and live streaming down 16% (undated secondary report). Management's own March outlook for 2026 growth already looks too high, and on the Q2 2026 call it said second-half visibility 'remains limited' with a 'relatively high base'. Douyin (ByteDance's Chinese TikTok) is larger and is taking advertising share; Kuaishou's users are flat, live streaming keeps shrinking, and Tencent cut its stake from 15.68% to 9.37% on 2026-07-06. The RMB 26 billion 2026 capex plan was partly debt-funded (borrowings up about RMB 21 billion in Q1 2026), so the net cash pile is not idle surplus; depreciation (RMB 2.6 billion in Q2 2026 versus 1.7 billion a year earlier) will keep pressing margins into 2027. Kling's private price was set at about 35-40 times its annual revenue run rate, in a market that has since de-rated, and shareholders own only 68% of it; its losses already sit inside the group's falling profit. The bear case is confirmed if Q3 2026 shows advertising revenue shrinking year on year, adjusted net profit below RMB 3 billion, or a fresh step-up in capex guidance for 2027.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: the street has swung from extrapolating growth (Jefferies at HK$94 earlier in the cycle) to extrapolating decline (Daiwa cut to hold at HK$40; consensus targets cut about 29% to roughly HK$51; the lowest target about HK$27.6, near today's price). The current price assumes the operating business plus 68% of Kling is worth only about HK$60 billion, around 5 times CMB International's lowered 2026 profit, as if the 2026 trough were permanent. Our view is that the profit decline is front-loaded by capex and depreciation, and that Kling has a third-party price far above what the market credits. Where the street is right: the core growth outlook has already proved too optimistic once this year, and we do not have the data to say advertising has bottomed. That is exactly what Q3 2026 settles.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) starts in three days. Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-19 face a high base (Q3 2025 adjusted profit RMB 5.0 billion at a 14% margin) and management already warned of limited visibility. A weak print plus a 2027 capex plan above 2026's RMB 26 billion could push the stock toward the adverse case near HK$17-18. There is no debt wall that threatens solvency: cash and short-term investments of RMB 80.6 billion exceed total debt of RMB 39.0 billion. The risks are earnings and sentiment, not liquidation. Further Hong Kong and China internet de-rating is a sector-wide drag outside the company's control.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has largely played out through a strategic holder: Tencent sold about 273 million shares on 2026-07-06, cutting its stake from 15.68% to 9.37%; the remaining 9.37% is an overhang if Tencent keeps selling. The stock trades about 43% below its 200-day average and at its 52-week low, with volume elevated on the 2026-08-20 results reaction (about 249 million shares). Growth-fund holders have likely exited after the revenue collapse; value and buyback support are what remain. No index deletion or lock-up expiry is known.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the Q3 2026 results pass the test (adjusted net profit of RMB 3.8 billion or more with advertising revenue still growing), due 2026-11-19. The thesis is in doubt until that test. At HK$25.30, Kuaishou trades at about HK$108.8 billion of market value, with about HK$49 billion of net cash and a 68% stake in Kling AI that outside investors valued at about US$18 billion in July 2026. Our base-case fair value of HK$36 per share (seven times CMB International's lowered 2027 profit, a quarter of Kling's private price, and 80% of net cash) is about 42% above the price, comfortably clearing the 20% bar the current macro backdrop sets. The adverse case is about HK$17.6 and net cash alone is about HK$11.2 per share. The reason not to buy today, three days before the print, is that the earnings trend is still falling and management's own 2026 growth outlook already slipped once: revenue growth went from +11.8% to +1.4% in two quarters, reported profit fell 36%, and gross margin lost about 8 points to compute costs. If Q3 shows profit holding near Q2's RMB 3.9 billion adjusted, the discount looks like a fear-print on a cash-rich business and the case to buy becomes strong. If advertising turns negative or profit drops below RMB 3 billion, the thesis has broken and this is a value trap on a narrowing moat. Conviction is moderate (3 of 5); the value case on its own is also moderate because the moat is narrow and the core is losing ground to Douyin, which caps how much the low multiple can be trusted.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst, what forces the re-rating: (1) Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-19, the dated test of whether profit stabilises; (2) Q4 2026 results and the 2027 capex outlook around March 2027; (3) a reported Hong Kong listing application for Kling AI targeted for early 2027, which would put a public price on the stake; (4) continued buybacks against a market value that is less than half covered by net cash.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Kuaishou Technology (1024.HK) - deep dive on management and the setup

Prepared 2026-11-16, three days before the third-quarter 2026 results (board meeting 2026-11-19). All company figures are in Chinese yuan (RMB) unless marked; the share price is in Hong Kong dollars (HK$25.30 on the 2026-11-16 close, FMP live quote). Five earnings calls were available: 2025-05-27 (Q1 2025), 2025-08-21 (Q2 2025), 2025-11-19 (Q3 2025), 2026-03-25 (Q4 and full-year 2025) and 2026-08-19 (Q2 2026). There is no Q1 2026 call in the bundle.

**Bottom line:** the story has turned from "steady profit growth with an AI kicker" (all of 2025) to "spend heavily on AI while the core slows" (2026). The numbers confirm the turn: revenue growth fell from +11.8% in Q4 2025 to +1.4% in Q2 2026, gross margin fell from about 55.7% to 47.9%, and reported net profit fell 36% year on year in Q2 2026. Management's 2025 promises were kept; its 2026 promises have not yet been tested at the bottom line, and the Q2 2026 print came in below the growth it outlined in March. The business is still profitable, still holds a large net cash pile, and still returns cash, but the earnings base is shrinking, not growing.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **2025 (Q1 to Q3 calls): growth plus efficiency.** Each call led with record daily active users (DAUs, the number of people opening the app each day; around 408-412 million), double-digit revenue growth and a rising adjusted net margin (adjusted profit excludes share-based pay and some investment items). Q2 2025 adjusted profit was a "new high in quarterly profitability" at a 16% margin, and a special dividend was declared. Kling AI, the company's video-generation model, was framed as a bonus that would not dent profits: in Q2 2025 management said the profit drag from AI would "hover around 1% to 2%" and that the full-year adjusted net margin would be "stable".
- **Q4 2025 call (2026-03-25): the investment pivot.** The tone shifted to AI infrastructure. The chief financial officer guided 2026 capital spending (capex, money spent on servers and data centres) to "approximately RMB 26 billion, an increase of about RMB 11 billion" versus 2025, and secondary reports from the same day put the 2026 advertising growth outlook at mid-single digits. The stock fell as much as 14% that day.
- **Q2 2026 call (2026-08-19): defending the core.** The headline became "profitability remained stable" and "resilience" rather than growth. Total revenue grew 1.4% to RMB 35.5 billion; live-streaming revenue fell 13.5% to RMB 8.7 billion; online marketing (advertising) grew only 4.4% to RMB 20.6 billion. Kling, now partly sold to outside investors (a July 2026 round at roughly US$15 billion before the new money, leaving Kuaishou with about 68%), became the main growth story at "over RMB 850 million" of quarterly revenue, up over 200%.

Growth drivers quietly dropped: overseas profitability (celebrated in Q1 2025) and e-commerce gross merchandise value (GMV, the value of goods sold on the platform) leadership got far less airtime by 2026. Drivers introduced: comic-style short plays made with AI, AI-app advertisers, and selling Kling compute and models to outside companies.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 2025: AI drag only 1-2% of margin; full-year adjusted margin stable (Q2 2025 call) | Full-year 2025 adjusted net profit RMB 20.6 billion, +16.5%, margin 14.5%; reported net profit RMB 18.6 billion vs 15.3 billion in 2024 | Delivered |
| 2025: Kling revenue to double the US$60 million target (Q2-Q3 2025 calls) | Q4 2025 Kling revenue RMB 314 million; December 2025 monthly revenue above US$20 million | Delivered, beaten |
| 2026: positive group free cash flow despite RMB 26 billion capex (Q4 2025 call) | FMP cash-flow data show Q1 2026 operating cash flow RMB 3.1 billion against about RMB 12.1 billion of capex (deeply negative); management says Q2 2026 was positive and capex was front-loaded. Debt rose by about RMB 21 billion in Q1 2026 | Not yet proven; the full-year claim rests on the second half |
| "High-quality growth" (Q2 2026 call) | Revenue +1.4%, gross margin 47.9% vs about 55.7% a year earlier; reported net profit RMB 3.13 billion vs 4.92 billion (-36%) | Poorer than the language |
| "Profitability remained stable" (Q2 2026 call) | Adjusted net margin 11.0% vs about 16% in Q2 2025 | Not stable; down about 5 points |
| Shareholder returns to exceed 2025 (Q2 2026 call) | About HK$2 billion of buybacks plus HK$3 billion of dividends paid by mid-August 2026 | Consistent so far |
| Net cash is ample | Cash and short-term investments RMB 80.6 billion vs total debt RMB 39.0 billion at 2026-06-30 = net cash about RMB 41.6 billion, plus RMB 44.0 billion of long-term investments | True, though the gap is narrowing as debt funds capex |

The screener's return-on-equity reading of -29.3% and return-on-invested-capital of -7.7% are inconsistent with five straight profitable years on RMB 82 billion of equity (2025 net profit RMB 18.6 billion is about 23% of equity); they appear to be a data artefact and are not used here. The Altman-Z reading of -0.1 is likewise distorted by the large accumulated deficit from pre-2022 losses (retained earnings of about -RMB 218 billion), not by current solvency.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining.** 2025 calls were offensive: "new high in quarterly profitability" (Q2 2025), Kling "more than double the target" (Q3 2025), "confident that our full-year adjusted operating margin will continue to improve" (Q3 2025). The Q4 2025 call kept the confidence but swapped profit promises for investment language ("every investment today will efficiently translate into future profit drivers"). By Q2 2026 the language is defensive: "complex macroeconomic environment and industry competition", "visibility on the external environment remains limited", second-half growth facing "a relatively high base", and client budgets "may also be affected by industry competition dynamics". Guidance has become less specific on the core business, while Kling disclosure has become more specific.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

2025 guidance was met or beaten on every item we can check (Kling revenue, adjusted margin, capex range). 2026 is a different matter: management's March outlook, as reported by several outlets, implied mid-single-digit revenue growth; Q2 2026 delivered +1.4%, and Daiwa now forecasts a 3.5% revenue decline for 2026 (undated secondary report). CMB International cut its 2026-2028 net profit forecasts to RMB 8.9 / 11.5 / 13.9 billion from 16.9 / 20.0 / 23.3 billion on 2026-08-20. The screener records 3 beats in the last 7 quarters (43%). **Reliability: Medium** - honest about the investment cycle, but the core growth outlook has been too optimistic once already this year.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Capex and margins** came up on every call from Q2 2025 onward (Citic's Yuan Liao asked in Q2 2025, Q4 2025 and Q2 2026). The answers moved from "1-2% drag" to "RMB 26 billion" to "leasing compute through Kling" - the concern was right.
- **Advertising growth outlook for the second half** (Q2 2026): management did not give a number.
- **Live streaming** keeps shrinking; management attributes it to building a "healthy live streaming ecosystem" (restructuring top-earning streamers after regulatory clean-ups, and a regulatory penalty reported by Caixin on 2026-02-06 after the December 2025 livestream security breach). Analysts have not received a floor.
- **Competition with Douyin** (ByteDance's Chinese TikTok) is mentioned obliquely as "industry competition" and never quantified.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: revenue growth collapse from +11.8% (Q4 2025) to +1.4% (Q2 2026).
- Red: gross margin down about 8 points year on year in Q2 2026, driven by AI compute depreciation and Kling costs; depreciation rose from RMB 1.73 billion (Q2 2025) to RMB 2.61 billion (Q2 2026).
- Red: debt up about RMB 21 billion in Q1 2026 to fund capex while cash returns continue.
- Red: Tencent sold about 273 million shares on 2026-07-06, cutting its stake from 15.68% to 9.37% - a strategic holder stepping back.
- Green: Kling revenue above RMB 850 million in Q2 2026 (+200%), and an outside round in July 2026 with Tencent, Alibaba Cloud and Baidu participating, putting a third-party price on the asset.
- Green: core commercial revenue (advertising plus e-commerce and Kling) still grew 7.4% in Q2 2026; DAUs steady at 412.5 million.
- Green: cash returns on track to exceed 2025; net cash about RMB 41.6 billion.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The vocabulary shifted from "growth" to "resilience" and "prudent financial strategy" in one call.
- Kling is being financed outside the parent ("leasing" compute, outside equity), which suggests the parent wants to cap its own capex burden - helpful for cash, but it also means shareholders own 68% rather than 100% of the most valuable growth asset.
- A Kling Hong Kong listing is reported for early 2027; a listing would put a public price on the stake.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: PIVOTING** - from a profit-growth platform to an AI-investment story with a shrinking core. The single most important thing to weigh: the market price (about HK$108.8 billion of market value, of which about HK$49 billion is net cash) values the operating business plus the 68% Kling stake at roughly HK$60 billion, around 5 times CMB International's lowered 2026 profit forecast. That is cheap if the Q3 2026 results show the earnings decline levelling off; it is a value trap if advertising turns negative and the compute bill keeps growing.

**Moat:** network and scale - a creator-and-viewer community of about 410 million daily users that is hard to replicate, with a distinctive lower-tier-city audience. It is narrow rather than wide: Douyin has the larger audience and pricing power, user numbers are flat, live streaming is shrinking, and gross margin has fallen. The trend is eroding at the core, partly offset by the Kling asset. **Secular threat:** manageable - short video is not being displaced; the risk is share loss and a heavy compute bill, not structural extinction of the format. The cheapness is mostly a fear-print layered on a real slowdown: part mispricing, part genuinely lower earnings.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# China Unicom (Hong Kong) Ltd (0762.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-09. Price used: HK$5.51 (FMP live quote, Hong Kong listing, 2026-11-09). Reported figures are in renminbi (RMB); we convert at about HK$1.17 per RMB, the same rate this committee used last time.*

**Source note.** FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing (transcript-dates lookup returned nothing on 2026-11-09), and this run's shared web-search budget was used up before this name, so no new call commentary could be pulled. This dossier rests on (a) the screener's multi-year financials, (b) FMP's half-year statements, and (c) the dated company disclosures already verified by this committee's reviewer on 2026-11-03: the interim results of 2026-08-18 (HKEX announcement a260818a, carried by Cision/AAP and The Standard) and the nine-month unaudited key data of 2026-10-29 (The Standard). Nothing below quotes a call we did not read.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

From 2021 to 2024 the story was steady, policy-friendly compounding: revenue rose from RMB327.9bn to RMB389.6bn and net profit from RMB14.4bn to RMB20.6bn, with management leaning on "computing power" (cloud, data centres) to offset a mature mobile and broadband base. FY2025 was the first stall - revenue slipped 1.9% to RMB382.1bn and profit was flat at RMB20.3bn.

2026 broke the arc. China reclassified basic telecom services from the 6% to the 9% value-added tax (VAT) band from 1 January 2026, which comes straight out of reported revenue and margin. The 2026-08-18 interim showed attributable profit of RMB9.47bn, down 34.6%, and the board declared no interim dividend (prior year RMB0.2841 per share). Management said the full-year profit contraction was "expected to narrow significantly" as a staff-cost timing effect reversed. The 2026-10-29 nine-month data did not show that narrowing yet: profit RMB13.28bn, down 33.6%, implying a third quarter of roughly RMB3.8bn, down about 31%. The growth engine is still computing power (+12.2% in nine months, data centres +10.4%) while core service revenue edged down 0.28% to RMB260.89bn.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim (dated) | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Profit fall will "narrow significantly" in H2 (2026-08-18) | 9M profit -33.6% vs H1 -34.6% (2026-10-29); Q3 alone about -31% | Not yet delivered; the claim now rides entirely on Q4 |
| Computing power is the new growth leg | +12.2% in 9M 2026; data centres +10.4% | Matches, but it is too small to offset a shrinking core |
| Balance sheet is strong | Net cash RMB44.1bn on 2026-06-30 (cash RMB75.4bn vs debt RMB31.3bn incl. leases) | Matches - about RMB1.44 (HK$1.69) per share |
| Cash generation intact | Trailing free cash flow RMB25.0bn (to 2026-06-30); H1 operating cash flow a multi-year high | Matches - cash is far stronger than accounting profit |
| Shareholder returns a priority | Interim dividend cancelled 2026-08-18 | Diverges sharply - the single biggest credibility hit |

Two screener figures are unreliable and we set them aside: the 23.5% ROIC sits beside a 5.2% ROE and is almost certainly a data artefact, and the "TTM EPS 0.66" is still the FY2025 figure - on the 2026 run-rate (about RMB13.3-14bn of profit) earnings per share are nearer RMB0.44-0.46.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining. The 2024-25 language was offensive (computing-power investment, rising payouts). By August 2026 it had turned defensive: a tax explanation for the profit drop, a promise of narrowing, and a dividend withheld without a restoration timetable. We have no transcript to quote the tone directly; the actions speak for it.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-to-Low. The screener shows earnings beats in only 1 of the last 7 quarters (14%). The one explicit 2026 promise (a narrowing profit decline) has not shown up in the third quarter. Delivery on cash flow has been good; delivery on per-share profit and payout has not.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

What investors will push on (inferred from the disclosures, not from a call we read): (1) when and at what level the dividend returns; (2) whether the VAT hit can be priced through, given state-guided tariff discipline; (3) whether the staff-cost reversal is real or a re-labelled run-rate; (4) how much of the data-centre build-out is spending ahead of demand. No FMP analyst price-target coverage exists for this listing, and no dated consensus target could be fetched this run.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: interim dividend cancelled (2026-08-18) for a stock owned by income holders.
- Red: H2 narrowing promised but not visible in Q3 (2026-10-29).
- Red: core service revenue shrinking (-0.28% in 9M 2026) and gross margin contracting.
- Red: shares fell 12% on 2026-08-19 on about eleven times normal volume; price still about 18% below its 200-day average (HK$6.73).
- Green: net cash RMB44.1bn and free cash flow about RMB25bn a year - roughly 15% of the market value per year.
- Green: computing power and data centres growing double digits.
- Green: margins held through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 71.1% to 70.3% on the repo's resilience file), so the business is not an inflation victim; the 2026 hit is a tax change, not a cost spiral.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The shift from "dividend growth" to "no interim dividend" while the cash pile and cash flow both rose is the tell: cash is being retained for something - state-directed computing-power capex or the tax hit - rather than paid out. For a state-controlled operator, payout policy is set with the parent and the regulator, so a restoration is a policy decision, not an earnings outcome.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: deteriorating. The single most important thing to weigh: the cash is real, but owners do not control it - the dividend was withheld in a year when cash flow rose, so the net cash and free cash flow cannot be counted at full value until the payout returns.

Moat: regulatory licence plus scale (one of three national operators). It is narrow rather than wide - returns on equity are only about 5%, profit is down a third this year, and core service revenue is flat-to-down. The trend looks stable at the franchise level (the licence is not at risk) even as reported profit falls on tax. Secular threat: manageable - no structural force is dismantling telecom demand; the pressure is policy (tax, tariffs, directed capex). The cheapness is mostly a fear-print about payout and policy, not a shrinking-base value trap, but it is a low-return franchise whose value depends on what the state lets it distribute.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis:
The bullish case is that a Multiconsult share is now a cheap ticket into a larger Nordic engineering group that the market still prices like two sub-scale firms, and that the savings and a recovering Norwegian business can lift it toward its larger peers' valuations.

Start with what you own. Since the 7 September 2026 merger agreement, approved by both sets of shareholders on 19 October 2026, each Multiconsult share converts into 0.9725 Rejlers class B shares, giving Multiconsult owners about 54% of Multiconsult Rejlers, a group of roughly 8,000 engineers listed in Stockholm and Oslo. At today's Rejlers price of SEK 151.00 and 0.955 kroner to the krona, those terms are worth about NOK 140, and Multiconsult trades at NOK 139.20 - a small discount rather than the 8% premium it carried in September.

Second, the Multiconsult half of the group is recovering. Second-quarter 2026 earnings per share were NOK 3.23 against NOK 1.45 a year earlier on revenue up 5.4%; trailing twelve-month earnings per share are back to NOK 10.11 from the NOK 9.22 trough, and trailing free cash flow has doubled to NOK 363 million. The business needs little capital, so recovered profit turns into cash.

Third, the savings. The companies stated SEK 100-120 million of annual cost savings. Capitalised at the group's own multiple of about 8 times operating cash profit, the full amount is worth roughly SEK 800-950 million of enterprise value, about 10% of the combined equity.

Fourth, the re-rating. The combined group trades at roughly 8 times trailing operating cash profit (EV/EBITDA, enterprise value divided by earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) against Norconsult near 9 times and Sweco near 11 times on our September check. Scale, a dual listing and index eligibility are the usual routes for a merged group to close part of that gap. If the group earns SEK 1.4 billion of operating cash profit after savings and the market pays 9.5 times, a Multiconsult share is worth about NOK 199.

What must hold: Multiconsult's margin recovery survives the seasonally weak second half; consultant attrition does not eat the savings; Nordic infrastructure, grid and energy spending keeps demand for engineering hours rising.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bearish case is that the merger has turned a cheap, high-return Norwegian business into a fixed slice of a lower-return Swedish one, and that what is left is a modest discount with real execution risk.

First, the ratio. On our 22 September 2026 check Multiconsult earned about 23% on equity against Rejlers' 8%, converted far more of its operating cash into free cash (Rejlers' capital spending absorbed about 78% of its operating cash flow), yet Rejlers traded at a slightly higher multiple of operating cash profit (8.4 times against 7.9 times). Multiconsult owners hand over 46% of the combined group to the weaker partner and pay for the privilege.

Second, the share no longer has its own price. It is 0.9725 Rejlers class B shares converted at the krona rate, so it falls with Rejlers, with the Swedish krona against the Norwegian krone, and with the Nordic consulting sector. None of those is under Multiconsult's control, and there is no cash element, no collar and no floor in the terms.

Third, the recovery is one quarter deep. The first quarter of 2026 (earnings per share NOK 3.99) was below the first quarter of 2025 (NOK 4.86); only the second quarter carried the half-year improvement. The company has beaten consensus in none of the last seven quarters, and reported operating margin of about 6% is well short of the 10% target.

Fourth, people businesses lose value in mergers. Savings in consultancy come from overlapping overhead and offices, and the engineers who walk take clients with them. If only SEK 45 million of net savings survive, the 2026 second half gives back the margin gain, and the sector multiple settles near 7 times, a Multiconsult share is worth about NOK 124.

Fifth, AI-assisted design tools can compress billable hours per project over the next decade, a material if not fatal pressure on an hourly-billing model. And the balance sheet carries NOK 1.41 billion of net debt including leases (about NOK 1.04 billion excluding them), so there is no cash cushion.
picks.consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market is now small. In September the market was paying 8% more for a Multiconsult share than the deal terms delivered; that disagreement has closed, and the share trades about 1% below terms. The remaining question is whether the combined group is worth more than the roughly 8 times operating cash profit the market pays for it. We think modestly yes - about NOK 152 per Multiconsult share - because the risk-adjusted savings and Multiconsult's second-half recovery are not in the trailing base. We do not think the market is pricing terminal decline into a company with recovering earnings power; it is pricing an ordinary, slightly cheap Nordic consultancy with merger execution risk, which is roughly right. The deep-value label in our screen came from 2025 trough figures and is stale.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead) holds no liquidity crisis - leverage is about 1.5 to 2 times operating cash profit and inside the company's own target - but four things can push the price lower before the value case pays. First, the third-quarter 2026 report on 3 November and the fourth quarter fall in the seasonally weaker half; the 2025 third quarter earned only NOK 1.41 per share, and a repeat would show the recovery is one quarter deep. Second, the share now moves with Rejlers and the Swedish krona: a weak Rejlers report or a krona drop against the krone moves Multiconsult mechanically. Third, integration: management attention, consultant departures and one-off costs (about SEK 150 million in our estimate) land before savings do. Fourth, a Nordic consulting de-rating; the stock touched NOK 127.80 within the last year, so our NOK 126 level is reachable on a sector move alone.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure is limited but has one plausible source. The register is mainly Norwegian long-only institutions, domestic retail and the employee-linked Stiftelsen Multiconsult, a committed owner. At completion, Oslo-only mandates and Norwegian small-cap funds will hold a Swedish-domiciled company; the planned Oslo listing softens this, but index reweighting and mandate drift can produce selling that has nothing to do with value. A sector-wide de-rating of Nordic engineering consultancies is the more likely route to our level. Trading is thin (about 22,500 shares on 2 November 2026 against 27.6 million outstanding), so modest selling moves the price.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near NOK 126, which a sector-wide sell-off of Nordic engineering consultancies could deliver.

The thesis holds. Multiconsult is a capital-light Norwegian engineering consultancy whose demand never left during the 2025 profit collapse and whose earnings are recovering: second-quarter 2026 earnings per share of NOK 3.23 against NOK 1.45, trailing free cash flow doubled to NOK 363 million. But a Multiconsult share is no longer priced on its own. Since shareholders approved the merger with Rejlers on 19 October 2026, each share is a claim on 0.9725 Rejlers class B shares, worth about NOK 140 today, and Multiconsult trades at NOK 139.20.

Our fair value is about NOK 152: the deal terms at today's prices, plus a risk-adjusted share of the stated savings, plus Multiconsult's recovery not yet in the trailing figures. That is about 9% above the price - a real but thin discount, short of the 20% we require before buying in the current reflationary backdrop. At NOK 126 the discount clears that bar; the level sits just above our adverse case of NOK 124 and just below the 52-week low of NOK 127.80, so it needs a sector or currency move rather than bad company news. The favourable case of NOK 199 requires the combined group to be re-rated toward its best-rated Nordic peers after completion.

Conviction stays at 3, unchanged from our last look: a good, recovering business inside a merger that pays the weaker partner too much, at a price that is fair rather than cheap. The 8% premium to the deal terms that stopped us in September is gone; what is missing now is the margin of safety. The third-quarter 2026 report due 3 November is the next check, and it was not available to us here.
picks.forcing_function: The shareholder vote, the nearest forcing event, has happened (19 October 2026). What remains: the third-quarter 2026 report on 3 November 2026, which tests whether the margin recovery held; completion of the merger, subject to closing conditions we could not date; and the first combined-group reports, where delivered savings and a combined set of financial targets give the market a reason to re-rate the group toward Norconsult and Sweco. None of these is a hard-dated payout; the re-rating is a judgement the market has to make after completion.

# Multiconsult ASA (MULTI.OL) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-03. Prices in Norwegian kroner (NOK), Oslo listing.

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript was bundled and none was retrievable this run (the paid FMP feed carries no transcript for this listing, and the web-search budget was exhausted). This review therefore rests on the hard numbers: FMP quarterly income statements through the second quarter of 2026, the screener's multi-year trajectory, Multiconsult's own investor-relations announcement list (read 2026-11-03) and Rejlers' investor page (read 2026-11-03). No management quote below is invented; where we describe management's position, we describe it from what they announced and what they did, not from words we have not seen. The third-quarter 2026 report is scheduled for release on 3 November 2026 at 08:30 CET (announced 27 October 2026); its figures were not available to us and are not used.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story changed category this autumn. Through mid-2026 Multiconsult was a stand-alone recovery story: a 118-year-old Norwegian engineering, design and architecture consultancy whose revenue kept growing (NOK 4.28 billion in 2021 to NOK 6.63 billion in 2025) while profit collapsed in 2025 (earnings per share down 39% to NOK 9.22) and then began to recover in 2026.

On 7 September 2026 the company announced a merger of equals with Rejlers AB, a Swedish engineering consultancy. Each Multiconsult share converts into 0.9725 Rejlers class B shares; Multiconsult holders end up with about 54% of a combined group to be called Multiconsult Rejlers, with roughly 8,000 staff and listings in both Stockholm and Oslo. Since then the narrative has been entirely about execution of the deal: an extraordinary general meeting (a shareholder meeting called outside the annual cycle) on 19 October 2026, at which both companies' owners approved the merger (Rejlers described "broad support" the same day); a chief financial officer for the combined group appointed on 8 October; and a proposed combined board on 12 October. Completion remains subject to "the other closing conditions", which the published pages do not date.

What this means for an investor: a Multiconsult share is now mostly a claim on a fixed number of Rejlers shares. The stand-alone recovery still matters, but only through its 54% share of the combined group.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim / narrative | What the numbers say | Read |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 is a recovery year | Second-quarter 2026 earnings per share NOK 3.23 vs NOK 1.45 a year earlier; first half NOK 7.22 vs NOK 6.31. Trailing twelve-month (TTM) earnings per share NOK 10.11 vs the NOK 9.22 full-year 2025 trough. | Corroborated, but the first quarter of 2026 (NOK 3.99) was below the first quarter of 2025 (NOK 4.86); the recovery is one strong quarter deep. |
| Demand held through the downturn | Revenue grew every year 2021-2025 (+10.8% three-year compound rate); 2025 +4.3%; second-quarter 2026 revenue NOK 1.75 billion, up 5.4%. | Corroborated. The 2025 problem was profitability, not demand. |
| Profit turns into cash | TTM free cash flow NOK 363 million vs NOK 173 million in full-year 2025; capital spending is light. | Corroborated on a TTM basis; 2025 free cash flow had fallen about 70%, so the cash conversion is recovering, not proven through a cycle. |
| Financial target of a 10% profitability margin | Second-quarter 2026 operating profit margin about 6.0% (NOK 106 million on NOK 1.75 billion); EBITDA (operating profit before depreciation and amortisation) margin about 9.8%. | The target is not being met on reported operating profit. |
| Leverage within the 1.0-2.0x target | Net debt NOK 1.41 billion including NOK 366 million of capitalised leases (about NOK 1.04 billion excluding leases) against TTM EBITDA of roughly NOK 690 million. | About 1.5x excluding leases, about 2.0x including them - within target, not net cash. |

Forensic caution: the reported cost-of-revenue line flips classification between quarters in the FMP data (gross profit of NOK 1,416 million in the second quarter of 2025 versus NOK 265 million in the second quarter of 2026 on similar revenue). Any valuation on enterprise value to gross profit (our methodology tag) would be anchored on noise, so we value on operating cash profit and earnings instead. The 85% "gross margin" in the screen is an artefact of this presentation, not a moat signal.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Without a transcript we cannot quote tone. What management did is itself informative: after a year of margin pressure it chose to merge with a peer of similar size and lower returns rather than run the recovery alone. Read plainly, that is a shift from an organic-recovery posture to a scale-and-synergy posture. The stated savings of SEK 100-120 million (as recorded in our prior review of the merger documents) are a cost-efficiency argument, not a growth argument. Trajectory of confidence: stable to defensive.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The screen records zero beats in the last seven quarters against consensus, and the 2025 earnings collapse was not flagged far ahead. The 2026 half-year delivered a genuine improvement. Reliability: Medium-Low. Multiconsult does not give numeric quarterly guidance, so the beat record is the best available measure, and it is poor.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

From the record, not a transcript: (a) why merge at a ratio that hands 46% of the combined group to a partner with lower returns on equity (Rejlers roughly 8% against Multiconsult roughly 23%, per our 22 September 2026 check) and much weaker free-cash conversion; (b) how much of the stated savings survive consultant attrition, the main risk in any people business; (c) whether the 2026 margin recovery holds in the seasonally weak second half. We could not verify how management answered these.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: the exchange ratio values Rejlers at a richer multiple than Multiconsult, so Multiconsult owners are paying, not receiving, a premium for the 46% (September 2026 terms).
- Red: zero of the last seven quarters beat consensus; first quarter 2026 was down year on year.
- Red: unstable cost-of-revenue classification in the reported data.
- Green: second quarter 2026 earnings per share more than doubled; TTM free cash flow doubled.
- Green: shareholders of both companies approved the merger on 19 October 2026, removing the vote risk.
- Green: the share's 8% premium to the deal terms (22 September 2026) has disappeared; it now trades about 1% below them.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The new chief financial officer (Hans-Jorgen Wibstad, effective 1 November 2026) is appointed to Multiconsult first and earmarked for the combined group, a sign the Norwegian side keeps financial control. The chief executive will be Rejlers' Viktor Svensson with Multiconsult's Kristin O. Augestad as deputy, so operating leadership tilts Swedish. Multiconsult's own financial targets (10% margin, more than 50% payout, 8-10% growth including acquisitions) predate the merger and will be replaced by combined-group targets; until then they are not a promise anyone is held to.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: turning. The company has moved from a stand-alone recovery to a merger that, once completed, converts every Multiconsult share into 0.9725 Rejlers class B shares. The single most important thing to weigh: the price of a Multiconsult share is now set by the price of Rejlers class B times the ratio times the krona exchange rate (today about NOK 140), so any edge must come from the combined group being worth more than the market currently pays for it - that is, from savings delivered and a re-rating toward Nordic peers - not from Multiconsult's own discount, which the ratio has absorbed.

Moat: a narrow but real moat built on reputation, framework contracts and long client relationships with Norwegian public and energy clients (an intangible and switching-cost moat). Returns are respectable (return on equity about 29% on the screen's latest-year basis, return on invested capital about 14%) but not rising steadily; margins fell sharply in 2025 and partly recovered in 2026, so the moat is stable rather than widening. Secular threat: material, not terminal. Engineering design is sold by the hour, and AI-assisted design tools can compress billable hours per project; that would pressure revenue per engineer, though demand for infrastructure, energy and grid work is structurally rising. The cheapness is therefore not a value trap, but neither is it a deep discount.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

# Universal Health Services (UHS) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Coverage window: five earnings calls, 2025-10-28 (Q3 2025) through 2026-10-28 (Q3 2026). Live price used: $180.65 (NYSE, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

Takeaway first: UHS is a well-financed, buyback-heavy hospital operator whose reported growth over the last two years leaned heavily on state Medicaid supplemental payments (extra funding states route to hospitals), and whose underlying operating results have now fallen short of management's own internal expectations for three quarters running. The business is not breaking, but the earnings base for 2027 is flat-to-down, and the 2028+ Medicaid cuts are a known, quantified-in-part headwind.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-28)** - offense. Adjusted EPS of $5.69 up 53% year on year; 2025 EPS guidance midpoint raised 6% to $21.80, helped by $90M from the newly approved Washington, D.C. supplemental Medicaid program. The story: acute-care demand strong, new hospitals (Cedar Hill in D.C., West Henderson in Nevada) ramping, Palm Beach Gardens opening spring 2026, outpatient build-out in both segments.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-02-26)** - adjusted EPS $5.88; acute same-facility adjusted admissions flat in the quarter. 2026 guidance issued.
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-28)** - steady: behavioral wage inflation moderating from ~8% (2025) to 6-7%; turnover "improving meaningfully".
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-28)** - the turn to defense. Adjusted EPS $5.98 (+12%), but only because of a $100M out-of-period Florida payment not in guidance; ex that, EBITDA "fell short of our internal expectations" by ~$63M (liability reserves $28M, the San Antonio behavioral facility $20M, Cedar Hill ramp $15M). Volume guidance trimmed 50bp; 2026 adjusted EBITDA net of minority interests guided to $2.61-2.72B.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-28)** - adjusted EPS $5.22, down 8%. Underlying EBITDA again "below our internal expectations despite modest sequential improvement". Full-year guidance reiterated but now "towards the lower end". Talkspace (acquired 2026-08-17) becomes a featured growth pillar. | Cash generation | Q3 operating cash flow $637M vs $381M; FY2025 FCF -24% on heavy capex; TTM FCF $1.12B | Improving as capex steps down from ~$1B toward ~$800M. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Rating: **Declining, then stabilizing.** Q3 2025 was confident ("increasing the midpoint of our 2025 adjusted EPS guidance by 6%"). By Q2 2026 the prepared remarks itemized shortfalls; by Q3 2026 management structured its remarks around "reported results and unusual items" and pre-announced 2027 headwinds: $175-200M of non-repeating Medicaid supplemental money, at least $15M from health-insurance exchange losses, and unquantifiable Medicaid work-requirement effects. The language is now explicitly defensive ("offset opportunities", "challenges that will come, especially from OB-3"), but specific and candid rather than evasive.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- 2025: raised and delivered (EPS $23.10 vs the raised $21.80 midpoint) - but the beat came from supplemental programs, not operations.
- 2026: EBITDA guidance cut in July to $2.61-2.72B; volume guidance trimmed; now pointed to the low end. Each of Q2 and Q3 underlying results missed internal plans; out-of-period Medicaid payments masked the misses in reported numbers.
- The screener shows 6 of 7 quarterly beats (86%), which flatters the record: several beats were supplemental-payment windfalls not in guidance.
- De novo timelines: missed twice (Cedar Hill).
- No sign of sandbagging; if anything, operating plans have been a touch optimistic.
**Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- 2027 supplemental-payment cliff (AJ Rice, UBS, Q3 2026) - now answered with a number, $175-200M, which is roughly 7% of 2026 EBITDA.
- Slow de novo ramps (Ann Hynes, Mizuho, Q3 2026: "I do not remember a time where the acute care hospitals are ramping below expectations").
- Medicaid work requirements: management declines to estimate; gives exposure instead (expansion-state Medicaid ~15% of acute adjusted admissions, ~30% of behavioral patient days) and leans on medical-frailty exemptions.
- Surgical softness: attributed to procedures leaving the hospital - an honest answer that concedes a structural drift.
- Professional and general liability reserves: recurring additions every quarter ($28M Q2, $26M Q3 for the Cumberland, Virginia settlement) - analysts have stopped treating these as one-offs.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: underlying EBITDA below internal plan in Q2 and Q3 2026.
- Red: 2027 faces a known $175-200M Medicaid supplemental headwind before the larger 2028+ provider-tax cuts under the 2025 budget law (OB-3).
- Red: recurring liability reserve top-ups and behavioral-health litigation; the San Antonio (Laurel Ridge) facility lost Medicare certification and recertification is only "expected during 2027".
- Red: open-market insider activity is all selling (0 buys, 5 sells, 5,456 shares) - small, but no insider is buying at these prices.
- Red: Talkspace bought at roughly 74 times its FY2025 EBITDA (prior check, 2026 filings) - a richly priced bet with benefits "over the next 12-24 months".
- Green: acute volumes accelerating (+2.9% Q2 to +4.9% Q3 2026); capacity additions working.
- Green: acute labor and supply costs under control; contract labor falling.
- Green: aggressive, well-funded buybacks with leverage still at 2.17x, inside the 2-3x target.
- Green: capex falling toward ~$800M frees roughly $150-200M a year of extra free cash flow.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The reporting vocabulary changed from "same-facility EBITDA growth" to "excluding out-of-period benefit from both periods" - management itself now separates windfall from run-rate, which is honest and tells you the run-rate is the softer number.
- Payer-mix strategy has become a Medicaid-avoidance strategy: outpatient behavioral (Talkspace, Thousand Branches) is framed as shifting volume to commercial and Medicare.
- "AI" appears for the first time as a cost lever (length-of-stay control, revenue cycle) - defensive use, not growth.
- Capex framing ("not having any of these big de novo projects in the pipeline") signals a shift from building to harvesting - supportive of buybacks.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: **STABLE** - the operating base is flat, not shrinking; volumes are improving while price and mix soften and government funding steps down. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly (buybacks near $180, falling capex) with one questionable outlier (Talkspace).

The single most important thing to weigh: the 2027 earnings base. With 2026 adjusted EBITDA near $2.61B, a $175-200M supplemental headwind, ~$15M of exchange losses and only a partial recovery of $80-100M de novo/San Antonio losses, 2027 EBITDA is roughly flat to slightly down - so per-share growth will come almost entirely from buybacks. The stock at ~$181 already prices that.

Moat: regulatory-license plus local scale (certificate-of-need licensing in several states, dense local networks in Las Vegas, D.C. and elsewhere, and the largest US behavioral-health footprint). Returns are modest (ROIC 9%, ROE 15.4%) and stable rather than falling - a **narrow** moat with a **stable** trend. Secular threat: reimbursement compression (Medicaid supplemental and provider-tax cuts from 2028, exchange disenrollment, work requirements) plus the steady migration of procedures out of hospitals. That is **material** but not terminal: hospitals remain essential, and roughly 85% of acute admissions and 70% of behavioral days sit outside expansion-state Medicaid. The cheapness is mostly a fair price for a flat-earnings, policy-exposed business plus a buyback, not a deep mispricing.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# CECV.DE - Ceconomy AG, tendered-shares line (deep dive on management and the setup)

**Read this first.** CECV.DE is not a normal Ceconomy share. It is the separate trading line (ISIN DE000A40ZVV0) for Ceconomy ordinary shares that holders already tendered (offered for sale) into JD.com's EUR 4.60-per-share cash takeover. Eurex moved its Ceconomy derivatives onto this tendered line on 17 November 2025 and used EUR 4.60 as the final settlement reference. The takeover closed on 12 November 2026, after the European Commission gave the last approval on 3 November 2026. A tendered share is now simply a claim on EUR 4.60 in cash. The last FMP quote for this line is EUR 4.60, dated 9 November 2026, with no newer prints. That fits a line that stops trading just before the cash is paid out. The peer-group file calls this a "preference share", but that is wrong: Ceconomy turned its preference shares into ordinary shares in May 2022, and the old preference line (CEC1) stopped trading on 1 June 2022.

No earnings-call transcript was bundled, and FMP has no Ceconomy transcripts or news. So this deep dive rests on the screener financials and dated public takeover documents. No management quotes are given, because none were sourced.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **2021-2023:** Ceconomy, the owner of MediaMarkt and Saturn, restructured. It bought out the Kellerhals family's minority stake in Media-Saturn through the Convergenta deal, turned its preference shares into ordinary shares in 2022, and lived through a profit collapse. Net income fell from EUR 269M in fiscal 2021 to a loss of EUR 41M in fiscal 2023.
- **2024-2025:** The story moved to services, retail media and marketplace "flywheel" revenue on top of a thin-margin electronics box-moving business. Revenue reached about EUR 27.0B in the latest fiscal year (screener figure), up about 9.8%, while net margin stayed close to zero (-0.2%).
- **July 2025 onward:** The story stopped being an operating one. JD.com announced a voluntary public takeover offer at EUR 4.60 cash per share, plus a strategic partnership with Convergenta. The acceptance period started in September 2025. The first result on 14 November 2025 put about 70.9% of shares and votes with the bidder side. The final result after the additional acceptance period gave JD.com 59.8% directly, and Convergenta's 25.3% brought the combined holding to 85.2%. Regulatory reviews, ending with the EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation review, pushed closing from the planned first half of 2026 to 12 November 2026.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / setup | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| The business is turning around | Revenue CAGR +8.3% over 3 years; TTM free cash flow (FCF, cash left after capital spending) EUR 837M at 2026-06-30, up ~48% YoY; Piotroski 8/9 | Cash generation improved for real |
| Earnings are inflecting | TTM diluted EPS -0.03; fiscal-2025 EPS -0.084; return on invested capital -0.9% | Reported profit is still around zero, so the turnaround has not reached the bottom line |
| Balance sheet is fine | Net debt EUR 1.72B at 2026-06-30 (borrowings 2.97B minus cash 1.25B, leases excluded); Altman-Z 2.4 (grey zone) | Adequate, not strong; FCF is seasonal and working-capital driven |
| "Deep value" at 3x FCF | P/FCF 3.0x and DCF margin of safety +73% from the screener | Not relevant to THIS line: a tendered share is worth the EUR 4.60 cash, not the business's intrinsic value |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable, but it no longer matters. With no transcripts, we cannot rate management tone quarter by quarter. Since July 2025 the dated communications have been takeover-procedural: the offer, the acceptance results and the closing conditions.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Medium. The screener records 1 of 1 tracked quarters beating. On the deal itself, the original "first half of 2026" closing target slipped about five months because the EU foreign-subsidies review ran long. The deal still closed on unchanged terms of EUR 4.60.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Whether JD.com will delist the remaining public float. Earlier reporting mentioned a delisting intention, and the offer terms ruled out a domination or profit-transfer agreement (contracts that let a parent control and take a subsidiary's profits) for three years. The closing release of 12 November 2026 says nothing on delisting.
- How the EU's ten-year conditions, which require JD to open its warehousing and logistics to rivals on equal terms, affect the synergy case.
- These questions concern the remaining ordinary shares (CEC.DE), not the tendered line.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- 🟢 The deal closed on 12 November 2026 at the full offer price, with all conditions met (EU clearance on 3 November 2026).
- 🟢 FCF improved: TTM EUR 837M at June 2026.
- 🔴 Bottom-line profit is still about zero, and return on invested capital is negative.
- 🔴 The data mislabels this line as a preference share and shows its price as a "52-week high". Both are artifacts of a tendered-shares line pinned to the offer price.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The tendered line's year range (EUR 3.86 to 4.60) compressed toward the offer as closing risk faded. The gap shut fully once the EU cleared the deal on 3 November 2026. The fact that the same price shows on both the tendered line (EUR 4.60) and the ordinary line (CEC.DE, EUR 4.595 on 16 November 2026) means the market now prices the remaining float at about the offer value as well.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: STABLE for the business. For this instrument, the story is over. The single most important point is that CECV.DE is a claim on EUR 4.60 of cash being paid now. It cannot gain anything, and the line is being retired. Any interest in Ceconomy's operating value belongs to the ordinary line (CEC.DE), where the open questions are a possible delisting and holding a minority stake under an 85%-controlling holder.

**Moat.** The moat comes from scale in buying, store density and service attach. It is narrow: gross margin is about 15% and stable, but return on invested capital is negative, so the scale advantage does not earn its cost of capital. **Secular threat.** The shift of electronics sales online and to marketplaces such as Amazon is material, not terminal. MediaMarkt is itself an omnichannel player, and JD's ownership is a response to that shift. Ceconomy's cheapness on FCF reflects thin, volatile margins more than a melting base. For the tendered line, none of this changes the EUR 4.60 payout.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.
