picks.thesis_evidence: The thesis holds. The load-bearing claims are a near-fully-used fleet, expanding margins and returns, domestic demand set by state policy rather than the oil price, and a falling interest bill - and all four are corroborated by the latest dated numbers. Third quarter 2026 (reported 2026-10-26): revenue RMB 11.94B, up 3.5% from RMB 11.53B a year earlier; operating profit RMB 1.53B. Nine months to 2026-09-30: revenue RMB 35.35B and net income RMB 3.21B, level with RMB 3.21B a year earlier only because of a non-operating RMB 720M exchange loss on intercompany balances, which the chief financial officer volunteered against his own interest on that call after an analyst offered him the softer reading. Gross margin for the nine months was 20.5%, up from 17.4% for the 2025 full year and 12.3% in 2022. Net debt fell from RMB 9.71B at 2026-06-30 to RMB 7.58B at 2026-09-30, and interest expense is down from RMB 969M (2023) to RMB 636M (2025) after the USD 1B repayment in June-July 2025. Management said on 2026-10-26 that the 2026 workload was 'better than the expectation we set at the beginning of the year'. Since that date the only new dated facts are market facts, and they are a sector-wide sell-off rather than company news: Brent peaked at $116.72 on 2026-10-23, held above $110 for seven straight sessions to 2026-10-30, gave back about $9 on 2026-11-02 on the Iran-Qatar Hormuz reopening plan and sits at $92.41 on 2026-11-10, with every peer in the group below its fifty-day and two-hundred-day averages; the Hong Kong line fell 10.2% from its HK$7.98 close on 2026-10-26. Brent at $92.41 is below its $96.35 two-hundred-day average but far above the $58.72 52-week low and far above offshore breakeven, so nothing in the domestic workload case is disproven. The risk we are watching, rather than a break, is capital allocation: management said on 2026-10-26 that 2026-2030 investment intensity 'will be even more than during the 14th 5-Year Plan period', which would compress the free cash flow our valuation leans on.
picks.macro_fit_note: The backdrop is a reflation quadrant - growth accelerating (real gross domestic product about +3.4% annualised to July 2026) against hot and sticky inflation (consumer prices running about 3.7% annualised over six months) - and the debt cycle is in a discipline phase, 17 weeks in, where positive real long rates (about 3.05% on the thirty-year, and rising) punish long-dated stories and reward cash now, over an expected 18-month horizon. The payback profile here is firmly in the rewarded camp: 5.3 times price to free cash flow, a 10.7% free-cash-flow margin and roughly a 19% free-cash-flow yield at today's price are cash-now characteristics, not a story, and reflation supports real-economy energy demand. Pulling the other way, this business is inflation-exposed on the record: gross margin fell from 18.8% in the year to December 2019 to 12.3% in the worst inflation year (2022), a 6.5-point fall, with operating margin down 2.7 points. On pass-through the transcript evidence is explicitly negative - asked on 2026-03-24 whether there is 'any mechanism for the passing on of the oil price increase' under the North Sea long-term agreements, management answered 'if such mechanism can be put in place, it is good. But then right now, we believe that our customers also encounter much difficulty', and on 2025-10-30 said state wage rules mean salaries 'would take up a rather big portion of our overall cost'; day rates with the parent are 'overall maintained steady' (2026-10-26). The margin recovery to 20.5% has come from cost work and mix, not price. Netting a rewarded cash profile against no contractual inflation protection, we read this as neutral. This is context only - it does not move the thesis, the entry, the verdict or the conviction.

picks.bull_thesis: Lagardere owns two genuinely good businesses that the market values as one mediocre one. Hachette Livre is the world's third-largest book publisher and number three in the United States; it earned roughly a 10% operating margin in 2025 and gained share while its French, US and UK book markets shrank (February 2026 call). Lagardere Travel Retail, the world's number-two airport and station retailer, had its best year on record in 2025: divisional operating profit up 17% and the margin up from 4.6% to 5.1%, with the Schiphol Amsterdam concession taken over on time in May 2025 and 2026 its first full year. The momentum has held into the autumn. Third-quarter 2026 revenue, published 15 October 2026, was 2,633 million euros, up 2.4% like-for-like (on a comparable scope and currency basis) and accelerating from 1.8% in the second quarter; travel retail grew 3.3% like-for-like and 4.6% excluding North Asia, after a record summer, and publishing grew 4% in the UK and US. The loss-making North Asia stores are due to be closed by the end of 2026, which removes a drag rather than adding one. On 9 September 2026 the group placed a 500 million euro six-year bond maturing in 2032, pushing out the 2027 maturity wall. At 18.34 euros the whole company, debt and leases included, is valued at about 5.0 times trailing cash profit (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation), below Avolta at about 6.2 times and Bloomsbury at about 9.5 times. Because 4.58 billion euros of net debt sits between the enterprise and the shareholder, each extra turn of multiple is worth roughly 10 euros a share. Value the divisions at peer-level multiples and the parts reach the low-thirties to mid-forties before any discount for the ownership structure, while a 0.67 euro dividend (about 3.7%) pays you to wait. Conditions: travel-retail margins keep inching up, publishing holds a 10% margin, and the discount for the controlled structure narrows.
picks.bear_thesis: You would not be buying two good businesses; you would be buying a 25%-float minority slice of a leveraged holding structure, and the leverage is the story. Net debt including capitalised airport-concession leases is 4.58 billion euros (30 June 2026) against a stock-market value of about 2.6 billion euros. Two years of management calling deleveraging its key priority moved that figure from 4,503 million euros (December 2024) to 4,494 million (December 2025) to 4,581 million (June 2026). The celebrated drop from 3.0 times to under 2 times leverage is measured on borrowings only, a definition never stated on any call, while the lease book grew. Interest of about 265 million euros a year takes roughly 42% of operating profit, and the February 2025 promise to cut it through refinancing has not been kept: the 9 September 2026 refinancing priced at a 5.25% coupon, which locks in a high cost for six years rather than lowering it. The owner's scoreboard is poor: revenue up about 80% from 2021 to 2025, but earnings per share only from 1.14 euros (2022) to 1.43 euros, book value per share compounding at 0.9% a year over five years, and return on invested capital at 5.8%, below any sensible cost of capital. Growth was bought with leased floor space whose rent and interest absorbed most of it. The screener's apparent bargain is a measurement error: its 2.6 times price-to-free-cash-flow ignores the debt and roughly 700 million euros a year of lease and interest payments, and its trailing earnings of 2.97 euros a share are two half-years mistaken for quarters - the true trailing figure is about 1.48 euros, about 12.3 times earnings. Finally, the controller: Louis Hachette Group holds 66.53%, and chairman Arnaud Lagardere told the February 2025 call he had cut his own stake here from about 5.11% to 0.4% and bought the parent instead. Growth is also slowing to low single digits, the third-quarter release calls the backdrop difficult, and about 40% of profit is earned in dollars. What would confirm the bear case: lease-inclusive net debt still above 4.5 billion euros at the full-year results on 25 February 2027.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is not pricing terminal decline into this company, and that is the crux. The deep-value question - is the street mistaking a steady business for a dying one? - gets a no. Both divisions are demonstrably fine, and third-quarter 2026 revenue (+2.4% like-for-like) confirms it. What the market prices, correctly, is the structure: a 25%-float minority in a company 66.53%-controlled by Louis Hachette Group, trading about 436,000 euros a day, whose chairman moved his own capital to the parent. Where this committee disagrees with the screening consensus is in the opposite direction: the apparent 50%-to-70%-plus margin of safety rests on an equity cash-flow multiple that ignores 4.58 billion euros of net debt and on trailing earnings that double-count half-years. Corrected, the discount is about 10% to 20% at the enterprise level. The one genuine disagreement with management's framing is that leverage has fallen only on a borrowings-only definition; on the lease-inclusive measure, nothing has been deleveraged in two years.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation risk, but three hazards over the next three to nine months. First, the interest bill: about 265 million euros a year, roughly 42% of operating profit, and the September 2026 refinancing priced at 5.25% fixes a high cost into 2032 while long rates sit near cycle highs. Second, cash: management said on 2026-02-19 that 2025's cash flow included about 80 million euros of one-offs that will not repeat, and borrowings rose into June 2026 on the usual first-half working-capital and dividend outflow; the full-year results on 25 February 2027 will show whether the second half reversed it. Third, currency and traffic: about 40% of profit is in dollars (a 90 million euro currency drag on nine-month 2026 revenue), North American air traffic is slowing per the 15 October 2026 release, and the Middle East business fell 15% in the quarter. Behind all three sits the unsized French logistics and IT modernisation.
picks.positioning_washout: No forced-selling event exists to wait for. The register is 66.53% Louis Hachette Group with a roughly 25% free float; there is no meaningful index or yield-focused base to be flushed, and the 0.67 euro dividend is well covered, so a cut is not a trigger. The informed flow runs the other way: the chairman's disclosed move from about 5.11% of Lagardere to 0.4%, and into the parent (February 2025), and an insider-buying ratio of zero. With about 436,000 euros of daily turnover, any position meaningful to a book would take weeks to build or exit. Illiquidity is the reason the discount exists, not a source of edge.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Pass for now.

The businesses deserve better than this write-up sounds; the security does not. Hachette Livre is a genuine franchise built on a backlist that keeps paying, travel retail had a record 2025 and a record summer in 2026, and third-quarter 2026 revenue rose 2.4% like-for-like, accelerating from the second quarter. Nothing is melting, and the thesis holds as a steady-operations story.

Three things keep it from being an investment at 18.34 euros. First, most of the cheapness is a measurement error: the screener's 2.6 times price-to-free-cash-flow ignores 4.58 billion euros of net debt including airport leases, and its trailing earnings double-count half-years. Corrected, the shares trade at about 12.3 times earnings and about 5.0 times enterprise value to cash profit, only modestly below live travel-retail peers. Second, the deleveraging that is supposed to unlock the equity has not happened on the measure that matters - lease-inclusive net debt is where it was in December 2024 - and the September 2026 bond refinanced at 5.25% rather than paying anything down. Third, and decisive, this is a 25%-float minority stake in a company two-thirds owned by its parent, with no announced route for minorities to realise the parts and a chairman who moved his own money to the parent.

Our base-case fair value is 21.00 euros, about 14.5% above today's price, below the 20% discount this book requires in the current backdrop, against an adverse case of 12.50 euros with no structural floor. The downside is about twice the upside. This committee reached the same answer on its last full review and nothing dated since - the in-line third-quarter revenue on 15 October 2026 or the September bond - changes it. What would change our mind: a tender or merger offer from Louis Hachette Group, or lease-inclusive net debt falling clearly below 4.3 billion euros at the 25 February 2027 results.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Lagardere SA (MMB.PA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16 (continuing coverage; previous full review 2026-10-26). Sources: five results calls in the transcript bundle (2024-02-27, 2024-07-23, 2025-02-13, 2025-07-24, 2026-02-19), the screener's financial trajectory, the third-quarter 2026 revenue release of 2026-10-15 and the bond placement of 2026-09-09 (both via French financial press), and a fresh news check on 2026-11-16 that found no new company announcement since the third-quarter release. Price used: 18.34 euros, the live Euronext Paris quote on 2026-11-16 (paid market-data feed).*

**The takeaway.** Lagardere is two decent operating businesses - Hachette Livre, the world's third-largest book publisher, and Lagardere Travel Retail, the number-two airport and station retailer - wrapped in a leveraged, majority-controlled holding structure. Management has been credible on operations and on the one leverage target it set, but that target is defined on borrowings only and leaves out the airport-concession leases that are the real economics of the travel-retail business. On the lease-inclusive measure, net debt has not fallen in two years. The controlling chairman has moved his own money from this company into its parent. The operating story is steady; the shareholder story is not improving.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **February 2024 (full-year 2023).** The story was recovery plus deleveraging. Travel retail was rebounding from the pandemic; finance chief Gregoire Castaing called reducing net debt "definitely one of our key priorities from now forward", and blamed higher finance costs on the rate rise.
- **July 2024 (first half 2024).** Refinancing done, maturities "mainly spread towards '27 and '29"; leverage "below 3x" and "improving semester by semester". The North Asia rationalisation began.
- **February 2025 (full-year 2024).** A new format: Lagardere results first, then the new parent, Louis Hachette Group. Leverage fell to 2.4 times "compared to 3" a year earlier. The most revealing moment of the five calls: Arnaud Lagardere explained that he had cut his personal stake in Lagardere from about 5.11% to 0.4% and bought 8.61% of Louis Hachette Group, saying the closer he is to the Bollore family "the happier I am" and that the future lies with the parent.
- **July 2025 (first half 2025).** Lagardere is now presented as embedded inside Louis Hachette Group, with Lagardere-only figures pushed to the press release. Schiphol Amsterdam taken over, "slightly above expectations". First explicit number: leverage of "around 2x" by end-2025.
- **February 2026 (full-year 2025).** Target hit: leverage "under 2x, a level that the group has not reached in a long time", borrowings-only net debt just below 1.6 billion euros. No successor target, no buyback, no new capital-allocation framework. Non-core Live assets are "definitely not for sale".
- **Since the last call (dated facts, 2026-09-09 and 2026-10-15; nothing further through 2026-11-16).** A 500 million euro six-year bond at a 5.25% coupon, maturing September 2032, placed to repay part of the June 2024 bank facility and part of the Vivendi loan. Third-quarter revenue of 2,633 million euros, up 2.4% like-for-like (accelerating from 1.8% in the second quarter); nine-month revenue 7,069 million euros, up 2.6% like-for-like.

The arc is a shift from "Lagardere the listed company" to "Lagardere the subsidiary". Each call gives less airtime to Lagardere's own shareholders and more to the parent.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Deleveraging is the key priority (Feb 2024, repeated every call) | Borrowings-only leverage went 3.0x to 2.4x to under 2x - delivered. Lease-inclusive net debt: 4,503m euros (Dec 2024), 4,494m (Dec 2025), 4,581m (Jun 2026). The lease book grew. | Delivered on the definition chosen; not delivered on the economic one. The definition is never stated on any call. |
| Interest cost will come down through refinancing (Feb 2025) | Interest expense around 265m euros a year, roughly 42% of operating profit, did not fall in 2025. The new September 2026 bond carries a 5.25% coupon - extending maturity, not cutting cost. | Not delivered. |
| Strong growth across businesses | Revenue 5.17bn (2021) to 9.42bn (2025), +10.5% three-year compound growth, and +2.6% like-for-like through nine months of 2026. | Delivered, but slowing to low single digits. |
| Results are "strong and remarkable" for shareholders | Earnings per share 1.14 euros (2022) to 1.43 (2025); book value per share +0.9% a year over five years; return on invested capital 5.8%. | Poorer than the narrative. Growth was bought with leased floor space whose rent and interest absorbed most of it. |
| Free cash flow is very high | Screener shows TTM free cash flow of 2.00bn and EPS of 2.97 - these are two years of half-year reports summed as if they were quarters. Corrected trailing figures are about 1.0bn and about 1.48 euros. Reported free cash flow is also before about 700m euros a year of lease payments and interest. | The screener's 2.6x price-to-free-cash-flow is a measurement error, not a bargain. |
| Gross margin "7%, contracting" (screener) | A travel retailer reports cost of sales differently; the figure is a data artefact, not an operating signal. | Ignore. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable.** Tone has been consistently upbeat on operations ("strong and remarkable" in February 2025, "very satisfactory" in July 2025, "solid growth trend in a rather challenging economic environment" in February 2026). It turned slightly more defensive on the macro in 2026: the third-quarter release calls the geopolitical and economic backdrop difficult and flags slower North American air traffic. Specificity is low throughout: "we don't give guidance, as you know" (July 2025). The one number given (leverage around 2x) was met.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium. The only quantified target - borrowings-only leverage around 2x by end-2025, set in July 2025 - was met in February 2026. The qualitative interest-cost promise of February 2025 was not met. The French logistics and IT modernisation ("we really need to modernize our equipment") has been raised and deferred across several calls without a figure or a date. No sandbagging pattern is visible because there is almost nothing to sandbag against.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The holding structure.** Analysts asked about the chairman's stake move and about asset sales; the answers were candid about the parent preference and firm that radio and Live assets are not for sale (February 2025: "the answer is no, definitely"; February 2026: "definitely not for sale").
- **Currency.** About 40% of operating profit is earned in dollars; management quantified a roughly 100m euro revenue and 10m euro profit drag in July 2025 and points to dollar debt as the offset - a balance-sheet hedge, not an earnings hedge. Nine-month 2026 currency drag on revenue: 90m euros.
- **Not asked:** no analyst on any call pressed on the lease-inclusive net debt, the definition of the leverage ratio, or a buyout of Lagardere's minorities by the parent.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: lease-inclusive net debt flat to up from December 2024 to June 2026 despite two years of "key priority" language.
- Red: interest cost not reduced (February 2025 promise); the September 2026 refinancing priced at 5.25%.
- Red: the chairman rotated from about 5.11% of Lagardere to 0.4% and into the parent (February 2025).
- Red: free float about 25%, roughly 436,000 euros a day traded - untradeable at size.
- Red: modernisation capital need acknowledged but never sized.
- Green: travel retail had its best year in 2025 (divisional profit up 17%, margin 4.6% to 5.1%) and summer 2026 revenue was a record; ex-North Asia travel retail grew 4.6% in the third quarter.
- Green: Hachette gained share in shrinking book markets (2025) and grew 4% in the UK and US in the third quarter of 2026.
- Green: North Asia closures due to be finished by end-2026, removing a loss-maker.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The 2026-2027 share buyback authorisation approved at the 5 May 2026 general meeting (ceiling 40 euros a share, valid to 5 November 2027) is a standard French renewal, not an announced programme; no purchases of size have been disclosed.

- Presentation order changed in 2025: the parent leads, Lagardere is "embedded". The investor-relations centre of gravity has moved upstairs.
- "Leverage" is always quoted without its denominator definition; "net debt just below 1.6 billion" in February 2026 is the ex-lease figure, while the balance sheet carries 4.58bn including leases.
- The September 2026 bond repays part of the Vivendi loan - a reminder that financing runs through the Bollore orbit.
- Leadership change at Hachette's English-language arm: David Shelley becomes global adviser to the Hachette Livre chief executive from 1 January 2027.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** The operating businesses are steady and modestly growing; the capital structure is not improving for the minority shareholder. The single most important thing to weigh: you are buying a 25%-float minority in a company 66.53%-owned by Louis Hachette Group, whose controlling family has shown on the record that it prefers to own the parent. Any path to the parts value requires either the parent buying out minorities (unannounced, no obligation) or real lease-inclusive deleveraging (not happening).

**Moat.** Intangible (Hachette's backlist, author relationships and French distribution scale) plus concession scale in travel retail. Width: narrow - publishing earns roughly a 10% operating margin and gains share, travel retail margins are rising slowly, but group return on invested capital is 5.8%, below the cost of capital, and the airport business re-tenders its concessions. Trend: stable - margins are edging up, not falling.

**Secular threat.** Manageable. Artificial-intelligence-generated content is a long-dated risk to trade publishing, but print and audiobook demand and backlist economics have held; travel retail is cyclical (air traffic), not structurally shrinking. The cheapness is mostly a structure discount plus a measurement error, not a melting base - which means it is neither a value trap nor a mispricing waiting to close.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis:
Jet2 is the best-run leisure travel business in the United Kingdom, trading at roughly seven times its earnings and about six times its free cash flow. The bull case is that the market is pricing a cyclical squeeze as if it were permanent.

The evidence: revenue reached a record 7.48 billion pounds in the year to March 2026 (up 4.3%), passengers passed 20 million, and free cash flow was 495 million pounds - 2.6 billion pounds since the pandemic (FY26 results call, 8 July 2026). Management has a high-credibility record: it flagged its own small miss on flight-only pricing early (November 2025) and landed full-year operating profit inside its 435-440 million pound guide. The September 2026 trading statement showed booked passengers up 8.8% on capacity up 7.6%, with Gatwick ahead of plan.

Three drivers can lift profit from here. First, the newer bases (Bournemouth, Luton and from March 2026 Gatwick) carry start-up costs today and should mature into profit; Gatwick is guided to break even by the year to March 2029. Second, the A321neo fleet (232 seats against 189, lower cost per seat, about 22% of the summer 2026 fleet) lowers unit costs as it grows. Third, the buyback shrinks the share count: about 22 million shares were bought back in the year to March 2026 and a further 250 million pounds runs to 31 May 2027, roughly 9% of today's market value of about 2.7 billion pounds.

Consensus, as cited in the committee's prior record, expects earnings per share to recover toward 188p for the year to March 2028 and 243p for the year to March 2029. On those numbers the stock trades at about eight and six times earnings respectively, with a balance sheet that carries roughly break-even own net debt and an undrawn 500 million pound credit line. If flight-only pricing stabilises and Gatwick scales, a multiple of nine to ten times recovery earnings gives 1,700-2,150p.

Conditions: flight-only yields stop falling, hotel cost inflation moderates toward package price growth, and no large demand shock (conflict, recession) hits the 2027 summer booking season.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case is that Jet2's profit has stopped growing even as it adds capacity, and that the cheap multiple reflects a narrowing moat in a crowded market rather than a mispricing.

The evidence: net income fell from 447 million pounds (FY25) to 410 million pounds (FY26) while seat capacity grew about 8%. Flight-only ticket yield fell 7% in both the November 2025 and July 2026 calls; management calls this 'investing in price' and 'investing in load factor', which is another way of saying it cannot hold fares. Hotel costs, 45% of the cost base, rose about 6.5% while package prices rose 3%, of which about one point was customers trading up. Return on capital employed slipped from a 17% three-year average to 14.4%, and our scan's return on invested capital of 6.4% is near the cost of capital. Free cash flow fell about 25% year on year as bookings moved closer to departure.

The headline net cash of about 2.0 billion pounds is mostly customer deposits; the CFO himself put own cash at about 1.2 billion pounds, roughly equal to the 1.28 billion pounds of debt including leases. In a shock those deposits become a refund liability, not a cushion, and the new 2 times leverage target signals more borrowing to fund the Airbus order book. Consensus earnings for the year to March 2027 of about 136p (cited in the prior record) imply the stock is not cheap on this year's numbers at about 11 times.

What would confirm the bear case: the 18 November 2026 interim results showing summer 2026 profit flat or down despite higher passenger numbers, winter flight-only yields still falling, or capacity guidance for summer 2027 that again outruns the market. The business is also exposed to inflation: its gross margin fell from 13.8% to a loss through the 2021-22 period (largely pandemic-driven), and it has shown only partial pass-through of hotel cost increases.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is not pricing terminal decline; it is pricing a profit plateau. Seven brokers average a target of about 1,617p (MarketBeat aggregator, 3 November 2026), only about 6% above today's price, with five buys and two holds. Our base case of 1,720p sits a little above that, so the disagreement with the market is modest. Where we differ is on composition: the street leans on the headline 2.0 billion pounds of net cash, which we largely exclude because most of it is customer deposits, and on the recovery in earnings per share to about 188p by the year to March 2028, which we accept only in the base case. The street may also be too relaxed about flight-only yield, which has fallen 7% in two reporting periods running. We do not see a large expectations gap at 1,525p.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation risk, debt wall or forced dilution: own cash roughly matches debt, the 500 million pound facility is undrawn to October 2030, and the fleet is financed through long-dated asset-backed borrowing. The risk over the next three to nine months is earnings disappointment. The 18 November 2026 interim results could show summer 2026 profit flat despite more passengers, and the winter booking season (typically sold from January) has been late and price-led in each of the last two years. Hotel cost inflation, sustainable aviation fuel mandates (32 million pounds of extra premium in FY26) and employment-tax rises all pressure margins. A demand shock - renewed Middle East conflict hitting eastern Mediterranean bookings, as in spring 2026, or a UK consumer slowdown - would compress the customer-deposit float and free cash flow quickly. Any of these could take the shares back toward the 1,250p entry level.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-seller setup specific to Jet2: no index deletion, no lock-up, no dividend cut to drive out yield holders, and the company itself is a steady buyer through the 250 million pound buyback. The path to 1,250p is a sector-wide sell-off: European leisure and airline shares de-rate together on fuel spikes, geopolitical shocks or UK consumer weakness, as they did in March 2026 when Jet2 set a 12-month low near 980p. That is why the wait is tied to a sector or style sell-off rather than to mechanical selling.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 1,250p, which a sector-wide sell-off of UK consumer and airline shares could deliver.

The thesis holds. Jet2 is a well-run, cash-generative leisure travel business with credible management, a strong own-cash position and an aggressive buyback. Nothing dated has changed since the committee's last look on 19 October 2026; the price has moved only from 1,510p to 1,525p.

The issue remains the price, not the business. Our fair value is about 1,720p, only about 13% above today's 1,525p, which does not clear the 20% bar we require in a growth-with-sticky-inflation backdrop, while the adverse case of about 1,200p is about 21% below. At 1,250p the trade becomes attractive: about 38% upside to fair value against little downside to the adverse case. The shares were near 980p as recently as March 2026, so a sector-wide sell-off of that kind is not far-fetched.

We hold the value case at a middle rating. The moat is real but narrow and being tested: profit fell in FY26 while capacity grew about 8%, flight-only fares have been cut 7% two periods running, and return on capital has slipped from 17% to 14.4%. Until pricing stabilises, the low multiple partly reflects a business that is buying growth with price, which limits how much we will pay.

The interim results on 18 November 2026 are the next dated test. A clear profit increase with stable winter yields would strengthen the case; a profit fall with more price-cutting would argue for a lower fair value.
picks.forcing_function: No single event forces a re-rating. The nearest dated checkpoint is the interim results on 18 November 2026, which will show whether summer 2026 converted higher bookings into profit and give the first read on winter pricing. Beyond that, the forcing mechanism is slow: the buyback steadily retiring stock to May 2027, Gatwick progressing toward break-even by the year to March 2029, and the summer 2027 capacity and yield guidance, typically given in the new year. A re-rating needs evidence that flight-only pricing has stopped falling.

# Jet2 plc (JET2.L) - a deep dive on management and the setup

Debate date: 16 November 2026. Live price 1,525p (FMP quote, London listing, pence). Transcripts read: interim results call of 19 November 2025 (half year to 30 September 2025) and full-year results call of 8 July 2026 (year to 31 March 2026). The next dated release is the interim results for the half year to 30 September 2026, scheduled for 18 November 2026 (FMP earnings calendar), two days after this debate.

The short version: management is credible and conservative, the balance sheet is strong, and the cash returns are real. But the last eighteen months show a business that is growing passengers by giving away price, with profit flat to slightly down while capacity grows about 8% a year. That is a narrow moat that is being tested, not a widening one.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

In November 2025 the story was "record numbers" and expansion: passengers up 6%, the new bases at Bournemouth and Luton, and the launch of London Gatwick, described as "a once-in-a-generation opportunity to accelerate our growth" (H1 FY26 call). The Gatwick base was explicitly not expected to make money until the year to March 2029.

By July 2026 the emphasis had shifted from growth to resilience. The words used most were "resilient", "robust" and "controlled": operating profit "remained resilient even after absorbing Gatwick startup investment costs and wider industry cost pressures" (FY26 call). The growth story is still there (over 20 million passengers, up 5%), but the profit story has become one of absorbing costs. Capital returns moved to the centre: 363 million pounds returned in the year, "more than ever before", and a further 250 million pound buyback to run to 31 May 2027.

A new strand appeared in July 2026: a medium-term leverage target of 2 times net debt to EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) on an own-cash basis. That is a quiet signal that management intends to use more of the balance sheet over time, mainly to finance the Airbus fleet.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record revenue" (FY26) | Revenue 7.48 billion pounds, up 4.3%; three-year growth about 14% a year, flattered by the post-pandemic rebound from 1.23 billion in 2022 | True, but growth has slowed sharply |
| Operating profit "resilient" | Net income fell from 447 million pounds (FY25) to 410 million (FY26); FY26 operating profit guided at 435-440 million against 446.5 million the year before (29 April 2026 trading update) | Profit fell while capacity grew about 8%. "Resilient" is generous |
| Package price "resilient, up 3%" | About 1 point of the 3% came from customers trading up to four- and five-star hotels; hotel costs, 45% of the cost base, rose about 6.5% | Partial pass-through only; the cost of the holiday rose faster than its price |
| Flight-only demand strong (+15% passengers) | Flight-only ticket yield down 7% in both calls | Volume bought with price |
| "Over 2 billion pounds of net cash" | True on the headline basis, but most of it is customer deposits. The CFO himself split out "1.2 billion pounds of our own cash, excluding customer advances"; against about 1.28 billion pounds of debt including leases, own cash is roughly break-even | The headline overstates distributable cash |
| Free cash flow 495 million pounds; 2.6 billion since the pandemic | Consistent with the trailing figures; free cash flow fell about 25% year on year as customers booked later | True, but declining and timing-sensitive |
| Earnings per share "stable" | Earnings per share roughly 208-211p in both FY25 and FY26 - stable only because about 22 million shares were bought back | Per-share stability is buyback-supported |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Trajectory: stable, with a defensive tilt.

- November 2025: confident, expansionary - "Further growth in the first half across all our key metrics." The CFO was candid about uncertainty: "there's a lot of moving parts ... I'm not being evasive, but there are."
- July 2026: still upbeat ("I hope you're as excited about the future as we are"), but the vocabulary moved to cost absorption, "investing in price" and capital returns. On the Middle East conflict, management described later bookings and a bounce-back in eastern Mediterranean destinations rather than a lasting hit.

There is no sign of panic and no sign of rising ambition either. The language is that of a well-run operator in a tougher market.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Reliability: high.

- The November 2025 guide for flight-only pricing was "mid-single digits down"; the CFO volunteered that the outcome was "slightly worse" at minus 7%. Flagging a small miss early is a good sign.
- FY26 operating profit landed inside the 435-440 million pound range guided in April 2026.
- The beat rate in our data is 50% (one of two quarters), and FMP shows the November 2025 half-year earnings per share at 300p against a 281p estimate.
- The July 2026 capital spending cut of about 350 million pounds for the following year was explained as Airbus delivery timing, "timing only, it doesn't undermine any of our growth plans". That is plausible given industry-wide Airbus delays, but it also flatters near-term free cash flow.

No sandbagging pattern, and no pattern of over-promising.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Capacity versus price: analysts asked in both calls whether growing capacity 8-9% when competitors grow less would force further fare cuts. Management answered with flexibility ("we can make adjustments") rather than with yield guidance. This is the central unresolved question.
- Cost per seat: management repeatedly declined to give unit-cost guidance before Eurocontrol fees and slot declarations were known.
- Booking curve: later bookings came up in both calls; management treats them as a timing effect, but they reduce visibility and the customer-deposit float.
- AI distribution (July 2026): asked whether large language models would change how holidays are booked, management said "We've not seen a big impact from LLMs at the moment" and that direct bookings are steady at just under 80% for holidays. Honest, but untested.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Profit falling while capacity grows about 8% a year (April 2026 trading update; FY26 results, July 2026).
- Flight-only yield down 7% two reporting periods running (November 2025, July 2026).
- Return on capital employed down from 17% (three-year average quoted in November 2025) to 14.4% in FY26.
- Hotel cost inflation (about 6.5%) running ahead of package price (3%, of which 1 point is mix).
- Gatwick start-up costs, with profitability not expected until the year to March 2029.

Green flags:
- Strong own-cash position, an undrawn 500 million pound revolving credit facility extended to October 2030.
- Shareholder returns at record levels, with the share count falling: about 22 million shares bought back in FY26 and a further 250 million pounds under way to May 2027.
- Fleet renewal to the A321neo (232 seats against 189, lower seat cost; about 22% of the summer 2026 fleet).
- Industry-leading customer service and low cancellation rates, which support the package-holiday brand.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "Investing in price" and "investing in load factor" have become standing phrases. When a company describes price cuts as investments, it is telling you that it does not have the pricing power to hold fares.
- The new 2 times leverage target signals a shift from a cash-rich to a more geared capital structure as the Airbus order book is financed.
- The CFO's own-cash framing (1.2 billion pounds excluding customer advances) is a welcome bit of honesty that the headline net-cash figure hides.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. Capital allocation is disciplined (buybacks at single-digit earnings multiples, fleet renewal, no acquisitions), and management is credible.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: Jet2's profit has stopped growing even as capacity grows. The investment case depends on Gatwick and the newer bases maturing into profit and on flight-only pricing stabilising. The interim results on 18 November 2026 are the next test of whether summer 2026 converted bookings into profit.

Moat: scale-cost plus brand (the integrated package-holiday model, about 80% direct distribution, customer-service reputation). It is real but narrow, and the evidence - return on capital falling from 17% to 14.4%, yields given away to fill seats - says it is being tested rather than widening. Our scan's return on invested capital of 6.4% sits near the cost of capital. Secular threat: manageable. AI-led travel search could change distribution over time, but management reports no impact so far and the direct-booking share is steady. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear-print on a competitive, cost-inflated leisure market, not a structurally shrinking base - but the moat needs proof that pricing can hold.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis: Harmony is a self-funding narcolepsy franchise priced like a melting ice cube even though the ice has a contractual floor. WAKIX revenue grew from $305M (2021) to $868M (2025), and 2026 is tracking to $1.0-1.04B ($745.6M through Q3, reiterated 2026-11-04). Average patients reached about 9,350 in Q3-2026, with 400 net adds in five of the last six quarters, against only about 20% brand penetration of roughly 80,000 diagnosed patients. Six of seven generic filers have settled for entry no earlier than March 2030 (including pediatric exclusivity), so about three and a quarter years of protected cash flow remain at a free-cash-flow margin of about 40%, plus about $15 a share of net cash (2026-09-30: $1.05B of cash and investments against $149M of debt). At about 5.5x free cash flow (price divided by free cash flow per share), the market prices WAKIX as if it ends far earlier than 2030. Upside options: the GR line extension (approval decision due 2027-04-01) can move patients onto a later-patented formulation before 2030, HD targets new labels with patents out to the 2040s, and BP-205 multiple-dose data (2026-11-04) kept its best-in-class case alive. Conditions: the AET litigation does not produce an at-risk generic launch before 2030, and the new CEO does not overpay for acquisitions.
picks.bear_thesis: This is a single-asset company with a dated cliff and one open door to an earlier one. AET and Sandoz say their generic uses an amorphous form that escapes the crystal-form patent, and Harmony itself has now asked for a preliminary injunction, which openly admits an at-risk launch in 2027 is possible (Bank of America asked about it on the 2026-11-04 call). If the polymorph ruling and the method-of-use challenge go against Harmony and the injunction fails, WAKIX could face generics two to three years early. The earnings line is also weaker than the sales line: Q3-2026 EPS of $0.81 missed about $1.00 and fell from $0.87 a year earlier, gross margin dropped to about 70% from 76% in Q2, R&D jumped to $71.7M, and EPS beat only 2 of the last 7 quarters (3-year EPS CAGR -3%). Leadership is churning: the CEO exit was announced 2026-10-12, and the CFO hired in May 2026 has been replaced by an interim officer. The new management has signalled it wants to deploy the cash pile on deals, so part of the $15-a-share cash floor could become an acquisition with its own risk. The orexin-2 agonist class has larger competitors, and BP-205 showed on-target side effects at low doses.
picks.consensus_delta: The street treats Harmony as a 2030 cliff stock with litigation risk and pays about 5.5x free cash flow for it. We think the market over-discounts the AET risk relative to the evidence: six settlements at 2030, three separate patents of which Harmony needs only one, and AET has not called the amorphous suit a sham (2026-11-04 call). Net cash alone is about 45% of the share price. Where the street is right: the earnings line is weaker than the sales line (Q3 EPS of $0.81 against about $1.00), and the post-2030 bridge (GR, HD, BP-205, acquisitions) is unproven. So the disagreement is about how probable the 2030 entry date is, not about a hidden growth story.
picks.valley_of_death: Over the next 3-9 months: (1) an adverse polymorph ruling or a denied preliminary injunction could allow an at-risk generic launch in 2027, the main path to the $24 adverse case; (2) a leadership handover on 2027-01-01 with an interim finance chief, during which the first big acquisition could be announced at a full price; (3) seasonal Q1 insurance resets, which hit Q1 revenue every year (Q1-2026 fell to $215M from $244M in Q4-2025); (4) further margin pressure from cost of goods and R&D. None of these threatens solvency, given about $900M of net cash.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-seller setup: there is no dividend to cut, no index event and no lock-up. The 2026-10-12 CEO-news gap and the post-Q3 drift down to about $33 look like holders exiting over uncertainty, not forced liquidation. The smart-money score is 64/100 and the institutional flow score 59/100, both middling. An adverse court ruling would cause a sharp gap, not a slow grind.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Buy now. Harmony trades at $33.21, about 5.5 times free cash flow, with about $15 a share of net cash and WAKIX patent protection settled to March 2030 with six of seven generic filers. Our base-case fair value of about $43 sits about 29% above today's price, which clears the 20% bar we require in the current reflation backdrop. The disappointments were costs, not demand: EPS of $0.81 against about $1.00 expected, and a lower gross margin. picks.bull_thesis: Geely is one of the few mass-market Chinese carmakers that still makes real money in a price war. In H1 2026 (results call 2026-08-17) it earned close to RMB 10 billion attributable profit at about a 5.6% margin while management put the industry average at 1.6%, and it ranked first in China by retail sales. Two engines are offsetting a shrinking home market: exports (the annual target was hit by mid-year, raised from 640,000 to 920,000, and nine-month exports reached 797,670, up 169%, per CnEVPost on 2026-10-01) and the premium ZEEKR brand (+97% in H1 2026), which lifts revenue per car. The One Geely programme is cutting costs measurably (admin ratio 1.9% to 1.7%, R&D ratio 5.5% to 5.2%, model count down 20%). The balance sheet carries RMB 56.6 billion of net cash at 2026-06-30, roughly 40% of the HK$148 billion market value, and the company pays out 30% of profit. At HK$13.71 the stock trades at roughly 7x annualised core earnings and a low single-digit multiple of free cash flow. If margins merely hold near current levels and the market re-rates toward 10-11x earnings, fair value is in the mid-to-high HK$20s. Conditions: gross margin stays near 16-17%, exports keep growing despite trade barriers, and no large value-destroying acquisition consumes the cash.
picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness may be deserved. Returns on capital are poor (ROIC about 2.5%, ROE 11.6%), reported EPS was flat in 2025 at RMB 1.63, the 2024 jump was about half one-off gains (core profit RMB 8.5 billion vs reported RMB 16.6 billion, per the 2025-03-12 call), the screener shows 0 of 2 recent quarters beating consensus, and latest-quarter EPS fell 22% year on year. The home market shrank by double digits in H1 2026 and domestic sales fell about 25% in August 2026; all of Geely's growth now comes from exports, which are exposed to tariffs and anti-subsidy actions in Europe and elsewhere, and exports slipped 3% month on month in September 2026. Management itself flagged rising chip and raw-material costs on 2026-08-17 and admitted 'a lack of blockbuster product' in the mainstream segment. The headline free cash flow and net cash are flattered by supplier credit (car makers pay suppliers late), so a slowdown could reverse working capital and shrink the cash pile quickly. If net margin falls toward 3% and the market keeps a 6x multiple, the stock could trade near HK$11.
picks.consensus_delta: The market is pricing Geely as if the Chinese price war will crush its margins the way it has crushed most rivals' profits. The numbers so far say otherwise: H1 2026 net margin about 5.6% against an industry average of 1.6% (2026-08-17), gross margin near 16-17%, and growth shifted to exports and the premium ZEEKR brand. At HK$13.71 the stock trades around 7x annualised core earnings with about 40% of its market value in net cash. Where we disagree with the market: we think it extrapolates the sector's losses onto the one large private carmaker that is still profitable. Where the market has a point: reported EPS is flat, the latest quarter fell 22%, and returns on capital are low; so our fair value assumes no margin expansion and a below-peer-leader multiple. No dated analyst consensus target could be verified via FMP (no coverage for this listing), so we cite none.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): Q4 2026 and Q1 2027. Domestic demand is shrinking (domestic sales -25% in August 2026), input costs (chips, raw materials) are rising, and Beijing's price-war curbs have not stopped discounting. Exports, now the only growth engine, slipped 3% month on month in September 2026 and face tariff and anti-subsidy risk in Europe and emerging markets. A weak October-December sales run or a second-half margin miss at the March 2027 full-year results could push the stock lower before any re-rating; supplier-credit unwinding could also shrink the reported cash pile. None of this threatens solvency given net cash.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure appears sector-driven rather than holder-specific: the stock is about 25% below its 200-day average and near its 52-week low (HK$13.15) after a China-auto de-rating, with low smart-money interest (score 4/100) and neutral institutional flow. There is no dividend cut, index deletion or lock-up that would force mechanical selling; the 30% payout policy keeps income holders in place. Further sector outflows could extend the drawdown, but that is a sector-wide sell-off, not forced selling by holders who must sell regardless of value.

# Torpol S.A. (TOR.WA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Prices and figures in Polish zloty (PLN), Warsaw listing.*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript exists for Torpol in our data provider (FMP returned no transcript dates for TOR.WA), and Polish small caps rarely publish English call transcripts. This deep dive therefore rests on (a) the quarterly statements carried by FMP through the September 2026 quarter, (b) management's own remarks at the half-year results meeting reported by Strefa Inwestorow on 2026-09-07, and (c) dated broker actions (DM BDM 2026-09-07, Noble Securities 2026-09-29). No quotes below are invented; where we paraphrase a press summary we say so.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Torpol is a Poznan-based rail-infrastructure contractor whose main client is PKP PLK, the state rail-network operator, with a smaller oil-and-gas engineering arm (Torpol Oil & Gas, "TOG"). Its story over the last two years has run in three stages:

- **2024 - margin squeeze, cash out.** Revenue rose to 1.46B PLN but net profit fell to 68M (scan data) and operating cash flow swung to about -212M as receivables ballooned by 367M. The narrative was "volume is coming; margins and cash will follow."
- **2025 - the volume arrives and the cash comes back.** Revenue jumped about 36% to 1.98B PLN, net profit recovered to 78M, and working capital released 426M, taking free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital spending) to about 473M and year-end cash to 656M. That one-year cash release is what makes the stock screen at 2.8 times free cash flow.
- **2026 - a record order book, flat sales.** At the half-year meeting (reported 2026-09-07) management guided full-year 2026 revenue to roughly the 2025 level, reported a record order book of 6.34B PLN net at end-June, and flagged the June 2026 award of the Warszawa Wschodnia station modernisation (about 2.8B PLN net base value) from PKP PLK. The new emphasis is independence: bidding alone where Torpol has the references, rather than in consortia, and diversifying TOG into biomethane, power, hydrogen and waste-to-energy (five tenders worth about 3.5B PLN combined, with Polimex Mostostal).

What was quietly conceded: management said there are no further contracts of Warszawa Wschodnia's size on the horizon, so the pipeline is now smaller tenders. And the largest new contract is still in its design phase, which management itself named as a revenue-timing uncertainty.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim (dated) | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 revenue about equal to 2025 (2026-09-07) | 9 months 2026 revenue = 334 + 579 + 547 = 1,461M PLN vs 2025 full year 1.98B; Q4 needs about 520M, below Q4 2025's 621M. Achievable. | Matches |
| Backlog gross margin 7.83% in H1 2026 vs 6.87% a year earlier, "not unrealistic" to hold (2026-09-07) | Reported gross margin H1 2026 = 71.6M / 913.9M = 7.8%, matching. But Q3 2026 operating profit was 19.9M on 547M revenue (3.6%), versus 24.8M on 505M (4.9%) in Q3 2025. | Matches in H1; Q3 contradicts the direction |
| Positive full-year 2026 operating cash flow, helped by Q3 invoicing and the Warszawa Wschodnia advance (2026-09-07) | H1 2026 operating cash flow about -193.5M; cash fell from 656M (Dec-2025) to 454M (Jun-2026). First advance instalment is only 56.5M PLN gross. | Unproven; depends on Q4 |
| Net cash is a core strength | Jun-2026 cash 454M against debt of 79M (incl. 23M leases) = 375M net. But a 3.39 PLN dividend (about 78M) was declared before the quarter-end and paid 2026-07-17, so post-dividend net cash is about 297M. Much of the remainder is customer advances: deferred revenue was 134M at June. | Real but overstated by the scan; a large part is working capital, not surplus |
| Strong profitability (scan: ROE 23.5%, ROIC 16.8%) | Trailing-twelve-month (TTM) net profit about 80M PLN (Q4-25 29.8 + Q1-26 10.3 + Q2-26 23.5 + Q3-26 16.3) on equity of about 530M, so ROE around 15%. Net margin 3.8%. | Respectable, not exceptional |

The headline cheapness in our screen (2.8 times free cash flow, 23.9% free-cash-flow margin) is an artifact of the 2025 working-capital release; the year before, free cash flow was -241M. Over 2022-2025 cumulative free cash flow was about 409M on cumulative net profit of about 521M - healthy, but nowhere near 24% of sales as a run-rate.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a defensive tilt.** Without transcripts we cannot track quarter-by-quarter wording. From the September 2026 summary, the tone is measured: revenue guided flat, the margin described as "not unrealistic" to maintain (a cautious formulation), and an open admission that no further mega-contracts are visible. The offensive notes are the independent-bidding strategy and TOG diversification. That reads as management managing expectations through a post-peak backlog phase rather than promising acceleration.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium.** Torpol does not issue formal profit guidance. The revenue-flat guide for 2026 is on track. The cash-flow promise for 2026 is the one to watch: H1 was heavily negative and the positive full-year outcome depends on Q4 billing and the advance. BDM's 2026-09-07 note put its EBITDA forecast 27% above the company's strategy assumptions, which says the sell-side is more bullish than management, not the reverse - no sign of sandbagging (deliberately low guidance).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Backlog trough.** Noble Securities expects the order book to fall to about 5.0B PLN by the end of Q1 2027 before rebuilding from mid-2027 (as reported by Comparic). Noble moved from "sell" (53 PLN target, March 2026) to "reduce" (59.70 PLN target, 2026-09-29).
- **Contract timing.** Warszawa Wschodnia is still in design; the revenue curve is back-end loaded.
- **Shareholder overhang.** Mirbud, a former consortium partner, sold its entire 10% stake (2,297,740 shares) in August 2026. The new holders of that block are an open question.
- **Funding cycle.** The pipeline is tied to EU-funded rail capex at PKP PLK and CPK (the central airport and rail programme); three further PLK tenders are expected in Q4 2026.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: Q3 2026 operating margin 3.6% vs 4.9% a year earlier, despite a "better-margin" backlog (FMP Q3 2026 figures).
- Red: H1 2026 operating cash outflow of about 194M; cash down 200M in six months.
- Red: No further contracts of Warszawa Wschodnia's scale in sight (management, 2026-09-07); broker sees backlog shrinking into 2027.
- Red: The share price has fallen from about 68 PLN (50-day average) to 56.30 and sits near its 52-week low of 53.50.
- Green: Record 6.34B PLN backlog at end-June 2026, about three years of revenue.
- Green: Real net cash (about 297M after the July dividend), no refinancing risk, and a 3.39 PLN dividend paid on 2026-07-17.
- Green: Gross margin on backlog up a full point year on year (H1 2026).
- Green: The company kept its margins through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 4.7% in 2019 to 13.0% in 2021).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The shift from "consortium partner" to "we bid alone where we have references" coincides with Mirbud's full exit in August 2026 - a relationship that cooled.
- TOG's push into hydrogen, biomethane and incineration is a hedge against a rail-funding lull, but its backlog is only about 180M PLN - immaterial to the group for now.
- The equity line fell from 586M (Mar-2026) to 532M (Jun-2026): the declared dividend (about 78M) exceeded the quarter's profit, consistent with a generous payout policy.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: stable.** The business is a competent, cash-rich, thin-margin rail contractor at a cyclical high in order intake, not a deeply discounted franchise. The single most important thing the director must weigh: **the cheapness in our screen is a working-capital artifact.** On normal earnings (about 80M PLN net TTM, roughly 3.5 PLN a share) and after removing the cash the company genuinely does not need, the shares trade at around 13-14 times earnings - fair for a lumpy contractor, not a bargain.

**Moat.** Narrow, of the regulatory-licence / references type: PKP PLK tenders require track-record references and qualified crews, which limits the field to a handful of Polish and regional contractors. Returns are respectable (ROE about 15% TTM) and backlog margins are rising, so the moat is stable rather than eroding, but contractors cannot price above the tender. **Secular threat:** none structural - rail investment in Poland is a long-term build-out supported by EU funding. The risk is cyclical (funding-programme timing), not terminal. The current price weakness is a cyclical fear-print around a backlog peak, not a melting franchise.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat none.

# MBB SE (MBB.DE) - Forensic dossier, 2026-11-09

Sources: FMP quarterly statements (Q2-2025 to Q2-2026), FMP quotes for MBB.DE, VH2.DE and AAG.DE (2026-11-09), MBB SE investor-relations pages (news list, ad-hoc list, share page) read 2026-11-09. No earnings-call transcript was available from FMP, and the web-search budget for this run was exhausted, so management quotes are limited to release headlines. Nothing below is a quoted remark unless marked as a headline.

Takeaway: MBB is a family-controlled German holding whose earnings now run mostly through its listed pipeline and grid builder Friedrich Vorwerk. The operating story is strong and getting stronger - guidance was raised twice in 2026 - but the screener's cheapness signals (price to free cash flow 5.8x, return on equity 4%) are artefacts of consolidating a subsidiary that MBB owns only about a third of. Counted stake by stake, the stock trades close to the value of its parts.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- 2026-01-26 preliminary FY2025: revenue EUR 1.17bn, EBITDA margin about 18%.
- 2026-03-31 FY2025 results: base dividend EUR 1.21 proposed; 2026 guidance EUR 1.1-1.2bn revenue at a 15-18% EBITDA margin.
- 2026-04-13: share buyback programme raised to EUR 25m and extended.
- 2026-07-22 preliminary Q2 (headline): adjusted EBITDA up 62% to EUR 75m; margin guidance raised to 18-20%.
- 2026-08-13: half-year report; sale of CT Formpolster to Nexeras.
- 2026-10-21 preliminary Q3 (headline): adjusted EBITDA up 25% to EUR 84m; margin guidance raised again, to 22-24%.
The story moved from "diversified buy-and-build holding" to "infrastructure contractor plus cash pile": the margin gains are concentrated in the service and infrastructure segment (Friedrich Vorwerk).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Q2-2026 (FMP): revenue EUR 298.5m, EBIT EUR 40.6m, pre-tax EUR 57.7m, profit from continuing operations EUR 38.3m, but profit to MBB shareholders only EUR 16.2m (EPS EUR 3.11). About 58% of group profit belongs to minority holders - mainly the roughly two-thirds of Friedrich Vorwerk MBB does not own.
- Q1-2026: revenue EUR 237.5m, EPS EUR 1.45. Trailing four quarters EPS (Q3-25 3.58 + Q4-25 3.19 + Q1-26 1.45 + Q2-26 3.11) = about EUR 11.3, so about 17x earnings at EUR 196.40 - not the deep-value multiple the free-cash-flow screen implies.
- Balance sheet 2026-06-30 (FMP): cash EUR 405m plus EUR 262m short-term investments plus EUR 207m long-term investments; debt EUR 92m; minority interest EUR 324m on EUR 1.04bn total equity. The company states net liquidity of EUR 764m at end-2025 including physical gold. Much of this cash sits inside listed subsidiaries (Friedrich Vorwerk, Aumann) and is not MBB's to spend.

picks.bear_thesis: The cheapness is a peak-price illusion attached to one Peruvian mine and a minority-heavy structure. Group copper output is flat year to date (344,521 tonnes of concentrate, 0%) and Las Bambas slipped in Q3 2026 (100,289 tonnes, -3% year on year, -8% on the quarter) on lower grade (0.80% vs 0.86%) and recovery (88.6% vs 90.4%), so the record profits are almost entirely copper, silver and gold prices. Silver already fell from US$84/oz in Q1 to US$63 in Q3, and gold from US$4,875 to US$4,258, eroding the by-product credits that make the zinc mines work. Shareholders own only 62.5% of Las Bambas and 55% of Khoemacau: minority holders hold US$3.72 billion of US$9.45 billion of book equity at 2026-06-30, so the US$3.70 billion trailing free cash flow overstates what belongs to MMG holders. The balance-sheet repair was partly paid for with new shares (issued capital up about US$0.8 billion in the first half). Debt due within a year jumped to US$2.56 billion. Guidance is slipping at the smaller assets (2026-10-14: Khoemacau cut about 10%, Rosebery zinc cut about a third after seismic events, Kinsevere C1 cost raised to US$3.00-3.10/lb on diesel and acid), two people died at Las Bambas in August, and management itself warned on 2026-08-12 that a super El Nino could destabilise Peru's new government and the mine's operating environment. MMG beat consensus earnings in only 2 of 7 quarters, pays no dividend, and is 67% controlled by China Minmetals, which limits any re-rating lever. If copper falls back to US$10,500, attributable earnings roughly halve and the stock is fairly priced near HK$5-6; a two-month blockade on the southern corridor (it happened for three months in late 2022) would take further cash out of the year.
picks.consensus_delta: Is the market pricing terminal decline into a business with growing earnings power? Partly, and for the wrong reason. At HK$6.98 the market value is about US$11.5B, roughly 6-7 times the US$1.8B annual run rate of shareholder earnings implied by the first half of 2026, and about 3 times consolidated trailing free cash flow. The market's implicit assumption is that copper equities must de-rate when rates rise, regardless of the metal: copper is flat this month near US$14,400/t while MMG fell about 20% and Zijin and CMOC about the same. Where we disagree: a miner that has cut net debt to US$0.74B and carries a first-half-of-the-cost-curve core asset does not need cheap credit, so the rate shock that is hurting leveraged balance sheets is not its problem. Where the market is right: the earnings are a function of a record copper price, minorities take 37.5% of Las Bambas, and the stock deserves a structural discount to Freeport and Southern Copper. We price that discount in (4.5 times attributable Las Bambas EBITDA at US$13,000 copper) and still find about 25% upside. # Weatherford International (WFRD) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 2026-11-09. Transcripts: Q3 2025 (2025-10-22), Q4 2025 (2026-02-04), Q1 2026 (2026-04-22), Q2 2026 (2026-07-22), Q3 2026 (2026-10-21). Live price $85.50 (NASDAQ, USD).*

**Bottom line:** Weatherford is an oilfield-services company whose management has done what it said it would: hold profit margins and keep generating cash while revenue fell about 11% in 2025 and the Middle East was disrupted by the Iran conflict in 2026. The numbers corroborate the story. The open questions are not about honesty but about the cycle: how quickly Middle East drilling comes back, whether Mexico keeps paying, and whether the 2027 growth items (a full year of the NCS acquisition, Venezuela, offshore completions) arrive on schedule.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **Q3 2025 to Q4 2025:** The story was "margins in a down market." Mexico revenue fell a little over 50% in 2025, yet Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization, adjusted for one-offs) margin reached 22.6% and free cash flow conversion was 76%. 2025 was the first full year of shareholder returns ($173M in dividends and buybacks) and the dividend was raised 10%.
- **Q4 2025 call (2026-02-04):** 2026 framed as "a tale of two halves" - international activity flat to slightly down, with second-half growth from awards in Saudi Arabia, Argentina, the UAE, Brazil and others, and a "stronger 2027."
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-22):** The Iran conflict (from March) knocked the Middle East back; margin fell to 20.2%. The narrative turned defensive - cost actions, portfolio pruning (Argentina pressure pumping sold), and the redomestication proposal (moving legal home from Ireland to Delaware).
- **Q2 2026 (2026-07-22):** Still 20.2% margin; the Saudi lump-sum turnkey contract ended (management said it was "comfortable" losing it at current pricing) and the original Oman contract finished 14 months early. NCS (a completions technology business) was acquired and offshore completions became a stated growth leg.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-21):** Revenue $1.143B (+3% sequentially, -7% year on year), adjusted EBITDA $254M at 22.2% (+204 basis points sequentially), adjusted free cash flow $155M (61% conversion). The story is now "margin expansion in a flat market, amplified once revenue turns," with Venezuela, offshore completions and managed pressure drilling (MPD, a system that controls well pressure while drilling) aftermarket named as 2027 drivers. The Saudi recovery the company hoped for in February has quietly been dropped from the near-term plan: "We have deliberately not built a regional recovery into our near-term outlook."

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Management claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Can expand margins with no revenue growth | Q3 2026 margin 22.2% on revenue down 7% y/y; margin up 39bp y/y | Matches |
| Generates cash "in any cycle" | TTM free cash flow $578M (9.3% of today's market value); Q3 FCF +57% y/y | Matches, though Q4 2025 was flattered by a catch-up Mexico payment |
| Mexico payments normalized | "several consecutive quarters of regular payments" (Q3 2026); collections cited in Q1, Q2 and Q3 | Matches so far; single-customer concentration remains |
| Second-half 2026 international growth (Feb 2026) | Middle East flat sequentially, Saudi down to 20% of the region | Missed - overtaken by the conflict, and management said so openly |
| Balance sheet is light | Net debt about $467M including leases (~$319M excluding) vs ~$1.0B TTM EBITDA; $236M of 8.625% notes redeemed with cash on 2026-10-30 | Matches |
| Earnings quality | GAAP EPS 5.93 (2025) vs TTM 5.61; Q3 2026 EPS $1.66 vs $1.21 consensus | Solid, but gross margin is contracting (21.7%) and Piotroski 5/9 is middling |

The narrative is, if anything, slightly poorer than what the numbers allow: management has repeatedly declined to bank a Middle East recovery.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY - Stable to rising
Q4 2025: confident ("demonstrating our ability to perform well even in a soft and challenging market"). Q1 2026: defensive, conflict-driven, focus on cost and safety. Q2 2026: steadier, guidance absorbed a larger conflict hit. Q3 2026: the most confident tone of the year ("Simply put, this was an excellent quarter"), with specific 2027 signposts (Venezuela "triple-digit" millions of revenue, MPD aftermarket "could further double"), yet still cautious on the Gulf ("the environment has not normalized").

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY - High
The company beat on earnings in 5 of 7 recent quarters, and Q3 2026 earnings beat consensus by about 37%. Its Q1 2026 framing of a $30-50M first-half conflict hit was met (Q2 call: "within the $30 million-$50 million profit range"). The one miss - the second-half international recovery - was a macro miss, flagged early. There is a mild sandbagging pattern: guidance is set without recovery assumptions and then beaten on cost execution.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Working capital rose to 29.2% of revenue in Q3 (target 25%); the CFO blamed NCS consolidation (about 150bp) and timing. Watch whether this normalizes in Q4.
- MPD market saturation (about 70% of drillships already equipped); management argues 85-90% is achievable plus an aftermarket tail.
- Size of the Middle East rebound - answered only vaguely ("mid-single digit incremental").
- MPD capital sales make results lumpy - Q3's 700bp margin jump in the drilling segment partly reflects equipment deliveries that will not repeat every quarter.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- 🔴 Middle East (39% of Q3 revenue) remains disrupted; rig counts in key countries "trending lower" and tenders slipping (Q3 2026).
- 🔴 Customer concentration in Mexico; payment history is good but recent.
- 🔴 Open-market insider activity: 2 buys (12,000 shares) against 12 sells (178,370 shares).
- 🔴 Gross margin contracting; Q3 margin helped by lumpy MPD equipment sales.
- 🟢 Margins held above 20% through a regional war and contract roll-offs (Q1-Q3 2026).
- 🟢 Debt paid down with cash (2026-10-30); dividend raised 10% (Q4 2025).
- 🟢 Offshore wins with Equinor (2026-10-08), Total, Exxon, Seplat; first Venezuela revenue (Q3 2026) and the Eni Junín-5 campaign (2026-10-28).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- The language shifted from "activity recovery" to "contract portfolio stability" - management is selling resilience, not a cycle.
- Walking away from the Saudi turnkey contract "given the pricing levels in the market" signals price discipline over volume.
- Completions is "now our largest product line"; the company is tilting toward product and technology content (MPD, completions, NCS) and away from commodity services (Argentina pressure pumping sold).
- The Delaware redomestication (court-approved 2026-10-27) is a quiet capital-markets move: US domicile can widen the shareholder base and index eligibility.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT
Trajectory: **STABLE**, edging toward strengthening. Capital allocation is disciplined - debt reduction, a growing dividend, buybacks, small tuck-in deals and exits from low-return lines. The single most important thing for the director: this is a cash-yielding cyclical whose 2027 earnings depend on items management has dated but not contracted (Venezuela ramp, Middle East stabilization); the valuation case rests on the free cash flow staying near $500-580M, not on a recovery.

**Moat:** narrow - an installed base and switching costs in MPD, tubular running and completions, plus scale in international markets. Return on invested capital of about 13% and EBITDA margins rising from 2022 to 2026 argue it is stable rather than eroding, though gross margin has slipped. **Secular threat:** manageable - the energy transition is a long-dated pressure on oil services, but offshore and international drilling (Weatherford's core) is the most durable part of the cycle over a 3-5 year view. The cheapness looks like a cyclical fear-print (Middle East), not a structurally shrinking base.

# Mixue Group (2097.HK) - a deep dive on management and the setup (2026-11-09)

Source note: no earnings-call transcript exists for this name in FMP, and this run could not search the web (the session's search budget was exhausted). The dossier therefore works from the screener's financial trajectory, the first-half 2026 interim figures (HKEX filing 2026-08-27, as reproduced by stockanalysis.com and verified by this committee's own fact-checker on 2026-10-05), the live FMP quote and the stockanalysis.com listing page fetched today. No management quotes are given because none were available to verify; nothing below is a quotation.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
Mixue listed in Hong Kong in March 2025 as the world's largest freshly-made-drinks network (tea drinks and soft-serve ice cream sold at very low price points), with the economics of a supply-chain business: it earns most of its money selling ingredients, packaging and equipment to its franchisees rather than collecting royalties. The listing story was scale and growth - revenue went from RMB 10.4bn in 2021 to RMB 32.7bn in 2025 (about 34% a year over three years) and net profit from RMB 1.9bn to RMB 5.7bn.

The story changed with the first-half 2026 results (2026-08-27): revenue grew only about 2.3% (RMB 15.2bn against 14.9bn), net profit fell about 15% (RMB 2.30bn against 2.69bn), and gross margin slipped about 1.2 points to about 30.4% while selling and administrative costs rose sharply. The narrative has moved from "how fast can the network grow" to "is the network saturated and are franchisee economics being squeezed". The first dividend (about HKD 3.08 per share, ex-date 2026-10-05, paid 2026-11-06) is the first sign of a shift towards returning cash.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / perception | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| High-growth franchisor | Revenue +31.7% in 2025, but +2.3% in 1H 2026 | Growth has stalled, not merely slowed |
| High-return, asset-light model | ROE about 29%, ROIC about 27%, free-cash-flow margin about 16% (FY2025) | Corroborated for 2025; 2026 returns will be lower on falling profit |
| Fortress balance sheet | Net cash about RMB 19.7bn at 2026-06-30 (cash and investments RMB 19.9bn, debt RMB 0.23bn) - about RMB 49 per share after the dividend, roughly HKD 54 | Corroborated; net cash is about 30% of the market value |
| Stable gross margin | 31.2% in FY2025, about 30.4% in 1H 2026 | Mild erosion; one half-year only |
| Cheap on the screener (fair value HKD 1,072, 490% margin of safety) | Built on extrapolating 30%+ growth | Ignore - the growth input is no longer true |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Without transcripts, tone cannot be scored from management's words. The behavioural signal is mixed: management chose to start paying a dividend after a weak half, which reads as confidence in cash generation, but no buyback has been authorised despite the shares trading near their lows with net cash at about a third of the market value. Trajectory: stable, with the burden of proof now on the second-half 2026 numbers.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Mixue gives no formal numeric guidance. The screener's beat rate is 2 of 3 periods (67%). The prospectus-era growth was delivered in full in 2025; the 1H 2026 stall is the first period where the market's expectation was clearly missed (shares slid after the print, CNBC 2026-08-28). Reliability: medium.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
The open questions the market is pricing: same-store sales and franchisee profitability at 50,000+ stores; how much of the delivery-platform subsidy war is being absorbed by store owners; overseas store closures (South-East Asia); whether the cash pile will be returned. Sell-side remains constructive - stockanalysis.com shows a Buy consensus from 21 analysts with an average target of about 251 (currency shown ambiguously on that page; treated as indicative only).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: 1H 2026 revenue +2.3% after +32% in FY2025 - a near-halt in growth.
- Red: 1H 2026 net profit about -15%, gross margin about -1.2 points, operating costs growing far faster than revenue.
- Red: the share price fell from a 52-week high of HKD 464 to a low of HKD 157.7; it is about a third below its 200-day average.
- Green: net cash of about HKD 54 per share, no meaningful debt, Altman-Z of 9.4.
- Green: first dividend declared with the interim results and paid 2026-11-06.
- Green: even after the decline the business converts profit to cash at a high rate (trailing free cash flow about RMB 5.45bn).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The decision to begin a dividend in the same release as a profit decline suggests management sees the business as entering a cash-return phase rather than a reinvestment sprint. The absence of a buyback with the stock at about 10 times earnings is the most telling non-signal: either the board sees more downside in earnings, or it wants to preserve cash for overseas expansion and the coffee brand.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: stable - the balance sheet and cash conversion are intact, growth has paused. The single most important thing to weigh: whether the 1H 2026 margin decline is a one-off reinvestment and subsidy-war cost or the start of franchisee-economics erosion. The full-year 2026 results (around late March 2027) are the test.

Moat: scale-cost. Mixue's procurement and manufacturing scale lets it sell drinks at price points rivals struggle to match, and its returns (ROIC about 27%) show the advantage is real. It is narrow rather than wide because the product is easy to copy and the network has hit saturation in its home market; one half-year of margin decline is not yet enough to call the moat eroding, but it is the thing to watch. Secular threat: manageable - no structural force (automation, channel shift) threatens the terminal value of cheap freshly-made drinks; the risks are cyclical consumption weakness and competition. The cheapness looks more like a fear-print on a stalled grower than a value trap on a shrinking base, but it is not proven.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
