picks.bull_thesis: Super Micro is earning real money at a scale the share price does not reflect. Revenue for the quarter to 2026-09-30 was $19.9B, about four times the $5.0B of a year earlier, net income was $1.59B, and management guided fiscal 2027 (to June 2027) revenue to $72-82B on 2026-11-03, against an original quarterly outlook of $15B that it beat by about a third. The 11 analysts FMP tracks expect about $6.52 of earnings per share this fiscal year and about $6.94 next year; at $25.28 that is under 4 times this year's earnings and about 5.3 times the trailing twelve-month diluted earnings of $4.75. Even after a large haircut the stock is cheap on earnings. Three things could close the gap. First, cash: the cash conversion cycle (the days between paying suppliers and collecting from customers) reportedly improved from 149 to 97 days, deferred revenue (customer prepayments) rose by about $3.1B in the quarter, and the moment growth slows the $24.7B of inventory and receivables starts releasing cash rather than absorbing it. Second, mix: enterprise and CPU servers, storage, and the DCBBS data-center kit (cooling, power, networking, software sold around the servers) carry better margins; gross margin recovered from 6.3% in the December 2025 quarter to 12.7% now, and management says DCBBS margins are 'most of the time more than 20%' (2026-05-05). Third, the legal overhang: the company says it is neither a defendant nor a target of the March 2026 indictment and that the entity in the 2026-11-12 reports was 'never a customer'; if no corporate charge follows, a governance discount of this size has room to narrow. Conditions: revenue lands inside the $72-82B range, gross margin holds above 10%, operating cash flow turns positive within two to three quarters, and no corporate export charge.

Cash first: trailing twelve-month free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was about -$6.5B while trailing net income was about $3.6B, and operating cash flow was still negative (about -$434M) in the record quarter despite $3.1B of prepayments. Inventory rose from $12.9B to $15.1B and receivables from $6.1B to $9.7B in one quarter; net debt swung from about $0.84B of net cash to about $1.75B of net debt. Concentration: one customer was about 44% of revenue and 49% of receivables in the quarter, after being 63% two quarters earlier - a single counterparty's capital-spending plan sets Super Micro's year. Cycle: consensus earnings are flat from fiscal 2027 (about $6.52) to fiscal 2029 (about $6.97), so even the Street sees this year as a plateau, and the whole demand case rests on one shared driver, AI capital spending, that is now being questioned (management addressed 'AI capital expenditure efficiency' concerns itself on 2026-11-03; server peers Dell and HPE sold off with it in November). Margin: the company has no pricing power - 'we can grow much faster if we accept lower margin business' (2026-05-05) - and the 17.6% gross margin of the June quarter fell back to 12.7%, with management admitting one-offs. Governance: a co-founder and two others were charged in March 2026 over about $2.5B of servers allegedly diverted to China; on 2026-11-12 reports of further Justice Department inquiries touching the company's hardware cut the stock about 11%, shareholder-lawsuit solicitations followed, and the chief financial officer changed around the same time. Where we disagree with the market: we think the right value is around $30, close to today's price rather than the $42 consensus target, because the discount for cash conversion, a 44% customer and the legal inquiry is earned, not a mispricing - and a single good cash-flow quarter would change that.
picks.valley_of_death: The risky window is the next three to nine months. (1) Working capital: guidance implies revenue of $72-82B for the year, which at the current conversion cycle needs billions more of inventory and receivables; with net debt already about $1.75B and a $1.8B working-capital facility, another round of debt, factoring or preferred-style funding is plausible if prepayments slow. (2) Legal: the Justice Department matter reported on 2026-11-12 has no timetable; any subpoena disclosure in the next 10-Q, a corporate charge, or export-licence restrictions would hit both the stock and customers' willingness to buy. (3) Concentration: one customer with about 49% of receivables means a single delayed payment or order push-out (the company has had three such push-outs in five quarters) can swing a quarter by billions. (4) Sector: the AI-hardware group has fallen about a third in a month on spending-efficiency worries; a capital-spending pause by large buyers would hit the most leveraged assembler hardest. (5) Supply: management says component shortages (GPUs, memory) cap shipments, which can push revenue between quarters again.
picks.positioning_washout: There is no forced-selling event of the classic kind (no index deletion, dividend cut or lock-up expiry). The selling so far has been a sector-wide de-rating of AI hardware from early October 2026 (Dell and HPE fell with it) followed by company-specific selling on the 2026-11-12 legal reports. Retail and momentum holders are a large part of the register for this name and shareholder-lawsuit solicitations (2026-11-13, 2026-11-16) tend to coincide with capitulation, but the 52-week low of $19.48 shows there is room below. Insiders have been sellers (about 600,000 shares sold in the open market against a 1,715-share buy). We do not name a forced-selling price level; the wait is for proof, not for a price.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for proof: we buy once the second-quarter fiscal 2027 report (expected early February 2027) shows operating cash flow at or above zero with no corporate legal escalation. The thesis is in doubt until that test passes. Super Micro is growing faster than any hardware peer - $19.9B of revenue in the September 2026 quarter, about four times a year earlier, and a fiscal 2027 guide of $72-82B - and at $25.28 it trades under 4 times this year's consensus earnings. But the profits are not turning into cash (trailing free cash flow about -$6.5B), about 44% of revenue comes from one customer, the company has no pricing power (gross margin 12.7% in a boom quarter), shareholders were diluted about 13% in a year, and reports on 2026-11-12 of further Justice Department inquiries widened the export-control cloud that began with the March 2026 indictment of a co-founder. Our base value of about $30 (fiscal 2027 consensus earnings cut about 30% for cash quality and concentration, at 6.5 times) is only modestly above the price; the downside to about $12 in an AI-spending pause is larger than the upside to base, and only the bull case near $58 makes the risk worth it. The guidance raise has already happened and did not lift the stock, so it is spent news and neither helps nor hurts our view. The macro backdrop, which rewards cash flow over long-dated stories, works against a company funding growth with debt, but that is context, not the reason for waiting. Conviction is low: we would not own it until the cash arrives, and even then the moat is thin.
picks.forcing_function: The catalyst is the second-quarter fiscal 2027 report, expected around early February 2027 (quiet period begins 2026-12-11). A quarter that shows positive operating cash flow while revenue stays near the $72-82B annual path, with no legal escalation in the 10-Q, would force the market to start treating reported earnings as cash and re-rate toward our $30 base value and beyond. A buyback authorisation would be the clearest signal management believes the cash is real; none has been announced. The Justice Department matter has no date and cannot be the forcing function.

# Super Micro Computer (SMCI) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Live price used: $25.28 (NASDAQ, US dollars, FMP quote, 2026-11-16 intraday, down about 6% on the day and roughly 30% over the past month). Sources: five earnings-call transcripts (2025-11-04, 2026-02-03, 2026-05-05, 2026-08-11, 2026-11-03), the screener's financial block, FMP quarterly statements (10-Q for the quarter to 2026-09-30, filed 2026-11-05) and dated FMP news.*

**The takeaway first.** Super Micro is growing faster than almost any hardware company in the world - revenue for the quarter to September 2026 was $19.9B, about four times the $5.0B of a year earlier - and on paper the stock trades near 4 times this fiscal year's consensus earnings. But three things the transcripts and filings reveal keep this from being clean value: the profits are not turning into cash (trailing twelve-month free cash flow, the cash left after running and investing in the business, was about -$6.5B), one customer is now about 44% of revenue, and the legal cloud over China exports has widened from three indicted individuals (March 2026) to a reported Justice Department inquiry touching the company's hardware (reported 2026-11-12). Management's revenue promises have been lumpy and its margin promises have been reset more than once.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **November 2025 (Q1 FY26):** a defensive opener. Revenue of $5.0B missed the $6-7B guide; management blamed "last-minute configuration upgrade" by a customer and pointed to "more than $13 billion in back orders" for Blackwell Ultra racks. The full-year promise was "at least $36 billion." Gross margin was openly sacrificed: "Some large-scale deals have pressure margin in the near term."
- **February 2026 (Q2 FY26):** the catch-up quarter. Revenue of $12.7B (up 123% year on year) included about $1.5B pushed from the prior quarter. The full-year guide went back up to "at least $40 billion." A new story arrived: DCBBS (Data Center Building Block Solutions - selling the whole data-center kit of cooling, power, networking and software around the servers) was pitched as the path to higher margins. Margin hit a low of 6.4% (non-GAAP) because one customer was 63% of revenue.
- **May 2026 (Q3 FY26):** the call opened with legal damage control - "Super Micro is not a defendant nor a target" - after the March 2026 indictment of a co-founder and two others for allegedly diverting about $2.5B of AI servers to China. Revenue of $10.2B missed the "at least $12.3 billion" guide ("customer site readiness delay"), but gross margin recovered to 10.1%.
- **August 2026 (Q4 FY26):** "over $60 billion in new orders," a 17.6% non-GAAP gross margin that management itself said had "few one-time positive contributions," and a $5.6B June financing.
- **November 2026 (Q1 FY27):** a new chief financial officer (Mark Long, replacing David Weigand). Record $19.9B revenue against an original $15B outlook, full-year FY27 revenue guided to $72-82B, gross margin back down to 12.7%. Management for the first time addressed "AI capital expenditure efficiency and return on investment" concerns directly.

**What shifted:** the story moved from "first-to-market GPU racks" toward "total data-center solution company" with software and services. What quietly faded: the old 14-17% long-term gross-margin target ("The market has changed," Weigand, 2025-11-04) and any disclosure of backlog size ("we don't give out our backlog number," 2026-05-05).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "At least $36B" then "at least $40B" for FY26 (2025-11-04, 2026-02-03) | FY26 revenue $39.06B | Beat the first promise, just missed the raised one |
| "At least $12.3B" for Q3 FY26 (2026-02-03) | $10.24B | Miss (about 17% short) |
| "Sustainable double-digit gross margin" (2026-05-05 onward) | Gross margin by quarter: 9.3%, 6.3%, 9.9%, 17.5%, 12.7% (GAAP, from FMP) | Double digits only in the last two quarters, one helped by one-offs |
| "We continue to make more total profit every quarter" (Liang, 2025-11-04) | Net income $168M, $401M, $483M, $1,178M, $1,594M over the last five quarters | Delivered |
| "We have adequate capital"; working-capital efficiency "has gone up" (2026-02-03, 2026-11-03) | Operating cash flow about -$434M in Q1 FY27 even with a $3.1B rise in deferred revenue (customer prepayments); inventory $15.1B and receivables $9.7B at 2026-09-30, up from $12.9B and $6.1B one quarter earlier | Not corroborated - growth is consuming all the cash and more |
| "Customer diversification" (every call since 2026-02) | Largest customer 63% of revenue (Q2 FY26), 27% (Q3), about 44% of revenue and 49% of receivables in Q1 FY27 (10-Q, as reported 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-10) | Contradicted |
| DCBBS "at least double-digit" share of profit by end of calendar 2026, "20% should be not far away" | Never disclosed as a number ("We didn't give that percentage out," 2026-05-05) | Unverifiable |
| "We don't have any plans to consider equity raises" (2026-11-03) | Diluted share count rose from 663M (Q1 FY26) to 749M (Q1 FY27), about +13%; $4.23B of preferred stock now sits on the balance sheet | Dilution has already happened |

Balance sheet at 2026-09-30: cash $6.90B, borrowings $8.65B, so net debt (borrowings minus cash, no leases) about $1.75B - a swing from about $0.84B of net cash one quarter earlier.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising on demand, defensive on governance and cash.** Revenue language grew steadily bolder - from "depending on the supply and production capability readiness" (2025-11-04) to "$72 billion to $82 billion becomes very, very conservative" (2026-11-03). Margin language moved from apologetic ("double-digit gross margin still in our plan, it just take a little bit longer," 2025-11-04) to triumphant (17.6% in 2026-08) and back to measured. Governance language is purely defensive: "the alleged actions of a few individuals do not define us" (2026-05-05). Guidance specificity has improved under the new CFO (ranges instead of "at least" floors), which is a modest positive.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Quarterly revenue guidance has missed (Q1 FY26, Q3 FY26), beaten (Q2 FY26 with shifted revenue, Q1 FY27) and slipped in turn, consistent with the screener's 4 of 7 quarters beaten (57%). Every miss was explained as a timing shift by a customer, and some did return the following quarter - but the pattern means any single quarter's guide is unreliable. No sandbagging pattern; rather the opposite, a habit of optimistic floors. **Reliability: Low to Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Backlog size** - asked on 2025-11-04 and 2026-05-05; refused both times.
- **Customer concentration** - "was that a previous 10% customer?" (KeyBanc, 2026-02-03): "I'll just refer you to the 10-Ks and Qs."
- **Cash and free cash flow** - "the revenue coming in is at a 0% contribution margin" (KeyBanc, 2025-11-04); answered with history, not numbers.
- **DCBBS profit share** - asked repeatedly, never quantified.
- **Export-control remediation cost** - "I don't want to add any more to that" (Weigand, 2026-05-05).
- **Unit growth versus price pass-through** - the CFO admitted on 2026-11-03 that average selling prices are "really driven by the cost of key components," so some of the headline growth is inflation in component costs passed through, not more racks.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- March 2026: a co-founder and two others charged with diverting about $2.5B of AI servers to China; on 2026-11-12 Semafor reported further Justice Department inquiries touching the company's hardware (stock down about 11% that day; shareholder-lawsuit solicitations followed 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-16). The company says the entity named, Megaspeed, was "never a customer."
- Cash: trailing free cash flow about -$6.5B while trailing earnings were about $3.6B. Earnings are running well ahead of cash.
- Concentration: about 44% of Q1 FY27 revenue and 49% of receivables from one customer.
- Dilution: about 13% more diluted shares in a year plus $4.23B of preferred stock.
- Insiders: 8 open-market sales totalling about 600,000 shares against one small buy (1,715 shares).
- CFO change announced around the Q1 FY27 call, in the middle of a legal inquiry.
- History (pre-transcript, widely reported): the 2024 auditor resignation and late annual filing.

Green flags:
- Revenue and profit genuinely compounding: net income up nearly tenfold year on year in Q1 FY27.
- Cash conversion cycle reportedly improved from 149 to 97 days (third-party analysis, 2026-11-07), and customer prepayments now fund part of the build.
- Software and services revenue small but growing ($34M to $46M per quarter, 2026-05-05).
- Enterprise and CPU server mix rising, which carries better margins.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "We have a choice to select healthy customers" (2026-11-03) - a new emphasis on credit quality of customers, implicitly acknowledging receivable risk.
- "We can grow much faster if we accept lower margin business" (2026-05-05) - management openly frames margin as a dial it trades for revenue, which means the gross margin is not protected by a moat.
- The CFO transition: the new CFO answered the capital-structure questions and opened the door to debt markets; equity raises were ruled out "at this point" only.
- Concern about "AI capital expenditure efficiency" was raised by management unprompted on 2026-11-03 - a sign the buy side is already asking.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning** - from a GPU-rack assembler toward a broader data-center supplier, with demand strengthening but governance and cash quality weakening at the same time.

**The single most important thing to weigh:** the cheap earnings multiple is only real if the earnings become cash. Until a quarter shows operating cash flow turning positive while revenue still grows, the market is right to discount reported earnings, and the legal inquiry adds a tail risk (loss of export privileges or a corporate charge) that cannot be sized from the outside.

**Moat:** none of substance. Super Micro's edge is speed to market and manufacturing scale in assembly, but gross margin of 10-13% in a peak-demand year, below its own former 14-17% target, shows customers and suppliers capture the value; management itself says big buyers have "pricing leverage." Return on invested capital of about 14% is respectable only because growth is extreme. **Secular threat:** material, not terminal - standardised reference racks from Nvidia and the Taiwanese contract manufacturers (Quanta, Wiwynn, Foxconn) commoditise rack integration over time, and demand rests on one shared driver, AI capital spending. The cheapness is partly a fear-print (legal) and partly a peak-cycle discount; it is not a shrinking business, but it is not a durable franchise either.

Management credibility 2 of 5 · trajectory turning · no real moat · moat trend eroding · structural threat material.

picks.bull_thesis:
Evolution is the company behind live casino: it films real dealers at real tables in 27 studios and streams those games to the online casinos that license them, and it owns slot-game studios (NetEnt, Red Tiger, Big Time Gaming, Nolimit City) alongside. The bull case is that a business with almost no rival at its scale is priced like an ordinary one, and that the growth stall is over.

The money is exceptional. Over the twelve months to September 2026 Evolution generated about EUR 1.21bn of free cash flow (cash left after running and reinvesting in the business) on roughly EUR 2.12bn of revenue, spends about 4% of revenue on capital investment, earns a 23-27% return on invested capital and carries net cash of about EUR 550m. At 837 kronor the shares trade at roughly 11.4 times enterprise value to free cash flow and 9.8 times enterprise value to EBITDA (operating cash profit), per FMP's trailing figures.

And growth has turned. The third quarter of 2026 (reported 23 October 2026) was the first in two years where every region grew on the quarter; revenue rose 3.7% year-on-year, North America 13.6%, Latin America 23.1%, Africa 23.7%. The slot studios grew 10.1% after 14% in the second quarter, so the line the market wrote off for three years is now the fastest-growing in the group. Management cleared the UK licence review and the Galaxy Gaming deal in July 2026, and the Hasbro 'Game Night' show, billed as 'the largest game show in the history of online casino', launches imminently.

The buyback does the rest. 16.9m shares were retired in the first nine months of 2026, so even flat profits deliver mid-single-digit earnings-per-share growth; adjusted EPS was up about 7.5% in the third quarter. If Brazil's ban lapses (the provisional measure needs Congress within 120 days) and growth holds at mid-single digits, a 13 times profit multiple on the live business is still below where the listed operators trade, and the shares are worth well over 1,100 kronor.

Conditions: growth sustains at least low single digits through 2027; margin holds near 66%; Brazil reopens or its players migrate to licensed offshore operators that still buy Evolution's content.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case is that Evolution's earnings base is permanently smaller and riskier than its margins suggest, and that at 837 kronor, up about 60% from the 515-kronor low, the market has already paid for the recovery.

Half of revenue comes from players outside regulated markets. The company's own estimate has held at 49% regulated for three quarters, and on 23 October 2026 the chief executive refused to say how much revenue comes from markets regulators call prohibited ('No, I won't comment on that'). Brazil has now shown that even a regulated market can disappear in two weeks: a provisional measure signed 25 September 2026 shut online casino from 6 October 2026, and Evolution closed its studio. At about 9% of revenue (a JP Morgan estimate), losing Brazil wipes out more than two years of the group's current growth rate.

Europe, the largest region, still fell 4.7% year-on-year in the third quarter; management's own verdict was 'It's not exciting and we should do better.' The October 2025 claim that Europe had 'a new foundation for growth' was followed by two further declines. Asia remains a cat-and-mouse fight with content pirates. Headcount rose 8.1% against revenue up 3.7%, so the 66% margin target needs a strong fourth quarter at precisely the moment Brazilian revenue drops out; the year-to-date margin is 65.7%.

The support under the shares is also weakening. The buyback, which was absorbing up to a quarter of daily volume, will run 'at a somewhat lower pace' in the fourth quarter and first quarter, and net cash has fallen from EUR 1.07bn in June to about EUR 550m. Earnings delivery is poor: one beat in seven quarters, and fiscal-2025 EPS fell 9.8%.

What would confirm the bear: a fourth-quarter margin below 66%, Congress converting the Brazil measure into law by late January 2027, or Europe declining again in the year-end report due in early February 2027.
picks.consensus_delta:
Where we disagree with the market is now small. The rally from 515 to about 840 kronor priced in exactly what the third quarter of 2026 delivered - a return to growth - and the shares barely moved on the 23 October report (the quote was 837 on 26 October 2026, against 811 a week earlier). Pre-report consensus had revenue near EUR 530m for the quarter (a Yahoo Finance snapshot dated 25 September 2026); the EUR 526.1m print was a slight miss.

Our residual disagreements run both ways. In the bulls' favour: the slot studios, growing double digits two quarters in a row, are still valued by most of the street as an impaired asset, which we put at about 100 kronor a share of hidden value. Against the bulls: the street's habit is to treat Brazil like India in 2025, a temporary wobble that stabilises, but the chief executive himself said on 23 October that 'this situation is new' - an abrupt ban on a market whose operators paid for five-year licences. And the 49% regulated share has not moved in three quarters, so the half of revenue that drives the discount is no closer to resolution.
picks.valley_of_death:
The risky window (the months just ahead) is about earnings, not survival: Evolution has net cash, no maturity wall and an Altman Z (a solvency score) of about 8.

Three things can hurt the shares before February 2027. First, Brazil: the fourth quarter of 2026 will show the revenue hole, and Congress must decide within 120 days of the 25 September measure (roughly late January 2027) whether the ban becomes law. Second, the 66% margin target needs a fourth quarter of about 66.5% while Brazil revenue drops out and headcount runs 8% higher; a miss in the year-end report (early February 2027) would break the one guidance line management has always held. Third, the buyback is slowing ('somewhat lower pace' in Q4 and Q1), so the price-insensitive bid that helped the rally weakens just as the news flow turns. A sector-wide sell-off in iGaming suppliers on Brazilian or European regulatory headlines is the plausible route to our 720-kronor level.
picks.positioning_washout: The forced-selling pressure in this name already ran its course: income funds left when the dividend (EUR 572m in 2025) was replaced by buybacks in 2026, which helped push the shares to 515 kronor. The current marginal buyer is the company itself, and it is buying less: the chief financial officer said on 23 October 2026 the pace will be 'somewhat lower than in Q3' to match cash generation, after net cash fell to about EUR 550m. There is no index deletion, lock-up or spin-off ahead. A return to our entry level would therefore have to come from a sector-wide de-rating of gaming suppliers on regulatory news (Brazil, European channelisation), not from forced sellers.
picks.moderator_conclusion:
Wait for a better price: we buy near 720 kronor, which a sector-wide sell-off in gaming suppliers on Brazilian or European regulatory news could deliver.

The thesis holds. Evolution is an excellent business: about EUR 1.2bn of free cash flow a year on EUR 2.1bn of revenue, a 66% operating cash margin, net cash, and a scale and licensing position no rival matches. The third quarter of 2026, reported on 23 October 2026, was the best news in two years - revenue up 3.7% year-on-year with every region growing on the quarter - and it is enough for us to stop calling the moat eroding; we now see a narrow but real moat that is holding steady.

But the price already reflects it. At 837 kronor our base-case fair value of about 870 kronor is only a few percent higher, while the adverse case of about 550 kronor, built on a permanent Brazil loss and continued European erosion, is a third lower. In today's market backdrop (growth and inflation both running hot) a buy needs at least a 20% discount to fair value, and this is nowhere close. The new Brazilian ban, in force since 6 October 2026, adds a fresh regulatory risk exactly as the old ones were cleared, and the buyback that supported the shares is slowing.

So this stays on the watchlist with the same conviction as last week's committee record (3 of 5). The level that works is 720 kronor, a 20% discount to fair value and well above the adverse case; a broad de-rating of gaming suppliers on regulatory headlines is the realistic way there. What would change our mind sooner: Congress letting the Brazilian measure lapse, or a fourth-quarter report in early February 2027 that shows growth holding with Brazil excluded and the margin at 66% or better.
picks.forcing_function: No dated event forces a re-rating. The UK settlement and the Galaxy exit fired in July 2026. Ahead lie a calendar, not a catalyst: the Brazilian Congress decision on the provisional ban (due roughly late January 2027), and the year-end report in early February 2027, which carries the 2027 margin target. The open-ended mechanisms - the buyback retiring 4-5% of shares a year and the Playtech litigation, which management has said will take 'years' - compound value slowly but do not time it.

# Evolution AB (EVO.ST) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 26 October 2026. Five calls reviewed: third quarter 2025 (23 Oct 2025), fourth quarter 2025 (5 Feb 2026), first quarter 2026 (22 Apr 2026), second quarter 2026 (17 Jul 2026) and third quarter 2026 (23 Oct 2026). Live price used: 837.00 Swedish kronor (SEK) on Nasdaq Stockholm, FMP quote of 26 October 2026. Company figures are in euros (EUR).

The takeaway: management is candid and the money is real, and the third quarter of 2026 is the first quarter in two years where every region grew sequentially. But growth is still only low single digits, and a new and sudden Brazilian ban on online gambling (in force since 6 October 2026) has replaced the old United Kingdom and Galaxy Gaming overhangs with a fresh one. The franchise is not shrinking any more; it is also not yet growing in a way that justifies paying up.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Third quarter 2025 (23 Oct 2025): defence.** The call opened with Asia "taking the bull by the horns": cyber-crime (pirated streams of Evolution's tables) plus self-inflicted damage - "we did too much, causing loss in revenue" with anti-piracy measures. Expectations were deliberately set low.
- **Fourth quarter 2025 (5 Feb 2026): stabilisation, Europe still falling.** Revenue EUR 540m, down 3.7% year-on-year; full-year 2025 EBITDA margin (operating cash profit as a share of revenue) 66.1%, "just within" the 66-68% range. Story shifted to product (Ice Fishing, crash games) and the slot studios' "great potential".
- **First and second quarter 2026: the clean-up year.** The dividend was replaced with a EUR 2bn buyback; the UK Gambling Commission review was settled (GBP 4.75m, disclosed 17 Jul 2026); the Galaxy Gaming deal was walked away from (terminated 21 Jul 2026). Revenue returned to sequential growth (+0.9% in the second quarter) but management refused to call an inflection: "Are we at an inflection point? It's too early to say."
- **Third quarter 2026 (23 Oct 2026): "uneventful, which I believe is something good".** Revenue EUR 526.1m, +3.7% year-on-year and +1.6% on the quarter; "all regions contributed to growth for the first time since 2024". Live (the dealer-streamed games, roughly 85% of revenue) +2.6% year-on-year; RNG (random-number-generator slot games) +10.1%, a second double-digit quarter. The new theme is Brazil: a provisional presidential measure banning online betting and casino took effect in early October, and Evolution has closed its São Paulo studio "ready to reopen on short notice".

What was quietly dropped: the full-year 66-68% margin range has become a single 66% target. What was added: an explicit regulated-share disclosure (49% of revenue from players in regulated markets, unchanged across three quarters) and an "AI dealer" question that management treats as a complement, not a threat.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Return to positive growth" (Q3 2026) | Revenue EUR 526.1m vs ~EUR 507m a year earlier (+3.7%); trailing twelve months (TTM) now about EUR 2.12bn vs EUR 2.21bn in fiscal 2024 | Matches, but from a lowered base; fiscal 2025 revenue fell 4.3% |
| 66% margin target "remains" | Q3 adjusted EBITDA 65.8%; year-to-date 65.7% (Q1 65.4%, Q2 65.9%) | Delivered within rounding, but needs Q4 at about 66.5% while Brazil revenue disappears |
| "Very strong cash flow" | Q3 operating cash flow after investment EUR 334.1m; rolling cash conversion 85%; TTM free cash flow EUR 1.21bn (FMP) on capex of about 4.2% of revenue | Fully corroborated - the strongest part of the file |
| Buyback creates per-share value | 16.9m shares repurchased year-to-date to 30 Sep 2026; Q3 adjusted EPS (earnings per share) up about 7.5% vs +2.4% reported | Corroborated; but pace will be "somewhat lower" in Q4 and Q1 |
| Fortress balance sheet | Cash EUR 656.4m vs total debt about EUR 110m (net cash about EUR 550m, down from EUR 1.07bn in June because of the buyback) | True but thinner; roughly EUR 0.9bn of accrued tax sat against the cash in June |
| "All our revenues are regulated" | Only 49% comes from players in regulated jurisdictions, by the company's own estimate | Definitional; the economically relevant number is 49% |

Earnings delivery is weak by the screener's measure: one beat in the last seven quarters (14%), and EPS fell 9.8% in fiscal 2025. TTM diluted EPS is EUR 5.37, latest quarter +4% year-on-year.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, edging up.** October 2025 was apologetic ("keep expectations low"); February 2026 matter-of-fact ("the market was not in favor during Q4. That's a fact"); July 2026 guarded ("too early to say"); October 2026 calm and slightly self-critical about Europe ("It's not exciting and we should do better"). Guidance has become less specific over time: no regional or growth guidance, only the margin target. On Brazil the chief executive explicitly declined to forecast: "we don't want to speculate about the final outcome."

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The one quantified promise - the margin range - has been met at its floor every year (66.1% in 2025; 65.7% year-to-date in 2026). Qualitative promises have a mixed record: the October 2025 claim of "a new foundation for growth" in Europe was followed by two further European declines; the Asia recovery has been "one small step forward" at a time. The low beat rate fits a company that does not guide revenue rather than one that sandbags. Reliability: **Medium**.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Brazil (23 Oct 2026, three separate analysts):** will Brazilian revenue go to zero? Management would not say. JP Morgan has estimated Brazil at about 9% of revenue (reported in September 2026 press coverage); the provisional measure needs Congress within 120 days to become permanent.
- **Revenue from prohibited markets (Deutsche Bank, 23 Oct 2026):** "No, I won't comment on that." This is the most persistent non-answer in the file.
- **Playtech / Black Cube litigation:** no settlement signal - "a full lawsuit... that will continue".
- **Variable cost base and net-cash policy (Kepler):** answered with adjectives, not numbers.
- **AI live dealers (BofA):** "a complement. I don't think that it will take over Live."

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 Brazil ban (in force 6 Oct 2026) removes a fast-growing LatAm market overnight; the studio is closed.
🔴 Europe still -4.7% year-on-year in Q3 2026, the largest region; regulatory channelisation (the share of play that stays in licensed markets) remains weak.
🔴 Refusal to size revenue from markets that regulators call prohibited (23 Oct 2026).
🔴 Net cash halved since June as buybacks outran free cash flow; pace now slowing.
🟢 All regions grew sequentially in Q3 2026 for the first time since 2024; North America +13.6%, LatAm +23.1% (pre-Brazil), Africa +23.7% year-on-year.
🟢 RNG slots double-digit growth two quarters running (+14% Q2, +10.1% Q3).
🟢 UK settlement and Galaxy exit cleared in July 2026; Hasbro "Game Night" launch imminent.
🟢 Cash conversion 85%, capex about 4% of revenue, return on invested capital about 23-27%.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- Headcount up 8.1% year-on-year in Q3 2026 against revenue up 3.7%: management says "don't read too much into" it, but it is an investment-for-growth signal and a margin risk at the same time.
- The buyback language moved from "maximum permitted rate" (July) to "adjust the pace to align more closely with cash generation" (October) - the marginal buyer of the shares is stepping back.
- Brazil is framed as "populistic agenda" overriding regulation - management is reading the ban as political and potentially reversible after the 25 October 2026 runoff, which we could not verify.
- The regulated-share disclosure has stuck at 49% for three quarters: no progress on the half of revenue that carries the regulatory risk.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: **STABLE**. Capital allocation is shareholder-aligned (all free cash flow returned via buyback, no debt, a bolt-on studio bought from a retreating rival), and the business has stopped shrinking.

The single thing to weigh before sizing: about half of revenue comes from players outside regulated markets, and Brazil just showed that a regulated market can also switch off in a fortnight. The cash flows are superb today; the uncertainty is how many of them are permanent.

Moat: scale-cost plus regulatory-licence. Twenty-seven studios, a licence footprint no rival matches, a rival abandoning Argentina to Evolution, and the Hasbro licence won from a 20-year incumbent. Width: margins held at about 66% and TTM return on invested capital about 27% (FMP) - not the profile of a collapsing moat - but revenue growth is only now turning positive and Europe still shrinks. That is a **narrow but real moat, now stable** rather than eroding: the October 2026 quarter removed the "measurably shrinking" evidence of the last two years, without yet proving widening.

Secular threat: regulatory channelisation of the unregulated half (material, not terminal); AI-generated dealers (manageable - management treats it as a product extension). The low multiple looks mostly like a fear-print on regulatory risk, not a structurally shrinking base, but the base is not growing fast enough to make the discount compelling.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat material.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# NORION.ST - Norion Bank AB (formerly Collector Bank) - forensic dossier, 2026-11-16

Source note: no earnings-call transcript is available (FMP has none for this listing). This dossier works from the third-quarter 2026 interim report (published 2026-10-22, read through the Inderes reprint of the bank's release), the 2026-08-03 non-performing-loan sale release, the FMP quarterly balance sheets to 2026-09-30, and the live FMP quote (SEK 69.80, 2026-11-16, Nasdaq Stockholm). There are no management quotes from a call, so none are given.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Norion is a Swedish niche bank: corporate and real-estate lending, consumer credit and payments, funded mostly by retail deposits. The 2025-26 story has three threads. First, an earnings dip: nine-month 2026 net profit of SEK 931 million is down from SEK 1,121 million a year earlier, mostly from one-off costs earlier in the year (adjusted nine-month profit SEK 1,040 million). Second, a sharp third-quarter recovery: net profit SEK 397 million (SEK 340 million a year earlier), earnings per share SEK 2.18 (SEK 1.70), return on equity 16.4%, cost-to-income 29.6%, credit losses steady at 1.6% of loans, loan book up 16% year on year to SEK 56.9 billion. Third, a capital-recycling push: about SEK 1 billion of buybacks in nine months (about 17 million shares, to be cancelled - approved at the 2026-10-20 extraordinary meeting), the sale of a SEK 6.2 billion gross non-performing-loan portfolio to Brocc Finance (announced 2026-08-03, price about SEK 2.6 billion against SEK 2.5 billion book), and two asset-manager purchases (Consensus, then Strand, completed 2026-08-17) forming a new wealth arm.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Lending growth is back | Loans SEK 56.9bn vs 49.1bn a year earlier (+16%); third-quarter income SEK 1,042m vs 919m | Matches |
| Profitability has recovered | Q3 return on equity 16.4%; nine months only 12.6% (adjusted 14.1%) | One strong quarter; the nine-month figure is the honest base |
| Credit is under control | Credit-loss level 1.6% (1.7%) | Stable, but high in absolute terms - this is a high-yield lender |
| The loan sale strengthens capital | Expected +1.5 points on the core capital ratio and about SEK 900m extra surplus capital; costs about SEK 100m of operating profit over 12 months | Plausible; completion not yet confirmed as of 2026-11-16 |
| Capital is ample | Core (CET1) capital ratio 13.1%, down from 16.1% a year earlier; total capital 16.1% (18.1%) | Buybacks and growth have used up the cushion; the next buyback depends on the loan sale closing |

Balance-sheet check (FMP, 2026-09-30): total equity SEK 9,370m, intangibles SEK 372m, issued debt SEK 3,801m. The separate hybrid (additional tier 1) line of SEK 793m seen at 2026-06-30 is gone from equity and issued debt rose by about SEK 906m; retained earnings moved from SEK 9,061m to SEK 9,222m, which is consistent with profit less buybacks and no hybrid capital left inside equity. Common tangible equity is therefore about SEK 9,000m, about SEK 52 per share on the roughly 172.8 million shares outstanding net of repurchased shares (FMP market value SEK 12.06bn at SEK 69.80).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

No transcript, so tone can only be read from actions: management is confident enough to keep returning capital (a further buyback of up to SEK 500m announced 2026-10-22) but it has made that buyback conditional on the loan sale closing, the share cancellation and supervisor approval - a sign that capital is now the binding constraint. Rating: stable.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The bank gives financial targets rather than earnings guidance. The loan-sale effects were quantified in advance (capital +1.5 points, profit -SEK 100m), which is checkable at the fourth-quarter report. Delivery history from the screener: beat in 3 of the last 7 quarters - mixed.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Questions an analyst should press: how much of the third-quarter profit is repeatable after the loan sale removes about SEK 100m a year of income; what the real-estate book's stage-2 and stage-3 trends look like; how the core capital ratio of 13.1% sits against the requirement plus the 200-400 basis-point management buffer; and what the payback on the asset-manager purchases is. No analyst price targets could be sourced (FMP has no coverage for this listing).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Green: loan growth +16%; third-quarter return on equity 16.4%; cost-to-income under 30%; NPL sale above book value; share count down by about 8-9% through buybacks.
Red: core capital ratio down 3 points in a year; nine-month profit down 17%; credit losses at 1.6% of loans leave little room for a real-estate downturn; the wealth arm is a new line of business with no track record; the next buyback is conditional.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The shift of hybrid capital out of equity in the third quarter means the reported equity figure is now cleanly common equity - the earlier uncertainty about book value per share (about SEK 2-4) is resolved in the bank's favour. The capital ratio falling while buybacks continue says the bank is running its capital tighter, which lifts returns on equity but thins the cushion against credit losses.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

A competent, shareholder-friendly lender that is recycling capital hard: buybacks, a loan sale above book, small fee-business purchases. The trajectory is stable to improving on the third quarter. The single most important thing to weigh: the shares at SEK 69.80 trade at about 1.34 times common tangible book of about SEK 52, which already prices a sustained return on tangible equity of about 14% - the improvement is in the price.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Haier Smart Home (6690.HK) — a deep dive on management and the setup
*As of 9 November 2026. Prices in Hong Kong dollars (HK$) for the H-share listing 6690.HK; financials reported in renminbi (RMB). HK$1 = RMB 0.8504 (FMP, 9 November 2026).*

**Source note.** No earnings-call transcript was bundled with this review, and FMP has none for this listing. A fresh web search was not available for this run, so the evidence here is: FMP's quarterly income, balance-sheet and cash-flow statements through 30 September 2026; the screener's multi-year trajectory; and dated Hong Kong news headlines (AASTOCKS) on the third-quarter results, broker target changes and buybacks. No management quotes appear below because none could be sourced. We have not made any up.

## 1. Narrative arc
Haier is the world's largest white-goods group (fridges, washers, air conditioners) across its own brand, GE Appliances in the US, Fisher & Paykel and Candy. From 2021 to 2025 it compounded steadily. Revenue grew from RMB 227.6 billion to RMB 302.4 billion (about 7.5% a year) and net income from RMB 13.1 billion to RMB 19.6 billion (about 10% a year). The story was "premiumisation plus global share gains plus digital cost cuts", and the numbers backed it.

2026 broke that rhythm. China's appliance trade-in subsidy, which pulled demand forward through 2025, has faded. US air-conditioner inventory is high. The story has moved from growth to defence: margin protection, buybacks and dividends.
- **Q1 2026:** revenue RMB 73.7 billion; net income RMB 4.65 billion.
- **Q2 2026:** revenue RMB 78.1 billion, about 1% higher than a year earlier; net income RMB 5.64 billion, about 14% lower.
- **Q3 2026 (reported at the end of October 2026):** revenue RMB 69.7 billion, about 10% lower than the RMB 77.5 billion a year earlier. Net income RMB 4.68 billion, about 12% lower than RMB 5.34 billion. Nine-month net profit was about RMB 15 billion, down 13.7%.

## 2. Claims vs financials (forensic)
| Claim (the committee's working thesis, management's stated strategy) | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Margins hold when sales fall | Gross margin was 27.1% in Q3 2026, against 27.9% in Q3 2025 and 29.0% in Q2 2026. Net margin was 6.7% in Q3 2026, against 6.9% a year earlier. BofA Securities says about RMB 0.5 billion of one-off expenses hit the quarter; excluding them, net profit fell only about 3% on 10% lower sales. | Mostly holds. Gross margin slipped, but operating cost control protected the bottom line. |
| Overseas growth offsets China | BofA: overseas revenue "broadly flat" in Q3. CLSA: weak China demand after the subsidy was withdrawn, plus high US air-conditioner inventory. | Not delivered this quarter. Both engines stalled together. |
| Cash generation funds dividends and buybacks | Trailing-twelve-month (TTM) free cash flow is RMB 10.2 billion. But Q3 2026 operating cash flow was only RMB 1.1 billion (Q3 2025: RMB 6.6 billion), and free cash flow was negative RMB 2.0 billion in a quarter that paid RMB 8.5 billion of dividends. | Annual cash generation is adequate; Q3 cash conversion was weak. |
| Shareholder returns | H-share buybacks continue. On 9 November 2026 the company bought 300,000 shares at HK$21.08-21.26; 5 million shares (0.18%) have been bought back under the current mandate. The company also bought back A-shares and D-shares (79 million D-shares for about EUR 148 million, undated on the page). | Real, but small against the share count. |
| Balance sheet is not a constraint | 30 September 2026: cash and short-term investments RMB 44.6 billion against borrowings of RMB 72.85 billion plus RMB 4.5 billion of leases. Net debt is RMB 32.8 billion including leases (RMB 28.3 billion excluding them), about 1.1x EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation). There is also RMB 44.8 billion of long-term investments. | Holds. |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory
No transcript is available, so we cannot rate tone from management's words. The actions read as defensive: steady small buybacks, a large dividend, and no growth acceleration. Brokers turned more cautious around the results. CLSA cut its target to HK$25, BofA to HK$24.5, Jefferies to HK$21, and J.P. Morgan and Goldman Sachs both cut. Rating from behaviour: **Declining (cyclical), not collapsing.**

## 4. Guidance credibility
Haier does not give hard numerical guidance. The screener records only 2 of 7 recent quarters as earnings beats (29%), and 2026 earnings are tracking down about 14% while consensus earlier assumed growth. Reliability: **Medium**. The long record is strong; the 2026 forecasts were too high.

## 5. Analyst pressure points
- How quickly does China demand normalise once the subsidy is gone, and how much channel destocking (dealers running down stock) is left?
- US air-conditioner inventory, and GE Appliances' margins if tariffs or price competition worsen.
- Whether Q3's weak cash conversion is timing (working capital) or a lasting change.
- Whether buybacks will be stepped up while the shares trade near 10x earnings.

## 6. Red flags / green flags
- Red flag: Q3 2026 revenue fell about 10% year on year, the first double-digit quarterly decline in the visible record.
- Red flag: Q3 2026 operating cash flow fell to RMB 1.1 billion from RMB 6.6 billion a year earlier.
- Red flag: Q3 2026 gross margin slipped about 0.8 percentage points year on year.
- Red flag: the screener's earnings-beat rate is low (2 of 7 quarters).
- Green flag: net margin was close to flat in Q3 (6.7% vs 6.9%) despite the sales drop; excluding one-offs, profit fell only about 3%.
- Green flag: five-year earnings per share growth was about 10.7% a year and book value per share growth about 10.8% a year. Return on equity is 16% and return on invested capital about 12%.
- Green flag: buybacks continue across all three share classes (9 November 2026 H-share purchase).
- Green flag: margins held through 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 29.8% in 2019, 31.2% in 2021).

## 7. Hidden signals
- The shares rallied about 10% in the ten trading days after the results (to HK$21.20 on 9 November from HK$19.30 on 26 October), even as every broker we saw cut its target. The market had already priced a bad quarter. The "worst is known" reflex is at work.
- Brokers cut their targets but none (in the headlines we saw) downgraded to sell. Their new targets cluster at HK$21-25, close to our fair value.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict (for the director)
**Trajectory: deteriorating (cyclical).** Earnings are falling in 2026 because China's subsidy-driven demand has reversed and overseas growth has paused. The franchise itself is not shrinking structurally.

**The single most important point for sizing:** the stock trades at about 10x trailing earnings, below its own five-year earnings growth. The 2026 profit decline (down about 14% for the nine months) is the base the market now prices, so the question is whether 2027 stabilises. Q3 cash conversion is the item to watch.

**Moat:** scale and cost advantages plus brand and channel (global manufacturing and purchasing scale, the GE Appliances, Fisher & Paykel and Haier/Casarte brands, and a large Chinese dealer network). Return on invested capital of about 12% and return on equity of about 16% are solid but not exceptional. Gross margin is in the high 20s, edging down this year for cyclical reasons. **A narrow but real moat, stable in trend.**

**Secular threat:** manageable. Appliances are a replacement-cycle category, and no structural force (such as artificial-intelligence displacement or a channel shift) threatens Haier's terminal value. The cheapness reflects fear of a cyclical trough, not a structurally shrinking business.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory weakening · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Axos Financial (AX) - a deep dive on management and the setup
*Prepared 2026-11-16. Price used: $89.71 (NYSE, USD, FMP live quote 2026-11-16). Transcripts read: fiscal Q1-2026 (2025-10-30), fiscal Q2-2026 (2026-01-29), fiscal Q3-2026 (2026-04-30), the block filed as 2026-07-30 (its content is actually the fiscal Q4-2025 call for the quarter ended 2025-06-30 - a mislabelled transcript, so the fiscal Q4-2026 call of July 2026 is missing from our file) and fiscal Q1-2027 (2026-10-29). Axos's fiscal year ends June 30.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Axos is a branchless US bank: it gathers deposits online and through specialty channels (consumer and small-business accounts, treasury management for companies, a custody-and-clearing broker-dealer business, fiduciary services) and lends them out at unusually high yields in niche commercial categories (commercial real-estate specialty lending, lender finance, capital-call lines to private funds, equipment finance, auto, jumbo mortgages).

The story has moved in three steps over the five calls:

- **2025-07 to 2025-10: organic engine plus a windfall.** Earnings were flattered by accretion (the gradual booking of a purchase discount as income) on loans bought from the FDIC (the US deposit insurer) out of the Signature Bank failure. Management stressed that net interest margin (NIM - what the bank earns on loans minus what it pays on deposits, as a share of assets) was "best-in-class with or without" that accretion.
- **2026-01 to 2026-04: buying growth.** Verdant (equipment leasing, closed 2025-09-30), an office building for a future headquarters, and two deposit purchases (Jenius Bank deposits, ~$2.3B, June 2026 quarter; Capital One IRA deposits, ~$1.8B, closed 2026-09-21). FDIC accretion was openly guided down ("dwindled to around 5 basis points", 2026-04-30).
- **2026-10: higher-for-longer and first credit scars.** The newest call frames the bank as "well positioned for a higher for longer interest rate environment" (75% of loans reprice within 30 days) and, for the first time in the period, had to explain two charged-off loans in its syndicated cash-flow book (both loans led by non-bank agents: one a healthcare company hit by regulation, one a tariff-hit borrower). A crypto (Bitcoin) offering inside the brokerage platform is "2 to 3 weeks" from production.

What was quietly dropped: the single-family warehouse and multifamily engine that drove 2021-23 growth now shrinks through payoffs; capital-call lending, the growth star of the prior three quarters, fell $345M in Q1-FY27 (mostly a deliberate $290M sell-down to other lenders).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Dated source | What the numbers show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low-to-mid-teens annual loan growth | Every call; reiterated 2026-10-29 for fiscal 2027 | Ending loans $25.9B at 2026-09-30, up only $317M in the quarter (~5% annualised); over $600M (~10%) ex the capital-call sell-down. Fiscal-2026 revenue +13.5%. | Roughly delivered over the year; the latest quarter is below guidance and leans on "a few large loans" slipping into the December quarter |
| NIM stays at the high end of 4.25-4.35% ex-accretion / roughly flat | 2025-10-30, 2026-04-30 | Reported NIM 4.75% -> 4.94% -> 4.57% -> 4.64% (Q1-FY27, +10bp linked). FMP: net interest income $331.3M in Q1-FY27 vs $306.3M in the March quarter | Delivered |
| Double-digit EPS and book growth | 2026-10-29 | Diluted EPS $2.25 vs $1.94 a year ago (+16%); TTM diluted EPS $8.78; equity $3.29B at 2026-09-30 | Delivered |
| Personnel + professional-services growth held under 30% of revenue growth | 2025-10-30, 2026-01-29 | Non-interest expense $195.4M in Q1-FY27, down $10.5M linked; efficiency ratio 49.5% (expenses as a share of revenue) | Delivered, but advertising will "stay elevated" to fight for consumer deposits (2026-10-29) |
| Credit is "solid", charge-offs low | Every call | Non-accrual loans 79bp -> 74bp -> 61bp of loans through 2025-12; substandard loans down ~$100M in Q1-FY27; but two syndicated loans charged off in Q1-FY27. The syndicated cash-flow book is $459M, under 2% of loans | Holds, with a first visible crack in a small book |
| "Net cash $1.5B" (screener field) | Our inputs | For a bank, cash and securities fund deposits; they are not surplus owner cash. Total liabilities are $27.6B against $30.8B of assets | Not a valuation add-back - ignore it |

The narrative is not richer than the numbers. Where it stretches is purchased growth: four acquisitions in a year mean higher depreciation and amortisation (management's own explanation for the efficiency ratio rising year on year), and deposit purchases bring higher-cost IRA time deposits.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable.** Every call opens with the same confident list ("double-digit year-over-year growth in ... earnings per share and book value"). Guidance specificity has stayed the same - a loan-growth range, a NIM range, an expense rail. The tone shifted modestly defensive on 2026-10-29: the CEO spent the closing answers on credit ("to be highly skeptical of EBITDA adjustments"), and the CFO flagged "the competitive nature of deposits, especially around consumer". The shift is small and specific rather than a general retreat.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Guidance reliability: **High.** NIM guidance was met each quarter after stripping out one-off FDIC loan payoffs, which management disclosed and quantified unprompted ($17M in the December 2025 quarter). The expense rail was met. Loan growth was met over the fiscal year though the latest quarter undershot. The screener shows earnings beats in 6 of 7 quarters (86%), and Zacks shows Q1-FY27 adjusted EPS of $2.34 against a $2.25 estimate (2026-10-29). There is a mild sandbagging pattern: the CEO talked the January 2026 loan guide down ("lower is unlikely") and then beat it.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Expenses with acquisitions** (2025-10-30, Tim Coffey: "Is my North Star an efficiency ratio?"). The CEO's answer ("So am I, Tim") was candid but admits that acquisition accounting blurs the run rate.
- **Credit in syndicated and non-bank-lender exposures** (2025-10-30 on NDFIs - non-depository financial institutions; 2026-10-29 on the two charge-offs, and whether they came out of the shared national credit exam). Management answered directly. The risk is that analysts keep finding new pockets.
- **Loan growth math** (2026-01-29, Kelly Motta). Answered.
- Not pressed by analysts but worth watching: commercial real-estate concentration (multifamily and small-balance commercial loans) at a time of higher rates, and the CEO's admission that cash-flow loans "made in very low interest rate environments" face "incremental pressure".

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 **2026-10-29:** two syndicated cash-flow loans charged off; management concedes these loans were underwritten at low rates and are now under rate pressure.
- 🔴 **2026-10-29:** consumer deposit competition is pushing advertising up; deposit purchases (Jenius, Capital One IRAs) bring costlier time deposits, and non-interest-bearing deposits slipped from $3.8B to $3.6B on lower brokerage cash sweeps.
- 🔴 **Ongoing:** the screener's open-market insider record is 0 buys against 6 small sells; a large one-off item keeps recurring (a $7M clearing-matter reserve on 2026-01-29, a $22M legal-settlement gain on 2026-04-30), so headline EPS needs adjusting each quarter.
- 🔴 **Structural:** a founder-style CEO dominates the story (key-person risk) and the company has a history of governance controversy - a reason the shares have long traded at a discount to peers.
- 🟢 **2026-10-29:** NIM up 10bp to 4.64%; EPS +16% year on year; buybacks of $14M at about $87 a share since July, with $112M of authorisation left.
- 🟢 **2025-12 to 2026-09:** non-accrual ratio fell from 79bp to 61bp, and substandard loans fell ~$100M in Q1-FY27.
- 🟢 **2026-04-30:** Verdant is "immediately profitable" on Axos's cheaper funding and is adding about $200M of loans a quarter.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **"Higher for longer"** replaced the 2025 language about "recent Fed actions" trimming loan yields. Management now sells the bank as a beneficiary of high rates (asset sensitive, meaning income rises with rates), and that is consistent with the 11bp rise in loan yields in Q1-FY27.
- **Sell-down and agenting** (acting as lead lender and selling pieces of loans to other lenders) of capital-call loans is new. It shows a bank managing its concentration and starting to earn fees, but it also flatters returns versus balance-sheet growth.
- **Crypto and an "Axos Complete" brokerage tech stack** show management reaching for fee income and cross-selling to customers. That is optional upside that does not need to be priced.
- A **mislabelled transcript** in our own file (the 2026-07-30 block is the 2025-07-30 call) means the fiscal Q4-2026 call was not read directly; its numbers come from the FMP income statement ($124.9M net income, $2.16 diluted EPS).

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** Earnings power is compounding at low-to-mid teens. Returns on equity run ~16% annualised, roughly 17% on tangible equity (book value minus goodwill: tangible book value about $53 a share against $3.29B of equity and $272M of goodwill). Management is buying back stock below $90. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **this is a credit-cycle-exposed lender priced at about 10 times trailing earnings and 1.7 times tangible book.** The upside is a rerating towards peer multiples as growth continues. The real downside is a commercial real-estate or leveraged-loan credit cycle under higher-for-longer rates, which the first two charge-offs hint at but do not prove.

**Moat:** narrow. It is a scale-cost advantage: a branchless, low-cost deposit-gathering platform with specialty deposit verticals and niche lending expertise. The evidence is a NIM of about 4.6% versus about 3.3-3.6% for typical regional banks, and an ROE in the mid-teens sustained for years. Width is stable rather than widening: margins are flat, and deposit competition plus costlier acquired deposits stop them expanding.

**Secular threat:** manageable. Fintech and stablecoin disintermediation of deposits is a long-run consideration for any deposit franchise, but Axos is itself the digital channel, and its deposits are diversified across consumer, commercial, fiduciary and brokerage. The low multiple reads as a fear-print (a mispricing driven by credit and governance worries), not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# GNTX - Gentex Corporation - forensic dossier (2026-11-09)

Price used: $19.50 (NASDAQ, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-09 close; 52-week low $19.49). Transcripts read: Q3-2025 (2025-10-24) through Q3-2026 (2026-10-23).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
A year ago (Q3-2025) the story was margin recovery: core gross margin climbed back toward 35-36% on purchasing savings and mix, and the VOXX acquisition (premium audio) was bolted on to diversify away from mirrors. Q4-2025 (2026-01-30) was the high-water mark - core gross margin 35.5%, "highest since 2021". Through 2026 the story shifted to defence: China exports shrinking on tariffs, a lost Volkswagen mirror program in Europe, and from mid-2026 precious-metal inflation (silver, gold, ruthenium) eating the bill of materials. By Q3-2026 the pitch is "content per vehicle offsets falling production, and diversification is working": non-auto revenue up about 17% to 15% of sales, premium audio up 27% to $54.7M, a first circuit-board assembly award worth about $180M a year, and a dimmable visor launching late 2027.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- Q3-2026 revenue $647.7M vs $655.2M a year earlier (-1%); about $35M below the company's own start-of-quarter forecast ("customer issues and delayed launches") - the second quarter running below its own plan.
- Gross margin 33.4% vs 34.4% (2026-10-23); the 10-Q filed 2026-11-06 confirms gross profit $216.3M on $647.7M.
- GAAP diluted EPS $0.43 vs $0.46; adjusted $0.47 in both periods. Trailing four quarters GAAP EPS = $1.85 (0.42 + 0.46 + 0.54 + 0.43).
- Claim "North America auto revenue +3% against -5% production" is consistent with the content-per-vehicle thesis; Europe ex-VW +13%.
- Inventory rose to $550.1M from $516.3M at year-end - management attributes it to precious-metal and electronic-component stockpiling; plausible given the commodity spike but it flatters current margins less than it ties up cash.
- Cash $134.4M plus investments $242.9M = $377M, no funded debt. Cash fell because buybacks ($270M year to date) exceeded free cash flow growth. Net cash per share about $1.80 on about 206M shares.
- Full-year 2026 revenue guide narrowed to about $2.65B (from $2.65-2.75B).

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Confident and prescriptive in late 2025 (margin targets hit), more defensive in 2026. In Q3-2026 management is candid about the miss and concentrated drivers, and openly says "we struggle to understand the stock price" - signalling buyback priority over M&A. Hedging on precious metals: "probably good all the way through midpoint next year" on supply, but costs are explicitly outside their control.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
Weakening. Revenue came in below the company's own quarterly forecast twice in 2026 and the annual range was trimmed to its bottom. The 2027 revenue target of $2.8-2.9B (Investor Day, August 2026) now looks stretched to sell-side (Seeking Alpha downgrade 2026-10-26). Gross-margin guidance credibility is the weakest link because it rides on silver and gold prices.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Precious-metal pass-through (no clear fix offered), China stabilisation in 2027, the Volkswagen gap in Europe, use of cash (buyback vs M&A). Analysts cut estimates after the print (Benzinga 2026-10-26). Several plaintiff firms announced "investigations" from 2026-10-23 onward - standard solicitations after a 7% drop on a miss; no allegation of misstatement and the 10-Q (2026-11-06) carried no restatement.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: second consecutive revenue shortfall vs own forecast; gross margin back below 34%; EPS flat for three years despite heavy buybacks; mirror units shrinking; inflation-exposed gross margin (fell 5.2pp in 2019-22). Green: debt-free, about $385M annual free cash flow (about 9.5x price/free cash flow), ROIC about 16%, non-auto diversification growing double digits, new circuit-board revenue stream, aggressive buyback at prices above today's ($23.44 average in Q3).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
Management bought 5.7M shares at $23.44 in Q3 - a revealed valuation at least 20% above today's price. Adjusted EPS held flat at $0.47 even in a bad quarter, so the earnings base is more resilient than the GAAP line suggests. The $180M circuit-board award is low-margin contract manufacturing - it diversifies revenue but dilutes gross margin.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
A clean, cash-rich niche franchise in a cyclical, cost-pressured patch; the numbers are honest and the balance sheet is a genuine cushion. The risk is earnings stagnation, not solvency or accounting. Buybacks at sub-10x free cash flow are accretive. Fair to underwrite on normalized earnings of about $1.85-1.95 a share.

# freenet AG (FNTN.DE) - a deep dive on management and the setup

As of 2026-11-16. Price used: EUR 24.50 (XETRA, FMP live quote). Calls read: FY2024 Q1 (2025-05-22), Q3 2025 (2025-11-08), FY2025 preliminary (2026-02-26), H1 2026 (2026-08-13), Q3 2026 (2026-11-12).

**Bottom line:** freenet is a cash machine that stopped growing. It resells mobile contracts on all three German networks and owns waipu.tv, the number-two internet-TV (IPTV) service in Germany. Revenue drifts down about 1.5% a year (EUR 2.56B in 2021, EUR 2.44B in 2025), but free cash flow holds near EUR 300M and nearly all of it goes back to shareholders. The story over the last year is a fight with one network partner (Telefonica) over a "sick agreement" that cost up to EUR 50M a year of operating profit (EBITDA, earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation). On 2026-11-10 the two sides signed a detailed term sheet, a non-binding outline of a new ten-year deal. That is the most important change in the file, but its numbers have not been disclosed and the contract is not yet signed.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **2025 calls:** the story was price discipline in mobile after two years of falling contract prices, the mobilezone acquisition (a rival reseller, bought late 2025), and waipu.tv turning profitable.
- **2026-02-26 (FY2025):** a new, sharper tone from CEO Robin Harries. He opened with bad news: an agreement with "the network provider" closed in 2024 "might lead to a minus EUR 13 million impact in '25 and to up to EUR 50 million negative EBITDA impact for the year '26 to '28." He called it "a sick agreement." New growth levers appeared: brand marketing behind the freenet name, a 1&1 shop partnership, AI voicebots in customer service, and a 2028 ambition (adjusted EBITDA of at least EUR 620M and adjusted free cash flow of at least EUR 340M, per the H1 2026 release).
- **2026-08-13 (H1):** "value over volume" became the refrain. Front-book prices (prices for new customers) up about 1%; customer base passed 10 million; a minimum dividend of EUR 2.00 a share for 2026-28 rising toward EUR 2.30. The Telefonica talks were "constructive" but "nothing decided yet."
- **2026-11-12 (Q3):** a victory-lap call. The term sheet with Telefonica ("The key issues between us have been resolved"), the buyout of the last 25% of waipu.tv for EUR 76M plus up to EUR 50M performance payment (implied value EUR 300M), and a EUR 75M share buyback funded partly by the sale of the CECONOMY stake. Advertising at waipu quietly became a soft spot ("weaker macroeconomics has affected revenues").

Dropped or downplayed: the old freenet TV broadcast business (DVB-T2 antenna TV) keeps shrinking and is now mentioned only in passing; mobilezone synergies are talked up but never quantified.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Our cash generation remains a key strength" (Q3 2026) | TTM free cash flow EUR 322M; FCF margin 14.9%; FY2026 adjusted free cash flow guided EUR 270-300M and now expected at the upper end | Holds |
| Mobile is "resilient", service revenue growing | Q3 postpaid service revenue +1.1% to EUR 480M; but group revenue CAGR -1.5% over three years and gross margin only ~26% | Partly holds: stable, not growing |
| Telefonica headwind is "fully factored" into guidance | 9-month EBITDA hit of EUR 32M disclosed on 2026-11-12; group EBITDA now guided to the low end of EUR 500-530M | Holds; the hit is real and showing up |
| waipu.tv growing ~20% | 9-month normalised IPTV EBITDA EUR 30.9M vs 24.5M (+26%) | Holds |
| Strong balance sheet | Net debt EUR 722M including EUR 180M leases (about EUR 542M excluding leases), roughly 1.4x EBITDA; interest cost rising after the mobilezone deal ("we have a higher leverage than we had last year") | Holds, but leverage rose |
| EPS growth | FY2025 EPS 2.30 (+10.6%), but TTM diluted EPS 1.84 and latest-quarter EPS down 30% year on year | Profit line weaker than the cash line in 2026 |
| waipu buyout is a "good deal" | EUR 300M valuation is under 3x the 2028 EBITDA ambition (UBS on the call). Either a bargain or a hint the 2028 waipu ambition is soft | Open question |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable to slightly rising.** February 2026 was defensive and candid about the contract problem. August was upbeat but hedged on second-half EBITDA ("it is challenging. But in our forecast, we do still reach it"). November was the most confident call in the set, but the CFO immediately lowered EBITDA to the low end of the range, and would not put the term sheet into guidance ("it is not good enough to put it in the guidance"). That restraint is a credibility plus.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- FY2025 guidance met (customer growth exceeded; dividend raised to EUR 2.07).
- FY2026: EBITDA drifting to the low end of EUR 500-530M (August said "challenging"; November confirmed the low end); free cash flow to the upper end of EUR 270-300M, helped by lower tax prepayments.
- The scan shows 0 of 7 quarters beating analyst EPS consensus: freenet steers on EBITDA and cash, not EPS, and consensus EPS has been too high. **Reliability: Medium.** Cash promises are kept; profit-line ambitions are trimmed.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The network contract** (BNP, 2026-02-26): what legal leverage does a reseller actually have? Management refused to discuss it and the CFO pointedly would not confirm the contract term ("I have not said that it ends in '28"). The term sheet answers this for now, but the economics remain undisclosed.
- **waipu valuation** (UBS, 2026-11-12): why so cheap? The CEO answered with "we are strong dealmakers", not numbers.
- **Agentic AI and switching** (Goldman, 2026-11-12): could AI shopping agents make customers switch more easily? The CEO's answer ("every smart AI agent will consider freenet") is assertion, not evidence.
- **ARPU** (average revenue per user): back-book ARPU keeps falling until "probably the second half of '27" (CEO, 2026-08-13).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 Dependence on network owners: the 2024 contract cost up to EUR 50M a year, and freenet had no visible leverage until Telefonica agreed to renegotiate (2026-02-26 to 2026-11-10).
- 🔴 TTM EPS 1.84 vs FY2025 2.30; latest quarter EPS -30% (Q3 2026).
- 🔴 waipu advertising weakened from mid-2026 (Q3 2026).
- 🔴 Higher leverage and interest cost after mobilezone (Q3 2026).
- 🟢 Term sheet with Telefonica on "improved commercial terms", a reported ten-year extension (2026-11-10).
- 🟢 Front-book prices rising for a third straight report (2026-02-26, 2026-08-13, 2026-11-12).
- 🟢 Full ownership of waipu.tv at a low price; EUR 75M buyback (announced 2026-11-05) on top of a EUR 2.00 minimum dividend.
- 🟢 The CFO kept the unsigned term sheet out of guidance (2026-11-12).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- "AI-first" now opens every call; the concrete proof so far is a voicebot handling just over 10% of calls (2026-08-13).
- The CFO answers specific questions with "I do not want to talk about it" (legal options, contract dates). Contract terms with the network owners are the one area where disclosure is thin.
- A two-person executive board (Harries and Arnold) speaks with one voice; the CFO is the one who tempers the CEO's optimism.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** Capital allocation is disciplined and shareholder-first: about 80% of free cash flow paid out, buybacks on top, and small bolt-ons (mobilezone, waipu minority) funded inside a leverage of about 1.4x EBITDA.

**The single thing to weigh before sizing:** the value of the Telefonica term sheet is not yet in any published number. If the final contract restores most of the up-to-EUR-50M yearly hit, free cash flow can reach the 2028 ambition of at least EUR 340M; if the contract slips or the terms prove thin, the business is a flat EUR 270-300M cash stream with a falling top line.

**Moat:** narrow. freenet's edge is distribution scale (shops, online brands, the only reseller with all three networks) and a regulatory-reseller position, not network ownership. ROIC (return on invested capital) of about 10.7% with stable gross margins says the moat is narrow but not eroding today. Structural threats (network owners steering customers to their own brands, AI agents making switching easier, the decline of antenna TV) are real but manageable: waipu.tv is growing into the gap, and the term sheet shows the network owners still value freenet's distribution. The cheapness reads as a high-payout, low-growth cash stock priced for a slow decline, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
