picks.bull_thesis: The branded half of Smithfield is worth roughly today's whole enterprise value on its own, and you get the pork chain, a 6.8% dividend and a cyclical recovery for little or nothing. Packaged meats (Smithfield, Eckrich, Nathan's, Armour, Prime Fresh) is on track for a fifth straight year above $1B of operating profit and grew profit and margin in the worst quarter of the pork cycle in years (Q3 2026: $230M versus $226M, margin 11.6% versus 10.8%), with share gains in five $1B-plus categories and distribution won 'not because of lower pricing' (Q2 2026). At $18.51 the company is worth about $7.3B of equity plus about $1.66B of pro-forma net debt including leases, roughly $9.0B of enterprise value (the company's total value to all capital providers) - about 8x packaged meats' operating profit alone. Fresh pork and hog production are deep in a cyclical trough (processing spread down about 35% year on year, hams -20%, bellies -25%); troughs in pork have historically lasted a few quarters, high hog prices already discourage expansion (breeding herd -1.2%, farrowing intentions -2%, July USDA data cited 2026-08-11), and management expects fresh pork to rebound into December. Self-help lowers the cycle's sting: a supply deal removes about 900,000 internally raised hogs a year from 2027, and Nathan's ownership repatriates about $33M a year of licence fees plus about $9M of synergies. The balance sheet (0.5x net debt to EBITDA at Q3, $3.5B liquidity) means no forced action at the bottom. Conditions: packaged meats holds about $1.1B of profit; the upstream returns to modest profit within 12-18 months; WH Group's selling does not swamp demand.
picks.bear_thesis: This is a low-return commodity processor with one good segment, and the good segment cannot fully carry the bad ones. Management promised 'another year of increased profitability' on 2026-03-24 and has cut the 2026 outlook three times since (2026-08-11, 2026-09-08, 2026-10-27), to $900M-$1B. The pork downturn is not a normal seasonal dip: management itself calls it 'unchartered territory' with no guardrails on duration, export outlets are eroding as Mexico and China add supply and tariffs persist, and the US consumer is squeezed by inflation, fuel costs and reduced SNAP benefits. Through the cycle the business earns poorly (ROIC 5.1%, ROE 8.6%, revenue 3-year CAGR -1.4%), so a 'normalized' upstream may be closer to breakeven than to the 2025 peak. Leverage is rising: the roughly $450M Nathan's purchase closed after the quarter, and the Sioux Falls plant - a multi-year capital project - is stalled after a court reversed its permit. WH Group, the majority holder, has been a steady seller (about 38.2M shares sold on the open market versus 1.9M bought), an overhang that caps rallies. If packaged-meats margins slip as lower pork costs are passed back to retailers and the upstream stays in loss into 2027, earnings power falls toward $1.80-2.00 per share and the stock re-rates to a low multiple of trough earnings. What would confirm it: a 2027 outlook below about $900M, packaged-meats profit falling year on year, or a dividend held only by borrowing.
picks.consensus_delta: The street is pricing Smithfield as a pork commodity company in a bad year, and on the upstream it is right. Where we disagree with the market is the branded core: at $18.51 (about $9.0B enterprise value including leases and the Nathan's cash outlay) the market pays roughly 8x packaged-meats operating profit for a franchise that just grew profit and margin through a 35% collapse in pork values, and assigns nothing to fresh pork and hogs. Analyst targets are falling fast toward the price - Barclays cut from $29 (2026-09-09) to $23 (2026-10-28), Stephens is at $20 (2026-10-28), Deutsche Bank at $21 (2026-10-09) - which tells us the street is extrapolating the trough, not the parts. But the market is not wrong to discount management's annual guidance after three cuts in 2026, and the screener's 5-of-6 beat rate is against already-lowered quarterly estimates. The disagreement is real but modest: the market is not pricing terminal decline, it is pricing an uncertain trough plus a seller overhang.
picks.valley_of_death: No liquidation risk: net debt to EBITDA was 0.5x at 2026-09-27, liquidity $3.5B, and there is no near maturity wall in the materials. The risky window is the next two to five months. Q4 2026 (the holiday quarter) is, in management's words, 'critically important' and could disappoint again if hams and bellies do not recover through the holidays; the futures curve implied Q4 hog losses of about $20 a head (2026-08-11). Cash flow will look weaker in 2027 if working capital reverses as pork prices recover. Leverage steps up after the roughly $450M Nathan's payment, and Sioux Falls capital spending (about $37M so far) is in limbo after the permit reversal. A 2027 outlook below about $900M would push the stock toward our adverse case near $15.
picks.positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure comes mainly from the majority holder, WH Group, which has sold heavily (open-market insider sales of about 38.2M shares versus about 1.9M bought); further secondary sales are a recurring supply overhang that can cap rallies independent of the fundamentals. Income holders are unlikely to be forced out: the $0.3125 quarterly dividend was reaffirmed on 2026-10-29 and is covered by trailing free cash flow of $927M (about $490M of annual dividends on about 394M shares). The stock sits about 24% below its 200-day average and 4% above its 52-week low ($17.91), so momentum sellers have largely done their work.
picks.moderator_conclusion: Wait for the event: we buy once the Q4 and full-year 2026 results and the 2027 outlook (expected late March 2027) confirm fresh pork is back to a profit and 2027 operating profit near $1.0B or better. The thesis holds: the packaged-meats business grew profit and margin in the third quarter (reported 2026-10-27) through one of the sharpest pork downturns in years, and the balance sheet is strong. On our sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately), the base fair value is about $22.5 per share against $18.51 today, with an adverse case near $15 and a favorable case near $30 over roughly 18 months. That discount only just clears the 20% bar we require in today's macro backdrop, and the one input that would widen or close it - when the pork cycle turns - is exactly what management could not answer on the call, after cutting its 2026 outlook three times since August. Nothing dated since our 2026-10-05 look justifies changing our answer: the Q3 print cut both ways and the price has not moved. The 6.8% dividend pays while we wait, and the majority holder's selling is the main reason the stock may stay cheap. Conviction stays moderate (3 of 5): a good branded business inside a low-return commodity chain, with a narrow, stable moat and no structural threat to its terminal value.
picks.forcing_function: No single hard event forces a re-rating. The next dated read is the Q4 and full-year 2026 release with the 2027 outlook (expected late March 2027): a 2027 outlook near $1.0B or above, fresh pork back in profit, packaged meats near $1.1B including Nathan's, and the first year of the 900,000-head hog reduction would let the market value the branded core properly. Secondary levers: buybacks are possible given 0.5x leverage, any end to WH Group's selling, and an eventual Sioux Falls decision.
picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Smithfield Foods (SFD) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-02 from five earnings calls (Q3 2025 on 2025-10-28 through Q3 2026 on 2026-10-27), the screener's financial trajectory, and the company's dated press releases. Price used: $18.51 (Nasdaq, US dollars, FMP quote 2026-11-02).*

**Bottom line:** Smithfield is two businesses wearing one ticker. The branded packaged-meats arm (Smithfield, Eckrich, Nathan's, Armour, Prime Fresh) is a steady, roughly $1.1 billion-a-year operating-profit franchise that grew profit and margin again in the latest quarter. The upstream arm - fresh pork processing and hog farming - is a commodity business that has swung from profit to loss inside six months. Management's credibility on the branded side is good; on the upstream side it has been repeatedly too optimistic in 2026.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3 2025 (2025-10-28):** confident. The company "raised the midpoint and tighten[ed] the range" of its 2025 profit outlook. The story was the first year as a listed company: an integrated pork chain, a fortress balance sheet, a $1-per-share dividend.
- **Q4 2025 (2026-03-24):** still offensive. Management said it expected "2026 to be another year of increased profitability, driven by margin expansion," lifted the dividend to an anticipated $1.25, and framed pork as a "long-term tailwind."
- **Q1 2026 (2026-04-28):** first defensive notes - "a challenging external environment with the Middle East conflict adding another layer of macro volatility," and analysts started probing pork input costs and disease reports.
- **Q2 2026 (2026-08-11):** a record quarter ($300 million adjusted operating profit, 8.1% margin) but the full-year outlook was cut "to reflect the current macroeconomic backdrop." Fresh pork spreads had already compressed. The CEO still saw "some upside that could come into the third and fourth quarters" on hog supply.
- **Pre-announcement (2026-09-08):** a third-quarter warning ahead of the Barclays conference reset the year again (Q3 adjusted operating profit guided to $115-175 million).
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-27):** the tone turned plainly defensive. Adjusted operating profit fell to $145 million from $310 million; the CEO described "a rapid deterioration in the pork value chain"; the pork president called it "unchartered territory." The full-year 2026 outlook was cut again to $900 million-$1 billion of adjusted operating profit (53 weeks, including about two months of Nathan's). The new emphasis is what management controls: packaged meats, the Nathan's purchase (closed 2026-10-26), and a supply deal that removes about 900,000 internally produced hogs a year.

The thesis contracted from "integrated growth" to "a resilient branded core carrying a cyclical upstream." The growth drivers quietly dropped were 2026 margin expansion at the consolidated level and export strength.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers say | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "2026 to be another year of increased profitability" (2026-03-24) | Full-year guide now $900M-$1B versus a 2025 base well above that; Q3 operating profit -53% year on year; latest-quarter EPS -63%; TTM diluted EPS $2.28 vs $2.51 for 2025 | Missed - three successive cuts (Aug, Sept, Oct) |
| Packaged meats is resilient | Q3 segment profit $230M vs $226M, margin 11.6% vs 10.8%, volume +0.2%; "on track" for a fifth straight year above $1B | Corroborated |
| Strong balance sheet | Net debt/adjusted EBITDA 0.5x at Q3; $1.2B cash, $3.5B liquidity; Altman-Z 3.2. Recomputed net debt $1.21B including $386M of leases (about $826M ex-leases) at 2026-09-27, before the roughly $450M cash-funded Nathan's close on 2026-10-26 - pro-forma about $1.66B including leases | Corroborated, but leverage rises after Nathan's |
| Strong cash generation | TTM free cash flow $927M on a $7.3B market cap (P/FCF about 10x on the scan); nine-month 2026 operating cash flow $365M, up $244M | Corroborated, flattered by working capital as pork prices fell |
| Hog production restructured for the cycle | Six profitable quarters to Q2, Q3 still +$34M (vs $89M); full-year guide now -$25M to +$25M | Partly corroborated - better than old Smithfield, still cyclical |
| Returns | ROIC 5.1%, ROE 8.6%; revenue 3-year CAGR -1.4% | Thin; the integrated model does not earn its cost of capital through the cycle |

The story is richer than the numbers on the consolidated growth claim and fair on the branded-segment claim.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Declining. From "raised the midpoint" (Q3 2025) and "another year of increased profitability" (Q4 2025) to "rapid deterioration" and "it's really too early to tell about spring of 2027" (Q3 2026). Guidance became less specific on the upstream: asked how long recovery takes, management offered no guardrails - "we're going to have to see how Q4 responds." Packaged-meats language stayed specific and confident throughout (share gains in five $1B+ categories, Prime Fresh distribution +24%).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

The screener records earnings beats in 5 of 6 quarters, but that counts quarterly consensus, which analysts cut ahead of each print. Against management's own annual guidance the record in 2026 is poor: the March outlook for higher profit was cut on 2026-08-11, again on 2026-09-08, and again on 2026-10-27. The Q3 print landed inside the September range, so the near-term pre-announcement was honest. Packaged-meats guidance has been reliable. Overall reliability: Medium (High for packaged meats, Low for the upstream commodity calls, where management leaned on the futures curve and then on hopes that hog supply would tighten).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- How long the upstream downturn lasts (Stephens and Bank of America, Q3 2026) - no answer beyond "Q4 is going to be critically important."
- The Sioux Falls plant after a court reversed its conditional-use permit - management will reapply but gave no new timing.
- Ham and belly price deflation (Q2 2026) - management called it temporary; it deepened into Q3 (hams -20%, bellies -25% year on year).
- Exports: Mexico and China supply growth plus tariffs eroding the outlet that normally clears US pork.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- Three cuts to the 2026 outlook in under three months (2026-08-11, 2026-09-08, 2026-10-27).
- Fresh pork lost $89M in Q3 2026; the processing spread is "well below the level needed to cover processing costs."
- Majority holder WH Group has been a heavy seller: open-market insider sales of about 38.2M shares versus 1.9M bought - a recurring supply overhang.
- Low through-cycle returns (ROIC 5.1%).

Green flags:
- Packaged meats profit and margin up in a deflating, value-seeking consumer market (Q3 2026).
- Nathan's ownership repatriates about $33M a year of licence costs (CFO, 2026-10-27) and secures the brand in perpetuity.
- Fewer internally owned hogs from 2027 (900,000-head supply deal) lowers commodity exposure.
- Dividend held: $0.3125 quarterly declared 2026-10-29 (about 6.8% yield at $18.51).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The vocabulary shifted from "integrated model advantage" to "actions within our control" and "resilience." Management now separates "commodity market-driven challenges" from the branded business in nearly every sentence - a tacit invitation to value the parts separately. The hog-reduction deal is a quiet strategic pivot toward a lighter upstream, which over time should make Smithfield look more like a branded packaged-food company and less like a pork commodity play.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable at the franchise level, with consolidated earnings in a cyclical downturn. Capital allocation has been sensible - a modestly priced bolt-on (Nathan's at about 10x post-synergy EBITDA, paid in cash), a lower-risk upstream, a held dividend, and leverage kept far inside policy.

The single thing to weigh before sizing: the price already assumes the upstream earns nothing - packaged meats alone at about 8x operating profit roughly equals today's enterprise value - but nobody, management included, can say when the pork cycle turns, and the fourth-quarter holiday season is the next real read.

Moat: a narrow scale-and-brand moat in packaged meats (number-one positions in several categories, distribution gains earned without price cuts), none in fresh pork or hogs. Returns are low and flat rather than high-and-falling, so this is narrow and stable, not eroding. Secular threat: manageable - plant-based or GLP-1-driven shifts in meat consumption are slow, and the main pressures today are cyclical (pork oversupply, export competition, a squeezed consumer). The cheapness is mostly a cyclical fear print plus a majority-holder overhang, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

picks.bull_thesis:
Electricite de Strasbourg is two businesses in one share price, and the market has sold both for a problem that lives in one. The half-year 2026 report, approved by the board on 30 July 2026, shows the regulated Alsatian grid earning an operating profit of 58.95 million euros against 59.47 million a year earlier, on revenue of 176.7 million against 176.5 million, with volumes carried up 1% to 3.34 terawatt-hours. The grid is the asset worth owning. Strasbourg Electricite Reseaux is one of a handful of local distribution operators allowed outside France's national grid monopoly; its revenue is set by the energy regulator under a settlement running to 2029, and its tariff rose 3.04% on 1 August 2026 under the regulator's decision of 21 May 2026. Electrification of Alsatian heating, transport and industry adds volume to a network that is paid to build.

The balance sheet is the second pillar: 362.4 million euros of cash and short-term investments against 11.4 million of total debt including leases at 30 June 2026, about 351 million of net cash, or roughly 49 euros of a 170.40 euro share price (16 November 2026). No refinancing, no maturity wall, and a thesis that turns on French tariff regulation rather than on interest rates, oil or AI spending.

At 170.40 euros on 16 November 2026 the shares sit in the lower fifth of their 152.60 to 252 euro one-year range, about 32% below the May 2026 high, on roughly 11 times a realistic 2026 earnings estimate of about 15.3 euros. Our base sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately) of 185 euros a share implies about 9% upside, and the favourable case of 245 euros, with the parent at 88.64% of the capital only 1.36 points from the squeeze-out threshold, carries free optionality.
picks.bear_thesis:
The bear case is that the cheapness is partly a data error and partly a dividend cut the register has not yet absorbed.

First, the error. Our metrics block reports trailing earnings per share of 39.84 euros and free cash flow of 237 million euros. Both are double the truth: this company reports half-yearly and the feed has summed four half-years as if they were quarters. The honest trailing twelve months is about 18.16 euros of earnings and 85 million of free cash flow, so the stock is on about 8.6 times trailing earnings and about 10 times 2026, not 4 times. Most of the screen's 55% margin of safety disappears once corrected.

Second, the earnings base is still falling and nobody will say where it stops. There is no guidance, no earnings call and no interim disclosure until the full-year 2026 result, expected around February 2027. The first half was the first clean period without regulated nuclear access, and supply profit halved; that may be a step, not the floor.

Third, the dividend. The 13.70 euro payment made from 9 June 2026 was set against peak earnings. Holding the 62% payout on about 15.3 euros of 2026 earnings gives about 9.30 euros. Underlying first-half free cash flow, stripping a 50.5 million euro working-capital release, was about 26.6 million against 98.2 million paid out, with investment running at twice depreciation. A local, income-driven register that sees its apparent 8.8% yield turn into about 6% may sell again.

Fourth, the structure. EDF Holding owns 88.64%, the free float is about 11%, turnover is around 2,500 shares a day, and the parent sets supply-purchase terms (90.7 million euros of related-party purchasing in six months). Part of the discount to listed network peers is a permanent minority discount that will not close by arbitrage. The idle Rittershoffen geothermal plant, shut since 4 December 2025, and the lithium programme are capital commitments minorities do not control.
picks.consensus_delta: There is no verifiable sell-side consensus to disagree with: the company publishes no guidance, holds no calls and reports twice a year, and we found no dated, named analyst target. Our disagreement is with the price and with the data most screens use. The market has priced a group-wide earnings collapse; the segment table shows a single-segment one, with about 70% of profit flat. But screening data is wrong in the bullish direction: trailing earnings and free cash flow on our feed are about double the truth because half-years were summed as quarters. Corrected, this is a roughly 10-times-earnings regulated utility with about 48 euros a share of net cash and a probable dividend cut ahead - cheap, but not the bargain the raw screen shows. The November rebound to 170.40 euros narrows our discount to about 9%.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Electricite de Strasbourg (ELEC.PA) - deep dive on management and the setup
*Updated 16 November 2026. Price used: 170.40 euros (Euronext Paris, live quote via our paid data feed, 16 November 2026).*

**Source note.** This company holds no earnings calls and publishes no transcripts, so there are no quarter-by-quarter management quotes to test. It reports twice a year in writing. This dossier rests on the written record: the full-year 2025 results release (board of 18 February 2026), the half-year 2026 financial report (board of 30 July 2026), the regulator's tariff decision of 21 May 2026, and a search on 16 November 2026 of the company's site, the market regulator's filing archive and French financial press, which found no company publication dated after 30 July 2026. No quotes below are invented; where we paraphrase, we say so.

**Data warning.** Our screening feed shows trailing earnings of 39.84 euros a share and trailing free cash flow of 237 million euros. Both are about double the truth: the company reports half-years and the feed has summed four half-years as if they were quarters. The honest trailing figures are about 18 euros of earnings a share and about 85 million euros of free cash flow. Everything below uses the corrected figures.

## 1. Narrative arc
The story has narrowed from "an energy group riding a windfall" to "a regulated grid plus a supply arm returning to normal." In 2022-24 the supply arm (ES Energies) earned exceptional margins from the energy-price spike and from ARENH, France's regulated access to cheap nuclear power for suppliers. Net income rose from 59 million euros in 2021 to 158 million in 2025. Management warned in writing with the 2025 results (February 2026) that ARENH would end on 31 December 2025 and that 2026 would be lower. The half-year 2026 report confirmed it: revenue down 7.2% to 628.3 million euros, operating income down 29.3% to 83.6 million, net income down 32.9% to 56.5 million. The fall sat almost entirely in supply, whose operating profit halved from 60.2 to 30.3 million; the regulated grid (Strasbourg Electricite Reseaux) earned 58.95 million against 59.47 million, on flat revenue and volumes up 1%. Side projects (geothermal heat at Rittershoffen and Soultz, lithium extraction from geothermal brine) have moved from growth options to drags: the geothermal plants have been idle since earthquakes in December 2025, with a restart targeted for the second half of 2026 pending the regional regulator's approval. No restart has been announced as of 16 November 2026.

## 2. Claims vs financials
| Claim (written record) | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| 2026 earnings would fall after ARENH ended (FY2025 release, Feb 2026) | First-half operating income -29.3%, supply profit halved | Delivered as warned - credible |
| The grid is a stable base | Grid operating profit 58.95M vs 59.47M; tariff +3.04% from 1 Aug 2026 | Matches |
| Strong balance sheet | Cash and short-term investments about 362-364M vs 11-19M of financial liabilities at 30 June 2026 (about 345-351M net cash, about 48-49 euros a share) | Matches |
| Generous dividend sustainable | 13.70 euros paid June 2026 = 98.2M; underlying first-half free cash flow only about 19-27M after stripping a 50.5M working-capital release, with investment at about twice depreciation | Does not match - a cut is likely in February 2027 |
| Diversification adds value | Geothermal idle since Dec 2025, 2.2M of penalties to an industrial customer | Story richer than the numbers |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory
Stable and conservative. The written releases are factual, carry no numeric guidance and flagged the ARENH cliff in advance. There is no shift from offence to defence because there was never offence: this is a subsidiary run for steady regulated returns and parent cash flow.

## 4. Guidance credibility
No numeric guidance is given. Qualitative warnings (lower 2026 after ARENH) were delivered as stated. Reliability: medium-high, on a thin sample. The company has no earnings-beat history to reconcile.

## 5. Analyst pressure points
There is effectively no sell-side coverage and no call to press management. The unanswered questions are: where the supply arm's earnings settle after the first clean year without ARENH; what dividend the board sets in February 2027; when the geothermal plants restart; and whether EDF, which holds 88.64% (1.36 points short of the 90% squeeze-out threshold, the level at which it could force out minorities), ever takes the company private.

## 6. Red flags / green flags
- Red: supply profit halved in the first half of 2026, with no floor stated.
- Red: the June 2026 dividend of 13.70 euros was far above underlying free cash flow; a cut toward about 9 euros looks likely with the full-year 2026 results.
- Red: a 20.6% exceptional French corporate-tax surcharge (about 6M booked in the first half) and 770M of forward energy-purchase commitments exposed to price swings.
- Red: free float of only about 11%, with daily trading of a few thousand shares.
- Green: about 48-49 euros a share of net cash, no debt maturities.
- Green: grid earnings flat and the regulated tariff up 3.04% from 1 August 2026, under a framework running to 2029.
- Green: management warned of the ARENH cliff in writing months ahead.

## 7. Hidden signals
The energy bought for regulated-tariff customers comes from EDF at a state-set transfer price that applies to every local distributor, not at terms the parent chooses, which removes one governance worry. The shares fell about 17% the day after the half-year report (31 July 2026), drifted to a 152.60 euro low, and have since recovered to 170.40 euros between 3 and 16 November 2026 on thin volume (1,000-3,800 shares a day) with no company publication. We read the rebound as low-liquidity noise, not information.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict
Trajectory: stable. The earnings reset is the one management announced, and the regulated core is intact. The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: corrected for the data error, this is a roughly 9-10 times earnings regulated utility with large net cash and a probable dividend cut ahead - cheap, not the bargain the raw screen shows - and its 11% free float makes it hard to buy or exit in size.

Moat: regulatory licence. Strasbourg Electricite Reseaux is one of a few local distributors operating outside the national grid monopoly, with tariffs set by the regulator. That is a narrow but real moat: returns are capped (group return on invested capital about 6%), but the franchise is not being eroded, and the supply arm's fall is the end of a windfall, not a loss of the licence. No secular force threatens the terminal value; electrification adds volume to the grid. The cheapness is a mix of a post-windfall earnings reset, a minority-control discount and a data error, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# MS&AD Insurance Group Holdings (8725.T) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-10. Evidence base: two earnings calls (fiscal 2025 full-year results on 2026-05-20; fiscal 2026 first-quarter results on 2026-08-14), the screener's financial trajectory, and a live Tokyo quote of 5,149 yen (2026-11-10). Both calls are partially truncated in the middle of the question-and-answer section, so the read below rests on the prepared remarks and the surviving analyst exchanges.*

**Bottom line:** MS&AD is a better insurer than it was two years ago, and management's numbers back their words. Domestic rate increases are sticking, the overseas book has broadened through the W.R. Berkley stake and the Barings investment, and capital is going back to shareholders at a disciplined pace. The caution for an investor is not credibility but quality of earnings: a large slice of reported profit still comes from selling down its portfolio of strategic shareholdings in other Japanese companies (a one-off, shrinking pool), and the first quarter of fiscal 2026 benefited from a benign catastrophe season and strong markets that management itself said should not be treated as normal.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **May 2026 (fiscal 2025 results):** the story was "record year plus a clean-up." Consolidated net income reached a record 787.3 billion yen and group adjusted profit (the company's own profit measure, which sets shareholder payouts) a record 1,000.9 billion yen. Management simultaneously did housekeeping: the life subsidiary sold yen loans to clear unrealised losses (a 51.9 billion yen loss at Mitsui Sumitomo Aioi Life), the group voluntarily switched to IFRS (international accounting standards), and the fiscal 2026 guide was reset to 800 billion yen of adjusted profit, or 532 billion yen excluding gains on strategic-shareholding sales, "the same level as the previous year."
- **August 2026 (first quarter):** the tone shifted from clean-up to delivery. Adjusted profit excluding shareholding gains was 251 billion yen, up 64.7 billion yen and 47.2% of the full-year guide after one quarter. International profit nearly doubled to 108.8 billion yen as W.R. Berkley equity earnings began contributing.
- **Drivers introduced:** W.R. Berkley (a US specialty insurer in which MS&AD built a stake) and the Barings business investment (closed May 2026) are the new growth legs abroad. The domestic merger of the two non-life companies (scheduled 2027-04-01) is the efficiency leg, with a 150 billion yen annual cost-saving target by 2030.
- **Quietly downplayed:** the European specialty book (MS Amlin) is facing market softening in property and energy lines; management acknowledged it but framed it as within plan.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence in the numbers | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Rate revisions are lifting domestic profit (May and Aug 2026) | Domestic non-life premiums +122.6 billion yen in fiscal 2025; auto loss ratio improved in Q1 fiscal 2026; group revenue +12.9% y/y, gross margin expanding | Matches |
| Record profit, rising earnings power | Net income 211 billion yen (FY2023) to 369 to 692 to 787 billion yen (FY2026 label); EPS 99.9 to 528.9 yen; trailing twelve-month diluted EPS 602 yen | Matches on reported basis, but flattered by shareholding sales (see below) |
| Underlying profit "same level as previous year" ex-gains (May 2026 guide of 532 billion yen) | Q1 alone delivered 251 billion yen, 47% of the year | Guide looks conservative, but management warned Q1 had light catastrophes and strong markets |
| Disciplined capital return (50% of adjusted profit, progressive dividend) | Dividend 145 to 160 yen (FY2025) to 170 yen guided; 270 billion yen of buybacks planned for fiscal 2026; share count down to roughly 1,420 million (market value 7.31 trillion yen at 5,149 yen) | Matches |
| Sound balance sheet | Economic solvency ratio (the regulator-style capital buffer) 214% at March 2026, 215% at June 2026; net cash about 439 billion yen at 2026-06-30 | Matches; the screener's Altman-Z of 1.0 is not meaningful for an insurer |
| Return on capital improving | ROE 11.4%, ROIC 11.6%, book value per share up about 13% a year over five years | Matches, though ROE is still below Tokio Marine-style levels the market rewards |

The main divergence: reported EPS (528.9 yen for the fiscal year; 602 yen trailing) includes strategic-shareholding gains targeted at 268 billion yen for fiscal 2026. Those gains are capital being released, not a recurring business. Stripping them out, the guided core is 532 billion yen, or roughly 375 yen a share on about 1,420 million shares - which is the number a valuation should lean on.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising, but measured.** In May the accounting head framed the 2030 target of 800 billion yen as more "probable" after scrutiny, not rounded up, and credited the international business for the uplift. In August he was candid in the other direction: "we should not consider this Q1 result is going to be the standard or average," and he declined to raise guidance despite a 47% progress ratio. That is offensive on strategy, defensive on near-term numbers - a credible posture for a Japanese insurer heading into its typecast November revision.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

- The fiscal 2025 dividend ended at 160 yen against an initial 155 yen guide: a small over-delivery.
- The fiscal 2025 adjusted profit came in at a record after an upward revision in November 2025 (per company announcements at the time), a pattern of guiding low and raising at the half-year.
- The screener's 2-of-4 quarterly beat rate reflects the IFRS transition noise and lumpy catastrophe losses more than poor forecasting; FMP shows the August 2026 quarter well above the estimate.
- **Reliability: High.** The sandbagging pattern is mild and consistent; the next test is the half-year results on 2026-11-19.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Is Q1 repeatable?** Analysts (Nomura, UBS) pushed for a guidance raise; management refused, citing benign catastrophes and markets.
- **Kumamoto earthquake (July 2026):** loss estimates were unavailable on 2026-08-14; management pointed to reinsurance and a 150 billion yen catastrophe reserve. This is the clearest open item for the half-year.
- **European softening (JPMorgan):** MS Amlin's property and energy lines are seeing price declines; management says profitability is secured technically. Worth watching.
- **Merger costs:** 111 billion yen of merger expenses in fiscal 2026, more in fiscal 2027; the 150 billion yen savings arrive gradually toward 2030.
- **Deflected:** management declined to say whether it sold its stake in the newly listed taxi app business.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: reported profit depends on a finite pool of strategic-shareholding gains (701 billion yen of holdings at March 2026 targeted down to 476 billion yen) - earnings quality will look weaker as the pool drains (May 2026).
- Red: the IFRS switch (from fiscal 2026) breaks year-on-year comparisons and recognises onerous-contract losses that Japanese standards did not (May 2026).
- Red: Kumamoto earthquake losses unquantified (Aug 2026); European property and energy softening (Aug 2026).
- Red: life subsidiary investment margins expected to decline (May 2026).
- Green: domestic auto loss ratios improving on rate increases; expense ratio down 0.3 points despite wage inflation (Aug 2026).
- Green: international profit diversified across the Americas (Berkley), Europe (MS Re, Amlin) and Asia (Aug 2026).
- Green: progressive dividend plus 270 billion yen of planned buybacks; solvency steady at 215% (Aug 2026).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The shift of the shareholder-return base from Japanese-standard group adjusted profit to an IFRS adjusted profit, with the IFRS restatement about 82 billion yen lower for fiscal 2025, subtly lowers the payout base.
- New voices: the August call was led by the named accounting head (Nakayama) rather than an anonymous executive - more open about variances.
- Capital allocation is moving from Japanese cross-shareholdings to stakes in foreign listed insurers and asset managers (Berkley, Barings): a structurally more mobile, higher-return capital base, but one that imports US equity-market sensitivity into reported earnings.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: strengthening.** The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: at 5,149 yen the stock trades at about 1.12 times restated book value (4,598 yen per share at 2026-06-30) and about 13.7 times guided core earnings excluding shareholding gains. The franchise is improving, but the price already reflects most of it; the visible cheapness on the screener's trailing EPS (8.6 times) is inflated by one-off shareholding gains.

**Moat:** a narrow but real moat built on scale and regulatory licence - one of three Japanese non-life megagroups in a consolidated, rational market where all three are pushing rate increases through. Returns are rising (ROE 11.4%, ROIC 11.6%, book value compounding about 13% a year), so the moat is stable to widening, not eroding. **Secular threat:** manageable. Over a decade, driver-assistance and autonomous vehicles could shrink auto claims frequency and premiums, auto being the largest domestic line; the diversification overseas and into fire, specialty and reinsurance blunts this. The valuation is not a fear-print on a shrinking base; it is a fair price on an improving one.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory improving · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Rithm Capital (RITM) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16 from five earnings calls (Q3-2025, 2025-10-30 through Q3-2026, 2026-10-23), the screener's financial trajectory and the Q3-2026 10-Q figures verified on 2026-11-02. Price used: $8.875 (NYSE, USD, FMP live quote 2026-11-16).*

**Takeaway.** Management tells a consistent story of a diversified mortgage-and-credit platform earning 18-19% on equity. The hard numbers say something more modest: book value per share has been roughly flat at about $12.5 for a year (US$12.66 at 2025-12-31, about $12.51 at 2026-09-30), and generally accepted accounting (GAAP) earnings over the last four quarters were $0.63 per share, a return on book of about 5%. Shareholders have been paid the $1.00 a year dividend and little else. The business is real, durable and covers its dividend; the gap between management's headline return and what owners actually earn is the single most important thing to weigh.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

- **Q3-2025 (2025-10-30):** the story was the operating businesses - Newrez (mortgage origination and servicing), Genesis (construction lending) and the investment portfolio - generating "an 18% ROE" (return on equity), plus two acquisitions announced: Crestline (an $18-20B credit manager) and Paramount (a New York and San Francisco office landlord, taken private). Management promised "we will not be raising equity" to fund them.
- **Q4-2025 (2026-02-03):** the emphasis widened to "over $100 billion in investable assets" across the firm, a record quarter for earnings available for distribution (EAD - management's preferred earnings measure, which strips out mark-to-market moves), and technology deals (Valon for servicing, HomeVision for origination).
- **Q1-2026 (2026-04-28):** a defensive turn into the private-credit headlines: "We do not see systemic risk in private credit," "a sentiment-driven dislocation." Paramount was renamed Elecor.
- **Q3-2026 (2026-10-23):** a new presentation framed Rithm as an asset manager in the making - "$60+ billion of third party AUM" (assets under management), and the first explicit hint at a structural change: "As asset management earnings scale, we have the potential to optimize our corporate structure." Origination was openly demoted: "We do not need to originate a mortgage to make money."

The arc moves from a mortgage REIT with operating companies toward a self-described alternative asset manager. That is a pivot in framing; the balance sheet and earnings mix (still dominated by servicing rights and the mortgage company) have not pivoted yet.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | What the numbers show | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Generating an 18% ROE" (Q3-2025); 19% operating ROE (Q1-2026) | GAAP EPS fell from $1.67 (2024) to $1.04 (2025) and $0.63 over the trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30; book per share roughly flat over the year. GAAP return on book is about 5%; book change plus dividends is roughly 6-8% a year | Narrative much richer than the evidence. EAD excludes the running decay in servicing-rights value that GAAP captures |
| EAD above the dividend for 28 straight quarters (Q3-2026) | Q3-2026 EAD $0.55 against a $0.25 dividend; GAAP Q3 $0.38 (10-Q) | True - the dividend is covered on every measure that matters |
| Book value "a little bit higher quarter over quarter" (Q3-2026) | Common book about $6.99B, $12.51 per share at 2026-09-30, versus $12.66 at 2025-12-31 | Roughly flat - holds, but shows no compounding |
| Acquisitions funded without new equity (Q3-2025) | Diluted share count stayed in the 550-575M range; total debt rose from $40.2B (2026-06-30) to $42.2B (2026-09-30) | Kept the promise on equity, but leverage carried the growth |
| Revenue growth (+20% in 2025, ~50% three-year growth rate) | Driven by acquisitions (Sculptor 2023, Crestline and Paramount 2025); net income did not follow (from $932M in 2024 to $681M in 2025) | Growth bought, not earned per share |
| Asset management "seeing real inflows" (Q3-2026) | Year-to-date inflows "a little bit south of $3 billion," and $569M raised in the quarter - below the 2025 pace | Softer than the tone |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable, with a promotional lean.** Every call opens with superlatives ("a great quarter," "demonstrated the power of the platform," "I have never been more excited about the trajectory of our firm" - Q3-2026). The tone survived a hard Q3-2026 tape ("Interest rates rose. Significantly... and we still had a great quarter"), which is fair: the servicing book is a natural hedge to rising rates. Guidance specificity has not improved - management gives almost no forward numbers, only targets like "a mid teens return" on new origination (Q3-2026) and about $125M of annualised cost savings (Q3-2026 coverage, 2026-11-03).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Rithm gives little formal guidance, so the test is the commitments it does make. Kept: no equity raise for the 2025 acquisitions; the dividend covered 28 quarters in a row; the earnings-beat rate is 6 of 7 quarters (86%) on consensus. Not delivered: the repeated "18-19% ROE" never reaches GAAP earnings or book-value growth, and the 2025 EPS fell 38%. Buybacks were explicitly ruled out (Q3-2025: "we're not going to be doing share buybacks") even at about 0.7 times book - a choice that tells you management prefers growing the platform over buying its own discount. **Reliability: Medium.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **The discount to book and buybacks** (Q1-2026, Piper Sandler): "trading low to mid-single-digit multiple sizable discount to book value... why you wouldn't be leaning more into the buyback." Answer: as a REIT "we continue to distribute more capital" and growth "is going to reward shareholders in a different way." A non-answer to the arithmetic.
- **Dividend increase** (Q3-2025 and Q1-2026): definitively no - "there's no desire to increase the dividend at this point."
- **Origination economics at 7%+ mortgage rates** (Q3-2026, Wedbush): management will originate only when the servicing right and gain on sale justify it - an honest admission that origination is a cyclical swing business.
- **Liquidity versus opportunities** (Q3-2026): "we are not here to just grow the balance sheet" - yet total debt rose $2B in that quarter.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: GAAP earnings per share down from $1.80 (2022) to $0.63 trailing twelve months; the 18-19% headline return is a non-GAAP measure.
- Red: total debt up about $2.0B quarter on quarter to $42.2B at 2026-09-30 while common equity was flat (10-Q, 2026-11-02).
- Red: open-market insider activity is 7 sells (about 525,000 shares) and 0 buys at a 30% discount to book.
- Red: office exposure via Elecor (New York and San Francisco) adds a credit-sensitive asset to a rate-sensitive book.
- Red: margins were squeezed through the 2021-22 inflation (gross margin 85.1% to 61.6%).
- Green: dividend covered 28 consecutive quarters; about 11% yield at today's price.
- Green: book held flat to slightly up in Q3-2026 despite wider spreads and sharply higher rates - the servicing hedge works as designed.
- Green: scale - third-largest US mortgage servicer, about $880B of servicing, about 4 million customers.
- Green: Genesis grew production from $1.7B (2022) to about $5B (2025) with no reported credit issues.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- The Q3-2026 presentation "changed... a bit" to tell "the Rithm journey" - and the phrase "optimize our corporate structure... have that as its own segment" is new. It hints at an eventual separation of the asset manager, but it is conditional ("we need to continue to grow our so called FRE," fee-related earnings) and undated.
- AI and Valon now feature in every call as the cost lever; conversion runs "throughout the end of 2027" (Q3-2026), so the savings are a 2027-28 story.
- The real estate voice (Peter Brindley, Elecor) now sits on the call alongside the mortgage president - office is being promoted to a core line.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: turning** - from a mortgage REIT toward an asset manager, still financed by the mortgage balance sheet. The single most important thing before sizing: the stock is cheap against book (about 0.71 times $12.51), but book has not grown, and the GAAP return on it (about 5-8%) sits below a roughly 11% cost of equity. The discount is mostly deserved unless returns rise.

**Moat.** Scale-cost in servicing (third-largest US servicer; servicing is a fixed-cost, technology-driven business where size lowers unit cost) plus a regulatory-licence and data advantage in owning the customer. It is a narrow but real moat: returns are low but not falling structurally, and the servicing book behaves as designed through rate cycles. Secular threat: manageable - AI is more likely to cut Rithm's servicing costs than to displace it, and fintech originators compete on origination, which management is already de-emphasising. The cheapness reads as part fear-print (mortgage-REIT and private-credit sentiment) and part fair discount for sub-par returns - not a structurally shrinking base.

picks.interrogator_dossier:
# Old Republic International (ORI) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Coverage: five earnings calls, Q3 2025 (2025-10-23) through Q3 2026 (2026-10-22). Live price used: $39.87 (NYSE, USD, FMP quote 2026-11-16).*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Old Republic is a decentralized group of 21-plus specialty property-and-casualty (P&C) insurance companies plus the third-largest-style national title insurer (Old Republic National Title). The story across the five calls has moved from **"record profits and excess capital"** to **"defending margins through a softening pricing cycle."**

- **Q3 2025 to Q4 2025 (2025-10-23, 2026-01-22):** the emphasis was harvest. Full-year 2025 pretax operating income reached about $900 million, the operating return on beginning equity (operating profit divided by shareholders' equity at the start of the period) ran around 14%, and a December 2025 special dividend sat alongside buybacks. Book value per share including dividends grew 22% in 2025. The ECM acquisition (a farm-and-agriculture mutual insurer bought through a sponsored demutualization, about $220-237 million of direct premium) was introduced as a niche bolt-on.
- **Q1 2026 to Q2 2026 (2026-04-23, 2026-07-23):** the combined ratio (claims plus expenses as a share of premiums; below 100% means an underwriting profit) drifted up from the low 93s a year earlier to 96.6% and then 95.3%. Return on equity fell to roughly 11-12%. Management began talking about newer start-up operating companies and auto-warranty growth as the top-line engine.
- **Q3 2026 (2026-10-22):** the language is now explicitly late-cycle: "competition remains active," "legal system abuse continues to put pressure on severity," and in title "the recent increase in mortgage interest rates does create some uncertainty." Growth is being sourced from ECM (consolidated for the first time) and a fast-growing auto-warranty book; excluding both, specialty net premiums written grew only 4.4%.

The thesis has contracted from "best-in-class underwriter compounding book value at mid-teens" to "disciplined underwriter holding a 12% return through a soft market."

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| Underwriting discipline keeps the combined ratio within 90-95% through the cycle (CEO, 2026-10-22) | Consolidated 95.3% (Q3'25) -> 96.6% (Q1'26) -> 95.3% (Q2'26) -> 96.1% (Q3'26). The CEO himself said "we're at the top end" and hopes to finish the year "within our range." | Matches today, but with no margin of error. The reserve-release cushion is shrinking: favorable development added 1.1 points in Q3'26 vs 2.5 points a year earlier, and only 0.8 points in specialty vs 3.4 points. |
| Reserving is conservative | Favorable prior-year development continued every quarter in aggregate. But Q3'26 shows elevated adverse development in general liability and financial indemnity, and lower workers' comp releases. | Still conservative overall; the composition is worsening in the liability lines that are most exposed to social inflation (rising jury awards and litigation costs). |
| Specialty premium growth +10.5% | Ex-ECM and ex-auto-warranty retail write-up: +4.4%. | The headline is flattered by acquisition and a new, lower-margin program business. |
| Earnings power is growing | FY EPS 2.10 (2023) -> 3.24 (2024) -> 3.73 (2025); TTM diluted EPS $4.45 includes investment gains. Q3'26 operating EPS $0.73 vs $0.78, missing the $0.77 consensus (Zacks, 2026-10-22). Latest-quarter EPS down 11% year over year. | GAAP EPS overstates run-rate; operating EPS is flat-to-down in 2026. Recurring operating EPS is about $3.00-3.10. |
| Capital return is generous | Q3'26: $76M dividends + $114M buybacks; another $60M bought after quarter-end; about $460M left on the program. Regular dividend 31.5 cents declared 2026-11-13 (payable 2026-12-15). | Corroborated. Buybacks at ~1.6 times book are less accretive than they were at 1.2 times. |
| Balance sheet strength | Recomputed net cash $2.11B at 2026-09-30 (cash $3.86B vs debt $1.75B). Debt was refinanced in 2026. The scan's Altman-Z of 1.4 is meaningless for an insurer. | Strong; but the cash is mostly insurance float backing reserves, not freely distributable. |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Declining, from confident to guarded.**
- Q4 2025 (2026-01-22): celebratory - "another all-time high" for specialty pretax income; explicit openness to repeating the special dividend.
- Q1 2026 (2026-04-23): neutral; heavy buybacks ($161M), ECM close guidance.
- Q2 2026 (2026-07-23): "if we are still in a position where we think we have excess capital, we will still consider issuing a special dividend" - conditional rather than expected.
- Q3 2026 (2026-10-22): defensive - "we're going to work very hard to not exceed the top end as we persevere through a softer market in the next few years," and "top line could suffer." The CEO calls top line "the wildcard."

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Old Republic gives little numeric guidance; it guides on a 90-95% combined-ratio range and ROE targets. It has stayed inside or at the edge of that range each quarter, and ECM closed on schedule (guided ~July 1). The earnings-beat rate is weak - 3 of the last 7 quarters (43%) - and Q3'26 missed. Management does not sandbag; it is candid that the cycle is turning. **Reliability: High on discipline and capital return, Medium on earnings trajectory.**

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Where the combined ratio goes in a soft market** (Q3'26): analysts pushed whether the ratio must breach 95% before it normalizes. Answer: aim to stay at or below 95%, with top line the variable.
- **Size of the auto-warranty book** (Raymond James, Q3'26): year-to-date net written $546M vs $350M a year earlier; the CEO said $600-700M annual "isn't out of the question and even higher." This is a new, fast-growing exposure whose loss experience is unproven at scale.
- **Title and mortgage rates:** the CEO said 30-year mortgage rates now have "a 7% in front" instead of 6%, which "gives us pause." Commercial title is the offset.
- **Under-asked:** the adverse development in general liability and financial indemnity, and the $20M credit charge in Q3'26 (1.4 points of specialty expense ratio).

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: favorable reserve development roughly halving year over year in specialty (Q3'26: 0.8 vs 3.4 points).
- Red: adverse development in general liability and financial indemnity (Q3'26).
- Red: growth increasingly from acquisition (ECM) and a new program business (auto warranty) rather than core lines (+4.4% organic).
- Red: insider open-market activity is net selling - 3 small buys (1,435 shares) vs 7 sells (52,230 shares).
- Red: Q3'26 operating EPS miss ($0.73 vs $0.77 consensus) and operating ROE stuck at 12.1%, down from about 14% in 2025.
- Green: still an underwriting profit every quarter; mid-teens rate increases on commercial auto and general liability (Q3'26) show a rational market in the riskiest lines.
- Green: new money bond yields 5.4% vs 4.4% rolling off; book yield near 4.9% (Q3'26) - investment income keeps rising.
- Green: consistent capital return; bargain-purchase gain on ECM added to book value.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- New disclosure in Q3'26: a combined ratio "excluding the retail write-up portion of our auto warranty business." Adding a carve-out metric when the headline worsens is a mild flag, though the stated reason (mix distortion) is plausible.
- Capital-allocation vocabulary has moved from "special dividend" as a regular reset (Q4'25) to conditional language (Q2'26) and silence in Q3'26, while buybacks rose.
- The vocabulary of growth now centers on "start-ups" and "partnerships with administrators" - Old Republic is buying growth that is less tied to the P&C cycle, which is sensible diversification but dilutes the proven core.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STABLE.** The franchise is sound and the capital return is real, but earnings are flat-to-down into a softening cycle and the reserve cushion is thinner. The single most important thing to weigh: **at $39.87 the stock is about 1.6 times book value ($24.65 at 2026-09-30) and about 13 times recurring operating earnings for a 12% return on equity** - that is a fair price for this business, not a discount; any edge has to come from the entry price, not from the thesis.

**Moat:** a narrow but real moat - scale-cost and underwriting-specialization advantages in niche commercial lines plus a regulatory-license and agency-network position in title. Returns are stable-to-slightly-softer rather than structurally falling: the 2026 dip in return on equity is the pricing cycle, not erosion. **Secular threat: manageable** - title has a long-running disintermediation debate (title waivers, alternative title products) and commercial auto faces social inflation, but neither is a terminal force today. The current price is neither a fear print nor a value trap; it is fair value.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Porto Seguro S.A. (PSSA3.SA) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*As of 2026-11-02. Price used: R$44.75 (B3 listing PSSA3.SA, Brazilian reais), FMP live quote, which is also the 52-week low (range R$44.75-55.72; 50-day average R$49.85, 200-day average R$50.68).*

**Source note.** FMP holds no earnings-call transcript for this listing, and no transcript text was retrievable in this run. This dossier therefore reads management through dated third-party coverage of the second-quarter 2026 release (Seu Dinheiro, 2026-08-07; AUVP Analitica, 2026-08-07; InfoMoney on the first quarter), plus FMP's quarterly statements. Short quotes are limited to what those sources printed. Nothing here is drawn from a call transcript, and no transcript phrase is invented.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Grupo Porto (the holding company, listed as Porto Seguro S.A.) has spent three years retelling itself from "Brazil's auto insurer" to "a diversified ecosystem" of four verticals: Porto Seguro (auto, home, life insurance), Porto Saude (health plans and dental), Porto Bank (credit cards, consumer loans, consortium, which are pooled purchase plans, and financing) and Porto Servicos (assistance and services). The second-quarter 2026 message from CEO Paulo Kakinoff was that the quarter "reflects how our diversification strategy" works: insurance and health carried the group while the bank stumbled.

The emphasis has shifted during 2026. Early in the year (fourth-quarter 2025 release, February 2026) the story was growth plus capital return - a buyback of up to 18.5 million shares was announced alongside a guidance set the market read as conservative. By August the story was defensive on credit: the bank "tightened credit criteria, strengthened collection" and steered growth toward products with stronger collateral.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Diversification protects earnings | Group net income R$879.4m in 2Q26, flat (+0.2%) year on year, while the bank's profit fell 32.5%; first-half 2026 net income R$2.01bn, +17.7% | Holds - the insurance and health lines absorbed a sharp bank miss |
| Core insurance is a high-return franchise | Insurance vertical profit R$455.8m (+4.9%), return on average equity (ROAE) about 32.9%; insurance loss ratio (claims as a share of premiums) down 1.4 points to 49.1% | Corroborated |
| Porto Saude is a growth engine | Health profit R$143.9m, +36.4%; premium growth guidance of +14% to +22% kept | Corroborated |
| Porto Bank credit is under control | 90-day-plus delinquency on the 360-day book rose to 9.4% from 8.2% a quarter earlier; provisions R$868m, +67% year on year; 2026 expected-credit-loss guidance raised to R$3.1-3.5bn from R$2.7-3.1bn | Not corroborated - the weak point |
| Group return stays above 20% | ROAE 22.1% in 2Q26, about 2 points below 2Q25; 3Q25 was about 23% | Holds, drifting lower |

FMP's trailing-twelve-month (TTM) earnings per share are R$5.71 (2025 fiscal year R$5.21, +27.7%), so the shares trade near 7.8 times trailing earnings and about 1.8 times book value (equity R$16.1bn, about R$25 per share on roughly 641 million shares). The negative TTM free cash flow (-R$202m) is not a useful signal for an insurer-plus-bank: loan-book growth and investment-portfolio flows run through operating cash. Likewise the "net debt" of R$21.7bn on FMP's 2026-06-30 balance sheet appeared in one quarter (total debt R$0.8bn at 2026-03-31) alongside a matching jump in long-term investments from R$0.4bn to R$42.5bn - a reclassification of bank funding and insurance liabilities, not new corporate borrowing.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable overall, defensive on credit. Insurance and health guidance were kept or improved in August (insurance loss-ratio range tightened to 50-54% from 50.5-54.5%; bank efficiency ratio range improved to 24-28% from 27-31%; tax-rate range lowered). The only line that worsened was bank credit losses. Management language moved from growth to "more conservative risk management" in the bank, which is the correct posture but a retreat from 2025's expansion.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium-high. The first quarter of 2026 (R$1.13bn profit) came in above expectations; the second quarter was flat on a year earlier with insurance beating and the bank missing (Santander noted pre-tax profit 12% below its estimate). The scan records beats in 4 of the last 7 quarters (57%). The August revisions were mostly favorable, with one material unfavorable change. No sign of sandbagging; the credit-loss raise shows a willingness to reset openly mid-year.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- Porto Bank asset quality: BTG called the bank "the clear weak point"; Citi said provisions consumed nearly all of the credit spread and stays cautious on consumer credit.
- Valuation premium versus insurance peers: Santander argued continued credit deterioration "challenges" Porto's premium to other insurers.
- Whether diversification is a hedge or a drag: if the bank keeps absorbing provisions near R$850m a quarter (BTG's reading of the new guide), the group return drifts toward 20%.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- Red: 90-day delinquency 8.2% to 9.4% in one quarter (2Q26); provisions +67% year on year (2Q26); credit-loss guidance raised (2026-08-07).
- Red: group ROAE down about 2 points year on year (2Q26); stock now at its 52-week low, about 11% below the R$50.45 it traded at on results day.
- Green: insurance loss ratio improved 1.4 points to 49.1% (2Q26); health profit +36% (2Q26); bank efficiency ratio 25.4%, better by 4 points year on year.
- Green: buyback of up to 18.5 million shares (announced February 2026); share count fell from about 651.6m (2Q25) to 649.5m weighted (2Q26).

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The bank's repositioning toward collateralised products is a quiet admission that unsecured card growth in 2024-25 was priced too thin for a high-rate Brazil. The group's financial result guidance (R$1.4-1.8bn) was left unchanged despite high local rates, which caps the float tailwind. The near-unchanged headline profit masks a mix shift: about two-thirds of profit now comes from insurance and health, where returns are highest.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. The single most important thing to weigh is whether Porto Bank's credit cycle has peaked. The insurance franchise alone (about R$1.8bn of annual profit at a 33% return) supports most of today's market value of about R$28.7bn; the question is whether the bank is a temporary drag or a structural leak.

Moat: a narrow but real moat - the brand, Brazil's largest auto-insurance broker network and claims/assistance scale give a cost and distribution edge that shows up in a 49% loss ratio and a 30%-plus insurance return; it is stable, not widening, because auto insurance in Brazil is competitive and the bank's returns are cyclical. Secular threat: manageable. Autonomous driving could eventually shrink auto-insurance premiums, but adoption in Brazil is far off and Porto has diversified into health and services. The cheapness reads as a credit-cycle fear print, not a structurally shrinking base.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# INVR.L - a deep dive on management and the setup (2026-11-16)

**The first finding decides everything else: INVR.L is not Investec's ordinary share.** The London line the screener calls "INVR.L" carries ISIN GB00B19RX541. That ISIN belongs to Investec plc's sterling **non-redeemable, non-cumulative, non-participating preference shares**. Investec's own dividend notices call the line INPP; market-data vendors list it as INVR. Investec's notice of 10 November 2025 gives the issued capital as **2,754,587 preference shares**. In plain terms:

- **Non-redeemable:** the company never has to pay the money back.
- **Non-cumulative:** a skipped dividend is lost for good. It is not owed later.
- **Non-participating:** the holder gets the fixed dividend formula and nothing more. They have no share in profit growth, buybacks or a re-rating.

Investec's ordinary share trades on a separate line, INVP.L, at 624p on 2026-11-16 (FMP live quote). The JSE line INP.JO traded at R140.93 the same day.

Every fundamental in the screener row belongs to the Investec plc group, not to this instrument. That covers revenue of £4.73B, EPS of 0.77, ROE of 11.2%, "net cash £3.71B", the earnings-power value margin of safety of +47% and the "Buffett fair value 661". So the deep-value signal is a category error: a bank's equity metrics were mapped onto a bond-like perpetual preference share. The 52-week low of 6.45 against a high of 709.7 is a pence-versus-pounds unit artifact in the price history, not a real move. The peer-group agent also flagged the line as unmapped.

No earnings-call transcript is bundled, and none applies to a preference share. The analysis below reads management's record as the **issuer** of the preference share: how able and willing Investec plc is to keep paying the dividend.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
The group's story over FY2024-FY2026 (fiscal years end 31 March) has been simplification and capital return:
- the Investec Wealth & Investment combination with Rathbones in 2023 (the FY2024 £303M gain from discontinued operations in FMP's income statement),
- a run of record ordinary dividends (FY2026 total 38.5p, final 21.0p, declared at the 21 May 2026 results),
- active management of legacy capital instruments. In January 2026 Investec plc tendered for its £350M 2.625% subordinated notes due 2032 (maximum acceptance £300M, 23 January 2026; £55.78M left outstanding per the 30 January 2026 result). From January to March 2026 the sister company Investec Limited bought back its own JSE preference shares in the market (23,819,526 in issue in late January, 23,345,033 by 20 March 2026), with the bought-back shares delisted and cancelled.

For this line the arc is quiet. The sterling preference shares keep receiving half-yearly dividends set by formula, and no tender or redemption of the plc sterling preference shares has been announced.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Claim / screen input | What it really is | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Margin of safety +47% (earnings-power value), Buffett fair value 661" | Group equity models applied to a preference share | Not applicable. Preference holders do not own these earnings. |
| "Net cash £3.71B" | A bank's cash against its funding debt. For a bank this is the operating balance sheet, not a surplus. | Not a sum-of-the-parts add-back for any holder, least of all a preference holder. |
| "Revenue +365% YoY" | FMP reclassified FY2025 revenue (£1.02B against about £4.7-4.8B in the other years) | Data artifact. |
| "52-week range 6.45-709.7" | Pence/pounds unit glitch | Data artifact. The line actually traded 687.5-700p from September to November 2026 (FMP daily history). |
| Dividend capacity | Group FY2026 net income about £340M (FMP plc line) against an annual preference cost of roughly 2.75M shares x about 50-55p, or about £1.4-1.5M | Coverage is very large. Payment risk comes from regulatory or stress blocks on discretionary distributions, not from earnings. |

Recent dividends on this line, from Investec notices:
- year to 31 March 2025 final (October 2024-March 2025): 28.55478p
- H1 FY2026 (April-September 2025, dividend number 39, paid 12 December 2025): 26.19862p

The fall between the two periods tracks the drop in UK policy rates. That is consistent with a dividend linked to Bank of England base rate. I could not open the terms of issue to confirm the exact formula (it appears to be about base rate plus 1% on a £10 subscription price). This is inferred, not verified. FMP lists the trailing dividend as 50.42p.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Stable. The issuer communicates through formula-driven dividend notices, and nothing in them is discretionary or promotional. Group tone at the FY2026 results (21 May 2026, "another record dividend") was confident.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
High for this line's purpose. The sterling preference dividend has been declared every half-year in the notices we found (numbers up to 39 by November 2025), and none was skipped in the period reviewed. The group beat 2 of 3 recent quarters per the screen, which matters only for coverage, and coverage is ample.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- No analyst covers this line. FMP has no price targets, and none were found on the web for the preference share.
- The live questions are fixed-income ones. How far will UK base rate fall, which cuts the dividend? Will Investec retire legacy preference shares that no longer count as regulatory capital? (Investec Limited did this in South Africa in 2026, but no plc action has been announced.)

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: the dividend floats down with base rate, so the yield on today's 700p price shrinks with each rate cut.
- Red: the shares are non-cumulative, so a skipped payment is lost for good.
- Red: liquidity is extremely thin. Average daily volume is about 1,000 shares, with many zero-volume days in October-November 2026, and HL showed a dealing spread of about 645-675p on an undated quote. Getting in or out costs several percent.
- Red: there is no participation, so the upside is capped by yield arithmetic.
- Green: the issuer is well capitalised and profitable, and the preference cost is immaterial to the group (about 0.4% of net income).
- Green: there is a precedent of the group retiring legacy capital (the plc subordinated-note tender in January 2026; Investec Limited's preference buybacks in January-March 2026). A tender for these shares at a premium is possible but unannounced.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The tell is in the data, not in management speech. The flat 690-700p price, the beta of -0.15 and the volume of about 1,000 shares a day are the fingerprint of a bond-like security. The screener's "deep value" label rests entirely on borrowed equity fundamentals.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Trajectory: stable. The single thing the director must weigh is that **this is not an equity position in Investec**. It is a perpetual, base-rate-linked, skippable preference dividend. At 700p it yields about 7% on trailing payments, with no claim on Investec's growth. Its fair value is the dividend divided by the yield investors demand for illiquid, non-cumulative bank preference shares. On today's numbers that lands at or slightly below the price, so there is no margin of safety. Anyone who wants the Investec equity value case has to evaluate INVP.L, a separate security.

Moat: the issuer is a specialist bank and wealth franchise in the UK and South Africa with a narrow but real moat (relationship banking, regulatory licence). Its group ROE is about 11% and steady (FMP), but a preference holder cannot capture it. Secular threat: manageable (fintech competition in private banking). The instrument's own risk is rate-driven, not structural.

Management credibility 4 of 5 · trajectory steady · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.

# Webuild S.p.A. (WBD.MI, Borsa Italiana, EUR) - forensic dossier, 2026-11-09

Takeaway: a growing, margin-improving contractor whose earnings are real on paper but have not turned into cash, run by management that leads with an adjusted "net cash" figure the statutory balance sheet does not show. The Italian state funded more of the disputed rail overruns in the budget bill on 2026-11-01, which eases the worst liquidity fear, but sites are still slowing over unpaid work and the promised 2026-2029 plan remains undated. Live price EUR 2.176 (FMP quote, Milan listing, 2026-11-09).

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
On the 2026-07-30 first-half call (the latest transcript), management told a story of scale turning into value: revenue held at a record EUR 6.7B despite two cancelled NEOM contracts in Saudi Arabia (about EUR 3.8B of backlog, more than EUR 550M of 2026 revenue), EBITDA up 14% to EUR 673M, a EUR 47B construction backlog, and a 2026-2029 business plan "at the end of September" built on vertical integration and "stable and predictable cash generation". The plan was then postponed on 2026-09-23 until after the Trevi takeover. Since our last review (2026-10-12) the story has moved to two fronts: winning Trevi (rival bidder ICOP withdrew on 2026-11-05; Webuild owns about 42% as of 2026-11-09 and the offer is now mandatory and unconditional, closing 2026-11-20, payment 2026-11-27) and getting paid by the state rail operator RFI.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
- "Net cash of EUR 110M" (company definition) versus statutory net debt of about EUR 960M at 2026-06-30 (borrowings EUR 3.25B plus EUR 77M leases, minus EUR 2.37B cash). The gap is the company excluding project-level and Panama Canal debt and including items it treats as cash-like. We use the statutory figure.
- Trailing free cash flow is negative EUR 559M (to 2026-06-30) against EUR 240M of 2025 net income. Earnings are not converting.
- Financial expenses rose EUR 93M in the half, explained as interest waived on receivables in settlement deals plus "a genuine one-off write-down". Waiving interest to collect faster is a sign the receivables are hard to collect.
- Return on invested capital about 3.5%, below any reasonable cost of capital for a BB+ issuer paying 5.1% on debt.
- Altman Z about 0.8 (a solvency stress score; below 1.8 is the distress zone), though typical of contractors carrying large advances and receivables.
- Positive: S&P confirmed the BB+ rating on 2026-11-09, citing the order book and rising margins; 95% of debt is fixed rate and little matures before late 2028.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
Confident and promotional on the call ("no single project or market can affect our ability to create value"). Since September the tone has turned defensive and public: a leaked letter to the government, a complaint to the market regulator Consob, RFI publicly contradicting Webuild (2026-09-18), "Works done, RFI must pay" (2026-10-22), and on 2026-11-06 press reports of Webuild pressing the government over accumulated receivables on the Brenner tunnel. Workers on several rail sites were put on short-time pay in October.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
2026 guidance was confirmed after the September headlines and the backlog does cover 2026 revenue, so the top-line guide is credible. The cash promise is not yet tested: capital spending of about EUR 700M this year was called "a peak", and the plan meant to set cash targets has slipped once already. The third-quarter update is still pending (date not confirmed in the sources we could reach).

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
Analysts pressed on Saudi exposure after NEOM, whether EUR 700M of capital spending is a peak (answer: yes), Trevi synergies (EUR 80-90M of EBITDA "from 2027", with no ramp detail) and Trevi's 60% emerging-market revenue, which runs against Webuild's stated low-risk-geography strategy. No analyst pushed on the net-cash definition or cash conversion, which is the real question. No current analyst price-target consensus could be verified for this listing.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
Red: statutory net debt versus headline net cash; negative free cash flow; interest waived to collect receivables; public payment fight with its largest domestic client; rail sites slowing and short-time work (2026-10-16 to 2026-11-03); arsenic-bearing spoil raising Brenner disposal costs (2026-11-02 and 2026-11-09); Libyan Autostrada della Pace contract torn up by the Haftar administration (2026-10-07); a debt-funded acquisition (mandatory offer of about EUR 222M for the remainder of Trevi) while cash is negative; finance chief departure in September.
Green: record backlog with price-adjustment clauses; margins rising (EBITDA margin 10.1%); the 2026 budget bill adds about EUR 1.6B for the Terzo Valico rail line (2026-11-01/02), showing the state is funding overruns rather than refusing them; new orders (Genoa sub-port tunnel lot B, EUR 803M, signed 2026-10-15; Toronto Ontario Line, 2026-08-05); S&P BB+ confirmed with stable outlook (2026-11-09); bond maturities pushed to 2028+.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
The rescue money is coming through the budget, not through settled claims: the state is paying more for the projects, but the receivable dispute itself is not closed, so cash timing still depends on RFI. Management's choice to spend on Trevi before publishing cash targets suggests growth and control rank ahead of cash return in their priorities. The share price recovered from EUR 1.81 to about EUR 2.18 into the budget news and the Trevi win, so some relief is already priced.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
Operations are improving and the state is still paying for its rail program, but cash conversion is the unproven link and management is spending on an acquisition before proving it. Treat the stock as an earnings-cheap, cash-unproven contractor: worth owning only at a price that pays for the cash risk, or after a plan with statutory free-cash-flow targets is published and starts to be met.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
